title: 013_polyhedron_formula
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Polyhedron Formula" from Hundred Theorems item 013:
% Euler's vertex-edge-facet formula for full-dimensional convex 3-polytopes. This file contains no proof.

polyhedron_formula_013: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real, z_coord: real #]
  point_set: TYPE = [point -> bool]
  face_collection: TYPE = [point_set -> bool]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[point]

  affine_combination(t: real, a, b: point): point =
    (# x_coord := (1 - t) * x_coord(a) + t * x_coord(b),
       y_coord := (1 - t) * y_coord(a) + t * y_coord(b),
       z_coord := (1 - t) * z_coord(a) + t * z_coord(b) #)

  subset(s, t: point_set): bool =
    FORALL (x: point): s(x) IMPLIES t(x)

  convex(s: point_set): bool =
    FORALL (a, b: point), (t: real):
      s(a) AND s(b) AND 0 <= t AND t <= 1
        IMPLIES s(affine_combination(t, a, b))

  convex_hull(s: point_set): point_set =
    LAMBDA (x: point):
      FORALL (c: point_set):
        convex(c) AND subset(s, c) IMPLIES c(x)

  polytope(p: point_set): bool =
    EXISTS (generators: finite_set[point]):
      FORALL (x: point):
        p(x) IFF convex_hull(generators)(x)

  face_of(f, p: point_set): bool =
    subset(f, p)
      AND convex(f)
      AND FORALL (a, b: point), (t: real):
        p(a) AND p(b) AND 0 < t AND t < 1
          AND f(affine_combination(t, a, b))
        IMPLIES f(a) AND f(b)

  delta_x(a, b: point): real = x_coord(b) - x_coord(a)
  delta_y(a, b: point): real = y_coord(b) - y_coord(a)
  delta_z(a, b: point): real = z_coord(b) - z_coord(a)

  cross_x(a, b, c: point): real =
    delta_y(a, b) * delta_z(a, c)
      - delta_z(a, b) * delta_y(a, c)

  cross_y(a, b, c: point): real =
    delta_z(a, b) * delta_x(a, c)
      - delta_x(a, b) * delta_z(a, c)

  cross_z(a, b, c: point): real =
    delta_x(a, b) * delta_y(a, c)
      - delta_y(a, b) * delta_x(a, c)

  determinant(a, b, c, d: point): real =
    delta_x(a, b)
      * (delta_y(a, c) * delta_z(a, d)
           - delta_z(a, c) * delta_y(a, d))
      - delta_y(a, b)
      * (delta_x(a, c) * delta_z(a, d)
           - delta_z(a, c) * delta_x(a, d))
      + delta_z(a, b)
      * (delta_x(a, c) * delta_y(a, d)
           - delta_y(a, c) * delta_x(a, d))

  collinear(a, b, c: point): bool =
    cross_x(a, b, c) = 0
      AND cross_y(a, b, c) = 0
      AND cross_z(a, b, c) = 0

  coplanar(a, b, c, d: point): bool =
    determinant(a, b, c, d) = 0

  affine_dimension(s: point_set, dimension: int): bool =
    (dimension = -1 AND FORALL (x: point): NOT s(x))
      OR (dimension = 0
          AND EXISTS (a: point):
            s(a) AND FORALL (x: point): s(x) IMPLIES x = a)
      OR (dimension = 1
          AND EXISTS (a, b: point):
            s(a) AND s(b) AND a /= b
              AND FORALL (x: point): s(x) IMPLIES collinear(a, b, x))
      OR (dimension = 2
          AND EXISTS (a, b, c: point):
            s(a) AND s(b) AND s(c) AND NOT collinear(a, b, c)
              AND FORALL (x: point): s(x) IMPLIES coplanar(a, b, c, x))
      OR (dimension = 3
          AND EXISTS (a, b, c, d: point):
            s(a) AND s(b) AND s(c) AND s(d)
              AND determinant(a, b, c, d) /= 0)

  faces_of_dimension(p: point_set, dimension: int): face_collection =
    LAMBDA (f: point_set):
      face_of(f, p) AND affine_dimension(f, dimension)

  has_cardinality(collection: face_collection, n: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (enumeration: [below(n) -> point_set]):
      (FORALL (i, j: below(n)):
        enumeration(i) = enumeration(j) IMPLIES i = j)
      AND (FORALL (f: point_set):
        collection(f) IFF
          EXISTS (i: below(n)): enumeration(i) = f)

  polyhedron_formula: bool =
    FORALL (p: point_set):
      polytope(p) AND affine_dimension(p, 3)
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (number_of_vertices, number_of_edges, number_of_facets: nat):
          has_cardinality(
            faces_of_dimension(p, 0), number_of_vertices)
          AND has_cardinality(
            faces_of_dimension(p, 1), number_of_edges)
          AND has_cardinality(
            faces_of_dimension(p, 2), number_of_facets)
          AND number_of_vertices + number_of_facets
            = number_of_edges + 2
END polyhedron_formula_013

title: 014_euler_s_summation_of_1_+__1_2_^2_+__1_3_^2_+
content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2022 David Loeffler. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: David Loeffler
-/
module

public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.BernoulliPolynomials
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.Basic
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Polynomial
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Polynomial
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Fourier.AddCircle
public import Mathlib.Analysis.PSeries

/-!
# Critical values of the Riemann zeta function

In this file we prove formulae for the critical values of `ζ(s)`, and more generally of Hurwitz
zeta functions, in terms of Bernoulli polynomials.

## Main results:

* `hasSum_zeta_nat`: the final formula for zeta values,
  $$\zeta(2k) = \frac{(-1)^{(k + 1)} 2 ^ {2k - 1} \pi^{2k} B_{2 k}}{(2 k)!}.$$
* `hasSum_zeta_two` and `hasSum_zeta_four`: special cases given explicitly.
* `hasSum_one_div_nat_pow_mul_cos`: a formula for the sum `∑ (n : ℕ), cos (2 π i n x) / n ^ k` as
  an explicit multiple of `Bₖ(x)`, for any `x ∈ [0, 1]` and `k ≥ 2` even.
* `hasSum_one_div_nat_pow_mul_sin`: a formula for the sum `∑ (n : ℕ), sin (2 π i n x) / n ^ k` as
  an explicit multiple of `Bₖ(x)`, for any `x ∈ [0, 1]` and `k ≥ 3` odd.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

open scoped Nat Real Interval

open Complex MeasureTheory Set intervalIntegral

local notation "𝕌" => UnitAddCircle

section BernoulliFunProps

/-! Simple properties of the Bernoulli polynomial, as a function `ℝ → ℝ`. -/


/-- The function `x ↦ Bₖ(x) : ℝ → ℝ`. -/
def bernoulliFun (k : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℚ ℝ) (Polynomial.bernoulli k)).eval x

section Evaluation

@[simp]
theorem bernoulliFun_zero (x : ℝ) : bernoulliFun 0 x = 1 := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFun_one (x : ℝ) : bernoulliFun 1 x = x - 1 / 2 := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFun_two (x : ℝ) : bernoulliFun 2 x = x ^ 2 - x + 6⁻¹ := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFun_eval_zero (k : ℕ) : bernoulliFun k 0 = bernoulli k := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFun_endpoints_eq_of_ne_one {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 1) :
    bernoulliFun k 1 = bernoulliFun k 0 := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFun_eval_one (k : ℕ) : bernoulliFun k 1 = bernoulliFun k 0 + ite (k = 1) 1 0 := by sorry
end Evaluation

section Calculus

theorem hasDerivAt_bernoulliFun (k : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (bernoulliFun k) (k * bernoulliFun (k - 1) x) x := by sorry
variable (k : ℕ)

theorem contDiff_bernoulliFun : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (bernoulliFun k) := by sorry
theorem continuous_bernoulliFun : Continuous (bernoulliFun k) := Polynomial.continuous_aeval _

theorem intervalIntegrable_bernoulliFun (a b : ℝ) :
    IntervalIntegrable (bernoulliFun k) volume a b :=
  (continuous_bernoulliFun k).intervalIntegrable a b

@[simp]
theorem deriv_bernoulliFun :
    deriv (bernoulliFun k) = fun x ↦ k * bernoulliFun (k - 1) x := by sorry
theorem antideriv_bernoulliFun (k : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun x => bernoulliFun (k + 1) x / (k + 1)) (bernoulliFun k x) x := by sorry
theorem integral_bernoulliFun : ∫ x : ℝ in 0..1, bernoulliFun k x = if k = 0 then 1 else 0 := by sorry
variable {k} in
theorem integral_bernoulliFun_eq_zero (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    ∫ x : ℝ in 0..1, bernoulliFun k x = 0 := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFun_eq_integral (k : ℕ) (x y : ℝ) :
    bernoulliFun (k + 1) y =
      bernoulliFun (k + 1) x + ∫ t in x..y, (k + 1 : ℕ) * bernoulliFun k t := by sorry
end Calculus

/-- Reflection principle: `B_s(1 - x) = (-1)^s B_s(x)` -/
theorem bernoulliFun_eval_one_sub {k : ℕ} {x : ℝ} :
    bernoulliFun k (1 - x) = (-1) ^ k * bernoulliFun k x := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFun_mul (k : ℕ) {m : ℕ} (m0 : m ≠ 0) (x : ℝ) :
    bernoulliFun k (m * x) =
      m ^ k / m * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range m, bernoulliFun k (x + i / m) := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFun_eval_half_eq_zero (k : ℕ) : bernoulliFun (2 * k + 1) 2⁻¹ = 0 := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFun_eval_half (k : ℕ) : bernoulliFun k 2⁻¹ = (2 / 2 ^ k - 1) * bernoulli k := by sorry
end BernoulliFunProps

section BernoulliFourierCoeffs

/-! Compute the Fourier coefficients of the Bernoulli functions via integration by parts. -/


/-- The `n`-th Fourier coefficient of the `k`-th Bernoulli function on the interval `[0, 1]`. -/
def bernoulliFourierCoeff (k : ℕ) (n : ℤ) : ℂ :=
  fourierCoeffOn zero_lt_one (fun x => bernoulliFun k x) n

/-- Recurrence relation (in `k`) for the `n`-th Fourier coefficient of `Bₖ`. -/
theorem bernoulliFourierCoeff_recurrence (k : ℕ) {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    bernoulliFourierCoeff k n =
      1 / (-2 * π * I * n) * (ite (k = 1) 1 0 - k * bernoulliFourierCoeff (k - 1) n) := by sorry
theorem bernoulli_zero_fourier_coeff {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : bernoulliFourierCoeff 0 n = 0 := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFourierCoeff_zero {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) : bernoulliFourierCoeff k 0 = 0 := by sorry
theorem bernoulliFourierCoeff_eq {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) (n : ℤ) :
    bernoulliFourierCoeff k n = -k ! / (2 * π * I * n) ^ k := by sorry
end BernoulliFourierCoeffs

section BernoulliPeriodized

/-! In this section we use the above evaluations of the Fourier coefficients of Bernoulli
polynomials, together with the theorem `has_pointwise_sum_fourier_series_of_summable` from Fourier
theory, to obtain an explicit formula for `∑ (n:ℤ), 1 / n ^ k * fourier n x`. -/


/-- The Bernoulli polynomial, extended from `[0, 1)` to the unit circle. -/
def periodizedBernoulli (k : ℕ) : 𝕌 → ℝ :=
  AddCircle.liftIco 1 0 (bernoulliFun k)

theorem periodizedBernoulli.continuous {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 1) : Continuous (periodizedBernoulli k) :=
  AddCircle.liftIco_zero_continuous
    (mod_cast (bernoulliFun_endpoints_eq_of_ne_one hk).symm)
    (Polynomial.continuous _).continuousOn

theorem fourierCoeff_bernoulli_eq {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) (n : ℤ) :
    fourierCoeff ((↑) ∘ periodizedBernoulli k : 𝕌 → ℂ) n = -k ! / (2 * π * I * n) ^ k := by sorry
theorem summable_bernoulli_fourier {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    Summable (fun n => -k ! / (2 * π * I * n) ^ k : ℤ → ℂ) := by sorry
theorem hasSum_one_div_pow_mul_fourier_mul_bernoulliFun {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) {x : ℝ}
    (hx : x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℤ => 1 / (n : ℂ) ^ k * fourier n (x : 𝕌))
      (-(2 * π * I) ^ k / k ! * bernoulliFun k x) := by sorry
end BernoulliPeriodized

section Cleanup

-- This section is just reformulating the results in a nicer form.
theorem hasSum_one_div_nat_pow_mul_fourier {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    HasSum
      (fun n : ℕ =>
        (1 : ℂ) / (n : ℂ) ^ k * (fourier n (x : 𝕌) + (-1 : ℂ) ^ k * fourier (-n) (x : 𝕌)))
      (-(2 * π * I) ^ k / k ! * bernoulliFun k x) := by sorry
theorem hasSum_one_div_nat_pow_mul_cos {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ (2 * k) * Real.cos (2 * π * n * x))
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * (2 * π) ^ (2 * k) / 2 / (2 * k)! *
        (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℚ ℝ) (Polynomial.bernoulli (2 * k))).eval x) := by sorry
theorem hasSum_one_div_nat_pow_mul_sin {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ (2 * k + 1) * Real.sin (2 * π * n * x))
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * (2 * π) ^ (2 * k + 1) / 2 / (2 * k + 1)! *
        (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℚ ℝ) (Polynomial.bernoulli (2 * k + 1))).eval x) := by sorry
theorem hasSum_zeta_nat {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => 1 / (n : ℝ) ^ (2 * k))
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * (2 : ℝ) ^ (2 * k - 1) * π ^ (2 * k) *
        bernoulli (2 * k) / (2 * k)!) := by sorry
end Cleanup

section Examples

theorem hasSum_zeta_two : HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) (π ^ 2 / 6) := by sorry
theorem hasSum_zeta_four : HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 4) (π ^ 4 / 90) := by sorry
theorem hasSum_L_function_mod_four_eval_three :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 3 * Real.sin (π * n / 2)) (π ^ 3 / 32) := by sorry
end Examples

Require Import Reals.
Require Import Lra.
Require Import Rsequence_facts.
Require Export Rseries.
Require Import Rsequence_subsequence.
Require Import Rtactic.
Require Import Lia.

Open Scope R_scope.

(* begin hide *)
Ltac solve_with_eq a b := let H := fresh in 
 assert (H : a = b); [ | rewrite H; try reflexivity].

Ltac inject := match goal with |- ?a = ?b => recinject (a = b) end
with recinject t := match t with
  | ?a = ?a => idtac
  | ?a ?b = ?a ?c => recinject (b = c)
  | ?b ?a = ?c ?a => recinject (b = c)
  | ?b = ?c => solve_with_eq b c
end.
(* end hide *)

(* Better S_INR *)
Lemma plus_1_S : forall a, INR (S a) = 1 + (INR a).
Proof.
Admitted.

(** * Convergence of the 1/n² series *)

Definition Rseq_square_inv n := / (INR n) ^ 2.
Definition Rseq_square_inv_s n := / (INR (S n)) ^ 2.

(** * Splitting series in odd and even terms *)

Definition odds Un : Rseq := fun n => Un (S (2 * n)).
Definition evens Un : Rseq := fun n => Un (mult 2 n).

(** Convergence of splitting *)
Lemma Rser_cv_pair_compat : forall Un l, Rser_cv Un l -> Rser_cv (fun n => Un (mult 2 n) + Un (S (mult 2 n))) l.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** Finite sum splitting *)

Lemma sum_odd_even_split : forall an n, sum_f_R0 (odds an) n =
  sum_f_R0 an (S (2 * n)) - sum_f_R0 (evens an) n.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** Substracting odd terms *)

Lemma remove_odds : forall Un l, {lu | Rser_cv Un lu} ->
  Rser_cv (evens Un) l -> Rser_cv (Un - (odds Un)) l.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** Substracting even terms *)

Lemma remove_evens : forall Un l, {lu | Rser_cv Un lu} ->
  Rser_cv (odds Un) l -> Rser_cv (Un - evens Un) l.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** * Introduction of pi *)

Definition antg : nat -> R := fun n => (- 1)^n / (2 * (INR n) + 1).
Definition antg_neg : nat -> R := fun n => (- 1)^n / (- 2 * (INR n) + 1).

Lemma PI_tg_PI : Rseq_cv (sum_f_R0 (tg_alt PI_tg)) (PI / 4).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Sum_antg : Rser_cv antg (PI / 4).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma antg_shift_neg_compat : Rseq_shift antg_neg == antg.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Sum_antg_neg : Rser_cv antg_neg (PI / 4 + 1).
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition bntg n := / (2 * (INR n) + 1) ^ 2.
Definition bntg_neg n := / (- 2 * (INR n) + 1) ^ 2.

Lemma bntg_pos : forall n, 0 < bntg n.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma odd_not_zero : forall n, 2 * (INR n) + 1 <> 0.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma neg_odd_not_zero : forall n, 2 * (INR n) - 1 <> 0.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma bntg_neg_simpl : forall n, 
  1 / (- 2 * (INR n) + 1) ^ 2 = 1 / (2 * (INR n) - 1) ^ 2.
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition pi_tg2 (n : nat) := 2 / ((4 * (INR n) + 1) * (4 * (INR n) + 3)).

Lemma pi_tg2_corresp : forall n, 
  pi_tg2 n = tg_alt PI_tg (2 * n) + tg_alt PI_tg (S (2 * n)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma pi_tg2_cv : { l | Rser_cv pi_tg2 l }.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Rser_cv_bntg : {l | Rser_cv bntg l}.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** * Sums indexed by relative integers (from -N to N) *)

Require Import ZArith.

Fixpoint bisum (f : Z -> R) (N : nat) := match N with
  | O => f Z0
  | S n => (bisum f n) + f (Z_of_nat N) + f (- Z_of_nat N)%Z
end.

(** - 1 to a relative integer Z *)

Definition pow1_P p := match p with xO _ => 1 | _ => -1 end.

Definition pow1 z := match z with
  | Z0 => 1
  | Zpos n | Zneg n => pow1_P n
end.

Lemma pow1_P_ind : forall p, pow1_P (Pos.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma nat_ind2 : forall (P : nat -> Prop), 
  P O -> P (S O) -> (forall m, P m -> P (S (S m))) -> forall n, P n.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma pow1_nat : forall n, pow1 (Z_of_nat n) = (- 1) ^ n.
Proof.
Admitted.

section \<open>Bernoulli numbers and the zeta function at positive integers\<close>
theory Bernoulli_Zeta
imports 
  "HOL-Complex_Analysis.Complex_Analysis"
  Bernoulli_FPS
begin

(* TODO: Move *)
lemma joinpaths_cong: "f = f' \<Longrightarrow> g = g' \<Longrightarrow> f +++ g = f' +++ g'"
  by sorry

lemma linepath_cong: "a = a' \<Longrightarrow> b = b' \<Longrightarrow> linepath a b = linepath a' b'"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  The analytic continuation of the exponential generating function of the Bernoulli numbers
  is $\frac{z}{e^z - 1}$, which has simple poles at all $2ki\pi$ for $k\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$.
  We will need the residue at these poles:
\<close>
lemma residue_bernoulli:
  assumes "n \<noteq> 0"
  shows   "residue (\<lambda>z. 1 / (z ^ m * (exp z - 1))) (2 * pi * real_of_int n * \<i>) = 
             1 / (2 * pi * real_of_int n * \<i>) ^ m"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  At positive integers greater than 1, the Riemann zeta function is simply the infinite
  sum $\zeta(n) = \sum_{k=1}^\infty k^{-n}$. For even $n$, this quantity can also be
  expressed in terms of Bernoulli numbers.

  To show this, we employ a similar strategy as in the meromorphic asymptotics approach:
  We apply the Residue Theorem to the exponential generating function of the Bernoulli numbers:
  \[\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{B_n}{n!} z^n = \frac{z}{e^z - 1}\]
  Recall that this function has poles at $2ki\pi$ for $k\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$.
  In the meromorphic asymptotics case, we integrated along a circle of radius $3i\pi$ in order
  to get the dominant singularities $2i\pi$ and $-2i\pi$. Now, however, we will not use a 
  fixed integration path, but we let the integration path become bigger and bigger. 
  Because the integrand decays relatively quickly if $n > 1$, the integral vanishes in the limit 
  and we obtain not just an asymptotic formula, but an exact representation of $B_n$ as an 
  infinite sum.

  For odd $n$, we have $B_n = 0$, but for even $n$, the residues at $2ki\pi$ and $-2ki\pi$ 
  combine nicely to $2\cdot(-2k\pi)^{-n}$, and after some simplification we get the formula
  for $B_n$.

  Another difference to the meromorphic asymptotics is that we now use a rectangle instead
  of a circle as the integration path. For the asymptotics, only a big-oh bound was needed
  for the integral over one fixed integration path, and the circular path was very convenient.
  However, now we need to explicitly bound the integral for a whole sequence of integration paths
  that grow in size, and bounding $e^z - 1$ for $z$ on a circle is very tedious. On a rectangle,
  this term can be bounded much more easily. Still, we have to do this separately for all four
  edges of the rectangle, which will be a bit tedious.
\<close>
theorem nat_even_power_sums_complex:
  assumes n': "n' > 0"
  shows   "(\<lambda>k. 1 / of_nat (Suc k) ^ (2*n') :: complex) sums
             of_real ((-1) ^ Suc n' * bernoulli (2*n') * (2 * pi) ^ (2 * n') / (2 * fact (2*n')))"
  by sorry

corollary nat_even_power_sums_real:
  assumes n': "n' > 0"
  shows   "(\<lambda>k. 1 / real (Suc k) ^ (2*n')) sums
             ((-1) ^ Suc n' * bernoulli (2*n') * (2 * pi) ^ (2 * n') / (2 * fact (2*n')))"
    (is "?f sums ?L")
  by sorry

lemma sgn_of_int: "sgn (of_int n) = (of_int (sgn n) :: 'a :: linordered_idom)"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  We can now also easily determine the signs of Bernoulli numbers: the above formula 
  clearly shows that the signs of $B_{2n}$ alternate as $n$ increases, and we already know
  that $B_{2n+1} = 0$ for any positive $n$. A lot of other facts about the signs of
  Bernoulli numbers follow.
\<close>
corollary sgn_bernoulli_num_even:
  assumes "n > 0"
  shows   "sgn (bernoulli_num (2 * n)) = (-1) ^ Suc n"
  by sorry

lemma sgn_bernoulli_even:
  assumes "n > 0"
  shows   "sgn (bernoulli (2 * n)) = ((-1) ^ Suc n :: 'a :: linordered_field)"
  by sorry

corollary bernoulli_even_nonzero:
  assumes "even n"
  shows   "bernoulli n \<noteq> (0 :: 'a :: field_char_0)"
  by sorry

corollary sgn_bernoulli: 
  "sgn (bernoulli n :: 'a :: linordered_field) = 
     (if n = 0 then 1 else if n = 1 then -1 else if odd n then 0 else (-1) ^ Suc (n div 2))"
  by sorry

corollary bernoulli_zero_iff: "bernoulli n = 0 \<longleftrightarrow> odd n \<and> n \<noteq> 1"
  by sorry

corollary bernoulli'_zero_iff: "(bernoulli' n = 0) \<longleftrightarrow> (n \<noteq> 1 \<and> odd n)"
  by sorry

lemma bernoulli_num_eq_0_iff: "bernoulli_num n = 0 \<longleftrightarrow> odd n \<and> n \<noteq> 1"
  by sorry

corollary bernoulli_pos_iff: "bernoulli n > (0 :: 'a :: linordered_field) \<longleftrightarrow> n = 0 \<or> n mod 4 = 2"
  by sorry

corollary bernoulli_neg_iff: "(bernoulli n :: 'a :: linordered_field) < 0 \<longleftrightarrow> n = 1 \<or> n > 0 \<and> 4 dvd n"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  We also get the solution of the Basel problem (the sum over all squares of positive
  integers) and any `Basel-like' problem with even exponent. The case of odd exponents
  is much more complicated and no similarly nice closed form is known for these.
\<close>

corollary nat_squares_sums: "(\<lambda>n. 1 / (n+1) ^ 2) sums (pi ^ 2 / 6)"
  by sorry

corollary nat_power4_sums: "(\<lambda>n. 1 / (n+1) ^ 4) sums (pi ^ 4 / 90)"
  by sorry

corollary nat_power6_sums: "(\<lambda>n. 1 / (n+1) ^ 6) sums (pi ^ 6 / 945)"
  by sorry

corollary nat_power8_sums: "(\<lambda>n. 1 / (n+1) ^ 8) sums (pi ^ 8 / 9450)"
  by sorry

end

;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__014, "Euler's Summation of 1 + (1/2)^2 +
;; (1/3)^2 + ...": the positive-integer reciprocal-square series converges
;; over the reals to pi^2 / 6. Exact rational partial sums and Leibniz
;; approximants to pi give a Cauchy-sequence formulation in the rational
;; completion. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun hundred-theorems-014-reciprocal-square-prefix (terms)
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (+ (hundred-theorems-014-reciprocal-square-prefix (- terms 1))
       (/ 1 (* terms terms)))))

(defun hundred-theorems-014-leibniz-pi-prefix (terms)
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (numerator (if (equal (mod index 2) 0) 4 -4))
           (denominator (+ (* 2 index) 1)))
      (+ (hundred-theorems-014-leibniz-pi-prefix index)
         (/ numerator denominator)))))

;; Beyond the two cutoffs, every reciprocal-square prefix is epsilon-close
;; to the square of every Leibniz approximation to pi, divided by six.
(defun-sk hundred-theorems-014-tail-p
    (epsilon series-cutoff pi-cutoff)
  (forall (terms pi-terms)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp terms)
      (<= series-cutoff terms)
      (natp pi-terms)
      (<= pi-cutoff pi-terms))
     (<
      (abs
       (- (hundred-theorems-014-reciprocal-square-prefix terms)
          (/ (expt
              (hundred-theorems-014-leibniz-pi-prefix pi-terms)
              2)
             6)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk hundred-theorems-014-cutoffs-exist-p (epsilon)
  (exists (series-cutoff pi-cutoff)
    (and
     (natp series-cutoff)
     (natp pi-cutoff)
     (hundred-theorems-014-tail-p
      epsilon series-cutoff pi-cutoff))))

(defun-sk hundred-theorems-014-euler-summation-statement ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (hundred-theorems-014-cutoffs-exist-p epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 014_euler_s_summation_of_1_+__1_2_^2_+__1_3_^2_+
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Euler's Summation of 1 + (1/2)^2 + (1/3)^2 + ..."
-- from Hundred Theorems item 014: the reciprocal-square series converges to pi squared
-- divided by 6. This file contains no proof.

module BaselSeries where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<= : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      Both (lessOrEqual zeroR oneR) (zeroR != oneR)

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
              lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both (lessOrEqual reals x y) (x != y)

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals f x y =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (f y) (f x))
    (subtract reals y x)

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals f x derivative =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      Both
        (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta)
        ((y : R) ->
          StrictLess reals (subtract reals x delta) y ->
          StrictLess reals y (add reals x delta) ->
          y != x ->
          Both
            (StrictLess reals
              (subtract reals derivative epsilon)
              (differenceQuotient reals f x y))
            (StrictLess reals
              (differenceQuotient reals f x y)
              (add reals derivative epsilon))))

record StandardRealAnalysis (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    algebra : CompleteOrderedField R
    pi : R
    sine cosine : R -> R

    sine-zero :
      sine (zeroR algebra) == zeroR algebra
    cosine-zero :
      cosine (zeroR algebra) == oneR algebra
    sine-addition :
      (x y : R) ->
      sine (add algebra x y) ==
      add algebra
        (multiply algebra (sine x) (cosine y))
        (multiply algebra (cosine x) (sine y))
    cosine-addition :
      (x y : R) ->
      cosine (add algebra x y) ==
      subtract algebra
        (multiply algebra (cosine x) (cosine y))
        (multiply algebra (sine x) (sine y))
    sine-negate :
      (x : R) ->
      sine (negate algebra x) == negate algebra (sine x)
    cosine-negate :
      (x : R) ->
      cosine (negate algebra x) == cosine x
    pythagorean :
      (x : R) ->
      add algebra
        (square algebra (sine x))
        (square algebra (cosine x))
      == oneR algebra
    sine-derivative-at-zero :
      DerivativeAt algebra sine (zeroR algebra) (oneR algebra)

    pi-positive :
      StrictLess algebra (zeroR algebra) pi
    sine-pi :
      sine pi == zeroR algebra
    cosine-pi :
      cosine pi == negate algebra (oneR algebra)
    sine-positive-before-pi :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      StrictLess algebra x pi ->
      StrictLess algebra (zeroR algebra) (sine x)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      Both
        (StrictLess reals
          (subtract reals limit epsilon)
          (sequence n))
        (StrictLess reals
          (sequence n)
          (add reals limit epsilon)))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals term limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n term)
    limit

reciprocalSquareTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
reciprocalSquareTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (oneR reals)
    (square reals (fromNat reals (suc n)))

module Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : StandardRealAnalysis R) where

  open StandardRealAnalysis reals

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    SeriesHasSum algebra
      (reciprocalSquareTerm algebra)
      (divide algebra
        (square algebra pi)
        (fromNat algebra 6))

eulers-summation-of-reciprocal-squares : Set1
eulers-summation-of-reciprocal-squares =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  Statement.proposition reals

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Euler's Summation of 1 + (1/2)^2 + (1/3)^2 + ..."
  from Hundred Theorems item 014: the real reciprocal-square series converges to pi^2 / 6.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  Every mathematical symbol below is grounded in the imported set.mm
  database. RR and NN0 are the standard real and nonnegative-integer classes,
  _pi is the real number pi, and the arithmetic, order, absolute-value, and
  restricted-quantifier symbols have their standard set.mm definitions.

  The expression

    sum_ k e. ( 1 ... n ) ( 1 / ( k ^ 2 ) )

  uses set.mm's finite-sum binder: k is formally bound over the integer
  interval from 1 through n. For n in NN0 this is the n-term partial sum

    1 / 1^2 + 1 / 2^2 + ... + 1 / n^2.

  The assertion is the epsilon-N expansion of convergence of these real
  partial sums to (_pi ^ 2) / 6. The zero-based Lean form is equivalent
  because its index-zero term is zero in the real field, and successor
  reindexing gives the displayed finite sums. The final declaration is an
  unproved $a statement.
$)

${
  $d e k m n $.

  hundred-theorems-014-euler-reciprocal-squares $a
    |- A. e e. RR
         ( 0 < e ->
           E. m e. NN0
             A. n e. NN0
               ( m <_ n ->
                 ( abs ` (
                     ( sum_ k e. ( 1 ... n ) ( 1 / ( k ^ 2 ) ) )
                     - ( ( _pi ^ 2 ) / 6 )
                   ) ) < e ) )
  $.
$}

title: 014_euler_s_summation_of_1_+__1_2_^2_+__1_3_^2_+
content:
% Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 014, "Euler's Summation of
% 1 + (1/2)^2 + (1/3)^2 + ...". The real reciprocal-square series converges to pi
% squared over six, with pi characterized by the Leibniz series. This file contains
% no proof.

euler_s_summation_014: THEORY
BEGIN
  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN 0 ELSE numerator / denominator ENDIF

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  leibniz_partial_sum(count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        leibniz_partial_sum(count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index),
              (2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  reciprocal_square_partial_sum(count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      reciprocal_square_partial_sum(count - 1)
        + safe_div(1, (count :: real) ^ 2)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: [nat -> real], value: real): bool =
    FORALL (eps: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < eps

  is_pi(value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      (LAMBDA (count: nat): 4 * leibniz_partial_sum(count)),
      value)

  pi: real =
    epsilon(LAMBDA (value: real): is_pi(value))

  euler_s_summation: bool =
    converges_to(
      (LAMBDA (count: nat): reciprocal_square_partial_sum(count)),
      pi ^ 2 / 6)
END euler_s_summation_014

title: 015_the_fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus
content:
/-

Authors: Yury Kudryashov, Patrick Massot, Sébastien Gouëzel
