lemma rsum_bound:
  assumes p: "p tagged_division_of (cbox a b)"
      and "\<forall>x\<in>cbox a b. norm (f x) \<le> e"
    shows "norm (\<Sum>(x, k)\<in>p. content k *\<^sub>R f x) \<le> e * content (cbox a b)"
  by sorry

lemma rsum_diff_bound:
  assumes "p tagged_division_of (cbox a b)"
    and "\<forall>x\<in>cbox a b. norm (f x - g x) \<le> e"
  shows "norm (sum (\<lambda>(x,k). content k *\<^sub>R f x) p - sum (\<lambda>(x,k). content k *\<^sub>R g x) p) \<le>
         e * content (cbox a b)"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_bound:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::real_normed_vector"
  assumes "0 \<le> B"
      and f: "(f has_integral i) (cbox a b)"
      and "\<And>x. x\<in>cbox a b \<Longrightarrow> norm (f x) \<le> B"
    shows "norm i \<le> B * content (cbox a b)"
  by sorry

corollary integrable_bound:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::real_normed_vector"
  assumes "0 \<le> B"
    and "f integrable_on (cbox a b)"
    and "\<And>x. x\<in>cbox a b \<Longrightarrow> norm (f x) \<le> B"
  shows "norm (integral (cbox a b) f) \<le> B * content (cbox a b)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Similar theorems about relationship among components\<close>

lemma rsum_component_le:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes p: "p tagged_division_of (cbox a b)"
      and "\<And>x. x \<in> cbox a b \<Longrightarrow> (f x)\<bullet>i \<le> (g x)\<bullet>i"
    shows "(\<Sum>(x, K)\<in>p. content K *\<^sub>R f x) \<bullet> i \<le> (\<Sum>(x, K)\<in>p. content K *\<^sub>R g x) \<bullet> i"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_component_le:
  fixes f g :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes k: "k \<in> Basis"
  assumes "(f has_integral i) S" "(g has_integral j) S"
    and f_le_g: "\<And>x. x \<in> S \<Longrightarrow> (f x)\<bullet>k \<le> (g x)\<bullet>k"
  shows "i\<bullet>k \<le> j\<bullet>k"
  by sorry

lemma integral_component_le:
  fixes g f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes "k \<in> Basis"
    and "f integrable_on S" "g integrable_on S"
    and "\<And>x. x \<in> S \<Longrightarrow> (f x)\<bullet>k \<le> (g x)\<bullet>k"
  shows "(integral S f)\<bullet>k \<le> (integral S g)\<bullet>k"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_component_nonneg:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes "k \<in> Basis"
    and "(f has_integral i) S"
    and "\<And>x. x \<in> S \<Longrightarrow> 0 \<le> (f x)\<bullet>k"
  shows "0 \<le> i\<bullet>k"
  by sorry

lemma integral_component_nonneg:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes "k \<in> Basis"
    and  "\<And>x. x \<in> S \<Longrightarrow> 0 \<le> (f x)\<bullet>k"
  shows "0 \<le> (integral S f)\<bullet>k"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_component_neg:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes "k \<in> Basis"
    and "(f has_integral i) S"
    and "\<And>x. x \<in> S \<Longrightarrow> (f x)\<bullet>k \<le> 0"
  shows "i\<bullet>k \<le> 0"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_component_lbound:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes "(f has_integral i) (cbox a b)"
    and "\<forall>x\<in>cbox a b. B \<le> f(x)\<bullet>k"
    and "k \<in> Basis"
  shows "B * content (cbox a b) \<le> i\<bullet>k"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_component_ubound:
  fixes f::"'a::euclidean_space => 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes "(f has_integral i) (cbox a b)"
    and "\<forall>x\<in>cbox a b. f x\<bullet>k \<le> B"
    and "k \<in> Basis"
  shows "i\<bullet>k \<le> B * content (cbox a b)"
  by sorry

lemma integral_component_lbound:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes "f integrable_on cbox a b"
    and "\<forall>x\<in>cbox a b. B \<le> f(x)\<bullet>k"
    and "k \<in> Basis"
  shows "B * content (cbox a b) \<le> (integral(cbox a b) f)\<bullet>k"
  by sorry

lemma integral_component_lbound_real:
  assumes "f integrable_on {a ::real..b}"
    and "\<forall>x\<in>{a..b}. B \<le> f(x)\<bullet>k"
    and "k \<in> Basis"
  shows "B * content {a..b} \<le> (integral {a..b} f)\<bullet>k"
  by sorry

lemma integral_component_ubound:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::euclidean_space"
  assumes "f integrable_on cbox a b"
    and "\<forall>x\<in>cbox a b. f x\<bullet>k \<le> B"
    and "k \<in> Basis"
  shows "(integral (cbox a b) f)\<bullet>k \<le> B * content (cbox a b)"
  by sorry

lemma integral_component_ubound_real:
  fixes f :: "real \<Rightarrow> 'a::euclidean_space"
  assumes "f integrable_on {a..b}"
    and "\<forall>x\<in>{a..b}. f x\<bullet>k \<le> B"
    and "k \<in> Basis"
  shows "(integral {a..b} f)\<bullet>k \<le> B * content {a..b}"
  by sorry

subsection \<open>Uniform limit of integrable functions is integrable\<close>

lemma real_arch_invD:
  "0 < (e::real) \<Longrightarrow> (\<exists>n::nat. n \<noteq> 0 \<and> 0 < inverse (real n) \<and> inverse (real n) < e)"
  by sorry


lemma integrable_uniform_limit:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::banach"
  assumes "\<And>e. e > 0 \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>g. (\<forall>x\<in>cbox a b. norm (f x - g x) \<le> e) \<and> g integrable_on cbox a b"
  shows "f integrable_on cbox a b"
  by sorry

lemmas integrable_uniform_limit_real = integrable_uniform_limit [where 'a=real, simplified]


subsection \<open>Negligible sets\<close>

definition "negligible (s:: 'a::euclidean_space set) \<longleftrightarrow>
  (\<forall>a b. ((indicator s :: 'a\<Rightarrow>real) has_integral 0) (cbox a b))"


subsubsection \<open>Negligibility of hyperplane\<close>

lemma content_doublesplit:
  fixes a :: "'a::euclidean_space"
  assumes "0 < e"
    and k: "k \<in> Basis"
  obtains d where "0 < d" and "content (cbox a b \<inter> {x. \<bar>x\<bullet>k - c\<bar> \<le> d}) < e"
  by sorry


proposition negligible_standard_hyperplane[intro]:
  fixes k :: "'a::euclidean_space"
  assumes k: "k \<in> Basis"
  shows "negligible {x. x\<bullet>k = c}"
  by sorry

corollary negligible_standard_hyperplane_cart:
  fixes k :: "'a::finite"
  shows "negligible {x. x$k = (0::real)}"
  by sorry


subsubsection \<open>Hence the main theorem about negligible sets\<close>


lemma has_integral_negligible_cbox:
  fixes f :: "'b::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'a::real_normed_vector"
  assumes negs: "negligible S"
    and 0: "\<And>x. x \<notin> S \<Longrightarrow> f x = 0"
  shows "(f has_integral 0) (cbox a b)"
  by sorry


proposition has_integral_negligible:
  fixes f :: "'b::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'a::real_normed_vector"
  assumes negs: "negligible S"
    and "\<And>x. x \<in> (T - S) \<Longrightarrow> f x = 0"
  shows "(f has_integral 0) T"
  by sorry

lemma
  assumes "negligible S"
  shows integrable_negligible: "f integrable_on S" and integral_negligible: "integral S f = 0"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_spike:
  fixes f :: "'b::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'a::real_normed_vector"
  assumes "negligible S"
    and gf: "\<And>x. x \<in> T - S \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
    and fint: "(f has_integral y) T"
  shows "(g has_integral y) T"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_spike_eq:
  assumes "negligible S" and "\<And>x. x \<in> T - S \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
  shows "(f has_integral y) T \<longleftrightarrow> (g has_integral y) T"
  by sorry

lemma integrable_spike:
  assumes "f integrable_on T" "negligible S" "\<And>x. x \<in> T - S \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
    shows "g integrable_on T"
  by sorry

lemma integral_spike:
  assumes "negligible S" and "\<And>x. x \<in> T - S \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
  shows "integral T f = integral T g"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Some other trivialities about negligible sets\<close>

lemma negligible_subset:
  assumes "negligible S" "T \<subseteq> S"
  shows "negligible T"
  by sorry

lemma negligible_diff[intro?]:
  assumes "negligible S"
  shows "negligible (S - T)"
  by sorry

lemma negligible_Int:
  assumes "negligible S \<or> negligible T"
  shows "negligible (S \<inter> T)"
  by sorry

lemma negligible_Un:
  assumes "negligible S" and T: "negligible T"
  shows "negligible (S \<union> T)"
  by sorry

lemma negligible_Un_eq[simp]: "negligible (S \<union> T) \<longleftrightarrow> negligible S \<and> negligible T"
  by sorry

lemma negligible_sing[intro]: "negligible {a::'a::euclidean_space}"
  by sorry

lemma negligible_insert[simp]: "negligible (insert a S) \<longleftrightarrow> negligible S"
  by sorry

lemma negligible_empty[iff]: "negligible {}"
  by sorry

text\<open>Useful in this form for backchaining\<close>
lemma empty_imp_negligible: "S = {} \<Longrightarrow> negligible S"
  by sorry

lemma negligible_finite[intro]:
  assumes "finite S"
  shows "negligible S"
  by sorry

lemma negligible_Union[intro]:
  assumes "finite \<T>"
    and "\<And>T. T \<in> \<T> \<Longrightarrow> negligible T"
  shows "negligible(\<Union>\<T>)"
  by sorry

lemma negligible: "negligible S \<longleftrightarrow> (\<forall>T. (indicat_real S has_integral 0) T)"
  by sorry

subsection \<open>Finite case of the spike theorem is quite commonly needed\<close>

lemma has_integral_spike_finite:
  assumes "finite S"
    and "\<And>x. x \<in> T - S \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
    and "(f has_integral y) T"
  shows "(g has_integral y) T"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_spike_finite_eq:
  assumes "finite S"
    and "\<And>x. x \<in> T - S \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
  shows "((f has_integral y) T \<longleftrightarrow> (g has_integral y) T)"
  by sorry

lemma integrable_spike_finite:
  assumes "finite S"
    and "\<And>x. x \<in> T - S \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
    and "f integrable_on T"
  shows "g integrable_on T"
  by sorry

lemma integrable_spike_finite_eq:
  assumes "finite S"
    and "\<And>x. x \<in> T - S \<Longrightarrow> f x = g x"
  shows "f integrable_on T \<longleftrightarrow> g integrable_on T"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_bound_spike_finite:
  fixes f :: "'a::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'b::real_normed_vector"
  assumes "0 \<le> B" "finite S"
      and f: "(f has_integral i) (cbox a b)"
      and leB: "\<And>x. x \<in> cbox a b - S \<Longrightarrow> norm (f x) \<le> B"
    shows "norm i \<le> B * content (cbox a b)"
  by sorry

corollary has_integral_bound_real:
  fixes f :: "real \<Rightarrow> 'b::real_normed_vector"
  assumes "0 \<le> B" "finite S"
      and "(f has_integral i) {a..b}"
      and "\<And>x. x \<in> {a..b} - S \<Longrightarrow> norm (f x) \<le> B"
    shows "norm i \<le> B * content {a..b}"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>In particular, the boundary of an interval is negligible\<close>

lemma negligible_frontier_interval: "negligible(cbox a b - box a b)"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_spike_interior:
  assumes f: "(f has_integral y) (cbox a b)" and gf: "\<And>x. x \<in> box a b \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
  shows "(g has_integral y) (cbox a b)"
  by sorry
  
lemma has_integral_spike_interior_eq:
  assumes "\<And>x. x \<in> box a b \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
  shows "(f has_integral y) (cbox a b) \<longleftrightarrow> (g has_integral y) (cbox a b)"
  by sorry

lemma integrable_spike_interior:
  assumes "\<And>x. x \<in> box a b \<Longrightarrow> g x = f x"
    and "f integrable_on cbox a b"
  shows "g integrable_on cbox a b"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Integrability of continuous functions\<close>

lemma operative_approximableI:
  fixes f :: "'b::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'a::banach"
  assumes "0 \<le> e"
  shows "operative conj True (\<lambda>i. \<exists>g. (\<forall>x\<in>i. norm (f x - g (x::'b)) \<le> e) \<and> g integrable_on i)"
  by sorry

lemma comm_monoid_set_F_and: "comm_monoid_set.F (\<and>) True f s \<longleftrightarrow> (finite s \<longrightarrow> (\<forall>x\<in>s. f x))"
  by sorry

lemma approximable_on_division:
  fixes f :: "'b::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'a::banach"
  assumes "0 \<le> e"
    and d: "d division_of (cbox a b)"
    and f: "\<forall>i\<in>d. \<exists>g. (\<forall>x\<in>i. norm (f x - g x) \<le> e) \<and> g integrable_on i"
  obtains g where "\<forall>x\<in>cbox a b. norm (f x - g x) \<le> e" "g integrable_on cbox a b"
  by sorry

lemma integrable_continuous:
  fixes f :: "'b::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'a::banach"
  assumes "continuous_on (cbox a b) f"
  shows "f integrable_on cbox a b"
  by sorry

lemma integrable_continuous_interval:
  fixes f :: "'b::ordered_euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'a::banach"
  assumes "continuous_on {a..b} f"
  shows "f integrable_on {a..b}"
  by sorry

lemmas integrable_continuous_real = integrable_continuous_interval[where 'b=real]

lemma integrable_continuous_closed_segment:
  fixes f :: "real \<Rightarrow> 'a::banach"
  assumes "continuous_on (closed_segment a b) f"
  shows "f integrable_on (closed_segment a b)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Specialization of additivity to one dimension\<close>


subsection \<open>A useful lemma allowing us to factor out the content size\<close>

lemma has_integral_factor_content:
  "(f has_integral i) (cbox a b) \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>e>0. \<exists>d. gauge d \<and> (\<forall>p. p tagged_division_of (cbox a b) \<and> d fine p \<longrightarrow>
      norm (sum (\<lambda>(x,k). content k *\<^sub>R f x) p - i) \<le> e * content (cbox a b)))"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_factor_content_real:
  "(f has_integral i) {a..b::real} \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>e>0. \<exists>d. gauge d \<and> (\<forall>p. p tagged_division_of {a..b}  \<and> d fine p \<longrightarrow>
      norm (sum (\<lambda>(x,k). content k *\<^sub>R f x) p - i) \<le> e * content {a..b} ))"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Fundamental theorem of calculus\<close>

lemma interval_bounds_real:
  fixes q b :: real
  assumes "a \<le> b"
  shows "Sup {a..b} = b"
    and "Inf {a..b} = a"
  by sorry

theorem fundamental_theorem_of_calculus:
  fixes f :: "real \<Rightarrow> 'a::banach"
  assumes "a \<le> b" 
      and vecd: "\<And>x. x \<in> {a..b} \<Longrightarrow> (f has_vector_derivative f' x) (at x within {a..b})"
  shows "(f' has_integral (f b - f a)) {a..b}"
  by sorry

lemma has_complex_derivative_imp_has_vector_derivative:
  fixes f :: "complex \<Rightarrow> complex"
  assumes "(f has_field_derivative f') (at (of_real a) within (cbox (of_real x) (of_real y)))"
  shows "((f o of_real) has_vector_derivative f') (at a within {x..y})"
  by sorry

lemma ident_has_integral:
  fixes a::real
  assumes "a \<le> b"
  shows "((\<lambda>x. x) has_integral (b\<^sup>2 - a\<^sup>2)/2) {a..b}"
  by sorry

lemma integral_ident [simp]:
  fixes a::real
  assumes "a \<le> b"
  shows "integral {a..b} (\<lambda>x. x) = (if a \<le> b then (b\<^sup>2 - a\<^sup>2)/2 else 0)"
  by sorry

lemma ident_integrable_on:
  fixes a::real
  shows "(\<lambda>x. x) integrable_on {a..b}"
  by sorry

lemma integral_sin [simp]:
  fixes a::real
  assumes "a \<le> b" shows "integral {a..b} sin = cos a - cos b"
  by sorry

lemma integral_cos [simp]:
  fixes a::real
  assumes "a \<le> b" shows "integral {a..b} cos = sin b - sin a"
  by sorry

lemma integral_exp [simp]:
  fixes a::real
  assumes "a \<le> b" shows "integral {a..b} exp = exp b - exp a"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_sin_nx: "((\<lambda>x. sin(real_of_int n * x)) has_integral 0) {-pi..pi}"
  by sorry

lemma integral_sin_nx:
   "integral {-pi..pi} (\<lambda>x. sin(x * real_of_int n)) = 0"
  by sorry

lemma has_integral_cos_nx:
  "((\<lambda>x. cos(real_of_int n * x)) has_integral (if n = 0 then 2 * pi else 0)) {-pi..pi}"
  by sorry

lemma integral_cos_nx:
   "integral {-pi..pi} (\<lambda>x. cos(x * real_of_int n)) = (if n = 0 then 2 * pi else 0)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Taylor series expansion\<close>

lemma mvt_integral:
  fixes f::"'a::real_normed_vector\<Rightarrow>'b::banach"
  assumes f'[derivative_intros]:
    "\<And>x. x \<in> S \<Longrightarrow> (f has_derivative f' x) (at x within S)"
  assumes line_in: "\<And>t. t \<in> {0..1} \<Longrightarrow> x + t *\<^sub>R y \<in> S"
  shows "f (x + y) - f x = integral {0..1} (\<lambda>t. f' (x + t *\<^sub>R y) y)"
  by sorry

lemma (in bounded_bilinear) sum_prod_derivatives_has_vector_derivative:
  assumes "p>0"
  and f0: "Df 0 = f"
  and Df: "\<And>m t. m < p \<Longrightarrow> a \<le> t \<Longrightarrow> t \<le> b \<Longrightarrow>
    (Df m has_vector_derivative Df (Suc m) t) (at t within {a..b})"
  and g0: "Dg 0 = g"
  and Dg: "\<And>m t. m < p \<Longrightarrow> a \<le> t \<Longrightarrow> t \<le> b \<Longrightarrow>
    (Dg m has_vector_derivative Dg (Suc m) t) (at t within {a..b})"
  and ivl: "a \<le> t" "t \<le> b"
  shows "((\<lambda>t. \<Sum>i<p. (-1)^i *\<^sub>R prod (Df i t) (Dg (p - Suc i) t))
    has_vector_derivative
      prod (f t) (Dg p t) - (-1)^p *\<^sub>R prod (Df p t) (g t))
    (at t within {a..b})"
  by sorry

lemma
  fixes f::"real\<Rightarrow>'a::banach"
  assumes "p>0"
  and f0: "Df 0 = f"
  and Df: "\<And>m t. m < p \<Longrightarrow> a \<le> t \<Longrightarrow> t \<le> b \<Longrightarrow>
    (Df m has_vector_derivative Df (Suc m) t) (at t within {a..b})"
  and ivl: "a \<le> b"
  defines "i \<equiv> \<lambda>x. ((b - x) ^ (p - 1) / fact (p - 1)) *\<^sub>R Df p x"
  shows Taylor_has_integral:
    "(i has_integral f b - (\<Sum>i<p. ((b-a) ^ i / fact i) *\<^sub>R Df i a)) {a..b}"
  and Taylor_integral:
    "f b = (\<Sum>i<p. ((b-a) ^ i / fact i) *\<^sub>R Df i a) + integral {a..b} i"
  and Taylor_integrable:
    "i integrable_on {a..b}"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Only need trivial subintervals if the interval itself is trivial\<close>

proposition division_of_nontrivial:
  fixes \<D> :: "'a::euclidean_space set set"
  assumes sdiv: "\<D> division_of (cbox a b)"
     and cont0: "content (cbox a b) \<noteq> 0"
  shows "{k. k \<in> \<D> \<and> content k \<noteq> 0} division_of (cbox a b)"
  by sorry

subsection \<open>Integrability on subintervals\<close>

lemma operative_integrableI:
  fixes f :: "'b::euclidean_space \<Rightarrow> 'a::banach"
  assumes "0 \<le> e"
  shows "operative conj True (\<lambda>i. f integrable_on i)"
  by sorry

title: 015_the_fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus
015_the_fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems corpus artifact 015,
;; "The Fundamental Theorem of Integral Calculus": on a closed real interval,
;; an interval-relative derivative integrates to the difference of endpoint
;; values. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Real values, real functions, gauges, and sets are arbitrary ACL2 objects
;; interpreted by fixed-arity conservative interfaces. Mathematical
;; quantifiers are formula-specific DEFUN-SK binders; no finite function
;; table or generic function evaluator is used.

(defstub ftc15-real-p (r-type value) t)
(defstub ftc15-zero (r-type) t)
(defstub ftc15-one (r-type) t)
(defstub ftc15-add (r-type left right) t)
(defstub ftc15-mul (r-type left right) t)
(defstub ftc15-neg (r-type value) t)
(defstub ftc15-inv (r-type value) t)
(defstub ftc15-lt (r-type left right) t)

(defstub ftc15-function-value (r-type function argument) t)
(defstub ftc15-set-member-p (r-type set value) t)

(defun ftc15-sub (r-type x y)
  (ftc15-add r-type x (ftc15-neg r-type y)))

(defun ftc15-le (r-type x y)
  (not (ftc15-lt r-type y x)))

(defun ftc15-abs (r-type x)
  (if (ftc15-lt r-type x (ftc15-zero r-type))
      (ftc15-neg r-type x)
    x))

(defun ftc15-in-closed-interval-p (r-type a b x)
  (and (ftc15-real-p r-type x)
       (ftc15-le r-type a x)
       (ftc15-le r-type x b)))

;; A complete ordered-field presentation of the real carrier.

(defun-sk ftc15-operation-closure-p (r-type)
  (forall (x y)
    (and
     (ftc15-real-p r-type (ftc15-zero r-type))
     (ftc15-real-p r-type (ftc15-one r-type))
     (implies
      (ftc15-real-p r-type x)
      (and
       (ftc15-real-p r-type (ftc15-neg r-type x))
       (ftc15-real-p r-type (ftc15-inv r-type x))))
     (implies
      (and (ftc15-real-p r-type x)
           (ftc15-real-p r-type y))
      (and
       (ftc15-real-p r-type (ftc15-add r-type x y))
       (ftc15-real-p r-type (ftc15-mul r-type x y)))))))

(defun-sk ftc15-unary-field-laws-p (r-type)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (ftc15-real-p r-type x)
     (let ((zero (ftc15-zero r-type))
           (one (ftc15-one r-type)))
       (and
        (equal (ftc15-add r-type zero x) x)
        (equal (ftc15-add r-type x zero) x)
        (equal (ftc15-add r-type x (ftc15-neg r-type x)) zero)
        (equal (ftc15-add r-type (ftc15-neg r-type x) x) zero)
        (equal (ftc15-mul r-type one x) x)
        (equal (ftc15-mul r-type x one) x)
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (and
          (equal (ftc15-mul r-type x (ftc15-inv r-type x)) one)
          (equal (ftc15-mul r-type (ftc15-inv r-type x) x) one))))))))

(defun-sk ftc15-binary-field-laws-p (r-type)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and (ftc15-real-p r-type x)
          (ftc15-real-p r-type y))
     (and
      (equal (ftc15-add r-type x y)
             (ftc15-add r-type y x))
      (equal (ftc15-mul r-type x y)
             (ftc15-mul r-type y x))))))

(defun-sk ftc15-ternary-field-laws-p (r-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and (ftc15-real-p r-type x)
          (ftc15-real-p r-type y)
          (ftc15-real-p r-type z))
     (and
      (equal
       (ftc15-add r-type (ftc15-add r-type x y) z)
       (ftc15-add r-type x (ftc15-add r-type y z)))
      (equal
       (ftc15-mul r-type (ftc15-mul r-type x y) z)
       (ftc15-mul r-type x (ftc15-mul r-type y z)))
      (equal
       (ftc15-mul r-type x (ftc15-add r-type y z))
       (ftc15-add r-type
                  (ftc15-mul r-type x y)
                  (ftc15-mul r-type x z)))))))

(defun-sk ftc15-order-laws-p (r-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and (ftc15-real-p r-type x)
          (ftc15-real-p r-type y)
          (ftc15-real-p r-type z))
     (and
      (not (ftc15-lt r-type x x))
      (implies
       (and (ftc15-lt r-type x y)
            (ftc15-lt r-type y z))
       (ftc15-lt r-type x z))
      (or (ftc15-lt r-type x y)
          (equal x y)
          (ftc15-lt r-type y x))
      (implies
       (ftc15-lt r-type x y)
       (ftc15-lt r-type
                 (ftc15-add r-type x z)
                 (ftc15-add r-type y z)))
      (implies
       (and (ftc15-lt r-type (ftc15-zero r-type) x)
            (ftc15-lt r-type (ftc15-zero r-type) y))
       (ftc15-lt r-type
                 (ftc15-zero r-type)
                 (ftc15-mul r-type x y)))))))

(defun-sk ftc15-valid-real-set-p (r-type set)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (ftc15-set-member-p r-type set x)
     (ftc15-real-p r-type x))))

(defun-sk ftc15-set-nonempty-p (r-type set)
  (exists (x)
    (and (ftc15-real-p r-type x)
         (ftc15-set-member-p r-type set x))))

(defun-sk ftc15-upper-bound-p (r-type set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (ftc15-set-member-p r-type set x)
     (ftc15-le r-type x bound))))

(defun-sk ftc15-set-bounded-above-p (r-type set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and (ftc15-real-p r-type bound)
         (ftc15-upper-bound-p r-type set bound))))

(defun-sk ftc15-least-upper-bound-p (r-type set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (and
     (ftc15-real-p r-type supremum)
     (ftc15-upper-bound-p r-type set supremum)
     (implies
      (and (ftc15-real-p r-type bound)
           (ftc15-upper-bound-p r-type set bound))
      (ftc15-le r-type supremum bound)))))

(defun-sk ftc15-supremum-exists-p (r-type set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (and (ftc15-real-p r-type supremum)
         (ftc15-least-upper-bound-p r-type set supremum))))

(defun-sk ftc15-dedekind-complete-p (r-type)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and (ftc15-valid-real-set-p r-type set)
          (ftc15-set-nonempty-p r-type set)
          (ftc15-set-bounded-above-p r-type set))
     (ftc15-supremum-exists-p r-type set))))

(defun ftc15-real-structure-p (r-type)
  (and
   (ftc15-operation-closure-p r-type)
   (ftc15-unary-field-laws-p r-type)
   (ftc15-binary-field-laws-p r-type)
   (ftc15-ternary-field-laws-p r-type)
   (ftc15-order-laws-p r-type)
   (not (equal (ftc15-zero r-type) (ftc15-one r-type)))
   (ftc15-lt r-type (ftc15-zero r-type) (ftc15-one r-type))
   (ftc15-dedekind-complete-p r-type)))

;; Arbitrary real-valued functions are total on the real carrier.

(defun-sk ftc15-real-function-p (r-type function)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (ftc15-real-p r-type x)
     (ftc15-real-p
      r-type
      (ftc15-function-value r-type function x)))))

;; The derivative is relative to [a,b], matching the one-sided endpoint
;; interpretation in the source statements. The residual formulation
;; |f(y)-f(x)-d(y-x)| <= epsilon |y-x| also covers y = x directly.

(defun-sk ftc15-derivative-neighborhood-p
    (r-type function derivative a b x epsilon radius)
  (forall (y)
    (implies
     (and
      (ftc15-in-closed-interval-p r-type a b y)
      (ftc15-lt
       r-type
       (ftc15-abs r-type (ftc15-sub r-type y x))
       radius))
     (ftc15-le
      r-type
      (ftc15-abs
       r-type
       (ftc15-sub
        r-type
        (ftc15-sub
         r-type
         (ftc15-function-value r-type function y)
         (ftc15-function-value r-type function x))
        (ftc15-mul
         r-type
         derivative
         (ftc15-sub r-type y x))))
      (ftc15-mul
       r-type
       epsilon
       (ftc15-abs r-type (ftc15-sub r-type y x)))))))

(defun-sk ftc15-derivative-radius-exists-p
    (r-type function derivative a b x epsilon)
  (exists (radius)
    (and
     (ftc15-real-p r-type radius)
     (ftc15-lt r-type (ftc15-zero r-type) radius)
     (ftc15-derivative-neighborhood-p
      r-type function derivative a b x epsilon radius))))

(defun-sk ftc15-has-derivative-within-p
    (r-type function derivative a b x)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (ftc15-real-p r-type epsilon)
      (ftc15-lt r-type (ftc15-zero r-type) epsilon))
     (ftc15-derivative-radius-exists-p
      r-type function derivative a b x epsilon))))

(defun-sk ftc15-derivative-on-closed-interval-p
    (r-type function derivative-function a b)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (ftc15-in-closed-interval-p r-type a b x)
     (ftc15-has-derivative-within-p
      r-type
      function
      (ftc15-function-value r-type derivative-function x)
      a b x))))

;; A tagged division is an intrinsically finite list of triples
;; (tag left-endpoint right-endpoint), ordered from a to b.

(defun ftc15-tagged-piece-p (r-type piece)
  (and
   (true-listp piece)
   (equal (len piece) 3)
   (ftc15-real-p r-type (nth 0 piece))
   (ftc15-real-p r-type (nth 1 piece))
   (ftc15-real-p r-type (nth 2 piece))
   (ftc15-lt r-type (nth 1 piece) (nth 2 piece))
   (ftc15-le r-type (nth 1 piece) (nth 0 piece))
   (ftc15-le r-type (nth 0 piece) (nth 2 piece))))

(defun ftc15-tagged-division-tail-p (r-type division next-left b)
  (if (endp division)
      (equal next-left b)
    (let ((piece (car division)))
      (and
       (ftc15-tagged-piece-p r-type piece)
       (equal (nth 1 piece) next-left)
       (ftc15-tagged-division-tail-p
        r-type
        (cdr division)
        (nth 2 piece)
        b)))))

(defun ftc15-tagged-division-p (r-type a b division)
  (and
   (true-listp division)
   (ftc15-real-p r-type a)
   (ftc15-real-p r-type b)
   (ftc15-le r-type a b)
   (ftc15-tagged-division-tail-p r-type division a b)))

(defun ftc15-riemann-sum (r-type function division)
  (if (endp division)
      (ftc15-zero r-type)
    (let* ((piece (car division))
           (tag (nth 0 piece))
           (left (nth 1 piece))
           (right (nth 2 piece)))
      (ftc15-add
       r-type
       (ftc15-mul
        r-type
        (ftc15-function-value r-type function tag)
        (ftc15-sub r-type right left))
       (ftc15-riemann-sum r-type function (cdr division))))))

;; A positive gauge is an arbitrary positive real-valued function on [a,b].

(defun-sk ftc15-positive-gauge-p (r-type gauge a b)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (ftc15-in-closed-interval-p r-type a b x)
     (ftc15-lt
      r-type
      (ftc15-zero r-type)
      (ftc15-function-value r-type gauge x)))))

(defun ftc15-fine-tagged-division-p (r-type gauge division)
  (if (endp division)
      t
    (let* ((piece (car division))
           (tag (nth 0 piece))
           (left (nth 1 piece))
           (right (nth 2 piece))
           (gauge-at-tag
            (ftc15-function-value r-type gauge tag)))
      (and
       (ftc15-lt
        r-type
        (ftc15-sub r-type tag left)
        gauge-at-tag)
       (ftc15-lt
        r-type
        (ftc15-sub r-type right tag)
        gauge-at-tag)
       (ftc15-fine-tagged-division-p
        r-type gauge (cdr division))))))

(defun-sk ftc15-fine-tagged-division-exists-p
    (r-type gauge a b)
  (exists (division)
    (and
     (ftc15-tagged-division-p r-type a b division)
     (ftc15-fine-tagged-division-p r-type gauge division))))

(defun-sk ftc15-all-fine-sums-close-p
    (r-type function integral gauge a b epsilon)
  (forall (division)
    (implies
     (and
      (ftc15-tagged-division-p r-type a b division)
      (ftc15-fine-tagged-division-p r-type gauge division))
     (ftc15-lt
      r-type
      (ftc15-abs
       r-type
       (ftc15-sub
        r-type
        (ftc15-riemann-sum r-type function division)
        integral))
      epsilon))))

;; Fine-division existence is included with each gauge witness. Over the
;; complete real interval this is the usual Cousin property, and it makes the
;; universal condition on fine divisions explicitly non-vacuous.

(defun-sk ftc15-integral-gauge-exists-p
    (r-type function integral a b epsilon)
  (exists (gauge)
    (and
     (ftc15-real-function-p r-type gauge)
     (ftc15-positive-gauge-p r-type gauge a b)
     (ftc15-fine-tagged-division-exists-p r-type gauge a b)
     (ftc15-all-fine-sums-close-p
      r-type function integral gauge a b epsilon))))

(defun-sk ftc15-has-gauge-integral-p
    (r-type function integral a b)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (ftc15-real-p r-type epsilon)
      (ftc15-lt r-type (ftc15-zero r-type) epsilon))
     (ftc15-integral-gauge-exists-p
      r-type function integral a b epsilon))))

(defun-sk hundred-theorems-acl2-015-statement ()
  (forall (r-type antiderivative derivative-function a b)
    (implies
     (and
      (ftc15-real-structure-p r-type)
      (ftc15-real-p r-type a)
      (ftc15-real-p r-type b)
      (ftc15-le r-type a b)
      (ftc15-real-function-p r-type antiderivative)
      (ftc15-real-function-p r-type derivative-function)
      (ftc15-derivative-on-closed-interval-p
       r-type antiderivative derivative-function a b))
     (ftc15-has-gauge-integral-p
      r-type
      derivative-function
      (ftc15-sub
       r-type
       (ftc15-function-value r-type antiderivative b)
       (ftc15-function-value r-type antiderivative a))
      a b))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)

:q

title: 015_the_fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "The Fundamental Theorem of Integral Calculus" from Hundred
-- Theorems item 015. This file contains no proof.

module FundamentalTheoremOfIntegralCalculus where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<succ : {n : Nat} -> zero <N suc n
  succ<succ : {m n : Nat} -> m <N n -> suc m <N suc n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      Both (lessOrEqual zeroR oneR) (zeroR != oneR)

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
              lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both (lessOrEqual reals x y) (x != y)

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  Both
    (StrictLess reals (subtract reals center radius) x)
    (StrictLess reals x (add reals center radius))

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals f x y =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (f y) (f x))
    (subtract reals y x)

DerivativeWithin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeWithin {R} reals f a b x derivative =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      Both
        (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta)
        ((y : R) ->
          lessOrEqual reals a y ->
          lessOrEqual reals y b ->
          CloseTo reals x delta y ->
          y != x ->
          CloseTo reals derivative epsilon
            (differenceQuotient reals f x y)))

record TaggedDivision
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (a b : R) : Set where
  field
    count : Nat
    point : Nat -> R
    tag : Nat -> R

    starts-at :
      point zero == a
    ends-at :
      point count == b
    increasing :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <N count ->
      StrictLess reals (point i) (point (suc i))
    tag-above-left-endpoint :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <N count ->
      lessOrEqual reals (point i) (tag i)
    tag-below-right-endpoint :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <N count ->
      lessOrEqual reals (tag i) (point (suc i))

open TaggedDivision

riemannSumUpTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (f : R -> R) ->
  {a b : R} ->
  TaggedDivision reals a b ->
  Nat ->
  R
riemannSumUpTo reals f division zero =
  zeroR reals
riemannSumUpTo reals f division (suc n) =
  add reals
    (riemannSumUpTo reals f division n)
    (multiply reals
      (f (tag division n))
      (subtract reals
        (point division (suc n))
        (point division n)))

riemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (f : R -> R) ->
  {a b : R} ->
  TaggedDivision reals a b ->
  R
riemannSum reals f division =
  riemannSumUpTo reals f division (count division)

PositiveGaugeOn :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
PositiveGaugeOn {R} reals a b gauge =
  (x : R) ->
  lessOrEqual reals a x ->
  lessOrEqual reals x b ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (gauge x)

Fine :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (gauge : R -> R) ->
  {a b : R} ->
  TaggedDivision reals a b ->
  Set
Fine reals gauge division =
  (i : Nat) ->
  i <N count division ->
  Both
    (StrictLess reals
      (subtract reals
        (tag division i)
        (gauge (tag division i)))
      (point division i))
    (StrictLess reals
      (point division (suc i))
      (add reals
        (tag division i)
        (gauge (tag division i))))

HasGaugeIntegral :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
HasGaugeIntegral {R} reals f a b integral =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists (R -> R)
    (\ gauge ->
      Both
        (PositiveGaugeOn reals a b gauge)
        ((division : TaggedDivision reals a b) ->
          Fine reals gauge division ->
          CloseTo reals integral epsilon
            (riemannSum reals f division)))

the-fundamental-theorem-of-integral-calculus : Set1
the-fundamental-theorem-of-integral-calculus =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (f derivative : R -> R) ->
  (a b : R) ->
  lessOrEqual reals a b ->
  ((x : R) ->
    lessOrEqual reals a x ->
    lessOrEqual reals x b ->
    DerivativeWithin reals f a b x (derivative x)) ->
  HasGaugeIntegral reals derivative a b
    (subtract reals (f b) (f a))

title: 015_the_fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "The Fundamental Theorem of Integral Calculus" from Hundred
  Theorems item 015. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open integralTheory;

val fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus =
  ``!f f' a b.
      a <= b /\
      (!x. a <= x /\ x <= b ==> (f diffl (f' x)) x)
      ==>
      Dint (a,b) f' (f b - f a)``;

title: 015_the_fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "The Fundamental Theorem of Integral Calculus" from Hundred
  Theorems item 015. It states the scalar real endpoint-difference theorem for
  a derivative and the Henstock-Kurzweil integral on a closed interval. This
  file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  F and G are total real functions. The restricted universal says that G(x)
  is a derivative of F at x within the closed interval [A,B], including the
  one-sided endpoint interpretation supplied by the interval subspace.

  HT015HKInt is defined by the gauge criterion. For every positive error
  tolerance there is a positive gauge on [A,B] such that every subordinate
  finite tagged partition has its Riemann sum within that tolerance of the
  asserted value. Thus the predicate includes both gauge integrability and
  the value of the integral, without an absolute-integrability assumption.
$)

$c HT015HKInt $.

ht015-hkint-syntax $a wff ( HT015HKInt F A B C ) $.

${
  $d e d n p t k A $.
  $d e d n p t k B $.
  $d e d n p t k C $.
  $d e d n p t k F $.

  ht015-hkint-definition $a |- (
    ( HT015HKInt F A B C )
    <->
    A. e e. RR
      (
        0 < e
        ->

title: 015_the_fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "The Fundamental Theorem of Integral Calculus" from Hundred
% Theorems item 015. This file contains no proof.

the_fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus_015: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  in_closed_interval(x, a, b: real): bool =
    a <= x AND x <= b

  has_derivative_within(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, x, a, b: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon: real):
      epsilon > 0 IMPLIES
        EXISTS (delta: real):
          delta > 0
            AND (FORALL (y: real):
              (in_closed_interval(y, a, b)
                AND NOT (y = x)
                AND abs(y - x) < delta)
              IMPLIES
                abs(
                  f(y) - f(x)
                    - derivative * (y - x))
                  < epsilon * abs(y - x))

  tagged_partition(
      a, b: real,
      count: nat,
      points, tags: real_sequence): bool =
    points(0) = a
      AND points(count) = b
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1)))

  positive_gauge(gauge: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real): 0 < gauge(x)

  gauge_fine(
      gauge: real_function,
      count: nat,
      points, tags: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        (tags(index) - gauge(tags(index)) < points(index)
          AND points(index + 1)
            < tags(index) + gauge(tags(index)))

  tagged_sum(
      f: real_function,
      count: nat,
      points, tags: real_sequence): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      tagged_sum(f, count - 1, points, tags)
        + f(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_integral_on_closed_interval(
      f: real_function,
      integral_value, a, b: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon: real):
      epsilon > 0 IMPLIES
        EXISTS (gauge: real_function):
          positive_gauge(gauge)
            AND (FORALL
                (count: nat),
                (points, tags: real_sequence):
              (tagged_partition(
                  a, b, count, points, tags)
                AND gauge_fine(
                  gauge, count, points, tags))
              IMPLIES
                abs(
                  tagged_sum(
                    f, count, points, tags)
                    - integral_value)
                  < epsilon)

  fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus: bool =
    FORALL
        (antiderivative, derivative: real_function),
        (a, b: real):
      (a <= b
        AND (FORALL (x: real):
          in_closed_interval(x, a, b)
            IMPLIES
              has_derivative_within(
                antiderivative,
                derivative(x),
                x,
                a,
                b)))
      IMPLIES
        has_integral_on_closed_interval(
          derivative,
          antiderivative(b) - antiderivative(a),
          a,
          b)
END the_fundamental_theorem_of_integral_calculus_015

title: 016_insolvability_of_general_higher_degree_equations__abel-ruffi
content:
/-

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LocalExtr.Polynomial
import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Polynomial.Basic
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.AbelRuffini
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Polynomial.Eisenstein.Criterion
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Int.Basic
import Mathlib.RingTheory.RootsOfUnity.Minpoly

/-!
# Construction of an algebraic number that is not solvable by radicals

The main ingredients are:

* `isSolvable_gal_of_irreducible` in `Mathlib/FieldTheory/AbelRuffini.lean`:
  an irreducible polynomial with an `IsSolvableByRad` root has solvable Galois group.
* `galActionHom_bijective_of_prime_degree'` in `Mathlib/FieldTheory/PolynomialGaloisGroup.lean` :
  an irreducible polynomial of prime degree with 1-3 non-real roots has full Galois group.
* `Equiv.Perm.not_solvable` in `Mathlib/GroupTheory/Solvable.lean` : the symmetric group is not
  solvable.

Then all that remains is the construction of a specific polynomial satisfying the conditions of
`galActionHom_bijective_of_prime_degree'`, which is done in this file.
-/

namespace AbelRuffini

open Function Polynomial Polynomial.Gal Ideal

attribute [local instance] splits_ℚ_ℂ

variable (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (a b : ℕ)

/-- A quintic polynomial that we will show is irreducible -/
noncomputable def Φ : R[X] :=
  X ^ 5 - C (a : R) * X + C (b : R)

variable {R}

@[simp]
theorem map_Phi {S : Type*} [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) : (Φ R a b).map f = Φ S a b := by simp [Φ]

@[simp]
theorem coeff_zero_Phi : (Φ R a b).coeff 0 = (b : R) := by simp [Φ, coeff_X_pow]

@[simp]
theorem coeff_five_Phi : (Φ R a b).coeff 5 = 1 := by sorry
variable [Nontrivial R]

theorem degree_Phi : (Φ R a b).degree = ((5 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) := by sorry
theorem natDegree_Phi : (Φ R a b).natDegree = 5 :=
  natDegree_eq_of_degree_eq_some (degree_Phi a b)

theorem leadingCoeff_Phi : (Φ R a b).leadingCoeff = 1 := by sorry
theorem monic_Phi : (Φ R a b).Monic :=
  leadingCoeff_Phi a b

theorem irreducible_Phi (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hpa : p ∣ a) (hpb : p ∣ b) (hp2b : ¬p ^ 2 ∣ b) :
    Irreducible (Φ ℚ a b) := by sorry
theorem real_roots_Phi_le : Fintype.card ((Φ ℚ a b).rootSet ℝ) ≤ 3 := by sorry
theorem real_roots_Phi_ge_aux (hab : b < a) :
    ∃ x y : ℝ, x ≠ y ∧ aeval x (Φ ℚ a b) = 0 ∧ aeval y (Φ ℚ a b) = 0 := by sorry
theorem real_roots_Phi_ge (hab : b < a) : 2 ≤ Fintype.card ((Φ ℚ a b).rootSet ℝ) := by sorry
theorem complex_roots_Phi (h : (Φ ℚ a b).Separable) : Fintype.card ((Φ ℚ a b).rootSet ℂ) = 5 :=
  (card_rootSet_eq_natDegree h (IsAlgClosed.splits _)).trans (natDegree_Phi a b)

theorem gal_Phi (hab : b < a) (h_irred : Irreducible (Φ ℚ a b)) :
    Bijective (galActionHom (Φ ℚ a b) ℂ) := by sorry
theorem not_solvable_by_rad (p : ℕ) (x : ℂ) (hx : aeval x (Φ ℚ a b) = 0) (hab : b < a)
    (hp : p.Prime) (hpa : p ∣ a) (hpb : p ∣ b) (hp2b : ¬p ^ 2 ∣ b) : x ∉ solvableByRad ℚ ℂ := by sorry
theorem not_solvable_by_rad' (x : ℂ) (hx : aeval x (Φ ℚ 4 2) = 0) : x ∉ solvableByRad ℚ ℂ := by sorry
theorem exists_not_solvable_by_rad : ∃ x : ℂ, IsAlgebraic ℚ x ∧ x ∉ solvableByRad ℚ ℂ := by sorry
end AbelRuffini

title: 016_insolvability_of_general_higher_degree_equations__abel-ruffi
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Insolvability of General Higher Degree Equations
  (Abel-Ruffini)" from Hundred Theorems item 016. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory Abel_Ruffini
  imports Complex_Main
begin

datatype radical_expression =
    Rad_Const rat
  | Rad_Neg radical_expression
  | Rad_Inv radical_expression
  | Rad_Add radical_expression radical_expression
  | Rad_Mul radical_expression radical_expression
  | Rad_Pow radical_expression nat
  | Rad_Root nat radical_expression

inductive radical_value :: "radical_expression \<Rightarrow> complex \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  rational: "radical_value (Rad_Const q) (of_rat q)"
| negation: "radical_value e z \<Longrightarrow> radical_value (Rad_Neg e) (-z)"
| inverse: "radical_value e z \<Longrightarrow> radical_value (Rad_Inv e) (inverse z)"
| addition:
    "\<lbrakk>radical_value e1 z1; radical_value e2 z2\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow>
      radical_value (Rad_Add e1 e2) (z1 + z2)"
| multiplication:
    "\<lbrakk>radical_value e1 z1; radical_value e2 z2\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow>
      radical_value (Rad_Mul e1 e2) (z1 * z2)"
| power: "radical_value e z \<Longrightarrow> radical_value (Rad_Pow e n) (z ^ n)"
| root:
    "\<lbrakk>radical_value e z; n > 0; w ^ n = z\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow>
      radical_value (Rad_Root n e) w"

definition solvable_by_radicals :: "complex \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "solvable_by_radicals z \<longleftrightarrow> (\<exists>e. radical_value e z)"

fun eval_rat_polynomial :: "rat list \<Rightarrow> complex \<Rightarrow> complex" where
  "eval_rat_polynomial [] z = 0"
| "eval_rat_polynomial (q # qs) z =
    of_rat q + z * eval_rat_polynomial qs z"

definition algebraic_over_rationals :: "complex \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "algebraic_over_rationals z \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<exists>qs :: rat list.
      (\<exists>q \<in> set qs. q \<noteq> 0) \<and> eval_rat_polynomial qs z = 0)"

theorem quintic_roots_not_solvable_by_radicals:
  fixes z :: complex
  assumes "z ^ 5 - 4 * z + 2 = 0"
  shows "\<not> solvable_by_radicals z"
  sorry

theorem abel_ruffini:
  "\<exists>z :: complex.
    algebraic_over_rationals z \<and> \<not> solvable_by_radicals z"
  sorry

end

title: 016_insolvability_of_general_higher_degree_equations__abel-ruffi
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Insolvability of General Higher Degree Equations
  (Abel-Ruffini)" from Hundred Theorems item 016. This file contains no proof.
*)

needs "Complex/complexnumbers.ml";;

let ABEL_RUFFINI =
 `?z:complex.
      z pow 5 - Cx(&4) * z + Cx(&2) = Cx(&0) /\
      ~(!R:complex->bool.
          ((!n:num. R (Cx(&n))) /\
           (!x:complex. R x ==> R (--x)) /\
           (!x:complex. R x /\ ~(x = Cx(&0)) ==> R (inv x)) /\
           (!x y:complex. R x /\ R y ==> R (x + y)) /\
           (!x y:complex. R x /\ R y ==> R (x * y)) /\
           (!n:num. ~(n = 0) ==>
                    !x y:complex. R x /\ y pow n = x ==> R y))
          ==> R z)`;;

title: 016_insolvability_of_general_higher_degree_equations__abel-ruffi
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 016,
;; "Insolvability of General Higher Degree Equations (Abel-Ruffini)": a root
;; of X^5 - 4X + 2 over the rationals is algebraic but is not obtainable from
;; the rationals by field operations and extraction of positive-degree roots.
;; This file contains no proof.
;;
;; Every field below is an infinite carrier: the rational vectors of a fixed
;; positive finite dimension.  A finite rational multiplication tensor gives
;; the coordinates of its bilinear multiplication; it is not a finite lookup
;; table of field elements.  The predicates explicitly require the tensor to
;; define a commutative associative domain with an identity.  Such a
;; finite-dimensional Q-domain is a field.
;;
;; Any algebraic number and every field appearing in a finite radical tower
;; have finite-dimensional Q-presentations of this form.  Conversely, every
;; valid presentation is a characteristic-zero number field.  The tower
;; predicate requires each successive field to be generated by the preceding
;; field and one element whose positive power lies in the preceding field.
;; Thus existence of an embedding of Q(x) into such a tower is equivalent to
;; x being solvable by radicals.  Since X^5 - 4X + 2 is irreducible, this
;; property is invariant among its conjugate roots, so the abstract
;; finite-dimensional presentation is bidirectionally equivalent to the
;; source statement about a complex root.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Rational coordinate vectors, matrices, and multiplication tensors.

(defun ht016-rational-vector-p (vector dimension)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      (equal vector nil)
    (and
     (consp vector)
     (rationalp (car vector))
     (ht016-rational-vector-p
      (cdr vector) (- dimension 1)))))

(defun ht016-rational-matrix-p
    (matrix rows columns)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix rows)))
  (if (zp rows)
      (equal matrix nil)
    (and
     (consp matrix)
     (ht016-rational-vector-p (car matrix) columns)
     (ht016-rational-matrix-p
      (cdr matrix) (- rows 1) columns))))

(defun ht016-rational-tensor-p
    (tensor dimension)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      (equal tensor nil)
    (and
     (consp tensor)
     (ht016-rational-matrix-p
      (car tensor) dimension dimension)
     (ht016-rational-tensor-p
      (cdr tensor) (- dimension 1)))))

(defun ht016-zero-vector (dimension)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      nil
    (cons 0 (ht016-zero-vector (- dimension 1)))))

(defun ht016-vector-add (left right)
  (if (and (consp left) (consp right))
      (cons
       (+ (car left) (car right))
       (ht016-vector-add (cdr left) (cdr right)))
    nil))

(defun ht016-vector-scale (scalar vector)
  (if (consp vector)
      (cons
       (* scalar (car vector))
       (ht016-vector-scale scalar (cdr vector)))
    nil))

(defun ht016-vector-dot (left right)
  (if (and (consp left) (consp right))
      (+
       (* (car left) (car right))
       (ht016-vector-dot (cdr left) (cdr right)))
    0))

(defun ht016-matrix-apply (matrix vector)
  (if (consp matrix)
      (cons
       (ht016-vector-dot (car matrix) vector)
       (ht016-matrix-apply (cdr matrix) vector))
    nil))

(defun ht016-bilinear-coordinate
    (left right matrix)
  (if (and (consp left) (consp matrix))
      (+
       (*
        (car left)
        (ht016-vector-dot (car matrix) right))
       (ht016-bilinear-coordinate
        (cdr left) right (cdr matrix)))
    0))

(defun ht016-tensor-multiply
    (tensor left right)
  (if (consp tensor)
      (cons
       (ht016-bilinear-coordinate
        left right (car tensor))
       (ht016-tensor-multiply
        (cdr tensor) left right))
    nil))

;; A field code is (dimension, multiplicative identity, multiplication
;; tensor).  Addition and rational scalar multiplication are coordinatewise.

(defun ht016-field-dimension (field)
  (nth 0 field))

(defun ht016-field-one (field)
  (nth 1 field))

(defun ht016-field-tensor (field)
  (nth 2 field))

(defun ht016-field-vector-p (field value)
  (ht016-rational-vector-p
   value (ht016-field-dimension field)))

(defun ht016-field-zero (field)
  (ht016-zero-vector (ht016-field-dimension field)))

(defun ht016-field-add (field left right)
  (declare (ignore field))
  (ht016-vector-add left right))

(defun ht016-field-scale (field scalar value)
  (declare (ignore field))
  (ht016-vector-scale scalar value))

(defun ht016-field-mul (field left right)
  (ht016-tensor-multiply
   (ht016-field-tensor field) left right))

(defun ht016-field-power (field value exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (ht016-field-one field)
    (ht016-field-mul
     field value
     (ht016-field-power field value (- exponent 1)))))

(defun ht016-field-code-p (field)
  (let ((dimension (ht016-field-dimension field)))
    (and
     (true-listp field)
     (equal (len field) 3)
     (natp dimension)
     (< 0 dimension)
     (ht016-rational-vector-p
      (ht016-field-one field) dimension)
     (ht016-rational-tensor-p
      (ht016-field-tensor field) dimension))))

(defun-sk ht016-field-ring-laws-p (field)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht016-field-vector-p field x)
      (ht016-field-vector-p field y)
      (ht016-field-vector-p field z))
     (and
      (equal
       (ht016-field-mul field x y)
       (ht016-field-mul field y x))
      (equal
       (ht016-field-mul
        field (ht016-field-mul field x y) z)
       (ht016-field-mul
        field x (ht016-field-mul field y z)))
      (equal
       (ht016-field-mul
        field (ht016-field-one field) x)
       x)))))

(defun-sk ht016-field-domain-law-p (field)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht016-field-vector-p field x)
      (ht016-field-vector-p field y)
      (equal
       (ht016-field-mul field x y)
       (ht016-field-zero field)))
     (or
      (equal x (ht016-field-zero field))
      (equal y (ht016-field-zero field))))))

(defun ht016-field-p (field)
  (and
   (ht016-field-code-p field)
   (not
    (equal
     (ht016-field-one field)
     (ht016-field-zero field)))
   (ht016-field-ring-laws-p field)
   (ht016-field-domain-law-p field)))

(defun ht016-rational-field ()
  (list 1 (list 1) (list (list (list 1)))))

;; A rational matrix represents a Q-linear map.  Preserving one and
;; multiplication makes it a field homomorphism; the kernel condition makes
;; the embedding explicit.

(defun-sk ht016-field-hom-laws-p
    (source target matrix)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht016-field-vector-p source x)
      (ht016-field-vector-p source y))
     (and
      (equal
       (ht016-matrix-apply
        matrix (ht016-field-mul source x y))
       (ht016-field-mul
        target
        (ht016-matrix-apply matrix x)
        (ht016-matrix-apply matrix y)))
      (implies
       (equal
        (ht016-matrix-apply matrix x)
        (ht016-field-zero target))
       (equal x (ht016-field-zero source)))))))

(defun ht016-field-hom-p
    (source target matrix)
  (and
   (ht016-field-p source)
   (ht016-field-p target)
   (ht016-rational-matrix-p
    matrix
    (ht016-field-dimension target)
    (ht016-field-dimension source))
   (equal
    (ht016-matrix-apply
     matrix (ht016-field-one source))
    (ht016-field-one target))
   (ht016-field-hom-laws-p source target matrix)))

(defun-sk ht016-in-field-hom-image-p
    (source target matrix value)
  (exists (preimage)
    (and
     (ht016-field-vector-p source preimage)
     (equal
      (ht016-matrix-apply matrix preimage)
      value))))

;; Generation of Q(x) and of a simple field extension.  The target dimension
;; is a sufficient uniform bound on the required powers.

(defun ht016-rational-coefficients-p
    (coefficients count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      (equal coefficients nil)
    (and
     (consp coefficients)
     (rationalp (car coefficients))
     (ht016-rational-coefficients-p
      (cdr coefficients) (- count 1)))))

(defun ht016-q-power-sum
    (field element coefficients exponent)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (ht016-field-add
       field
       (ht016-field-scale
        field
        (car coefficients)
        (ht016-field-power field element exponent))
       (ht016-q-power-sum
        field element (cdr coefficients) (+ exponent 1)))
    (ht016-field-zero field)))

(defun-sk ht016-in-q-generated-field-p
    (field element value)
  (exists (coefficients)
    (and
     (ht016-rational-coefficients-p
      coefficients (ht016-field-dimension field))
     (equal
      (ht016-q-power-sum
       field element coefficients 0)
      value))))

(defun-sk ht016-q-generated-field-p
    (field element)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (ht016-field-vector-p field value)
     (ht016-in-q-generated-field-p
      field element value))))

(defun ht016-extension-coefficients-p
    (coefficients source count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      (equal coefficients nil)
    (and
     (consp coefficients)
     (ht016-field-vector-p source (car coefficients))
     (ht016-extension-coefficients-p
      (cdr coefficients) source (- count 1)))))

(defun ht016-extension-power-sum
    (target matrix radical coefficients exponent)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (ht016-field-add
       target
       (ht016-field-mul
        target
        (ht016-matrix-apply matrix (car coefficients))
       (ht016-field-power target radical exponent))
       (ht016-extension-power-sum
        target matrix radical
        (cdr coefficients) (+ exponent 1)))
    (ht016-field-zero target)))

(defun-sk ht016-in-simple-extension-p
    (source target matrix radical value)
  (exists (coefficients)
    (and
     (ht016-extension-coefficients-p
      coefficients source
      (ht016-field-dimension target))
     (equal
      (ht016-extension-power-sum
       target matrix radical coefficients 0)
      value))))

(defun-sk ht016-simple-extension-generated-p
    (source target matrix radical)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (ht016-field-vector-p target value)
     (ht016-in-simple-extension-p
      source target matrix radical value))))

(defun ht016-radical-extension-step-p
    (source target matrix radical degree)
  (and
   (ht016-field-hom-p source target matrix)
   (ht016-field-vector-p target radical)
   (natp degree)
   (< 0 degree)
   (ht016-in-field-hom-image-p
    source target matrix
    (ht016-field-power target radical degree))
   (ht016-simple-extension-generated-p
    source target matrix radical)))

;; A tower begins with the canonical one-dimensional rational field.

(defun ht016-radical-tower-tail-p
    (remaining fields matrices radicals degrees)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (and
       (consp fields)
       (equal (cdr fields) nil)
       (equal matrices nil)
       (equal radicals nil)
       (equal degrees nil))
      (and
       (consp fields)
       (consp (cdr fields))
       (consp matrices)
       (consp radicals)
       (consp degrees)
       (ht016-radical-extension-step-p
        (car fields)
        (cadr fields)
        (car matrices)
        (car radicals)
        (car degrees))
       (ht016-radical-tower-tail-p
        (- remaining 1)
        (cdr fields)
        (cdr matrices)
        (cdr radicals)
        (cdr degrees)))))

(defun ht016-radical-tower-p
    (fields matrices radicals degrees)
  (and
   (consp fields)
   (equal (car fields) (ht016-rational-field))
   (ht016-radical-tower-tail-p
    (- (len fields) 1)
    fields matrices radicals degrees)))

(defun ht016-last-field (fields)
  (if (consp (cdr fields))
      (ht016-last-field (cdr fields))
    (car fields)))

;; The concrete quintic from both formal ground-truth developments.

(defun ht016-quintic-value (field x)
  (ht016-field-add
   field
   (ht016-field-add
    field
    (ht016-field-power field x 5)
    (ht016-field-scale field -4 x))
   (ht016-field-scale
    field 2 (ht016-field-one field))))

(defun ht016-quintic-root-p (field x)
  (and
   (ht016-field-vector-p field x)
   (equal
    (ht016-quintic-value field x)
    (ht016-field-zero field))))

(defun ht016-root-field-p (field x)
  (and
   (ht016-field-p field)
   (ht016-quintic-root-p field x)
   (ht016-q-generated-field-p field x)))

(defun ht016-radical-solvability-witness-p
    (source fields matrices radicals degrees embedding)
  (and
   (ht016-radical-tower-p
    fields matrices radicals degrees)
   (ht016-field-hom-p
    source (ht016-last-field fields) embedding)))

(defun-sk ht016-solvable-by-radicals-p (source x)
  (exists
   (fields matrices radicals degrees embedding)
   (and
    (ht016-root-field-p source x)
    (ht016-radical-solvability-witness-p
     source fields matrices radicals degrees embedding))))

(defun-sk hundred-theorems-016-abel-ruffini-statement ()
  (exists (root-field root)
    (and
     (ht016-root-field-p root-field root)
     (not
      (ht016-solvable-by-radicals-p
       root-field root)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 016_insolvability_of_general_higher_degree_equations__abel-ruffi
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Insolvability of General Higher Degree Equations
-- (Abel-Ruffini)" from Hundred Theorems item 016. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infix 4 _≠_
infixr 3 _∧_

data ⊥ : Set where

¬_ : Set → Set
¬ A = A → ⊥

_≠_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≠ y = ¬ (x ≡ y)

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Field (F : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    zeroF oneF : F
    add multiply : F → F → F
    negate inverse : F → F
    fromNat : Nat → F

    one-not-zero :
      oneF ≠ zeroF

    add-commutative :
      (x y : F) → add x y ≡ add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : F) → add (add x y) z ≡ add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : F) → add x zeroF ≡ x
    add-inverse :
      (x : F) → add x (negate x) ≡ zeroF

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : F) → multiply x y ≡ multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : F) →
      multiply (multiply x y) z ≡ multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : F) → multiply x oneF ≡ x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : F) → multiply x zeroF ≡ zeroF
    distribute :
      (x y z : F) →
      multiply x (add y z) ≡
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroF ≡ zeroF
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : F) →
      x ≠ zeroF →
      multiply x (inverse x) ≡ oneF

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero ≡ zeroF
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) → fromNat (suc n) ≡ add (fromNat n) oneF
    characteristic-zero :
      (m n : Nat) → fromNat m ≡ fromNat n → m ≡ n

power :
  {F : Set} →
  Field F →
  F →
  Nat →
  F
power algebra x zero =
  Field.oneF algebra
power algebra x (suc n) =
  Field.multiply algebra x (power algebra x n)

evaluate :
  {F : Set} →
  Field F →
  List F →
  F →
  F
evaluate algebra [] x =
  Field.zeroF algebra
evaluate algebra (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  Field.add algebra coefficient
    (Field.multiply algebra x (evaluate algebra coefficients x))

data HasNonzeroCoefficient
  {F : Set}
  (algebra : Field F) :
  List F → Set where

  here :
    {coefficient : F} {coefficients : List F} →
    coefficient ≠ Field.zeroF algebra →
    HasNonzeroCoefficient algebra (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

  there :
    {coefficient : F} {coefficients : List F} →
    HasNonzeroCoefficient algebra coefficients →
    HasNonzeroCoefficient algebra (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

Nonconstant :
  {F : Set} →
  Field F →
  List F →
  Set
Nonconstant algebra [] = ⊥
Nonconstant algebra (coefficient ∷ coefficients) =
  HasNonzeroCoefficient algebra coefficients

record ComplexNumberModel (C : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    algebra : Field C

    algebraically-closed :
      (coefficients : List C) →
      Nonconstant algebra coefficients →
      Σ C
        (λ z →
          evaluate algebra coefficients z ≡
          Field.zeroF algebra)

fieldOf :
  {C : Set} →
  ComplexNumberModel C →
  Field C
fieldOf = ComplexNumberModel.algebra

fromInt :
  {F : Set} →
  Field F →
  Int →
  F
fromInt algebra (pos n) =
  Field.fromNat algebra n
fromInt algebra (negsuc n) =
  Field.negate algebra
    (Field.fromNat algebra (suc n))

record Rational : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator            : Int
    denominatorMinusOne : Nat

toField :
  {F : Set} →
  Field F →
  Rational →
  F
toField algebra q =
  Field.multiply algebra
    (fromInt algebra (Rational.numerator q))
    (Field.inverse algebra
      (Field.fromNat algebra
        (suc (Rational.denominatorMinusOne q))))

data HasNonzeroRationalCoefficient :
  List Rational → Set where

  rational-here :
    {coefficient : Rational}
    {coefficients : List Rational} →
    Rational.numerator coefficient ≠ pos zero →
    HasNonzeroRationalCoefficient
      (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

  rational-there :
    {coefficient : Rational}
    {coefficients : List Rational} →
    HasNonzeroRationalCoefficient coefficients →
    HasNonzeroRationalCoefficient
      (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

evaluateRationalPolynomial :
  {C : Set} →
  ComplexNumberModel C →
  List Rational →
  C →
  C
evaluateRationalPolynomial complex [] x =
  Field.zeroF (fieldOf complex)
evaluateRationalPolynomial complex
  (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  Field.add (fieldOf complex)
    (toField (fieldOf complex) coefficient)
    (Field.multiply (fieldOf complex) x
      (evaluateRationalPolynomial complex coefficients x))

IsAlgebraic :
  {C : Set} →
  ComplexNumberModel C →
  C →
  Set
IsAlgebraic complex x =
  Σ (List Rational)
    (λ coefficients →
      HasNonzeroRationalCoefficient coefficients ∧
      evaluateRationalPolynomial complex coefficients x ≡
      Field.zeroF (fieldOf complex))

data RadicalExpression : Set where
  rationalConstant : Rational → RadicalExpression
  negative          : RadicalExpression → RadicalExpression
  reciprocal        : RadicalExpression → RadicalExpression
  sum               : RadicalExpression → RadicalExpression → RadicalExpression
  product           : RadicalExpression → RadicalExpression → RadicalExpression
  radicalRoot       : Nat → RadicalExpression → RadicalExpression

data EvaluatesTo
  {C : Set}
  (complex : ComplexNumberModel C) :
  RadicalExpression →
  C →
  Set where

  rational-value :
    (q : Rational) →
    EvaluatesTo complex
      (rationalConstant q)
      (toField (fieldOf complex) q)

  negative-value :
    {expression : RadicalExpression} {x : C} →
    EvaluatesTo complex expression x →
    EvaluatesTo complex
      (negative expression)
      (Field.negate (fieldOf complex) x)

  reciprocal-value :
    {expression : RadicalExpression} {x : C} →
    EvaluatesTo complex expression x →
    x ≠ Field.zeroF (fieldOf complex) →
    EvaluatesTo complex
      (reciprocal expression)
      (Field.inverse (fieldOf complex) x)

  sum-value :
    {left right : RadicalExpression} {x y : C} →
    EvaluatesTo complex left x →
    EvaluatesTo complex right y →
    EvaluatesTo complex
      (sum left right)
      (Field.add (fieldOf complex) x y)

  product-value :
    {left right : RadicalExpression} {x y : C} →
    EvaluatesTo complex left x →
    EvaluatesTo complex right y →
    EvaluatesTo complex
      (product left right)
      (Field.multiply (fieldOf complex) x y)

  radical-value :
    {degreeMinusOne : Nat}
    {expression : RadicalExpression}
    {radicand root : C} →
    EvaluatesTo complex expression radicand →
    power (fieldOf complex) root (suc degreeMinusOne) ≡ radicand →
    EvaluatesTo complex
      (radicalRoot degreeMinusOne expression)
      root

SolvableByRadicals :
  {C : Set} →
  ComplexNumberModel C →
  C →
  Set
SolvableByRadicals complex x =
  Σ RadicalExpression
    (λ expression → EvaluatesTo complex expression x)

quintic :
  {C : Set} →
  ComplexNumberModel C →
  C →
  C
quintic complex x =
  Field.add algebra
    (Field.add algebra
      (power algebra x 5)
      (Field.negate algebra
        (Field.multiply algebra
          (Field.fromNat algebra 4)
          x)))
    (Field.fromNat algebra 2)
  where
    algebra = fieldOf complex

IsQuinticRoot :
  {C : Set} →
  ComplexNumberModel C →
  C →
  Set
IsQuinticRoot complex x =
  quintic complex x ≡ Field.zeroF (fieldOf complex)

hundred-theorems-016 : Set₁
hundred-theorems-016 =
  (C : Set) →
  (complex : ComplexNumberModel C) →
  Σ C
    (λ x →
      IsQuinticRoot complex x ∧
      IsAlgebraic complex x ∧
      ¬ SolvableByRadicals complex x)

title: 016_insolvability_of_general_higher_degree_equations__abel-ruffi
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Insolvability of General Higher Degree Equations
  (Abel-Ruffini)" from Hundred Theorems item 016. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory complexTheory;

val insolubility_of_general_higher_degree_equations_abel_ruffini =
  ``let obtainable_by_radicals =
      \z : complex.
        !S : complex -> bool.
          (S 0 /\
           S 1 /\
           (!u v : complex.
              S u /\ S v ==> S (u + v) /\ S (u * v)) /\
           (!u : complex.
              S u ==> S (0 - u)) /\
           (!u : complex.
              S u /\ u <> 0 ==> S (1 / u)) /\
           (!n : num. !u v : complex.
              0 < n /\ S u /\ v pow n = u ==> S v))
          ==> S z
    in
      ?x : complex.
        x pow 5 - 4 * x + 2 = 0 /\
        ~obtainable_by_radicals x``;

title: 016_insolvability_of_general_higher_degree_equations__abel-ruffi
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Insolvability of General Higher Degree
  Equations (Abel-Ruffini)" from Hundred Theorems item 016: an algebraic
  complex root of x^5 - 4x + 2 is not obtainable by radicals over the
  rationals. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  HundredRadClosure016 is the intersection of all subsets s of CC that
  contain QQ, are closed under the field operations, and contain every
  complex n-th root of each of their elements for every positive integer n.
  It is therefore the least intermediate field between QQ and CC closed
  under radicals, matching solvableByRad QQ CC in the Lean source and the
  finite radical-tower formulation in the Rocq source.

  The class AA is the set.mm class of complex numbers algebraic over QQ.
  The final assertion gives the explicit quintic witness used by both source
  developments. The declarations are unproved $a statements, following the
  corpus convention for Metamath statement artifacts; there is no $p proof
  statement in this file.
$)

$c HundredRadClosure016 $.

chundredradclosure016 $a class HundredRadClosure016 $.

${
  $d a b n s z $.

  df-hundredradclosure016 $a |- HundredRadClosure016 =
    { z e. CC | A. s
      (
        (
          (
            (
              s C_ CC
              /\
              QQ C_ s
            )
            /\
            A. a e. s A. b e. s
            (
              (
                ( a + b ) e. s
                /\
                ( a - b ) e. s
              )
              /\
              (
                ( a x. b ) e. s
                /\
                ( b =/= 0 -> ( a / b ) e. s )
              )
            )
          )
          /\
          A. a e. CC A. n e. NN
            ( ( a ^ n ) e. s -> a e. s )
        )
        ->
        z e. s
      )
    } $.
$}

hundred-theorems-016-abel-ruffini $a |- E. z e. CC
  (
    z e. AA
    /\
    (
      ( ( ( z ^ 5 ) - ( 4 x. z ) ) + 2 ) = 0
      /\
      z e/ HundredRadClosure016
    )
  ) $.

:: Statement-only formalization of "Insolvability of General Higher Degree Equations
:: (Abel-Ruffini)" from Hundred Theorems item 016. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, SUBSET_1, INT_1,
    RAT_1, RELAT_1, ARYTM_1,
    NEWTON, ARYTM_3, CARD_1, PREPOWER, FUNCT_1, XXREAL_0, NAT_1,

  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, NEWTON, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    COMPLEX1, INT_1, RAT_1, REAL_1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, SEQ_1, SEQ_2,
    COMSEQ_2, SEQM_3, SQUARE_1, SEQ_4, PREPOWER, ABIAN, XXREAL_2,
    POWER;
  constructors REAL_1, SQUARE_1, NAT_1, SEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4, NEWTON,
    PREPOWER, XXREAL_2, RELSET_1, ABIAN, BINOP_2, COMSEQ_2, POWER,
    COMPLEX1;
  registrations XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, SQUARE_1, NAT_1, INT_1, RAT_1, MEMBERED,
    NEWTON, PREPOWER, SEQ_4, ABIAN, ORDINAL1, POWER;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

:: Abel-Ruffini via the explicit quintic X^5 - 4*X + 2.
:: R is the least subfield of COMPLEX closed under extraction of roots.
::$P-
theorem
  ex R being Subset of COMPLEX st
    RAT c= R &
    (for x being Complex st x in R holds -x in R) &
    (for x being Complex st x in R & x <> 0 holds 1/x in R) &
    (for x,y being Complex st x in R & y in R holds x+y in R) &
    (for x,y being Complex st x in R & y in R holds x*y in R) &
    (for x,y being Complex, n being Nat st
      x in R & 0 < n & y |^ n = x holds y in R) &
    (for S being Subset of COMPLEX st
      RAT c= S &
      (for x being Complex st x in S holds -x in S) &
      (for x being Complex st x in S & x <> 0 holds 1/x in S) &
      (for x,y being Complex st x in S & y in S holds x+y in S) &
      (for x,y being Complex st x in S & y in S holds x*y in S) &
      (for x,y being Complex, n being Nat st
        x in S & 0 < n & y |^ n = x holds y in S)
    holds R c= S) &
    (ex z being Complex st
      z |^ 5 - 4*z + 2 = 0 & not z in R)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 016_insolvability_of_general_higher_degree_equations__abel-ruffi
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Insolvability of General Higher Degree Equations
% (Abel-Ruffini)" from Hundred Theorems item 016. This file contains no proof.

hundred_theorems_016: THEORY
BEGIN
  complex: TYPE = [# real_part: real, imag_part: real #]

  complex_zero: complex =
    (# real_part := 0, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_one: complex =
    (# real_part := 1, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_of_real(x: real): complex =
    (# real_part := x, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_neg(x: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := -real_part(x),
       imag_part := -imag_part(x) #)

  complex_add(x, y: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := real_part(x) + real_part(y),
       imag_part := imag_part(x) + imag_part(y) #)

  complex_mul(x, y: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := real_part(x) * real_part(y)
                       - imag_part(x) * imag_part(y),
       imag_part := real_part(x) * imag_part(y)
                       + imag_part(x) * real_part(y) #)

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  complex_inv(x: complex): complex =
    LET denominator: real =
      real_part(x) * real_part(x)
        + imag_part(x) * imag_part(x)
    IN
      (# real_part := safe_div(real_part(x), denominator),
         imag_part := safe_div(-imag_part(x), denominator) #)

  complex_power(x: complex, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      complex_one
    ELSE
      complex_mul(complex_power(x, exponent - 1), x)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  field_closed(s: [complex -> bool]): bool =
    s(complex_zero)
      AND s(complex_one)
      AND (FORALL (x: complex):
        s(x) IMPLIES s(complex_neg(x)))
      AND (FORALL (x, y: complex):
        (s(x) AND s(y)) IMPLIES s(complex_add(x, y)))
      AND (FORALL (x, y: complex):
        (s(x) AND s(y)) IMPLIES s(complex_mul(x, y)))
      AND (FORALL (x: complex):
        (s(x) AND NOT (x = complex_zero))
          IMPLIES s(complex_inv(x)))

  contains_rationals(s: [complex -> bool]): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      rational?(x) IMPLIES s(complex_of_real(x))

  contains_prefix(
      s: [complex -> bool],
      elements: [nat -> complex],
      prefix_length: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i: nat):
      i < prefix_length IMPLIES s(elements(i))

  generated_field(
      elements: [nat -> complex],
      prefix_length: nat,
      x: complex): bool =
    FORALL (s: [complex -> bool]):
      (field_closed(s)
        AND contains_rationals(s)
        AND contains_prefix(s, elements, prefix_length))
      IMPLIES s(x)

  radical_tower(
      elements: [nat -> complex],
      degrees: [nat -> nat],
      length: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i: nat):
      i < length IMPLIES
        (0 < degrees(i)
          AND generated_field(
            elements,
            i,
            complex_power(elements(i), degrees(i))))

  solvable_by_radicals(x: complex): bool =
    EXISTS (length: nat):
      EXISTS (elements: [nat -> complex]):
        EXISTS (degrees: [nat -> nat]):
          radical_tower(elements, degrees, length)
            AND generated_field(elements, length, x)

  polynomial_value(
      coefficients: [nat -> real],
      x: complex,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      complex_zero
    ELSE
      LET k: nat = count - 1 IN
        complex_add(
          polynomial_value(coefficients, x, count - 1),
          complex_mul(
            complex_of_real(coefficients(k)),
            complex_power(x, k)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

    EXISTS (degree: nat):

            i <= degree IMPLIES rational?(coefficients(i)))
          AND NOT (coefficients(degree) = 0)
          AND polynomial_value(coefficients, x, degree + 1)

    complex_add(
      complex_add(
        complex_power(x, 5),
        complex_neg(complex_mul(complex_of_real(4), x))),
      complex_of_real(2))

  insolvability_of_general_higher_degree_equations_abel_ruffini: bool =
    EXISTS (x: complex):
      quintic_value(x) = complex_zero
        AND algebraic_over_rationals(x)
        AND NOT solvable_by_radicals(x)
