content:
; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact 017,
; "De Moivre's Theorem": for every complex z and natural n,
; (cos z + i sin z)^n = cos(nz) + i sin(nz).  The two sides are entire,
; so universal equality on the full complex plane is equivalent to equality
; of every Taylor coefficient.  This file contains the statement and no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun ht017-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n (ht017-factorial (- n 1)))))

(defun ht017-cosine-coefficient (degree)
  (if (and (natp degree)
           (evenp degree))
      (/ (expt -1 (floor degree 2))
         (ht017-factorial degree))
    0))

(defun ht017-sine-coefficient (degree)
  (if (and (natp degree)
           (oddp degree))
      (/ (expt -1 (floor degree 2))
         (ht017-factorial degree))
    0))

(defun ht017-cos-plus-i-sin-coefficient (degree)
  (+ (ht017-cosine-coefficient degree)
     (* #c(0 1) (ht017-sine-coefficient degree))))

; A number below (degree + 1)^power encodes one power-tuple in base
; (degree + 1).  The following two functions compute its total degree and
; the product of the corresponding Taylor coefficients.
(defun ht017-tuple-degree (code positions radix)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix positions)))
  (if (zp positions)
      0
    (+ (mod code radix)
       (ht017-tuple-degree (floor code radix)
                           (- positions 1)
                           radix))))

(defun ht017-tuple-coefficient-product (code positions radix)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix positions)))
  (if (zp positions)
      1
    (* (ht017-cos-plus-i-sin-coefficient (mod code radix))
       (ht017-tuple-coefficient-product (floor code radix)
                                        (- positions 1)
                                        radix))))

(defun ht017-cauchy-coefficient-sum
    (count positions radix target-degree)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      0
    (let ((code (- count 1)))
      (+ (if (equal (ht017-tuple-degree code positions radix)
                    target-degree)
             (ht017-tuple-coefficient-product code positions radix)
           0)
         (ht017-cauchy-coefficient-sum code
                                      positions
                                      radix
                                      target-degree)))))

(defun ht017-power-coefficient (power degree)
  (if (and (natp power)
           (natp degree))
      (let* ((radix (+ degree 1))
             (tuple-count (expt radix power)))
        (ht017-cauchy-coefficient-sum tuple-count
                                     power
                                     radix
                                     degree))
    0))

; Substitution of n*z into an entire power series multiplies its coefficient
; of z^degree by n^degree.  Hence this predicate, universally quantified over
; n and degree by its free ACL2 arguments, is bidirectionally equivalent to
; the full-complex De Moivre identity stated above.
(defun hundred-theorems-017-de-moivre-statement (n degree)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (natp degree))
   (equal
    (ht017-power-coefficient n degree)
    (* (expt n degree)
       (ht017-cos-plus-i-sin-coefficient degree)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of "De Moivre's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 017. This
-- file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Field (C : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroC oneC : C
    add multiply : C -> C -> C
    negate inverse : C -> C
    fromNat : Nat -> C

    one-not-zero :
      oneC != zeroC

    add-commutative :
      (x y : C) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : C) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : C) -> add x zeroC == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : C) -> add x (negate x) == zeroC

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : C) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : C) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : C) -> multiply x oneC == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : C) -> multiply x zeroC == zeroC
    distribute :
      (x y z : C) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroC == zeroC
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : C) ->
      x != zeroC ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneC

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroC
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneC
    characteristic-zero :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

open Field

subtract :
  {C : Set} ->
  Field C ->
  C ->
  C ->
  C
subtract algebra x y =
  add algebra x (negate algebra y)

power :
  {C : Set} ->
  Field C ->
  C ->
  Nat ->
  C
power algebra x zero =
  oneC algebra
power algebra x (suc n) =
  multiply algebra x (power algebra x n)

record StandardComplexTrigonometry (C : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    algebra : Field C
    imaginaryUnit : C
    sine cosine : C -> C

    imaginary-unit-square :
      multiply algebra imaginaryUnit imaginaryUnit ==
      negate algebra (oneC algebra)

    sine-zero :
      sine (zeroC algebra) == zeroC algebra
    cosine-zero :
      cosine (zeroC algebra) == oneC algebra
    sine-addition :
      (x y : C) ->
      sine (add algebra x y) ==
      add algebra
        (multiply algebra (sine x) (cosine y))
        (multiply algebra (cosine x) (sine y))
    cosine-addition :
      (x y : C) ->
      cosine (add algebra x y) ==
      subtract algebra
        (multiply algebra (cosine x) (cosine y))
        (multiply algebra (sine x) (sine y))

module Statement
  {C : Set}
  (complex : StandardComplexTrigonometry C) where

  open StandardComplexTrigonometry complex

  cis : C -> C
  cis z =
    add algebra
      (cosine z)
      (multiply algebra imaginaryUnit (sine z))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (z : C) ->
    (n : Nat) ->
    power algebra (cis z) n ==
    cis (multiply algebra (fromNat algebra n) z)

hundred-theorems-017 : Set1
hundred-theorems-017 =
  (C : Set) ->
  (complex : StandardComplexTrigonometry C) ->
  Statement.proposition complex

val de_moivre_s_theorem =

      let ccos =
        \w : complex.
          (complex_exp (i * w) + complex_exp (-i * w)) / 2
      in
      let csin =
        \w : complex.
          (complex_exp (i * w) - complex_exp (-i * w)) / (2 * i)
      in
        (ccos z + i * csin z) pow n =
        ccos (complex_of_real (&n) * z) +
          i * csin (complex_of_real (&n) * z)``;

title: 017_de_moivre_s_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "De Moivre's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 017. This
% file contains no proof.

de_moivre_s_theorem_017: THEORY
BEGIN
  complex: TYPE = [# real_part: real, imag_part: real #]

  complex_zero: complex =
    (# real_part := 0, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_one: complex =
    (# real_part := 1, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_i: complex =
    (# real_part := 0, imag_part := 1 #)

  complex_add(x, y: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := real_part(x) + real_part(y),
       imag_part := imag_part(x) + imag_part(y) #)

  complex_mul(x, y: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := real_part(x) * real_part(y)
                       - imag_part(x) * imag_part(y),
       imag_part := real_part(x) * imag_part(y)
                       + imag_part(x) * real_part(y) #)

  complex_scale(scalar: real, x: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := scalar * real_part(x),
       imag_part := scalar * imag_part(x) #)

  complex_power(x: complex, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      complex_one
    ELSE
      complex_mul(complex_power(x, exponent - 1), x)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      n * nat_factorial(n - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  alternating_sign(n: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(n - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  complex_cosine_partial(
      z: complex,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      complex_zero
    ELSE
      LET k: nat = count - 1 IN
        complex_add(
          complex_cosine_partial(z, count - 1),
          complex_scale(
            safe_div(
              alternating_sign(k),
              nat_factorial(2 * k) :: real),
            complex_power(z, 2 * k)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  complex_sine_partial(
      z: complex,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      complex_zero
    ELSE
      LET k: nat = count - 1 IN
        complex_add(
          complex_sine_partial(z, count - 1),
          complex_scale(
            safe_div(
              alternating_sign(k),
              nat_factorial(2 * k + 1) :: real),
            complex_power(z, 2 * k + 1)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  complex_converges_to(
      sequence: [nat -> complex],
      value: complex): bool =
    FORALL (eps: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(real_part(sequence(index)) - real_part(value)) < eps
              AND abs(imag_part(sequence(index)) - imag_part(value)) < eps

  complex_cosine_value(z, value: complex): bool =
    complex_converges_to(
      (LAMBDA (count: nat):
        complex_cosine_partial(z, count)),
      value)

  complex_sine_value(z, value: complex): bool =
    complex_converges_to(
      (LAMBDA (count: nat):
        complex_sine_partial(z, count)),
      value)

  de_moivre_s_theorem: bool =
    FORALL (z: complex), (n: nat),
           (cos_z, sin_z, cos_nz, sin_nz: complex):
      LET nz: complex = complex_scale(n :: real, z) IN
        (complex_cosine_value(z, cos_z)
          AND complex_sine_value(z, sin_z)
          AND complex_cosine_value(nz, cos_nz)
          AND complex_sine_value(nz, sin_nz))
        IMPLIES
          complex_power(
            complex_add(cos_z, complex_mul(sin_z, complex_i)),
            n)
          =
          complex_add(cos_nz, complex_mul(sin_nz, complex_i))
END de_moivre_s_theorem_017

title: 018_liouville_s_theorem_and_the_construction_of_transcendental_n
content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2020 Jujian Zhang. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Damiano Testa, Jujian Zhang
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.DenomsClearable
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.MeanValue
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Polynomial
public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.Real.Irrational
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Polynomial
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Interval.Set.Group

/-!

# Liouville's theorem

This file contains a proof of Liouville's theorem stating that all Liouville numbers are
transcendental.

To obtain this result, there is first a proof that Liouville numbers are irrational and two
technical lemmas.  These lemmas exploit the fact that a polynomial with integer coefficients
takes integer values at integers.  When evaluating at a rational number, we can clear denominators
and obtain precise inequalities that ultimately allow us to prove transcendence of
Liouville numbers.
-/

@[expose] public section


/-- A Liouville number is a real number `x` such that for every natural number `n`, there exist
`a, b ∈ ℤ` with `1 < b` such that `0 < |x - a/b| < 1/bⁿ`.
In the implementation, the condition `x ≠ a/b` replaces the traditional equivalent `0 < |x - a/b|`.
-/
def Liouville (x : ℝ) :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ a b : ℤ, 1 < b ∧ x ≠ a / b ∧ |x - a / b| < 1 / (b : ℝ) ^ n

namespace Liouville

protected theorem irrational {x : ℝ} (h : Liouville x) : Irrational x := by sorry
open Polynomial Metric Set Real RingHom

open scoped Polynomial

/-- Let `Z, N` be types, let `R` be a metric space, let `α : R` be a point and let
`j : Z → N → R` be a function.  We aim to estimate how close we can get to `α`, while staying
in the image of `j`.  The points `j z a` of `R` in the image of `j` come with a "cost" equal to
`d a`.  As we get closer to `α` while staying in the image of `j`, we are interested in bounding
the quantity `d a * dist α (j z a)` from below by a strictly positive amount `1 / A`: the intuition
is that approximating well `α` with the points in the image of `j` should come at a high cost.  The
hypotheses on the function `f : R → R` provide us with sufficient conditions to ensure our goal.
The first hypothesis is that `f` is Lipschitz at `α`: this yields a bound on the distance.
The second hypothesis is specific to the Liouville argument and provides the missing bound
involving the cost function `d`.

This lemma collects the properties used in the proof of `exists_pos_real_of_irrational_root`.
It is stated in more general form than needed: in the intended application, `Z = ℤ`, `N = ℕ`,
`R = ℝ`, `d a = (a + 1) ^ f.nat_degree`, `j z a = z / (a + 1)`, `f ∈ ℤ[x]`, `α` is an irrational
root of `f`, `ε` is small, `M` is a bound on the Lipschitz constant of `f` near `α`, `n` is
the degree of the polynomial `f`.
-/
theorem exists_one_le_pow_mul_dist {Z N R : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace R] {d : N → ℝ}
    {j : Z → N → R} {f : R → R} {α : R} {ε M : ℝ}
    -- denominators are positive
    (d0 : ∀ a : N, 1 ≤ d a)
    (e0 : 0 < ε)
    -- function is Lipschitz at α
    (B : ∀ ⦃y : R⦄, y ∈ closedBall α ε → dist (f α) (f y) ≤ dist α y * M)
    -- clear denominators
    (L : ∀ ⦃z : Z⦄, ∀ ⦃a : N⦄, j z a ∈ closedBall α ε → 1 ≤ d a * dist (f α) (f (j z a))) :
    ∃ A : ℝ, 0 < A ∧ ∀ z : Z, ∀ a : N, 1 ≤ d a * (dist α (j z a) * A) := by sorry
theorem exists_pos_real_of_irrational_root {α : ℝ} (ha : Irrational α) {f : ℤ[X]} (f0 : f ≠ 0)
    (fa : eval α (map (algebraMap ℤ ℝ) f) = 0) :
    ∃ A : ℝ, 0 < A ∧ ∀ a : ℤ, ∀ b : ℕ,
      (1 : ℝ) ≤ ((b : ℝ) + 1) ^ f.natDegree * (|α - a / (b + 1)| * A) := by sorry

/-- Liouville's theorem: every Liouville number is transcendental. -/
protected theorem transcendental {x : ℝ} (lx : Liouville x) : Transcendental ℤ x := by sorry

end Liouville

Require Import CRing_Homomorphisms.
Require Import CPoly_NthCoeff.
Require Import MoreFunctions.
Require Import Rolle.

Require Import Zlcm Q_can RX_deg QX_ZX QX_root_loc QX_extract_roots.

Section CPoly_bounded.

Variable I : interval.
Hypothesis I_fin : finite I.

Fixpoint AbsPoly (P : cpoly_cring IR) : cpoly_cring IR :=
  match P with
    | cpoly_zero _ => cpoly_zero IR
    | cpoly_linear _ c P => cpoly_linear IR (AbsIR c) (AbsPoly P)
  end.

Lemma AbsPoly_zero : AbsPoly [0] = [0].
Proof.
Admitted.
Lemma AbsPoly_linear : forall c P, AbsPoly (c[+X*]P) = AbsIR c[+X*]AbsPoly P.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Abs_poly_nth_coeff : forall P i, nth_coeff i (AbsPoly P) [=] AbsIR (nth_coeff i P).
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition CPoly_bound (P : cpoly_cring IR)  : IR :=
            (AbsPoly P) ! (Max (AbsIR (left_end I I_fin)) (AbsIR (right_end I I_fin))).

Lemma AbsIR_leEq : forall a b, a [<=] b -> [--]a [<=] b -> AbsIR a [<=] b.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma abs_max : forall a b x, a [<=] x -> x [<=] b -> AbsIR x [<=] Max (AbsIR a) (AbsIR b).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Abs_min_max : forall x, I x ->
        AbsIR x [<=] Max (AbsIR (left_end I I_fin)) (AbsIR (right_end I I_fin)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma CPoly_bound_spec : forall x P, I x -> AbsIR (P ! x) [<=] CPoly_bound P.
Proof.
Admitted.

End CPoly_bounded.

Section poly_law_of_mean.

Variable I : interval.
Hypothesis I_fin : finite I.
Hypothesis I_proper : proper I.
Variable P : cpoly_cring IR.

Let C := CPoly_bound I I_fin (_D_ P).
Let Hderiv := Derivative_poly I I_proper P.

Lemma poly_law_of_mean : forall a b, I a -> I b ->
     AbsIR (P ! b [-] P ! a) [<=] C [*] (AbsIR (b [-] a)).
Proof.
Admitted.

End poly_law_of_mean.

Section liouville_lemmas.

Variable a : IR.
Definition Ia : interval := clcr (a[-]Two) (a[+]Two).
Lemma Ia_fin : finite Ia.
Proof.
Admitted.
Lemma Ia_proper : proper Ia.
Proof.
Admitted.
Lemma a_in_Ia : Ia a.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Liouville_lemma1 : forall x : IR, AbsIR (x[-]a) [<=] Two -> Ia x.
Proof.
Admitted.

Variable P : cpoly_cring IR.
Let C := CPoly_bound Ia Ia_fin (_D_ P).

Lemma Liouville_lemma2 : forall x : IR, AbsIR (x[-]a) [<=] Two ->
    AbsIR (P ! x [-] P ! a) [<=] C [*] AbsIR (x [-] a).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Liouville_lemma3 : forall x : IR, [1] [<] x or x [<] Two.
Proof.
Admitted.

End liouville_lemmas.

Section liouville_lemmas2.

Let ZX_deg := RX_deg Z_as_CRing Z_dec.
Variable P : cpoly_cring Z_as_CRing.

Lemma Liouville_lemma4 : forall p : Z_as_CRing,
            p [#] [0] -> [1] [<=] AbsIR (inj_Q_rh p).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Liouville_lemma5 : forall (p : Z_as_CRing) (q : positive), (zx2qx P) ! (p#q)%Q [#] [0] ->
      [1] [<=] (inj_Q_rh q)[^](ZX_deg P) [*] AbsIR (inj_Q_rh ((zx2qx P) ! (p#q)%Q)).
Proof.
Admitted.

End liouville_lemmas2.

Section liouville_lemmas3.

Let ZX_deg := RX_deg Z_as_CRing Z_dec.
Let QX_deg := RX_deg Q_as_CRing Q_dec.
Variable P : cpoly_cring Q_as_CRing.

Lemma Liouville_lemma6 : forall (p : Z_as_CRing) (q : positive), P ! (p#q)%Q [#] [0] ->
      [1] [<=] (inj_Q_rh q)[^](QX_deg P) [*] AbsIR (inj_Q_rh ((Zlcm_den_poly P:Q_as_CRing)[*]P ! (p#q)%Q)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Liouville_lemma7 : forall (p : Z_as_CRing) (q : positive), P ! (p#q)%Q [#] [0] ->
      [1] [<=] (inj_Q_rh q)[^](QX_deg P) [*] AbsIR (inj_Q_rh (Zlcm_den_poly P:Q_as_CRing)) [*] AbsIR (inj_Q_rh (P ! (p#q)%Q)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Variable a : IR.
Let C := AbsIR (inj_Q_rh (Zlcm_den_poly P:Q_as_CRing)) [*] CPoly_bound (Ia a) (Ia_fin a) (_D_ (inj_QX_rh P)).
Hypothesis Ha : (inj_QX_rh P) ! a [=] [0].

Lemma Liouville_lemma8 : forall (n : nat) (q : positive), [1] [<=] (inj_Q_rh q)[^]n.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Liouville_lemma9 : forall (p : Z_as_CRing) (q : positive),
      P ! (p#q)%Q [#] [0] -> AbsIR ((inj_Q_rh (p#q)%Q) [-] a) [<=] Two ->
      [1] [<=] (inj_Q_rh q)[^](QX_deg P) [*] C [*] AbsIR ((inj_Q_rh (p#q)%Q) [-] a).
Proof.
Admitted.

Let C' := Max [1] C.

Lemma Liouville_lemma10 : forall (p : Z_as_CRing) (q : positive),
      P ! (p#q)%Q [#] [0] ->
      [1] [<=] (inj_Q_rh q)[^](QX_deg P) [*] C' [*] AbsIR ((inj_Q_rh (p#q)%Q) [-] a).
Proof.
Admitted.

End liouville_lemmas3.

Section liouville_theorem.

Variable a : IR.
Hypothesis a_irrat : forall x : Q, a [~=] inj_Q _ x.
Variable P : cpoly_cring Q_as_CRing.
Hypothesis P_nz : P [#] [0].
Hypothesis a_alg : (inj_QX_rh P) ! a [=] [0].

Let C : IR := Max [1] (AbsIR (inj_Q_rh (Zlcm_den_poly (QX_extract_roots P):Q_as_CRing)) [*] CPoly_bound (Ia a) (Ia_fin a) (_D_ (inj_QX_rh (QX_extract_roots P)))).
Lemma constant_pos : [0] [<] C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma constant_nz : C [#] [0].
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition Liouville_constant : IR := [1] [/] C [//] constant_nz.

Definition Liouville_degree := RX_deg _ Q_dec (QX_extract_roots P).

Theorem Liouville_theorem : forall (x : Q),
       (Liouville_constant[*]inj_Q IR (1#Qden x)%Q[^]Liouville_degree)
                             [<=] AbsIR (inj_Q _ x [-] a).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Liouville_theorem2 :
    {n : nat | {C : IR | [0] [<] C | forall (x : Q),
         (C[*]inj_Q IR (1#Qden x)%Q[^]n) [<=] AbsIR (inj_Q _ x [-] a)}}.
Proof.
Admitted.

End liouville_theorem.

title: 018_liouville_s_theorem_and_the_construction_of_transcendental_n
content:
(* 
  File:    Liouville_Numbers.thy
  Author:  Manuel Eberl <manuel@pruvisto.org>

  The definition of Liouville numbers and their standard construction, plus the proof
  that any Liouville number is transcendental.
*)

theory Liouville_Numbers
imports 
  Complex_Main
  "HOL-Computational_Algebra.Polynomial"
  Liouville_Numbers_Misc
begin

(* 
  TODO: Move definition of algebraic numbers out of Algebraic_Numbers to reduce unnecessary
  dependencies.
*)

text \<open>
A Liouville number is a real number that can be approximated well -- but not perfectly -- 
by a sequence of rational numbers. ``Well``, in this context, means that the error of the
 $n$-th rational in the sequence is bounded by the $n$-th power of its denominator.

Our approach will be the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item Liouville numbers cannot be rational.
\item Any irrational algebraic number cannot be approximated in the Liouville sense
\item Therefore, all Liouville numbers are transcendental.
\item The standard construction fulfils all the properties of Liouville numbers.
\end{itemize}
\<close>

subsection \<open>Definition of Liouville numbers\<close>

text \<open>
  The following definitions and proofs are largely adapted from those in the Wikipedia
  article on Liouville numbers.~\<^cite>\<open>"wikipedia"\<close>
\<close>

text \<open>
  A Liouville number is a real number that can be approximated well -- but not perfectly --
  by a sequence of rational numbers. The error of the $n$-th term $\frac{p_n}{q_n}$ is at most
  $q_n^{-n}$, where $p_n\in\isasymint$ and $q_n \in\isasymint_{\geq 2}$.

  We will say that such a number can be approximated in the Liouville sense.
\<close>
locale liouville =
  fixes x :: real and p q :: "nat \<Rightarrow> int"
  assumes approx_int_pos: "abs (x - p n / q n) > 0" 
      and denom_gt_1:     "q n > 1"
      and approx_int:     "abs (x - p n / q n) < 1 / of_int (q n) ^ n"

text \<open>
  First, we show that any Liouville number is irrational.
\<close>
lemma (in liouville) irrational: "x \<notin> \<rat>"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  Next, any irrational algebraic number cannot be approximated with rational 
  numbers in the Liouville sense.
\<close>
lemma liouville_irrational_algebraic:
  fixes x :: real
  assumes irrationsl: "x \<notin> \<rat>" and "algebraic x"
  obtains c :: real and n :: nat
    where "c > 0" and "\<And>(p::int) (q::int). q > 0 \<Longrightarrow> abs (x - p / q) > c / of_int q ^ n"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  Since Liouville numbers are irrational, but can be approximated well by rational 
  numbers in the Liouville sense, they must be transcendental.
\<close>
lemma (in liouville) transcendental: "\<not>algebraic x"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Standard construction for Liouville numbers\<close>

text \<open>
  We now define the standard construction for Liouville numbers.
\<close>
definition standard_liouville :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> int) \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> real" where
  "standard_liouville p q = (\<Sum>k. p k / of_int q ^ fact (Suc k))"

lemma standard_liouville_summable:
  fixes p :: "nat \<Rightarrow> int" and q :: int
  assumes "q > 1" "range p \<subseteq> {0..<q}"
  shows   "summable (\<lambda>k. p k / of_int q ^ fact (Suc k))"
  by sorry

lemma standard_liouville_sums:
  assumes "q > 1" "range p \<subseteq> {0..<q}"
  shows   "(\<lambda>k. p k / of_int q ^ fact (Suc k)) sums standard_liouville p q"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  Now we prove that the standard construction indeed yields Liouville numbers.
\<close>
lemma standard_liouville_is_liouville:
  assumes "q > 1" "range p \<subseteq> {0..<q}" "frequently (\<lambda>n. p n \<noteq> 0) sequentially"
  defines "b \<equiv> \<lambda>n. q ^ fact (Suc n)"
  defines "a \<equiv> \<lambda>n. (\<Sum>k\<le>n. p k * q ^ (fact (Suc n) - fact (Suc k)))"
  shows   "liouville (standard_liouville p q) a b"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  We can now show our main result: any standard Liouville number is transcendental.
\<close>
theorem transcendental_standard_liouville:
  assumes "q > 1" "range p \<subseteq> {0..<q}" "frequently (\<lambda>k. p k \<noteq> 0) sequentially"
  shows   "\<not>algebraic (standard_liouville p q)"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  In particular: The the standard construction for constant sequences, such as the
  ``classic'' Liouville constant $\sum_{n=1}^\infty 10^{-n!} = 0.11000100\ldots$,
  are transcendental. 

  This shows that Liouville numbers exists and therefore gives a concrete and 
  elementary proof that transcendental numbers exist.
\<close>
corollary transcendental_standard_standard_liouville:
  "a \<in> {0<..<b} \<Longrightarrow> \<not>algebraic (standard_liouville (\<lambda>_. int a) (int b))"
  by sorry

corollary transcendental_liouville_constant:
  "\<not>algebraic (standard_liouville (\<lambda>_. 1) 10)"
  by sorry

end

title: 018_liouville_s_theorem_and_the_construction_of_transcendental_n
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of the hundred-theorems corpus artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__018, "Liouville's Theorem and the Construction of
;; Transcendental Numbers": every Liouville real is transcendental, and the
;; real Liouville constant sum_{k>=1} 10^(-k!) is a concrete example. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The general theorem is stated over a real-closed ordered field. This is an
;; algebraic presentation of the real-number operations used by the source and
;; avoids silently restricting the theorem to ACL2's built-in rationals.

(defstub ht018-carrier (x) t)
(defstub ht018-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht018-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht018-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub ht018-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub ht018-less-op (x y) t)

(defun ht018-member-p (x)
  (if (ht018-carrier x) t nil))

(defun ht018-add (x y)
  (ht018-add-op x y))

(defun ht018-multiply (x y)
  (ht018-multiply-op x y))

(defun ht018-negate (x)
  (ht018-negate-op x))

(defun ht018-inverse (x)
  (ht018-inverse-op x))

(defun ht018-subtract (x y)
  (ht018-add x (ht018-negate y)))

(defun ht018-less (x y)
  (if (ht018-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun-sk ht018-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht018-member-p x)
      (ht018-member-p y)
      (ht018-member-p z))
     (and
      (ht018-member-p (ht018-add x y))
      (ht018-member-p (ht018-multiply x y))
      (ht018-member-p (ht018-negate x))
      (ht018-member-p (ht018-inverse x))
      (equal (ht018-add (ht018-add x y) z)
             (ht018-add x (ht018-add y z)))
      (equal (ht018-add x y)
             (ht018-add y x))
      (equal (ht018-add x zero) x)
      (equal (ht018-add x (ht018-negate x)) zero)
      (equal (ht018-multiply (ht018-multiply x y) z)
             (ht018-multiply x (ht018-multiply y z)))
      (equal (ht018-multiply x y)
             (ht018-multiply y x))
      (equal (ht018-multiply x one) x)
      (equal
       (ht018-multiply x (ht018-add y z))
       (ht018-add
        (ht018-multiply x y)
        (ht018-multiply x z)))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (ht018-multiply x (ht018-inverse x))
        one))))))

(defun-sk ht018-order-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht018-member-p x)
      (ht018-member-p y)
      (ht018-member-p z))
     (and
      (not (ht018-less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (ht018-less x y)
       (ht018-less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht018-less x y)
        (ht018-less y z))
       (ht018-less x z))
      (implies
       (ht018-less x y)
       (ht018-less
        (ht018-add x z)
        (ht018-add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht018-less zero x)
        (ht018-less zero y))
       (ht018-less zero (ht018-multiply x y)))))))

(defun ht018-carrier-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (ht018-member-p (car values))
       (ht018-carrier-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun ht018-carrier-polynomial-value
    (coefficients x zero)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (ht018-add
       (car coefficients)
       (ht018-multiply
        x
        (ht018-carrier-polynomial-value
         (cdr coefficients) x zero)))
    zero))

(defun ht018-odd-degree-carrier-polynomial-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (and
   (consp coefficients)
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (ht018-carrier-list-p coefficients)
   (evenp (len coefficients))
   (not (equal (car (last coefficients)) zero))))

(defun-sk ht018-has-square-root-p (x)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (ht018-member-p root)
     (equal (ht018-multiply root root) x))))

(defun-sk ht018-carrier-polynomial-has-root-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (ht018-member-p root)
     (equal
      (ht018-carrier-polynomial-value
       coefficients root zero)
      zero))))

;; These are the standard first-order real-closedness conditions.
(defun-sk ht018-real-closure-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x coefficients)
    (and
     (implies
      (and
       (ht018-member-p x)
       (not (ht018-less x zero)))
      (ht018-has-square-root-p x))
     (implies
      (ht018-odd-degree-carrier-polynomial-p
       coefficients zero)
      (ht018-carrier-polynomial-has-root-p
       coefficients zero)))))

(defun ht018-natural-value (n zero one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (ht018-add
     one
     (ht018-natural-value (- n 1) zero one))))

(defun-sk ht018-natural-bound-exists-p (x zero one)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (natp n)
     (ht018-less
      x
      (ht018-natural-value n zero one)))))

(defun-sk ht018-archimedean-law-p (zero one)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (ht018-member-p x)
     (ht018-natural-bound-exists-p x zero one))))

(defun ht018-real-scalar-context-p (zero one)
  (and
   (ht018-member-p zero)
   (ht018-member-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (ht018-less zero one)
   (ht018-field-laws-p zero one)
   (ht018-order-laws-p zero)
   (ht018-real-closure-laws-p zero)
   (ht018-archimedean-law-p zero one)))

(defun ht018-integer-value (integer zero one)
  (if (< integer 0)
      (ht018-negate
       (ht018-natural-value (- integer) zero one))
    (ht018-natural-value integer zero one)))

(defun ht018-power (value exponent one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      one
    (ht018-multiply
     value
     (ht018-power value (- exponent 1) one))))

(defun ht018-absolute-value (value zero)
  (if (ht018-less value zero)
      (ht018-negate value)
    value))

(defun ht018-rational-value
    (numerator denominator zero one)
  (ht018-multiply
   (ht018-integer-value numerator zero one)
   (ht018-inverse
    (ht018-integer-value denominator zero one))))

(defun-sk ht018-liouville-approximation-exists-p
    (x exponent zero one)
  (exists (numerator denominator)
    (let* ((approximation
            (ht018-rational-value
             numerator denominator zero one))
           (denominator-value
            (ht018-integer-value denominator zero one))
           (distance
            (ht018-absolute-value
             (ht018-subtract x approximation)
             zero))
           (bound
            (ht018-inverse
             (ht018-power
              denominator-value exponent one))))
      (and
       (integerp numerator)
       (integerp denominator)
       (< 1 denominator)
       (not (equal x approximation))
       (ht018-less distance bound)))))

(defun-sk ht018-liouville-number-p (x zero one)
  (forall (exponent)
    (implies
     (natp exponent)
     (ht018-liouville-approximation-exists-p
      x exponent zero one))))

(defun ht018-field-integer-polynomial-value
    (coefficients x zero one)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (ht018-add
       (ht018-integer-value (car coefficients) zero one)
       (ht018-multiply
        x
        (ht018-field-integer-polynomial-value
         (cdr coefficients) x zero one)))
    zero))

(defun ht018-integer-coefficient-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and (integerp (car coefficients))
           (ht018-integer-coefficient-list-p
            (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun ht018-nonzero-coefficient-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (or (not (equal (car coefficients) 0))
          (ht018-nonzero-coefficient-list-p
           (cdr coefficients)))
    nil))

(defun-sk ht018-algebraic-over-integers-p
    (x zero one)
  (exists (coefficients)
    (and
     (true-listp coefficients)
     (ht018-integer-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
     (ht018-nonzero-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
     (equal
      (ht018-field-integer-polynomial-value
       coefficients x zero one)
      zero))))

(defun-sk ht018-general-liouville-theorem-p ()
  (forall (zero one x)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht018-real-scalar-context-p zero one)
      (ht018-member-p x)
      (ht018-liouville-number-p x zero one))
     (not
      (ht018-algebraic-over-integers-p
       x zero one)))))

(defun ht018-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n (ht018-factorial (- n 1)))))

;; For natural terms, this is sum_{k=1}^terms 10^(-k!).
(defun ht018-liouville-prefix (terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (+ (ht018-liouville-prefix (- terms 1))
       (/ 1 (expt 10 (ht018-factorial terms))))))

;; Coefficients are listed in ascending order of exponent.
(defun ht018-polynomial-value (coefficients x)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (car coefficients)
         (* x
            (ht018-polynomial-value
             (cdr coefficients) x)))
    0))

;; A polynomial vanishes at the real limit represented by the Liouville
;; prefixes exactly when its values on those prefixes converge to zero.
(defun-sk ht018-polynomial-zero-tail-p
  (coefficients epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and (natp index)
          (<= cutoff index))
     (<
      (abs
       (ht018-polynomial-value
        coefficients
        (ht018-liouville-prefix index)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht018-polynomial-zero-cutoff-exists-p
  (coefficients epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (ht018-polynomial-zero-tail-p
      coefficients epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk ht018-polynomial-tends-to-zero-p (coefficients)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp epsilon)
          (< 0 epsilon))
     (ht018-polynomial-zero-cutoff-exists-p
      coefficients epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht018-liouville-is-algebraic-p ()
  (exists (coefficients)
    (and
     (true-listp coefficients)
     (ht018-integer-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
     (ht018-nonzero-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
     (ht018-polynomial-tends-to-zero-p coefficients))))

(defun hundred-theorems-018-transcendental-liouville-statement ()
  (and
   (ht018-general-liouville-theorem-p)
   (not (ht018-liouville-is-algebraic-p))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 018_liouville_s_theorem_and_the_construction_of_transcendental_n
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Liouville's Theorem and the Construction of Transcendental
-- Numbers" from Hundred Theorems item 018. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infix 4 _≠_ _≤_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 2 _∨_

data ⊥ : Set where

¬_ : Set → Set
¬ A = A → ⊥

_≠_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≠ y = ¬ (x ≡ y)

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R → R → R
    negate reciprocal absoluteValue : R → R
    lessOrEqual : R → R → Set
    fromNat : Nat → R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR ≠ zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) → add x y ≡ add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) → add (add x y) z ≡ add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) → add x zeroR ≡ x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) → add x (negate x) ≡ zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) → multiply x y ≡ multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiply (multiply x y) z ≡ multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) → multiply x oneR ≡ x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) → multiply x zeroR ≡ zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiply x (add y z) ≡
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) →
      x ≠ zeroR →
      multiply x (reciprocal x) ≡ oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) → lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y →
      lessOrEqual y z →
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y →
      lessOrEqual y x →
      x ≡ y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y ∨ lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y →
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual zeroR x →
      lessOrEqual zeroR y →
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR ∧ oneR ≠ zeroR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero ≡ zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) → fromNat (suc n) ≡ add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat (m + n) ≡ add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat (m * n) ≡ multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    characteristic-zero :
      (m n : Nat) → fromNat m ≡ fromNat n → m ≡ n

    absolute-nonnegative :
      (x : R) → lessOrEqual zeroR (absoluteValue x)
    absolute-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) →
      lessOrEqual zeroR x →
      absoluteValue x ≡ x
    absolute-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) →
      lessOrEqual x zeroR →
      absoluteValue x ≡ negate x

    archimedean :
      (x : R) → Σ Nat (λ n → lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R → Set) →
      Σ R (λ x → P x) →
      Σ R (λ upper → (x : R) → P x → lessOrEqual x upper) →
      Σ R
        (λ supremum →
          ((x : R) → P x → lessOrEqual x supremum) ∧
          ((upper : R) →
            ((x : R) → P x → lessOrEqual x upper) →
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

subtract :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  R
subtract reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.add reals x
    (CompleteOrderedField.negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  R
divide reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.multiply reals x
    (CompleteOrderedField.reciprocal reals y)

fromInt :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Int →
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  CompleteOrderedField.negate reals
    (CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals (suc n))

power :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Nat →
  R
power reals x zero =
  CompleteOrderedField.oneR reals
power reals x (suc n) =
  CompleteOrderedField.multiply reals x (power reals x n)

factorial : Nat → Nat
factorial zero = suc zero
factorial (suc n) = suc n * factorial n

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.lessOrEqual reals x y ∧ x ≠ y

Positive :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
Positive reals x =
  StrictLess reals (CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals) x

partialSum :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → R) →
  Nat →
  R
partialSum reals sequence zero =
  CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals
partialSum reals sequence (suc n) =
  CompleteOrderedField.add reals
    (partialSum reals sequence n)
    (sequence n)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → R) →
  R →
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) →
  Positive reals epsilon →
  Σ Nat
    (λ cutoff →
      (n : Nat) →
      cutoff ≤ n →
      CompleteOrderedField.lessOrEqual reals
        (CompleteOrderedField.absoluteValue reals
          (subtract reals (sequence n) limit))
        epsilon)

SeriesSum :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → R) →
  R →
  Set
SeriesSum reals terms limit =
  SequentialLimit reals (partialSum reals terms) limit

data HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient : List Int → Set where
  here :
    {coefficient : Int} {coefficients : List Int} →
    coefficient ≠ pos zero →
    HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

  there :
    {coefficient : Int} {coefficients : List Int} →
    HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient coefficients →
    HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

evaluateIntegerPolynomial :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  List Int →
  R →
  R
evaluateIntegerPolynomial reals [] x =
  CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals
evaluateIntegerPolynomial reals
  (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  CompleteOrderedField.add reals
    (fromInt reals coefficient)
    (CompleteOrderedField.multiply reals x
      (evaluateIntegerPolynomial reals coefficients x))

Algebraic :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
Algebraic reals x =
  Σ (List Int)
    (λ coefficients →
      HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient coefficients ∧
      evaluateIntegerPolynomial reals coefficients x ≡
      CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals)

Transcendental :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
Transcendental reals x =
  ¬ Algebraic reals x

positiveDenominator : Nat → Nat
positiveDenominator denominatorMinusOne =
  suc denominatorMinusOne

positiveRationalValue :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Int →
  Nat →
  R
positiveRationalValue reals numerator denominatorMinusOne =
  divide reals
    (fromInt reals numerator)
    (CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals
      (positiveDenominator denominatorMinusOne))

Irrational :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
Irrational reals x =
  (numerator : Int) →
  (denominatorMinusOne : Nat) →
  x ≠ positiveRationalValue reals numerator denominatorMinusOne

LiouvilleLowerBound :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
LiouvilleLowerBound {R} reals x =
  Σ Nat
    (λ degree →
      Σ R
        (λ constant →
          Positive reals constant
          ∧
          ((numerator : Int) →
            (denominatorMinusOne : Nat) →
            StrictLess reals
              (divide reals constant
                (power reals
                  (CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals
                    (positiveDenominator denominatorMinusOne))
                  degree))
              (CompleteOrderedField.absoluteValue reals
                (subtract reals x
                  (positiveRationalValue reals numerator
                    denominatorMinusOne))))))

rationalDenominator : Nat → Nat
rationalDenominator denominatorMinusTwo =
  suc (suc denominatorMinusTwo)

rationalValue :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Int →
  Nat →
  R
rationalValue reals numerator denominatorMinusTwo =
  divide reals
    (fromInt reals numerator)
    (CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals
      (rationalDenominator denominatorMinusTwo))

approximationError :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Int →
  Nat →
  R
approximationError reals x numerator denominatorMinusTwo =
  CompleteOrderedField.absoluteValue reals
    (subtract reals x
      (rationalValue reals numerator denominatorMinusTwo))

Liouville :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
Liouville reals x =
  (n : Nat) →
  Σ Int
    (λ numerator →
      Σ Nat
        (λ denominatorMinusTwo →
          Positive reals
            (approximationError reals x numerator denominatorMinusTwo)
          ∧
          StrictLess reals
            (approximationError reals x numerator denominatorMinusTwo)
            (divide reals
              (CompleteOrderedField.oneR reals)
              (power reals
                (CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals
                  (rationalDenominator denominatorMinusTwo))
                n))))

liouvilleTerm :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Nat →
  R
liouvilleTerm reals k =
  divide reals
    (CompleteOrderedField.oneR reals)
    (power reals
      (CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals 10)
      (factorial (suc k)))

IsLiouvilleConstant :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
IsLiouvilleConstant reals x =
  SeriesSum reals (liouvilleTerm reals) x

hundred-theorems-018 : Set₁
hundred-theorems-018 =
  (R : Set) →
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) →
  ((x : R) →
    Algebraic reals x →
    Irrational reals x →
    LiouvilleLowerBound reals x)
  ∧
  ((x : R) →
    Liouville reals x →
    Transcendental reals x)
  ∧
  Σ R
    (λ x →
      IsLiouvilleConstant reals x ∧
      Liouville reals x ∧
      Transcendental reals x)

title: 018_liouville_s_theorem_and_the_construction_of_transcendental_n
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Liouville's Theorem and the Construction of Transcendental
  Numbers" from Hundred Theorems item 018. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory realTheory intrealTheory
     real_sigmaTheory;

val liouville_numbers_are_transcendental =
  ``!x : real.
      (!n : num.
         ?a b : int.
           1 < b /\
           x <> real_of_int a / real_of_int b /\
           abs (x - real_of_int a / real_of_int b) <
             1 / (real_of_int b pow n))
      ==>
      !p : num -> int.
        FINITE {k | p k <> 0} /\
        (?k. p k <> 0)
        ==>
        SIGMA
          (\k. real_of_int (p k) * x pow k)
          {k | p k <> 0} <> 0``;

title: 018_liouville_s_theorem_and_the_construction_of_transcendental_n
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Liouville's Theorem and the Construction of
  Transcendental Numbers" from Hundred Theorems item 018: Liouville's
  approximation bound, transcendence of Liouville numbers, and the factorial
  series construction including the base-ten Liouville constant. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  Every mathematical symbol below is grounded in the imported set.mm
  database. RR, ZZ, NN, and NN0 are the standard real, integer, positive
  integer, and nonnegative-integer classes. AA is the set of complex
  algebraic numbers, defined in set.mm as the roots of nonzero integer
  polynomials. Thus a real number outside AA is transcendental.

  The first assertion is Liouville's inverse-power lower bound for irrational
  algebraic reals. The second states directly that a real admitting distinct
  rational approximations of every inverse-power order is transcendental.

  In the first construction assertion, p is an arbitrary integer-valued
  sequence, q is an integer base greater than one, and every digit p(k) lies
  in [0,q). Under just these bounds, the grounded infinite sum

    sum_ k e. NN0 ( ( p ` k ) / ( q ^ ( ! ` ( k + 1 ) ) ) )

  is asserted to be real, which by the set.mm definition means that the
  corresponding partial sums converge. The next assertion additionally
  assumes that nonzero digits occur at arbitrarily large indices and concludes
  the Liouville approximation property and transcendence. The final assertion
  covers both source indexings of the base-ten constant and states their exact
  difference of 1/10. All five declarations are unproved $a statements.
$)

${
  $d A a $.
  $d A b $.
  $d A c $.
  $d A n $.

  hundred-theorems-018-liouville-lower-bound $a
    |- (
         A e. RR
         ->
         (
           ( A e. AA /\ A e/ QQ )
           ->
           E. n e. NN E. c e. RR+
             A. a e. ZZ A. b e. NN
               ( ( c / ( b ^ n ) ) <
                 ( abs ` ( A - ( a / b ) ) ) )
         )
       )
  $.
$}

${
  $d A a $.
  $d A b $.
  $d A n $.

  hundred-theorems-018-liouville-transcendental $a
    |- (
         A e. RR
         ->
         (
           (
             A. n e. NN0
               E. a e. ZZ E. b e. ZZ
                 (
                   ( 1 < b /\ A =/= ( a / b ) )
                   /\
                   (
                     ( abs ` ( A - ( a / b ) ) )
                     <
                     ( 1 / ( b ^ n ) )
                   )
                 )
           )
           ->
           A e/ AA
         )
       )
  $.
$}

${
  $d p k $.
  $d q k $.

  hundred-theorems-018-standard-liouville-convergence $a
    |- A. p A. q
         (
           (
             ( p : NN0 --> ZZ /\ q e. ZZ )
             /\
             (
               1 < q
               /\
               A. k e. NN0
                 ( 0 <_ ( p ` k ) /\ ( p ` k ) < q )
             )
           )
           ->
           sum_ k e. NN0
             ( ( p ` k ) / ( q ^ ( ! ` ( k + 1 ) ) ) )
             e. RR
         )
  $.
$}

${
  $d a k $.
  $d a n $.
  $d b k $.
  $d b n $.
  $d k n $.
  $d p a $.
  $d p b $.
  $d p k $.
  $d p n $.
  $d q a $.
  $d q b $.
  $d q k $.
  $d q n $.

  hundred-theorems-018-standard-liouville-construction $a
    |- A. p A. q
         (
           (
             ( p : NN0 --> ZZ /\ q e. ZZ )
             /\
             (
               (
                 1 < q
                 /\
                 A. k e. NN0
                   ( 0 <_ ( p ` k ) /\ ( p ` k ) < q )
               )
               /\
               A. n e. NN0 E. k e. NN0
                 ( n <_ k /\ ( p ` k ) =/= 0 )
             )
           )
           ->
           (
             (
               A. n e. NN0
                 E. a e. ZZ E. b e. ZZ
                   (
                     (
                       1 < b
                       /\
                       sum_ k e. NN0
                         ( ( p ` k ) / ( q ^ ( ! ` ( k + 1 ) ) ) )
                         =/= ( a / b )
                     )
                     /\
                     (
                       (
                         abs ` (
                           ( sum_ k e. NN0
                               ( ( p ` k ) /
                                 ( q ^ ( ! ` ( k + 1 ) ) ) ) )
                           - ( a / b )
                         )
                       )
                       <
                       ( 1 / ( b ^ n ) )
                     )
                   )
             )
             /\
             sum_ k e. NN0
               ( ( p ` k ) / ( q ^ ( ! ` ( k + 1 ) ) ) )
               e/ AA
           )
         )
  $.
$}

${
  $d k j $.

  hundred-theorems-018-liouville-constant $a
    |- (
         (
           sum_ k e. NN0
             ( 1 / ( ; 1 0 ^ ( ! ` ( k + 1 ) ) ) )
           e. RR
           /\
           sum_ k e. NN0
             ( 1 / ( ; 1 0 ^ ( ! ` ( k + 1 ) ) ) )
           e/ AA
         )
         /\
         (
           (
             sum_ j e. NN0
               ( 1 / ( ; 1 0 ^ ( ! ` j ) ) )
           )
           =
           (
             ( 1 / ; 1 0 )
             +
             sum_ k e. NN0
               ( 1 / ( ; 1 0 ^ ( ! ` ( k + 1 ) ) ) )
           )
           /\
           (
             sum_ j e. NN0
               ( 1 / ( ; 1 0 ^ ( ! ` j ) ) )
             e. RR
             /\
             sum_ j e. NN0
               ( 1 / ( ; 1 0 ^ ( ! ` j ) ) )
             e/ AA
           )
         )
       )
  $.
$}

title: 018_liouville_s_theorem_and_the_construction_of_transcendental_n
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Liouville's Theorem and the Construction of Transcendental
% Numbers" from Hundred Theorems item 018. This file contains no proof.

hundred_theorems_018: THEORY
BEGIN
  digit_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      n * nat_factorial(n - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  integer_polynomial_value(
      coefficients: [nat -> int],
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET k: nat = count - 1 IN
        integer_polynomial_value(coefficients, x, count - 1)
          + (coefficients(k) :: real) * x ^ k
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  algebraic_real(x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (degree: nat):
      EXISTS (coefficients: [nat -> int]):
        NOT (coefficients(degree) = 0)
          AND integer_polynomial_value(
            coefficients, x, degree + 1) = 0

  transcendental_real(x: real): bool =
    NOT algebraic_real(x)

  irrational_real(x: real): bool =
    NOT rational?(x)

  liouville_lower_bound(x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (exponent: nat):
      EXISTS (constant: real):
        constant > 0
          AND FORALL (p, q: int):
            q > 0 IMPLIES
              abs(x - safe_div((p :: real), (q :: real)))
                > safe_div(
                    constant,
                    (q :: real) ^ exponent)

  liouville_approximation_theorem: bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      (algebraic_real(x) AND irrational_real(x))
        IMPLIES liouville_lower_bound(x)

  liouville_number(x: real): bool =
    FORALL (exponent: nat):
      EXISTS (p, q: int):
        q > 1
          AND NOT (
            x = safe_div((p :: real), (q :: real)))
          AND abs(
            x - safe_div((p :: real), (q :: real)))
              < safe_div(
                  1,
                  (q :: real) ^ exponent)

  liouville_numbers_are_transcendental: bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      liouville_number(x)
        IMPLIES transcendental_real(x)

  valid_standard_digits(
      digits: digit_sequence,
      base: int): bool =
    base > 1
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        0 <= digits(index)
          AND digits(index) < base

  frequently_nonzero(digits: digit_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (cutoff: nat):
      EXISTS (index: nat):
        cutoff <= index
          AND NOT (digits(index) = 0)

  standard_liouville_partial_sum(
      digits: digit_sequence,
      base: int,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET k: nat = count - 1 IN
        standard_liouville_partial_sum(
          digits, base, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              (digits(k) :: real),
              (base :: real) ^ nat_factorial(count))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(
      sequence: [nat -> real],
      value: real): bool =
    FORALL (eps: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < eps

  standard_liouville_value(
      digits: digit_sequence,
      base: int,
      value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      (LAMBDA (count: nat):
        standard_liouville_partial_sum(
          digits, base, count)),
      value)

  standard_liouville_construction: bool =
    FORALL (digits: digit_sequence), (base: int):
      (valid_standard_digits(digits, base)
        AND frequently_nonzero(digits))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (value: real):
          standard_liouville_value(
            digits, base, value)
            AND liouville_number(value)
            AND transcendental_real(value)

  unit_digits(index: nat): int = 1

  liouville_constant_construction: bool =
    EXISTS (value: real):
      standard_liouville_value(
        unit_digits, 10, value)
        AND liouville_number(value)
        AND transcendental_real(value)

  liouville_s_theorem_and_the_construction_of_transcendental_numbers: bool =
    liouville_approximation_theorem
      AND liouville_numbers_are_transcendental
      AND standard_liouville_construction
      AND liouville_constant_construction
END hundred_theorems_018

module

public import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finite.Basic

/-!
# Lagrange's four square theorem

The main result in this file is `sum_four_squares`,
a proof that every natural number is the sum of four square numbers.

## Implementation Notes

The proof used is close to Lagrange's original proof.
-/

public section


open Finset Polynomial FiniteField Equiv

/-- **Euler's four-square identity**. -/
theorem euler_four_squares {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (a b c d x y z w : R) :
    (a * x - b * y - c * z - d * w) ^ 2 + (a * y + b * x + c * w - d * z) ^ 2 +
      (a * z - b * w + c * x + d * y) ^ 2 + (a * w + b * z - c * y + d * x) ^ 2 =
      (a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) * (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + z ^ 2 + w ^ 2) := by ring

/-- **Euler's four-square identity**, a version for natural numbers. -/
theorem Nat.euler_four_squares (a b c d x y z w : ℕ) :
    ((a : ℤ) * x - b * y - c * z - d * w).natAbs ^ 2 +
      ((a : ℤ) * y + b * x + c * w - d * z).natAbs ^ 2 +
      ((a : ℤ) * z - b * w + c * x + d * y).natAbs ^ 2 +
      ((a : ℤ) * w + b * z - c * y + d * x).natAbs ^ 2 =
      (a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2) * (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + z ^ 2 + w ^ 2) := by sorry
namespace Int

theorem sq_add_sq_of_two_mul_sq_add_sq {m x y : ℤ} (h : 2 * m = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) :
    m = ((x - y) / 2) ^ 2 + ((x + y) / 2) ^ 2 :=
  have : Even (x ^ 2 + y ^ 2) := by simp [← h]
  mul_right_injective₀ (show (2 * 2 : ℤ) ≠ 0 by decide) <|
    calc
      2 * 2 * m = (x - y) ^ 2 + (x + y) ^ 2 := by rw [mul_assoc, h]; ring
      _ = (2 * ((x - y) / 2)) ^ 2 + (2 * ((x + y) / 2)) ^ 2 := by sorry
theorem lt_of_sum_four_squares_eq_mul {a b c d k m : ℕ}
    (h : a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2 = k * m)
    (ha : 2 * a < m) (hb : 2 * b < m) (hc : 2 * c < m) (hd : 2 * d < m) :
    k < m := by nlinarith

theorem exists_sq_add_sq_add_one_eq_mul (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] :
    ∃ (a b k : ℕ), 0 < k ∧ k < p ∧ a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + 1 = k * p := by sorry
end Int

namespace Nat

open Int

private theorem sum_four_squares_of_two_mul_sum_four_squares {m a b c d : ℤ}
    (h : a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2 = 2 * m) :
    ∃ w x y z : ℤ, w ^ 2 + x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + z ^ 2 = m := by sorry
theorem sum_four_squares (n : ℕ) : ∃ a b c d : ℕ, a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2 = n := by sorry
end Nat

title: 019_four_squares_theorem
content:
Require Import ZArith Lia Znumtheory.
Require Import Natsets MyNat Ztools Zeqm Znumfacts.

(** Definition of the predicate : being the sum of four squares *)

Definition foursquare (n : Z) : Type :=
  {a : _ & { b: _ & { c : _ & { d |
    n = a * a + b * b + c * c + d * d
  }}}}.


(** Euler's identity and compatibility of the 4-square property wrt. multiplication *)

Lemma euler's_identity : forall a b c d w x y z : Z,
  let s z := z * z in
  (a * a + b * b + c * c + d * d) * (w * w + x * x + y * y + z * z) =
  s (a*w + b*x + c*y + d*z) +
  s (a*x - b*w - c*z + d*y) +
  s (a*y + b*z - c*w - d*x) +
  s (a*z - b*y + c*x - d*w).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma mult_foursquare_compat : forall n m : Z,
  foursquare n -> foursquare m -> foursquare (n * m)%Z.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Zmod_sqrt_eq_compat : forall p i j, prime p ->
  (0 <= i -> 0 <= j -> 2 * i < p -> 2 * j < p ->
  i * i ≡ j * j [p] -> i = j)%Z.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma prime_odd : forall p, 2 <> p -> prime p -> p mod 2 = 1.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma odd_bound_1 : forall p i, p mod 2 = 1 -> i < Z.
Proof.
Admitted.


(** [modsym x m] is the unique y congruent to x such that -m/2≤x<m/2 *)

Definition modsym x m := (x + m / 2) mod m - m / 2.

Lemma modsym_bounds : forall x m, 0 < m -> - m <= 2 * modsym x m < m.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma modsym_mod_compat : forall x m, (modsym x m) mod m = x mod m.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma mod_modsym_compat : forall x m, modsym (x mod m) m = modsym x m.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma modsym_mod_diff : forall x m, 0 < m -> { k | modsym x m = x mod m + m * k }.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma modsym_eqm : forall x m, modsym x m ≡ x [ m ].
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma prime_div_false : forall a p, prime p -> (a | p) -> 1 < a < p -> False.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Zbounding_square : forall x m, 0 < m -> -m <= x <= m -> x ^ 2 <= m ^ 2.
Proof.
Admitted.


(** All prime numbers divides some [1+l²+m²] (plus convenient conditions on [l,m]) *)

Lemma prime_dividing_sum_of_two_squares_plus_one : forall p,
  prime p -> 3 <= p ->	
    {l : _ & {m : _ & { k |
      p * k = 1 + l * l + m * m /\
      2 * m < p /\  2 * l < p /\ 0 < k /\ 0 <= l /\ 0 <= m /\ (0 < l \/ 0 < m)}}}.
Proof.
Admitted.


(** Building bounds to prove things like x1²+x2²+x3²+x4²=m² /\ -m/2≤xi<m/2 => xi=-m/2 *)

Lemma egality_case_sum_of_four : forall a b c d M,
  a <= M -> b <= M -> c <= M -> d <= M ->
  a + b + c + d = 4 * M -> ((a = M) /\ (b = M)) /\ ((c = M) /\ (d = M)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma square_bound_equality_case : forall a M,
  -M <= a < M -> M * M <= a * a -> a = - M.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma square_bound : forall x m, -m <= x <= m -> x * x <= m * m.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma square_bound_opp : forall x m, m <= x <= -m -> x * x <= m * m.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma egality_case_sum_of_four_squares : forall a b c d M,
  -M <= a < M -> -M <= b < M -> -M <= c < M -> -M <= d < M ->
  a * a + b * b + c * c + d * d = 4 * (M * M) ->
    ((a = -M) /\ (b = -M)) /\ ((c = -M) /\ (d = -M)).
Proof.
Admitted.


(** If [mp] is the sum of four squares, then so is [np] for a smaller [n] *)

Lemma foursquare_prime_factor_decreasing :
  forall p, prime p -> forall m, (1 < m /\ m < p)%Z ->
    foursquare (m * p) ->
      sigT (fun n => ((0 < n /\ n < m)%Z * foursquare (n * p))%type).
Proof.
Admitted.


(** Induction scheme to use the previous lemma *)
(* TODO déplacer ça ? *)
Definition lt_wf_rect :=
  fun p (P : nat -> Type) F =>
    well_founded_induction_type
      (well_founded_ltof nat (fun m => m)) P F p.


(** Using the previous lemma, one can decrease [mp] into [np] to eventually get [p] *)

Lemma foursquare_prime : forall p, prime p -> foursquare p.
Proof.
Admitted.


(** Trivial application of the previous lemma and euler's identity *)

Theorem lagrange_4_square_theorem : forall n, 0 <= n -> foursquare n.
Proof.
Admitted.


Definition lagrange_fun (n : Z) : (Z * Z) * (Z * Z) :=
  let (a, ha) := lagrange_4_square_theorem (Z.abs n) (Zabs_pos n) in
  let (b, hb) := ha in
  let (c, hc) := hb in
  let (d, _ ) := hc in
  ((a, b), (c, d)).

Lemma lagrange_fun_spec (n : Z) :
  (let (ab, cd) := lagrange_fun n in let (a, b) := ab in let (c, d) := cd in
  Z.
Proof.
Admitted.

(*
Require Extraction.
Extraction "Lagrange_four_square.ml" lagrange_fun.
*)

(*
Eval compute in lagrange_fun 0.

Print Opaque Dependencies lagrange_4_square_theorem.
*)

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__019, "Four Squares Theorem": every natural number
;; is the sum of four squares of natural numbers. Four bounded searches from
;; n down to 0 encode the existential witnesses. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun hundred-theorems-019-four-square-with-abc-through-d-p
    (n a b c d)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix d)))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp a)
           (natp b)
           (natp c)
           (natp d))
      (or (equal n
                 (+ (+ (* a a) (* b b))
                    (+ (* c c) (* d d))))
          (and (not (zp d))
               (hundred-theorems-019-four-square-with-abc-through-d-p
                n a b c (- d 1))))
    nil))

(defun hundred-theorems-019-four-square-with-ab-through-c-p
    (n a b c)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix c)))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp a)
           (natp b)
           (natp c))
      (or (hundred-theorems-019-four-square-with-abc-through-d-p
           n a b c n)
          (and (not (zp c))
               (hundred-theorems-019-four-square-with-ab-through-c-p
                n a b (- c 1))))
    nil))

(defun hundred-theorems-019-four-square-with-a-through-b-p
    (n a b)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix b)))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp a)
           (natp b))
      (or (hundred-theorems-019-four-square-with-ab-through-c-p
           n a b n)
          (and (not (zp b))
               (hundred-theorems-019-four-square-with-a-through-b-p
                n a (- b 1))))
    nil))

(defun hundred-theorems-019-four-square-through-a-p (n a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix a)))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp a))
      (or (hundred-theorems-019-four-square-with-a-through-b-p
           n a n)
          (and (not (zp a))
               (hundred-theorems-019-four-square-through-a-p
                n (- a 1))))
    nil))

(defun hundred-theorems-019-four-squares-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (hundred-theorems-019-four-square-through-a-p n n)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 019_four_squares_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Four Squares Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 019. This
-- file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; _+_; _*_)

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value : A
    property : P value

square : Nat → Nat
square n = n * n

four-squares-theorem : Set
four-squares-theorem =
  (n : Nat) →
  Exists Nat (λ a →
    Exists Nat (λ b →
      Exists Nat (λ c →
        Exists Nat (λ d →
          n ≡ square a + square b + square c + square d))))

four_squares_theorem_019: THEORY
BEGIN
  four_squares_theorem: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):

        n = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + c ^ 2 + d ^ 2

title: 002_the_fundamental_theorem_of_algebra
content:

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Polynomial
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Liouville
public import Mathlib.FieldTheory.PolynomialGaloisGroup
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Complex.FiniteDimensional
public import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Polynomial

/-!
# The fundamental theorem of algebra

This file proves that every nonconstant complex polynomial has a root using Liouville's theorem.

As a consequence, the complex numbers are algebraically closed.

We also provide some specific results about the Galois groups of ℚ-polynomials with specific numbers
of non-real roots.

We also show that an irreducible real polynomial has degree at most two.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Polynomial Bornology Complex

open scoped ComplexConjugate

namespace Complex

/-- **Fundamental theorem of algebra**: every nonconstant complex polynomial
  has a root. -/
theorem exists_root {f : ℂ[X]} (hf : 0 < degree f) : ∃ z : ℂ, IsRoot f z := by sorry
instance isAlgClosed : IsAlgClosed ℂ :=
  IsAlgClosed.of_exists_root _ fun _p _ hp => Complex.exists_root <| degree_pos_of_irreducible hp

end Complex

/-- An algebraic extension of ℝ is isomorphic to either ℝ or ℂ as an ℝ-algebra. -/
theorem Real.nonempty_algEquiv_or (F : Type*) [Field F] [Algebra ℝ F] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic ℝ F] :
    Nonempty (F ≃ₐ[ℝ] ℝ) ∨ Nonempty (F ≃ₐ[ℝ] ℂ) :=
  IsAlgClosed.nonempty_algEquiv_or_of_finrank_eq_two F Complex.finrank_real_complex

namespace Polynomial.Gal

section Rationals

theorem splits_ℚ_ℂ {p : ℚ[X]} : Fact ((p.map (algebraMap ℚ ℂ)).Splits) :=
  ⟨IsAlgClosed.splits _⟩

attribute [local instance] splits_ℚ_ℂ
attribute [local ext] Complex.ext

/-- The number of complex roots equals the number of real roots plus
the number of roots not fixed by complex conjugation (i.e. with some imaginary component). -/
theorem card_complex_roots_eq_card_real_add_card_not_gal_inv (p : ℚ[X]) :
    (p.rootSet ℂ).toFinset.card =
      (p.rootSet ℝ).toFinset.card +
        (galActionHom p ℂ (restrict p ℂ
        (AlgEquiv.restrictScalars ℚ Complex.conjAe))).support.card := by sorry
theorem galActionHom_bijective_of_prime_degree {p : ℚ[X]} (p_irr : Irreducible p)
    (p_deg : p.natDegree.Prime)
    (p_roots : Fintype.card (p.rootSet ℂ) = Fintype.card (p.rootSet ℝ) + 2) :
    Function.Bijective (galActionHom p ℂ) := by sorry
theorem galActionHom_bijective_of_prime_degree' {p : ℚ[X]} (p_irr : Irreducible p)
    (p_deg : p.natDegree.Prime)
    (p_roots1 : Fintype.card (p.rootSet ℝ) + 1 ≤ Fintype.card (p.rootSet ℂ))
    (p_roots2 : Fintype.card (p.rootSet ℂ) ≤ Fintype.card (p.rootSet ℝ) + 3) :
    Function.Bijective (galActionHom p ℂ) := by sorry
end Rationals

end Polynomial.Gal

lemma Polynomial.mul_star_dvd_of_aeval_eq_zero_im_ne_zero (p : ℝ[X]) {z : ℂ} (h0 : aeval z p = 0)
    (hz : z.im ≠ 0) : (X - C ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)) * (X - C z) ∣ map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) p := by sorry
lemma Polynomial.quadratic_dvd_of_aeval_eq_zero_im_ne_zero (p : ℝ[X]) {z : ℂ} (h0 : aeval z p = 0)
    (hz : z.im ≠ 0) : X ^ 2 - C (2 * z.re) * X + C (‖z‖ ^ 2) ∣ p := by sorry
lemma Irreducible.natDegree_le_two {p : ℝ[X]} (hp : Irreducible p) : natDegree p ≤ 2 := by sorry
lemma Irreducible.degree_le_two {p : ℝ[X]} (hp : Irreducible p) : degree p ≤ 2 :=
  natDegree_le_iff_degree_le.1 hp.natDegree_le_two
