title: 026_leibniz_s_series_for_pi
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__026, "Leibniz's Series for Pi": over the real
;; numbers, the alternating series of reciprocals of the positive odd
;; integers converges to pi/4. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; These conservative symbols present an unbounded complete ordered field.
;; The distinguished pi value is fixed independently by convergence of
;; Machin's arctangent series, rather than by the Leibniz series whose limit
;; is the conclusion.

(defstub ht026-real-p (real-type value) t)
(defstub ht026-zero (real-type) t)
(defstub ht026-one (real-type) t)
(defstub ht026-add (real-type left right) t)
(defstub ht026-mul (real-type left right) t)
(defstub ht026-neg (real-type value) t)
(defstub ht026-inv (real-type value) t)
(defstub ht026-less (real-type left right) t)
(defstub ht026-pi (real-type) t)

(defstub ht026-real-set-p (real-type set) t)
(defstub ht026-real-set-member-p (real-type set value) t)
(defstub ht026-supremum (real-type set) t)

(defun ht026-leq (real-type left right)
  (not (ht026-less real-type right left)))

(defun ht026-positive-p (real-type value)
  (and (ht026-real-p real-type value)
       (ht026-less real-type (ht026-zero real-type) value)))

(defun ht026-sub (real-type left right)
  (ht026-add real-type left (ht026-neg real-type right)))

(defun ht026-div (real-type numerator denominator)
  (ht026-mul real-type numerator (ht026-inv real-type denominator)))

(defun ht026-abs (real-type value)
  (if (ht026-less real-type value (ht026-zero real-type))
      (ht026-neg real-type value)
    value))

(defun ht026-nat (real-type n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (ht026-zero real-type)
    (ht026-add real-type
               (ht026-one real-type)
               (ht026-nat real-type (1- n)))))

(defun ht026-power (real-type base exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (ht026-one real-type)
    (ht026-mul real-type
               base
               (ht026-power real-type base (1- exponent)))))

(defun-sk ht026-field-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and (ht026-real-p real-type x)
          (ht026-real-p real-type y)
          (ht026-real-p real-type z))
     (let* ((zero (ht026-zero real-type))
            (one (ht026-one real-type))
            (xy-add (ht026-add real-type x y))
            (yz-add (ht026-add real-type y z))
            (xy-mul (ht026-mul real-type x y))
            (yz-mul (ht026-mul real-type y z))
            (neg-x (ht026-neg real-type x))
            (inv-x (ht026-inv real-type x)))
       (and
        (ht026-real-p real-type xy-add)
        (ht026-real-p real-type xy-mul)
        (ht026-real-p real-type neg-x)
        (ht026-real-p real-type inv-x)
        (equal (ht026-add real-type xy-add z)
               (ht026-add real-type x yz-add))
        (equal xy-add (ht026-add real-type y x))
        (equal (ht026-add real-type x zero) x)
        (equal (ht026-add real-type x neg-x) zero)
        (equal (ht026-mul real-type xy-mul z)
               (ht026-mul real-type x yz-mul))
        (equal xy-mul (ht026-mul real-type y x))
        (equal (ht026-mul real-type x one) x)
        (implies (equal x zero)
                 (equal inv-x zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal (ht026-mul real-type x inv-x) one))
        (equal
         (ht026-mul real-type x yz-add)
         (ht026-add real-type
                    (ht026-mul real-type x y)
                    (ht026-mul real-type x z))))))))

(defun-sk ht026-order-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and (ht026-real-p real-type x)
          (ht026-real-p real-type y)
          (ht026-real-p real-type z))
     (let ((zero (ht026-zero real-type)))
       (and
        (not (ht026-less real-type x x))
        (or (ht026-less real-type x y)
            (equal x y)
            (ht026-less real-type y x))
        (implies
         (and (ht026-less real-type x y)
              (ht026-less real-type y z))
         (ht026-less real-type x z))
        (implies
         (ht026-less real-type x y)
         (ht026-less
          real-type
          (ht026-add real-type x z)
          (ht026-add real-type y z)))
        (implies
         (and (ht026-less real-type zero x)
              (ht026-less real-type zero y))
         (ht026-less
          real-type zero (ht026-mul real-type x y))))))))

(defun-sk ht026-upper-bound-p (real-type set upper)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and (ht026-real-p real-type x)
          (ht026-real-set-member-p real-type set x))
     (ht026-leq real-type x upper))))

(defun-sk ht026-real-set-nonempty-p (real-type set)
  (exists (x)
    (and (ht026-real-p real-type x)
         (ht026-real-set-member-p real-type set x))))

(defun-sk ht026-real-set-bounded-p (real-type set)
  (exists (upper)
    (and (ht026-real-p real-type upper)
         (ht026-upper-bound-p real-type set upper))))

(defun-sk ht026-least-upper-bound-p (real-type set supremum)
  (forall (upper)
    (implies
     (and (ht026-real-p real-type upper)
          (ht026-upper-bound-p real-type set upper))
     (ht026-leq real-type supremum upper))))

(defun-sk ht026-completeness-p (real-type)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and (ht026-real-set-p real-type set)
          (ht026-real-set-nonempty-p real-type set)
          (ht026-real-set-bounded-p real-type set))
     (let ((supremum (ht026-supremum real-type set)))
       (and
        (ht026-real-p real-type supremum)
        (ht026-upper-bound-p real-type set supremum)
        (ht026-least-upper-bound-p
         real-type set supremum))))))

(defun ht026-real-field-p (real-type)
  (let ((zero (ht026-zero real-type))
        (one (ht026-one real-type)))
    (and
     (ht026-real-p real-type zero)
     (ht026-real-p real-type one)
     (not (equal zero one))
     (ht026-field-laws-p real-type)
     (ht026-order-laws-p real-type)
     (ht026-less real-type zero one)
     (ht026-completeness-p real-type))))

;; The arctangent power series is used only to identify the geometric
;; constant pi independently. Machin's identity is
;; pi = 16*arctan(1/5) - 4*arctan(1/239).

(defun ht026-arctan-prefix (real-type z terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      (ht026-zero real-type)
    (let* ((index (1- terms))
           (exponent (+ (* 2 index) 1))
           (unsigned
            (ht026-div
             real-type
             (ht026-power real-type z exponent)
             (ht026-nat real-type exponent)))
           (term
            (if (equal (mod index 2) 0)
                unsigned
              (ht026-neg real-type unsigned))))
      (ht026-add
       real-type
       (ht026-arctan-prefix real-type z index)
       term))))

(defun ht026-machin-pi-prefix (real-type terms)
  (let* ((one (ht026-one real-type))
         (five (ht026-nat real-type 5))
         (two-thirty-nine (ht026-nat real-type 239))
         (sixteen (ht026-nat real-type 16))
         (four (ht026-nat real-type 4)))
    (ht026-sub
     real-type
     (ht026-mul
      real-type
      sixteen
      (ht026-arctan-prefix
       real-type (ht026-div real-type one five) terms))
     (ht026-mul
      real-type
      four
      (ht026-arctan-prefix
       real-type
       (ht026-div real-type one two-thirty-nine)
       terms)))))

(defun-sk ht026-machin-pi-tail-p
    (real-type epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (terms)
    (implies
     (and (natp terms)
          (natp cutoff)
          (<= cutoff terms))
     (ht026-less
      real-type
      (ht026-abs
       real-type
       (ht026-sub
        real-type
        (ht026-machin-pi-prefix real-type terms)
        (ht026-pi real-type)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht026-machin-pi-cutoff-exists-p
    (real-type epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (ht026-machin-pi-tail-p
      real-type epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk ht026-exact-pi-p (real-type)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (ht026-positive-p real-type epsilon)
     (ht026-machin-pi-cutoff-exists-p
      real-type epsilon))))

;; These are exactly the partial sums
;; sum_{i < terms} (-1)^i / (2*i+1) in the represented real field.

(defun ht026-leibniz-prefix (real-type terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      (ht026-zero real-type)
    (let* ((index (1- terms))
           (denominator (+ (* 2 index) 1))
           (unsigned
            (ht026-inv
             real-type
             (ht026-nat real-type denominator)))
           (term
            (if (equal (mod index 2) 0)
                unsigned
              (ht026-neg real-type unsigned))))
      (ht026-add
       real-type
       (ht026-leibniz-prefix real-type index)
       term))))

(defun ht026-pi-over-four (real-type)
  (ht026-div
   real-type
   (ht026-pi real-type)
   (ht026-nat real-type 4)))

(defun-sk ht026-leibniz-tail-p
    (real-type epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (terms)
    (implies
     (and (natp terms)
          (natp cutoff)
          (<= cutoff terms))
     (ht026-less
      real-type
      (ht026-abs
       real-type
       (ht026-sub
        real-type
        (ht026-leibniz-prefix real-type terms)
        (ht026-pi-over-four real-type)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht026-leibniz-cutoff-exists-p
    (real-type epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (ht026-leibniz-tail-p
      real-type epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk ht026-leibniz-limit-p (real-type)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (ht026-positive-p real-type epsilon)
     (ht026-leibniz-cutoff-exists-p
      real-type epsilon))))

(defun hundred-theorems-026-leibniz-series-for-pi-statement
    (real-type)
  (implies
   (and
    (ht026-real-field-p real-type)
    (ht026-real-p real-type (ht026-pi real-type))
    (ht026-exact-pi-p real-type))
   (ht026-leibniz-limit-p real-type)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 026_leibniz_s_series_for_pi
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Leibniz's Series for Pi" from Hundred Theorems item 026.
-- This file contains no proof.

-- Hundred Theorems item 026, "Leibniz's Series for Pi": the real partial sums
-- sum_{i < n} (-1)^i / (2i + 1) converge to pi / 4. This is a statement-only
-- formalization and contains no proof.

module LeibnizSeriesForPi where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      Both (lessOrEqual zeroR oneR) (zeroR != oneR)

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
              lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both (lessOrEqual reals x y) (x != y)

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals f x y =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (f y) (f x))
    (subtract reals y x)

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals f x derivative =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      Both
        (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta)
        ((y : R) ->
          StrictLess reals (subtract reals x delta) y ->
          StrictLess reals y (add reals x delta) ->
          y != x ->
          Both
            (StrictLess reals
              (subtract reals derivative epsilon)
              (differenceQuotient reals f x y))
            (StrictLess reals
              (differenceQuotient reals f x y)
              (add reals derivative epsilon))))

record StandardRealAnalysis (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    algebra : CompleteOrderedField R
    pi : R
    sine cosine : R -> R

    sine-zero :
      sine (zeroR algebra) == zeroR algebra
    cosine-zero :
      cosine (zeroR algebra) == oneR algebra
    sine-addition :
      (x y : R) ->
      sine (add algebra x y) ==
      add algebra
        (multiply algebra (sine x) (cosine y))
        (multiply algebra (cosine x) (sine y))
    cosine-addition :
      (x y : R) ->
      cosine (add algebra x y) ==
      subtract algebra
        (multiply algebra (cosine x) (cosine y))
        (multiply algebra (sine x) (sine y))
    sine-negate :
      (x : R) ->
      sine (negate algebra x) == negate algebra (sine x)
    cosine-negate :
      (x : R) ->
      cosine (negate algebra x) == cosine x
    pythagorean :
      (x : R) ->
      add algebra
        (square algebra (sine x))
        (square algebra (cosine x))
      == oneR algebra
    sine-derivative-at-zero :
      DerivativeAt algebra sine (zeroR algebra) (oneR algebra)

    pi-positive :
      StrictLess algebra (zeroR algebra) pi
    sine-pi :
      sine pi == zeroR algebra
    cosine-pi :
      cosine pi == negate algebra (oneR algebra)
    sine-positive-before-pi :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      StrictLess algebra x pi ->
      StrictLess algebra (zeroR algebra) (sine x)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      Both
        (StrictLess reals
          (subtract reals limit epsilon)
          (sequence n))
        (StrictLess reals
          (sequence n)
          (add reals limit epsilon)))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals term limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n term)
    limit

power :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
power reals base zero =
  oneR reals
power reals base (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (power reals base n)
    base

leibnizTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
leibnizTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (power reals (negate reals (oneR reals)) n)
    (fromNat reals (suc (2 * n)))

module Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : StandardRealAnalysis R) where

  open StandardRealAnalysis reals

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    SeriesHasSum algebra
      (leibnizTerm algebra)
      (divide algebra pi (fromNat algebra 4))

leibniz-series-for-pi : Set1
leibniz-series-for-pi =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  Statement.proposition reals

title: 026_leibniz_s_series_for_pi
026_leibniz_s_series_for_pi
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Leibniz's Series for Pi" from Hundred
  Theorems item 026: the real partial sums of the alternating odd-reciprocal
  series converge to pi / 4. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  Every mathematical symbol below is grounded in the imported set.mm
  database. RR and NN0 are the standard real and nonnegative-integer classes,
  _pi is the real number pi, and the arithmetic, order, absolute-value,
  finite-sum, and restricted-quantifier symbols have their standard set.mm
  definitions.

  For n in NN0, the expression

    sum_ k e. ( 0 ..^ n )
      ( ( ( -u 1 ) ^ k ) / ( ( 2 x. k ) + 1 ) )

  is the n-term real partial sum

    1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - ... + (-1)^(n-1)/(2n-1).

  The assertion is the epsilon-N expansion of convergence of these partial
  sums to _pi / 4. The half-open interval 0 ..^ n is the set.mm rendering of
  the zero-based range used by the Lean source and gives the same series as
  the HOL Light and Rocq sources. The final declaration is an unproved $a
  statement.
$)

hundred-theorems-026-leibniz-series-for-pi $a
  |- A. e e. RR
       ( 0 < e ->
         E. m e. NN0
           A. n e. NN0
             ( m <_ n ->
               ( abs ` (
                   ( sum_ k e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                       ( ( ( -u 1 ) ^ k ) / ( ( 2 x. k ) + 1 ) ) )
                   - ( _pi / 4 )
                 ) ) < e ) ) )
$.

title: 026_leibniz_s_series_for_pi
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Leibniz's Series for Pi" from Hundred Theorems
% item 026. The alternating odd-reciprocal partial sums converge to one quarter
% of the independently power-series-defined circle constant. This file contains
% no proof.

leibniz_s_series_for_pi_026: THEORY
BEGIN
  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN 0 ELSE numerator / denominator ENDIF

  factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  leibniz_partial_sum(count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        leibniz_partial_sum(count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index),
              (2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  cosine_partial_sum(count: nat, x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial_sum(count - 1, x)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: [nat -> real], value: real): bool =
    FORALL (eps: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(count) - value) < eps

  power_series_cosine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          (LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial_sum(count, x)),
          value))

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        2 < value AND value < 4
          AND power_series_cosine(value / 2) = 0)

  leibniz_s_series_for_pi: bool =
    converges_to(
      (LAMBDA (count: nat): leibniz_partial_sum(count)),
      pi / 4)
END leibniz_s_series_for_pi_026

title: 027_sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle
content:
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Joseph Myers, Manuel Candales

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Affine.AddTorsor
public import Mathlib.Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Oriented.Affine
public import Mathlib.Geometry.Euclidean.Angle.Unoriented.Affine
public import Mathlib.Tactic.IntervalCases

/-!
# Triangles

This file proves basic geometrical results about distances and angles
in (possibly degenerate) triangles in real inner product spaces and
Euclidean affine spaces. More specialized results, and results
developed for simplices in general rather than just for triangles, are
in separate files. Definitions and results that make sense in more
general affine spaces rather than just in the Euclidean case go under
`LinearAlgebra.AffineSpace`.

## Implementation notes

Results in this file are generally given in a form with only those
non-degeneracy conditions needed for the particular result, rather
than requiring affine independence of the points of a triangle
unnecessarily.

## References

* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_cosines
* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pons_asinorum
* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sum_of_angles_of_a_triangle
* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_sines

-/

public section

noncomputable section

open scoped CharZero Real RealInnerProductSpace

namespace InnerProductGeometry

/-!
### Geometrical results on triangles in real inner product spaces

This section develops some results on (possibly degenerate) triangles
in real inner product spaces, where those definitions and results can
most conveniently be developed in terms of vectors and then used to
deduce corresponding results for Euclidean affine spaces.
-/

variable {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]

/-- **Law of cosines** (cosine rule), vector angle form. -/
theorem norm_sub_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_sub_two_mul_norm_mul_norm_mul_cos_angle (x y : V) :
    ‖x - y‖ * ‖x - y‖ = ‖x‖ * ‖x‖ + ‖y‖ * ‖y‖ - 2 * ‖x‖ * ‖y‖ * Real.cos (angle x y) := by sorry
theorem sin_angle_mul_norm_eq_sin_angle_mul_norm (x y : V) :
    Real.sin (angle x y) * ‖x‖ = Real.sin (angle y (x - y)) * ‖x - y‖ := by sorry
theorem sin_angle_div_norm_eq_sin_angle_div_norm (x y : V) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hxy : x - y ≠ 0) :
    Real.sin (angle x y) / ‖x - y‖ = Real.sin (angle y (x - y)) / ‖x‖ := by sorry
theorem angle_sub_eq_angle_sub_rev_of_norm_eq {x y : V} (h : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖) :
    angle x (x - y) = angle y (y - x) := by sorry
theorem norm_eq_of_angle_sub_eq_angle_sub_rev_of_angle_ne_pi {x y : V}
    (h : angle x (x - y) = angle y (y - x)) (hpi : angle x y ≠ π) : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖ := by sorry
theorem angle_eq_angle_add_add_angle_add (x : V) {y : V} (hy : y ≠ 0) :
    angle x y = angle x (x + y) + angle y (x + y) := by sorry
theorem angle_add_angle_sub_add_angle_sub_eq_pi (x : V) {y : V} (hy : y ≠ 0) :
    angle x y + angle x (x - y) + angle y (y - x) = π := by sorry
end InnerProductGeometry

namespace Orientation

open Module InnerProductGeometry

variable {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [Fact (finrank ℝ V = 2)]
variable (o : Orientation ℝ V (Fin 2))

/-- **Converse of pons asinorum**, oriented vector angle form (given equality of angles mod `π`). -/
theorem norm_eq_of_two_zsmul_oangle_sub_eq {x y : V}
    (h : (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle x (x - y) = (2 : ℤ) • o.oangle (y - x) y) (h0 : o.oangle x y ≠ 0)
    (hpi : o.oangle x y ≠ π) : ‖x‖ = ‖y‖ := by sorry
end Orientation

namespace EuclideanGeometry

/-!
### Geometrical results on triangles in Euclidean affine spaces

This section develops some geometrical definitions and results on
(possibly degenerate) triangles in Euclidean affine spaces.
-/

open InnerProductGeometry
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

variable {V : Type*} {P : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [MetricSpace P]
  [NormedAddTorsor V P]

/-- **Law of cosines** (cosine rule), angle-at-point form. -/
theorem dist_sq_eq_dist_sq_add_dist_sq_sub_two_mul_dist_mul_dist_mul_cos_angle (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) :
    dist p₁ p₃ * dist p₁ p₃ = dist p₁ p₂ * dist p₁ p₂ + dist p₃ p₂ * dist p₃ p₂ -
      2 * dist p₁ p₂ * dist p₃ p₂ * Real.cos (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) := by sorry
theorem sin_angle_mul_dist_eq_sin_angle_mul_dist (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) :
    Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) * dist p₂ p₃ = Real.sin (∠ p₃ p₁ p₂) * dist p₃ p₁ := by sorry
theorem sin_angle_div_dist_eq_sin_angle_div_dist {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h23 : p₂ ≠ p₃) (h31 : p₃ ≠ p₁) :
    Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) / dist p₃ p₁ = Real.sin (∠ p₃ p₁ p₂) / dist p₂ p₃ := by sorry
theorem dist_eq_dist_mul_sin_angle_div_sin_angle {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P}
    (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({p₁, p₂, p₃} : Set P)) :
    dist p₁ p₂ = dist p₃ p₁ * Real.sin (∠ p₂ p₃ p₁) / Real.sin (∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) := by sorry
theorem angle_eq_angle_of_dist_eq {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : dist p₁ p₂ = dist p₁ p₃) :
    ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p₁ p₃ p₂ := by sorry
theorem dist_eq_of_angle_eq_angle_of_angle_ne_pi {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = ∠ p₁ p₃ p₂)
    (hpi : ∠ p₂ p₁ p₃ ≠ π) : dist p₁ p₂ = dist p₁ p₃ := by sorry
theorem dist_eq_of_two_zsmul_oangle_eq [Module.Oriented ℝ V (Fin 2)]
    [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ V = 2)] {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : (2 : ℤ) • ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ = (2 : ℤ) • ∡ p₂ p₃ p₁)
    (h0 : ∡ p₃ p₁ p₂ ≠ 0) (hpi : ∡ p₃ p₁ p₂ ≠ π) : dist p₁ p₂ = dist p₁ p₃ := by sorry
theorem angle_add_angle_add_angle_eq_pi {p₁ p₂ : P} (p₃ : P) (h : p₂ ≠ p₁) :
    ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ + ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ + ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂ = π := by sorry
theorem exterior_angle_eq_angle_add_angle {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (p : P) (h : Sbtw ℝ p p₁ p₂) :
    ∠ p₃ p₁ p = ∠ p₁ p₃ p₂ + ∠ p₃ p₂ p₁ := by sorry
theorem oangle_add_oangle_add_oangle_eq_pi [Module.Oriented ℝ V (Fin 2)]
    [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ V = 2)] {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h21 : p₂ ≠ p₁) (h32 : p₃ ≠ p₂)
    (h13 : p₁ ≠ p₃) : ∡ p₁ p₂ p₃ + ∡ p₂ p₃ p₁ + ∡ p₃ p₁ p₂ = π := by sorry
lemma angle_add_of_ne_of_ne {a b c p : P} (hb : a ≠ b) (hc : a ≠ c) (hp : Wbtw ℝ b p c) :
    ∠ b a p + ∠ p a c = ∠ b a c := by sorry
theorem dist_sq_mul_dist_add_dist_sq_mul_dist (a b c p : P) (h : ∠ b p c = π) :
    dist a b ^ 2 * dist c p + dist a c ^ 2 * dist b p =
    dist b c * (dist a p ^ 2 + dist b p * dist c p) := by sorry
theorem dist_sq_add_dist_sq_eq_two_mul_dist_midpoint_sq_add_half_dist_sq (a b c : P) :
    dist a b ^ 2 + dist a c ^ 2 = 2 * (dist a (midpoint ℝ b c) ^ 2 + (dist b c / 2) ^ 2) := by sorry
theorem dist_mul_of_eq_angle_of_dist_mul (a b c a' b' c' : P) (r : ℝ) (h : ∠ a' b' c' = ∠ a b c)
    (hab : dist a' b' = r * dist a b) (hcb : dist c' b' = r * dist c b) :
    dist a' c' = r * dist a c := by sorry
theorem dist_lt_of_angle_lt {a b c : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({a, b, c} : Set P)) :
    ∠ a c b < ∠ a b c → dist a b < dist a c := by sorry
theorem angle_lt_iff_dist_lt {a b c : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({a, b, c} : Set P)) :
    ∠ a c b < ∠ a b c ↔ dist a b < dist a c := by sorry
theorem angle_le_iff_dist_le {a b c : P} (h : ¬Collinear ℝ ({a, b, c} : Set P)) :
    ∠ a c b ≤ ∠ a b c ↔ dist a b ≤ dist a c := by sorry
lemma pi_div_three_le_angle_of_le_of_le {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h₂₃₁ : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ ≤ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃)
    (h₃₁₂ : ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂ ≤ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃) : π / 3 ≤ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ := by sorry
lemma pi_div_three_lt_angle_of_le_of_le_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h₂₃₁ : ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ ≤ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃)
    (h₃₁₂ : ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂ ≤ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃)
    (hne : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≠ ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ ∨ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≠ ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂ ∨ ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ ≠ ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂) :
    π / 3 < ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ := by sorry
lemma angle_le_pi_div_three_of_le_of_le {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h₂₃₁ : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≤ ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁)
    (h₃₁₂ : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≤ ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂) (hnd : p₁ ≠ p₂ ∨ p₁ ≠ p₃ ∨ p₂ ≠ p₃) :
    ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≤ π / 3 := by sorry
lemma angle_lt_pi_div_three_of_le_of_le_of_ne {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h₂₃₁ : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≤ ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁)
    (h₃₁₂ : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≤ ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂)
    (hne : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≠ ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ ∨ ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ ≠ ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂ ∨ ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ ≠ ∠ p₃ p₁ p₂) :
    ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ < π / 3 := by sorry
end EuclideanGeometry
