From HighSchoolGeometry Require Export repere_ortho_plan.
Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Parameter AV : Type.
Parameter cons_AV : PP -> PP -> AV.
Parameter plus : AV -> AV -> AV.
Parameter opp : AV -> AV.
 
Axiom
  existence_AB_unitaire : exists A : PO, (exists B : PO, distance A B = 1).
(* Tout angle a un représentant non unique parmi les angles orientés de vecteurs unitaires*)
 
Axiom
  existence_representant_cons :
    forall (a : AV) (A B C : PO),
    distance A B = 1 ->
    exists D : PO, distance C D = 1 /\ a = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D).
(* Tout angle orienté de vecteurs non nuls est égal à l'angle orienté des vecteurs unitaires correspondants*)
 
Axiom
  angles_representants_unitaires :
    forall A B C D E F : PO,
    A <> B ->
    C <> D ->
    cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D) =
    cons_AV (representant_unitaire (vec A B))
      (representant_unitaire (vec C D)).
 
Axiom
  Chasles :
    forall A B C D E F : PO,
    A <> B ->
    C <> D ->
    E <> F ->
    plus (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D)) (cons_AV (vec C D) (vec E F)) =
    cons_AV (vec A B) (vec E F).
 
Axiom
  def_opp :
    forall A B C D : PO,
    A <> B ->
    C <> D -> opp (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D)) = cons_AV (vec C D) (vec A B).
Parameter AV0 : AV.
(* Enroulement de R sur le cercle trigonométrique*)
Parameter image_angle : R -> AV.
 
Axiom AV0_zero : AV0 = image_angle 0.
 
Axiom
  unicite_representant_angle_nul :
    forall A B C : PO,
    distance A B = 1 ->
    distance A C = 1 -> cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) = image_angle 0 -> C = B.
 
Axiom
  tout_angle_a_une_mesure :
    forall A B C D : PO,
    A <> B :>PO ->
    C <> D :>PO ->
    exists x : R, image_angle x = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D) :>AV.
(* Compatibilité des opérations *)
 
Axiom
  add_mes_compatible :
    forall x y : R,
    image_angle (x + y) = plus (image_angle x) (image_angle y).
 
Axiom mes_opp : forall x : R, image_angle (- x) = opp (image_angle x).
(* Cas particuliers : angles plats et angles droits*)
Parameter pisurdeux : R.
 
Definition pi := pisurdeux + pisurdeux.
 
Definition deuxpi := pi + pi.
 
Axiom
  angle_plat :
    forall A B : PO, A <> B -> image_angle pi = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec B A).
 
Axiom
  pisurdeux_droit :
    forall A B C : PO,
    image_angle pisurdeux = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->
    orthogonal (vec A B) (vec A C).
 
Axiom
  droit_direct_ou_indirect :
    forall A B C : PO,
    A <> B ->
    A <> C ->
    orthogonal (vec A B) (vec A C) ->
    image_angle pisurdeux = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) \/
    image_angle (- pisurdeux) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C).
 
Lemma existence_representant_angle :
 forall (A B C : PO) (x : R),
 distance A B = 1 ->
 exists D : PO,
   distance C D = 1 /\ image_angle x = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma tout_angle_mesure : forall a : AV, exists x : R, a = image_angle x :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve mes_opp add_mes_compatible: geo.
 
Ltac mes a :=
  elim (tout_angle_mesure a); intros;
   match goal with
   | h:(a = image_angle ?X1) |- _ =>
       try rewrite h; repeat rewrite <- mes_opp;
        repeat rewrite <- add_mes_compatible; repeat rewrite <- mes_opp
   end.
#[export] Hint Resolve def_opp Chasles angles_representants_unitaires: geo.
 
Ltac mesure A B C D :=
  elim (tout_angle_a_une_mesure (A:=A) (B:=B) (C:=C) (D:=D)); auto with geo;
   intros;
   match goal with
   | h:(image_angle ?X1 = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D)) |- _ =>
       try rewrite <- h; repeat rewrite <- mes_opp;
        repeat rewrite <- add_mes_compatible; repeat rewrite <- mes_opp
   end.
 
Lemma plus_commutative : forall a b : AV, plus a b = plus b a :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma plus_angle_zero : forall a : AV, plus a (image_angle 0) = a.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma plus_associative :
 forall a b c : AV, plus a (plus b c) = plus (plus a b) c :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve plus_angle_zero: geo.
 
Lemma opp_angle :
 forall a b : AV, plus a b = image_angle 0 :>AV -> b = opp a :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma plus_angle_oppose : forall a : AV, plus a (opp a) = image_angle 0.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma mes_oppx :
 forall (A B C D : PO) (x : R),
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 image_angle x = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D) ->
 image_angle (- x) = cons_AV (vec C D) (vec A B).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma mes_opp_opp :
 forall (A B C D E F G I : PO) (a b : R),
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 E <> F ->
 G <> I ->
 image_angle a = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D) ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec E F) (vec G I) ->
 image_angle b = image_angle (- a) ->
 cons_AV (vec E F) (vec G I) = opp (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D)).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma permute_angles :
 forall A B C D E F G I : PO,
 A <> B :>PO ->
 C <> D :>PO ->
 E <> F :>PO ->
 G <> I :>PO ->
 cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D) = cons_AV (vec E F) (vec G I) :>AV ->
 cons_AV (vec C D) (vec A B) = cons_AV (vec G I) (vec E F) :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve permute_angles: geo.
 
Lemma opp_plus_plus_opp :
 forall A B C D E F G I : PO,
 A <> B :>PO ->
 C <> D :>PO ->
 E <> F :>PO ->
 G <> I :>PO ->
 opp (plus (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D)) (cons_AV (vec E F) (vec G I))) =
 plus (opp (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D))) (opp (cons_AV (vec E F) (vec G I)))
 :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve opp_plus_plus_opp: geo.
 
Lemma Chasles_diff :
 forall A B C D E F : PO,
 A <> B :>PO ->
 C <> D :>PO ->
 E <> F :>PO ->
 plus (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D)) (opp (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec E F))) =
 cons_AV (vec E F) (vec C D) :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve pisurdeux_droit: geo.
 
Lemma pisurdeux_scalaire_nul :
 forall A B C : PO,
 image_angle pisurdeux = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->
 scalaire (vec A B) (vec A C) = 0.
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve pisurdeux_scalaire_nul: geo.
 
Lemma orthogonal_pisurdeux_or :
 forall A B C D : PO,
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 orthogonal (vec A B) (vec C D) ->
 image_angle pisurdeux = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D) \/
 image_angle (- pisurdeux) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_nul :
 forall A B : PO, A <> B -> image_angle 0 = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A B).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma pi_plus_pi : image_angle deuxpi = image_angle 0.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma mesure_mod_deuxpi :
 forall (x : R) (A B C D : PO),
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 image_angle x = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D) ->
 image_angle (x + deuxpi) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_oppu_oppv :
 forall A B C D : PO,
 A <> B :>PO ->
 C <> D :>PO ->
 cons_AV (vec B A) (vec D C) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D) :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve angle_oppu_oppv: geo.
 
Theorem somme_triangle :
 forall A B C : PO,
 A <> B :>PO ->
 A <> C :>PO ->
 B <> C :>PO ->
 plus (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C))
   (plus (cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B A)) (cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C B))) =
 image_angle pi :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_triangle :
 forall A B C : PO,
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 B <> C ->
 plus (image_angle pi)
   (opp (plus (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C)) (cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B A)))) =
 cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C B).
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve angle_triangle: geo.
 
Lemma angles_complementaires_triangle_rectangle :
 forall (A B C : PO) (a : R),
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 B <> C ->
 orthogonal (vec B A) (vec B C) ->
 image_angle a = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->
 image_angle (pisurdeux + - a) = cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C B) \/
 image_angle (- pisurdeux + - a) = cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C B).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_produit_positif_r :
 forall (k : R) (A B C D E : PO),
 A <> B :>PO ->
 D <> E :>PO ->
 k > 0 ->
 vec A C = mult_PP k (vec A B) :>PP ->
 cons_AV (vec D E) (vec A C) = cons_AV (vec D E) (vec A B).
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve angles_representants_unitaires: geo.
 
Lemma angle_produit_negatif_r :
 forall (k : R) (A B C D E : PO),
 A <> B ->
 D <> E ->
 k < 0 ->
 vec A C = mult_PP k (vec A B) ->
 cons_AV (vec D E) (vec A C) =
 plus (cons_AV (vec D E) (vec A B)) (image_angle pi).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_produit_negatif_r2 :
 forall (k : R) (A B C D : PO),
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 k < 0 ->
 cons_AV (vec C D) (mult_PP k (vec A B)) =
 plus (cons_AV (vec C D) (vec A B)) (image_angle pi).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_produit_negatif_l :
 forall (k : R) (A B C D : PO),
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 k < 0 ->
 cons_AV (mult_PP k (vec A B)) (vec C D) =
 plus (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D)) (image_angle pi).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_produit_positif_r2 :
 forall (k : R) (A B C D : PO),
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 k > 0 ->
 cons_AV (vec C D) (mult_PP k (vec A B)) = cons_AV (vec C D) (vec A B).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_produit_positif_l :
 forall (k : R) (A B C D : PO),
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 k > 0 ->
 cons_AV (mult_PP k (vec A B)) (vec C D) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec C D).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_nul_positif_colineaire :
 forall A B C : PO,
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) = image_angle 0 ->
 exists k : R, k > 0 /\ vec A C = mult_PP k (vec A B).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angles_milieu :
 forall A B C I : PO,
 B <> C :>PO ->
 B <> A :>PO ->
 I = milieu B C :>PO ->
 cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B A) = cons_AV (vec B I) (vec B A) :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angles_milieu2 :
 forall A B C I : PO,
 B <> C :>PO ->
 C <> A :>PO ->
 I = milieu B C :>PO ->
 cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C B) = cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C I) :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma milieu_angles :
 forall A B M N : PO,
 A <> B ->
 M <> N ->
 M = milieu A B ->
 cons_AV (vec M A) (vec M N) =
 plus (cons_AV (vec M B) (vec M N)) (image_angle pi) :>AV.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Axiom
  milieu_angles_orthogonaux :
    forall A B M N : PO,
    A <> B ->
    M <> N ->
    M = milieu A B ->
    orthogonal (vec A B) (vec M N) ->
    cons_AV (vec M A) (vec M N) = cons_AV (vec M N) (vec M B) :>AV.
 
Lemma alignes_distance_positif_colineaire :
 forall (k : R) (A B C : PO),
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) = image_angle 0 ->
 distance A C = k * distance A B -> vec A C = mult_PP k (vec A B).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma angle_pi_negatif_colineaire :
 forall A B C : PO,
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) = image_angle pi ->
 exists k : R, k < 0 /\ vec A C = mult_PP k (vec A B).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma alignes_distance_negatif_colineaire :
 forall (k : R) (A B C : PO),
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) = image_angle pi ->
 distance A C = k * distance A B -> vec A C = mult_PP (- k) (vec A B).
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve plus_angle_zero: geo.

title: 027_sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle
content:
(*
  File:    Triangle.thy
  Author:  Manuel Eberl <manuel@pruvisto.org>

  Sine and cosine laws, angle sum in a triangle, congruence theorems,
  Isosceles Triangle Theorem
*)

section \<open>Basic Properties of Triangles\<close>
theory Triangle
imports
  Angles
begin

text \<open>
  We prove a number of basic geometric properties of triangles. All theorems hold
  in any real inner product space.
\<close>
subsection \<open>Thales' theorem\<close>

theorem thales:
  fixes A B C :: "'a :: real_inner"
  assumes "dist B (midpoint A C) = dist A C / 2"
  shows   "orthogonal (A - B) (C - B)"
  by sorry

subsection \<open>Sine and cosine laws\<close>

text \<open>
  The proof of the Law of Cosines follows trivially from the definition of the angle,
  the definition of the norm in vector spaces with an inner product and the bilinearity
  of the inner product.
\<close>

lemma cosine_law_vector:
  "norm (u - v) ^ 2 = norm u ^ 2 + norm v ^ 2 - 2 * norm u * norm v * cos (vangle u v)"
  by sorry

lemma cosine_law_triangle:
  "dist b c ^ 2 = dist a b ^ 2 + dist a c ^ 2 - 2 * dist a b * dist a c * cos (angle b a c)"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  According to our definition, angles are always between $0$ and $\pi$ and therefore,
  the sign of an angle is always non-negative. We can therefore look at
  $\sin(\alpha)^2$, which we can express in terms of $\cos(\alpha)$ using the
  identity $\sin(\alpha)^2 + \cos(\alpha)^2 = 1$. The remaining proof is then a
  trivial consequence of the definitions.
\<close>
lemma sine_law_triangle:
  "sin (angle a b c) * dist b c = sin (angle b a c) * dist a c" (is "?A = ?B")
  by sorry


text \<open>
  The following forms of the Law of Sines/Cosines are more convenient for eliminating
  sines/cosines from a goal completely.
\<close>

lemma cosine_law_triangle':
  "2 * dist a b * dist a c * cos (angle b a c) = (dist a b ^ 2 + dist a c ^ 2 - dist b c ^ 2)"
  by sorry

lemma cosine_law_triangle'':
  "cos (angle b a c) = (dist a b ^ 2 + dist a c ^ 2 - dist b c ^ 2) / (2 * dist a b * dist a c)"
  by sorry

lemma sine_law_triangle':
  "b \<noteq> c \<Longrightarrow> sin (angle a b c) = sin (angle b a c) * dist a c / dist b c"
  by sorry

lemma sine_law_triangle'':
  "b \<noteq> c \<Longrightarrow> sin (angle c b a) = sin (angle b a c) * dist a c / dist b c"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Sum of angles\<close>

context
begin

private lemma gather_squares: "a * (a * b) = a^2 * (b :: real)"
  by (simp_all add: power2_eq_square)

private lemma eval_power: "x ^ numeral n = x * x ^ pred_numeral n"
  by (subst numeral_eq_Suc, subst power_Suc) simp

text \<open>
  The proof that the sum of the angles in a triangle is $\pi$ is somewhat more
  involved. Following the HOL Light proof by John Harrison, we first prove
  that $\cos(\alpha + \beta + \gamma) = -1$ and $\alpha + \beta + \gamma \in [0;3\pi)$,
  which then implies the theorem.

  The main work is proving $\cos(\alpha + \beta + \gamma)$. This is done using the
  addition theorems for the sine and cosine, then using the Laws of Sines to eliminate
  all $\sin$ terms save $\sin(\gamma)^2$, which only appears squared in the remaining goal.
  We then use $\sin(\gamma)^2 = 1 - \cos(\gamma)^2$ to eliminate this term and apply
  the law of cosines to eliminate this term as well.

  The remaining goal is a non-linear equation containing only the length of the sides
  of the triangle. It can be shown by simple algebraic rewriting.
\<close>
lemma angle_sum_triangle:
  assumes "a \<noteq> b \<or> b \<noteq> c \<or> a \<noteq> c"
  shows   "angle c a b + angle a b c + angle b c a = pi"
  by sorry

end


subsection \<open>Congruence Theorems\<close>

text \<open>
  If two triangles agree on two angles at a non-degenerate side, the third angle
  must also be equal.
\<close>
lemma similar_triangle_aa:
  assumes "b1 \<noteq> c1" "b2 \<noteq> c2"
  assumes "angle a1 b1 c1 = angle a2 b2 c2"
  assumes "angle b1 c1 a1 = angle b2 c2 a2"
  shows   "angle b1 a1 c1 = angle b2 a2 c2"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  A triangle is defined by its three angles and the lengths of three sides up to congruence.
  Two triangles are congruent if they have their angles are the same and their sides have
  the same length.
\<close>

locale congruent_triangle =
  fixes a1 b1 c1 :: "'a :: real_inner" and a2 b2 c2 :: "'b :: real_inner"
  assumes sides':  "dist a1 b1 = dist a2 b2" "dist a1 c1 = dist a2 c2" "dist b1 c1 = dist b2 c2"
      and angles': "angle b1 a1 c1 = angle b2 a2 c2" "angle a1 b1 c1 = angle a2 b2 c2"
                   "angle a1 c1 b1 = angle a2 c2 b2"
begin

lemma sides:
  "dist a1 b1 = dist a2 b2" "dist a1 c1 = dist a2 c2" "dist b1 c1 = dist b2 c2"
  "dist b1 a1 = dist a2 b2" "dist c1 a1 = dist a2 c2" "dist c1 b1 = dist b2 c2"
  "dist a1 b1 = dist b2 a2" "dist a1 c1 = dist c2 a2" "dist b1 c1 = dist c2 b2"
  "dist b1 a1 = dist b2 a2" "dist c1 a1 = dist c2 a2" "dist c1 b1 = dist c2 b2"
  by sorry

lemma angles:
  "angle b1 a1 c1 = angle b2 a2 c2" "angle a1 b1 c1 = angle a2 b2 c2" "angle a1 c1 b1 = angle a2 c2 b2"
  "angle c1 a1 b1 = angle b2 a2 c2" "angle c1 b1 a1 = angle a2 b2 c2" "angle b1 c1 a1 = angle a2 c2 b2"
  "angle b1 a1 c1 = angle c2 a2 b2" "angle a1 b1 c1 = angle c2 b2 a2" "angle a1 c1 b1 = angle b2 c2 a2"
  "angle c1 a1 b1 = angle c2 a2 b2" "angle c1 b1 a1 = angle c2 b2 a2" "angle b1 c1 a1 = angle b2 c2 a2"
  by sorry

end

lemmas congruent_triangleD = congruent_triangle.sides congruent_triangle.angles



text \<open>
  Given two triangles that agree on a subset of its side lengths and angles that are
  sufficient to define a triangle uniquely up to congruence, one can conclude that they
  must also agree on all remaining quantities, i.e. that they are congruent.

  The following four congruence theorems state what constitutes such a uniquely-defining
  subset of quantities. Each theorem states in its name which quantities are required and
  in which order (clockwise or counter-clockwise): an ``s'' stands for a side,
  an ``a'' stands for an angle.

  The lemma ``congruent-triangleI-sas, for example, requires that two adjacent sides and the
  angle inbetween are the same in both triangles.
\<close>

lemma congruent_triangleI_sss:
  fixes a1 b1 c1 :: "'a :: real_inner" and a2 b2 c2 :: "'b :: real_inner"
  assumes "dist a1 b1 = dist a2 b2"
  assumes "dist b1 c1 = dist b2 c2"
  assumes "dist a1 c1 = dist a2 c2"
  shows   "congruent_triangle a1 b1 c1 a2 b2 c2"
  by sorry

lemmas congruent_triangle_sss = congruent_triangleD[OF congruent_triangleI_sss]

lemma congruent_triangleI_sas:
  assumes "dist a1 b1 = dist a2 b2"
  assumes "dist b1 c1 = dist b2 c2"
  assumes "angle a1 b1 c1 = angle a2 b2 c2"
  shows   "congruent_triangle a1 b1 c1 a2 b2 c2"
  by sorry

lemmas congruent_triangle_sas = congruent_triangleD[OF congruent_triangleI_sas]

lemma congruent_triangleI_aas:
  assumes "angle a1 b1 c1 = angle a2 b2 c2"
  assumes "angle b1 c1 a1 = angle b2 c2 a2"
  assumes "dist a1 b1 = dist a2 b2"
  assumes "\<not>collinear {a1,b1,c1}"
  shows   "congruent_triangle a1 b1 c1 a2 b2 c2"
  by sorry

lemmas congruent_triangle_aas = congruent_triangleD[OF congruent_triangleI_aas]

lemma congruent_triangleI_asa:
  assumes "angle a1 b1 c1 = angle a2 b2 c2"
  assumes "dist a1 b1 = dist a2 b2"
  assumes "angle b1 a1 c1 = angle b2 a2 c2"
  assumes "\<not>collinear {a1, b1, c1}"
  shows   "congruent_triangle a1 b1 c1 a2 b2 c2"
  by sorry

lemmas congruent_triangle_asa = congruent_triangleD[OF congruent_triangleI_asa]


subsection \<open>Isosceles Triangle Theorem\<close>

text \<open>
  We now prove the Isosceles Triangle Theorem: in a triangle where two sides have
  the same length, the two angles that are adjacent to only one of the two sides
  must be equal.
\<close>
lemma isosceles_triangle:
  assumes "dist a c = dist b c"
  shows   "angle b a c = angle a b c"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  For the non-degenerate case (i.e. the three points are not collinear), We also
  prove the converse.
\<close>
lemma isosceles_triangle_converse:
  assumes "angle a b c = angle b a c" "\<not>collinear {a,b,c}"
  shows   "dist a c = dist b c"
  by sorry


subsection\<open>Contributions by Lukas Bulwahn\<close>
  
lemma Pythagoras:
  fixes A B C :: "'a :: real_inner"
  assumes "orthogonal (A - C) (B - C)"
  shows "(dist B C) ^ 2 + (dist C A) ^ 2 = (dist A B) ^ 2"
  by sorry

lemma isosceles_triangle_orthogonal_on_midpoint:
  fixes A B C :: "'a :: euclidean_space"
  assumes "dist C A = dist C B"
  shows "orthogonal (C - midpoint A B) (A - midpoint A B)"
  by sorry

end

title: 027_sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle
027_sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of the hundred-theorems corpus artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__027, "Sum of the Angles of a Triangle": for any
;; three not-all-equal points in a real inner-product affine space, the three
;; principal interior angles, with a zero ray assigned pi/2, sum to pi. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The context below presents a Dedekind-complete ordered field, hence the real
;; field up to ordered-field isomorphism. Three points in any real
;; inner-product affine space lie in an affine subspace of dimension at most
;; two, and their two displacement vectors have an isometric realization in
;; R^2. Thus universal quantification over the R^2 points below is
;; bidirectionally equivalent to universal quantification over the source
;; spaces for this three-point, angle-preserving statement.
;;
;; A principal angle is represented without transcendental primitives by a
;; homogeneous direction pair. For nonzero rays u and v the pair
;;
;;   (dot(u,v), |det(u,v)|)
;;
;; is the positive scalar multiple |u||v| * (cos(theta),sin(theta)), with
;; theta in [0,pi]. If either ray is zero, the pair is (0,1), exactly the
;; source convention theta = pi/2. Multiplication of these pairs is complex
;; multiplication. Since each of the three represented angles lies in
;; [0,pi], their product has zero imaginary part and negative real part
;; exactly when their sum is pi or 3*pi; the latter case occurs exactly when
;; all three angles are pi. Excluding that winding case therefore gives a
;; definitional, bidirectional encoding of equality of the angle sum with pi.

(defun ht027-member-p (carrier x)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list x)) t nil))

(defun ht027-unary-value (operation x)
  (apply$ operation (list x)))

(defun ht027-binary-value (operation x y)
  (apply$ operation (list x y)))

(defun-sk ht027-valid-set-p (carrier set)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (apply$ set (list x))
     (ht027-member-p carrier x))))

(defun-sk ht027-field-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and (ht027-member-p carrier x)
          (ht027-member-p carrier y)
          (ht027-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (ht027-member-p
       carrier (ht027-binary-value add x y))
      (ht027-member-p
       carrier (ht027-binary-value multiply x y))
      (ht027-member-p
       carrier (ht027-unary-value negate x))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (ht027-member-p
        carrier (ht027-unary-value inverse x)))
      (equal
       (ht027-binary-value
        add (ht027-binary-value add x y) z)
       (ht027-binary-value
        add x (ht027-binary-value add y z)))
      (equal (ht027-binary-value add x y)
             (ht027-binary-value add y x))
      (equal (ht027-binary-value add x zero) x)
      (equal
       (ht027-binary-value
        add x (ht027-unary-value negate x))
       zero)
      (equal
       (ht027-binary-value
        multiply
        (ht027-binary-value multiply x y)
        z)
       (ht027-binary-value
        multiply
        x
        (ht027-binary-value multiply y z)))
      (equal (ht027-binary-value multiply x y)
             (ht027-binary-value multiply y x))
      (equal (ht027-binary-value multiply x one) x)
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (ht027-binary-value
         multiply x (ht027-unary-value inverse x))
        one))
      (equal
       (ht027-binary-value
        multiply x (ht027-binary-value add y z))
       (ht027-binary-value
        add
        (ht027-binary-value multiply x y)
        (ht027-binary-value multiply x z)))))))

(defun-sk ht027-order-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply zero less)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and (ht027-member-p carrier x)
          (ht027-member-p carrier y)
          (ht027-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (not (ht027-binary-value less x x))
      (or (equal x y)
          (ht027-binary-value less x y)
          (ht027-binary-value less y x))
      (implies
       (and (ht027-binary-value less x y)
            (ht027-binary-value less y z))
       (ht027-binary-value less x z))
      (implies
       (ht027-binary-value less x y)
       (ht027-binary-value
        less
        (ht027-binary-value add x z)
        (ht027-binary-value add y z)))
      (implies
       (and (ht027-binary-value less zero x)
            (ht027-binary-value less zero y))
       (ht027-binary-value
        less
        zero
        (ht027-binary-value multiply x y)))))))

(defun-sk ht027-set-nonempty-p (carrier set)
  (exists (x)
    (and (ht027-member-p carrier x)
         (apply$ set (list x)))))

(defun-sk ht027-upper-bound-p
    (carrier less set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and (ht027-member-p carrier x)
          (apply$ set (list x)))
     (not (ht027-binary-value less bound x)))))

(defun-sk ht027-bounded-above-p
    (carrier less set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (ht027-member-p carrier bound)
     (ht027-upper-bound-p
      carrier less set bound))))

(defun-sk ht027-supremum-p
    (carrier less set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (and
     (ht027-member-p carrier supremum)
     (ht027-upper-bound-p
      carrier less set supremum)
     (implies
      (and
       (ht027-member-p carrier bound)
       (ht027-upper-bound-p
        carrier less set bound))
      (not
       (ht027-binary-value
        less bound supremum))))))

(defun-sk ht027-has-supremum-p
    (carrier less set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (ht027-supremum-p
     carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk ht027-dedekind-complete-p
    (carrier less)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (ht027-valid-set-p carrier set)
      (ht027-set-nonempty-p carrier set)
      (ht027-bounded-above-p carrier less set))
     (ht027-has-supremum-p
      carrier less set))))

(defun ht027-real-field-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp multiply)
   (tamep-functionp negate)
   (tamep-functionp inverse)
   (tamep-functionp less)
   (ht027-member-p carrier zero)
   (ht027-member-p carrier one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (ht027-field-laws-p
    carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
   (ht027-order-laws-p
    carrier add multiply zero less)
   (ht027-binary-value less zero one)
   (ht027-dedekind-complete-p carrier less)))

(defun ht027-r-carrier (ctx) (nth 0 ctx))
(defun ht027-r-zero (ctx) (nth 1 ctx))
(defun ht027-r-one (ctx) (nth 2 ctx))
(defun ht027-r-add (ctx) (nth 3 ctx))
(defun ht027-r-mul (ctx) (nth 4 ctx))
(defun ht027-r-neg (ctx) (nth 5 ctx))
(defun ht027-r-inv (ctx) (nth 6 ctx))
(defun ht027-r-lt (ctx) (nth 7 ctx))

(defun ht027-context-p (ctx)
  (and
   (true-listp ctx)
   (equal (len ctx) 8)
   (ht027-real-field-p
    (ht027-r-carrier ctx)
    (ht027-r-add ctx)
    (ht027-r-mul ctx)
    (ht027-r-neg ctx)
    (ht027-r-inv ctx)
    (ht027-r-zero ctx)
    (ht027-r-one ctx)
    (ht027-r-lt ctx))))

(defun ht027-r-add-value (ctx x y)
  (ht027-binary-value (ht027-r-add ctx) x y))

(defun ht027-r-mul-value (ctx x y)
  (ht027-binary-value (ht027-r-mul ctx) x y))

(defun ht027-r-neg-value (ctx x)
  (ht027-unary-value (ht027-r-neg ctx) x))

(defun ht027-r-sub-value (ctx x y)
  (ht027-r-add-value
   ctx x (ht027-r-neg-value ctx y)))

(defun ht027-r-lt-p (ctx x y)
  (if (ht027-binary-value
       (ht027-r-lt ctx) x y)
      t nil))

(defun ht027-r-abs-value (ctx x)
  (if (ht027-r-lt-p
       ctx x (ht027-r-zero ctx))
      (ht027-r-neg-value ctx x)
    x))

(defun ht027-point-p (ctx point)
  (and
   (true-listp point)
   (equal (len point) 2)
   (ht027-member-p
    (ht027-r-carrier ctx) (nth 0 point))
   (ht027-member-p
    (ht027-r-carrier ctx) (nth 1 point))))

(defun ht027-vector-subtract (ctx left right)
  (list
   (ht027-r-sub-value
    ctx (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right))
   (ht027-r-sub-value
    ctx (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right))))

(defun ht027-vector-zero-p (ctx vector)
  (and
   (equal (nth 0 vector) (ht027-r-zero ctx))
   (equal (nth 1 vector) (ht027-r-zero ctx))))

(defun ht027-inner-product (ctx left right)
  (ht027-r-add-value
   ctx
   (ht027-r-mul-value
    ctx (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right))
   (ht027-r-mul-value
    ctx (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right))))

(defun ht027-determinant (ctx left right)
  (ht027-r-sub-value
   ctx
   (ht027-r-mul-value
    ctx (nth 0 left) (nth 1 right))
   (ht027-r-mul-value
    ctx (nth 1 left) (nth 0 right))))

(defun ht027-principal-angle-code
    (ctx first-point vertex third-point)
  (let ((first-ray
         (ht027-vector-subtract
          ctx first-point vertex))
        (second-ray
         (ht027-vector-subtract
          ctx third-point vertex)))
    (if (or (ht027-vector-zero-p ctx first-ray)
            (ht027-vector-zero-p ctx second-ray))
        (list (ht027-r-zero ctx)
              (ht027-r-one ctx))
      (list
       (ht027-inner-product
        ctx first-ray second-ray)
       (ht027-r-abs-value
        ctx
        (ht027-determinant
         ctx first-ray second-ray))))))

(defun ht027-angle-code-multiply (ctx left right)
  (list
   (ht027-r-sub-value
    ctx
    (ht027-r-mul-value
     ctx (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right))
    (ht027-r-mul-value
     ctx (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right)))
   (ht027-r-add-value
    ctx
    (ht027-r-mul-value
     ctx (nth 0 left) (nth 1 right))
    (ht027-r-mul-value
     ctx (nth 1 left) (nth 0 right)))))

(defun ht027-angle-code-pi-p (ctx code)
  (and
   (equal (nth 1 code) (ht027-r-zero ctx))
   (ht027-r-lt-p
    ctx (nth 0 code) (ht027-r-zero ctx))))

(defun ht027-three-principal-angles-sum-to-pi-p
    (ctx point-a point-b point-c)
  (let* ((angle-at-a
          (ht027-principal-angle-code
           ctx point-b point-a point-c))
         (angle-at-b
          (ht027-principal-angle-code
           ctx point-a point-b point-c))
         (angle-at-c
          (ht027-principal-angle-code
           ctx point-b point-c point-a))
         (product
          (ht027-angle-code-multiply
           ctx
           (ht027-angle-code-multiply
            ctx angle-at-a angle-at-b)
           angle-at-c)))
    (and
     (equal (nth 1 product) (ht027-r-zero ctx))
     (ht027-r-lt-p
      ctx (nth 0 product) (ht027-r-zero ctx))
     (not
      (and
       (ht027-angle-code-pi-p ctx angle-at-a)
       (ht027-angle-code-pi-p ctx angle-at-b)
       (ht027-angle-code-pi-p ctx angle-at-c))))))

(defun-sk
  hundred-theorems-027-sum-of-the-angles-of-a-triangle-statement
  (ctx)
  (forall (point-a point-b point-c)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht027-context-p ctx)
      (ht027-point-p ctx point-a)
      (ht027-point-p ctx point-b)
      (ht027-point-p ctx point-c)
      (not
       (and
        (equal point-a point-b)
        (equal point-b point-c)
        (equal point-a point-c))))
     (ht027-three-principal-angles-sum-to-pi-p
      ctx point-a point-b point-c))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 027_sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Sum of the Angles of a Triangle" from Hundred Theorems
-- item 027. In a real inner-product space with the standard radian angle, the three
-- angles of a triangle whose vertices are not all equal add to pi. This file contains
-- no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _≠_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 2 _∨_

data ⊥ : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → ⊥

_≠_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≠ y = Not (x ≡ y)

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R → R → R
    negate inverse : R → R
    lessOrEqual : R → R → Set
    fromNat : Nat → R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR ≠ zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) → add x y ≡ add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) → add (add x y) z ≡ add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) → add x zeroR ≡ x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) → add x (negate x) ≡ zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) → multiply x y ≡ multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiply (multiply x y) z ≡ multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) → multiply x oneR ≡ x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) → multiply x zeroR ≡ zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiply x (add y z) ≡
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) →
      x ≠ zeroR →
      multiply x (inverse x) ≡ oneR
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR ≡ zeroR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) → lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y →
      lessOrEqual y z →
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y →
      lessOrEqual y x →
      x ≡ y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y ∨ lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y →
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual zeroR x →
      lessOrEqual zeroR y →
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR ∧ oneR ≠ zeroR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero ≡ zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) →
      fromNat (suc n) ≡ add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat (m + n) ≡ add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat (m * n) ≡ multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat m ≡ fromNat n →
      m ≡ n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) →
      Exists Nat (λ n → lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R → Set) →
      Exists R P →
      Exists R
        (λ upper →
          (x : R) →
          P x →
          lessOrEqual x upper) →
      Exists R
        (λ supremum →
          ((x : R) → P x → lessOrEqual x supremum) ∧
          ((upper : R) →
            ((x : R) → P x → lessOrEqual x upper) →
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

subtractR :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  R
subtractR reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.add reals x
    (CompleteOrderedField.negate reals y)

divideR :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  R
divideR reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.multiply reals x
    (CompleteOrderedField.inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.lessOrEqual reals x y ∧ x ≠ y

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} →
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) →
  (R → R) →
  R →
  R →
  R
differenceQuotient reals f x y =
  divideR reals
    (subtractR reals (f y) (f x))
    (subtractR reals y x)

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} →
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) →
  (R → R) →
  R →
  R →
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals f x derivative =
  (epsilon : R) →
  StrictLess reals (CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals) epsilon →
  Exists R
    (λ delta →
      StrictLess reals (CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals) delta ∧
      ((y : R) →
        StrictLess reals (subtractR reals x delta) y →
        StrictLess reals y (CompleteOrderedField.add reals x delta) →
        y ≠ x →
        StrictLess reals
          (subtractR reals derivative epsilon)
          (differenceQuotient reals f x y) ∧
        StrictLess reals
          (differenceQuotient reals f x y)
          (CompleteOrderedField.add reals derivative epsilon)))

record RealInnerProductAngleSpace
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (V : Set) : Set₁ where

  open CompleteOrderedField reals

  field
    zeroV : V
    addV : V → V → V
    negateV : V → V
    scale : R → V → V

    addV-commutative :
      (u v : V) → addV u v ≡ addV v u
    addV-associative :
      (u v w : V) → addV (addV u v) w ≡ addV u (addV v w)
    addV-zero :
      (v : V) → addV v zeroV ≡ v
    addV-inverse :
      (v : V) → addV v (negateV v) ≡ zeroV

    scale-addV :
      (a : R) (u v : V) →
      scale a (addV u v) ≡ addV (scale a u) (scale a v)
    add-scale :
      (a b : R) (v : V) →
      scale (add a b) v ≡ addV (scale a v) (scale b v)
    multiply-scale :
      (a b : R) (v : V) →
      scale (multiply a b) v ≡ scale a (scale b v)
    one-scale :
      (v : V) → scale oneR v ≡ v

    inner : V → V → R
    inner-add-left :
      (u v w : V) →
      inner (addV u v) w ≡ add (inner u w) (inner v w)
    inner-scale-left :
      (a : R) (u v : V) →
      inner (scale a u) v ≡ multiply a (inner u v)
    inner-symmetric :
      (u v : V) → inner u v ≡ inner v u
    inner-nonnegative :
      (v : V) → lessOrEqual zeroR (inner v v)
    inner-definite :
      (v : V) → inner v v ≡ zeroR → v ≡ zeroV

    norm : V → R
    norm-nonnegative :
      (v : V) → lessOrEqual zeroR (norm v)
    norm-square :
      (v : V) → multiply (norm v) (norm v) ≡ inner v v
    norm-zero :
      (v : V) → norm v ≡ zeroR → v ≡ zeroV
    norm-negate :
      (v : V) → norm (negateV v) ≡ norm v

    pi halfPi : R
    sine cosine : R → R
    vectorAngle : V → V → R

    pi-positive :
      StrictLess reals zeroR pi
    pi-lower-bound :
      StrictLess reals (fromNat 3) pi
    pi-upper-bound :
      StrictLess reals pi (fromNat 4)
    half-pi-doubles :
      add halfPi halfPi ≡ pi

    sine-zero :
      sine zeroR ≡ zeroR
    sine-half-pi :
      sine halfPi ≡ oneR
    sine-pi :
      sine pi ≡ zeroR
    cosine-zero :
      cosine zeroR ≡ oneR
    cosine-half-pi :
      cosine halfPi ≡ zeroR
    cosine-pi :
      cosine pi ≡ negate oneR

    sine-addition :
      (x y : R) →
      sine (add x y) ≡
      add
        (multiply (sine x) (cosine y))
        (multiply (cosine x) (sine y))
    cosine-addition :
      (x y : R) →
      cosine (add x y) ≡
      add
        (multiply (cosine x) (cosine y))
        (negate (multiply (sine x) (sine y)))
    sine-negate :
      (x : R) →
      sine (negate x) ≡ negate (sine x)
    cosine-negate :
      (x : R) →
      cosine (negate x) ≡ cosine x
    trigonometric-circle :
      (x : R) →
      add
        (multiply (sine x) (sine x))
        (multiply (cosine x) (cosine x))
      ≡ oneR

    sine-at-least-negative-one :
      (x : R) →
      lessOrEqual (negate oneR) (sine x)
    sine-at-most-one :
      (x : R) →
      lessOrEqual (sine x) oneR
    cosine-at-least-negative-one :
      (x : R) →
      lessOrEqual (negate oneR) (cosine x)
    cosine-at-most-one :
      (x : R) →
      lessOrEqual (cosine x) oneR
    sine-positive-before-pi :
      (x : R) →
      StrictLess reals zeroR x →
      StrictLess reals x pi →
      StrictLess reals zeroR (sine x)

    sine-derivative-at-zero :
      DerivativeAt reals sine zeroR oneR
    sine-two-pi-periodic :
      (x : R) →
      sine (add x (add pi pi)) ≡ sine x
    cosine-two-pi-periodic :
      (x : R) →
      cosine (add x (add pi pi)) ≡ cosine x

    vector-angle-symmetric :
      (u v : V) → vectorAngle u v ≡ vectorAngle v u
    vector-angle-zero-left :
      (v : V) → vectorAngle zeroV v ≡ halfPi
    vector-angle-zero-right :
      (v : V) → vectorAngle v zeroV ≡ halfPi
    vector-angle-self :
      (v : V) → v ≠ zeroV → vectorAngle v v ≡ zeroR
    vector-angle-nonnegative :
      (u v : V) → lessOrEqual zeroR (vectorAngle u v)
    vector-angle-at-most-pi :
      (u v : V) → lessOrEqual (vectorAngle u v) pi
    vector-angle-cosine :
      (u v : V) →
      inner u v ≡
      multiply
        (multiply (norm u) (norm v))
        (cosine (vectorAngle u v))
    cosine-injective-on-angle-range :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual zeroR x →
      lessOrEqual x pi →
      lessOrEqual zeroR y →
      lessOrEqual y pi →
      cosine x ≡ cosine y →
      x ≡ y

open CompleteOrderedField
open RealInnerProductAngleSpace

subtractV :
  {R V : Set} →
  {reals : CompleteOrderedField R} →
  RealInnerProductAngleSpace reals V →
  V →
  V →
  V
subtractV space u v =
  addV space u (negateV space v)

angleAt :
  {R V : Set} →
  {reals : CompleteOrderedField R} →
  RealInnerProductAngleSpace reals V →
  V →
  V →
  V →
  R
angleAt space a b c =
  vectorAngle space
    (subtractV space a b)
    (subtractV space c b)

module TriangleAngleSumStatement
  {R V : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (space : RealInnerProductAngleSpace reals V) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a b c : V) →
    Not ((a ≡ b) ∧ ((b ≡ c) ∧ (a ≡ c))) →
    add reals
      (add reals
        (angleAt space b a c)
        (angleAt space a b c))
      (angleAt space b c a)
    ≡ pi space

sum-of-the-angles-of-a-triangle : Set₁
sum-of-the-angles-of-a-triangle =
  (R V : Set) →
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) →
  (space : RealInnerProductAngleSpace reals V) →
  TriangleAngleSumStatement.proposition reals space

title: 027_sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Sum of the Angles of a Triangle" from Hundred Theorems item
  027. This file contains no proof.
*)

(*
  Hundred Theorems item 027, "Sum of the Angles of a Triangle": the three Euclidean vertex
  angles of any triangle whose vertices are not all equal sum to pi. This statement-only
  formalization contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pairTheory realTheory transcTheory;

val sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle =
  ``let vertex_angle =
      \P Q R : real # real.
        if P = Q \/ R = Q then
          pi / 2
        else
          acs
            (((FST P - FST Q) * (FST R - FST Q) +
               (SND P - SND Q) * (SND R - SND Q)) /
             (sqrt ((FST P - FST Q) pow 2 +
                    (SND P - SND Q) pow 2) *
              sqrt ((FST R - FST Q) pow 2 +
                    (SND R - SND Q) pow 2)))
    in
      !A B C : real # real.
        ~(A = B /\ B = C /\ A = C) ==>
        vertex_angle B A C + vertex_angle A B C + vertex_angle B C A = pi``;

title: 027_sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Sum of the Angles of a Triangle" from
  Hundred Theorems item 027: in an arbitrary real inner-product space, the
  three total unoriented vertex angles of a nontrivial triangle sum to pi.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The points are vectors in the carrier of a set.mm CPreHil structure whose
  scalar field is RRfld.  This is the vector-space presentation of the affine
  geometry used by the sources: W HT027Ray A B is A minus B.

  W HT027Angle A B C is the total unoriented angle at B.  It is pi/2 when
  either ray is zero, matching the total-angle convention in the source
  formulations; otherwise it is arccos of the real inner product divided by
  the product of the two norms.  Thus equality, real arithmetic, pi, arccos,
  the inner product, the norm, and the vector operations all have their
  definitions from set.mm.

  Metamath assertion variables are schematic, so W, A, B, and C are
  universally quantified subject to the displayed structure and carrier
  conditions.  The final declaration is the sole unproved geometric $a
  statement and is not a proof.
$)

$c HT027Ray HT027Angle $.

ht027-ray-syntax $a class ( W HT027Ray A B ) $.
ht027-angle-syntax $a class ( W HT027Angle A B C ) $.

ht027-ray-definition $a |- (
  W HT027Ray A B
) = (
  A ( -g ` W ) B
) $.

ht027-angle-definition $a |- (
  W HT027Angle A B C
) = if (
  (
    ( ( W HT027Ray A B ) = ( 0g ` W ) )
    \/
    ( ( W HT027Ray C B ) = ( 0g ` W ) )
  )
  ,
  ( _pi / 2 )
  ,
  (
    arccos
    `
    (
      (
        ( W HT027Ray A B )
        ( .i ` W )
        ( W HT027Ray C B )
      )
      /
      (
        ( ( norm ` W ) ` ( W HT027Ray A B ) )
        x.
        ( ( norm ` W ) ` ( W HT027Ray C B ) )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

hundred-triangle-angle-sum $a |- (
  (
    W e. CPreHil
    /\
    (
      ( Scalar ` W ) = RRfld
      /\
      (
        A e. ( Base ` W )
        /\
        (
          B e. ( Base ` W )
          /\
          C e. ( Base ` W )
        )
      )
    )
  )
  ->
  (
    ( -. ( ( A = B ) /\ ( ( B = C ) /\ ( A = C ) ) ) )
    ->
    (
      (
        (
          ( W HT027Angle B A C )
          +
          ( W HT027Angle A B C )
        )
        +
        ( W HT027Angle B C A )
      )
      =
      _pi
    )
  )
) $.

title: 027_sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of "Sum of the Angles of a Triangle" from
:: Hundred Theorems, item 027. In any finite-dimensional Euclidean space, the
:: three unoriented angles of a triangle whose vertices are not all equal sum
:: to PI. The angles use normalized inner products, with a zero ray giving
:: arccos 0. This file contains no proof.

environ

 vocabularies REAL_1, NAT_1, SUBSET_1, NUMBERS, CARD_1, RELAT_1, ARYTM_3,
      EUCLID, FINSEQ_2, COMPLEX1, ARYTM_1, SQUARE_1, RVSUM_1, FINSEQ_1,
      XXREAL_0, PRE_TOPC, STRUCT_0, SIN_COS, SIN_COS6, XBOOLE_0;
 notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0,
      XREAL_0, COMPLEX1, REAL_1, STRUCT_0, PRE_TOPC, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
      RVSUM_1, SQUARE_1, RLVECT_1, EUCLID, XXREAL_0, SIN_COS, SIN_COS6;
 constructors REAL_1, SQUARE_1, BINOP_2, COMPLEX1, FINSEQOP, MONOID_0,
      EUCLID, RELSET_1, BINOP_1, SIN_COS, SIN_COS6;
 registrations RELSET_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, BINOP_2, MEMBERED, MONOID_0,
      EUCLID, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, SQUARE_1, SIN_COS, SIN_COS6, ORDINAL1;
 requirements NUMERALS, BOOLE, SUBSET, ARITHM, REAL;
 equalities SQUARE_1, RVSUM_1, EUCLID, VALUED_1;
 expansions XBOOLE_0, RVSUM_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat, A, B, C being Element of REAL n st
    not (A = B & B = C & A = C)
  holds
    arccos (|(B-A,C-A)| / (|.B-A.| * |.C-A.|)) +
    arccos (|(A-B,C-B)| / (|.A-B.| * |.C-B.|)) +
    arccos (|(B-C,A-C)| / (|.B-C.| * |.A-C.|)) = PI
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 027_sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Sum of the Angles of a Triangle" from Hundred
% Theorems item 027. In an arbitrary real inner product space, the three unoriented
% interior angles of any triangle whose vertices are not all equal sum to pi, with
% a zero incident side assigned angle pi / 2. This file contains no proof.

sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle_027[
  V: TYPE+,
  zero: V,
  vadd: [V, V -> V],
  vneg: [V -> V],
  scale: [real, V -> V],
  inner: [V, V -> real]
]: THEORY
BEGIN
  vector_space_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (u, v: V): vadd(u, v) = vadd(v, u))
      AND (FORALL (u, v, w: V):
        vadd(vadd(u, v), w) = vadd(u, vadd(v, w)))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): vadd(u, zero) = u)
      AND (FORALL (u: V): vadd(u, vneg(u)) = zero)
      AND (FORALL (a: real), (u, v: V):
        scale(a, vadd(u, v)) = vadd(scale(a, u), scale(a, v)))
      AND (FORALL (a, b: real), (u: V):
        scale(a + b, u) = vadd(scale(a, u), scale(b, u)))
      AND (FORALL (a, b: real), (u: V):
        scale(a * b, u) = scale(a, scale(b, u)))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): scale(1, u) = u)
      AND (FORALL (u: V): scale(0, u) = zero)
      AND (FORALL (u: V): vneg(u) = scale(-1, u))

  inner_product_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (u, v, w: V):
      inner(vadd(u, v), w) = inner(u, w) + inner(v, w))
      AND (FORALL (a: real), (u, v: V):
        inner(scale(a, u), v) = a * inner(u, v))
      AND (FORALL (u, v: V): inner(u, v) = inner(v, u))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): 0 <= inner(u, u))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): inner(u, u) = 0 IFF u = zero)

  real_inner_product_space: bool =
    vector_space_laws AND inner_product_laws

  displacement(P, Q: V): V =
    vadd(Q, vneg(P))

  squared_distance(P, Q: V): real =
    inner(displacement(P, Q), displacement(P, Q))

  dot_from(O, P, Q: V): real =
    inner(displacement(O, P), displacement(O, Q))

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  cosine_partial_sum(count: nat, x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial_sum(count - 1, x)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: [nat -> real], value: real): bool =
    FORALL (eps: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(count) - value) < eps

  power_series_cosine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          (LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial_sum(count, x)),
          value))

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        2 < value AND value < 4
          AND power_series_cosine(value / 2) = 0)

  positive_length(length: real, P, Q: V): bool =
    0 < length
      AND length * length = squared_distance(P, Q)

  interior_angle_value(A, O, B: V, theta: real): bool =
    0 <= theta
      AND theta <= pi
      AND
      IF A = O OR B = O THEN
        theta = pi / 2
      ELSE
        EXISTS (OA_length, OB_length: real):
          positive_length(OA_length, O, A)
            AND positive_length(OB_length, O, B)
            AND power_series_cosine(theta) * OA_length * OB_length =
              dot_from(O, A, B)
      ENDIF

  sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle: bool =
    real_inner_product_space IMPLIES
      (FORALL (A, B, C: V):
        NOT (A = B AND B = C AND A = C)
          IMPLIES
            EXISTS (alpha, beta, gamma: real):
              interior_angle_value(B, A, C, alpha)
                AND interior_angle_value(A, B, C, beta)
                AND interior_angle_value(B, C, A, gamma)
                AND alpha + beta + gamma = pi)
END sum_of_the_angles_of_a_triangle_027

title: 028_pascal_s_hexagon_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Pascal's Hexagon Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 028.
-- For a nondegenerate hexagon on an affine conic, its three opposite-side intersections are
-- collinear. This file contains no proof.

/-!
# Pascal's Hexagon Theorem

An affine form of Pascal's theorem over an abstract Dedekind-complete ordered field, hence
over a presentation of the real numbers. The six vertices are ordered around the hexagon,
and `P`, `Q`, and `R` lie on the three pairs of opposite sides.
-/

namespace Theorems100.PascalHexagon

universe u

/-- A Dedekind-complete linearly ordered field, used as a presentation of the real numbers. -/
structure RealScalar where
  Carrier : Type u
  zero : Carrier
  one : Carrier
  add : Carrier → Carrier → Carrier
  mul : Carrier → Carrier → Carrier
  neg : Carrier → Carrier
  inv : Carrier → Carrier
  le : Carrier → Carrier → Prop
  add_assoc : ∀ a b c, add (add a b) c = add a (add b c)
  add_comm : ∀ a b, add a b = add b a
  zero_add : ∀ a, add zero a = a
  add_neg : ∀ a, add (neg a) a = zero
  mul_assoc : ∀ a b c, mul (mul a b) c = mul a (mul b c)
  mul_comm : ∀ a b, mul a b = mul b a
  one_mul : ∀ a, mul one a = a
  left_distrib : ∀ a b c, mul a (add b c) = add (mul a b) (mul a c)
  zero_ne_one : zero ≠ one
  mul_inv : ∀ a, a ≠ zero → mul (inv a) a = one
  le_refl : ∀ a, le a a
  le_trans : ∀ a b c, le a b → le b c → le a c
  le_antisymm : ∀ a b, le a b → le b a → a = b
  le_total : ∀ a b, le a b ∨ le b a
  add_le_add_right : ∀ a b c, le a b → le (add a c) (add b c)
  mul_nonneg : ∀ a b, le zero a → le zero b → le zero (mul a b)
  complete :
    ∀ s : Carrier → Prop,
      (∃ x, s x) →
      (∃ upper, ∀ x, s x → le x upper) →
      ∃ leastUpper,
        (∀ x, s x → le x leastUpper) ∧
          ∀ upper, (∀ x, s x → le x upper) → le leastUpper upper

abbrev Real (K : RealScalar) := K.Carrier
abbrev Point (K : RealScalar) := Fin 2 → Real K
abbrev Set (α : Type u) := α → Prop

def sub (K : RealScalar) (x y : Real K) : Real K :=
  K.add x (K.neg y)

def sq (K : RealScalar) (x : Real K) : Real K :=
  K.mul x x

/-- Three affine-plane points are collinear when their signed-area determinant vanishes. -/
def Collinear3 (K : RealScalar) (p q r : Point K) : Prop :=
  K.mul (sub K (q 0) (p 0)) (sub K (r 1) (p 1)) =
    K.mul (sub K (q 1) (p 1)) (sub K (r 0) (p 0))

/-- Evaluation of a general affine quadratic polynomial in two variables. -/
def quadraticValue (K : RealScalar)
    (a b c d e f : Real K) (x : Point K) : Real K :=
  K.add
    (K.add
      (K.add
        (K.mul a (sq K (x 0)))
        (K.mul b (sq K (x 1))))
      (K.mul c (K.mul (x 0) (x 1))))
    (K.add (K.mul d (x 0)) (K.add (K.mul e (x 1)) f))

/-- A nonzero quadratic equation defining a conic in the affine plane. -/
def AffineConic (K : RealScalar) (con : Set (Point K)) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c d e f : Real K,
    ¬(a = K.zero ∧ b = K.zero ∧ c = K.zero ∧
      d = K.zero ∧ e = K.zero ∧ f = K.zero) ∧
      ∀ x, con x ↔ quadraticValue K a b c d e f x = K.zero

/-- The six vertices are pairwise distinct. -/
def PairwiseDistinct6 (A B C D E F : Point K) : Prop :=
  A ≠ B ∧ A ≠ C ∧ A ≠ D ∧ A ≠ E ∧ A ≠ F ∧
    B ≠ C ∧ B ≠ D ∧ B ≠ E ∧ B ≠ F ∧
    C ≠ D ∧ C ≠ E ∧ C ≠ F ∧
    D ≠ E ∧ D ≠ F ∧ E ≠ F

/--
The vertices are distinct, and no triple containing vertices from both alternating classes
`{A, C, E}` and `{B, D, F}` is collinear.
-/
def PascalNondegenerate (K : RealScalar) (A B C D E F : Point K) : Prop :=
  PairwiseDistinct6 A B C D E F ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K A C B ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K A C D ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K A C F ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K A E B ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K A E D ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K A E F ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K C E B ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K C E D ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K C E F ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K B D A ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K B D C ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K B D E ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K B F A ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K B F C ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K B F E ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K D F A ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K D F C ∧
    ¬Collinear3 K D F E

/-- `P`, `Q`, and `R` lie on the three pairs of opposite sides of the hexagon. -/
def PascalIntersections (K : RealScalar)
    (A B C D E F P Q R : Point K) : Prop :=
  Collinear3 K P A B ∧
    Collinear3 K P D E ∧
    Collinear3 K Q B C ∧
    Collinear3 K Q E F ∧
    Collinear3 K R C D ∧
    Collinear3 K R F A

/-- **Pascal's hexagon theorem** for an affine conic. -/
theorem pascal_hexagon_theorem
    (K : RealScalar)
    {con : Set (Point K)} {A B C D E F P Q R : Point K}
    (hnondegenerate : PascalNondegenerate K A B C D E F)
    (hconic : AffineConic K con)
    (honConic : con A ∧ con B ∧ con C ∧ con D ∧ con E ∧ con F)
    (hintersections : PascalIntersections K A B C D E F P Q R) :
    Collinear3 K P Q R := sorry

end Theorems100.PascalHexagon

title: 028_pascal_s_hexagon_theorem
content:
Require Export projective_plane_inst.
Require Export FSets.

Module Export uniq := (uniqueness_axioms AbstractProjectivePlane).
Module uniqdec := (decidability AbstractProjectivePlane).

Definition line A B := (proj1_sig (a1_exist A B)).
Definition inter l m := (proj1_sig (a2_exist l m)).

Definition on_inter A P Q R S := Incid A (line P Q) /\ Incid A (line R S).
Definition on_inter' A P Q R S := A = inter (line P Q) (line R S).

Definition Col A B C := 
 exists l : Line, 
 Incid A l /\ Incid B l /\ Incid C l.

Definition Meet l1 l2 l3 := 
 exists P : Point, Incid P l1 /\ Incid P l2 /\ Incid P l3.

Definition is_transverse A' B' C' A B C :=
Col A' B' C' /\ Col A B' C /\ Col A C' B /\ Col B A' C.

Definition is_on_inter P A B C D :=
Col P A B /\ Col P C D.

Definition is_on_proper_inter P A B C D :=
Col P A B /\ Col P C D /\ A<>B /\ C<>D /\ line A B <> line C D.

Definition is_hexamy A B C D E F := 
  (A<>B /\ A<>C /\ A<>D /\ A<>E /\ A<>F /\
  B<>C /\ B<>D /\ B<>E /\ B<>F /\
  C<>D /\ C<>E /\ C<>F /\
  D<>E /\ D<>F /\
  E<>F) /\
  let a:= inter (line B C) (line E F) in
  let b:= inter (line C D) (line F A) in 
  let c:= inter (line A B) (line D E) in
Col a b c.

Definition hexamy := forall A B C D E F, 
is_hexamy A B C D E F -> 
is_hexamy B A C D E F.


Ltac apply_unicity_hyps := match goal with
H1: ?A <> ?B, 
H2: ?Incid ?A ?l, 
H3: ?Incid ?B ?l, 
H4 : ?Incid ?A ?m, 
H5: ?Incid ?B ?m |- _ =>
let id:= fresh in assert (id: l=m); try apply (uniq.a1_unique A B l m H1 H2 H3 H4 H5);idtac "we have " l " = " m;subst l
| H1: ?l <> ?m, 
  H2: ?Incid ?A ?l, 
  H3: ?Incid ?A ?m, 
  H4 : ?Incid ?B ?l, 
  H5: ?Incid ?B ?m |- _ =>
let id:= fresh in assert (id: A=B); try apply (uniq.a2_unique l m A B H1 H2 H3 H4 H5);idtac "we have : " A " = " B;subst A
end.

Ltac collapse_hyps :=  progress (repeat (apply_unicity_hyps; CleanDuplicatedHyps)).

Ltac solve_eq := solve [intro; repeat subst; try collapse_hyps;intuition].

Ltac apply_unicity_no_hyps := match goal with
HAl: ?Incid ?A ?l, 
HBl: ?Incid ?B ?l, 
HAm: ?Incid ?A ?m, 
HBm: ?Incid ?B ?m |- _ =>
let id:= fresh in assert (id: l=m) 
by ( apply (uniq.a1_unique A B l m);
[solve_eq| apply HAl | apply HBl| apply HAm| apply HBm]);
idtac "we have " l " = " m;subst l
|
HAl: ?Incid ?A ?l, 
HBl: ?Incid ?B ?l, 
HAm: ?Incid ?A ?m, 
HBm: ?Incid ?B ?m |- _ =>
let id:= fresh in assert (id: A=B)
by ( apply (uniq.a2_unique l m A B);
[solve_eq| apply HAl | apply HAm| apply HBl| apply HBm]);
idtac "we have " A " = " B;subst A
end.

Ltac aide :=
 match goal with
H2: ?Incid ?A ?l, 
H3: ?Incid ?B ?l, 
H4: ?Incid ?A ?m, 
H5: ?Incid ?B ?m |- _ => idtac A " = " B " ou " l "=" m
end.

Ltac collapse_no_hyps := progress (repeat (apply_unicity_no_hyps; CleanDuplicatedHyps)).

Ltac collapse := progress ( try collapse_hyps; try collapse_no_hyps).

Ltac not_eq A B:= assert (A<>B) by solve_eq.

Definition Col_on A B C l := Incid A l /\ Incid B l /\ Incid C l.

Ltac geo_norm := 
 unfold Col_on, 
            is_on_inter, is_on_proper_inter,
            dist3, dist4, dist6, 
            Col in * |-; use_all.

Ltac cases_line l m := 
   elim (uniqdec.eq_line_dec l m); intro;
   [subst;try collapse|idtac].

Ltac cases_point A B := 
   elim (uniqdec.eq_point_dec A B); intro;
   [subst;try collapse|idtac].

Lemma line_wd : forall A B l,
 Incid A l ->
 Incid B l ->
 A<>B ->
 line A B = l.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma line_wd_sym : forall A B l,
 Incid A l ->
 Incid B l ->
 B<>A ->
 line A B = l.
Proof.
Admitted.

Ltac create_line A B l := elim (a1_exist A B);intros l Hl;decompose[and] Hl;clear Hl.

Ltac create_point l m P := elim (a2_exist l m);intros P HP;decompose[and] HP;clear HP.

Ltac create_inter A B C D P := 
  let AB:=fresh "l" in 
  let CD:= fresh "l" in
  create_line A B AB; create_line C D CD; create_point AB CD P.

Ltac create_non_existing_line A B := progress first [ (match goal with
 HA : Incid A ?l , HB : Incid B ?l |- _ => idtac 
end) | (let id:= fresh "l" in create_line A B id) ].


Ltac add_non_existing_lines := repeat (match goal with
_: context[line ?A ?B] |- _ => create_non_existing_line A B
| _: _ |- context[line ?A ?B] => create_non_existing_line A B
end).

Ltac remove_line_occ := repeat ( match goal with
 HAB: ?A<>?B, HA: Incid ?A ?l, HB: Incid ?B ?l, 
 H: context[line ?A ?B] |- _ => rewrite (line_wd A B l) in * by assumption
| HAB: ?B<>?A, HA: Incid ?A ?l, HB: Incid ?B ?l, 
 H: context[line ?A ?B] |- _ => rewrite (line_wd_sym A B l) in * by assumption
| HAB: ?A<>?B, HA: Incid ?A ?l, HB: Incid ?B ?l 
 |- context[line ?A ?B] => rewrite (line_wd A B l) in * by assumption
| HAB: ?B<>?A, HA: Incid ?A ?l, HB: Incid ?B ?l 
 |- context[line ?A ?B] => rewrite (line_wd_sym A B l) in * by assumption
end).

Lemma test2 : forall A B  C D l , line A B = l -> line C D = l -> True.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma on_inter_points_wd : forall A B C D P l m,
 Incid A l ->
 Incid B l ->
 Incid C m ->
 Incid D m ->
 Incid P l ->
 Incid P m ->
 l <> m ->
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 P = inter (line A B) (line C D).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma on_inter_points_wd_spec_1 : forall A B C D l m,
 Incid A l ->
 Incid B l ->
 Incid C m ->
 Incid D m ->
 Incid A m ->
 l <> m ->
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 A = inter (line A B) (line C D).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma on_inter_points_wd_spec_2 : forall A B C D l m,
 Incid A l ->
 Incid B l ->
 Incid C m ->
 Incid D m ->
 Incid B m ->
 l <> m ->
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 B = inter (line A B) (line C D).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma on_inter_points_wd_spec_3 : forall A B C D l m,
 Incid A l ->
 Incid B l ->
 Incid C m ->
 Incid D m ->
 Incid C l ->
 l <> m ->
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 C = inter (line A B) (line C D).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma on_inter_points_wd_spec_4 : forall A B C D l m,
 Incid A l ->
 Incid B l ->
 Incid C m ->
 Incid D m ->
 Incid D l ->
 l <> m ->
 A <> B ->
 C <> D ->
 D = inter (line A B) (line C D).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma not_eq_sym_point : forall A B : Point, A<>B -> B<>A.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma not_eq_sym_line : forall A B : Line, A<>B -> B<>A.
Proof.
Admitted.

Ltac assumption_or_sym := 
  assumption || 
  (apply not_eq_sym_point;assumption) || 
  (apply not_eq_sym_line;assumption).

Ltac assumptions_or_sym := repeat split;try assumption_or_sym.

Ltac remove_inter_points_occ := repeat (match goal with

HA: Incid ?A ?l, 
HB: Incid ?B ?l, 
HC: Incid ?C ?m, 
HD: Incid ?D ?m,
HP1 : Incid ?P ?l,
HP2 : Incid ?P ?m |- context[inter (line ?A ?B) (line ?C ?D)] =>
rewrite <- (on_inter_points_wd A B C D P l m) in *; try assumption_or_sym

| HA: Incid ?A ?l, 
HB: Incid ?B ?l, 
HC: Incid ?C ?m, 
HD: Incid ?D ?m,
HP2 : Incid ?A ?m |- context[inter (line ?A ?B) (line ?C ?D)] =>
rewrite <- (on_inter_points_wd_spec_1 A B C D l m) in *; try assumption_or_sym

| HA: Incid ?A ?l, 
HB: Incid ?B ?l, 
HC: Incid ?C ?m, 
HD: Incid ?D ?m,
HP2 : Incid ?B ?m |- context[inter (line ?A ?B) (line ?C ?D)] =>
rewrite <- (on_inter_points_wd_spec_2 A B C D l m) in *; try assumption_or_sym

| HA: Incid ?A ?l, 
HB: Incid ?B ?l, 
HC: Incid ?C ?m, 
HD: Incid ?D ?m,
HP2 : Incid ?C ?l |- context[inter (line ?A ?B) (line ?C ?D)] =>
rewrite <- (on_inter_points_wd_spec_3 A B C D l m) in *; try assumption_or_sym

| HA: Incid ?A ?l, 
HB: Incid ?B ?l, 
HC: Incid ?C ?m, 
HD: Incid ?D ?m,
HP2 : Incid ?D ?l |- context[inter (line ?A ?B) (line ?C ?D)] =>
rewrite <- (on_inter_points_wd_spec_4 A B C D l m) in *; try assumption_or_sym

| 

HA: Incid ?A ?l, 
HB: Incid ?B ?l, 
HC: Incid ?C ?m, 
HD: Incid ?D ?m,
HP1 : Incid ?P ?l,
HP2 : Incid ?P ?m , 
H: context[inter (line ?A ?B) (line ?C ?D)] |- _ =>
rewrite <- (on_inter_points_wd A B C D P l m) in H; try assumption_or_sym

| HA: Incid ?A ?l, 
HB: Incid ?B ?l, 
HC: Incid ?C ?m, 
HD: Incid ?D ?m,
HP2 : Incid ?A ?m,

  line B C' <> line B' C /\ B<>C' /\ B'<>C /\

 is_on_inter P A B' A' B ->
 is_on_inter Q B C' B' C ->
 is_on_inter R A C' A' C ->
 Col P Q R.

and that the intersection are all well defined. This implies also that the line AB and A'B'
are distinct. This is the figure without any particular case. *)

Definition pappus_weak :=

 is_on_proper_inter Q B C' B' C ->
 is_on_proper_inter R A C' A' C ->
