title: 028_pascal_s_hexagon_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Pascal's Hexagon Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 028.
  In the real affine plane, it states that six points on an arbitrary nonzero quadratic
  conic determine three collinear opposite-side intersection points, under the stated
  mixed-triple noncollinearity conditions. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory Pascal_Hexagon_Theorem
  imports Complex_Main
begin

type_synonym affine_point = "real \<times> real"

definition affine_conic :: "affine_point set \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "affine_conic con \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<exists>a b c d e f :: real.
      \<not> (a = 0 \<and> b = 0 \<and> c = 0 \<and> d = 0 \<and> e = 0 \<and> f = 0) \<and>
      con = {x.
        a * (fst x) ^ 2 + b * (snd x) ^ 2 + c * fst x * snd x +
        d * fst x + e * snd x + f = 0})"

definition collinear_points :: "affine_point \<Rightarrow> affine_point \<Rightarrow> affine_point \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "collinear_points a b c \<longleftrightarrow>
    (fst b - fst a) * (snd c - snd a) =
    (snd b - snd a) * (fst c - fst a)"

theorem pascal_affine:
  fixes con :: "affine_point set"
    and x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 x8 x9 :: affine_point
  assumes mixed_triples_noncollinear:
      "\<not> collinear_points x1 x2 x4"
      "\<not> collinear_points x1 x2 x5"
      "\<not> collinear_points x1 x2 x6"
      "\<not> collinear_points x1 x3 x4"
      "\<not> collinear_points x1 x3 x5"
      "\<not> collinear_points x1 x3 x6"
      "\<not> collinear_points x2 x3 x4"
      "\<not> collinear_points x2 x3 x5"
      "\<not> collinear_points x2 x3 x6"
      "\<not> collinear_points x4 x5 x1"
      "\<not> collinear_points x4 x5 x2"
      "\<not> collinear_points x4 x5 x3"
      "\<not> collinear_points x4 x6 x1"
      "\<not> collinear_points x4 x6 x2"
      "\<not> collinear_points x4 x6 x3"
      "\<not> collinear_points x5 x6 x1"
      "\<not> collinear_points x5 x6 x2"
      "\<not> collinear_points x5 x6 x3"
    and conic_configuration:
      "affine_conic con"
      "x1 \<in> con"
      "x2 \<in> con"
      "x3 \<in> con"
      "x4 \<in> con"
      "x5 \<in> con"
      "x6 \<in> con"
    and opposite_side_intersections:
      "collinear_points x1 x9 x5"
      "collinear_points x1 x8 x6"
      "collinear_points x2 x9 x4"
      "collinear_points x2 x7 x6"
      "collinear_points x3 x8 x4"
      "collinear_points x3 x7 x5"
  shows "collinear_points x7 x8 x9"
  sorry

end

title: 028_pascal_s_hexagon_theorem
content:
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* Pascal's hexagon theorem for projective and affine planes.                *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

needs "Multivariate/cross.ml";;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* A lemma we want to justify some of the axioms.                            *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let NORMAL_EXISTS = `!u v:real^3. ?w. ~(w = vec 0) /\ orthogonal u w /\ orthogonal v w`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Type of directions.                                                       *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let direction_tybij = new_type_definition "direction" ("mk_dir","dest_dir")
 (MESON[BASIS_NONZERO; LE_REFL; DIMINDEX_GE_1] `?x:real^3. ~(x = vec 0)`);;

parse_as_infix("||",(11,"right"));;
parse_as_infix("_|_",(11,"right"));;

let perpdir = new_definition
 `x _|_ y <=> orthogonal (dest_dir x) (dest_dir y)`;;

let pardir = new_definition
 `x || y <=> (dest_dir x) cross (dest_dir y) = vec 0`;;

let DIRECTION_CLAUSES = `((!x. P(dest_dir x)) <=> (!x. ~(x = vec 0) ==> P x)) /\
   ((?x. P(dest_dir x)) <=> (?x. ~(x = vec 0) /\ P x))`;;

let [PARDIR_REFL; PARDIR_SYM; PARDIR_TRANS] = (CONJUNCTS o prove)
 (`(!x. x || x) /\
   (!x y. x || y <=> y || x) /\
   (!x y z. x || y /\ y || z ==> x || z)`,
  REWRITE_TAC[pardir; DIRECTION_CLAUSES] THEN VEC3_TAC);;

let PARDIR_EQUIV = `!x y. ((||) x = (||) y) <=> x || y`;;

let DIRECTION_AXIOM_1 = `!p p'. ~(p || p') ==> ?l. p _|_ l /\ p' _|_ l /\
                             !l'. p _|_ l' /\ p' _|_ l' ==> l' || l`;;

let DIRECTION_AXIOM_2 = `!l l'. ?p. p _|_ l /\ p _|_ l'`;;

let DIRECTION_AXIOM_3 = `?p p' p''.
        ~(p || p') /\ ~(p' || p'') /\ ~(p || p'') /\
        ~(?l. p _|_ l /\ p' _|_ l /\ p'' _|_ l)`;;

let DIRECTION_AXIOM_4_WEAK = `!l. ?p p'. ~(p || p') /\ p _|_ l /\ p' _|_ l`;;

let ORTHOGONAL_COMBINE = `!x a b. a _|_ x /\ b _|_ x /\ ~(a || b)
           ==> ?c. c _|_ x /\ ~(a || c) /\ ~(b || c)`;;

let DIRECTION_AXIOM_4 = `!l. ?p p' p''. ~(p || p') /\ ~(p' || p'') /\ ~(p || p'') /\
                  p _|_ l /\ p' _|_ l /\ p'' _|_ l`;;

let line_tybij = define_quotient_type "line" ("mk_line","dest_line") `(||)`;;

let PERPDIR_WELLDEF = `!x y x' y'. x || x' /\ y || y' ==> (x _|_ y <=> x' _|_ y')`;;

let perpl,perpl_th =
  lift_function (snd line_tybij) (PARDIR_REFL,PARDIR_TRANS)
                "perpl" PERPDIR_WELLDEF;;

let line_lift_thm = lift_theorem line_tybij
 (PARDIR_REFL,PARDIR_SYM,PARDIR_TRANS) [perpl_th];;

let LINE_AXIOM_1 = line_lift_thm DIRECTION_AXIOM_1;;
let LINE_AXIOM_2 = line_lift_thm DIRECTION_AXIOM_2;;
let LINE_AXIOM_3 = line_lift_thm DIRECTION_AXIOM_3;;
let LINE_AXIOM_4 = line_lift_thm DIRECTION_AXIOM_4;;

let point_tybij = new_type_definition "point" ("mk_point","dest_point")
 (prove(`?x:line. T`,REWRITE_TAC[]));;

parse_as_infix("on",(11,"right"));;

let on = new_definition `p on l <=> perpl (dest_point p) l`;;

let POINT_CLAUSES = `((p = p') <=> (dest_point p = dest_point p')) /\
   ((!p. P (dest_point p)) <=> (!l. P l)) /\
   ((?p. P (dest_point p)) <=> (?l. P l))`;;

let POINT_TAC th = REWRITE_TAC[on; POINT_CLAUSES] THEN ACCEPT_TAC th;;

let AXIOM_1 = `!p p'. ~(p = p') ==> ?l. p on l /\ p' on l /\
          !l'. p on l' /\ p' on l' ==> (l' = l)`;;

let AXIOM_2 = `!l l'. ?p. p on l /\ p on l'`;;

let AXIOM_3 = `?p p' p''. ~(p = p') /\ ~(p' = p'') /\ ~(p = p'') /\
    ~(?l. p on l /\ p' on l /\ p'' on l)`;;

let AXIOM_4 = `!l. ?p p' p''. ~(p = p') /\ ~(p' = p'') /\ ~(p = p'') /\
    p on l /\ p' on l /\ p'' on l`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Mappings from vectors in R^3 to projective lines and points.              *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let projl = new_definition
 `projl x = mk_line((||) (mk_dir x))`;;

let projp = new_definition
 `projp x = mk_point(projl x)`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Mappings in the other direction, to (some) homogeneous coordinates.       *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let PROJL_TOTAL = `!l. ?x. ~(x = vec 0) /\ l = projl x`;;

let homol = new_specification ["homol"]
  (REWRITE_RULE[SKOLEM_THM] PROJL_TOTAL);;

let PROJP_TOTAL = `!p. ?x. ~(x = vec 0) /\ p = projp x`;;

let homop_def = new_definition
 `homop p = homol(dest_point p)`;;

let homop = `!p. ~(homop p = vec 0) /\ p = projp(homop p)`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Key equivalences of concepts in projective space and homogeneous coords.  *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let parallel = new_definition
 `parallel x y <=> x cross y = vec 0`;;

let ON_HOMOL = `!p l. p on l <=> orthogonal (homop p) (homol l)`;;

let EQ_HOMOL = `!l l'. l = l' <=> parallel (homol l) (homol l')`;;

let EQ_HOMOP = `!p p'. p = p' <=> parallel (homop p) (homop p')`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* A "welldefinedness" result for homogeneous coordinate map.                *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let PARALLEL_PROJL_HOMOL = `!x. parallel x (homol(projl x))`;;

let PARALLEL_PROJP_HOMOP = `!x. parallel x (homop(projp x))`;;

let PARALLEL_PROJP_HOMOP_EXPLICIT = `!x. ~(x = vec 0) ==> ?a. ~(a = &0) /\ homop(projp x) = a % x`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Brackets, collinearity and their connection.                              *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bracket = define
 `bracket[a;b;c] = det(vector[homop a;homop b;homop c])`;;

let COLLINEAR = new_definition
 `COLLINEAR s <=> ?l. !p. p IN s ==> p on l`;;

let COLLINEAR_SINGLETON = `!a. COLLINEAR {a}`;;

let COLLINEAR_PAIR = `!a b. COLLINEAR{a,b}`;;

let COLLINEAR_TRIPLE = `!a b c. COLLINEAR{a,b,c} <=> ?l. a on l /\ b on l /\ c on l`;;

let COLLINEAR_BRACKET = `!p1 p2 p3. COLLINEAR {p1,p2,p3} <=> bracket[p1;p2;p3] = &0`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Conics and bracket condition for 6 points to be on a conic.               *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let homogeneous_conic = new_definition
 `homogeneous_conic con <=>
    ?a b c d e f.
       ~(a = &0 /\ b = &0 /\ c = &0 /\ d = &0 /\ e = &0 /\ f = &0) /\
       con = {x:real^3 | a * x$1 pow 2 + b * x$2 pow 2 + c * x$3 pow 2 +
                         d * x$1 * x$2 + e * x$1 * x$3 + f * x$2 * x$3 = &0}`;;

let projective_conic = new_definition
 `projective_conic con <=>
        ?c. homogeneous_conic c /\ con = {p | (homop p) IN c}`;;

let HOMOGENEOUS_CONIC_BRACKET = `!con x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6.
        homogeneous_conic con /\
        x1 IN con /\ x2 IN con /\ x3 IN con /\
        x4 IN con /\ x5 IN con /\ x6 IN con
        ==> det(vector[x6;x1;x4]) * det(vector[x6;x2;x3]) *
            det(vector[x5;x1;x3]) * det(vector[x5;x2;x4]) =
            det(vector[x6;x1;x3]) * det(vector[x6;x2;x4]) *
            det(vector[x5;x1;x4]) * det(vector[x5;x2;x3])`;;

let PROJECTIVE_CONIC_BRACKET = `!con p1 p2 p3 p4 p5 p6.
        projective_conic con /\
        p1 IN con /\ p2 IN con /\ p3 IN con /\
        p4 IN con /\ p5 IN con /\ p6 IN con
        ==> bracket[p6;p1;p4] * bracket[p6;p2;p3] *
            bracket[p5;p1;p3] * bracket[p5;p2;p4] =
            bracket[p6;p1;p3] * bracket[p6;p2;p4] *
            bracket[p5;p1;p4] * bracket[p5;p2;p3]`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Pascal's theorem with all the nondegeneracy principles we use directly.   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let PASCAL_DIRECT = `!con x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x6 x8 x9.
        ~COLLINEAR {x2,x5,x7} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x2,x5} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x3,x6} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x2,x4,x6} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x3,x4,x5} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x5,x7} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x2,x5,x9} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x2,x6} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x3,x6,x8} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x2,x4,x5} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x2,x4,x7} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x2,x6,x8} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x3,x4,x6} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x3,x5,x8} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x3,x5}
        ==> projective_conic con /\
            x1 IN con /\ x2 IN con /\ x3 IN con /\
            x4 IN con /\ x5 IN con /\ x6 IN con /\
            COLLINEAR {x1,x9,x5} /\
            COLLINEAR {x1,x8,x6} /\
            COLLINEAR {x2,x9,x4} /\
            COLLINEAR {x2,x7,x6} /\
            COLLINEAR {x3,x8,x4} /\
            COLLINEAR {x3,x7,x5}
            ==> COLLINEAR {x7,x8,x9}`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* With longer but more intuitive non-degeneracy conditions, basically that  *)
(* the 6 points divide into two groups of 3 and no 3 are collinear unless    *)
(* they are all in the same group.                                           *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let PASCAL = `!con x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x6 x8 x9.
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x2,x4} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x2,x5} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x2,x6} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x3,x4} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x3,x5} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x1,x3,x6} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x2,x3,x4} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x2,x3,x5} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x2,x3,x6} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x4,x5,x1} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x4,x5,x2} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x4,x5,x3} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x4,x6,x1} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x4,x6,x2} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x4,x6,x3} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x5,x6,x1} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x5,x6,x2} /\
        ~COLLINEAR {x5,x6,x3}
        ==> projective_conic con /\
            x1 IN con /\ x2 IN con /\ x3 IN con /\
            x4 IN con /\ x5 IN con /\ x6 IN con /\
            COLLINEAR {x1,x9,x5} /\
            COLLINEAR {x1,x8,x6} /\
            COLLINEAR {x2,x9,x4} /\
            COLLINEAR {x2,x7,x6} /\
            COLLINEAR {x3,x8,x4} /\
            COLLINEAR {x3,x7,x5}
            ==> COLLINEAR {x7,x8,x9}`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Homogenization and hence mapping from affine to projective plane.         *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let homogenize = new_definition
 `(homogenize:real^2->real^3) x = vector[x$1; x$2; &1]`;;

let projectivize = new_definition
 `projectivize = projp o homogenize`;;

let HOMOGENIZE_NONZERO = `!x. ~(homogenize x = vec 0)`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Conic in affine plane.                                                    *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let affine_conic = new_definition
 `affine_conic con <=>
    ?a b c d e f.
       ~(a = &0 /\ b = &0 /\ c = &0 /\ d = &0 /\ e = &0 /\ f = &0) /\
       con = {x:real^2 | a * x$1 pow 2 + b * x$2 pow 2 + c * x$1 * x$2 +
                         d * x$1 + e * x$2 + f = &0}`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Relationships between affine and projective notions.                      *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let COLLINEAR_PROJECTIVIZE = `!a b c. collinear{a,b,c} <=>
           COLLINEAR{projectivize a,projectivize b,projectivize c}`;;

let AFFINE_PROJECTIVE_CONIC = `!con. affine_conic con <=> ?con'. projective_conic con' /\
                                     con = {x | projectivize x IN con'}`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Hence Pascal's theorem for the affine plane.                              *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let PASCAL_AFFINE = `!con x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 x8 x9:real^2.
        ~collinear {x1,x2,x4} /\
        ~collinear {x1,x2,x5} /\
        ~collinear {x1,x2,x6} /\
        ~collinear {x1,x3,x4} /\
        ~collinear {x1,x3,x5} /\
        ~collinear {x1,x3,x6} /\
        ~collinear {x2,x3,x4} /\
        ~collinear {x2,x3,x5} /\
        ~collinear {x2,x3,x6} /\
        ~collinear {x4,x5,x1} /\
        ~collinear {x4,x5,x2} /\
        ~collinear {x4,x5,x3} /\
        ~collinear {x4,x6,x1} /\
        ~collinear {x4,x6,x2} /\
        ~collinear {x4,x6,x3} /\
        ~collinear {x5,x6,x1} /\
        ~collinear {x5,x6,x2} /\
        ~collinear {x5,x6,x3}
        ==> affine_conic con /\
            x1 IN con /\ x2 IN con /\ x3 IN con /\
            x4 IN con /\ x5 IN con /\ x6 IN con /\
            collinear {x1,x9,x5} /\
            collinear {x1,x8,x6} /\
            collinear {x2,x9,x4} /\
            collinear {x2,x7,x6} /\
            collinear {x3,x8,x4} /\
            collinear {x3,x7,x5}
            ==> collinear {x7,x8,x9}`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Special case of a circle where nondegeneracy is simpler.                  *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let COLLINEAR_NOT_COCIRCULAR = `!r c x y z:real^2.
        dist(c,x) = r /\ dist(c,y) = r /\ dist(c,z) = r /\
        ~(x = y) /\ ~(x = z) /\ ~(y = z)
        ==> ~collinear {x,y,z}`;;

let PASCAL_AFFINE_CIRCLE = `!c r x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 x8 x9:real^2.
        PAIRWISE (\x y. ~(x = y)) [x1;x2;x3;x4;x5;x6] /\
        dist(c,x1) = r /\ dist(c,x2) = r /\ dist(c,x3) = r /\
        dist(c,x4) = r /\ dist(c,x5) = r /\ dist(c,x6) = r /\
        collinear {x1,x9,x5} /\
        collinear {x1,x8,x6} /\
        collinear {x2,x9,x4} /\
        collinear {x2,x7,x6} /\
        collinear {x3,x8,x4} /\
        collinear {x3,x7,x5}
        ==> collinear {x7,x8,x9}`;;

title: 028_pascal_s_hexagon_theorem
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems__acl2__028,
;; "Pascal's Hexagon Theorem": six nondegenerate points on an affine conic
;; determine three collinear opposite-side intersections. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; ACL2 has no native abstract field type. These conservative function symbols
;; represent an arbitrary scalar carrier and its operations. The explicit field
;; hypotheses below expose all algebraic assumptions; no geometric conclusion
;; is installed as an axiom. Pascal's theorem is purely field-theoretic, so
;; stating it over an arbitrary commutative field is a conservative
;; generalization of the real affine-plane source.

(defstub ht028-scalar-member-p (scalar-type value) t)
(defstub ht028-zero (scalar-type) t)
(defstub ht028-one (scalar-type) t)
(defstub ht028-add (scalar-type left right) t)
(defstub ht028-multiply (scalar-type left right) t)
(defstub ht028-negate (scalar-type value) t)
(defstub ht028-inverse (scalar-type value) t)

(defun-sk ht028-field-laws-p (scalar-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type x)
      (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type y)
      (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type z))
     (let ((zero (ht028-zero scalar-type))
           (one (ht028-one scalar-type)))
       (and
        (ht028-scalar-member-p
         scalar-type (ht028-add scalar-type x y))
        (ht028-scalar-member-p
         scalar-type (ht028-multiply scalar-type x y))
        (ht028-scalar-member-p
         scalar-type (ht028-negate scalar-type x))
        (ht028-scalar-member-p
         scalar-type (ht028-inverse scalar-type x))

        (equal
         (ht028-add scalar-type x y)
         (ht028-add scalar-type y x))
        (equal
         (ht028-add
          scalar-type (ht028-add scalar-type x y) z)
         (ht028-add
          scalar-type x (ht028-add scalar-type y z)))
        (equal (ht028-add scalar-type x zero) x)
        (equal
         (ht028-add scalar-type x (ht028-negate scalar-type x))
         zero)

        (equal
         (ht028-multiply scalar-type x y)
         (ht028-multiply scalar-type y x))
        (equal
         (ht028-multiply
          scalar-type (ht028-multiply scalar-type x y) z)
         (ht028-multiply
          scalar-type x (ht028-multiply scalar-type y z)))
        (equal (ht028-multiply scalar-type x one) x)
        (equal (ht028-multiply scalar-type x zero) zero)
        (equal
         (ht028-multiply
          scalar-type x (ht028-add scalar-type y z))
         (ht028-add
          scalar-type
          (ht028-multiply scalar-type x y)
          (ht028-multiply scalar-type x z)))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal
          (ht028-multiply
           scalar-type x (ht028-inverse scalar-type x))
          one)))))))

(defun ht028-field-p (scalar-type)
  (and
   (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type (ht028-zero scalar-type))
   (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type (ht028-one scalar-type))
   (not
    (equal
     (ht028-zero scalar-type)
     (ht028-one scalar-type)))
   (ht028-field-laws-p scalar-type)))

;; Points are pairs of scalar coordinates. The source's type discipline becomes
;; explicit carrier checks in ACL2's untyped logic.

(defun ht028-point-p (scalar-type point)
  (and
   (true-listp point)
   (equal (len point) 2)
   (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type (nth 0 point))
   (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type (nth 1 point))))

(defun ht028-point-x (point)
  (nth 0 point))

(defun ht028-point-y (point)
  (nth 1 point))

(defun ht028-subtract (scalar-type left right)
  (ht028-add scalar-type left (ht028-negate scalar-type right)))

(defun ht028-square (scalar-type value)
  (ht028-multiply scalar-type value value))

;; The determinant criterion is exactly affine collinearity.

(defun ht028-collinear-p (scalar-type first second third)
  (equal
   (ht028-multiply
    scalar-type
    (ht028-subtract
     scalar-type
     (ht028-point-x second)
     (ht028-point-x first))
    (ht028-subtract
     scalar-type
     (ht028-point-y third)
     (ht028-point-y first)))
   (ht028-multiply
    scalar-type
    (ht028-subtract
     scalar-type
     (ht028-point-y second)
     (ht028-point-y first))
    (ht028-subtract
     scalar-type
     (ht028-point-x third)
     (ht028-point-x first)))))

;; Evaluation of a*x^2 + b*y^2 + c*x*y + d*x + e*y + f.

(defun ht028-quadratic-value
    (scalar-type a b c d e f point)
  (ht028-add
   scalar-type
   (ht028-add
    scalar-type
    (ht028-add
     scalar-type
     (ht028-multiply
      scalar-type a
      (ht028-square scalar-type (ht028-point-x point)))
     (ht028-multiply
      scalar-type b
      (ht028-square scalar-type (ht028-point-y point))))
    (ht028-multiply
     scalar-type c
     (ht028-multiply
      scalar-type
      (ht028-point-x point)
      (ht028-point-y point))))
   (ht028-add
    scalar-type
    (ht028-multiply scalar-type d (ht028-point-x point))
    (ht028-add
     scalar-type
     (ht028-multiply scalar-type e (ht028-point-y point))
     f))))

(defun ht028-on-conic-p
    (scalar-type a b c d e f point)
  (equal
   (ht028-quadratic-value scalar-type a b c d e f point)
   (ht028-zero scalar-type)))

(defun ht028-nonzero-conic-p (scalar-type a b c d e f)
  (not
   (and
    (equal a (ht028-zero scalar-type))
    (equal b (ht028-zero scalar-type))
    (equal c (ht028-zero scalar-type))
    (equal d (ht028-zero scalar-type))
    (equal e (ht028-zero scalar-type))
    (equal f (ht028-zero scalar-type)))))

(defun ht028-pairwise-distinct-six-p
    (p1 p2 p3 p4 p5 p6)
  (and
   (not (equal p1 p2))
   (not (equal p1 p3))
   (not (equal p1 p4))
   (not (equal p1 p5))
   (not (equal p1 p6))
   (not (equal p2 p3))
   (not (equal p2 p4))
   (not (equal p2 p5))
   (not (equal p2 p6))
   (not (equal p3 p4))
   (not (equal p3 p5))
   (not (equal p3 p6))
   (not (equal p4 p5))
   (not (equal p4 p6))
   (not (equal p5 p6))))

;; No triple meeting both alternating vertex classes {p1,p3,p5} and
;; {p2,p4,p6} is collinear. This is the source's general-position condition,
;; not a replacement for the conic hypothesis.

(defun ht028-pascal-nondegenerate-p
    (scalar-type p1 p2 p3 p4 p5 p6)
  (and
   (ht028-pairwise-distinct-six-p p1 p2 p3 p4 p5 p6)
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p1 p3 p2))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p1 p3 p4))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p1 p3 p6))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p1 p5 p2))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p1 p5 p4))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p1 p5 p6))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p3 p5 p2))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p3 p5 p4))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p3 p5 p6))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p2 p4 p1))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p2 p4 p3))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p2 p4 p5))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p2 p6 p1))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p2 p6 p3))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p2 p6 p5))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p4 p6 p1))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p4 p6 p3))
   (not (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type p4 p6 p5))))

(defun ht028-pascal-intersections-p
    (scalar-type p1 p2 p3 p4 p5 p6 i1 i2 i3)
  (and
   (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type i1 p1 p2)
   (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type i1 p4 p5)
   (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type i2 p2 p3)
   (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type i2 p5 p6)
   (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type i3 p3 p4)
   (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type i3 p6 p1)))

(defun-sk hundred-theorems-028-pascal-hexagon-statement
    (scalar-type)
  (forall (a b c d e f p1 p2 p3 p4 p5 p6 i1 i2 i3)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht028-field-p scalar-type)
      (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type a)
      (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type b)
      (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type c)
      (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type d)
      (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type e)
      (ht028-scalar-member-p scalar-type f)
      (ht028-point-p scalar-type p1)
      (ht028-point-p scalar-type p2)
      (ht028-point-p scalar-type p3)
      (ht028-point-p scalar-type p4)
      (ht028-point-p scalar-type p5)
      (ht028-point-p scalar-type p6)
      (ht028-point-p scalar-type i1)
      (ht028-point-p scalar-type i2)
      (ht028-point-p scalar-type i3)
      (ht028-nonzero-conic-p scalar-type a b c d e f)
      (ht028-pascal-nondegenerate-p
       scalar-type p1 p2 p3 p4 p5 p6)
      (ht028-on-conic-p scalar-type a b c d e f p1)
      (ht028-on-conic-p scalar-type a b c d e f p2)
      (ht028-on-conic-p scalar-type a b c d e f p3)
      (ht028-on-conic-p scalar-type a b c d e f p4)
      (ht028-on-conic-p scalar-type a b c d e f p5)
      (ht028-on-conic-p scalar-type a b c d e f p6)
      (ht028-pascal-intersections-p
       scalar-type p1 p2 p3 p4 p5 p6 i1 i2 i3))
     (ht028-collinear-p scalar-type i1 i2 i3))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 028_pascal_s_hexagon_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Pascal's Hexagon Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 028.
-- It states the real affine conic theorem and the projective implication from
-- Pappus's property to the hexamy property.
-- This file contains no proof.

module HundredTheorems028 where

open import Agda.Primitive using (lzero; lsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not proposition = proposition -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
left != right = Not (left == right)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField (R : Set) : Set (lsuc lzero) where
  field
    zero one : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      one != zero

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zero == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zero

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x one == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zero == zero
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zero ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == one

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zero x ->
      lessOrEqual zero y ->
      lessOrEqual zero (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zero one and zero != one

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat Agda.Builtin.Nat.zero == zero
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) one
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum) and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

Collinear :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
Collinear reals a b c =
  multiply reals
    (subtract reals (x-coordinate b) (x-coordinate a))
    (subtract reals (y-coordinate c) (y-coordinate a))
  ==
  multiply reals
    (subtract reals (y-coordinate b) (y-coordinate a))
    (subtract reals (x-coordinate c) (x-coordinate a))

record AffineConic
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R) :
  Set where

  field
    x2-coefficient : R
    y2-coefficient : R
    xy-coefficient : R
    x-coefficient  : R
    y-coefficient  : R
    constant       : R

    nonzero-quadratic :
      Not
        (x2-coefficient == zero reals and
         y2-coefficient == zero reals and
         xy-coefficient == zero reals and
         x-coefficient == zero reals and
         y-coefficient == zero reals and
         constant == zero reals)

open AffineConic

OnConic :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R) ->
  AffineConic reals ->
  Point R ->
  Set
OnConic reals conic p =
  add reals
    (multiply reals
      (x2-coefficient conic)
      (square reals (x-coordinate p)))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (y2-coefficient conic)
        (square reals (y-coordinate p)))
      (add reals
        (multiply reals
          (xy-coefficient conic)
          (multiply reals (x-coordinate p) (y-coordinate p)))
        (add reals
          (multiply reals
            (x-coefficient conic)
            (x-coordinate p))
          (add reals
            (multiply reals
              (y-coefficient conic)
              (y-coordinate p))
            (constant conic)))))
  == zero reals

PascalNondegenerate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
PascalNondegenerate reals a b c d e f =
  Not (Collinear reals a c b) and
  Not (Collinear reals a c d) and
  Not (Collinear reals a c f) and
  Not (Collinear reals a e b) and
  Not (Collinear reals a e d) and
  Not (Collinear reals a e f) and
  Not (Collinear reals c e b) and
  Not (Collinear reals c e d) and
  Not (Collinear reals c e f) and
  Not (Collinear reals b d a) and
  Not (Collinear reals b d c) and
  Not (Collinear reals b d e) and
  Not (Collinear reals b f a) and
  Not (Collinear reals b f c) and
  Not (Collinear reals b f e) and
  Not (Collinear reals d f a) and
  Not (Collinear reals d f c) and
  Not (Collinear reals d f e)

PascalIntersections :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
PascalIntersections reals a b c d e f p q r =
  Collinear reals p a b and
  Collinear reals p d e and
  Collinear reals q b c and
  Collinear reals q e f and
  Collinear reals r c d and
  Collinear reals r f a

module AffinePascalStatement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (conic : AffineConic reals) ->
    (a b c d e f p q r : Point R) ->
    PascalNondegenerate reals a b c d e f ->
    OnConic reals conic a ->
    OnConic reals conic b ->
    OnConic reals conic c ->
    OnConic reals conic d ->
    OnConic reals conic e ->
    OnConic reals conic f ->
    PascalIntersections reals a b c d e f p q r ->
    Collinear reals p q r

pascals-hexagon-theorem : Set (lsuc lzero)
pascals-hexagon-theorem =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R) ->
  AffinePascalStatement.proposition reals

record ProjectivePlane (P L : Set) : Set (lsuc lzero) where
  field
    incident : P -> L -> Set
    join     : P -> P -> L
    meet     : L -> L -> P

    join-left :
      (a b : P) ->
      incident a (join a b)
    join-right :
      (a b : P) ->
      incident b (join a b)
    meet-left :
      (l m : L) ->
      incident (meet l m) l
    meet-right :
      (l m : L) ->
      incident (meet l m) m

    join-unique :
      (a b : P) ->
      a != b ->
      (l : L) ->
      incident a l ->
      incident b l ->
      l == join a b
    meet-unique :
      (l m : L) ->
      l != m ->
      (p : P) ->
      incident p l ->
      incident p m ->
      p == meet l m

    noncollinear-points :
      Exists P
        (\ a ->
          Exists P
            (\ b ->
              Exists P
                (\ c ->
                  a != b and
                  b != c and
                  a != c and
                  Not
                    (Exists L
                      (\ l ->
                        incident a l and
                        incident b l and
                        incident c l)))))

    three-points-on-line :
      (l : L) ->
      Exists P
        (\ a ->
          Exists P
            (\ b ->
              Exists P
                (\ c ->
                  a != b and
                  b != c and
                  a != c and
                  incident a l and
                  incident b l and
                  incident c l)))

open ProjectivePlane

ProjectiveCollinear :
  {P L : Set} ->
  ProjectivePlane P L ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  Set
ProjectiveCollinear plane a b c =
  Exists _
    (\ l ->
      incident plane a l and
      incident plane b l and
      incident plane c l)

DistinctSix :
  {A : Set} ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set
DistinctSix a b c d e f =
  a != b and
  a != c and
  a != d and
  a != e and
  a != f and
  b != c and
  b != d and
  b != e and
  b != f and
  c != d and
  c != e and
  c != f and
  d != e and
  d != f and
  e != f

OnIntersection :
  {P L : Set} ->
  ProjectivePlane P L ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  Set
OnIntersection plane p a b c d =
  ProjectiveCollinear plane p a b and
  ProjectiveCollinear plane p c d

HexamyConfiguration :
  {P L : Set} ->
  ProjectivePlane P L ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  Set
HexamyConfiguration plane a b c d e f =
  DistinctSix a b c d e f and
  ProjectiveCollinear plane
    (meet plane (join plane b c) (join plane e f))
    (meet plane (join plane c d) (join plane f a))
    (meet plane (join plane a b) (join plane d e))

HexamyProperty :
  {P L : Set} ->
  ProjectivePlane P L ->
  Set
HexamyProperty {P} plane =
  (a b c d e f : P) ->
  HexamyConfiguration plane a b c d e f ->
  HexamyConfiguration plane b a c d e f

PappusRegular :
  {P L : Set} ->
  ProjectivePlane P L ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  P ->
  Set
PappusRegular plane a b c a-prime b-prime c-prime =
  join plane a b-prime != join plane a-prime b and
  a != b-prime and
  a-prime != b and
  join plane b c-prime != join plane b-prime c and
  b != c-prime and
  b-prime != c and
  join plane a c-prime != join plane a-prime c and
  a != c-prime and
  a-prime != c

PappusStrong :
  {P L : Set} ->
  ProjectivePlane P L ->
  Set
PappusStrong {P} plane =
  (a b c a-prime b-prime c-prime p q r : P) ->
  (DistinctSix a b c a-prime b-prime c-prime or
   PappusRegular plane a b c a-prime b-prime c-prime) ->
  ProjectiveCollinear plane a b c ->
  ProjectiveCollinear plane a-prime b-prime c-prime ->
  OnIntersection plane p a b-prime a-prime b ->
  OnIntersection plane q b c-prime b-prime c ->
  OnIntersection plane r a c-prime a-prime c ->
  ProjectiveCollinear plane p q r

PappusImpliesHexamy :
  {P L : Set} ->
  ProjectivePlane P L ->
  Set
PappusImpliesHexamy {P} plane =
  PappusStrong plane ->
  (a b c d e f : P) ->
  join plane c d != join plane a f ->
  join plane b c != join plane e f ->
  join plane a b != join plane d e ->
  join plane a c != join plane e f ->
  join plane b f != join plane c d ->
  HexamyConfiguration plane a b c d e f ->
  HexamyConfiguration plane b a c d e f

rocq-pappus-implies-hexamy : Set (lsuc lzero)
rocq-pappus-implies-hexamy =
  (P L : Set) ->
  (plane : ProjectivePlane P L) ->
  PappusImpliesHexamy plane

title: 028_pascal_s_hexagon_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Pascal's Hexagon Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 028.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

(*
  Hundred Theorems item 028, "Pascal's Hexagon Theorem": six suitably nondegenerate affine
  points on a conic determine three collinear intersections of opposite sides. This is a
  statement-only formalization and contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pairTheory realTheory;

val pascals_hexagon_theorem =
  ``let collinear =
      \P Q R : real # real.
        (FST P - FST Q) * (SND R - SND Q) =
        (SND P - SND Q) * (FST R - FST Q)
    in
      !a b c d e f : real.
      !x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 x8 x9 : real # real.
        let on_conic =
          \P : real # real.
            a * ((FST P) pow 2) + b * ((SND P) pow 2) +
            c * FST P * SND P + d * FST P + e * SND P + f = 0
        in
          ~(a = 0 /\ b = 0 /\ c = 0 /\ d = 0 /\ e = 0 /\ f = 0) /\
          ~collinear x1 x2 x4 /\
          ~collinear x1 x2 x5 /\
          ~collinear x1 x2 x6 /\
          ~collinear x1 x3 x4 /\
          ~collinear x1 x3 x5 /\
          ~collinear x1 x3 x6 /\
          ~collinear x2 x3 x4 /\
          ~collinear x2 x3 x5 /\
          ~collinear x2 x3 x6 /\
          ~collinear x4 x5 x1 /\
          ~collinear x4 x5 x2 /\
          ~collinear x4 x5 x3 /\
          ~collinear x4 x6 x1 /\
          ~collinear x4 x6 x2 /\
          ~collinear x4 x6 x3 /\
          ~collinear x5 x6 x1 /\
          ~collinear x5 x6 x2 /\
          ~collinear x5 x6 x3
          ==>
          on_conic x1 /\ on_conic x2 /\ on_conic x3 /\
          on_conic x4 /\ on_conic x5 /\ on_conic x6 /\
          collinear x1 x9 x5 /\
          collinear x1 x8 x6 /\
          collinear x2 x9 x4 /\
          collinear x2 x7 x6 /\
          collinear x3 x8 x4 /\
          collinear x3 x7 x5
          ==>
          collinear x7 x8 x9``;

title: 028_pascal_s_hexagon_theorem
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Pascal's Hexagon Theorem" from Hundred
  Theorems item 028: Pascal collinearity for conics in the real projective
  and affine planes, its circle specialization, and the abstract
  projective-plane Pappus-to-hexamy formulation. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The HOL Light domains are represented definitionally in set.mm.

  HT028R2 is RR X. RR. HT028R3 is RR X. ( RR X. RR ). A real projective
  point is an equivalence class of nonzero triples under multiplication by a
  nonzero real scalar. Projective collinearity is vanishing of the 3 by 3
  determinant for representatives, and affine/projective conics are exactly
  zero sets of nonzero real quadratic forms.

  For the Rocq formulation, P and L are explicit point and line carriers, I
  is an incidence relation, J chooses a line through two points, and N chooses
  an intersection point of two lines. HT028Plane states the projective-plane
  existence, uniqueness, and nondegeneracy laws and specifies both choices.

  The malformed HOL Light projective binder repeats x6 and leaves x7 free.
  The projective assertion below binds the seventh point, as required by its
  occurrences and by the correctly bound affine assertion.

  All final theorem declarations are unproved $a statements.
$)

$c
  HT028R2 HT028R3 HT028X HT028Y HT028PY HT028Z HT028Scale HT028HClass
  HT028PPlane HT028Det HT028ACol HT028PCol HT028APoly HT028PPoly
  HT028AConic HT028PConic HT028Circle HT028Distinct6 HT028AND
  HT028PND HT028AConfig HT028PConfig HT028Inc HT028AbsCol
  HT028Plane HT028OnInter HT028Hex HT028Pappus
$.

ht028-r3-syntax $a class HT028R3 $.
ht028-x-syntax $a class ( HT028X A ) $.
ht028-y-syntax $a class ( HT028Y A ) $.

ht028-ppoly-syntax $a class ( HT028PPoly A B C D E F G ) $.

  $a wff ( HT028AConfig A B C D E F G H I J ) $.

ht028-r2-definition $a |- HT028R2 = ( RR X. RR ) $.

ht028-r3-definition $a |- HT028R3 = ( RR X. ( RR X. RR ) ) $.

ht028-x-definition $a |- ( HT028X A ) = ( 1st ` A ) $.

ht028-y-definition $a |- ( HT028Y A ) = ( 2nd ` A ) $.

ht028-py-definition $a |- ( HT028PY A ) = ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` A ) ) $.

  <.
    ( A x. ( HT028X B ) )
    ,
    <.
      ( A x. ( HT028PY B ) )

    >.

$.

${
  $d A b k $.
  ht028-hclass-definition $a |- ( HT028HClass A ) =

$}

${
  $d a b $.
  ht028-pplane-definition $a |- HT028PPlane =
    { a |
      E. b e. HT028R3
        (

ht028-det-definition $a |- ( HT028Det A B C ) =
  (
    (
      ( HT028X A )
      x.
      (
        (
          ( HT028PY B ) x. ( HT028Z C )
        )

        ( HT028PY B ) x. ( HT028X C )

$.

ht028-affine-collinearity-definition $a |- (
  ( HT028ACol A B C )
  <->
  (
    (
      (
        ( HT028X B ) - ( HT028X A )

      x.
      (
        ( HT028Y C ) - ( HT028Y A )

        ( HT028Y B ) - ( HT028Y A )

      (
        ( HT028X C ) - ( HT028X A )

${
  $d A B C p q r $.
  ht028-projective-collinearity-definition $a |- (
    ( HT028PCol A B C )
    <->
    E. p e. A
    E. q e. B
    E. r e. C
      ( ( HT028Det p q r ) = 0 )

$}

ht028-affine-polynomial-definition $a |- (
  HT028APoly A B C D E F G
) =
  (
    (
      ( A x. ( ( HT028X G ) ^ 2 ) )
      +
      ( B x. ( ( HT028Y G ) ^ 2 ) )

    +
    (
      ( C x. ( ( HT028X G ) x. ( HT028Y G ) ) )

$.

ht028-projective-polynomial-definition $a |- (
  HT028PPoly A B C D E F G
) =
  (

      ( A x. ( ( HT028X G ) ^ 2 ) )
      +
      ( B x. ( ( HT028PY G ) ^ 2 ) )
    )
    +
    (
      ( C x. ( ( HT028Z G ) ^ 2 ) )
      +

          +

        )

    )

$.

${
  $d K a b c d e f p $.
  ht028-affine-conic-definition $a |- (
    ( HT028AConic K )
    <->
    E. a e. RR
    E. b e. RR
    E. c e. RR
    E. d e. RR
    E. e e. RR
    E. f e. RR
      (
        -.
        (
          a = 0
          /\
          (
            b = 0
            /\
            (
              c = 0
              /\
              (
                d = 0
                /\
                (
                  e = 0
                  /\

                )
              )
            )
          )
        )
        /\
        K =
        { p e. HT028R2 |
          ( HT028APoly a b c d e f p ) = 0
        }
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d K p a b c d e f v $.
  ht028-projective-conic-definition $a |- (
    ( HT028PConic K )
    <->
    E. a e. RR
    E. b e. RR
    E. c e. RR
    E. d e. RR
    E. e e. RR
    E. f e. RR
      (
        -.
        (
          a = 0
          /\
          (
            b = 0
            /\
            (
              c = 0
              /\
              (
                d = 0
                /\
                (
                  e = 0
                  /\
                  f = 0
                )
              )
            )
          )
        )
        /\
        K =
        { p e. HT028PPlane |
          E. v e. p
            ( HT028PPoly a b c d e f v ) = 0
        }
      )
  ) $.
$}

ht028-circle-definition $a |- (
  ( HT028Circle A B C )
  <->
  (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      (
        (
          ( HT028X B ) - ( HT028X A )
        )
        ^ 2
      )
      +
      (
        (
          ( HT028Y B ) - ( HT028Y A )
        )
        ^ 2
      )
    )
  )
  =
  C
) $.

ht028-distinct-six-definition $a |- (
  ( HT028Distinct6 A B C D E F )
  <->
  (
    A =/= B
    /\
    (
      A =/= C
      /\
      (
        A =/= D

title: 028_pascal_s_hexagon_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Pascal's Hexagon Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 028.
% In homogeneous coordinates for the real projective plane, six suitably nondegenerate
% points on one conic have collinear intersections of their three pairs of opposite sides.
% This file contains no proof.

pascal_s_hexagon_theorem_028: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE =
    [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real, z_coord: real #]

  projective_point(P: point): bool =
    NOT (x_coord(P) = 0 AND y_coord(P) = 0 AND z_coord(P) = 0)

  collinear(P, Q, R: point): bool =
    x_coord(P) *
        (y_coord(Q) * z_coord(R) - z_coord(Q) * y_coord(R))
      - y_coord(P) *
        (x_coord(Q) * z_coord(R) - z_coord(Q) * x_coord(R))
      + z_coord(P) *
        (x_coord(Q) * y_coord(R) - y_coord(Q) * x_coord(R))
      = 0

  nontrivial_conic(a, b, c, d, e, f: real): bool =
    NOT (a = 0 AND b = 0 AND c = 0
      AND d = 0 AND e = 0 AND f = 0)

  on_projective_conic(
      P: point, a, b, c, d, e, f: real): bool =
    a * x_coord(P) * x_coord(P)
      + b * y_coord(P) * y_coord(P)
      + c * z_coord(P) * z_coord(P)
      + d * x_coord(P) * y_coord(P)
      + e * x_coord(P) * z_coord(P)
      + f * y_coord(P) * z_coord(P)
      = 0

  on_same_projective_conic(
      x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6: point): bool =
    EXISTS (a, b, c, d, e, f: real):
      nontrivial_conic(a, b, c, d, e, f)
        AND on_projective_conic(x1, a, b, c, d, e, f)
        AND on_projective_conic(x2, a, b, c, d, e, f)
        AND on_projective_conic(x3, a, b, c, d, e, f)
        AND on_projective_conic(x4, a, b, c, d, e, f)
        AND on_projective_conic(x5, a, b, c, d, e, f)
        AND on_projective_conic(x6, a, b, c, d, e, f)

  pascal_nondegenerate(
      x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6: point): bool =
    NOT collinear(x1, x2, x4)
      AND NOT collinear(x1, x2, x5)
      AND NOT collinear(x1, x2, x6)
      AND NOT collinear(x1, x3, x4)
      AND NOT collinear(x1, x3, x5)
      AND NOT collinear(x1, x3, x6)
      AND NOT collinear(x2, x3, x4)
      AND NOT collinear(x2, x3, x5)
      AND NOT collinear(x2, x3, x6)
      AND NOT collinear(x4, x5, x1)
      AND NOT collinear(x4, x5, x2)
      AND NOT collinear(x4, x5, x3)
      AND NOT collinear(x4, x6, x1)
      AND NOT collinear(x4, x6, x2)
      AND NOT collinear(x4, x6, x3)
      AND NOT collinear(x5, x6, x1)
      AND NOT collinear(x5, x6, x2)
      AND NOT collinear(x5, x6, x3)

  on_both_lines(I, A, B, C, D: point): bool =
    collinear(A, I, B) AND collinear(C, I, D)

  pascal_intersection_configuration(
      x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7, x8, x9: point): bool =
    on_both_lines(x9, x1, x5, x2, x4)
      AND on_both_lines(x8, x1, x6, x3, x4)
      AND on_both_lines(x7, x2, x6, x3, x5)

  all_projective_points(
      x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7, x8, x9: point): bool =
    projective_point(x1)
      AND projective_point(x2)
      AND projective_point(x3)
      AND projective_point(x4)
      AND projective_point(x5)
      AND projective_point(x6)
      AND projective_point(x7)
      AND projective_point(x8)
      AND projective_point(x9)

  pascal_s_hexagon_theorem: bool =
    FORALL (x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7, x8, x9: point):
      (all_projective_points(x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7, x8, x9)
        AND on_same_projective_conic(x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6)
        AND pascal_nondegenerate(x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6)
        AND pascal_intersection_configuration(
          x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7, x8, x9))
      IMPLIES collinear(x7, x8, x9)
END pascal_s_hexagon_theorem_028

title: 029_feuerbach_s_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Feuerbach's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 029.
-- For a nondegenerate triangle, the nine-point circle is tangent to each inscribed or
-- escribed circle, expressed by equality of circles or a unique common point.
-- This file contains no proof.

namespace Theorems100.Feuerbach

universe u

/-- A Dedekind-complete linearly ordered field, used as a presentation of the real numbers. -/
structure RealScalar where
  Carrier : Type u
  zero : Carrier
  one : Carrier
  add : Carrier → Carrier → Carrier
  mul : Carrier → Carrier → Carrier
  neg : Carrier → Carrier
  inv : Carrier → Carrier
  le : Carrier → Carrier → Prop
  add_assoc : ∀ a b c, add (add a b) c = add a (add b c)
  add_comm : ∀ a b, add a b = add b a
  zero_add : ∀ a, add zero a = a
  add_neg : ∀ a, add (neg a) a = zero
  mul_assoc : ∀ a b c, mul (mul a b) c = mul a (mul b c)
  mul_comm : ∀ a b, mul a b = mul b a
  one_mul : ∀ a, mul one a = a
  left_distrib : ∀ a b c, mul a (add b c) = add (mul a b) (mul a c)
  zero_ne_one : zero ≠ one
  mul_inv : ∀ a, a ≠ zero → mul (inv a) a = one
  le_refl : ∀ a, le a a
  le_trans : ∀ a b c, le a b → le b c → le a c
  le_antisymm : ∀ a b, le a b → le b a → a = b
  le_total : ∀ a b, le a b ∨ le b a
  add_le_add_right : ∀ a b c, le a b → le (add a c) (add b c)
  mul_nonneg : ∀ a b, le zero a → le zero b → le zero (mul a b)
  complete :
    ∀ s : Carrier → Prop,
      (∃ x, s x) →
      (∃ upper, ∀ x, s x → le x upper) →
      ∃ leastUpper,
        (∀ x, s x → le x leastUpper) ∧
          ∀ upper, (∀ x, s x → le x upper) → le leastUpper upper

abbrev Real (K : RealScalar) := K.Carrier
abbrev Point (K : RealScalar) := Fin 2 → Real K

def sub (K : RealScalar) (x y : Real K) : Real K :=
  K.add x (K.neg y)

def sq (K : RealScalar) (x : Real K) : Real K :=
  K.mul x x

/-- Squared Euclidean distance between two points. -/
def distanceSq (K : RealScalar) (p q : Point K) : Real K :=
  K.add (sq K (sub K (q 0) (p 0))) (sq K (sub K (q 1) (p 1)))

/-- The point `m` is the midpoint of `a` and `b`. -/
def IsMidpoint (K : RealScalar) (a b m : Point K) : Prop :=
  K.mul (K.add K.one K.one) (m 0) = K.add (a 0) (b 0) ∧
    K.mul (K.add K.one K.one) (m 1) = K.add (a 1) (b 1)

/-- Three affine-plane points are collinear when their signed-area determinant vanishes. -/
def Collinear3 (K : RealScalar) (a b c : Point K) : Prop :=
  K.mul (sub K (a 0) (b 0)) (sub K (c 1) (b 1)) =
    K.mul (sub K (a 1) (b 1)) (sub K (c 0) (b 0))

/-- The directed lines `ab` and `cd` have perpendicular direction vectors. -/
def Perpendicular (K : RealScalar) (a b c d : Point K) : Prop :=
  K.add
      (K.mul (sub K (a 0) (b 0)) (sub K (c 0) (d 0)))
      (K.mul (sub K (a 1) (b 1)) (sub K (c 1) (d 1))) =
    K.zero

/-- A point lies on the circle with the given center and nonnegative radius. -/
def OnCircle (K : RealScalar) (center : Point K) (radius : Real K) (p : Point K) : Prop :=
  K.le K.zero radius ∧ distanceSq K center p = sq K radius

/-- Two circles are equal or meet at exactly one point. -/
def CirclesTangent (K : RealScalar)
    (center₁ : Point K) (radius₁ : Real K)
    (center₂ : Point K) (radius₂ : Real K) : Prop :=
  (center₁ = center₂ ∧ radius₁ = radius₂) ∨
    ∃ p : Point K,
      OnCircle K center₁ radius₁ p ∧
        OnCircle K center₂ radius₂ p ∧
          ∀ q : Point K,
            OnCircle K center₁ radius₁ q ∧ OnCircle K center₂ radius₂ q → q = p

/--
Feuerbach's theorem: the circle through the three side midpoints of a nondegenerate
triangle is tangent to any circle tangent to all three side lines.
-/
theorem feuerbach
    (K : RealScalar)
    (a b c mbc mac mab pbc pac pab ncenter icenter : Point K)
    (nradius iradius : Real K)
    (h_noncollinear : ¬Collinear3 K a b c)
    (h_mab : IsMidpoint K a b mab)
    (h_mbc : IsMidpoint K b c mbc)
    (h_mac : IsMidpoint K c a mac)
    (h_n_mbc : OnCircle K ncenter nradius mbc)
    (h_n_mac : OnCircle K ncenter nradius mac)
    (h_n_mab : OnCircle K ncenter nradius mab)
    (h_i_pbc : OnCircle K icenter iradius pbc)
    (h_i_pac : OnCircle K icenter iradius pac)
    (h_i_pab : OnCircle K icenter iradius pab)
    (h_pab_on_ab : Collinear3 K a b pab)
    (h_pab_perp : Perpendicular K a b icenter pab)
    (h_pbc_on_bc : Collinear3 K b c pbc)
    (h_pbc_perp : Perpendicular K b c icenter pbc)
    (h_pac_on_ac : Collinear3 K a c pac)
    (h_pac_perp : Perpendicular K a c icenter pac) :
    CirclesTangent K ncenter nradius icenter iradius := sorry

end Theorems100.Feuerbach

#[local] Open Scope R_scope.

(* See the interactive pictures of Laurent Théry
