Record point:Type:={
 X:R;
 Y:R}.

Definition collinear(A B C:point):=
  (X A - X B)*(Y C - Y B)-(Y A - Y B)*(X C - X B)=0.

Definition parallel (A B C D:point):=
  ((X A)-(X B))*((Y C)-(Y D))=((Y A)-(Y B))*((X C)-(X D)).

Definition notparallel (A B C D:point)(x:R):=
  x*(((X A)-(X B))*((Y C)-(Y D))-((Y A)-(Y B))*((X C)-(X D)))=1.

Definition orthogonal (A B C D:point):=
  ((X A)-(X B))*((X C)-(X D))+((Y A)-(Y B))*((Y C)-(Y D))=0.

Definition equal2(A B:point):=
  (X A)=(X B) /\ (Y A)=(Y B).

Definition equal3(A B:point):=
  ((X A)-(X B))^2%Z+((Y A)-(Y B))^2%Z = 0.

Definition nequal2(A B:point):=
  (X A)<>(X B) \/ (Y A)<>(Y B).

Definition nequal3(A B:point):=
  not (((X A)-(X B))^2%Z+((Y A)-(Y B))^2%Z = 0).

Definition middle(A B I:point):=
  2%R*(X I)=(X A)+(X B) /\ 2%R*(Y I)=(Y A)+(Y B).

Definition distance2(A B:point):=
  (X B - X A)^2%Z + (Y B - Y A)^2%Z.

(* AB = CD *)
Definition samedistance2(A B C D:point):=
  (X B - X A)^2%Z + (Y B - Y A)^2%Z = (X D - X C)^2%Z + (Y D - Y C)^2%Z.
Definition determinant(A O B:point):=
  (X A - X O)*(Y B - Y O) - (Y A - Y O)*(X B - X O).
Definition scalarproduct(A O B:point):=
  (X A - X O)*(X B - X O) + (Y A - Y O)*(Y B - Y O).
Definition norm2(A O B:point):=
  ((X A - X O)^2%Z+(Y A - Y O)^2%Z)*((X B - X O)^2%Z+(Y B - Y O)^2%Z).

Definition equaldistance(A B C D:point):=
  ((X B) - (X A))^2%Z + ((Y B) - (Y A))^2%Z =
  ((X D) - (X C))^2%Z + ((Y D) - (Y C))^2%Z.

Definition equaltangente(A B C D E F:point):=
  let s1:= determinant A B C in
  let c1:= scalarproduct A B C in
  let s2:= determinant D E F in
  let c2:= scalarproduct D E F in
  s1 * c2 = s2 * c1.

Ltac cnf2 f :=
  match f with
   | ?A \/ (?B /\ ?C) =>
     let c1 := cnf2 (A\/B) in
     let c2 := cnf2 (A\/C) in constr:(c1/\c2)
   | (?B /\ ?C) \/ ?A =>
     let c1 := cnf2 (B\/A) in
     let c2 := cnf2 (C\/A) in constr:(c1/\c2)
   | (?A \/ ?B) \/ ?C =>
     let c1 := cnf2 (B\/C) in cnf2 (A \/ c1)
   | _ => f
  end
with cnf f :=
  match f with
   | ?A \/ ?B =>
     let c1 := cnf A in
       let c2 := cnf B in
         cnf2 (c1 \/ c2)
   | ?A /\ ?B =>
     let c1 := cnf A in
       let c2 := cnf B in
         constr:(c1 /\ c2)
   | _ => f
  end.

Ltac scnf :=
  match goal with
    | |- ?f => let c := cnf f in
      assert c;[repeat split| tauto]
  end.

Ltac disj_to_pol f :=
  match f with
   | ?a = ?b \/ ?g => let p := disj_to_pol g in constr:((a - b)* p)
   | ?a = ?b => constr:(a - b)
  end.

Lemma fastnsatz1:forall x y:R, x - y = 0 -> x = y.
Proof.
Admitted.

Ltac fastnsatz:=
  try trivial; try apply fastnsatz1; try trivial; nsatz.

Ltac proof_pol_disj :=
  match goal with
   | |- ?g => let p := disj_to_pol g in
     let h := fresh "hp" in
     assert (h:p = 0);
     [idtac|
      prod_disj h p]
   | _ => idtac
  end
with prod_disj h p :=
  match goal with
   | |- ?a = ?b \/ ?g =>
        match p with
          | ?q * ?p1 =>
        let h0 := fresh "hp" in
        let h1 := fresh "hp" in
        let h2 := fresh "hp" in
        assert (h0:a - b = 0 \/ p1 = 0);
        [apply Rmult_integral; exact h|
         destruct h0 as [h1|h2];
         [left; fastnsatz|
          right; prod_disj h2 p1]]
        end
   | _ => fastnsatz
  end.

(*
Goal forall a b c d e f:R, a=b \/ c=d \/ e=f \/ e=a.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Pythagore: forall A B C:point,
  orthogonal A B A C ->
  distance2 A C + distance2 A B = distance2 B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Thales: forall O A B C D:point,
  collinear O A C -> collinear O B D ->
  parallel A B C D ->
  (distance2 O B * distance2 O C = distance2 O D * distance2 O A
  /\ distance2 O B * distance2 C D = distance2 O D * distance2 A B)
 \/ collinear O A B.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma segments_of_chords: forall A B C D M O:point,
  equaldistance O A O B ->
  equaldistance O A O C ->
  equaldistance O A O D ->
  collinear A B M ->
  collinear C D M ->
  (distance2 M A) * (distance2 M B) = (distance2 M C) * (distance2 M D)
  \/ parallel A B C D.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma isoceles: forall A B C:point,
  equaltangente A B C B C A ->
  distance2 A B = distance2 A C
  \/ collinear A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma minh: forall A B C D O E H I:point,
  X A = 0 -> Y A = 0 -> Y O = 0 ->
  equaldistance O A O B ->
  equaldistance O A O C ->
  equaldistance O A O D ->
  orthogonal A C B D ->
  collinear A C E ->
  collinear B D E ->
  collinear A B H ->
  orthogonal E H A B ->
  collinear C D I ->
  middle C D I ->
  collinear H E I
  \/ (X C)^2%Z * (X B)^5%Z * (X O)^2%Z
     * (X C - 2%Z * X O)^3%Z * (-2%Z * X O + X B)=0
  \/  parallel A C B D.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Pappus: forall A B C A1 B1 C1 P Q S:point,
  X A = 0 -> Y A = 0 -> Y B = 0 -> Y C = 0 ->
  collinear A1 B1 C1 ->
  collinear A B1 P -> collinear A1 B P ->
  collinear A C1 Q -> collinear A1 C Q ->
  collinear B C1 S -> collinear B1 C S ->
  collinear P Q S
  \/ (Y A1 - Y B1)^2%Z=0 \/ (X A = X B1)
  \/ (X A1 = X C) \/ (X C = X B1)
  \/ parallel A B1 A1 B \/ parallel A C1 A1 C \/ parallel B C1 B1 C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Simson: forall A B C O D E F G:point,
  X A = 0 -> Y A = 0 ->
  equaldistance O A O B ->
  equaldistance O A O C ->
  equaldistance O A O D ->
  orthogonal  E D B C ->
  collinear B C E ->
  orthogonal F D A C ->
  collinear A C F ->
  orthogonal G D A B ->
  collinear A B G ->
  collinear E F G
  \/ (X C)^2%Z = 0 \/ (Y C)^2%Z = 0 \/ (X B)^2%Z = 0 \/ (Y B)^2%Z = 0 \/ (Y C - Y B)^2%Z = 0
  \/ equal3 B A
  \/ equal3 A C \/ (X C - X B)^2%Z = 0
  \/ equal3 B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma threepoints: forall A B C A1 B1 A2 B2 H1 H2 H3:point,
  (* H1 intersection of bisections *)
  middle B C A1 ->  orthogonal H1 A1 B C ->
  middle A C B1 -> orthogonal H1 B1 A C ->
  (* H2 intersection of medians *)
  collinear A A1 H2 -> collinear B B1 H2 ->
  (* H3 intersection of altitudes *)
  collinear B C A2 ->  orthogonal A A2 B C ->
  collinear A C B2 -> orthogonal B B2 A C ->
  collinear A A1 H3 -> collinear B B1 H3 ->
  collinear H1 H2 H3
  \/ collinear A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Feuerbach:  forall A B C A1 B1 C1 O A2 B2 C2 O2:point,
  forall r r2:R,
  X A = 0 -> Y A =  0 -> X B = 1 -> Y B =  0->
  middle A B C1 -> middle B C A1 -> middle C A B1 ->
  distance2 O A1 = distance2 O B1 ->
  distance2 O A1 = distance2 O C1 ->
  collinear A B C2 -> orthogonal A B O2 C2 ->
  collinear B C A2 -> orthogonal B C O2 A2 ->
  collinear A C B2 -> orthogonal A C O2 B2 ->
  distance2 O2 A2 = distance2 O2 B2 ->
  distance2 O2 A2 = distance2 O2 C2 ->
  r^2%Z = distance2 O A1 ->
  r2^2%Z = distance2 O2 A2 ->
  distance2 O O2 = (r + r2)^2%Z
  \/ distance2 O O2 = (r - r2)^2%Z
  \/ collinear A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Euler_circle: forall A B C A1 B1 C1 A2 B2 C2 O:point,
  middle A B C1 -> middle B C A1 -> middle C A B1 ->
  orthogonal A B C C2 -> collinear A B C2 ->
  orthogonal B C A A2 -> collinear B C A2 ->
  orthogonal A C B B2 -> collinear A C B2 ->
  distance2 O A1 = distance2 O B1 ->
  distance2 O A1 = distance2 O C1 ->
  (distance2 O A2 = distance2 O A1
   /\distance2 O B2 = distance2 O A1
   /\distance2 O C2 = distance2 O A1)
  \/ collinear A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Desargues: forall A B C A1 B1 C1 P Q T S:point,
  X S = 0 -> Y S = 0 -> Y A = 0 ->
  collinear A S A1 -> collinear B S B1 -> collinear C S C1 ->
  collinear B1 C1 P -> collinear B C P ->
  collinear A1 C1 Q -> collinear A C Q ->
  collinear A1 B1 T -> collinear A B T ->
  collinear P Q T
  \/ X A = X B \/ X A = X C \/ X B = X C  \/ X A = 0 \/ Y B = 0 \/ Y C = 0
  \/ collinear S B C \/ parallel A C A1 C1 \/ parallel A B A1 B1.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma chords: forall O A B C D M:point,
  equaldistance O A O B ->
  equaldistance O A O C ->
  equaldistance O A O D ->
  collinear A B M -> collinear C D M ->
  scalarproduct A M B = scalarproduct C M D
  \/ parallel A B C D.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Ceva: forall A B C D E F M:point,
  collinear M A D -> collinear M B E -> collinear M C F ->
  collinear B C D -> collinear E A C -> collinear F A B ->
  (distance2 D B) * (distance2 E C) * (distance2 F A) =
  (distance2 D C) * (distance2 E A) * (distance2 F B)
  \/ collinear A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma bissectrices: forall A B C M:point,
  equaltangente C A M M A B ->
  equaltangente A B M M B C ->
  equaltangente B C M M C A
  \/ equal3 A B.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma bisections: forall A B C A1 B1 C1 H:point,
  middle B C A1 ->  orthogonal H A1 B C ->
  middle A C B1 -> orthogonal H B1 A C ->
  middle A B C1 ->
  orthogonal H C1 A B
  \/ collinear A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma altitudes: forall A B C A1 B1 C1 H:point,
  collinear B C A1 ->  orthogonal A A1 B C ->
  collinear A C B1 -> orthogonal B B1 A C ->
  collinear A B C1 -> orthogonal C C1 A B ->
  collinear A A1 H -> collinear B B1 H ->
  collinear C C1 H
  \/ equal2 A B
  \/ collinear A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma hauteurs:forall A B C A1 B1 C1 H:point,
  collinear B C A1 ->  orthogonal A A1 B C ->
  collinear A C B1 -> orthogonal B B1 A C ->
  collinear A B C1 -> orthogonal C C1 A B ->
  collinear A A1 H -> collinear B B1 H ->

  collinear C C1 H
  \/ collinear A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.


End Geometry.

title: 029_feuerbach_s_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Feuerbach's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 029.
  Using real coordinate pairs for the Euclidean plane, it states that for a nondegenerate
  triangle the circle through the side midpoints is tangent to a circle tangent to all
  three side-lines. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory Feuerbach_Theorem
  imports Complex_Main
begin

type_synonym plane_point = "real \<times> real"

definition euclidean_distance :: "plane_point \<Rightarrow> plane_point \<Rightarrow> real" where
  "euclidean_distance p q =
    sqrt ((fst p - fst q) ^ 2 + (snd p - snd q) ^ 2)"

definition plane_midpoint :: "plane_point \<Rightarrow> plane_point \<Rightarrow> plane_point" where
  "plane_midpoint p q =
    ((fst p + fst q) / 2, (snd p + snd q) / 2)"

definition collinear_points :: "plane_point \<Rightarrow> plane_point \<Rightarrow> plane_point \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "collinear_points p q r \<longleftrightarrow>
    (fst q - fst p) * (snd r - snd p) =
    (snd q - snd p) * (fst r - fst p)"

definition perpendicular_at ::
    "plane_point \<Rightarrow> plane_point \<Rightarrow> plane_point \<Rightarrow> plane_point \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "perpendicular_at p q center foot \<longleftrightarrow>
    (fst p - fst q) * (fst center - fst foot) +
    (snd p - snd q) * (snd center - snd foot) = 0"

theorem feuerbach:
  fixes a b c mbc mac mab pbc pac pab ncenter icenter :: plane_point
    and nradius iradius :: real
  assumes nondegenerate: "\<not> collinear_points a b c"
    and midpoint_ab: "plane_midpoint a b = mab"
    and midpoint_bc: "plane_midpoint b c = mbc"
    and midpoint_ca: "plane_midpoint c a = mac"
    and nine_point_radius_bc: "euclidean_distance ncenter mbc = nradius"
    and nine_point_radius_ca: "euclidean_distance ncenter mac = nradius"
    and nine_point_radius_ab: "euclidean_distance ncenter mab = nradius"
    and tangent_radius_bc: "euclidean_distance icenter pbc = iradius"
    and tangent_radius_ca: "euclidean_distance icenter pac = iradius"
    and tangent_radius_ab: "euclidean_distance icenter pab = iradius"
    and contact_ab: "collinear_points a b pab"
    and perpendicular_ab: "perpendicular_at a b icenter pab"
    and contact_bc: "collinear_points b c pbc"
    and perpendicular_bc: "perpendicular_at b c icenter pbc"
    and contact_ac: "collinear_points a c pac"
    and perpendicular_ac: "perpendicular_at a c icenter pac"
  shows "(ncenter = icenter \<and> nradius = iradius) \<or>
    (\<exists>!x :: plane_point.
      euclidean_distance ncenter x = nradius \<and>
      euclidean_distance icenter x = iradius)"
  sorry

end

title: 029_feuerbach_s_theorem
content:
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* Feuerbach's theorem.                                                      *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

needs "Multivariate/convex.ml";;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Algebraic condition for two circles to be tangent to each other.          *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let CIRCLES_TANGENT = `!r1 r2 c1 c2.
        &0 <= r1 /\ &0 <= r2 /\
        (dist(c1,c2) = r1 + r2 \/ dist(c1,c2) = abs(r1 - r2))
        ==> c1 = c2 /\ r1 = r2 \/
            ?!x:real^2. dist(c1,x) = r1 /\ dist(c2,x) = r2`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(*                       Feuerbach's theorem                                 *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Given a non-degenerate triangle abc, let the circle passing through       *)
(* the midpoints of its sides (the "9 point circle") have center "ncenter"   *)
(* and radius "nradius". Now suppose the circle with center "icenter" and    *)
(* radius "iradius" is tangent to three sides (either internally or          *)
(* externally to one side and two produced sides), meaning that it's either  *)
(* the inscribed circle or one of the three escribed circles. Then the two   *)
(* circles are tangent to each other, i.e. either they are identical or they *)
(* touch at exactly one point.                                               *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let FEUERBACH = `!a b c mbc mac mab pbc pac pab ncenter icenter nradius iradius.
      ~(collinear {a,b,c}) /\
      midpoint(a,b) = mab /\
      midpoint(b,c) = mbc /\
      midpoint(c,a) = mac /\
      dist(ncenter,mbc) = nradius /\
      dist(ncenter,mac) = nradius /\
      dist(ncenter,mab) = nradius /\
      dist(icenter,pbc) = iradius /\
      dist(icenter,pac) = iradius /\
      dist(icenter,pab) = iradius /\
      collinear {a,b,pab} /\ orthogonal (a - b) (icenter - pab) /\
      collinear {b,c,pbc} /\ orthogonal (b - c) (icenter - pbc) /\
      collinear {a,c,pac} /\ orthogonal (a - c) (icenter - pac)
      ==> ncenter = icenter /\ nradius = iradius \/
          ?!x:real^2. dist(ncenter,x) = nradius /\ dist(icenter,x) = iradius`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* As a little bonus, verify that the circle passing through the             *)
(* midpoints of the sides is indeed a 9-point circle, i.e. it passes         *)
(* through the feet of the altitudes and the midpoints of the lines joining  *)
(* the vertices to the orthocenter (where the alititudes intersect).         *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let NINE_POINT_CIRCLE_1 = `!a b c:real^2 mbc mac mab fbc fac fab ncenter nradius.
      ~(collinear {a,b,c}) /\
      midpoint(a,b) = mab /\
      midpoint(b,c) = mbc /\
      midpoint(c,a) = mac /\
      dist(ncenter,mbc) = nradius /\
      dist(ncenter,mac) = nradius /\
      dist(ncenter,mab) = nradius /\
      collinear {a,b,fab} /\ orthogonal (a - b) (c - fab) /\
      collinear {b,c,fbc} /\ orthogonal (b - c) (a - fbc) /\
      collinear {c,a,fac} /\ orthogonal (c - a) (b - fac)
      ==> dist(ncenter,fab) = nradius /\
          dist(ncenter,fbc) = nradius /\
          dist(ncenter,fac) = nradius`;;

let NINE_POINT_CIRCLE_2 = `!a b c:real^2 mbc mac mab fbc fac fab ncenter nradius.
      ~(collinear {a,b,c}) /\
      midpoint(a,b) = mab /\
      midpoint(b,c) = mbc /\
      midpoint(c,a) = mac /\
      dist(ncenter,mbc) = nradius /\
      dist(ncenter,mac) = nradius /\
      dist(ncenter,mab) = nradius /\
      collinear {a,b,fab} /\ orthogonal (a - b) (c - fab) /\
      collinear {b,c,fbc} /\ orthogonal (b - c) (a - fbc) /\
      collinear {c,a,fac} /\ orthogonal (c - a) (b - fac) /\
      collinear {oc,a,fbc} /\ collinear {oc,b,fac} /\ collinear{oc,c,fab}
      ==> dist(ncenter,midpoint(oc,a)) = nradius /\
          dist(ncenter,midpoint(oc,b)) = nradius /\
          dist(ncenter,midpoint(oc,c)) = nradius`;;

title: 029_feuerbach_s_theorem
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 029,
;; "Feuerbach's Theorem." The nine-point circle of a noncollinear real
;; triangle is tangent to each in/excircle specified by perpendicular contacts
;; with the three side lines. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A real-closed ordered field is enough for this coordinate theorem. Its
;; first-order algebraic sentences have the same truth value as over the real
;; numbers, while avoiding ACL2's built-in rational-number specialization.

(defstub ht029-carrier (x) t)
(defstub ht029-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht029-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht029-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub ht029-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub ht029-less-op (x y) t)

(defun ht029-member-p (x)
  (if (ht029-carrier x) t nil))

(defun ht029-add (x y)
  (ht029-add-op x y))

(defun ht029-multiply (x y)
  (ht029-multiply-op x y))

(defun ht029-negate (x)
  (ht029-negate-op x))

(defun ht029-inverse (x)
  (ht029-inverse-op x))

(defun ht029-subtract (x y)
  (ht029-add x (ht029-negate y)))

(defun ht029-less (x y)
  (if (ht029-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun ht029-square (x)
  (ht029-multiply x x))

(defun-sk ht029-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht029-member-p x)
      (ht029-member-p y)
      (ht029-member-p z))
     (and
      (ht029-member-p (ht029-add x y))
      (ht029-member-p (ht029-multiply x y))
      (ht029-member-p (ht029-negate x))
      (ht029-member-p (ht029-inverse x))
      (equal (ht029-add (ht029-add x y) z)
             (ht029-add x (ht029-add y z)))
      (equal (ht029-add x y)
             (ht029-add y x))
      (equal (ht029-add x zero) x)
      (equal (ht029-add x (ht029-negate x)) zero)
      (equal (ht029-multiply (ht029-multiply x y) z)
             (ht029-multiply x (ht029-multiply y z)))
      (equal (ht029-multiply x y)
             (ht029-multiply y x))
      (equal (ht029-multiply x one) x)
      (equal
       (ht029-multiply x (ht029-add y z))
       (ht029-add
        (ht029-multiply x y)
        (ht029-multiply x z)))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (ht029-multiply x (ht029-inverse x))
        one))))))

(defun-sk ht029-order-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht029-member-p x)
      (ht029-member-p y)
      (ht029-member-p z))
     (and
      (not (ht029-less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (ht029-less x y)
       (ht029-less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht029-less x y)
        (ht029-less y z))
       (ht029-less x z))
      (implies
       (ht029-less x y)
       (ht029-less
        (ht029-add x z)
        (ht029-add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht029-less zero x)
        (ht029-less zero y))
       (ht029-less zero (ht029-multiply x y)))))))

(defun ht029-field-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (ht029-member-p (car values))
       (ht029-field-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

;; Coefficients are stored in ascending order. Real closedness is expressed by
;; the standard characterization: nonnegative elements have square roots and
;; every odd-degree polynomial has a root.
(defun ht029-polynomial-value (coefficients x zero)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (ht029-add
       (car coefficients)
       (ht029-multiply
        x
        (ht029-polynomial-value (cdr coefficients) x zero)))
    zero))

(defun ht029-odd-degree-polynomial-p (coefficients zero)
  (and
   (consp coefficients)
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (ht029-field-list-p coefficients)
   (evenp (len coefficients))
   (not (equal (car (last coefficients)) zero))))

(defun-sk ht029-has-square-root-p (x zero)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (ht029-member-p root)
     (equal (ht029-square root) x))))

(defun-sk ht029-has-polynomial-root-p (coefficients zero)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (ht029-member-p root)
     (equal
      (ht029-polynomial-value coefficients root zero)
      zero))))

(defun-sk ht029-real-closure-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x coefficients)
    (and
     (implies
      (and
       (ht029-member-p x)
       (not (ht029-less x zero)))
      (ht029-has-square-root-p x zero))
     (implies
      (ht029-odd-degree-polynomial-p coefficients zero)
      (ht029-has-polynomial-root-p coefficients zero)))))

(defun ht029-real-scalar-context-p (zero one)
  (and
   (ht029-member-p zero)
   (ht029-member-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (ht029-less zero one)
   (ht029-field-laws-p zero one)
   (ht029-order-laws-p zero)
   (ht029-real-closure-laws-p zero)))

;; Points are represented by dotted coordinate pairs (x . y).
(defun ht029-point-p (point)
  (and
   (consp point)
   (ht029-member-p (car point))
   (ht029-member-p (cdr point))))

(defun ht029-distance-squared (first second)
  (let ((dx (ht029-subtract (car second) (car first)))
        (dy (ht029-subtract (cdr second) (cdr first))))
    (ht029-add
     (ht029-square dx)
     (ht029-square dy))))

(defun ht029-midpoint-p (first second midpoint one)
  (let ((two (ht029-add one one)))
    (and
     (equal
      (ht029-multiply two (car midpoint))
      (ht029-add (car first) (car second)))
     (equal
      (ht029-multiply two (cdr midpoint))
      (ht029-add (cdr first) (cdr second))))))

(defun ht029-collinear-p (first second third)
  (equal
   (ht029-multiply
    (ht029-subtract (car first) (car second))
    (ht029-subtract (cdr third) (cdr second)))
   (ht029-multiply
    (ht029-subtract (cdr first) (cdr second))
    (ht029-subtract (car third) (car second)))))

(defun ht029-orthogonal-p
    (first-start first-end second-start second-end zero)
  (equal
   (ht029-add
    (ht029-multiply
     (ht029-subtract (car first-start) (car first-end))
     (ht029-subtract (car second-start) (car second-end)))
    (ht029-multiply
     (ht029-subtract (cdr first-start) (cdr first-end))
     (ht029-subtract (cdr second-start) (cdr second-end))))
   zero))

(defun ht029-nonnegative-p (zero value)
  (and
   (ht029-member-p value)
   (not (ht029-less value zero))))

(defun ht029-on-circle-p (center radius point zero)
  (and
   (ht029-point-p center)
   (ht029-point-p point)
   (ht029-nonnegative-p zero radius)
   (equal
    (ht029-distance-squared center point)
    (ht029-square radius))))

;; For nonnegative radii this is equivalent, over a real-closed ordered field,
;; to equality of the circles or existence of exactly one common point.
(defun ht029-circles-tangent-p
    (first-center first-radius second-center second-radius)
  (or
   (equal
    (ht029-distance-squared first-center second-center)
    (ht029-square (ht029-add first-radius second-radius)))
   (equal
    (ht029-distance-squared first-center second-center)
    (ht029-square (ht029-subtract first-radius second-radius)))))

(defun ht029-feuerbach-hypotheses-p
    (a b c mbc mac mab pbc pac pab
       ncenter icenter nradius iradius zero one)
  (and
   (ht029-point-p a)
   (ht029-point-p b)
   (ht029-point-p c)
   (ht029-point-p mbc)
   (ht029-point-p mac)
   (ht029-point-p mab)
   (ht029-point-p pbc)
   (ht029-point-p pac)
   (ht029-point-p pab)
   (ht029-point-p ncenter)
   (ht029-point-p icenter)
   (not (ht029-collinear-p a b c))
   (ht029-midpoint-p a b mab one)
   (ht029-midpoint-p b c mbc one)
   (ht029-midpoint-p c a mac one)
   (ht029-on-circle-p ncenter nradius mbc zero)
   (ht029-on-circle-p ncenter nradius mac zero)
   (ht029-on-circle-p ncenter nradius mab zero)
   (ht029-on-circle-p icenter iradius pbc zero)
   (ht029-on-circle-p icenter iradius pac zero)
   (ht029-on-circle-p icenter iradius pab zero)
   (ht029-collinear-p a b pab)
   (ht029-orthogonal-p a b icenter pab zero)
   (ht029-collinear-p b c pbc)
   (ht029-orthogonal-p b c icenter pbc zero)
   (ht029-collinear-p a c pac)
   (ht029-orthogonal-p a c icenter pac zero)))

(defun-sk hundred-theorems-029-feuerbach-statement (zero one)
  (forall
   (a b c mbc mac mab pbc pac pab
      ncenter icenter nradius iradius)
   (implies
    (and
     (ht029-real-scalar-context-p zero one)
     (ht029-feuerbach-hypotheses-p
      a b c mbc mac mab pbc pac pab
      ncenter icenter nradius iradius zero one))
    (ht029-circles-tangent-p
     ncenter nradius icenter iradius))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 029_feuerbach_s_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Feuerbach's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 029.
-- In the real Euclidean plane, the circle through a nondegenerate triangle's side
-- midpoints is tangent to any circle tangent to its three side lines.
-- This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record ExistsUniqueBy
  (A : Set)
  (equal : A -> A -> Set)
  (P : A -> Set) :
  Set where

  constructor unique-witness
  field
    value      : A
    property   : P value
    uniqueness : (other : A) -> P other -> equal other value

data NatLe : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero-le : (n : Nat) -> NatLe zero n
  suc-le  : {m n : Nat} -> NatLe m n -> NatLe (suc m) (suc n)

two : Nat
two = suc (suc zero)

powTwo : Nat -> Nat
powTwo zero = suc zero
powTwo (suc n) = two * powTwo n

record Integer : Set where
  constructor integer
  field
    positive : Nat
    negative : Nat

open Integer

integerZero : Integer
integerZero = integer zero zero

integerFromNat : Nat -> Integer
integerFromNat n = integer n zero

integerAdd : Integer -> Integer -> Integer
integerAdd x y =
  integer
    (positive x + positive y)
    (negative x + negative y)

integerNegate : Integer -> Integer
integerNegate x =
  integer (negative x) (positive x)

integerSubtract : Integer -> Integer -> Integer
integerSubtract x y =
  integerAdd x (integerNegate y)

integerMultiply : Integer -> Integer -> Integer
integerMultiply x y =
  integer
    ((positive x * positive y) + (negative x * negative y))
    ((positive x * negative y) + (negative x * positive y))

integerScale : Nat -> Integer -> Integer
integerScale n x =
  integer (n * positive x) (n * negative x)

IntegerLe : Integer -> Integer -> Set
IntegerLe x y =
  NatLe
    (positive x + negative y)
    (positive y + negative x)

IntegerClose : Nat -> Nat -> Integer -> Integer -> Set
IntegerClose denominatorPower precision x y =
  IntegerLe
    (integerNegate (integerFromNat (powTwo denominatorPower)))
    (integerScale (powTwo precision) (integerSubtract x y))
  and
  IntegerLe
    (integerScale (powTwo precision) (integerSubtract x y))
    (integerFromNat (powTwo denominatorPower))

CauchySequence : (Nat -> Integer) -> Set
CauchySequence approximation =
  (precision : Nat) ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ threshold ->
      (m n : Nat) ->
      NatLe threshold m ->
      NatLe threshold n ->
      IntegerClose
        (m + n)
        precision
        (integerSubtract
          (integerScale (powTwo n) (approximation m))
          (integerScale (powTwo m) (approximation n)))
        integerZero)

record Real : Set where
  constructor real
  field
    approximation : Nat -> Integer
    cauchy         : CauchySequence approximation

open Real

SequenceEqual :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  (Nat -> Integer) ->
  (Nat -> Integer) ->
  Set
SequenceEqual denominatorPower x y =
  (precision : Nat) ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ threshold ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      NatLe threshold n ->
      IntegerClose (denominatorPower n) precision (x n) (y n))

LinearEqual :
  (Nat -> Integer) ->
  (Nat -> Integer) ->
  Set
LinearEqual =
  SequenceEqual (\ n -> n)

QuadraticEqual :
  (Nat -> Integer) ->
  (Nat -> Integer) ->
  Set
QuadraticEqual =
  SequenceEqual (\ n -> n + n)

RealEqual : Real -> Real -> Set
RealEqual x y =
  LinearEqual (approximation x) (approximation y)

StrictlyNegative : Real -> Set
StrictlyNegative x =
  Exists Nat
    (\ precision ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ threshold ->
          (n : Nat) ->
          NatLe threshold n ->
          IntegerLe
            (integerAdd
              (integerScale
                (powTwo precision)
                (approximation x n))
              (integerFromNat (powTwo n)))
            integerZero))

Nonnegative : Real -> Set
Nonnegative x =
  Not (StrictlyNegative x)

record Point : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : Real
    y-coordinate : Real

open Point

PointEqual : Point -> Point -> Set
PointEqual p q =
  RealEqual (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)
  and
  RealEqual (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)

zeroSequence : Nat -> Integer
zeroSequence n =
  integerZero

xDifference : Point -> Point -> Nat -> Integer
xDifference p q n =
  integerSubtract
    (approximation (x-coordinate p) n)
    (approximation (x-coordinate q) n)

yDifference : Point -> Point -> Nat -> Integer
yDifference p q n =
  integerSubtract
    (approximation (y-coordinate p) n)
    (approximation (y-coordinate q) n)

squaredDistanceNumerator : Point -> Point -> Nat -> Integer
squaredDistanceNumerator p q n =
  integerAdd
    (integerMultiply (xDifference p q n) (xDifference p q n))
    (integerMultiply (yDifference p q n) (yDifference p q n))

radiusSquareNumerator : Real -> Nat -> Integer
radiusSquareNumerator radius n =
  integerMultiply
    (approximation radius n)
    (approximation radius n)

Midpoint : Point -> Point -> Point -> Set
Midpoint a b midpoint =
  LinearEqual
    (\ n ->
      integerScale two
        (approximation (x-coordinate midpoint) n))
    (\ n ->
      integerAdd
        (approximation (x-coordinate a) n)
        (approximation (x-coordinate b) n))
  and
  LinearEqual
    (\ n ->
      integerScale two
        (approximation (y-coordinate midpoint) n))
    (\ n ->
      integerAdd
        (approximation (y-coordinate a) n)
        (approximation (y-coordinate b) n))

determinantNumerator : Point -> Point -> Point -> Nat -> Integer
determinantNumerator a b c n =
  integerSubtract
    (integerMultiply
      (xDifference a b n)
      (yDifference c b n))
    (integerMultiply
      (yDifference a b n)
      (xDifference c b n))

Collinear : Point -> Point -> Point -> Set
Collinear a b c =
  QuadraticEqual
    (determinantNumerator a b c)
    zeroSequence

dotProductNumerator :
  Point ->
  Point ->
  Point ->
  Point ->
  Nat ->
  Integer
dotProductNumerator a b c d n =
  integerAdd
    (integerMultiply
      (xDifference a b n)
      (xDifference c d n))
    (integerMultiply
      (yDifference a b n)
      (yDifference c d n))

Orthogonal : Point -> Point -> Point -> Point -> Set
Orthogonal a b c d =
  QuadraticEqual
    (dotProductNumerator a b c d)
    zeroSequence

OnCircle : Point -> Real -> Point -> Set
OnCircle center radius p =
  Nonnegative radius
  and
  QuadraticEqual
    (squaredDistanceNumerator center p)
    (radiusSquareNumerator radius)

CirclesTangent : Point -> Real -> Point -> Real -> Set
CirclesTangent center1 radius1 center2 radius2 =
  (PointEqual center1 center2 and RealEqual radius1 radius2)
  or
  ExistsUniqueBy Point PointEqual
    (\ p ->
      OnCircle center1 radius1 p
      and
      OnCircle center2 radius2 p)

feuerbachs-theorem : Set
feuerbachs-theorem =
  (a b c mbc mac mab pbc pac pab ncenter icenter : Point) ->
  (nradius iradius : Real) ->
  Not (Collinear a b c) ->
  Midpoint a b mab ->
  Midpoint b c mbc ->
  Midpoint c a mac ->
  OnCircle ncenter nradius mbc ->
  OnCircle ncenter nradius mac ->
  OnCircle ncenter nradius mab ->
  OnCircle icenter iradius pbc ->
  OnCircle icenter iradius pac ->
  OnCircle icenter iradius pab ->
  Collinear a b pab ->
  Orthogonal a b icenter pab ->
  Collinear b c pbc ->
  Orthogonal b c icenter pbc ->
  Collinear a c pac ->
  Orthogonal a c icenter pac ->
  CirclesTangent ncenter nradius icenter iradius

title: 029_feuerbach_s_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 029, "Feuerbach's Theorem":
  for a nondegenerate real-plane triangle, the circle through the side midpoints and a
  circle tangent to all three side-lines are identical or have exactly one common point.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pairTheory realTheory transcTheory;

val feuerbachs_theorem =
  ``let collinear =
      \P Q R : real # real.
        (FST P - FST Q) * (SND R - SND Q) =
        (SND P - SND Q) * (FST R - FST Q)
    in
    let midpoint =
      \P Q : real # real.
        ((FST P + FST Q) / 2, (SND P + SND Q) / 2)
    in
    let orthogonal =
      \A B C D : real # real.
        (FST A - FST B) * (FST C - FST D) +
        (SND A - SND B) * (SND C - SND D) = 0
    in
    let dist =
      \P Q : real # real.
        sqrt ((FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2)
    in
      !a b c mbc mac mab pbc pac pab ncenter icenter : real # real.
      !nradius iradius : real.
        ~collinear a b c /\
        midpoint a b = mab /\
        midpoint b c = mbc /\
        midpoint c a = mac /\
        dist ncenter mbc = nradius /\
        dist ncenter mac = nradius /\
        dist ncenter mab = nradius /\
        dist icenter pbc = iradius /\
        dist icenter pac = iradius /\
        dist icenter pab = iradius /\
        collinear a b pab /\ orthogonal a b icenter pab /\
        collinear b c pbc /\ orthogonal b c icenter pbc /\
        collinear a c pac /\ orthogonal a c icenter pac
        ==>
        (ncenter = icenter /\ nradius = iradius) \/
        (?!x : real # real.
           dist ncenter x = nradius /\ dist icenter x = iradius)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 029, "Feuerbach's
  Theorem". This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  The Euclidean plane is the actual set RR X. RR. Coordinates, squared
  distance, distance, midpoint, collinearity, perpendicularity, circle
  membership, and circle tangency are all conservative definitions over
  set.mm's real arithmetic.

  The final assertion follows the Lean and HOL Light statement. For a
  noncollinear triangle, one circle passes through the three side midpoints.
  A second circle has three radius feet on the side lines, with each radius
  perpendicular to its side. The circles are equal or have exactly one common
  point. The auxiliary circle criterion used in the HOL Light proof is not an
  axiom here.
$)

$c HT029Plane HT029X HT029Y HT029DistanceSq HT029Distance $.
$c HT029Midpoint HT029Collinear HT029Perpendicular $.
$c HT029OnCircle HT029CirclesTangent $.

ht029-plane-syntax $a class HT029Plane $.
ht029-x-syntax $a class ( HT029X A ) $.
ht029-y-syntax $a class ( HT029Y A ) $.
ht029-distance-sq-syntax $a class ( HT029DistanceSq A B ) $.
ht029-distance-syntax $a class ( HT029Distance A B ) $.
ht029-midpoint-syntax $a wff ( HT029Midpoint A B C ) $.
ht029-collinear-syntax $a wff ( HT029Collinear A B C ) $.
ht029-perpendicular-syntax $a wff ( HT029Perpendicular A B C D ) $.
ht029-on-circle-syntax $a wff ( HT029OnCircle A R B ) $.
ht029-circles-tangent-syntax $a wff ( HT029CirclesTangent A R B S ) $.

ht029-plane-definition $a |- HT029Plane = ( RR X. RR ) $.

ht029-x-definition $a |- (
  HT029X A
  =
  ( 1st ` A )
) $.

ht029-y-definition $a |- (
  HT029Y A
  =
  ( 2nd ` A )
) $.

ht029-distance-sq-definition $a |- (
  HT029DistanceSq A B
  =
  (
    ( ( ( HT029X B ) - ( HT029X A ) ) ^ 2 )
    +
    ( ( ( HT029Y B ) - ( HT029Y A ) ) ^ 2 )
  )
) $.

ht029-distance-definition $a |- (
  HT029Distance A B
  =
  ( sqrt ` ( HT029DistanceSq A B ) )
) $.

ht029-midpoint-definition $a |- (
  ( HT029Midpoint A B C )
  <->
  (
    (
      ( A e. HT029Plane /\ B e. HT029Plane )
      /\
      C e. HT029Plane
    )
    /\
    (
      ( 2 x. ( HT029X C ) )
      =
      ( ( HT029X A ) + ( HT029X B ) )
      /\
      ( 2 x. ( HT029Y C ) )
      =
      ( ( HT029Y A ) + ( HT029Y B ) )
    )
  )
) $.

ht029-collinear-definition $a |- (
  ( HT029Collinear A B C )
  <->
  (
    (
      ( A e. HT029Plane /\ B e. HT029Plane )
      /\
      C e. HT029Plane
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        ( ( HT029X A ) - ( HT029X B ) )
        x.
        ( ( HT029Y C ) - ( HT029Y B ) )
      )
      =
      (
        ( ( HT029Y A ) - ( HT029Y B ) )
        x.
        ( ( HT029X C ) - ( HT029X B ) )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

ht029-perpendicular-definition $a |- (
  ( HT029Perpendicular A B C D )
  <->
  (
    (
      (
        ( A e. HT029Plane /\ B e. HT029Plane )
        /\
        C e. HT029Plane
      )
      /\
      D e. HT029Plane
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        (
          ( ( HT029X A ) - ( HT029X B ) )
          x.
          ( ( HT029X C ) - ( HT029X D ) )
        )
        +
        (
          ( ( HT029Y A ) - ( HT029Y B ) )
          x.
          ( ( HT029Y C ) - ( HT029Y D ) )
        )
      )
      =
      0
    )
  )
) $.

ht029-on-circle-definition $a |- (
  ( HT029OnCircle A R B )
  <->
  (
    (
      ( A e. HT029Plane /\ B e. HT029Plane )
      /\
      R e. RR
    )
    /\
    (
      0 <_ R
      /\
      ( HT029Distance A B ) = R
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d A B R S x $.

  ht029-circles-tangent-definition $a |- (
    ( HT029CirclesTangent A R B S )
    <->
    (
      (
        (
          ( A e. HT029Plane /\ B e. HT029Plane )
          /\
          ( R e. RR /\ S e. RR )
        )
        /\
        ( 0 <_ R /\ 0 <_ S )
      )
      /\
      (
        ( A = B /\ R = S )
        \/
        E! x e. HT029Plane
          (
            ( HT029OnCircle A R x )
            /\
            ( HT029OnCircle B S x )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

hundred-theorems-029-feuerbach $a |- (

        )

                ( HT029OnCircle J R E )
                /\

                  ( HT029OnCircle J R F )
                  /\
                  (
                    ( HT029OnCircle K S G )
                    /\
                    (
                      ( HT029OnCircle K S H )
                      /\
                      (
                        ( HT029OnCircle K S I )
                        /\

                          (

                          )

:: Statement-only formalization of "Feuerbach's Theorem" from Hundred
:: Theorems, item 029. The nine-point circle of a nondegenerate triangle is
:: tangent to every circle tangent to its three side lines (the incircle or
:: an excircle), with planar points represented by real coordinate pairs.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    NUMBERS, XREAL_0, XCMPLX_0, COMPLEX1, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1,
    ARYTM_3, SQUARE_1, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1, VALUED_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, REAL_1, INT_1,
    COMPLEX1, SQUARE_1, XXREAL_0;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, REAL_1, SQUARE_1, COMPLEX1,
    INT_1, XXREAL_0;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, SQUARE_1, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, INT_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for a1,a2,b1,b2,c1,c2,
      d1,d2,e1,e2,f1,f2,g1,g2,h1,h2,j1,j2,
      u1,u2,v1,v2,r1,r2 being Real st
    0 <= r1 & 0 <= r2 &
    (a1 - b1) * (c2 - b2) <> (a2 - b2) * (c1 - b1) &
    2 * f1 = a1 + b1 &
    2 * f2 = a2 + b2 &
    2 * d1 = b1 + c1 &
    2 * d2 = b2 + c2 &
    2 * e1 = c1 + a1 &
    2 * e2 = c2 + a2 &
    (u1 - d1)^2 + (u2 - d2)^2 = r1^2 &
    (u1 - e1)^2 + (u2 - e2)^2 = r1^2 &
    (u1 - f1)^2 + (u2 - f2)^2 = r1^2 &
    (v1 - g1)^2 + (v2 - g2)^2 = r2^2 &
    (v1 - h1)^2 + (v2 - h2)^2 = r2^2 &
    (v1 - j1)^2 + (v2 - j2)^2 = r2^2 &
    (a1 - b1) * (j2 - b2) = (a2 - b2) * (j1 - b1) &
    (a1 - b1) * (v1 - j1) + (a2 - b2) * (v2 - j2) = 0 &
    (b1 - c1) * (g2 - c2) = (b2 - c2) * (g1 - c1) &
    (b1 - c1) * (v1 - g1) + (b2 - c2) * (v2 - g2) = 0 &
    (a1 - c1) * (h2 - c2) = (a2 - c2) * (h1 - c1) &
    (a1 - c1) * (v1 - h1) + (a2 - c2) * (v2 - h2) = 0
  holds
    (u1 - v1)^2 + (u2 - v2)^2 = (r1 + r2)^2 or
    (u1 - v1)^2 + (u2 - v2)^2 = (r1 - r2)^2
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 029_feuerbach_s_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Feuerbach's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 029. This
% file contains no proof.

% Hundred Theorems item 029, "Feuerbach's Theorem": the nine-point circle of a
% nondegenerate triangle is tangent to its incircle or any excircle.
% This is a statement-only formalization and contains no proof.

feuerbach_s_theorem_029: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) * (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q))
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) * (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q))

  midpoint(P, Q: point): point =
    (# x_coord := (x_coord(P) + x_coord(Q)) / 2,
       y_coord := (y_coord(P) + y_coord(Q)) / 2 #)

  collinear(P, Q, R: point): bool =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) * (y_coord(P) - y_coord(R))
      = (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) * (x_coord(P) - x_coord(R))

  orthogonal(P, Q, R, S: point): bool =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) * (x_coord(R) - x_coord(S))
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) * (y_coord(R) - y_coord(S))
      = 0

  on_circle(P, center: point, radius: real): bool =
    squared_distance(center, P) = radius * radius

  feuerbach_s_theorem: bool =
    FORALL
        (A, B, C, M_bc, M_ca, M_ab, P_bc, P_ac, P_ab,
         N_center, I_center: point),
        (N_radius, I_radius: real):
      (0 <= N_radius
        AND 0 <= I_radius
        AND NOT collinear(A, B, C)
        AND M_ab = midpoint(A, B)
        AND M_bc = midpoint(B, C)
        AND M_ca = midpoint(C, A)
        AND on_circle(M_bc, N_center, N_radius)
        AND on_circle(M_ca, N_center, N_radius)
        AND on_circle(M_ab, N_center, N_radius)
        AND on_circle(P_bc, I_center, I_radius)
        AND on_circle(P_ac, I_center, I_radius)
        AND on_circle(P_ab, I_center, I_radius)
        AND collinear(A, B, P_ab)
        AND orthogonal(A, B, I_center, P_ab)
        AND collinear(B, C, P_bc)
        AND orthogonal(B, C, I_center, P_bc)
        AND collinear(A, C, P_ac)
        AND orthogonal(A, C, I_center, P_ac))
      IMPLIES
        ((N_center = I_center AND N_radius = I_radius)
          OR
          (EXISTS (T: point):
            on_circle(T, N_center, N_radius)
              AND on_circle(T, I_center, I_radius)
              AND
              (FORALL (U: point):
                (on_circle(U, N_center, N_radius)
                  AND on_circle(U, I_center, I_radius))
                IMPLIES U = T)))
END feuerbach_s_theorem_029

(** We start by some general notions for expressing the bijection *)

Definition identity (A:Type) := fun (a:A) => a.
Definition compose (A B C:Type) (g:B->C) (f:A->B) := fun (a:A) => g(f a).

Section Denumerability.

(** What it means to have the same cardinality *)
Definition same_cardinality (A:Type) (B:Type) :=
 {f:A->B & { g:B->A | 
  (forall b,(compose _ _ _ f g) b = (identity B) b) /\
   forall a,(compose _ _ _ g f) a = (identity A) a}}.

(** What it means to be a denumerable *)
Definition is_denumerable A := same_cardinality A nat.

Lemma same_cardinality_transitive :
 forall A B C, same_cardinality A B -> same_cardinality B C -> same_cardinality A C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma is_denumerable_transitive :
 forall A B, is_denumerable A -> same_cardinality B A -> is_denumerable B.
Proof.
Admitted.

End Denumerability.

(** We first prove that [Z] is denumerable *)

From Coq Require Import ZArith.
From Coq Require Import Lia.

(** An injection from [Z] to [nat] *)
Definition Z_to_nat_i (z:Z) :nat :=
   match z with 
   | Z0 => O
   | Zpos p => Nat.double (nat_of_P p)
   | Zneg p => pred (Nat.double (nat_of_P p))
   end.

(** Some lemmas about parity. *)
Lemma odd_pred2n: forall n : nat, Nat.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma even_2n : forall n : nat, Nat.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma even_odd_exists_dec : forall n, {p : nat | n = Nat.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** An injection from [nat] to [Z] *)
Definition nat_to_Z_i (n:nat) := 
  match even_odd_exists_dec n with
  | inl s => let (k, _) := s in Z_of_nat k
  | inr s => let (k, _) := s in Z.opp (Z_of_nat k)
  end.

Lemma double_eq_half_eq:forall m n, Nat.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma parity_mismatch_not_eq:forall m n, Nat.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma even_double : forall n, Nat.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma double_S_neq_pred:forall m n, ~Nat.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma eq_add_pred : forall n m : nat, pred n = pred m -> {n = m} + {n < 2 /\ m < 2}.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** We prove that the maps [Z_to_nat_i] is the right inverse of [nat_to_Z_i].*)

Lemma nat_to_Z_to_nat_i : forall (z:Z), nat_to_Z_i (Z_to_nat_i z) = z.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** We prove that the maps [Z_to_nat_i] is the left inverse of [nat_to_Z_i].*)

Lemma Z_to_nat_to_Z_i : forall (n:nat), Z_to_nat_i (nat_to_Z_i n) = n.
Proof.
Admitted. 

(** And hence [Z] is denumerable: *)

Theorem Z_is_denumerable:is_denumerable Z.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** Next we prove that [Q] and [Z] have the same cardinality *)

From QArithSternBrocot Require Import Q_field.

(** Here there is not much to prove, as [Z] and [Q] are isomorphic data-types.*)

(** An injection from [positive] to [Qpositive]: *)
Fixpoint positive_to_Qpositive_i (p:positive) : Qpositive := 
   match p with 
   | xI p => nR (positive_to_Qpositive_i p)
   | xO p => dL (positive_to_Qpositive_i p)
   | xH => One
   end. 

(** An injection from [Z] to [Q] *)
Definition Z_to_Q_i (z:Z) :=
   match z with 
   | Z0 => Zero
   | Zpos p => Qpos (positive_to_Qpositive_i p)
   | Zneg p => Qneg (positive_to_Qpositive_i p)
   end. 

(** An injection from [Qpositive] to [positive] *) 
Fixpoint Qpositive_to_positive_i (qp:Qpositive) : positive := 
   match qp with 
   | nR qp => xI (Qpositive_to_positive_i qp)
   | dL qp => xO (Qpositive_to_positive_i qp)
   | One => xH
   end. 

(** An injection from [Q] to [Z] *)
Definition Q_to_Z_i (q:Q) :=
   match q with 
   | Zero => Z0
   | Qpos qp => Zpos (Qpositive_to_positive_i qp)
   | Qneg qp => Zneg (Qpositive_to_positive_i qp)
   end. 

(** Proof that [Qpositive_to_positive_i] is the left inverse of [positive_to_Qpositive_i]:*)
Lemma Qpositive_to_positive_to_Qpositive_i : forall (p:positive), Qpositive_to_positive_i (positive_to_Qpositive_i p) = p.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** Proof that [Qpositive_to_positive_i] is the right inverse of [positive_to_Qpositive_i]:*)
Lemma positive_to_Qpositive_to_positive_i : forall qp, positive_to_Qpositive_i (Qpositive_to_positive_i qp) = qp.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** Proof that [Q_to_Z_i] is the left inverse of [Z_to_Q_i]:*)
Lemma Q_to_Z_to_Q_i : forall (z:Z), Q_to_Z_i (Z_to_Q_i z) = z.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** Proof that [Q_to_Z_i] is the right inverse of [Z_to_Q_i]:*)
Lemma Z_to_Q_to_Z_i : forall (q:Q), Z_to_Q_i (Q_to_Z_i q) = q.
Proof.
Admitted.

(** And hence [Q] is denumerable: *)
Theorem Q_is_denumerable: is_denumerable Q.
Proof.
Admitted.

title: 003_the_denumerability_of_the_rational_numbers
content:
(*  Title:      HOL/Library/Countable.thy
    Author:     Alexander Krauss, TU Muenchen
    Author:     Brian Huffman, Portland State University
    Author:     Jasmin Blanchette, TU Muenchen
*)

section \<open>Encoding (almost) everything into natural numbers\<close>

theory Countable
imports Old_Datatype HOL.Rat Nat_Bijection
begin

subsection \<open>The class of countable types\<close>

class countable =
  assumes ex_inj: "\<exists>to_nat :: 'a \<Rightarrow> nat. inj to_nat"

lemma countable_classI:
  fixes f :: "'a \<Rightarrow> nat"
  assumes "\<And>x y. f x = f y \<Longrightarrow> x = y"
  shows "OFCLASS('a, countable_class)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Conversion functions\<close>

definition to_nat :: "'a::countable \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "to_nat = (SOME f. inj f)"

definition from_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a::countable" where
  "from_nat = inv (to_nat :: 'a \<Rightarrow> nat)"

lemma inj_to_nat [simp]: "inj to_nat"
  by sorry

lemma inj_on_to_nat[simp, intro]: "inj_on to_nat S"
  by sorry

lemma surj_from_nat [simp]: "surj from_nat"
  by sorry

lemma to_nat_split [simp]: "to_nat x = to_nat y \<longleftrightarrow> x = y"
  by sorry

lemma from_nat_to_nat [simp]:
  "from_nat (to_nat x) = x"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Finite types are countable\<close>

subclass (in finite) countable
proof
  obtain n and f :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a"
    where "UNIV = f ` {i. i < n}" 
    by (metis finite_conv_nat_seg_image local.finite)
  then show "\<exists>to_nat :: 'a \<Rightarrow> nat. inj to_nat" 
    by (meson finite_imp_inj_to_nat_seg local.finite)
qed


subsection \<open>Automatically proving countability of old-style datatypes\<close>

context
begin

qualified inductive finite_item :: "'a Old_Datatype.item \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  undefined: "finite_item undefined"
| In0: "finite_item x \<Longrightarrow> finite_item (Old_Datatype.In0 x)"
| In1: "finite_item x \<Longrightarrow> finite_item (Old_Datatype.In1 x)"
| Leaf: "finite_item (Old_Datatype.Leaf a)"
| Scons: "\<lbrakk>finite_item x; finite_item y\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow> finite_item (Old_Datatype.Scons x y)"

qualified function nth_item :: "nat \<Rightarrow> ('a::countable) Old_Datatype.item"
where
  "nth_item 0 = undefined"
| "nth_item (Suc n) =
  (case sum_decode n of
    Inl i \<Rightarrow>
    (case sum_decode i of
      Inl j \<Rightarrow> Old_Datatype.In0 (nth_item j)
    | Inr j \<Rightarrow> Old_Datatype.In1 (nth_item j))
  | Inr i \<Rightarrow>
    (case sum_decode i of
      Inl j \<Rightarrow> Old_Datatype.Leaf (from_nat j)
    | Inr j \<Rightarrow>
      (case prod_decode j of
        (a, b) \<Rightarrow> Old_Datatype.Scons (nth_item a) (nth_item b))))"
by pat_completeness auto

lemma le_sum_encode_Inl: "x \<le> y \<Longrightarrow> x \<le> sum_encode (Inl y)"
  by sorry

lemma le_sum_encode_Inr: "x \<le> y \<Longrightarrow> x \<le> sum_encode (Inr y)"
  by sorry

qualified termination
by (relation "measure id")
  (auto simp flip: sum_encode_eq prod_encode_eq
    simp: le_imp_less_Suc le_sum_encode_Inl le_sum_encode_Inr
    le_prod_encode_1 le_prod_encode_2)

lemma nth_item_covers: "finite_item x \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>n. nth_item n = x"
  by sorry

theorem countable_datatype:
  fixes Rep :: "'b \<Rightarrow> ('a::countable) Old_Datatype.item"
  fixes Abs :: "('a::countable) Old_Datatype.item \<Rightarrow> 'b"
  fixes rep_set :: "('a::countable) Old_Datatype.item \<Rightarrow> bool"
  assumes type: "type_definition Rep Abs (Collect rep_set)"
  assumes finite_item: "\<And>x. rep_set x \<Longrightarrow> finite_item x"
  shows "OFCLASS('b, countable_class)"
  by sorry

ML \<open>
  fun old_countable_datatype_tac ctxt =
    SUBGOAL (fn (goal, _) =>
      let
        val ty_name =
          (case goal of
            (_ $ Const (\<^const_name>\<open>Pure.type\<close>, Type (\<^type_name>\<open>itself\<close>, [Type (n, _)]))) => n
          | _ => raise Match)
        val typedef_info = hd (Typedef.get_info ctxt ty_name)
        val typedef_thm = #type_definition (snd typedef_info)
        val pred_name =
          (case HOLogic.dest_Trueprop (Thm.concl_of typedef_thm) of
            (_ $ _ $ _ $ (_ $ Const (n, _))) => n
          | _ => raise Match)
        val induct_info = Inductive.the_inductive_global ctxt pred_name
        val pred_names = #names (fst induct_info)
        val induct_thms = #inducts (snd induct_info)
        val alist = pred_names ~~ induct_thms
        val induct_thm = the (AList.lookup (op =) alist pred_name)
        val vars = rev (Term.add_vars (Thm.prop_of induct_thm) [])
        val insts = vars |> map (fn (_, T) => try (Thm.cterm_of ctxt)
          (Const (\<^const_name>\<open>Countable.finite_item\<close>, T)))
        val induct_thm' = Thm.instantiate' [] insts induct_thm
        val rules = @{thms finite_item.intros}
      in
        SOLVED' (fn i => EVERY
          [resolve_tac ctxt @{thms countable_datatype} i,
           resolve_tac ctxt [typedef_thm] i,
           eresolve_tac ctxt [induct_thm'] i,
           REPEAT (resolve_tac ctxt rules i ORELSE assume_tac ctxt i)]) 1
      end)
\<close>

end


subsection \<open>Automatically proving countability of datatypes\<close>

ML_file \<open>../Tools/BNF/bnf_lfp_countable.ML\<close>

ML \<open>
fun countable_datatype_tac ctxt st =
  (case \<^try>\<open>HEADGOAL (old_countable_datatype_tac ctxt) st\<close> of
    SOME res => res
  | NONE => BNF_LFP_Countable.countable_datatype_tac ctxt st);

(* compatibility *)
fun countable_tac ctxt =
  SELECT_GOAL (countable_datatype_tac ctxt);
\<close>

method_setup countable_datatype = \<open>
  Scan.succeed (SIMPLE_METHOD o countable_datatype_tac)
\<close> "prove countable class instances for datatypes"


subsection \<open>More Countable types\<close>

text \<open>Naturals\<close>

instance nat :: countable
  by (rule countable_classI [of "id"]) simp

text \<open>Pairs\<close>

instance prod :: (countable, countable) countable
  by (rule countable_classI [of "\<lambda>(x, y). prod_encode (to_nat x, to_nat y)"])
    (auto simp add: prod_encode_eq)

text \<open>Sums\<close>

instance sum :: (countable, countable) countable
  by (rule countable_classI [of "(\<lambda>x. case x of Inl a \<Rightarrow> to_nat (False, to_nat a)
                                     | Inr b \<Rightarrow> to_nat (True, to_nat b))"])
    (simp split: sum.split_asm)

text \<open>Integers\<close>

instance int :: countable
  by (rule countable_classI [of int_encode]) (simp add: int_encode_eq)

text \<open>Options\<close>

instance option :: (countable) countable
  by countable_datatype

text \<open>Lists\<close>

instance list :: (countable) countable
  by countable_datatype

text \<open>String literals\<close>

instance String.literal :: countable
  by (rule countable_classI [of "to_nat \<circ> String.explode"]) (simp add: String.explode_inject)

text \<open>Functions\<close>

instance "fun" :: (finite, countable) countable
proof
  obtain xs :: "'a list" where xs: "set xs = UNIV"
    using finite_list [OF finite_UNIV] ..
  show "\<exists>to_nat::('a \<Rightarrow> 'b) \<Rightarrow> nat. inj to_nat"
  proof
    show "inj (\<lambda>f. to_nat (map f xs))"
      by (metis (no_types, lifting) ext UNIV_I injI map_eq_conv to_nat_split xs)
  qed
qed

text \<open>Typereps\<close>

instance typerep :: countable
  by countable_datatype


subsection \<open>The rationals are countably infinite\<close>

definition nat_to_rat_surj :: "nat \<Rightarrow> rat" where
  "nat_to_rat_surj n = (let (a, b) = prod_decode n in Fract (int_decode a) (int_decode b))"

lemma surj_nat_to_rat_surj: "surj nat_to_rat_surj"
  by sorry

lemma Rats_eq_range_nat_to_rat_surj: "\<rat> = range nat_to_rat_surj"
  by sorry

context field_char_0
begin

lemma Rats_eq_range_of_rat_o_nat_to_rat_surj:
  "\<rat> = range (of_rat \<circ> nat_to_rat_surj)"
  by sorry

lemma surj_of_rat_nat_to_rat_surj:
  "r \<in> \<rat> \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>n. r = of_rat (nat_to_rat_surj n)"
  by sorry

end

instance rat :: countable
proof
  show "\<exists>to_nat::rat \<Rightarrow> nat. inj to_nat"
    using surj_imp_inj_inv surj_nat_to_rat_surj by blast
qed

theorem rat_denum: "\<exists>f :: nat \<Rightarrow> rat. surj f"
  by sorry

end

;; Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 003,
;; "The Denumerability of the Rational Numbers": explicit Calkin-Wilf maps are
;; mutual inverses between ACL2 rational numbers and natural numbers. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun ht003-cw-encode (p q)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (nfix p) (nfix q))))
  (if (and (posp p) (posp q))
      (cond ((equal p q) 1)
            ((< p q)
             (* 2 (ht003-cw-encode p (- q p))))
            (t
             (+ 1 (* 2 (ht003-cw-encode (- p q) q)))))
    1))

(defun ht003-cw-decode-pair (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (and (posp n) (< 1 n))
      (let* ((previous (ht003-cw-decode-pair (- n 1)))
             (p (car previous))
             (q (cdr previous))
             (k (floor p q))
             (next-q (- (* (+ (* 2 k) 1) q) p)))
        (cons q next-q))
    (cons 1 1)))

(defun ht003-positive-index-to-rational (n)
  (let ((pair (ht003-cw-decode-pair n)))
    (/ (car pair) (cdr pair))))

(defun ht003-rational-to-natural (x)
  (if (rationalp x)
      (cond ((equal x 0) 0)
            ((< 0 x)
             (- (* 2
                   (ht003-cw-encode (numerator x) (denominator x)))
                1))
            (t
             (* 2
                (ht003-cw-encode (- (numerator x)) (denominator x)))))
    0))

(defun ht003-natural-to-rational (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (cond ((equal n 0) 0)
            ((equal (mod n 2) 1)
             (ht003-positive-index-to-rational (/ (+ n 1) 2)))
            (t
             (- (ht003-positive-index-to-rational (/ n 2)))))
    0))

(defun hundred-theorems-003-statement (x n)
  (and (implies (rationalp x)
                (and (natp (ht003-rational-to-natural x))
                     (equal
                      (ht003-natural-to-rational
                       (ht003-rational-to-natural x))
                      x)))
       (implies (natp n)
                (and (rationalp (ht003-natural-to-rational n))
                     (equal
                      (ht003-rational-to-natural
                       (ht003-natural-to-rational n))
                      n)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "The Denumerability of the Rational Numbers" from Hundred
-- Theorems item 003. This file contains no proof.

module DenumerabilityRationals where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infix 4 _≈_

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

scale : Int → Nat → Int
scale (pos m) n = pos (m * n)
scale (negsuc m) n = negative (suc m * n)

record Fraction : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator : Int
    denominator-minus-one : Nat

denominator : Fraction → Nat
denominator q = suc (Fraction.denominator-minus-one q)

_≈_ : Fraction → Fraction → Set
x ≈ y =
  scale (Fraction.numerator x) (denominator y) ≡
  scale (Fraction.numerator y) (denominator x)

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor exists
  field
    exists-value : A
    exists-property : P exists-value

record ExistsUnique (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor exists-unique
  field
    unique-value : A
    unique-property : P unique-value
    uniqueness : (x : A) → P x → x ≡ unique-value

denumerability-of-rational-numbers : Set
denumerability-of-rational-numbers =
  Exists (Nat → Fraction) (λ enumerate →
    (q : Fraction) →
    ExistsUnique Nat (λ n → enumerate n ≈ q))

% Statement-only formalization of "The Denumerability of the Rational Numbers" from Hundred
% Theorems item 003: a bijection between the natural and rational numbers. This file contains
% no proof.

the_denumerability_of_the_rational_numbers: THEORY
BEGIN
  the_denumerability_of_the_rational_numbers: bool =
    EXISTS (enumeration: [nat -> rat]):
      (FORALL (m, n: nat):
        enumeration(m) = enumeration(n) IMPLIES m = n)
      AND (FORALL (q: rat):
        EXISTS (n: nat): enumeration(n) = q)
END the_denumerability_of_the_rational_numbers

title: 030_the_ballot_problem
content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2022 Bhavik Mehta, Kexing Ying. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Bhavik Mehta, Kexing Ying
-/
import Mathlib.Probability.UniformOn

/-!
# Ballot problem

This file proves Theorem 30 from the [100 Theorems List](https://www.cs.ru.nl/~freek/100/).

The ballot problem asks, if in an election, candidate A receives `p` votes whereas candidate B
receives `q` votes where `p > q`, what is the probability that candidate A is strictly ahead
throughout the count. The probability of this is `(p - q) / (p + q)`.

## Main definitions

* `countedSequence`: given natural numbers `p` and `q`, `countedSequence p q` is the set of
  all lists containing `p` of `1`s and `q` of `-1`s representing the votes of candidate A and B
  respectively.
* `staysPositive`: is the set of lists of integers which suffix has positive sum. In particular,
  the intersection of this set with `countedSequence` is the set of lists where candidate A is
  strictly ahead.

## Main result

* `ballot_problem`: the ballot problem.

-/


open Set ProbabilityTheory MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal

namespace Ballot

/-- The set of nonempty lists of integers which suffix has positive sum. -/
def staysPositive : Set (List ℤ) :=
  {l | ∀ l₂, l₂ ≠ [] → l₂ <:+ l → 0 < l₂.sum}

@[simp]
theorem staysPositive_nil : [] ∈ staysPositive :=
  fun _ hl hl₁ => (hl (List.eq_nil_of_suffix_nil hl₁)).elim

theorem staysPositive_suffix {l₁ l₂ : List ℤ} (hl₂ : l₂ ∈ staysPositive) (h : l₁ <:+ l₂) :
    l₁ ∈ staysPositive := fun l hne hl ↦ hl₂ l hne <| hl.trans h

theorem staysPositive_cons {x : ℤ} {l : List ℤ} :
    x::l ∈ staysPositive ↔ l ∈ staysPositive ∧ 0 < x + l.sum := by sorry
theorem sum_nonneg_of_staysPositive : ∀ {l : List ℤ}, l ∈ staysPositive → 0 ≤ l.sum := by sorry
theorem staysPositive_cons_pos (x : ℤ) (hx : 0 < x) (l : List ℤ) :
    (x::l) ∈ staysPositive ↔ l ∈ staysPositive := by sorry
def countedSequence (p q : ℕ) : Set (List ℤ) :=
  {l | l.count 1 = p ∧ l.count (-1) = q ∧ ∀ x ∈ l, x = (1 : ℤ) ∨ x = -1}

open scoped List in
/-- An alternative definition of `countedSequence` that uses `List.Perm`. -/
theorem mem_countedSequence_iff_perm {p q l} :
    l ∈ countedSequence p q ↔ l ~ List.replicate p (1 : ℤ) ++ List.replicate q (-1) := by sorry
theorem counted_right_zero (p : ℕ) : countedSequence p 0 = {List.replicate p 1} := by sorry
theorem counted_left_zero (q : ℕ) : countedSequence 0 q = {List.replicate q (-1)} := by sorry
theorem mem_of_mem_countedSequence {p q} {l} (hl : l ∈ countedSequence p q) {x : ℤ} (hx : x ∈ l) :
    x = 1 ∨ x = -1 :=
  hl.2.2 x hx

theorem length_of_mem_countedSequence {p q} {l : List ℤ} (hl : l ∈ countedSequence p q) :
    l.length = p + q := by simp [(mem_countedSequence_iff_perm.1 hl).length_eq]

theorem counted_eq_nil_iff {p q : ℕ} {l : List ℤ} (hl : l ∈ countedSequence p q) :
    l = [] ↔ p = 0 ∧ q = 0 :=
  List.length_eq_zero_iff.symm.trans <| by simp [length_of_mem_countedSequence hl]

theorem counted_ne_nil_left {p q : ℕ} (hp : p ≠ 0) {l : List ℤ} (hl : l ∈ countedSequence p q) :
    l ≠ [] := by simp [counted_eq_nil_iff hl, hp]

theorem counted_ne_nil_right {p q : ℕ} (hq : q ≠ 0) {l : List ℤ} (hl : l ∈ countedSequence p q) :
    l ≠ [] := by simp [counted_eq_nil_iff hl, hq]

theorem counted_succ_succ (p q : ℕ) :
    countedSequence (p + 1) (q + 1) =
      List.cons 1 '' countedSequence p (q + 1) ∪ List.cons (-1) '' countedSequence (p + 1) q := by sorry
theorem countedSequence_finite : ∀ p q : ℕ, (countedSequence p q).Finite := by sorry
theorem countedSequence_nonempty : ∀ p q : ℕ, (countedSequence p q).Nonempty := by sorry
theorem sum_of_mem_countedSequence {p q} {l : List ℤ} (hl : l ∈ countedSequence p q) :
    l.sum = p - q := by simp [(mem_countedSequence_iff_perm.1 hl).sum_eq, sub_eq_add_neg]

theorem disjoint_bits (p q : ℕ) :
    Disjoint (List.cons 1 '' countedSequence p (q + 1))
      (List.cons (-1) '' countedSequence (p + 1) q) := by sorry
open MeasureTheory.Measure

private local instance measurableSpace_list_int : MeasurableSpace (List ℤ) := ⊤

private local instance measurableSingletonClass_list_int : MeasurableSingletonClass (List ℤ) :=
  { measurableSet_singleton := fun _ => trivial }

private theorem list_int_measurableSet {s : Set (List ℤ)} : MeasurableSet s := trivial

theorem count_countedSequence : ∀ p q : ℕ, count (countedSequence p q) = (p + q).choose p := by sorry
theorem first_vote_pos :
    ∀ p q,
      0 < p + q → uniformOn (countedSequence p q : Set (List ℤ)) {l | l.headI = 1} = p / (p + q) := by sorry
theorem headI_mem_of_nonempty {α : Type*} [Inhabited α] : ∀ {l : List α} (_ : l ≠ []), l.headI ∈ l := by sorry
theorem first_vote_neg (p q : ℕ) (h : 0 < p + q) :
    uniformOn (countedSequence p q) {l | l.headI = 1}ᶜ = q / (p + q) := by sorry
theorem ballot_same (p : ℕ) : uniformOn (countedSequence (p + 1) (p + 1)) staysPositive = 0 := by sorry
theorem ballot_edge (p : ℕ) : uniformOn (countedSequence (p + 1) 0) staysPositive = 1 := by sorry
theorem countedSequence_int_pos_counted_succ_succ (p q : ℕ) :
    countedSequence (p + 1) (q + 1) ∩ {l | l.headI = 1} =
      (countedSequence p (q + 1)).image (List.cons 1) := by sorry
theorem ballot_pos (p q : ℕ) :
    uniformOn (countedSequence (p + 1) (q + 1) ∩ {l | l.headI = 1}) staysPositive =
      uniformOn (countedSequence p (q + 1)) staysPositive := by sorry
theorem countedSequence_int_neg_counted_succ_succ (p q : ℕ) :
    countedSequence (p + 1) (q + 1) ∩ {l | l.headI = 1}ᶜ =
      (countedSequence (p + 1) q).image (List.cons (-1)) := by sorry
theorem ballot_neg (p q : ℕ) (qp : q < p) :
    uniformOn (countedSequence (p + 1) (q + 1) ∩ {l | l.headI = 1}ᶜ) staysPositive =
      uniformOn (countedSequence (p + 1) q) staysPositive := by sorry
theorem ballot_problem' :
    ∀ q p, q < p → (uniformOn (countedSequence p q) staysPositive).toReal = (p - q) / (p + q) := by sorry
theorem ballot_problem :
    ∀ q p, q < p → uniformOn (countedSequence p q) staysPositive = (p - q) / (p + q) := by sorry
end Ballot

SOFTWARE.

Require Import Arith.
Require Import ZArith.
Require Import String.
Require Import List.
Require Import Psatz.
Require Import Factorial.

(* Recurrence part of the inductive proof:  *)

Lemma recurrence a b Afirst Bfirst all Afirst_ahead Bfirst_ahead ahead :
  0 < b -> b < a ->
  (a + b) * Afirst = a * all ->
  (a + b) * Bfirst = b * all ->
  Afirst + Bfirst = all ->
  (a - 1 + b) * Afirst_ahead = (a - b - 1) * Afirst ->
  (a - 1 + b) * Bfirst_ahead = (a - (b - 1)) * Bfirst ->
  Afirst_ahead + Bfirst_ahead = ahead ->
  (a + b) * ahead = (a - b) * all.
Proof.
Admitted.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint cartesian_product {A B} (xs : list A) (ys : list B) : list (A * B) :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs => map (pair x) ys ++ cartesian_product xs ys
  end.

Fixpoint picks {A} n (l : list A) : list (list A) :=
  match n with
  | O => [[]]
  | S n => map (fun x => fst x :: snd x) (cartesian_product l (picks n l))
  end.

Fixpoint pickbools n :=
  match n with
  | O => [[]]
  | S n => map (cons true) (pickbools n) ++ map (cons false) (pickbools n)
  end.

(** non empty suffixes *)
Fixpoint proper_suffixes {A} (l : list A) : list (list A) :=
  match l with
  | [] => []
  | x :: l => (x :: l) :: proper_suffixes l
  end.

(** For our notion of "throughout" we choose that lists represent the
    last vote first, and hence we use suffixes *)
Definition throughout {A} f (l : list A) := forallb f (proper_suffixes l).

Definition countb b l := count_occ Bool.bool_dec l b.

Notation length := length.

Lemma countb_false l : countb false l = length l - countb true l.
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition winb votes := countb false votes <? countb true votes.

Definition sumtrue p l := countb true l =? p.

Lemma filter_app {A} f (l1 l2 : list A) :
  filter f (l1 ++ l2) = filter f l1 ++ filter f l2.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma map_filter {A B} f (g : A -> B) l :
  filter f (map g l) = map g (filter (fun b => f (g b)) l).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma filter_filter {A} (f g : A -> bool) l :
  filter f (filter g l) = filter (fun b => andb (g b) (f b)) l.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma filter_ext {A} f g l : (forall x : A, f x = g x) -> filter f l = filter g l.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma filter_sub {A} f g l : (forall x : A, f x = true -> g x = true) -> filter f l = filter g (filter f l).
Proof.
Admitted.

Fixpoint binomial (n k : nat) : nat :=
  match n with
  | 0 =>
    match k with
    | 0 => 1
    | S _ => 0
    end
  | S n' =>
    match k with
    | 0 => 1
    | S k' => (binomial n' k') + (binomial n' k)
    end
  end.

Lemma binomial_lt n p : n < p -> binomial n p = 0.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma binomial_0_r n : binomial n 0 = 1.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma binomial_1_r n : binomial n 1 = n.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma binomial_diag n : binomial n n = 1.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma binomial_factorial n k : k <= n -> fact k * fact (n - k) * binomial n k = fact n.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma binomial_complement n k : k <= n -> binomial n k = binomial n (n - k).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma binomial_S n k :
  k <= n ->
  S n * binomial n k = S k * binomial (S n) (S k).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma count_sumtrue_cons_true p l :
  filter (sumtrue (S p)) (map (cons true) l) =
  map (cons true) (filter (sumtrue p) l).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma count_0_wins_cons_true l :
  filter (sumtrue 0) (map (cons true) l) = [].
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma count_sumtrue_cons_false p l :
  filter (sumtrue p) (map (cons false) l) =
  map (cons false) (filter (sumtrue p) l).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma count_sumtrue p n :
  length (filter (sumtrue p) (pickbools n)) = binomial n p.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma first_vote_split p q :
  filter (sumtrue (1 + p)) (pickbools (1 + p + q)) =
  map (cons true) (filter (sumtrue p) (pickbools (p + q))) ++
  map (cons false) (filter (sumtrue (1 + p)) (pickbools (p + q))).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma pickbools_length n : pickbools n = filter (fun l => length l =? n) (pickbools n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma counting_wins p q :
  q < p ->
  filter winb (filter (sumtrue p) (pickbools (p + q))) =
  filter (sumtrue p) (pickbools (p + q)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma pickbools_wins_minus p q :
  q <= p ->
  (p - q) * length (filter (sumtrue p) (pickbools (p + q))) =
  (p - q) * length (filter winb (filter (sumtrue p) (pickbools (p + q)))).
Proof.
Admitted.
  
Lemma bertrand_ballot_bool_eq p q :
  p <> 0 ->
  p = q ->
  let l := filter (fun votes => countb true votes =? p) (pickbools (p + q)) in
  (p + q) * length (filter (throughout winb) l) =
  (p - q) * length (filter winb l).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem bertrand_ballot_bool p q :
  q <= p ->
  let l := filter (sumtrue p) (pickbools (p + q)) in
  (p + q) * length (filter (throughout winb) l) =
  (p - q) * length (filter winb l).
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition count_votes := count_occ string_dec.

Definition wins A B votes := count_votes votes B <? count_votes votes A.

Open Scope string_scope.

(** we enumerate all lists of votes with:
     - p + q votes for (A or B)
     - p votes for A   *)

Theorem bertrand_ballot p q :
  let l := filter (fun votes => count_votes votes "A" =? p)%nat (picks (p + q) ["A"; "B"]) in
  p >= q ->
  (p + q) * List.length (filter (throughout (wins "A" "B")) l) =
  (p - q) * List.length (filter (wins "A" "B") l).
Proof.
Admitted.

title: 030_the_ballot_problem
content:
(*   Title: HOL/ex/Ballot.thy
     Author: Lukas Bulwahn <lukas.bulwahn-at-gmail.com>
     Author: Johannes Hölzl <hoelzl@in.tum.de>
*)

section \<open>Bertrand's Ballot Theorem\<close>

theory Ballot
imports
  Complex_Main
  "HOL-Library.FuncSet"
begin

subsection \<open>Preliminaries\<close>

lemma card_bij':
  assumes "f \<in> A \<rightarrow> B" "\<And>x. x \<in> A \<Longrightarrow> g (f x) = x"
    and "g \<in> B \<rightarrow> A" "\<And>x. x \<in> B \<Longrightarrow> f (g x) = x"
  shows "card A = card B"
  by sorry

subsection \<open>Formalization of Problem Statement\<close>

subsubsection \<open>Basic Definitions\<close>

datatype vote = A | B

definition
  "all_countings a b = card {f \<in> {1 .. a + b} \<rightarrow>\<^sub>E {A, B}.
      card {x \<in> {1 .. a + b}. f x = A} = a \<and> card {x \<in> {1 .. a + b}. f x = B} = b}"

definition
  "valid_countings a b =
    card {f\<in>{1..a+b} \<rightarrow>\<^sub>E {A, B}.
      card {x\<in>{1..a+b}. f x = A} = a \<and> card {x\<in>{1..a+b}. f x = B} = b \<and>
      (\<forall>m\<in>{1..a+b}. card {x\<in>{1..m}. f x = A} > card {x\<in>{1..m}. f x = B})}"

subsubsection \<open>Equivalence with Set Cardinality\<close>

lemma Collect_on_transfer:
  assumes "rel_set R X Y"
  shows "rel_fun (rel_fun R (=)) (rel_set R) (\<lambda>P. {x\<in>X. P x}) (\<lambda>P. {y\<in>Y. P y})"
  by sorry

lemma rel_fun_trans:
  "rel_fun P Q g g' \<Longrightarrow> rel_fun R P f f' \<Longrightarrow> rel_fun R Q (\<lambda>x. g (f x)) (\<lambda>y. g' (f' y))"
  by sorry

lemma rel_fun_trans2:
  "rel_fun P1 (rel_fun P2 Q) g g' \<Longrightarrow> rel_fun R P1 f1 f1' \<Longrightarrow> rel_fun R P2 f2 f2' \<Longrightarrow>
    rel_fun R Q (\<lambda>x. g (f1 x) (f2 x)) (\<lambda>y. g' (f1' y) (f2' y))"
  by sorry

lemma rel_fun_trans2':
  "rel_fun R (=) f1 f1' \<Longrightarrow> rel_fun R (=) f2 f2' \<Longrightarrow>
    rel_fun R (=) (\<lambda>x. g (f1 x) (f2 x)) (\<lambda>y. g (f1' y) (f2' y))"
  by sorry

lemma rel_fun_const: "rel_fun R (=) (\<lambda>x. a) (\<lambda>y. a)"
  by sorry

lemma rel_fun_conj:
  "rel_fun R (=) f f' \<Longrightarrow> rel_fun R (=) g g' \<Longrightarrow> rel_fun R (=) (\<lambda>x. f x \<and> g x) (\<lambda>y. f' y \<and> g' y)"
  by sorry

lemma rel_fun_ball:
  "(\<And>i. i \<in> I \<Longrightarrow> rel_fun R (=) (f i) (f' i)) \<Longrightarrow> rel_fun R (=) (\<lambda>x. \<forall>i\<in>I. f i x) (\<lambda>y. \<forall>i\<in>I. f' i y)"
  by sorry

lemma
  shows all_countings_set: "all_countings a b = card {V\<in>Pow {0..<a+b}. card V = a}"
      (is "_ = card ?A")
    and valid_countings_set: "valid_countings a b =
      card {V\<in>Pow {0..<a+b}. card V = a \<and> (\<forall>m\<in>{1..a+b}. card ({0..<m} \<inter> V) > m - card ({0..<m} \<inter> V))}"
      (is "_ = card ?V")
  by sorry

lemma all_countings [code]: "all_countings a b = (a + b) choose a"
  by sorry

subsection \<open>Facts About \<^term>\<open>valid_countings\<close>\<close>

subsubsection \<open>Non-Recursive Cases\<close>

lemma card_V_eq_a: "V \<subseteq> {0..<a} \<Longrightarrow> card V = a \<longleftrightarrow> V = {0..<a}"
  by sorry

lemma valid_countings_a_0: "valid_countings a 0 = 1"
  by sorry

lemma valid_countings_eq_zero:
  "a \<le> b \<Longrightarrow> 0 < b \<Longrightarrow> valid_countings a b = 0"
  by sorry

lemma Ico_subset_finite: "i \<subseteq> {a ..< b::nat} \<Longrightarrow> finite i"
  by sorry

lemma Icc_Suc2: "a \<le> b \<Longrightarrow> {a..Suc b} = insert (Suc b) {a..b}"
  by sorry

lemma Ico_Suc2: "a \<le> b \<Longrightarrow> {a..<Suc b} = insert b {a..<b}"
  by sorry

lemma valid_countings_Suc_Suc:
  assumes "b < a"
  shows "valid_countings (Suc a) (Suc b) = valid_countings a (Suc b) + valid_countings (Suc a) b"
  by sorry

lemma valid_countings:
  "(a + b) * valid_countings a b = (a - b) * ((a + b) choose a)"
  by sorry

lemma valid_countings_eq[code]:
  "valid_countings a b = (if a + b = 0 then 1 else ((a - b) * ((a + b) choose a)) div (a + b))"
  by sorry

subsection \<open>Relation Between \<^term>\<open>valid_countings\<close> and \<^term>\<open>all_countings\<close>\<close>

lemma main_nat: "(a + b) * valid_countings a b = (a - b) * all_countings a b"
  by sorry

lemma main_real:
  assumes "b < a"
  shows "valid_countings a b = (a - b) / (a + b) * all_countings a b"
  by sorry

lemma
  "valid_countings a b = (if a \<le> b then (if b = 0 then 1 else 0) else (a - b) / (a + b) * all_countings a b)"
  by sorry

subsubsection \<open>Executable Definition\<close>

value "all_countings 1 0"
value "all_countings 0 1"
value "all_countings 1 1"
value "all_countings 2 1"
value "all_countings 1 2"
value "all_countings 2 4"
value "all_countings 4 2"

subsubsection \<open>Executable Definition\<close>

value "valid_countings 1 0"
value "valid_countings 0 1"
value "valid_countings 1 1"
value "valid_countings 2 1"
value "valid_countings 1 2"
value "valid_countings 2 4"
value "valid_countings 4 2"

end

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__030, "The Ballot Problem": for natural vote totals
;; p and q, the number of A/B vote sequences in which A is strictly ahead
;; after every vote satisfies the classical ballot counting identity relative
;; to all sequences with p votes for A and q votes for B. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun ht030-prepend-vote-to-each (vote sequences)
  (if (consp sequences)
      (cons (cons vote (car sequences))
            (ht030-prepend-vote-to-each vote (cdr sequences)))
    nil))

(defun ht030-vote-sequences (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (list nil)
    (let ((shorter (ht030-vote-sequences (- n 1))))
      (append (ht030-prepend-vote-to-each :a shorter)
              (ht030-prepend-vote-to-each :b shorter)))))

(defun ht030-count-vote (vote votes)
  (if (consp votes)
      (+ (if (equal (car votes) vote) 1 0)
         (ht030-count-vote vote (cdr votes)))
    0))

(defun ht030-has-vote-totals-p (votes p q)
  (and (true-listp votes)
       (equal (ht030-count-vote :a votes) p)
       (equal (ht030-count-vote :b votes) q)))

(defun ht030-strictly-ahead-from-p (votes a-count b-count)
  (if (consp votes)
      (let* ((next-a (+ a-count
                        (if (equal (car votes) :a) 1 0)))
             (next-b (+ b-count
                        (if (equal (car votes) :b) 1 0))))
        (and (< next-b next-a)
             (ht030-strictly-ahead-from-p
              (cdr votes) next-a next-b)))
    t))

(defun ht030-strictly-ahead-p (votes)
  (and (true-listp votes)
       (ht030-strictly-ahead-from-p votes 0 0)))

(defun ht030-count-all-with-totals (sequences p q)
  (if (consp sequences)
      (+ (if (ht030-has-vote-totals-p (car sequences) p q)
             1
           0)
         (ht030-count-all-with-totals (cdr sequences) p q))
    0))

(defun ht030-count-valid-with-totals (sequences p q)
  (if (consp sequences)
      (+ (if (and (ht030-has-vote-totals-p
                   (car sequences) p q)
                  (ht030-strictly-ahead-p (car sequences)))
             1
           0)
         (ht030-count-valid-with-totals
          (cdr sequences) p q))
    0))

(defun ht030-all-countings (p q)
  (if (and (natp p) (natp q))
      (ht030-count-all-with-totals
       (ht030-vote-sequences (+ p q)) p q)
    0))

(defun ht030-valid-countings (p q)
  (if (and (natp p) (natp q))
      (ht030-count-valid-with-totals
       (ht030-vote-sequences (+ p q)) p q)
    0))

(defun ht030-natural-difference (p q)
  (if (and (natp p)
           (natp q)
           (<= q p))
      (- p q)
    0))

(defun hundred-theorems-030-the-ballot-problem-statement (p q)
  (implies
   (and (natp p)
        (natp q))
   (equal
    (* (+ p q)
       (ht030-valid-countings p q))
    (* (ht030-natural-difference p q)
       (ht030-all-countings p q)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q
