module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Body
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Measure
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Group.FundamentalDomain

/-!
# Geometry of numbers

In this file we prove some of the fundamental theorems in the geometry of numbers, as studied by
Hermann Minkowski.

## Main results

* `exists_pair_mem_lattice_not_disjoint_vadd`: Blichfeldt's principle, existence of two distinct
  points in a subgroup such that the translates of a set by these two points are not disjoint when
  the covolume of the subgroup is larger than the volume of the set.
* `exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_lt_measure`: Minkowski's theorem, existence of
  a non-zero lattice point inside a convex symmetric domain of large enough volume.

## TODO

* Calculate the volume of the fundamental domain of a finite index subgroup
* Voronoi diagrams
* See [Pete L. Clark, *Abstract Geometry of Numbers: Linear Forms* (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2119)
  for some more ideas.

## References

* [Pete L. Clark, *Geometry of Numbers with Applications to Number Theory*][clark_gon] p.28
-/

public section


namespace MeasureTheory

open ENNReal Module MeasureTheory MeasureTheory.Measure Set Filter

open scoped Pointwise NNReal

variable {E L : Type*} [MeasurableSpace E] {μ : Measure E} {F s : Set E}

/-- **Blichfeldt's Theorem**. If the volume of the set `s` is larger than the covolume of the
countable subgroup `L` of `E`, then there exist two distinct points `x, y ∈ L` such that `(x + s)`
and `(y + s)` are not disjoint. -/
theorem exists_pair_mem_lattice_not_disjoint_vadd [AddGroup L] [Countable L] [AddAction L E]
    [MeasurableSpace L] [MeasurableVAdd L E] [VAddInvariantMeasure L E μ]
    (fund : IsAddFundamentalDomain L F μ) (hS : NullMeasurableSet s μ) (h : μ F < μ s) :
    ∃ x y : L, x ≠ y ∧ ¬Disjoint (x +ᵥ s) (y +ᵥ s) := by sorry
theorem exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_lt_measure [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [NormedSpace ℝ E] [BorelSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [IsAddHaarMeasure μ]
    {L : AddSubgroup E} [Countable L] (fund : IsAddFundamentalDomain L F μ)
    (h_symm : ∀ x ∈ s, -x ∈ s) (h_conv : Convex ℝ s) (h : μ F * 2 ^ finrank ℝ E < μ s) :
    ∃ x ≠ 0, ((x : L) : E) ∈ s := by sorry
theorem exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_le_measure [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [NormedSpace ℝ E] [BorelSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [Nontrivial E] [IsAddHaarMeasure μ]
    {L : AddSubgroup E} [Countable L] [DiscreteTopology L] (fund : IsAddFundamentalDomain L F μ)
    (h_symm : ∀ x ∈ s, -x ∈ s) (h_conv : Convex ℝ s) (h_cpt : IsCompact s)
    (h : μ F * 2 ^ finrank ℝ E ≤ μ s) :
    ∃ x ≠ 0, ((x : L) : E) ∈ s := by sorry
end MeasureTheory

title: 040_minkowski_s_fundamental_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Minkowski's Fundamental Theorem" from
  Hundred Theorems item 040. It states Blichfeldt's lattice-point principle
  and the strict and compact forms of Minkowski's convex-body theorem for
  Lebesgue volume and the integer lattice in finite-dimensional real space.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

From Stdlib Require Import Vectors.Fin Reals ZArith.

Local Open Scope R_scope.

Definition euclidean_point (n : nat) : Type := Fin.t n -> R.

Definition euclidean_set (n : nat) : Type := euclidean_point n -> Prop.

Definition point_equal {n : nat}
    (x y : euclidean_point n) : Prop :=
  forall i : Fin.t n, x i = y i.

Definition point_sub {n : nat}
    (x y : euclidean_point n) : euclidean_point n :=
  fun i => x i - y i.

Definition point_neg {n : nat}
    (x : euclidean_point n) : euclidean_point n :=
  fun i => - x i.

Definition point_zero {n : nat} : euclidean_point n :=
  fun _ => 0.

Definition point_distinct {n : nat}
    (x y : euclidean_point n) : Prop :=
  ~ point_equal x y.

Definition point_nonzero {n : nat}
    (x : euclidean_point n) : Prop :=
  point_distinct x point_zero.

Definition integer_vector {n : nat}
    (x : euclidean_point n) : Prop :=
  forall i : Fin.t n, exists z : Z, x i = IZR z.

Definition convex_euclidean_set {n : nat}
    (body : euclidean_set n) : Prop :=
  forall x y : euclidean_point n,
    body x ->
    body y ->
    forall t : R,
      0 <= t <= 1 ->
      body (fun i => (1 - t) * x i + t * y i).

Definition origin_symmetric {n : nat}
    (body : euclidean_set n) : Prop :=
  forall x : euclidean_point n, body x -> body (point_neg x).

Definition euclidean_close {n : nat}
    (x y : euclidean_point n) (epsilon : R) : Prop :=
  forall i : Fin.t n, Rabs (x i - y i) < epsilon.

Definition euclidean_converges {n : nat}
    (u : nat -> euclidean_point n) (x : euclidean_point n) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists N : nat,
      forall k : nat,
        (N <= k)%nat ->
        euclidean_close (u k) x epsilon.

Definition strictly_increasing (r : nat -> nat) : Prop :=
  forall i j : nat, (i < j)%nat -> (r i < r j)%nat.

Definition compact_euclidean_set {n : nat}
    (body : euclidean_set n) : Prop :=
  forall u : nat -> euclidean_point n,
    (forall k : nat, body (u k)) ->
    exists r : nat -> nat,
      strictly_increasing r /\
      exists x : euclidean_point n,
        body x /\ euclidean_converges (fun k => u (r k)) x.

Fixpoint fin_product (n : nat) : (Fin.t n -> R) -> R :=
  match n as k return (Fin.t k -> R) -> R with
  | O => fun _ => 1
  | S k =>
      fun factors =>
        factors Fin.F1 *
        fin_product k (fun i => factors (Fin.FS i))
  end.

Fixpoint partial_sum (terms : nat -> R) (count : nat) : R :=
  match count with
  | O => 0
  | S k => partial_sum terms k + terms k
  end.

(* The lower-cut relation c <= sum terms, including divergent sums as infinity. *)
Definition nonnegative_series_ge
    (terms : nat -> R) (c : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists count : nat,
      c - epsilon < partial_sum terms count.

Definition open_box {n : nat}
    (lower upper x : euclidean_point n) : Prop :=
  forall i : Fin.t n, lower i < x i /\ x i < upper i.

Definition valid_box {n : nat}
    (lower upper : euclidean_point n) : Prop :=
  forall i : Fin.t n, lower i < upper i.

Definition box_volume {n : nat}
    (lower upper : euclidean_point n) : R :=
  fin_product n (fun i => upper i - lower i).

Definition countable_open_box_cover {n : nat}
    (body : euclidean_set n)
    (lower upper : nat -> euclidean_point n) : Prop :=
  (forall k : nat, valid_box (lower k) (upper k)) /\
  forall x : euclidean_point n,
    body x ->
    exists k : nat, open_box (lower k) (upper k) x.

(*
  This is the lower Dedekind cut of Lebesgue outer volume: c belongs to
  the cut exactly when every countable open-box cover has total volume
  at least c. It represents finite values and positive infinity uniformly.
*)
Definition lebesgue_outer_volume_ge {n : nat}
    (body : euclidean_set n) (c : R) : Prop :=
  forall lower upper : nat -> euclidean_point n,
    countable_open_box_cover body lower upper ->
    nonnegative_series_ge
      (fun k => box_volume (lower k) (upper k)) c.

Definition outer_volume_sum_ge {n : nat}
    (left right : euclidean_set n) (c : R) : Prop :=
  exists a b : R,
    lebesgue_outer_volume_ge left a /\
    lebesgue_outer_volume_ge right b /\
    c <= a + b.

Definition set_intersection {n : nat}
    (left right : euclidean_set n) : euclidean_set n :=
  fun x => left x /\ right x.

Definition set_difference {n : nat}
    (left right : euclidean_set n) : euclidean_set n :=
  fun x => left x /\ ~ right x.

(* Caratheodory measurability for the concrete outer volume above. *)
Definition lebesgue_measurable {n : nat}
    (body : euclidean_set n) : Prop :=
  forall (test : euclidean_set n) (c : R),
    lebesgue_outer_volume_ge test c <->
    outer_volume_sum_ge
      (set_intersection test body)
      (set_difference test body) c.

Definition lebesgue_volume_ge {n : nat}
    (body : euclidean_set n) (c : R) : Prop :=
  lebesgue_outer_volume_ge body c.

Definition lebesgue_volume_gt {n : nat}
    (body : euclidean_set n) (c : R) : Prop :=
  exists epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon /\
    lebesgue_outer_volume_ge body (c + epsilon).

Theorem blichfeldt_principle :
  forall (dimension_index : nat)
         (body : euclidean_set (S dimension_index)),
    lebesgue_measurable body ->
    lebesgue_volume_gt body 1 ->
    exists x y : euclidean_point (S dimension_index),
      body x /\
      body y /\
      point_distinct x y /\
      integer_vector (point_sub x y).
Admitted.

Theorem minkowski_fundamental_theorem :
  forall (dimension_index : nat)
         (body : euclidean_set (S dimension_index)),
    convex_euclidean_set body ->
    origin_symmetric body ->
    lebesgue_measurable body ->
    lebesgue_volume_gt body (2 ^ (S dimension_index)) ->
    exists x : euclidean_point (S dimension_index),
      body x /\ point_nonzero x /\ integer_vector x.
Admitted.

Theorem minkowski_compact :
  forall (dimension_index : nat)
         (body : euclidean_set (S dimension_index)),
    convex_euclidean_set body ->
    compact_euclidean_set body ->
    origin_symmetric body ->
    lebesgue_volume_ge body (2 ^ (S dimension_index)) ->
    exists x : euclidean_point (S dimension_index),
      body x /\ point_nonzero x /\ integer_vector x.
Admitted.

title: 040_minkowski_s_fundamental_theorem
content:
(*
  File:    Minkowskis_Theorem.thy
  Author:  Manuel Eberl <manuel@pruvisto.org>

  A proof of Blichfeldt's and Minkowski's theorem about the relation between
  subsets of the Euclidean space, the Lebesgue measure, and the integer lattice.
*)
section \<open>Minkowski's theorem\<close>
theory Minkowskis_Theorem
  imports "HOL-Analysis.Equivalence_Lebesgue_Henstock_Integration"
begin

(* Could be generalised to arbitrary euclidean spaces and full-dimensional lattices *)

subsection \<open>Miscellaneous material\<close>

lemma bij_betw_UN:
  assumes "bij_betw f A B"
  shows   "(\<Union>n\<in>A. g (f n)) = (\<Union>n\<in>B. g n)"
  by sorry

definition of_int_vec where
  "of_int_vec v = (\<chi> i. of_int (v $ i))"

lemma of_int_vec_nth [simp]: "of_int_vec v $ n = of_int (v $ n)"
  by sorry

lemma of_int_vec_eq_iff [simp]:
  "(of_int_vec a :: ('a :: ring_char_0) ^ 'n) = of_int_vec b \<longleftrightarrow> a = b"
  by sorry

lemma inj_axis:
  assumes "c \<noteq> 0"
  shows   "inj (\<lambda>k. axis k c :: ('a :: {zero}) ^ 'n)"
  by sorry

lemma compactD:
  assumes "compact (A :: 'a :: metric_space set)" "range f \<subseteq> A"
  shows   "\<exists>h l. strict_mono (h::nat\<Rightarrow>nat) \<and> (f \<circ> h) \<longlonglongrightarrow> l"
  by sorry

lemma closed_lattice:
  fixes A :: "(real ^ 'n) set"
  assumes "\<And>v i. v \<in> A \<Longrightarrow> v $ i \<in> \<int>"
  shows   "closed A"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Auxiliary theorems about measure theory\<close>

lemma emeasure_lborel_cbox_eq':
  "emeasure lborel (cbox a b) = ennreal (\<Prod>e\<in>Basis. max 0 ((b - a) \<bullet> e))"
  by sorry

lemma emeasure_lborel_cbox_cart_eq:
  fixes a b :: "real ^ ('n :: finite)"
  shows "emeasure lborel (cbox a b) = ennreal (\<Prod>i \<in> UNIV. max 0 ((b - a) $ i))"
  by sorry

lemma sum_emeasure':
  assumes [simp]: "finite A"
  assumes [measurable]: "\<And>x. x \<in> A \<Longrightarrow> B x \<in> sets M"
  assumes "\<And>x y. x \<in> A \<Longrightarrow> y \<in> A \<Longrightarrow> x \<noteq> y \<Longrightarrow> emeasure M (B x \<inter> B y) = 0"
  shows   "(\<Sum>x\<in>A. emeasure M (B x)) = emeasure M (\<Union>x\<in>A. B x)"
  by sorry

lemma sums_emeasure':
  assumes [measurable]: "\<And>x. B x \<in> sets M"
  assumes "\<And>x y. x \<noteq> y \<Longrightarrow> emeasure M (B x \<inter> B y) = 0"
  shows   "(\<lambda>x. emeasure M (B x)) sums emeasure M (\<Union>x. B x)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Blichfeldt's theorem\<close>

text \<open>
  Blichfeldt's theorem states that, given a subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n > 0$ and a
  volume of more than 1, there exist two different points in that set whose difference
  vector has integer components.

  This will be the key ingredient in proving Minkowski's theorem.

  Note that in the HOL Light version, it is additionally required -- both for
  Blichfeldt's theorem and for Minkowski's theorem -- that the set is bounded,
  which we do not need.
\<close>
proposition blichfeldt:
  fixes S :: "(real ^ 'n) set"
  assumes [measurable]: "S \<in> sets lebesgue"
  assumes "emeasure lebesgue S > 1"
  obtains x y where "x \<noteq> y" and "x \<in> S" and "y \<in> S" and "\<And>i. (x - y) $ i \<in> \<int>"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Minkowski's theorem\<close>

text \<open>
  Minkowski's theorem now states that, given a convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ that is
  symmetric around the origin and has a volume greater than $2^n$, that set must contain
  a non-zero point with integer coordinates.
\<close>
theorem minkowski:
  fixes B :: "(real ^ 'n) set"
  assumes "convex B" and symmetric: "uminus ` B \<subseteq> B"
  assumes meas_B [measurable]: "B \<in> sets lebesgue"
  assumes measure_B: "emeasure lebesgue B > 2 ^ CARD('n)"
  obtains x where "x \<in> B" and "x \<noteq> 0" and "\<And>i. x $ i \<in> \<int>"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  If the set in question is compact, the restriction to the volume can be weakened
  to ``at least 1'' from ``greater than 1''.
\<close>
theorem minkowski_compact:
  fixes B :: "(real ^ 'n) set"
  assumes "convex B" and "compact B" and symmetric: "uminus ` B \<subseteq> B"
  assumes measure_B: "emeasure lebesgue B \<ge> 2 ^ CARD('n)"
  obtains x where "x \<in> B" and "x \<noteq> 0" and "\<And>i. x $ i \<in> \<int>"
  by sorry

end

title: 040_minkowski_s_fundamental_theorem
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 040,
;; "Minkowski's Fundamental Theorem." In positive-dimensional real
;; coordinate space, a measurable convex set symmetric about the origin and
;; of Lebesgue volume greater than 2^n contains a nonzero integer point. The
;; compact form permits volume equal to 2^n. The corresponding concrete
;; Blichfeldt principle is included as in the other corpus formalizations.
;; This file contains no proof.
;;
;; Semantic status: the first-order rewrite below repairs the former vacuous
;; generated-lambda encoding, but its stub-coded real sets and measures have
;; no comprehension principle. It cannot preserve the source's full real
;; measurable-set and Lebesgue-volume domains in standard ACL2, so it is not
;; counted as a faithful translation.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Generic first-order application interfaces interpret tags as predicates
;; and unary functions. All mathematical quantifiers are direct DEFUN-SK
;; quantifiers; no generated lambda is passed through APPLY$.

(defstub ht040-apply1 (function argument) t)

(defstub ht040-apply2 (function left right) t)

(defun ht040-member-p (predicate object)
  (if (ht040-apply1 predicate object) t nil))

;; A scalar context consists of a carrier predicate, zero, one, addition,
;; multiplication, negation, inversion, and strict order.

(defun ht040-r-carrier (real) (nth 0 real))
(defun ht040-r-zero (real) (nth 1 real))
(defun ht040-r-one (real) (nth 2 real))
(defun ht040-r-add (real) (nth 3 real))
(defun ht040-r-multiply (real) (nth 4 real))
(defun ht040-r-negate (real) (nth 5 real))
(defun ht040-r-inverse (real) (nth 6 real))
(defun ht040-r-less (real) (nth 7 real))

(defun ht040-real-p (real value)
  (ht040-member-p (ht040-r-carrier real) value))

(defun ht040-zero (real)
  (ht040-r-zero real))

(defun ht040-one (real)
  (ht040-r-one real))

(defun ht040-add (real left right)
  (ht040-apply2 (ht040-r-add real) left right))

(defun ht040-multiply (real left right)
  (ht040-apply2 (ht040-r-multiply real) left right))

(defun ht040-negate (real value)
  (ht040-apply1 (ht040-r-negate real) value))

(defun ht040-inverse (real value)
  (ht040-apply1 (ht040-r-inverse real) value))

(defun ht040-less (real left right)
  (if (ht040-apply2 (ht040-r-less real) left right)
      t
    nil))

(defun ht040-subtract (real left right)
  (ht040-add real left (ht040-negate real right)))

(defun ht040-less-equal-p (real left right)
  (not (ht040-less real right left)))

(defun ht040-absolute-value (real value)
  (if (ht040-less real value (ht040-zero real))
      (ht040-negate real value)
    value))

(defun ht040-positive-real-p (real value)
  (and
   (ht040-real-p real value)
   (ht040-less real (ht040-zero real) value)))

;; A Dedekind-complete ordered field presents the real numbers.

(defun-sk ht040-field-laws-p (real)
  (forall (a b c)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht040-real-p real a)
      (ht040-real-p real b)
      (ht040-real-p real c))
     (let* ((ab-add (ht040-add real a b))
            (bc-add (ht040-add real b c))
            (ab-mul (ht040-multiply real a b))
            (bc-mul (ht040-multiply real b c))
            (neg-a (ht040-negate real a))
            (inv-a (ht040-inverse real a))
            (zero (ht040-zero real))
            (one (ht040-one real)))
       (and
        (ht040-real-p real ab-add)
        (ht040-real-p real ab-mul)
        (ht040-real-p real neg-a)
        (ht040-real-p real inv-a)
        (equal
         (ht040-add real ab-add c)
         (ht040-add real a bc-add))
        (equal ab-add (ht040-add real b a))
        (equal (ht040-add real a zero) a)
        (equal (ht040-add real a neg-a) zero)
        (equal
         (ht040-multiply real ab-mul c)
         (ht040-multiply real a bc-mul))
        (equal ab-mul (ht040-multiply real b a))
        (equal (ht040-multiply real a one) a)
        (equal
         (ht040-multiply real a bc-add)
         (ht040-add
          real
          (ht040-multiply real a b)
          (ht040-multiply real a c)))
        (implies
         (equal a zero)
         (equal inv-a zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal a zero))
         (equal
          (ht040-multiply real a inv-a)
          one)))))))

(defun-sk ht040-order-laws-p (real)
  (forall (a b c)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht040-real-p real a)
      (ht040-real-p real b)
      (ht040-real-p real c))
     (and
      (not (ht040-less real a a))
      (or
       (ht040-less real a b)
       (equal a b)
       (ht040-less real b a))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht040-less real a b)
        (ht040-less real b c))
       (ht040-less real a c))
      (implies
       (ht040-less real a b)
       (ht040-less
        real
        (ht040-add real a c)
        (ht040-add real b c)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht040-less real (ht040-zero real) a)
        (ht040-less real (ht040-zero real) b))
       (ht040-less
        real
        (ht040-zero real)
        (ht040-multiply real a b)))))))

(defun-sk ht040-valid-real-set-p (real set)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (ht040-member-p set value)
     (ht040-real-p real value))))

(defun-sk ht040-real-set-nonempty-p (real set)
  (exists (value)
    (and
     (ht040-real-p real value)
     (ht040-member-p set value))))

(defun-sk ht040-real-upper-bound-p
    (real set upper)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht040-real-p real value)
      (ht040-member-p set value))
     (ht040-less-equal-p real value upper))))

(defun-sk ht040-real-bounded-above-p
    (real set)
  (exists (upper)
    (and
     (ht040-real-p real upper)
     (ht040-real-upper-bound-p
      real set upper))))

(defun-sk ht040-real-supremum-p
    (real set supremum)
  (forall (upper)
    (and
     (ht040-real-p real supremum)
     (ht040-real-upper-bound-p
      real set supremum)
     (implies
      (and
       (ht040-real-p real upper)
       (ht040-real-upper-bound-p
        real set upper))
      (ht040-less-equal-p
       real supremum upper)))))

(defun-sk ht040-real-has-supremum-p
    (real set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (ht040-real-supremum-p
     real set supremum)))

(defun-sk ht040-completeness-p (real)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht040-valid-real-set-p real set)
      (ht040-real-set-nonempty-p real set)
      (ht040-real-bounded-above-p real set))
     (ht040-real-has-supremum-p
      real set))))

(defun ht040-field-natural (real n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (ht040-zero real)
    (ht040-add
     real
     (ht040-one real)
     (ht040-field-natural real (- n 1)))))

(defun-sk ht040-archimedean-witness-exists-p
    (real value)
  (exists (natural)
    (and
     (natp natural)
     (ht040-less
      real
      value
      (ht040-field-natural real natural)))))

(defun-sk ht040-archimedean-p (real)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (ht040-real-p real value)
     (ht040-archimedean-witness-exists-p
      real value))))

(defun ht040-real-field-p (real)
  (and
   (true-listp real)
   (equal (len real) 8)
   (ht040-real-p real (ht040-zero real))
   (ht040-real-p real (ht040-one real))
   (not
    (equal
     (ht040-zero real)
     (ht040-one real)))
   (ht040-less
    real (ht040-zero real) (ht040-one real))
   (ht040-field-laws-p real)
   (ht040-order-laws-p real)
   (ht040-completeness-p real)
   (ht040-archimedean-p real)))

;; Natural powers and the canonical integer embedding into the real field.

(defun ht040-field-power (real base exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (ht040-one real)
    (ht040-multiply
     real
     base
     (ht040-field-power
      real base (- exponent 1)))))

(defun ht040-two-power (real dimension)
  (ht040-field-power
   real
   (ht040-add
    real (ht040-one real) (ht040-one real))
   dimension))

(defun ht040-field-integer (real integer)
  (if (< integer 0)
      (ht040-negate
       real
       (ht040-field-natural real (- integer)))
    (ht040-field-natural real integer)))

(defun-sk ht040-scalar-integer-p
    (real value)
  (exists (integer)
    (and
     (integerp integer)
     (equal
      value
      (ht040-field-integer real integer)))))

;; Points of R^n are exact lists of n real coordinates.

(defun ht040-point-p (real dimension point)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      (equal point nil)
    (and
     (consp point)
     (ht040-real-p real (car point))
     (ht040-point-p
      real (- dimension 1) (cdr point)))))

(defun ht040-zero-point (real dimension)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      nil
    (cons
     (ht040-zero real)
     (ht040-zero-point real (- dimension 1)))))

(defun ht040-point-add
    (real dimension left right)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      nil
    (cons
     (ht040-add real (car left) (car right))
     (ht040-point-add
      real
      (- dimension 1)
      (cdr left)
      (cdr right)))))

(defun ht040-point-negate
    (real dimension point)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      nil
    (cons
     (ht040-negate real (car point))
     (ht040-point-negate
      real (- dimension 1) (cdr point)))))

(defun ht040-point-subtract
    (real dimension left right)
  (ht040-point-add
   real
   dimension
   left
   (ht040-point-negate real dimension right)))

(defun ht040-point-scale
    (real dimension scalar point)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      nil
    (cons
     (ht040-multiply real scalar (car point))
     (ht040-point-scale
      real
      (- dimension 1)
      scalar
      (cdr point)))))

(defun ht040-point-close-p
    (real dimension left right epsilon)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      t
    (and
     (ht040-less
      real
      (ht040-absolute-value
       real
       (ht040-subtract
        real (car left) (car right)))
      epsilon)
     (ht040-point-close-p
      real
      (- dimension 1)
      (cdr left)
      (cdr right)
      epsilon))))

(defun ht040-integer-point-p
    (real dimension point)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      (equal point nil)
    (and
     (consp point)
     (ht040-scalar-integer-p real (car point))
     (ht040-integer-point-p
      real (- dimension 1) (cdr point)))))

;; Region descriptors make intersection and difference explicit without
;; constructing executable lambdas.

(defun ht040-base-region (predicate)
  (list :ht040-base predicate))

(defun ht040-intersection-region (left right)
  (list :ht040-intersection left right))

(defun ht040-difference-region (left right)
  (list :ht040-difference left right))

(defun ht040-base-region-p (region)
  (and
   (true-listp region)
   (equal (len region) 2)
   (equal (car region) :ht040-base)))

(defun ht040-base-region-member-p
    (region point)
  (and
   (ht040-base-region-p region)
   (ht040-member-p (cadr region) point)))

(defun ht040-region-member-p (region point)
  (cond
   ((ht040-base-region-p region)
    (ht040-base-region-member-p region point))
   ((and
     (true-listp region)
     (equal (len region) 3)
     (equal (car region) :ht040-intersection)
     (ht040-base-region-p (cadr region))
     (ht040-base-region-p (caddr region)))
    (and
     (ht040-base-region-member-p
      (cadr region) point)
     (ht040-base-region-member-p
      (caddr region) point)))
   ((and
     (true-listp region)
     (equal (len region) 3)
     (equal (car region) :ht040-difference)
     (ht040-base-region-p (cadr region))
     (ht040-base-region-p (caddr region)))
    (and
     (ht040-base-region-member-p
      (cadr region) point)
     (not
      (ht040-base-region-member-p
       (caddr region) point))))
   (t nil)))

(defun-sk ht040-region-valid-p
    (real dimension region)
  (forall (point)
    (implies
     (ht040-region-member-p region point)
     (ht040-point-p real dimension point))))

;; Countable open-box covers and their nonnegative volume series define
;; Lebesgue outer volume by its lower Dedekind cut.

(defun ht040-valid-box-p
    (real dimension lower upper)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      (and (equal lower nil) (equal upper nil))
    (and
     (consp lower)
     (consp upper)
     (ht040-real-p real (car lower))
     (ht040-real-p real (car upper))
     (ht040-less real (car lower) (car upper))
     (ht040-valid-box-p
      real
      (- dimension 1)
      (cdr lower)
      (cdr upper)))))

(defun ht040-open-box-member-p
    (real dimension lower upper point)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      (equal point nil)
    (and
     (consp lower)
     (consp upper)
     (consp point)
     (ht040-less real (car lower) (car point))
     (ht040-less real (car point) (car upper))
     (ht040-open-box-member-p
      real
      (- dimension 1)
      (cdr lower)
      (cdr upper)
      (cdr point)))))

(defun-sk ht040-box-sequences-valid-p
    (real dimension lower-sequence upper-sequence)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (natp index)
     (ht040-valid-box-p
      real
      dimension
      (ht040-apply1 lower-sequence index)
      (ht040-apply1 upper-sequence index)))))

(defun-sk ht040-cover-index-exists-p
    (real dimension lower-sequence upper-sequence point)
  (exists (index)
    (and
     (natp index)
     (ht040-open-box-member-p
      real
      dimension
      (ht040-apply1 lower-sequence index)
      (ht040-apply1 upper-sequence index)
      point))))

(defun-sk ht040-box-sequences-cover-p
    (real dimension region lower-sequence upper-sequence)
  (forall (point)
    (implies
     (ht040-region-member-p region point)
     (ht040-cover-index-exists-p
      real
      dimension
      lower-sequence
      upper-sequence
      point))))

(defun ht040-countable-open-box-cover-p
    (real dimension region lower-sequence upper-sequence)
  (and
   (ht040-box-sequences-valid-p
    real dimension lower-sequence upper-sequence)
   (ht040-box-sequences-cover-p
    real dimension region lower-sequence upper-sequence)))

(defun ht040-box-volume
    (real dimension lower upper)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix dimension)))
  (if (zp dimension)
      (ht040-one real)
    (ht040-multiply
     real
     (ht040-subtract
      real (car upper) (car lower))
     (ht040-box-volume
      real
      (- dimension 1)
      (cdr lower)
      (cdr upper)))))

(defun ht040-box-volume-at
    (real dimension lower-sequence upper-sequence index)
  (ht040-box-volume
   real
   dimension
   (ht040-apply1 lower-sequence index)
   (ht040-apply1 upper-sequence index)))

(defun ht040-box-volume-partial-sum
    (real dimension lower-sequence upper-sequence count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      (ht040-zero real)
    (let ((index (- count 1)))
      (ht040-add
       real
       (ht040-box-volume-partial-sum
        real
        dimension
        lower-sequence
        upper-sequence
        index)
       (ht040-box-volume-at
        real
        dimension
        lower-sequence
        upper-sequence
        index)))))

(defun-sk ht040-series-cutoff-exists-p
    (real dimension lower-sequence upper-sequence
          threshold epsilon)
  (exists (count)
    (and
     (natp count)
     (ht040-less
      real
      (ht040-subtract real threshold epsilon)
      (ht040-box-volume-partial-sum
       real
       dimension
       lower-sequence
       upper-sequence
       count)))))

(defun-sk ht040-nonnegative-series-ge-p
    (real dimension lower-sequence upper-sequence threshold)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (ht040-positive-real-p real epsilon)
     (ht040-series-cutoff-exists-p
      real
      dimension
      lower-sequence
      upper-sequence
      threshold
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht040-lebesgue-outer-volume-ge-p
    (real dimension region threshold)
  (forall (lower-sequence upper-sequence)
    (implies
     (ht040-countable-open-box-cover-p
      real
      dimension
      region
      lower-sequence
      upper-sequence)
     (ht040-nonnegative-series-ge-p
      real
      dimension
      lower-sequence
      upper-sequence
      threshold))))

(defun-sk ht040-outer-volume-sum-ge-p
    (real dimension left right threshold)
  (exists (left-bound right-bound)
    (and
     (ht040-real-p real left-bound)
     (ht040-real-p real right-bound)
     (ht040-lebesgue-outer-volume-ge-p
      real dimension left left-bound)
     (ht040-lebesgue-outer-volume-ge-p
      real dimension right right-bound)
     (ht040-less-equal-p
      real
      threshold
      (ht040-add real left-bound right-bound)))))

;; Caratheodory measurability for the concrete outer volume above.

(defun-sk ht040-lebesgue-measurable-p
    (real dimension body)
  (forall (test-predicate threshold)
    (let ((test (ht040-base-region test-predicate)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht040-real-p real threshold)
        (ht040-region-valid-p real dimension test))
       (iff
        (ht040-lebesgue-outer-volume-ge-p
         real dimension test threshold)
        (ht040-outer-volume-sum-ge-p
         real
         dimension
         (ht040-intersection-region test body)
         (ht040-difference-region test body)
         threshold))))))

(defun-sk ht040-lebesgue-volume-gt-p
    (real dimension region threshold)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (ht040-positive-real-p real margin)
     (ht040-lebesgue-outer-volume-ge-p
      real
      dimension
      region
      (ht040-add real threshold margin)))))

;; Convexity, central symmetry, and sequential compactness in R^n.

(defun ht040-affine-combination
    (real dimension parameter left right)
  (ht040-point-add
   real
   dimension
   (ht040-point-scale
    real
    dimension
    (ht040-subtract
     real (ht040-one real) parameter)
    left)
   (ht040-point-scale
    real dimension parameter right)))

(defun-sk ht040-convex-region-p
    (real dimension region)
  (forall (left right parameter)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht040-point-p real dimension left)
      (ht040-point-p real dimension right)
      (ht040-region-member-p region left)
      (ht040-region-member-p region right)
      (ht040-real-p real parameter)
      (ht040-less-equal-p
       real (ht040-zero real) parameter)
      (ht040-less-equal-p
       real parameter (ht040-one real)))
     (ht040-region-member-p
      region
      (ht040-affine-combination
       real dimension parameter left right)))))

(defun-sk ht040-origin-symmetric-p
    (real dimension region)
  (forall (point)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht040-point-p real dimension point)
      (ht040-region-member-p region point))
     (ht040-region-member-p
      region
      (ht040-point-negate
       real dimension point)))))

(defun-sk ht040-sequence-in-region-p
    (real dimension region sequence)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (natp index)
     (let ((point (ht040-apply1 sequence index)))
       (and
        (ht040-point-p real dimension point)
        (ht040-region-member-p region point))))))

(defun-sk ht040-index-sequence-natural-p
    (indices)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (natp index)
     (natp (ht040-apply1 indices index)))))

(defun-sk ht040-index-sequence-strict-p
    (indices)
  (forall (left right)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp left)
      (natp right)
      (< left right))
     (<
      (ht040-apply1 indices left)
      (ht040-apply1 indices right)))))

(defun-sk ht040-convergence-cutoff-p
    (real dimension sequence indices limit epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (<= cutoff index))
     (ht040-point-close-p
      real
      dimension
      (ht040-apply1
       sequence
       (ht040-apply1 indices index))
      limit
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht040-convergence-cutoff-exists-p
    (real dimension sequence indices limit epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (ht040-convergence-cutoff-p
      real
      dimension
      sequence
      indices
      limit
      epsilon
      cutoff))))

(defun-sk ht040-subsequence-converges-p
    (real dimension sequence indices limit)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (ht040-positive-real-p real epsilon)
     (ht040-convergence-cutoff-exists-p
      real
      dimension
      sequence
      indices
      limit
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht040-compact-witness-exists-p
    (real dimension region sequence)
  (exists (indices limit)
    (and
     (ht040-index-sequence-natural-p indices)
     (ht040-index-sequence-strict-p indices)
     (ht040-point-p real dimension limit)
     (ht040-region-member-p region limit)
     (ht040-subsequence-converges-p
      real dimension sequence indices limit))))

(defun-sk ht040-compact-region-p
    (real dimension region)
  (forall (sequence)
    (implies
     (ht040-sequence-in-region-p
      real dimension region sequence)
     (ht040-compact-witness-exists-p
      real dimension region sequence))))

;; Lattice-point witnesses.

(defun-sk ht040-blichfeldt-witness-p
    (real dimension region)
  (exists (left right)
    (and
     (ht040-point-p real dimension left)
     (ht040-point-p real dimension right)
     (ht040-region-member-p region left)
     (ht040-region-member-p region right)
     (not (equal left right))
     (ht040-integer-point-p
      real
      dimension
      (ht040-point-subtract
       real dimension left right)))))

(defun-sk ht040-minkowski-witness-p
    (real dimension region)
  (exists (point)
    (and
     (ht040-point-p real dimension point)
     (ht040-region-member-p region point)
     (not
      (equal
       point
       (ht040-zero-point real dimension)))
     (ht040-integer-point-p
      real dimension point))))

(defun-sk
    hundred-theorems-040-blichfeldt-principle-statement ()
  (forall (real dimension body-predicate)
    (let ((body (ht040-base-region body-predicate)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht040-real-field-p real)
        (posp dimension)
        (ht040-region-valid-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-lebesgue-measurable-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-lebesgue-volume-gt-p
         real
         dimension
         body
         (ht040-one real)))
       (ht040-blichfeldt-witness-p
        real dimension body)))))

(defun-sk
    hundred-theorems-040-minkowski-fundamental-theorem-statement ()
  (forall (real dimension body-predicate)
    (let ((body (ht040-base-region body-predicate)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht040-real-field-p real)
        (posp dimension)
        (ht040-region-valid-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-convex-region-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-origin-symmetric-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-lebesgue-measurable-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-lebesgue-volume-gt-p
         real
         dimension
         body
         (ht040-two-power real dimension)))
       (ht040-minkowski-witness-p
        real dimension body)))))

(defun-sk
    hundred-theorems-040-minkowski-compact-statement ()
  (forall (real dimension body-predicate)
    (let ((body (ht040-base-region body-predicate)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht040-real-field-p real)
        (posp dimension)
        (ht040-region-valid-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-convex-region-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-compact-region-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-origin-symmetric-p
         real dimension body)
        (ht040-lebesgue-outer-volume-ge-p
         real
         dimension
         body
         (ht040-two-power real dimension)))
       (ht040-minkowski-witness-p
        real dimension body)))))

:q

title: 040_minkowski_s_fundamental_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Minkowski's Fundamental Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item
-- 040. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _≠_ _≤ₙ_ _<ₙ_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 2 _∨_
infix 2 _↔_

data ⊥ : Set where

_≠_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≠ y = x ≡ y → ⊥

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A → B
    backward : B → A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _≤ₙ_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ₙ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ₙ n → suc m ≤ₙ suc n

_<ₙ_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m <ₙ n = suc m ≤ₙ n

data PositiveDimension : Nat → Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} → PositiveDimension (suc n)

data Fin : Nat → Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} → Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} → Fin n → Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R → R → R
    negate inverse : R → R
    lessThan : R → R → Set
    fromNat : Nat → R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR ≠ zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) → add x y ≡ add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) → add (add x y) z ≡ add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) → add x zeroR ≡ x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) → add x (negate x) ≡ zeroR
    negate-involutive :
      (x : R) → negate (negate x) ≡ x

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) → multiply x y ≡ multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiply (multiply x y) z ≡ multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) → multiply x oneR ≡ x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) → multiply x zeroR ≡ zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiply x (add y z) ≡
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR ≡ zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) →
      x ≠ zeroR →
      multiply x (inverse x) ≡ oneR

    order-irreflexive :
      (x : R) →
      lessThan x x →
      ⊥
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) →
      lessThan x y →
      lessThan y z →
      lessThan x z
    order-trichotomy :
      (x y : R) →
      lessThan x y ∨
      (x ≡ y ∨ lessThan y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) →
      lessThan x y →
      lessThan (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-positive :
      (x y : R) →
      lessThan zeroR x →
      lessThan zeroR y →
      lessThan zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessThan zeroR oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero ≡ zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) →
      fromNat (suc n) ≡ add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat (m + n) ≡
      add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat (m * n) ≡
      multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat m ≡ fromNat n →
      m ≡ n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) →
      Exists Nat (λ n → lessThan x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R → Set) →
      Exists R P →
      Exists R
        (λ upper →
          (x : R) →
          P x →
          lessThan x upper ∨ x ≡ upper) →
      Exists R
        (λ supremum →
          ((x : R) →
            P x →
            lessThan x supremum ∨ x ≡ supremum) ∧
          ((upper : R) →
            ((x : R) →
              P x →
              lessThan x upper ∨ x ≡ upper) →
            lessThan supremum upper ∨ supremum ≡ upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

LessOrEqual :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  Set
LessOrEqual reals x y =
  lessThan reals x y ∨ x ≡ y

subtract :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

fromInt :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Int →
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

power :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Nat →
  R
power reals x zero =
  oneR reals
power reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals x (power reals x n)

twoPower :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Nat →
  R
twoPower reals n =
  power reals
    (add reals (oneR reals) (oneR reals))
    n

Vector : Set → Nat → Set
Vector R n = Fin n → R

Region : Set → Nat → Set₁
Region R n = Vector R n → Set

zeroVector :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Vector R n
zeroVector reals _ =
  zeroR reals

addVector :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n
addVector reals x y i =
  add reals (x i) (y i)

negateVector :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n
negateVector reals x i =
  negate reals (x i)

subtractVector :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n
subtractVector reals x y =
  addVector reals x (negateVector reals y)

scaleVector :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n
scaleVector reals scalar x i =
  multiply reals scalar (x i)

linearCombination :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n
linearCombination reals t x y =
  addVector reals
    (scaleVector reals t x)
    (scaleVector reals
      (subtract reals (oneR reals) t)
      y)

Convex :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Region R n →
  Set
Convex {R} {n} reals body =
  (x y : Vector R n) →
  body x →
  body y →
  (t : R) →
  LessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) t →
  LessOrEqual reals t (oneR reals) →
  body (linearCombination reals t x y)

OriginSymmetric :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Region R n →
  Set
OriginSymmetric {R} {n} reals body =
  (x : Vector R n) →
  body x →
  body (negateVector reals x)

IntegerCoordinate :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
IntegerCoordinate reals x =
  Exists Int (λ z → x ≡ fromInt reals z)

IntegerVector :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Vector R n →
  Set
IntegerVector {n = n} reals x =
  (i : Fin n) →
  IntegerCoordinate reals (x i)

DistinctVectors :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n →
  Set
DistinctVectors {n = n} x y =
  Exists (Fin n) (λ i → x i ≠ y i)

NonzeroVector :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Vector R n →
  Set
NonzeroVector {n = n} reals x =
  Exists (Fin n) (λ i → x i ≠ zeroR reals)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → R) →
  R →
  Set
ConvergesTo reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : _) →
  lessThan reals (zeroR reals) epsilon →
  Exists Nat
    (λ cutoff →
      (n : Nat) →
      cutoff ≤ₙ n →
      lessThan reals
        (subtract reals limit epsilon)
        (sequence n) ∧
      lessThan reals
        (sequence n)
        (add reals limit epsilon))

VectorConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → Vector R n) →
  Vector R n →
  Set
VectorConvergesTo {n = n} reals sequence limit =
  (i : Fin n) →
  ConvergesTo reals
    (λ k → sequence k i)
    (limit i)

StrictlyIncreasing : (Nat → Nat) → Set
StrictlyIncreasing subsequence =
  (k : Nat) →
  subsequence k <ₙ subsequence (suc k)

Compact :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Region R n →
  Set
Compact {R} {n} reals body =
  (sequence : Nat → Vector R n) →
  ((k : Nat) → body (sequence k)) →
  Exists (Nat → Nat)
    (λ subsequence →
      StrictlyIncreasing subsequence ∧
      Exists (Vector R n)
        (λ limit →
          VectorConvergesTo reals
            (λ k → sequence (subsequence k))
            limit ∧
          body limit))

Empty :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  Region R n
Empty _ =
  ⊥

Complement :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  Region R n →
  Region R n
Complement body x =
  body x → ⊥

UnionAll :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  (Nat → Region R n) →
  Region R n
UnionAll regions x =
  Exists Nat (λ k → regions k x)

Disjoint :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  Region R n →
  Region R n →
  Set
Disjoint {R} {n} leftBody rightBody =
  (x : Vector R n) →
  leftBody x →
  rightBody x →
  ⊥

PairwiseDisjoint :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  (Nat → Region R n) →
  Set
PairwiseDisjoint regions =
  (m n : Nat) →
  m ≠ n →
  Disjoint (regions m) (regions n)

translateRegion :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Vector R n →
  Region R n →
  Region R n
translateRegion {R} {n} reals offset body x =
  Exists (Vector R n)
    (λ y →
      body y ∧
      x ≡ addVector reals offset y)

HalfOpenBox :
  {R : Set} →
  {n : Nat} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n →
  Region R n
HalfOpenBox {R} {n} reals lower upper x =
  (i : Fin n) →
  LessOrEqual reals (lower i) (x i) ∧
  lessThan reals (x i) (upper i)

productFin :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  {n : Nat} →
  (Fin n → R) →
  R
productFin reals {zero} values =
  oneR reals
productFin reals {suc n} values =
  multiply reals
    (values fzero)
    (productFin reals (λ i → values (fsuc i)))

data ExtendedNonnegative (R : Set) : Set where
  finite   : R → ExtendedNonnegative R
  infinity : ExtendedNonnegative R

data ExtendedLessOrEqual
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) :
  ExtendedNonnegative R →
  ExtendedNonnegative R →
  Set where

  finite≤finite :
    {x y : R} →
    LessOrEqual reals x y →
    ExtendedLessOrEqual reals (finite x) (finite y)

  finite≤infinity :
    {x : R} →
    ExtendedLessOrEqual reals (finite x) infinity

  infinity≤infinity :
    ExtendedLessOrEqual reals infinity infinity

data ExtendedLess
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) :
  ExtendedNonnegative R →
  ExtendedNonnegative R →
  Set where

  finite<finite :
    {x y : R} →
    lessThan reals x y →
    ExtendedLess reals (finite x) (finite y)

  finite<infinity :
    {x : R} →
    ExtendedLess reals (finite x) infinity

addExtended :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  ExtendedNonnegative R →
  ExtendedNonnegative R →
  ExtendedNonnegative R
addExtended reals infinity rightValue =
  infinity
addExtended reals (finite x) infinity =
  infinity
addExtended reals (finite x) (finite y) =
  finite (add reals x y)

sumFirstExtended :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Nat →
  (Nat → ExtendedNonnegative R) →
  ExtendedNonnegative R
sumFirstExtended reals zero term =
  finite (zeroR reals)
sumFirstExtended reals (suc n) term =
  addExtended reals
    (sumFirstExtended reals n term)
    (term n)

UpperBoundExtended :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → ExtendedNonnegative R) →
  ExtendedNonnegative R →
  Set
UpperBoundExtended reals values bound =
  (n : Nat) →
  ExtendedLessOrEqual reals (values n) bound

LeastUpperBoundExtended :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → ExtendedNonnegative R) →
  ExtendedNonnegative R →
  Set
LeastUpperBoundExtended reals values supremum =
  UpperBoundExtended reals values supremum ∧
  ((upper : ExtendedNonnegative _) →
    UpperBoundExtended reals values upper →
    ExtendedLessOrEqual reals supremum upper)

record StandardEuclideanLebesgueMeasure
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (n : Nat) :
  Set₁ where

  field
    measurable : Region R n → Set
    volume : Region R n → ExtendedNonnegative R

    measurable-empty :
      measurable Empty
    measurable-complement :
      (body : Region R n) →
      measurable body →
      measurable (Complement body)
    measurable-union-all :
      (regions : Nat → Region R n) →
      ((k : Nat) → measurable (regions k)) →
      measurable (UnionAll regions)
    compact-measurable :
      (body : Region R n) →
      Compact reals body →
      measurable body
    measurable-translation :
      (offset : Vector R n) →
      (body : Region R n) →
      measurable body →
      measurable (translateRegion reals offset body)
    measurable-box :
      (lower upper : Vector R n) →
      measurable (HalfOpenBox reals lower upper)

    volume-congruent :
      (leftBody rightBody : Region R n) →
      ((x : Vector R n) →
        leftBody x ↔ rightBody x) →
      volume leftBody ≡ volume rightBody
    volume-empty :
      volume Empty ≡ finite (zeroR reals)
    volume-nonnegative :
      (body : Region R n) →
      measurable body →
      ExtendedLessOrEqual reals
        (finite (zeroR reals))
        (volume body)
    volume-countable-additive :
      (regions : Nat → Region R n) →
      ((k : Nat) → measurable (regions k)) →
      PairwiseDisjoint regions →
      LeastUpperBoundExtended reals
        (λ count →
          sumFirstExtended reals count
            (λ k → volume (regions k)))
        (volume (UnionAll regions))
    volume-translation-invariant :
      (offset : Vector R n) →
      (body : Region R n) →
      measurable body →
      volume (translateRegion reals offset body) ≡
      volume body
    volume-box :
      (lower upper : Vector R n) →
      ((i : Fin n) →
        LessOrEqual reals (lower i) (upper i)) →
      volume (HalfOpenBox reals lower upper) ≡
      finite
        (productFin reals
          (λ i →
            subtract reals (upper i) (lower i)))

module MinkowskiStatement
  {R : Set}
  (n : Nat)
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (euclidean : StandardEuclideanLebesgueMeasure reals n)
  where

  open StandardEuclideanLebesgueMeasure euclidean

  blichfeldt-principle : Set₁
  blichfeldt-principle =
    (body : Region R n) →
    measurable body →
    ExtendedLess reals
      (finite (oneR reals))
      (volume body) →
    Exists (Vector R n)
      (λ x →
        Exists (Vector R n)
          (λ y →
            DistinctVectors x y ∧
            (body x ∧
            (body y ∧
             IntegerVector reals
               (subtractVector reals x y)))))

  strict-minkowski : Set₁
  strict-minkowski =
    (body : Region R n) →
    Convex reals body →
    OriginSymmetric reals body →
    measurable body →
    ExtendedLess reals
      (finite (twoPower reals n))
      (volume body) →
    Exists (Vector R n)
      (λ latticePoint →
        NonzeroVector reals latticePoint ∧
        (IntegerVector reals latticePoint ∧
         body latticePoint))

  compact-minkowski : Set₁
  compact-minkowski =
    (body : Region R n) →
    Convex reals body →
    Compact reals body →
    OriginSymmetric reals body →
    ExtendedLessOrEqual reals
      (finite (twoPower reals n))
      (volume body) →
    Exists (Vector R n)
      (λ latticePoint →
        NonzeroVector reals latticePoint ∧
        (IntegerVector reals latticePoint ∧
         body latticePoint))

  record MinkowskiClaims : Set₁ where
    field
      blichfeldt :
        blichfeldt-principle
      strict-form :
        strict-minkowski
      compact-form :
        compact-minkowski

minkowskis-fundamental-theorem : Set₁
minkowskis-fundamental-theorem =
  (R : Set) →
  (n : Nat) →
  PositiveDimension n →
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) →
  (euclidean : StandardEuclideanLebesgueMeasure reals n) →
  MinkowskiStatement.MinkowskiClaims n reals euclidean

title: 040_minkowski_s_fundamental_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Minkowski's Fundamental Theorem" from
  Hundred Theorems item 040. A convex set in finite-dimensional Euclidean
  space that is symmetric about the origin and has completed Lebesgue volume
  greater than 2^n contains a nonzero integer-lattice point; for compact sets,
  equality is allowed. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open extrealTheory sigma_algebraTheory measureTheory;

val minkowski_s_fundamental_theorem =
  ``!borel_nd_measure m. !(s : ('i -> real) -> bool).
      let half_open_box =
        \a b : 'i -> real.
          {x : 'i -> real | !i. a i <= x i /\ x i < b i}
      in
      let coordinate_boxes =
        \t : ('i -> real) -> bool.
          ?a b : 'i -> real. t = half_open_box a b
      in
      let lebesgue_nd =
        (measure_space borel_nd_measure /\
         m_space borel_nd_measure = (UNIV : ('i -> real) -> bool) /\
         measurable_sets borel_nd_measure =
           subsets
             (sigma (UNIV : ('i -> real) -> bool) coordinate_boxes) /\
         (!a b : 'i -> real.
            measure borel_nd_measure (half_open_box a b) =
            Normal
              (REAL_PROD_IMAGE
                (\i. max (0 : real) (b i - a i))
                (UNIV : 'i -> bool))) /\
         measure_space m /\
         m_space m = (UNIV : ('i -> real) -> bool) /\
         measurable_sets m = subsets (completion borel_nd_measure) /\
         (!t. t IN measurable_sets borel_nd_measure ==>
              measure m t = measure borel_nd_measure t))
      in
      let convex_euclidean =
        \t.
          !x y u.
            x IN t /\ y IN t /\ 0 <= u /\ u <= 1 ==>
            (\i. (1 - u) * x i + u * y i) IN t
      in
      let origin_symmetric =
        \t. !x. x IN t ==> (\i. ~(x i)) IN t
      in
        FINITE (UNIV : 'i -> bool) /\
        lebesgue_nd /\
        convex_euclidean s /\
        origin_symmetric s /\
        Normal
          ((2 : real) pow CARD (UNIV : 'i -> bool)) <
          measure m s
        ==>
        ?u : 'i -> real.
          u IN s /\
          u <> (\i. 0) /\
          !i. ?z : int. u i = real_of_int z``;

val minkowski_s_fundamental_theorem_compact =
  ``!borel_nd_measure m. !(s : ('i -> real) -> bool).
      let half_open_box =
        \a b : 'i -> real.
          {x : 'i -> real | !i. a i <= x i /\ x i < b i}
      in
      let coordinate_boxes =
        \t : ('i -> real) -> bool.
          ?a b : 'i -> real. t = half_open_box a b
      in
      let lebesgue_nd =
        (measure_space borel_nd_measure /\
         m_space borel_nd_measure = (UNIV : ('i -> real) -> bool) /\
         measurable_sets borel_nd_measure =
           subsets
             (sigma (UNIV : ('i -> real) -> bool) coordinate_boxes) /\
         (!a b : 'i -> real.
            measure borel_nd_measure (half_open_box a b) =
            Normal
              (REAL_PROD_IMAGE
                (\i. max (0 : real) (b i - a i))
                (UNIV : 'i -> bool))) /\
         measure_space m /\
         m_space m = (UNIV : ('i -> real) -> bool) /\
         measurable_sets m = subsets (completion borel_nd_measure) /\
         (!t. t IN measurable_sets borel_nd_measure ==>
              measure m t = measure borel_nd_measure t))
      in
      let sqdist =
        \x y : 'i -> real.
          SIGMA (\i. (x i - y i) pow 2) (UNIV : 'i -> bool)
      in
      let compact_euclidean =
        \t.
          !(a : num -> 'i -> real).
            (!n. a n IN t) ==>
            ?r x.
              x IN t /\
              (!p q. p < q ==> r p < r q) /\
              !e. 0 < e ==>
                  ?N. !n. N <= n ==> sqdist (a (r n)) x < e
      in
      let convex_euclidean =
        \t.
          !x y u.
            x IN t /\ y IN t /\ 0 <= u /\ u <= 1 ==>
            (\i. (1 - u) * x i + u * y i) IN t
      in
      let origin_symmetric =
        \t. !x. x IN t ==> (\i. ~(x i)) IN t
      in
        FINITE (UNIV : 'i -> bool) /\
        lebesgue_nd /\
        compact_euclidean s /\
        convex_euclidean s /\
        origin_symmetric s /\
        Normal
          ((2 : real) pow CARD (UNIV : 'i -> bool)) <=
          measure m s
        ==>
        ?u : 'i -> real.
          u IN s /\
          u <> (\i. 0) /\
          !i. ?z : int. u i = real_of_int z``;

title: 040_minkowski_s_fundamental_theorem
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Minkowski's Fundamental Theorem" from
  Hundred Theorems artifact 040. It states that a measurable convex subset of
  finite-dimensional real space, symmetric about the origin and of volume
  greater than 2 to the dimension, contains a nonzero integer-lattice point.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  For N e. NN, the coordinate set I = ( 1 ... N ) gives the Euclidean space
  RR ^m I. The domain of voln ` I is the collection of Lebesgue-measurable
  subsets of that space. Convexity and symmetry are expanded coordinatewise,
  and ZZ ^m I is the integer lattice.

  The final $a assertion is the unproved corpus statement.
$)

${
  $d N B I t u x y k $.

  ht040-minkowski $a
    |- A. N e. NN A. I
      ( I = ( 1 ... N ) ->
        A. B
          (
            (
              (
                B e. dom ( voln ` I )
                /\
                A. x e. B
                  ( k e. I |-> -u ( x ` k ) ) e. B
              )
              /\
              (
                A. x e. B A. y e. B A. t e. ( 0 [,] 1 )
                  ( k e. I |->
                    (
                      ( ( 1 - t ) x. ( x ` k ) )
                      +
                      ( t x. ( y ` k ) )
                    )
                  ) e. B
                /\
                ( 2 ^ N ) < ( ( voln ` I ) ` B )
              )
            )
            ->
            E. u e. ( ZZ ^m I )
              (
                u e. B
                /\
                u =/= ( k e. I |-> 0 )
              )
          )
      )
  $.
$}
