    ( CoeffFunction R F )
    ->
    ( E.s s (
      ( A.q q ( A.c a (
        ( R q a )
        <->
        ( ( scoeff F s q ) =C a )
      ) ) )
    ) )
  ) )
) $.

full-series-space-foundation $a |- (
  A.f F ( FullSeriesSpace F )
) $.

$(
  PuiseuxOver s F is therefore the full subtype of rational-indexed
  F-valued functions satisfying the exact support condition: support is
  bounded below, and multiplication by one positive natural denominator
  sends every supported exponent to an integer.
$)
series-over-definition $a |- (
  ( SeriesOver s F ) <->
  ( A.q q ( InC ( scoeff F s q ) F ) )
) $.

puiseux-series-definition $a |- (
  ( PuiseuxOver s F ) <->
  (
    ( SeriesOver s F )
    /\
    ( E.q r ( E.n n (
      ( PositiveN n )
      /\
      ( A.q q (
        ( -. ( ( scoeff F s q ) =C ( zeroC F ) ) )
        ->
        (
          ( leQ r q )
          /\
          ( IsIntegerQ ( mulQ q ( natQ n ) ) )
        )
      ) )
    ) ) )
  )
) $.

$(
  The list L in ConvSupportList enumerates exactly the nonzero summands
  coeff(s,r) * coeff(t,q-r).  convPartial recursively adds those summands,
  so CauchyCoeff is the ordinary finite Cauchy coefficient without replacing
  a series by a finite table.
$)
convolution-support-definition $a |- (
  ( ConvSupportList F s t q L ) <->
  (
    ( NoDupL L )
    /\
    ( A.q r (
      ( InL r L )
      <->
      (
        -.
        (
          ( mulC F
            ( scoeff F s r )
            ( scoeff F t ( addQ q ( negQ r ) ) )
          )
          =C
          ( zeroC F )
        )
      )
    ) )
  )
) $.

convolution-sum-nil $a |- (
  ( convPartial F s t q nilL ) =C ( zeroC F )
) $.
convolution-sum-cons $a |- (
  ( convPartial F s t q ( consL r L ) )
  =C
  ( addC F
    ( mulC F
      ( scoeff F s r )
      ( scoeff F t ( addQ q ( negQ r ) ) )
    )
    ( convPartial F s t q L )
  )
) $.

cauchy-coefficient-definition $a |- (
  ( CauchyCoeff F s t q a ) <->
  ( E.l L (
    ( ConvSupportList F s t q L )
    /\
    ( a =C ( convPartial F s t q L ) )
  ) )
) $.

$(
  PuiseuxField F fixes the standard coefficientwise zero, one, negation and
  addition, the Cauchy product above, closure on the exact Puiseux carrier,
  and the commutative-field laws.  Its inverse is thereby the unique field
  inverse for the Cauchy multiplication.
$)
puiseux-field-definition $a |- (
  ( PuiseuxField F ) <->
  (
    ( ( PuiseuxOver ( zeroS F ) F )
      /\
      ( PuiseuxOver ( oneS F ) F )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( A.q q (
        ( ( scoeff F ( zeroS F ) q ) =C ( zeroC F ) )
        /\
        (
          (
            ( q =Q zeroQ )
            ->
            ( ( scoeff F ( oneS F ) q ) =C ( oneC F ) )
          )
          /\
          (
            ( -. ( q =Q zeroQ ) )
            ->
            ( ( scoeff F ( oneS F ) q ) =C ( zeroC F ) )
          )
        )
      ) )
      /\
      (
        ( A.s s (
          ( PuiseuxOver s F )
          ->
          (
            ( PuiseuxOver ( negS F s ) F )
            /\
            ( A.q q (
              ( scoeff F ( negS F s ) q )
              =C
              ( negC F ( scoeff F s q ) )
            ) )
          )
        ) )
        /\
        (
          ( A.s s (
            (
              ( PuiseuxOver s F )
              /\
              ( -. ( s =S F ( zeroS F ) ) )
            )
            ->
            ( PuiseuxOver ( invS F s ) F )
          ) )
          /\
          (
            ( A.s s ( A.s t (
              (
                ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                /\
                ( PuiseuxOver t F )
              )
              ->
              (
                ( PuiseuxOver ( addS F s t ) F )
                /\
                (
                  ( PuiseuxOver ( mulS F s t ) F )
                  /\
                  ( A.q q (
                    (
                      ( scoeff F ( addS F s t ) q )
                      =C
                      ( addC F
                        ( scoeff F s q )
                        ( scoeff F t q )
                      )
                    )
                    /\
                    ( E.c a (
                      ( CauchyCoeff F s t q a )
                      /\
                      ( ( scoeff F ( mulS F s t ) q ) =C a )
                    ) )
                  ) )
                )
              )
            ) ) )
            /\
            (
              ( -. ( ( zeroS F ) =S F ( oneS F ) ) )
              /\
              (
                ( A.s s ( A.s t (
                  (
                    ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                    /\
                    ( PuiseuxOver t F )
                  )
                  ->
                  ( ( addS F s t ) =S F ( addS F t s ) )
                ) ) )
                /\
                (
                  ( A.s s ( A.s t ( A.s v (
                    (
                      ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                      /\
                      (
                        ( PuiseuxOver t F )
                        /\
                        ( PuiseuxOver v F )
                      )
                    )
                    ->
                    (
                      ( addS F ( addS F s t ) v )
                      =S F
                      ( addS F s ( addS F t v ) )
                    )
                  ) ) ) )
                  /\
                  (
                    ( A.s s (
                      ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                      ->
                      ( ( addS F s ( zeroS F ) ) =S F s )
                    ) )
                    /\
                    (
                      ( A.s s (
                        ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                        ->
                        (
                          ( addS F s ( negS F s ) )
                          =S F
                          ( zeroS F )
                        )
                      ) )
                      /\
                      (
                        ( A.s s ( A.s t (
                          (
                            ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                            /\
                            ( PuiseuxOver t F )
                          )
                          ->
                          ( ( mulS F s t ) =S F ( mulS F t s ) )
                        ) ) )
                        /\
                        (
                          ( A.s s ( A.s t ( A.s v (
                            (
                              ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                              /\
                              (
                                ( PuiseuxOver t F )
                                /\
                                ( PuiseuxOver v F )
                              )
                            )
                            ->
                            (
                              ( mulS F ( mulS F s t ) v )
                              =S F
                              ( mulS F s ( mulS F t v ) )
                            )
                          ) ) ) )
                          /\
                          (
                            ( A.s s (
                              ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                              ->
                              ( ( mulS F s ( oneS F ) ) =S F s )
                            ) )
                            /\
                            (
                              ( A.s s (
                                (
                                  ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                                  /\
                                  ( -. ( s =S F ( zeroS F ) ) )
                                )
                                ->
                                (
                                  ( mulS F s ( invS F s ) )
                                  =S F
                                  ( oneS F )
                                )
                              ) )
                              /\
                              ( A.s s ( A.s t ( A.s v (
                                (
                                  ( PuiseuxOver s F )
                                  /\
                                  (
                                    ( PuiseuxOver t F )
                                    /\
                                    ( PuiseuxOver v F )
                                  )
                                )
                                ->
                                (
                                  ( mulS F s ( addS F t v ) )
                                  =S F
                                  ( addS F
                                    ( mulS F s t )
                                    ( mulS F s v )
                                  )
                                )
                              ) ) ) )
                            )
                          )
                        )
                      )
                    )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

$(
  This is the foundational construction clause for the standard Puiseux
  field on the full function space above.  It supplies the explicitly
  defined operations and their closure/field laws for every coefficient
  field; it is not an additional premise of the final theorem and contains
  no polynomial-root or algebraic-closedness assertion.
$)
puiseux-field-foundation $a |- (
  A.f F (
    ( Field F )
    ->
    ( PuiseuxField F )
  )
) $.

$(
  SeriesPolyMap H F is the analogous equality-extensional, total,
  single-valued, eventually-zero graph with Puiseux-series values.
  FullPPolySpace F gives every such graph a polynomial representative.
$)
series-polynomial-map-definition $a |- (
  ( SeriesPolyMap H F ) <->
  (
    ( A.n n ( E.s s (
      ( PuiseuxOver s F )
      /\
      ( H n s )
    ) ) )
    /\
    (
      ( A.n n ( A.s s (
        ( H n s )
        ->
        ( PuiseuxOver s F )
      ) ) )
      /\
      (
        ( A.n n ( A.s s ( A.s t (
          (
            ( H n s )
            /\
            ( H n t )
          )
          ->
          ( s =S F t )
        ) ) ) )
        /\
        (
          ( A.n n ( A.s s ( A.s t (
            (
              ( H n s )
              /\
              ( s =S F t )
            )
            ->
            ( H n t )
          ) ) ) )
          /\
          ( E.n n ( A.n m (
            ( ltN n m )
            ->
            ( H m ( zeroS F ) )
          ) ) )
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

polynomial-definition $a |- (
  ( PolyOver p F ) <->
  (
    ( A.n n ( PuiseuxOver ( pcoeff F p n ) F ) )
    /\
    ( E.n n ( A.n m (
      ( ltN n m )
      ->
      ( ( pcoeff F p m ) =S F ( zeroS F ) )
    ) ) )
  )
) $.

full-puiseux-polynomial-space-definition $a |- (
  ( FullPPolySpace F ) <->
  ( A.NS H (
    ( SeriesPolyMap H F )
    ->
    ( E.p p (
      ( PolyOver p F )
      /\
      ( A.n n ( A.s s (
        ( H n s )
        <->
        ( ( pcoeff F p n ) =S F s )
      ) ) )
    ) )
  ) )
) $.

full-puiseux-polynomial-space-foundation $a |- (
  A.f F ( FullPPolySpace F )
) $.

$(
  PDegree is the greatest nonzero coefficient index.  partial is the finite
  evaluation sum, and PEvalZero means that this evaluation is the zero
  Puiseux series.
$)
polynomial-degree-definition $a |- (
  ( PDegree p n F ) <->
  (
    ( PolyOver p F )
    /\
    (
      ( -. ( ( pcoeff F p n ) =S F ( zeroS F ) ) )
      /\
      ( A.n m (
        ( ltN n m )
        ->
        ( ( pcoeff F p m ) =S F ( zeroS F ) )
      ) )
    )
  )
) $.

series-power-zero $a |- (
  ( spow F s zeroN ) =S F ( oneS F )
) $.
series-power-successor $a |- (
  ( spow F s ( succN n ) )
  =S F
  ( mulS F ( spow F s n ) s )
) $.

polynomial-evaluation-zero $a |- (
  ( partial F p s zeroN ) =S F ( pcoeff F p zeroN )
) $.
polynomial-evaluation-successor $a |- (
  ( partial F p s ( succN n ) )
  =S F
  ( addS F
    ( partial F p s n )
    ( mulS F
      ( pcoeff F p ( succN n ) )
      ( spow F s ( succN n ) )
    )
  )
) $.

polynomial-root-definition $a |- (
  ( PEvalZero p s F ) <->
  ( E.n n (
    ( PDegree p n F )
    /\
    ( ( partial F p s n ) =S F ( zeroS F ) )
  ) )
) $.

$(
  Puiseux's Theorem.  The foundational declarations above construct the
  fixed natural, rational, full series, and standard Puiseux-field domains.
  The theorem's assumptions are exactly that F is a field, has
  characteristic zero, and is algebraically closed.
$)
puiseux-series-algebraically-closed $a |- (
  ( A.f F (
    (
      ( Field F )
      /\
      (
        ( CharZero F )
        /\
        ( AlgebraicClosed F )
      )
    )
    ->
    ( A.p p (
      (
        ( PolyOver p F )
        /\
        ( E.n n (
          ( PositiveN n )
          /\
          ( PDegree p n F )
        ) )
      )
      ->
      ( E.s s (
        ( PuiseuxOver s F )
        /\
        ( PEvalZero p s F )
      ) )
    ) )
  ) )
) $.

title: 041_puiseux_s_theorem
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of "Puiseux's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems
:: item 041. It states that the field of formal Puiseux series over an
:: algebraically closed field of characteristic zero is algebraically closed.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ

 vocabularies NUMBERS, SUBSET_1, CARD_1, RELAT_1, ZFMISC_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3,
      XXREAL_0, XCMPLX_0, FINSEQ_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, TARSKI,
      XBOOLE_0, STRUCT_0, ALGSTR_0, VECTSP_1, RLVECT_1, GROUP_1, RING_3,
      POLYNOM1, ALGSEQ_1, POLYNOM3, POLYNOM5, INT_1, BINOP_1, FVSUM_1,
      FINSOP_1;
 notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0,
      XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, NAT_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
      PARTFUN1, FINSEQ_1, STRUCT_0, ALGSTR_0, RLVECT_1, GROUP_1,
      VECTSP_1, ALGSEQ_1, POLYNOM3, POLYNOM5, RAT_1, RING_3, BINOP_1,
      FINSOP_1;
 constructors ZFMISC_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, FINSEQ_1, REAL_1, ORDINAL1, NAT_D,
      RAT_1, STRUCT_0, RLVECT_1, RING_3, ALGSTR_1, POLYNOM1, POLYNOM4,
      POLYNOM5, BINOP_1, FVSUM_1, FINSOP_1;
 registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS,
      XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XREAL_0, NAT_1, INT_1, RAT_1, MEMBERED,
      FINSEQ_1, STRUCT_0, ALGSTR_0, RLVECT_1, GROUP_1, VECTSP_1, ALGSTR_1,
      POLYNOM3, POLYNOM4, POLYNOM5, ORDINAL1;
 requirements NUMERALS, BOOLE, SUBSET, REAL, ARITHM;
 definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ALGSTR_0, RING_3, POLYNOM5;
 equalities XBOOLE_0, STRUCT_0, ALGSTR_0;
 expansions TARSKI;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for K being algebraic-closed Field,
      P being Field,
      coeff being
        Function of [:the carrier of P,RAT:],the carrier of K
  st
    Char K = 0 &
    (for x,y being Element of P st
      (for q being Element of RAT holds coeff.(x,q) = coeff.(y,q))
      holds x = y) &
    (for s being Function of RAT,the carrier of K holds
      ((ex x being Element of P st
          for q being Element of RAT holds coeff.(x,q) = s.q)
       iff
       ((ex b being Element of RAT st
           for q being Element of RAT st q < b
           holds s.q = the ZeroF of K) &
        (ex n being Element of NAT st n <> 0 &
           (for q being Element of RAT st s.q <> the ZeroF of K
            holds ex i being Integer st q = i/n))))) &
    (for q being Element of RAT holds
      coeff.(the ZeroF of P,q) = the ZeroF of K) &
    (for q being Element of RAT st q = 0
      holds coeff.(the OneF of P,q) = the OneF of K) &
    (for q being Element of RAT st q <> 0
      holds coeff.(the OneF of P,q) = the ZeroF of K) &
    (for x,y being Element of P, q being Element of RAT holds
      coeff.(x+y,q) = coeff.(x,q) + coeff.(y,q)) &
    (for x,y being Element of P, q being Element of RAT holds
      ex exponents being FinSequence of RAT,
         terms being FinSequence of the carrier of K st
        exponents is one-to-one &
        len exponents = len terms &
        coeff.(x*y,q) = (the addF of K) "**" terms &
        (for j being Element of NAT st j in dom exponents holds
          terms/.j =
            (the multF of K).
              (coeff.(x,exponents/.j),coeff.(y,q-exponents/.j))) &
        (for a being Element of RAT holds
          (a in rng exponents iff
            coeff.(x,a) <> the ZeroF of K &
            coeff.(y,q-a) <> the ZeroF of K)))
  holds
    P is algebraic-closed
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 041_puiseux_s_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Puiseux's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems
% item 041. This file contains no proof.

hundred_theorems_041: THEORY
BEGIN
  coefficient: TYPE+

  coefficient_zero, coefficient_one: coefficient
  coefficient_add, coefficient_multiply:
    [coefficient, coefficient -> coefficient]
  coefficient_negate, coefficient_inverse:
    [coefficient -> coefficient]

  coefficient_field_axioms: bool =
    NOT (coefficient_zero = coefficient_one)
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: coefficient):
        coefficient_add(coefficient_add(x, y), z)
          = coefficient_add(x, coefficient_add(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x, y: coefficient):
        coefficient_add(x, y) = coefficient_add(y, x))
      AND (FORALL (x: coefficient):
        coefficient_add(x, coefficient_zero) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x: coefficient):
        coefficient_add(x, coefficient_negate(x)) = coefficient_zero)
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: coefficient):
        coefficient_multiply(coefficient_multiply(x, y), z)
          = coefficient_multiply(x, coefficient_multiply(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x, y: coefficient):
        coefficient_multiply(x, y) = coefficient_multiply(y, x))
      AND (FORALL (x: coefficient):
        coefficient_multiply(x, coefficient_one) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: coefficient):
        coefficient_multiply(x, coefficient_add(y, z))
          = coefficient_add(
              coefficient_multiply(x, y),
              coefficient_multiply(x, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x: coefficient):
        NOT (x = coefficient_zero)
          IMPLIES
            coefficient_multiply(x, coefficient_inverse(x))
              = coefficient_one)

  natural_coefficient(n: nat): RECURSIVE coefficient =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      coefficient_zero
    ELSE
      coefficient_add(natural_coefficient(n - 1), coefficient_one)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  coefficient_characteristic_zero: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      0 < n IMPLIES NOT (natural_coefficient(n) = coefficient_zero)

  coefficient_power(x: coefficient, exponent: nat):
      RECURSIVE coefficient =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      coefficient_one
    ELSE
      coefficient_multiply(
        coefficient_power(x, exponent - 1),
        x)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  coefficient_polynomial_value(
      coefficients: [nat -> coefficient],
      x: coefficient,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE coefficient =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      coefficient_zero
    ELSE
      LET k: nat = count - 1 IN
        coefficient_add(
          coefficient_polynomial_value(coefficients, x, count - 1),
          coefficient_multiply(
            coefficients(k),
            coefficient_power(x, k)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  coefficient_algebraically_closed: bool =
    FORALL (coefficients: [nat -> coefficient]), (degree: nat):
      (0 < degree
        AND NOT (coefficients(degree) = coefficient_zero))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (root: coefficient):
          coefficient_polynomial_value(
            coefficients,
            root,
            degree + 1)
            = coefficient_zero

  puiseux_series: TYPE = [rat -> coefficient]

  supported_on_grid_above(
      series: puiseux_series,
      denominator: posnat,
      lower_index: int): bool =
    FORALL (exponent: rat):
      NOT (series(exponent) = coefficient_zero)
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (index: int):
            lower_index <= index
              AND exponent
                = (index :: rat) / (denominator :: rat)

  is_puiseux_series(series: puiseux_series): bool =
    EXISTS (denominator: posnat), (lower_index: int):
      supported_on_grid_above(series, denominator, lower_index)

  zero_series: puiseux_series =
    LAMBDA (exponent: rat): coefficient_zero

  one_series: puiseux_series =
    LAMBDA (exponent: rat):
      IF exponent = 0 THEN coefficient_one ELSE coefficient_zero ENDIF

  series_add(left, right: puiseux_series): puiseux_series =
    LAMBDA (exponent: rat):
      coefficient_add(left(exponent), right(exponent))

  series_negate(series: puiseux_series): puiseux_series =
    LAMBDA (exponent: rat):
      coefficient_negate(series(exponent))

  series_multiply:
    [puiseux_series, puiseux_series -> puiseux_series]

  coefficient_sum(
      values: [nat -> coefficient],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE coefficient =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      coefficient_zero
    ELSE
      coefficient_add(
        coefficient_sum(values, count - 1),
        values(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  is_convolution_coefficient(
      left, right: puiseux_series,
      denominator: posnat,
      left_lower, right_lower, total_index: int,
      value: coefficient): bool =
    EXISTS (count: nat):
      (((total_index - right_lower < left_lower) AND count = 0)
        OR
        (left_lower <= total_index - right_lower
          AND count
            = total_index - right_lower - left_lower + 1))
      AND value
        = coefficient_sum(
            LAMBDA (offset: nat):
              coefficient_multiply(
                left(
                  ((left_lower + offset) :: rat)
                    / (denominator :: rat)),
                right(
                  ((total_index - left_lower - offset) :: rat)
                    / (denominator :: rat))),
            count)

  is_cauchy_product(
      left, right, product: puiseux_series): bool =
    FORALL (denominator: posnat),
        (left_lower, right_lower: int):
      (supported_on_grid_above(left, denominator, left_lower)
        AND supported_on_grid_above(right, denominator, right_lower))
      IMPLIES
        ((FORALL (total_index: int):
          is_convolution_coefficient(
            left,
            right,
            denominator,
            left_lower,
            right_lower,
            total_index,
            product(
              (total_index :: rat) / (denominator :: rat))))
        AND
        (FORALL (exponent: rat):
          (FORALL (index: int):
            NOT (exponent
              = (index :: rat) / (denominator :: rat)))
          IMPLIES product(exponent) = coefficient_zero))

  series_multiplication_is_cauchy: bool =
    FORALL (left, right: puiseux_series):
      (is_puiseux_series(left) AND is_puiseux_series(right))
      IMPLIES
        is_cauchy_product(
          left,
          right,
          series_multiply(left, right))

  puiseux_field_axioms: bool =
    is_puiseux_series(zero_series)
      AND is_puiseux_series(one_series)
      AND NOT (zero_series = one_series)
      AND (FORALL (x, y: puiseux_series):
        (is_puiseux_series(x) AND is_puiseux_series(y))
        IMPLIES
          (is_puiseux_series(series_add(x, y))
            AND is_puiseux_series(series_multiply(x, y))))
      AND (FORALL (x: puiseux_series):
        is_puiseux_series(x)
        IMPLIES is_puiseux_series(series_negate(x)))
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: puiseux_series):
        (is_puiseux_series(x)
          AND is_puiseux_series(y)
          AND is_puiseux_series(z))
        IMPLIES
          series_add(series_add(x, y), z)
            = series_add(x, series_add(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x, y: puiseux_series):
        (is_puiseux_series(x) AND is_puiseux_series(y))
        IMPLIES series_add(x, y) = series_add(y, x))
      AND (FORALL (x: puiseux_series):
        is_puiseux_series(x)
        IMPLIES series_add(x, zero_series) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x: puiseux_series):
        is_puiseux_series(x)
        IMPLIES series_add(x, series_negate(x)) = zero_series)
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: puiseux_series):
        (is_puiseux_series(x)
          AND is_puiseux_series(y)
          AND is_puiseux_series(z))
        IMPLIES
          series_multiply(series_multiply(x, y), z)
            = series_multiply(x, series_multiply(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x, y: puiseux_series):
        (is_puiseux_series(x) AND is_puiseux_series(y))
        IMPLIES series_multiply(x, y) = series_multiply(y, x))
      AND (FORALL (x: puiseux_series):
        is_puiseux_series(x)
        IMPLIES series_multiply(x, one_series) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: puiseux_series):
        (is_puiseux_series(x)
          AND is_puiseux_series(y)
          AND is_puiseux_series(z))
        IMPLIES
          series_multiply(x, series_add(y, z))
            = series_add(
                series_multiply(x, y),
                series_multiply(x, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x: puiseux_series):
        (is_puiseux_series(x) AND NOT (x = zero_series))
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (inverse: puiseux_series):
            is_puiseux_series(inverse)
              AND series_multiply(x, inverse) = one_series)

  series_power(
      series: puiseux_series,
      exponent: nat): RECURSIVE puiseux_series =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      one_series
    ELSE
      series_multiply(
        series_power(series, exponent - 1),
        series)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  series_polynomial_value(
      coefficients: [nat -> puiseux_series],
      value: puiseux_series,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE puiseux_series =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      zero_series
    ELSE
      LET k: nat = count - 1 IN
        series_add(
          series_polynomial_value(coefficients, value, count - 1),
          series_multiply(
            coefficients(k),
            series_power(value, k)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  positive_degree_puiseux_polynomial(
      coefficients: [nat -> puiseux_series],
      degree: nat): bool =
    0 < degree
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index <= degree
          IMPLIES is_puiseux_series(coefficients(index)))
      AND NOT (coefficients(degree) = zero_series)

  puiseux_s_theorem: bool =
    (coefficient_field_axioms
      AND coefficient_characteristic_zero
      AND coefficient_algebraically_closed
      AND series_multiplication_is_cauchy
      AND puiseux_field_axioms)
    IMPLIES
      FORALL (coefficients: [nat -> puiseux_series]), (degree: nat):
        positive_degree_puiseux_polynomial(coefficients, degree)
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (root: puiseux_series):
            is_puiseux_series(root)
              AND series_polynomial_value(
                coefficients,
                root,
                degree + 1)
                = zero_series
END hundred_theorems_041

import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Powerset

/-!
# Sum of the Reciprocals of the Triangular Numbers

This file proves Theorem 42 from the [100 Theorems List](https://www.cs.ru.nl/~freek/100/).

We interpret “triangular numbers” as naturals of the form $\frac{k(k+1)}{2}$ for natural `k`.
We prove that the sum of the reciprocals of the first `n` triangular numbers is $2 - \frac2n$.

## Tags

discrete_sum
-/


open Finset

/-- **Sum of the Reciprocals of the Triangular Numbers** -/
theorem Theorems100.inverse_triangle_sum (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ k ∈ range n, (2 : ℚ) / (k * (k + 1)) = if n = 0 then 0 else 2 - (2 : ℚ) / n := by sorry

Require Import Rseries_facts.
Require Import Rtactic.

Require Import Lra.

Definition triangle n := INR (n * S n) / 2.

Lemma triangle_sum n : sum_f_R0 INR n = triangle n.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma triangle_non_negative n : 0 <= triangle n.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma triangle_positive n : 0 < triangle (S n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma sum_consecutive_triangle n : triangle (S n) + triangle n = INR (S n) * INR (S n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma difference_consecutive_triangle n : (triangle (S n) - triangle n)² = INR (S n) * INR (S n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma sum_triangular_tetrahedral n : sum_f_R0 triangle n = INR (n * S n * S (S n)) / 6.
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition inv_snssn n := / INR (S n * S (S n)).

Definition inv_sn n := / INR (S n).

Lemma diff_inv_snssn n : inv_snssn n = inv_sn n - inv_sn (S n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma sum_inv_snssn n : sum_f_R0 inv_snssn n = 1 - inv_sn (S n).

Admitted.

Admitted.

Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma sum_reciprocal_triangular : Rser_cv (fun n => / triangle (S n)) 2.
Proof.
Admitted.

(*
  Title:     HOL/ex/Triangular_Numbers.thy
  Author:    Manuel Eberl, TU München
*)
section \<open>Triangular Numbers\<close>
theory Triangular_Numbers
  imports Complex_Main
begin

definition triangle_num :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "triangle_num n = (n * (n + 1)) div 2"

lemma real_triangle_num:
  "real (triangle_num n) = real n * (real n + 1) / 2"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_altdef: "triangle_num n = (\<Sum>k\<le>n. k)"
  by sorry


lemma triangle_num_ge: "triangle_num n \<ge> n"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_Suc: "triangle_num (Suc n) = triangle_num n + Suc n"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_0 [simp]: "triangle_num 0 = 0"
  and triangle_num_1 [simp]: "triangle_num 1 = 1"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_numeral [simp]:
  "triangle_num (numeral n) = fst (divmod (n * Num.inc n) (Num.Bit0 Num.One))"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_eq_0_iff [simp]: "triangle_num n = 0 \<longleftrightarrow> n = 0"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_gt_0_iff [simp]: "triangle_num n > 0 \<longleftrightarrow> n > 0"
  by sorry


lemma strict_mono_triangle_num: "strict_mono triangle_num"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_le: "m \<le> n \<Longrightarrow> triangle_num m \<le> triangle_num n"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_less: "m < n \<Longrightarrow> triangle_num m < triangle_num n"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_less_iff: "triangle_num m < triangle_num n \<longleftrightarrow> m < n"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_le_iff: "triangle_num m \<le> triangle_num n \<longleftrightarrow> m \<le> n"
  by sorry

lemma triangle_num_eq_iff: "triangle_num m = triangle_num n \<longleftrightarrow> m = n"
  by sorry


theorem inverse_triangle_num_sums: "(\<lambda>n. 1 / triangle_num (Suc n)) sums 2"
  by sorry

end

title: 042_sum_of_the_reciprocals_of_the_triangular_numbers
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__042, "Sum of the Reciprocals of the Triangular
;; Numbers": for T_k = k(k+1)/2, the exact reciprocal partial sum is
;; sum_{k=1}^n 1/T_k = 2 - 2/(n+1), and these sums converge to 2.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun hundred-theorems-042-triangular-number (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (/ (* n (+ n 1)) 2)
    0))

(defun hundred-theorems-042-reciprocal-triangular-prefix (terms)
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (+ (hundred-theorems-042-reciprocal-triangular-prefix (- terms 1))
       (/ 1
          (hundred-theorems-042-triangular-number terms)))))

(defun hundred-theorems-042-finite-sum-statement (terms)
  (implies
   (natp terms)
   (equal
    (hundred-theorems-042-reciprocal-triangular-prefix terms)
    (- 2 (/ 2 (+ terms 1))))))

;; For positive reduced rational epsilon = p/q, 2q+1 is an internal natural
;; cutoff witness: at every later natural term count the exact error
;; 2/(terms+1) is strictly below epsilon.
(defun hundred-theorems-042-cutoff (epsilon)
  (if (and (rationalp epsilon)
           (< 0 epsilon))
      (+ 1 (* 2 (denominator epsilon)))
    0))

;; Universal predicate matrix for the explicit witness above. Positive
;; rational tolerances are cofinal in the positive reals, so this is
;; equivalent to convergence of the rational-valued prefixes to 2 over R.
(defun hundred-theorems-042-sum-of-reciprocals-statement
    (epsilon terms)
  (implies
   (and (rationalp epsilon)
        (< 0 epsilon)
        (natp terms)
        (<= (hundred-theorems-042-cutoff epsilon)
            terms))
   (< (abs
       (- (hundred-theorems-042-reciprocal-triangular-prefix terms)
          2))
      epsilon)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 042_sum_of_the_reciprocals_of_the_triangular_numbers
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Sum of the Reciprocals of the Triangular Numbers" from
-- Hundred Theorems item 042. This file contains no proof.

module SumReciprocalsTriangularNumbers where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<= : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      Both (lessOrEqual zeroR oneR) (zeroR != oneR)

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
              lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both (lessOrEqual reals x y) (x != y)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      Both
        (StrictLess reals
          (subtract reals limit epsilon)
          (sequence n))
        (StrictLess reals
          (sequence n)
          (add reals limit epsilon)))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals term limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n term)
    limit

triangularNumber :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
triangularNumber reals n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (fromNat reals n)
      (fromNat reals (suc n)))
    (fromNat reals 2)

reciprocalTriangularTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
reciprocalTriangularTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (oneR reals)
    (triangularNumber reals (suc n))

sum-of-the-reciprocals-of-the-triangular-numbers : Set1
sum-of-the-reciprocals-of-the-triangular-numbers =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  SeriesHasSum reals
    (reciprocalTriangularTerm reals)
    (fromNat reals 2)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Sum of the Reciprocals of the Triangular Numbers" from
  Hundred Theorems item 042. The partial sums of the reciprocals of the nonzero triangular
  numbers converge to 2. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val sum_of_the_reciprocals_of_the_triangular_numbers =
  ``!e : real.
      0 < e
      ==>
      ?N : num.
        !n : num.
          N <= n
          ==>
          abs
            (SIGMA
               (\k : num.
                  (1 : real) /
                  &((k * (k + 1)) DIV 2))
               (IMAGE SUC (count n)) -
             2) < e``;
