     standard-normal-measure lintegral exp sin cos)
  (list
   'lambda '(t-value)
   (ht047-implies-term
    (ht047-static-apply-term real-carrier '(t-value))
    (let* ((two
            (ht047-real-nat-value
             2 real-zero real-one real-add))
           (t-square
            (ht047-static-apply-term
             real-multiply '(t-value t-value)))
           (minus-half-square
            (ht047-static-apply-term
             real-negate
             (list
              (ht047-static-apply-term
               real-multiply
               (list
                t-square
                (ht047-static-apply-term
                 real-inverse
                 (list (ht047-quoted two)))))))))
      (ht047-and-terms
       (list
        (list
         'equal
         (list
          'ht047-real-integral-value
          (ht047-quoted real-zero)
          (ht047-quoted real-add)
          (ht047-quoted real-negate)
          (ht047-quoted real-less)
          (ht047-quoted real-carrier)
          (ht047-quoted real-borel)
          (ht047-quoted standard-normal-measure)
          (ht047-quoted real-carrier)
          (list
           'ht047-characteristic-cos-function
           't-value
           (ht047-quoted real-multiply)
           (ht047-quoted cos))
          (ht047-quoted lintegral))
         (ht047-static-apply-term exp (list minus-half-square)))
        (list
         'equal
         (list
          'ht047-real-integral-value
          (ht047-quoted real-zero)
          (ht047-quoted real-add)
          (ht047-quoted real-negate)
          (ht047-quoted real-less)
          (ht047-quoted real-carrier)
          (ht047-quoted real-borel)
          (ht047-quoted standard-normal-measure)
          (ht047-quoted real-carrier)
          (list
           'ht047-characteristic-sin-function
           't-value
           (ht047-quoted real-multiply)
           (ht047-quoted sin))
          (ht047-quoted lintegral))
         (ht047-quoted real-zero))))))))

(defun ht047-standard-normal-distribution-p
    (real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
     real-negate real-inverse real-less real-borel
     standard-normal-measure lintegral exp sin cos)
  (and
   (ht047-probability-measure-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-less
    real-carrier real-borel standard-normal-measure)
   (ht047-lintegral-operation-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-add real-multiply real-less
    real-carrier real-borel standard-normal-measure lintegral)
   (ht047-universal-p
    (ht047-standard-normal-characteristic-function
     real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply real-negate
     real-inverse real-less real-carrier real-borel
     standard-normal-measure lintegral exp sin cos)
    '(t-value))))

;; Constant source-space families let the general weak-convergence definition
;; express weak convergence of the laws of random variables on one space.

(defun ht047-constant-source-carrier-family (sample-carrier)
  (list
   'lambda '(n x)
   (ht047-static-apply-term sample-carrier '(x))))

(defun ht047-constant-source-measurable-family (sample-measurable)
  (list
   'lambda '(n set)
   (ht047-static-apply-term sample-measurable '(set))))

(defun ht047-constant-source-measure-family (sample-measure)
  (list
   'lambda '(n set)
   (ht047-static-apply-term sample-measure '(set))))

(defun ht047-real-identity-function ()
  (list 'lambda '(x) 'x))

(defun ht047-weak-convergence-to-standard-normal-p
    (real-carrier real-zero real-add real-negate real-less real-topology
     sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure lintegral
     normalized-family real-borel standard-normal-measure)
  (ht047-weak-convergence-p
   real-carrier real-zero real-add real-negate real-less real-topology
   (ht047-natural-carrier)
   (ht047-sequential-filter)
   (ht047-constant-source-carrier-family sample-carrier)
   (ht047-constant-source-measurable-family sample-measurable)
   (ht047-constant-source-measure-family sample-measure)
   lintegral
   normalized-family
   real-carrier
   real-borel
   standard-normal-measure
   lintegral
   (ht047-real-identity-function)
   real-carrier
   real-topology))

;; Shared structural and probabilistic hypotheses of the two source theorems.

(defun ht047-central-limit-context-p
    (real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
     real-negate real-inverse real-less real-supremum
     real-topology real-borel exp sin cos square-root
     sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure
     common-measure standard-normal-measure lintegral
     x-family mean sigma)
  (and
   (ht047-real-field-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
    real-negate real-inverse real-less real-supremum)
   (ht047-order-topology-p
    real-carrier real-less real-topology)
   (ht047-borel-space-p
    real-carrier real-topology real-borel)
   (ht047-filter-p
    (ht047-natural-carrier)
    (ht047-sequential-filter))
   (ht047-analytic-functions-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
    real-negate real-inverse real-less exp sin cos)
   (ht047-square-root-operation-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-multiply real-less square-root)
   (ht047-probability-measure-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-less
    sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure)
   (ht047-lintegral-operation-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-add real-multiply real-less
    sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure lintegral)
   (ht047-measure-space-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-add real-less
    real-carrier real-borel common-measure)
   (ht047-standard-normal-distribution-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
    real-negate real-inverse real-less real-borel
    standard-normal-measure lintegral exp sin cos)
   (ht047-random-variable-family-p
    sample-carrier sample-measurable
    real-carrier real-borel x-family)
   (ht047-independent-random-variables-p
    sample-carrier sample-measure real-borel x-family
    real-zero real-one real-multiply)
   (ht047-common-distribution-family-p
    sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure
    real-carrier real-borel common-measure x-family)
   (ht047-member-p real-carrier mean)
   (ht047-member-p real-carrier sigma)
   (ht047-binary-value real-less real-zero sigma)
   (ht047-moment-laws-p
    real-zero real-add real-multiply real-negate real-less
    sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure
    real-carrier x-family lintegral mean sigma)))

(defun hundred-theorems-047-central-limit-theorem-zero-mean-statement
    (real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
     real-negate real-inverse real-less real-supremum
     real-topology real-borel exp sin cos square-root
     sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure
     common-measure standard-normal-measure lintegral
     x-family sigma s-family)
  (implies
   (and
    (ht047-central-limit-context-p
     real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
     real-negate real-inverse real-less real-supremum
     real-topology real-borel exp sin cos square-root
     sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure
     common-measure standard-normal-measure lintegral
     x-family real-zero sigma)
    (ht047-partial-sum-family-p
     sample-carrier x-family s-family real-zero real-add))
   (ht047-weak-convergence-to-standard-normal-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-add real-negate real-less real-topology
    sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure lintegral
    (ht047-normalized-s-family
     s-family sigma
     real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
     real-inverse square-root)
    real-borel standard-normal-measure)))

(defun hundred-theorems-047-central-limit-theorem-statement
    (real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
     real-negate real-inverse real-less real-supremum
     real-topology real-borel exp sin cos square-root
     sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure
     common-measure standard-normal-measure lintegral
     x-family mean sigma)
  (implies
   (ht047-central-limit-context-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-one real-add real-multiply
    real-negate real-inverse real-less real-supremum
    real-topology real-borel exp sin cos square-root
    sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure
    common-measure standard-normal-measure lintegral
    x-family mean sigma)
   (ht047-weak-convergence-to-standard-normal-p
    real-carrier real-zero real-add real-negate real-less real-topology
    sample-carrier sample-measurable sample-measure lintegral
    (ht047-centered-normalized-x-family
     x-family mean sigma

    real-borel standard-normal-measure)))

title: 047_the_central_limit_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 047, "The Central Limit Theorem":
-- the zero-mean and centered forms for independent, identically distributed, square-integrable
-- real random variables with positive variance and weak convergence to the standard normal law.
-- This file contains no proof.

module CentralLimitTheorem where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data List (A : Set) : Set where
  empty : List A
  cons  : A -> List A -> List A

data Member {A : Set} (x : A) : List A -> Set where
  at-head : {xs : List A} -> Member x (cons x xs)
  in-tail : {y : A} {xs : List A} -> Member x xs -> Member x (cons y xs)

data NoDuplicates {A : Set} : List A -> Set where
  no-duplicates-empty :
    NoDuplicates empty
  no-duplicates-cons :
    {x : A} {xs : List A} ->
    Not (Member x xs) ->
    NoDuplicates xs ->
    NoDuplicates (cons x xs)

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate reciprocal absoluteValue : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    reciprocal-zero :
      reciprocal zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-reciprocal :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (reciprocal x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      Both (lessOrEqual zeroR oneR) (zeroR != oneR)

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    absolute-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      absoluteValue x == x
    absolute-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      absoluteValue x == negate x

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
              lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (reciprocal reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both (lessOrEqual reals x y) (x != y)

Close :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
Close reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (absoluteValue reals (subtract reals x center))
    radius

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      StrictLess reals
        (absoluteValue reals (subtract reals (sequence n) limit))
        epsilon)

BoundedFunction :
  {A R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (A -> R) ->
  Set
BoundedFunction {A} {R} reals f =
  Exists R
    (\ bound ->
      Both
        (lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) bound)
        ((x : A) ->
          lessOrEqual reals
            (absoluteValue reals (f x))
            bound))

Continuous :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
Continuous {R} reals f =
  (x epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      Both
        (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta)
        ((y : R) ->
          Close reals x delta y ->
          Close reals (f x) epsilon (f y)))

record BoundedContinuous
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (f : R -> R) : Set where
  field
    bounded    : BoundedFunction reals f
    continuous : Continuous reals f

power :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
power reals x zero =
  oneR reals
power reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals (power reals x n) x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingSign reals zero =
  oneR reals
alternatingSign reals (suc n) =
  negate reals (alternatingSign reals n)

evenIndex : Nat -> Nat
evenIndex n =
  n + n

oddIndex : Nat -> Nat
oddIndex n =
  suc (evenIndex n)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
sumFirst reals term zero =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals term (suc n) =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals term n)
    (term n)

exponentialPartialSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialPartialSum reals x n =
  sumFirst reals
    (\ k ->
      divide reals
        (power reals x k)
        (fromNat reals (factorial k)))
    n

cosinePartialSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
cosinePartialSum reals x n =
  sumFirst reals
    (\ k ->
      multiply reals
        (alternatingSign reals k)
        (divide reals
          (power reals x (evenIndex k))
          (fromNat reals (factorial (evenIndex k)))))
    n

sinePartialSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sinePartialSum reals x n =
  sumFirst reals
    (\ k ->
      multiply reals
        (alternatingSign reals k)
        (divide reals
          (power reals x (oddIndex k))
          (fromNat reals (factorial (oddIndex k)))))
    n

Predicate : Set -> Set1
Predicate A = A -> Set

emptySet :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A
emptySet _ =
  Bottom

wholeSet :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A
wholeSet _ =
  Top

complement :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A ->
  Predicate A
complement E x =
  Not (E x)

countableUnion :
  {A : Set} ->
  (Nat -> Predicate A) ->
  Predicate A
countableUnion sets x =
  Exists Nat (\ n -> sets n x)

record SigmaAlgebra (A : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    measurable : Predicate A -> Set

    measurable-empty :
      measurable emptySet
    measurable-complement :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      measurable E ->
      measurable (complement E)
    measurable-countable-union :
      (sets : Nat -> Predicate A) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> measurable (sets n)) ->
      measurable (countableUnion sets)
    measurable-congruent :
      (E F : Predicate A) ->
      ((x : A) -> Iff (E x) (F x)) ->
      measurable E ->
      measurable F

open SigmaAlgebra

record StandardRealAnalysis (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    algebra : CompleteOrderedField R
    squareRoot exponential cosine sine : R -> R

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      square algebra (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra x (zeroR algebra) ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR algebra

    exponential-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SequentialLimit algebra
        (exponentialPartialSum algebra x)
        (exponential x)
    cosine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SequentialLimit algebra
        (cosinePartialSum algebra x)
        (cosine x)
    sine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SequentialLimit algebra
        (sinePartialSum algebra x)
        (sine x)

    borel : SigmaAlgebra R
    borel-open-ray :
      (a : R) ->
      measurable borel (\ x -> StrictLess algebra a x)
    borel-minimal :
      (candidate : SigmaAlgebra R) ->
      ((a : R) ->
        measurable candidate (\ x -> StrictLess algebra a x)) ->
      (E : Predicate R) ->
      measurable borel E ->
      measurable candidate E

open StandardRealAnalysis

preimage :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Predicate B ->
  Predicate A
preimage f E x =
  E (f x)

MeasurableFunction :
  {A B : Set} ->
  SigmaAlgebra A ->
  SigmaAlgebra B ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set1
MeasurableFunction source target f =
  (E : Predicate _) ->
  measurable target E ->
  measurable source (preimage f E)

PairwiseDisjoint :
  {A : Set} ->
  (Nat -> Predicate A) ->
  Set
PairwiseDisjoint {A} sets =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  i != j ->
  (x : A) ->
  sets i x ->
  sets j x ->
  Bottom

record Measure
  {A R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) : Set1 where
  field
    mass : Predicate A -> R

    mass-congruent :
      (E F : Predicate A) ->
      ((x : A) -> Iff (E x) (F x)) ->
      mass E == mass F
    mass-empty :
      mass emptySet == zeroR (algebra analysis)
    mass-nonnegative :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      measurable events E ->
      lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
        (zeroR (algebra analysis))
        (mass E)
    countable-additivity :
      (sets : Nat -> Predicate A) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> measurable events (sets n)) ->
      PairwiseDisjoint sets ->
      SequentialLimit (algebra analysis)
        (\ count ->
          sumFirst (algebra analysis)
            (\ n -> mass (sets n))
            count)
        (mass (countableUnion sets))

open Measure

record Integration
  {A R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A)
  (measure : Measure analysis events) : Set1 where
  field
    integrable : (A -> R) -> Set
    integral : (A -> R) -> R
    indicator : Predicate A -> A -> R

    integrable-congruent :
      (f g : A -> R) ->
      ((x : A) -> f x == g x) ->
      Iff (integrable f) (integrable g)
    integral-congruent :
      (f g : A -> R) ->
      ((x : A) -> f x == g x) ->
      integral f == integral g

    integrable-zero :
      integrable (\ _ -> zeroR (algebra analysis))
    integral-zero :
      integral (\ _ -> zeroR (algebra analysis)) ==
      zeroR (algebra analysis)
    integrable-add :
      (f g : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integrable g ->
      integrable
        (\ x -> add (algebra analysis) (f x) (g x))
    integral-add :
      (f g : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integrable g ->
      integral
        (\ x -> add (algebra analysis) (f x) (g x)) ==
      add (algebra analysis) (integral f) (integral g)
    integrable-negate :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integrable (\ x -> negate (algebra analysis) (f x))
    integral-negate :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integral (\ x -> negate (algebra analysis) (f x)) ==
      negate (algebra analysis) (integral f)
    integrable-scale :
      (c : R) ->
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integrable
        (\ x -> multiply (algebra analysis) c (f x))
    integral-scale :
      (c : R) ->
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integral
        (\ x -> multiply (algebra analysis) c (f x)) ==
      multiply (algebra analysis) c (integral f)
    integrable-absolute :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      Iff
        (integrable f)
        (integrable
          (\ x -> absoluteValue (algebra analysis) (f x)))
    integral-nonnegative :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      ((x : A) ->
        lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
          (zeroR (algebra analysis))
          (f x)) ->
      lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
        (zeroR (algebra analysis))
        (integral f)

    indicator-on :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      (x : A) ->
      E x ->
      indicator E x == oneR (algebra analysis)
    indicator-off :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      (x : A) ->
      Not (E x) ->
      indicator E x == zeroR (algebra analysis)
    indicator-integrable :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      measurable events E ->
      integrable (indicator E)
    integral-indicator :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      measurable events E ->
      integral (indicator E) == mass measure E

    bounded-measurable-integrable :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      MeasurableFunction events (borel analysis) f ->
      BoundedFunction (algebra analysis) f ->
      integrable f

    monotone-convergence :
      (functions : Nat -> A -> R) ->
      (limitFunction : A -> R) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> integrable (functions n)) ->
      ((n : Nat) ->
        (x : A) ->
        lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
          (zeroR (algebra analysis))
          (functions n x)) ->
      ((n : Nat) ->
        (x : A) ->
        lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
          (functions n x)
          (functions (suc n) x)) ->
      ((x : A) ->
        SequentialLimit (algebra analysis)
          (\ n -> functions n x)
          (limitFunction x)) ->
      (limitIntegral : R) ->
      SequentialLimit (algebra analysis)
        (\ n -> integral (functions n))
        limitIntegral ->
      Both
        (integrable limitFunction)
        (integral limitFunction == limitIntegral)

open Integration

record IntegratedMeasure
  {A R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) : Set1 where
  field
    measure : Measure analysis events
    integration : Integration analysis events measure

open IntegratedMeasure

record ProbabilitySpace
  {A R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) : Set1 where
  field
    integratedMeasure : IntegratedMeasure analysis events
    total-mass-one :
      mass (measure integratedMeasure) wholeSet ==
      oneR (algebra analysis)

open ProbabilitySpace

spaceMeasure :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  Measure analysis events
spaceMeasure space =
  measure (integratedMeasure space)

spaceIntegration :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  (space : ProbabilitySpace analysis events) ->
  Integration analysis events (spaceMeasure space)
spaceIntegration space =
  integration (integratedMeasure space)

probabilityOf :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  Predicate A ->
  R
probabilityOf space E =
  mass (spaceMeasure space) E

IsIntegrable :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (A -> R) ->
  Set
IsIntegrable space f =
  integrable (spaceIntegration space) f

expectation :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (A -> R) ->
  R
expectation space f =
  integral (spaceIntegration space) f

variance :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (A -> R) ->
  R
variance {analysis = analysis} space f =
  expectation space
    (\ x ->
      square (algebra analysis)
        (subtract (algebra analysis) (f x) (expectation space f)))

SquareIntegrable :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (A -> R) ->
  Set
SquareIntegrable {analysis = analysis} space f =
  IsIntegrable space
    (\ x -> square (algebra analysis) (f x))

record StandardProbabilityTheory (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R
    standardNormal :
      ProbabilitySpace analysis (borel analysis)

    normal-cosine-integrable :
      (t : R) ->
      IsIntegrable standardNormal
        (\ x ->
          cosine analysis
            (multiply (algebra analysis) t x))
    normal-sine-integrable :
      (t : R) ->
      IsIntegrable standardNormal
        (\ x ->
          sine analysis
            (multiply (algebra analysis) t x))
    normal-cosine-transform :
      (t : R) ->
      expectation standardNormal
        (\ x ->
          cosine analysis
            (multiply (algebra analysis) t x)) ==
      exponential analysis
        (negate (algebra analysis)
          (divide (algebra analysis)
            (square (algebra analysis) t)
            (fromNat (algebra analysis) (suc (suc zero)))))
    normal-sine-transform :
      (t : R) ->
      expectation standardNormal
        (\ x ->
          sine analysis
            (multiply (algebra analysis) t x)) ==
      zeroR (algebra analysis)

open StandardProbabilityTheory

realAlgebra :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardProbabilityTheory R ->
  CompleteOrderedField R
realAlgebra theory =
  algebra (analysis theory)

realBorel :
  {R : Set} ->
  (theory : StandardProbabilityTheory R) ->
  SigmaAlgebra R
realBorel theory =
  borel (analysis theory)

finiteIntersection :
  {R A : Set} ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  (Nat -> Predicate R) ->
  List Nat ->
  Predicate A
finiteIntersection X sets empty _ =
  Top
finiteIntersection X sets (cons i indices) x =
  Both
    (sets i (X i x))
    (finiteIntersection X sets indices x)

finiteProbabilityProduct :
  {R A : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  (Nat -> Predicate R) ->
  List Nat ->
  R
finiteProbabilityProduct {analysis = analysis} space X sets empty =
  oneR (algebra analysis)
finiteProbabilityProduct {analysis = analysis} space X sets
  (cons i indices) =
  multiply (algebra analysis)
    (probabilityOf space (\ x -> sets i (X i x)))
    (finiteProbabilityProduct space X sets indices)

record IndependentVariables
  {R A : Set}
  (theory : StandardProbabilityTheory R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A)
  (space : ProbabilitySpace (analysis theory) events)
  (X : Nat -> A -> R) : Set1 where
  field
    measurable-variable :
      (n : Nat) ->
      MeasurableFunction events (realBorel theory) (X n)
    independent-events :
      (indices : List Nat) ->
      NoDuplicates indices ->
      (sets : Nat -> Predicate R) ->
      ((i : Nat) ->
        Member i indices ->
        measurable (realBorel theory) (sets i)) ->
      probabilityOf space (finiteIntersection X sets indices) ==
      finiteProbabilityProduct space X sets indices

HasDistribution :
  {R A : Set} ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) ->
  (space : ProbabilitySpace analysis events) ->
  (randomVariable : A -> R) ->
  Measure analysis (borel analysis) ->
  Set1
HasDistribution analysis events space randomVariable distribution =
  (E : Predicate _) ->
  measurable (borel analysis) E ->
  mass distribution E ==
  probabilityOf space (preimage randomVariable E)

partialSum :
  {R A : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  A ->
  R
partialSum reals X n x =
  sumFirst reals (\ i -> X i x) n

centeredPartialSum :
  {R A : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  A ->
  R
centeredPartialSum reals X mean n x =
  sumFirst reals
    (\ i -> subtract reals (X i x) mean)
    n

normalizingScale :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
normalizingScale analysis sigma n =
  squareRoot analysis
    (multiply (algebra analysis)
      (fromNat (algebra analysis) n)
      (square (algebra analysis) sigma))

normalizedPartialSum :
  {R A : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  A ->
  R
normalizedPartialSum analysis X sigma n x =
  divide (algebra analysis)
    (partialSum (algebra analysis) X n x)
    (normalizingScale analysis sigma n)

normalizedCenteredPartialSum :
  {R A : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  A ->
  R
normalizedCenteredPartialSum analysis X mean sigma n x =
  divide (algebra analysis)
    (centeredPartialSum (algebra analysis) X mean n x)
    (normalizingScale analysis sigma n)

WeakConvergenceOfLaws :
  {R A : Set} ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis (borel analysis) ->
  Set
WeakConvergenceOfLaws {R = R} analysis events space randomVariables limitLaw =
  (test : R -> R) ->
  BoundedContinuous (algebra analysis) test ->
  SequentialLimit (algebra analysis)
    (\ n ->
      expectation space
        (\ x -> test (randomVariables n x)))
    (expectation limitLaw test)

central-limit-theorem-zero-mean : Set1
central-limit-theorem-zero-mean =
  (R A : Set) ->
  (theory : StandardProbabilityTheory R) ->
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) ->
  (space : ProbabilitySpace (analysis theory) events) ->
  (X : Nat -> A -> R) ->
  (commonDistribution :
    Measure (analysis theory) (realBorel theory)) ->
  (sigma : R) ->
  IndependentVariables theory events space X ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    expectation space (X n) ==
    zeroR (realAlgebra theory)) ->
  StrictLess (realAlgebra theory)
    (zeroR (realAlgebra theory))
    sigma ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    SquareIntegrable space (X n)) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    variance space (X n) ==
    square (realAlgebra theory) sigma) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    HasDistribution
      (analysis theory)
      events
      space
      (X n)
      commonDistribution) ->
  WeakConvergenceOfLaws
    (analysis theory)
    events
    space
    (normalizedPartialSum (analysis theory) X sigma)
    (standardNormal theory)

central-limit-theorem : Set1
central-limit-theorem =
  (R A : Set) ->
  (theory : StandardProbabilityTheory R) ->
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) ->
  (space : ProbabilitySpace (analysis theory) events) ->
  (X : Nat -> A -> R) ->
  (commonDistribution :
    Measure (analysis theory) (realBorel theory)) ->
  (mean sigma : R) ->
  IndependentVariables theory events space X ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    expectation space (X n) == mean) ->
  StrictLess (realAlgebra theory)
    (zeroR (realAlgebra theory))
    sigma ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    SquareIntegrable space (X n)) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    variance space (X n) ==
    square (realAlgebra theory) sigma) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    HasDistribution
      (analysis theory)
      events
      space
      (X n)
      commonDistribution) ->
  WeakConvergenceOfLaws
    (analysis theory)
    events
    space
    (normalizedCenteredPartialSum
      (analysis theory)
      X
      mean
      sigma)
    (standardNormal theory)

title: 047_the_central_limit_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "The Central Limit Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 047.
  It states the zero-mean and centered i.i.d. finite-variance forms as weak convergence of
  normalized partial-sum distributions to the standard normal distribution. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory iterateTheory realTheory transcTheory;
open topologyTheory real_topologyTheory extrealTheory measureTheory borelTheory;
open lebesgueTheory lebesgue_measureTheory probabilityTheory;

val central_limit_theorem_zero_mean =
  ``!(p : 'a p_space) (X : num -> 'a -> real)
      (mu : real measure) (sigma : real) (S : num -> 'a -> real).
      let std_normal_density =
        \x : real. (1 / sqrt (2 * pi)) * exp (-(x pow 2) / 2)
      in
      let std_normal_measure =
        density_measure lborel (Normal o std_normal_density)
      in
        prob_space p /\
        measure_space (space borel, subsets borel, mu) /\
        (!n. random_variable (X n) p borel) /\
        indep_vars p X (\i. borel) UNIV /\
        (!n. expectation p (Normal o X n) = 0) /\
        0 < sigma /\
        (!n. integrable p (\x. Normal ((X n x) pow 2))) /\
        (!n. variance p (Normal o X n) = Normal (sigma pow 2)) /\
        (!n s. s IN subsets borel ==> distribution p (X n) s = mu s) /\
        (!n x. S n x = SIGMA (\i. X i x) (count n))
        ==>
        !f. f IN bounded_continuous euclidean ==>
            (((\n.
                 integral
                   (space borel, subsets borel,
                    distribution p
                      (\x. S n x / sqrt (&n * sigma pow 2)))
                   (Normal o f)) -->
              integral
                (space borel, subsets borel, std_normal_measure)
                (Normal o f))
             sequentially)``;

val central_limit_theorem =
  ``!(p : 'a p_space) (X : num -> 'a -> real)
      (mu : real measure) (sigma m : real) (S : num -> 'a -> real).
      let std_normal_density =
        \x : real. (1 / sqrt (2 * pi)) * exp (-(x pow 2) / 2)
      in
      let std_normal_measure =
        density_measure lborel (Normal o std_normal_density)
      in
        prob_space p /\
        measure_space (space borel, subsets borel, mu) /\
        (!n. random_variable (X n) p borel) /\
        indep_vars p X (\i. borel) UNIV /\
        (!n. expectation p (Normal o X n) = Normal m) /\
        0 < sigma /\
        (!n. integrable p (\x. Normal ((X n x) pow 2))) /\
        (!n. variance p (Normal o X n) = Normal (sigma pow 2)) /\
        (!n s. s IN subsets borel ==> distribution p (X n) s = mu s)
        ==>
        !f. f IN bounded_continuous euclidean ==>
            (((\n.
                 integral
                   (space borel, subsets borel,
                    distribution p
                      (\x.
                         SIGMA (\i. X i x - m) (count n) /
                         sqrt (&n * sigma pow 2)))
                   (Normal o f)) -->
              integral
                (space borel, subsets borel, std_normal_measure)
                (Normal o f))
             sequentially)``;

title: 047_the_central_limit_theorem
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 047, "The Central
  Limit Theorem". This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  The definitions below are conservative abbreviations over set.mm objects.
  P e. Prob is a probability measure, dom P is its sigma-algebra, and
  rRndVar supplies real-valued random variables.

  HT047Integral is the signed real integral obtained from the nonnegative
  simple-function integral. HT047Independent is the usual finite-event
  factorization definition of independence. HT047Law is the pushforward
  probability law on the Borel real line.

  Weak convergence is expressed through characteristic functions: the
  integrals of cos(t x) and sin(t x) converge for every real t. On Borel
  probability laws on RR this is equivalent to convergence in distribution.
  HT047StandardNormal fixes the target law by the characteristic function
  exp(-t^2/2), written as its real and imaginary parts.

  The two final assertions are respectively the zero-mean theorem in the Lean
  source and its explicitly centered form. The normalized sum contains the
  first n variables, indexed by 0 ..^ n, and n ranges over positive integers
  in the convergent law sequence. Every statement is an unproved $a
  assertion; this database contains no $p proof statements.
$)

$c HT047Simple HT047SimpleIntegral HT047NnIntegral $.
$c HT047L1 HT047Integral HT047Expectation HT047Variance $.
$c HT047SquareIntegrable HT047Law HT047RealLaw HT047Independent $.
$c HT047Normalized HT047StandardNormal HT047WeakConverges $.

ht047-simple-syntax $a wff ( HT047Simple P G ) $.
ht047-simple-integral-syntax $a class ( HT047SimpleIntegral P G ) $.
ht047-nn-integral-syntax $a class ( HT047NnIntegral P H ) $.
ht047-l1-syntax $a class ( HT047L1 P ) $.
ht047-integral-syntax $a class ( HT047Integral P ) $.
ht047-expectation-syntax $a class ( HT047Expectation P H ) $.
ht047-variance-syntax $a class ( HT047Variance P H ) $.
ht047-square-integrable-syntax $a wff ( HT047SquareIntegrable P H ) $.
ht047-law-syntax $a class ( HT047Law P H ) $.
ht047-real-law-syntax $a wff ( HT047RealLaw M ) $.
ht047-independent-syntax $a wff ( HT047Independent P X ) $.
ht047-normalized-syntax $a class ( HT047Normalized P X M S N ) $.
ht047-standard-normal-syntax $a wff ( HT047StandardNormal M ) $.
ht047-weak-converges-syntax $a wff ( HT047WeakConverges L M ) $.

${
  $d G P x $.

  ht047-simple-definition $a |- (
    ( HT047Simple P G )
    <->
    (
      G e. ( dom P MblFnM BrSiga )
      /\
      (
        G : U. dom P --> RR
        /\
        (
          ran G e. Fin
          /\
          A. x e. U. dom P 0 <_ ( G ` x )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d G P y $.

  ht047-simple-integral-definition $a |- (
    HT047SimpleIntegral P G
    =
    sum_ y e. ( ran G \ { 0 } )
      ( y x. ( P ` ( `' G " { y } ) ) )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d H P g r x $.

  ht047-nn-integral-definition $a |- (
    HT047NnIntegral P H
    =
    sup
    (
      { r e. RR |
        E. g
          (
            ( HT047Simple P g )
            /\
            (
              A. x e. U. dom P ( g ` x ) <_ ( H ` x )
              /\
              r = ( HT047SimpleIntegral P g )
            )
          )
      } ,
      RR* ,
      <
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d P h x $.

  ht047-l1-definition $a |- (
    HT047L1 P
    =
    { h e. ( rRndVar ` P ) |
      ( HT047NnIntegral P
        ( x e. U. dom P |-> ( abs ` ( h ` x ) ) )
      ) e. RR
    }
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d H P x $.

  ht047-integral-definition $a |- (
    HT047Integral P
    =
    ( H e. ( HT047L1 P ) |->
      (
        ( HT047NnIntegral P
          ( x e. U. dom P |->
            if ( 0 <_ ( H ` x ) , ( H ` x ) , 0 ) )
        )
        -
        ( HT047NnIntegral P
          ( x e. U. dom P |->
            if ( ( H ` x ) < 0 , -u ( H ` x ) , 0 ) )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

ht047-expectation-definition $a |- (
  HT047Expectation P H
  =
  ( ( HT047Integral P ) ` H )
) $.

${
  $d H P x $.

  ht047-variance-definition $a |- (
    HT047Variance P H
    =
    (
      ( HT047Integral P )
      `
      ( x e. U. dom P |->
        ( ( ( H ` x ) - ( HT047Expectation P H ) ) ^ 2 )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d H P x $.

  ht047-square-integrable-definition $a |- (
    ( HT047SquareIntegrable P H )
    <->
    (
      H e. ( HT047L1 P )
      /\
      ( x e. U. dom P |-> ( ( H ` x ) ^ 2 ) )
        e. ( HT047L1 P )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d H P a $.

  ht047-law-definition $a |- (
    HT047Law P H
    =
    ( a e. BrSiga |-> ( P ` ( `' H " a ) ) )
  ) $.
$}

ht047-real-law-definition $a |- (
  ( HT047RealLaw M )
  <->
  ( M e. Prob /\ dom M = BrSiga )
) $.

${
  $d P X b i s $.

  ht047-independent-definition $a |- (
    ( HT047Independent P X )
    <->
    (
      X : NN0 --> ( rRndVar ` P )
      /\
      A. s e. Fin
        (
          ( s C_ NN0 /\ s =/= (/) )
          ->
          A. b
            (
              b : s --> BrSiga
              ->
              (
                P
                `
                |^|_ i e. s
                  ( `' ( X ` i ) " ( b ` i ) )
              )
              =
              prod_ i e. s
                ( P ` ( `' ( X ` i ) " ( b ` i ) ) )
            )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d M N P S X i x $.

  ht047-normalized-definition $a |- (
    HT047Normalized P X M S N
    =
    ( x e. U. dom P |->
      (
        sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ N )
          ( ( ( X ` i ) ` x ) - M )
      )
      /
      ( sqrt ` ( N x. ( S ^ 2 ) ) )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d M t x $.

  ht047-standard-normal-definition $a |- (
    ( HT047StandardNormal M )
    <->
    (
      ( HT047RealLaw M )
      /\
      A. t e. RR
        (
          (
            ( HT047Integral M )
            `
            ( x e. RR |-> ( cos ` ( t x. x ) ) )
          )
          =
          ( exp ` ( -u ( ( t ^ 2 ) / 2 ) ) )
          /\
          (
            ( HT047Integral M )
            `
            ( x e. RR |-> ( sin ` ( t x. x ) ) )
          )
          =
          0
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d L M e k n q t x $.

  ht047-weak-converges-definition $a |- (
    ( HT047WeakConverges L M )
    <->
    (
      (
        L : NN --> { q e. Prob | dom q = BrSiga }
        /\
        ( HT047RealLaw M )
      )
      /\
      A. t e. RR A. e e. RR+
        E. k e. NN A. n e. ( ZZ>= ` k )
          (
            (
              abs
              `
              (
                (
                  ( HT047Integral ( L ` n ) )
                  `
                  ( x e. RR |-> ( cos ` ( t x. x ) ) )
                )
                -
                (
                  ( HT047Integral M )
                  `
                  ( x e. RR |-> ( cos ` ( t x. x ) ) )
                )
              )
            )
            <
            e
            /\
            (
              abs
              `
              (
                (
                  ( HT047Integral ( L ` n ) )
                  `
                  ( x e. RR |-> ( sin ` ( t x. x ) ) )
                )
                -
                (
                  ( HT047Integral M )
                  `
                  ( x e. RR |-> ( sin ` ( t x. x ) ) )
                )
              )
            )
            <
            e
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d D P R X i n u $.

  hundred-theorems-047-central-limit-theorem-zero-mean $a |- (
    (
      (
        P e. Prob
        /\
        ( HT047RealLaw D )
      )
      /\
      (
        ( HT047Independent P X )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. NN0 ( HT047Expectation P ( X ` i ) ) = 0
          /\
          (
            0 < R
            /\
            (
              A. i e. NN0
                ( HT047SquareIntegrable P ( X ` i ) )
              /\
              (
                A. i e. NN0
                  ( HT047Variance P ( X ` i ) ) = ( R ^ 2 )
                /\
                A. i e. NN0
                  ( HT047Law P ( X ` i ) ) = D
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
    ->
    E. u
      (
        ( HT047StandardNormal u )
        /\
        (
          HT047WeakConverges
          ( n e. NN |->
            ( HT047Law P
              ( HT047Normalized P X 0 R n )
            )
          )
          u
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d D M P R X i n u $.

  hundred-theorems-047-central-limit-theorem $a |- (
    (
      (
        (
          P e. Prob
          /\
          ( HT047RealLaw D )
        )
        /\
        M e. RR
      )
      /\
      (
        ( HT047Independent P X )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. NN0 ( HT047Expectation P ( X ` i ) ) = M
          /\
          (
            0 < R
            /\
            (
              A. i e. NN0
                ( HT047SquareIntegrable P ( X ` i ) )
              /\
              (
                A. i e. NN0
                  ( HT047Variance P ( X ` i ) ) = ( R ^ 2 )
                /\
                A. i e. NN0
                  ( HT047Law P ( X ` i ) ) = D
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
    ->
    E. u
      (
        ( HT047StandardNormal u )
        /\
        (
          HT047WeakConverges
          ( n e. NN |->
            ( HT047Law P
              ( HT047Normalized P X M R n )
            )
          )
          u
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

title: 047_the_central_limit_theorem
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact 047, "The Central Limit
:: Theorem": identically distributed independent real random variables with positive
:: variance have normalized centered partial sums converging in distribution to the
:: standard normal law. This file contains no proof.

environ

 vocabularies NUMBERS, XBOOLE_0, PROB_1, MEASURE1, PARTFUN1, SUBSET_1,
      TARSKI, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, ARYTM_3, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, FUNCT_2,
      VALUED_0, MESFUNC1, SUPINF_2, FINSEQ_1, NAT_1, CARD_3, CARD_1,
      ZFMISC_1, FINSET_1, PROB_4, RANDOM_1, RANDOM_2, RANDOM_3, FUNCOP_1,
      FINANCE1, REAL_1, SETFAM_1, SEQ_2, SQUARE_1, POWER, MEASUR12,
      SIN_COS, COMPLEX1, RVSUM_1, MESFUNC5, INTEGRA5, XCMPLX_0, ARYTM_1,
      VALUED_1;
 notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, SETFAM_1, RELAT_1,
      FUNCT_1, ORDINAL1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, FUNCOP_1, FINSET_1,
      CARD_1, NUMBERS, XXREAL_3, XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, NAT_1,
      XREAL_0, VALUED_0, FINSEQ_1, SUPINF_2, PROB_1, PROB_2, MEASURE1,
      MEASURE6, MESFUNC1, PROB_4, MESFUNC6, MESFUNC5, RANDOM_1, RANDOM_2,
      RANDOM_3, FINANCE1, REAL_1, SQUARE_1, POWER, RVSUM_1, MEASUR12,
      SIN_COS, COMPLEX1, VALUED_1, MESFUN6C;
 constructors REAL_1, MESFUNC6, MEASURE6, PROB_3, PROB_4, MESFUNC1,
      MESFUNC5, RELSET_1, COMSEQ_2, RANDOM_1, RANDOM_2, RANDOM_3, FINANCE1,
      RVSUM_1, MEASUR12, SIN_COS, SQUARE_1, POWER, SETFAM_1, MESFUN6C,
      COMPLEX1;
 registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, NAT_1, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, ORDINAL1,
      MEASURE1, FUNCOP_1, FINANCE1, VALUED_0, FINSEQ_1, FUNCT_2, RELAT_1,
      FINSET_1, NUMBERS, PROB_1, PARTFUN1, RELSET_1, CARD_1, MEMBERED,
      SQUARE_1, XXREAL_3, RANDOM_2, RANDOM_3, MEASUR12, MESFUN6C;
 requirements NUMERALS, BOOLE, SUBSET, ARITHM, REAL;
 definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, FINSET_1;
 equalities PROB_1, RANDOM_2, PROB_4, RELAT_1, FINSEQ_1, SQUARE_1;
 expansions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1, FINSEQ_1;

begin

:: Zero-mean iid central limit theorem
::$P-
theorem
  for Omega being non empty set,
      Sigma being SigmaField of Omega,
      P being Probability of Sigma,
      mu,Normal being Probability of Borel_Sets,
      X,S,Z being Function of NAT,Funcs(Omega,REAL),
      g being Function of REAL,REAL,
      stdev being Real
  st
    X is Sigma-Random-Variable-Family &
    S is Sigma-Random-Variable-Family &
    Z is Sigma-Random-Variable-Family &
    0 < stdev &
    g is_integrable_on B-Meas &
    (for x being Real holds
      g.x = exp_R.(-(x^2)/2) / sqrt(2*PI)) &
    (for A being Element of Borel_Sets holds
      Normal.A = Integral(B-Meas,g|A)) &
    (for n being Nat,
         Xn being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma,
         FXn being random_variable of Sigma,Borel_Sets
      st Xn = X.n & FXn = Xn
      holds
        Xn is_integrable_on P &
        (abs(Xn) to_power 2) is_integrable_on P2M(P) &
        expect(Xn,P) = 0 &
        variance(Xn,P) = stdev^2 &
        probability(FXn,P) = mu) &
    (for k being Nat,
         I being one-to-one FinSequence of NAT,
         B being FinSequence of Borel_Sets,
         E being FinSequence of Sigma,
         q being FinSequence of REAL
      st 0 < k &
         len I = k & len B = k & len E = k & len q = k &
         (for j being Nat st j in Seg k holds
           E.j = (X.(I.j))"(B.j) &
           q.j = (P.(E.j) qua Real))
      holds P.(meet rng E) = Product q) &
    (for n being Nat,
         x being Element of Omega,
         a being FinSequence of REAL
      st len a = n &
         (for j being Nat st j in dom a holds
           a.j = (X.(j-'1)).x)
      holds S.n.x = Sum a) &
    (for n being Nat,
         x being Element of Omega,
         Zn,Sn being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma
      st Zn = Z.n & Sn = S.n
      holds Zn.x = Sn.x / sqrt((n qua Real)*stdev^2))
  holds
    for t being Real,
        A being Element of Borel_Sets
      st A = ].-infty,t.]
    holds
      for e being positive Real
      ex N being Nat
      st for n being Nat,
             Zn being random_variable of Sigma,Borel_Sets
           st N <= n & Zn = Z.n
         holds
           |.(((probability(Zn,P)).A qua Real) -
             (Normal.A qua Real) qua Complex).| < e
proof
end;
::$P+

:: General iid central limit theorem after centering by the common mean
::$P-
theorem
  for Omega being non empty set,
      Sigma being SigmaField of Omega,
      P being Probability of Sigma,
      mu,Normal being Probability of Borel_Sets,
      X,Y,S,Z being Function of NAT,Funcs(Omega,REAL),
      g being Function of REAL,REAL,
      m,stdev being Real
  st
    X is Sigma-Random-Variable-Family &
    Y is Sigma-Random-Variable-Family &
    S is Sigma-Random-Variable-Family &
    Z is Sigma-Random-Variable-Family &
    0 < stdev &
    g is_integrable_on B-Meas &
    (for x being Real holds
      g.x = exp_R.(-(x^2)/2) / sqrt(2*PI)) &
    (for A being Element of Borel_Sets holds
      Normal.A = Integral(B-Meas,g|A)) &
    (for n being Nat,
         Xn being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma,
         FXn being random_variable of Sigma,Borel_Sets
      st Xn = X.n & FXn = Xn
      holds
        Xn is_integrable_on P &
        (abs(Xn) to_power 2) is_integrable_on P2M(P) &
        expect(Xn,P) = m &
        variance(Xn,P) = stdev^2 &
        probability(FXn,P) = mu) &
    (for k being Nat,
         I being one-to-one FinSequence of NAT,
         B being FinSequence of Borel_Sets,
         E being FinSequence of Sigma,
         q being FinSequence of REAL
      st 0 < k &
         len I = k & len B = k & len E = k & len q = k &
         (for j being Nat st j in Seg k holds
           E.j = (X.(I.j))"(B.j) &
           q.j = (P.(E.j) qua Real))
      holds P.(meet rng E) = Product q) &
    (for n being Nat,
         x being Element of Omega,
         Yn,Xn being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma
      st Yn = Y.n & Xn = X.n
      holds Yn.x = Xn.x - m) &
    (for n being Nat,
         x being Element of Omega,
         a being FinSequence of REAL
      st len a = n &
         (for j being Nat st j in dom a holds
           a.j = (Y.(j-'1)).x)
      holds S.n.x = Sum a) &
    (for n being Nat,
         x being Element of Omega,
         Zn,Sn being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma
      st Zn = Z.n & Sn = S.n
      holds Zn.x = Sn.x / sqrt((n qua Real)*stdev^2))
  holds
    for t being Real,
        A being Element of Borel_Sets
      st A = ].-infty,t.]
    holds
      for e being positive Real
      ex N being Nat
      st for n being Nat,
             Zn being random_variable of Sigma,Borel_Sets
           st N <= n & Zn = Z.n
         holds
           |.(((probability(Zn,P)).A qua Real) -
             (Normal.A qua Real) qua Complex).| < e
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 047_the_central_limit_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 047, "The Central
% Limit Theorem." Independent identically distributed real random variables
% with finite positive variance have centered normalized sums converging in
% distribution to the standard normal law. Convergence is stated through
% characteristic functions, using Levy's equivalent criterion. This file
% contains no proof.

the_central_limit_theorem_047: THEORY
BEGIN
  sample_space: TYPE+

  event: TYPE = [sample_space -> bool]
  event_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> event]
  sigma_algebra: TYPE = [event -> bool]
  probability_measure: TYPE = [event -> real]
  random_variable: TYPE = [sample_space -> real]
  random_variable_family: TYPE = [nat -> random_variable]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  index_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  absolute_value(x: real): real =
    IF 0 <= x THEN x ELSE -x ENDIF

  full_event: event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space): TRUE

  empty_event: event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space): FALSE

  event_complement(A: event): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space): NOT A(omega)

  countable_union(events: event_sequence): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      EXISTS (index: nat): events(index)(omega)

  pairwise_disjoint(events: event_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index /= right_index IMPLIES
        FORALL (omega: sample_space):
          NOT (events(left_index)(omega)
            AND events(right_index)(omega))

  pairwise_disjoint_below(
      events: event_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index < count
        AND right_index < count
        AND left_index /= right_index
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (omega: sample_space):
          NOT (events(left_index)(omega)
            AND events(right_index)(omega))

  finite_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat):
      RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_sum(values, count - 1)
        + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  finite_product(values: real_sequence, count: nat):
      RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      finite_product(values, count - 1)
        * values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to_real(
      values: real_sequence,
      limit: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            absolute_value(values(index) - limit)
              < epsilon_value

  is_sigma_algebra(Sigma: sigma_algebra): bool =
    Sigma(full_event)
      AND (FORALL (A: event):
        Sigma(A) IMPLIES Sigma(event_complement(A)))
      AND (FORALL (events: event_sequence):
        (FORALL (index: nat): Sigma(events(index)))
          IMPLIES Sigma(countable_union(events)))

  is_probability_measure(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra): bool =
    is_sigma_algebra(Sigma)
      AND M(empty_event) = 0
      AND M(full_event) = 1
      AND (FORALL (A: event):
        Sigma(A) IMPLIES
          0 <= M(A) AND M(A) <= 1)
      AND (FORALL (events: event_sequence):
        ((FORALL (index: nat): Sigma(events(index)))
          AND pairwise_disjoint(events))
        IMPLIES
          converges_to_real(
            LAMBDA (count: nat):
              finite_sum(
                LAMBDA (index: nat):
                  M(events(index)),
                count),
            M(countable_union(events))))

  sublevel_event(
      X: random_variable,
      bound: real): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      X(omega) <= bound

  random_variable_on(
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable): bool =
    FORALL (bound: real):
      Sigma(sublevel_event(X, bound))

  positive_part(X: random_variable): random_variable =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      IF 0 <= X(omega) THEN X(omega) ELSE 0 ENDIF

  negative_part(X: random_variable): random_variable =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      IF X(omega) <= 0 THEN -X(omega) ELSE 0 ENDIF

  simple_value(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: event_sequence,
      count: nat,
      omega: sample_space): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      simple_value(
        coefficients, pieces, count - 1, omega)
        + IF pieces(count - 1)(omega) THEN
            coefficients(count - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  simple_integral(
      M: probability_measure,
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: event_sequence,
      count: nat): real =
    finite_sum(
      LAMBDA (index: nat):
        coefficients(index) * M(pieces(index)),
      count)

  nonnegative_simple_minorant(
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable,
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: event_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    pairwise_disjoint_below(pieces, count)
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          0 <= coefficients(index)
            AND Sigma(pieces(index)))
      AND (FORALL (omega: sample_space):
        0 <= simple_value(
          coefficients, pieces, count, omega)
          AND simple_value(
            coefficients, pieces, count, omega)
            <= X(omega))

  nonnegative_integral_upper_bound(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable,
      upper: real): bool =
    FORALL
        (coefficients: real_sequence),
        (pieces: event_sequence),
        (count: nat):
      nonnegative_simple_minorant(
        Sigma, X, coefficients, pieces, count)
      IMPLIES
        simple_integral(
          M, coefficients, pieces, count) <= upper

  has_nonnegative_integral(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable,
      value: real): bool =
    (FORALL (omega: sample_space): 0 <= X(omega))
      AND 0 <= value
      AND nonnegative_integral_upper_bound(
        M, Sigma, X, value)
      AND (FORALL (upper: real):
        nonnegative_integral_upper_bound(
          M, Sigma, X, upper)
        IMPLIES value <= upper)

  has_expectation(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable,
      value: real): bool =
    random_variable_on(Sigma, X)
      AND EXISTS
          (positive_integral, negative_integral: real):
        has_nonnegative_integral(
          M, Sigma, positive_part(X), positive_integral)
          AND has_nonnegative_integral(
            M, Sigma, negative_part(X), negative_integral)
          AND value =
            positive_integral - negative_integral

  integrable(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable): bool =
    EXISTS (value: real):
      has_expectation(M, Sigma, X, value)

  square_integrable(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable): bool =
    integrable(
      M,
      Sigma,
      LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
        X(omega) * X(omega))

  has_variance(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable,
      mean, variance_value: real): bool =
    has_expectation(M, Sigma, X, mean)
      AND has_expectation(
        M,
        Sigma,
        LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
          (X(omega) - mean) * (X(omega) - mean),
        variance_value)

  all_distinct_below(
      indices: index_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index < count
        AND right_index < count
        AND left_index /= right_index
      IMPLIES
        indices(left_index) /= indices(right_index)

  threshold_intersection_holds(
      X: random_variable_family,
      indices: index_sequence,
      thresholds: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      omega: sample_space): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSE
      threshold_intersection_holds(
        X, indices, thresholds, count - 1, omega)
        AND X(indices(count - 1))(omega)
          <= thresholds(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  threshold_intersection(
      X: random_variable_family,
      indices: index_sequence,
      thresholds: real_sequence,
      count: nat): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      threshold_intersection_holds(
        X, indices, thresholds, count, omega)

  independent_random_variables(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable_family): bool =
    (FORALL (index: nat):
      random_variable_on(Sigma, X(index)))
      AND (FORALL
          (indices: index_sequence),
          (thresholds: real_sequence),
          (count: nat):
        all_distinct_below(indices, count)
        IMPLIES
          Sigma(
            threshold_intersection(
              X, indices, thresholds, count))
            AND M(
              threshold_intersection(
                X, indices, thresholds, count))
              = finite_product(
                  LAMBDA (position: nat):
                    M(
                      sublevel_event(
                        X(indices(position)),
                        thresholds(position))),
                  count))

  identically_distributed(
      M: probability_measure,
      X: random_variable_family): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat), (threshold: real):
      M(sublevel_event(X(index), threshold))
        = M(sublevel_event(X(0), threshold))

  centered_partial_sum(
      X: random_variable_family,
      mean: real,
      count: nat,
      omega: sample_space): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      centered_partial_sum(
        X, mean, count - 1, omega)
        + X(count - 1)(omega) - mean
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  normalized_centered_sum(
      X: random_variable_family,
      mean: real,
      count: nat,
      denominator: real): random_variable =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      safe_div(
        centered_partial_sum(X, mean, count, omega),
        denominator)

  sqrt_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    0 <= radicand
      AND 0 <= root
      AND root * root = radicand

  normalizing_sequence(
      denominators: real_sequence,
      sigma: real): bool =
    FORALL (count: nat):
      sqrt_value(
        denominators(count),
        (count :: real) * (sigma * sigma))

  factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial_sum(
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial_sum(x, count - 1)
          + x ^ index / (factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  sine_partial_sum(
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        sine_partial_sum(x, count - 1)
          + alternating_sign(index)
            * x ^ (2 * index + 1)
            / (factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  cosine_partial_sum(
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial_sum(x, count - 1)
          + alternating_sign(index)
            * x ^ (2 * index)
            / (factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  standard_real_analytic_functions(
      sine_function,
      cosine_function,
      exponential_function: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      converges_to_real(
        LAMBDA (count: nat):
          sine_partial_sum(x, count),
        sine_function(x))
        AND converges_to_real(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            cosine_partial_sum(x, count),
          cosine_function(x))
        AND converges_to_real(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial_sum(x, count),
          exponential_function(x))

  converges_to_standard_normal(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      Y: random_variable_family): bool =
    (FORALL (count: nat):
      random_variable_on(Sigma, Y(count)))
      AND EXISTS
          (sine_function,
           cosine_function,
           exponential_function: real_function):
        standard_real_analytic_functions(
          sine_function,
          cosine_function,
          exponential_function)
          AND (FORALL (frequency: real):
            EXISTS
                (real_parts,
                 imaginary_parts: real_sequence):
              (FORALL (count: nat):
                has_expectation(
                  M,
                  Sigma,
                  LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
                    cosine_function(
                      frequency * Y(count)(omega)),
                  real_parts(count))
                  AND has_expectation(
                    M,
                    Sigma,
                    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
                      sine_function(
                        frequency * Y(count)(omega)),
                    imaginary_parts(count)))
                AND converges_to_real(
                  real_parts,
                  exponential_function(
                    -(frequency * frequency) / 2))
                AND converges_to_real(
                  imaginary_parts,
                  0))

  central_limit_hypotheses(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable_family,
      sigma, mean: real): bool =
    is_probability_measure(M, Sigma)
      AND independent_random_variables(M, Sigma, X)
      AND identically_distributed(M, X)
      AND 0 < sigma
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        has_expectation(
          M, Sigma, X(index), mean))
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        square_integrable(M, Sigma, X(index)))
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        has_variance(
          M,
          Sigma,
          X(index),
          mean,
          sigma * sigma))

  central_limit_conclusion(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_variable_family,
      sigma, mean: real): bool =
    EXISTS (denominators: real_sequence):
      normalizing_sequence(denominators, sigma)
        AND converges_to_standard_normal(
          M,
          Sigma,
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            normalized_centered_sum(
              X,
              mean,
              count,
              denominators(count)))

  central_limit_theorem_zero_mean: bool =
    FORALL
        (M: probability_measure),
        (Sigma: sigma_algebra),
        (X: random_variable_family),
        (sigma: real):
      central_limit_hypotheses(
        M, Sigma, X, sigma, 0)
      IMPLIES
        central_limit_conclusion(
          M, Sigma, X, sigma, 0)

  central_limit_theorem: bool =
    FORALL
        (M: probability_measure),
        (Sigma: sigma_algebra),
        (X: random_variable_family),
        (sigma, mean: real):
      central_limit_hypotheses(
        M, Sigma, X, sigma, mean)
      IMPLIES
        central_limit_conclusion(
          M, Sigma, X, sigma, mean)
END the_central_limit_theorem_047

title: 048_dirichlet_s_theorem
content:

module

public import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Coprime
public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.DirichletCharacter.Orthogonality
public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.Linearity
public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.Nonvanishing

/-!
# Dirichlet's Theorem on primes in arithmetic progression

The goal of this file is to prove **Dirichlet's Theorem**: If `q` is a positive natural number
and `a : ZMod q` is invertible, then there are infinitely many prime numbers `p` such that
`(p : ZMod q) = a`.

The main steps of the proof are as follows.
1. Define `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.residueClass a` for `a : ZMod q`, which is
   a function `ℕ → ℝ` taking the value zero when `(n : ZMod q) ≠ a` and `Λ n` else
   (where `Λ` is the von Mangoldt function `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt`; we have
   `Λ (p^k) = log p` for prime powers and `Λ n = 0` otherwise.)
2. Show that this function can be written as a linear combination of functions
   of the form `χ * Λ` (pointwise product) with Dirichlet characters `χ` mod `q`.
   See `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.residueClass_eq`.
3. This implies that the L-series of `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.residueClass a`
   agrees (on `re s > 1`) with the corresponding linear combination of negative logarithmic
   derivatives of Dirichlet L-functions.
   See `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.LSeries_residueClass_eq`.
4. Define an auxiliary function `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.LFunctionResidueClassAux a` that is
   this linear combination of negative logarithmic derivatives of L-functions minus
   `(q.totient)⁻¹/(s-1)`, which cancels the pole at `s = 1`.
   See `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.eqOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux` for the statement
   that the auxiliary function agrees with the L-series of
   `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.residueClass` up to the term `(q.totient)⁻¹/(s-1)`.
5. Show that the auxiliary function is continuous on `re s ≥ 1`;
   see `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.continuousOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux`.
   This relies heavily on the non-vanishing of Dirichlet L-functions on the *closed*
   half-plane `re s ≥ 1` (`DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_one_le_re`), which
   in turn can only be stated since we know that the L-series of a Dirichlet character
   extends to an entire function (unless the character is trivial; then there is a
   simple pole at `s = 1`); see `DirichletCharacter.LFunction_eq_LSeries`
   (contributed by David Loeffler).
6. Show that the sum of `Λ n / n` over any residue class, but *excluding* the primes, converges.
   See `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.summable_residueClass_non_primes_div`.
7. Combining these ingredients, we can deduce that the sum of `Λ n / n` over
   the *primes* in a residue class must diverge.
   See `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.not_summable_residueClass_prime_div`.
8. This finally easily implies that there must be infinitely many primes in the residue class.

## Definitions

* `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.residueClass a` (see above).
* `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.continuousOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux` (see above).

## Main Result

We give two versions of **Dirichlet's Theorem**:
* `Nat.infinite_setOf_prime_and_eq_mod` states that the set of primes `p`
  such that `(p : ZMod q) = a` is infinite (when `a` is invertible in `ZMod q`).
* `Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod` states that for any natural number `n`
  there is a prime `p > n` such that `(p : ZMod q) = a`.

## Tags

prime number, arithmetic progression, residue class, Dirichlet's Theorem
-/

@[expose] public section

/-!
### Auxiliary statements

An infinite product or sum over a function supported in prime powers can be written
as an iterated product or sum over primes and natural numbers.
-/

section auxiliary

variable {α β γ : Type*} [CommGroup α] [UniformSpace α] [IsUniformGroup α] [CompleteSpace α]
  [T0Space α]

open Nat.Primes in
@[to_additive tsum_eq_tsum_primes_of_support_subset_prime_powers]
lemma tprod_eq_tprod_primes_of_mulSupport_subset_prime_powers {f : ℕ → α}
    (hfm : Multipliable f) (hf : Function.mulSupport f ⊆ {n | IsPrimePow n}) :
    ∏' n : ℕ, f n = ∏' (p : Nat.Primes) (k : ℕ), f (p ^ (k + 1)) := by sorry
lemma tprod_eq_tprod_primes_mul_tprod_primes_of_mulSupport_subset_prime_powers {f : ℕ → α}
    (hfm : Multipliable f) (hf : Function.mulSupport f ⊆ {n | IsPrimePow n}) :
    ∏' n : ℕ, f n = (∏' p : Nat.Primes, f p) * ∏' (p : Nat.Primes) (k : ℕ), f (p ^ (k + 2)) := by sorry
end auxiliary

/-!
### The L-series of the von Mangoldt function restricted to a residue class
-/

section arith_prog

namespace ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt

open Complex LSeries DirichletCharacter

open scoped LSeries.notation

variable {q : ℕ} (a : ZMod q)

/-- The von Mangoldt function restricted to the residue class `a` mod `q`. -/
noncomputable abbrev residueClass : ℕ → ℝ :=
  {n : ℕ | (n : ZMod q) = a}.indicator (vonMangoldt ·)

lemma residueClass_nonneg (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ residueClass a n :=
  Set.indicator_apply_nonneg fun _ ↦ vonMangoldt_nonneg

lemma residueClass_le (n : ℕ) : residueClass a n ≤ vonMangoldt n :=
  Set.indicator_apply_le' (fun _ ↦ le_rfl) (fun _ ↦ vonMangoldt_nonneg)

@[simp]
lemma residueClass_apply_zero : residueClass a 0 = 0 := by sorry
lemma abscissaOfAbsConv_residueClass_le_one :
    abscissaOfAbsConv ↗(residueClass a) ≤ 1 := by sorry
lemma support_residueClass_prime_div :
    Function.support (fun n : ℕ ↦ (if n.Prime then residueClass a n else 0) / n) =
      {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ (p : ZMod q) = a} := by sorry
open Nat.Primes

private lemma summable_F'' : Summable F'' := by sorry
lemma summable_residueClass_non_primes_div :
    Summable fun n : ℕ ↦ (if n.Prime then 0 else residueClass a n) / n := by sorry
variable [NeZero q] {a}

/-- We can express `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.residueClass` as a linear combination
of twists of the von Mangoldt function by Dirichlet characters. -/
lemma residueClass_apply (ha : IsUnit a) (n : ℕ) :
    residueClass a n =
      (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ a⁻¹ * χ n * vonMangoldt n := by sorry
lemma residueClass_eq (ha : IsUnit a) :
    ↗(residueClass a) = (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ •
      ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ a⁻¹ • (fun n : ℕ ↦ χ n * vonMangoldt n) := by sorry
lemma LSeries_residueClass_eq (ha : IsUnit a) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    LSeries ↗(residueClass a) s =
      -(q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∑ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ a⁻¹ *
        (deriv (LFunction χ) s / LFunction χ s) := by sorry
variable (a)

open Classical in
/-- The auxiliary function used, e.g., with the Wiener-Ikehara Theorem to prove
Dirichlet's Theorem. On `re s > 1`, it agrees with the L-series of the von Mangoldt
function restricted to the residue class `a : ZMod q` minus the principal part
`(q.totient)⁻¹/(s-1)` of the pole at `s = 1`;
see `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.eqOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux`. -/
noncomputable
abbrev LFunctionResidueClassAux (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ * (-deriv (LFunctionTrivChar₁ q) s / LFunctionTrivChar₁ q s -
    ∑ χ ∈ ({1}ᶜ : Finset (DirichletCharacter ℂ q)), χ a⁻¹ * deriv (LFunction χ) s / LFunction χ s)

/-- The auxiliary function is continuous away from the zeros of the L-functions of the Dirichlet
characters mod `q` (including at `s = 1`). -/
lemma continuousOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux' :
    ContinuousOn (LFunctionResidueClassAux a)
      {s | s = 1 ∨ ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, LFunction χ s ≠ 0} := by sorry
lemma continuousOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux :
    ContinuousOn (LFunctionResidueClassAux a) {s | 1 ≤ s.re} := by sorry
variable {a}

open scoped LSeries.notation

/-- The auxiliary function agrees on `re s > 1` with the L-series of the von Mangoldt function
restricted to the residue class `a : ZMod q` minus the principal part `(q.totient)⁻¹/(s-1)`
of its pole at `s = 1`. -/
lemma eqOn_LFunctionResidueClassAux (ha : IsUnit a) :
    Set.EqOn (LFunctionResidueClassAux a)
      (fun s ↦ L ↗(residueClass a) s - (q.totient : ℂ)⁻¹ / (s - 1))
      {s | 1 < s.re} := by sorry
lemma LFunctionResidueClassAux_real (ha : IsUnit a) {x : ℝ} (hx : 1 < x) :
    LFunctionResidueClassAux a x = (LFunctionResidueClassAux a x).re := by sorry
variable {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] {a : ZMod q}

/-- As `x` approaches `1` from the right along the real axis, the L-series of
`ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt.residueClass` is bounded below by `(q.totient)⁻¹/(x-1) - C`. -/
lemma LSeries_residueClass_lower_bound (ha : IsUnit a) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ {x : ℝ} (_ : x ∈ Set.Ioc 1 2),
      (q.totient : ℝ)⁻¹ / (x - 1) - C ≤ ∑' n, residueClass a n / (n : ℝ) ^ x := by sorry
open vonMangoldt Filter Topology in
/-- The function `n ↦ Λ n / n` restricted to primes in an invertible residue class
is not summable. This then implies that there must be infinitely many such primes. -/
lemma not_summable_residueClass_prime_div (ha : IsUnit a) :
    ¬ Summable fun n : ℕ ↦ (if n.Prime then residueClass a n else 0) / n := by sorry
end ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt

end arith_prog

/-!
### Dirichlet's Theorem
-/

section DirichletsTheorem

namespace Nat

open ArithmeticFunction vonMangoldt

variable {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] {a : ZMod q}

/-- **Dirichlet's Theorem** on primes in arithmetic progression: if `q` is a positive
integer and `a : ZMod q` is a unit, then there are infinitely many prime numbers `p`
such that `(p : ZMod q) = a`. -/
theorem infinite_setOf_prime_and_eq_mod (ha : IsUnit a) :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ (p : ZMod q) = a}.Infinite := by sorry
theorem forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod (ha : IsUnit a) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ (p : ZMod q) = a := by sorry
theorem forall_exists_prime_gt_and_zmodEq (n : ℕ) {q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (h : IsCoprime a q) :
    ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ a [ZMOD q] := by sorry
theorem forall_exists_prime_gt_and_modEq (n : ℕ) {q a : ℕ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (h : a.Coprime q) :
    ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ a [MOD q] := by sorry
open Filter in
lemma frequently_atTop_prime_and_modEq {q a : ℕ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (h : a.Coprime q) :
    ∃ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ a [MOD q] := by sorry
lemma infinite_setOf_prime_and_modEq {q a : ℕ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (h : a.Coprime q) :
    Set.Infinite {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ≡ a [MOD q]} :=
  frequently_atTop_iff_infinite.1 (frequently_atTop_prime_and_modEq hq h)

end Nat

end DirichletsTheorem

title: 048_dirichlet_s_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 048, "Dirichlet's Theorem".
  Every residue class coprime to a positive natural modulus contains arbitrarily large natural
  prime numbers. This file contains no proof.
*)

From Stdlib Require Import PeanoNat.

Definition is_prime (p : nat) : Prop :=
  2 <= p /\
  forall a b : nat,
    p = a * b ->
    a = 1 \/ b = 1.

Theorem dirichlets_theorem :
  forall d k : nat,
    1 <= d ->
    Nat.gcd k d = 1 ->
    forall n : nat,
      exists p : nat,
        n < p /\
        is_prime p /\
        Nat.modulo p d = Nat.modulo k d.
Admitted.

title: 048_dirichlet_s_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Dirichlet's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 048.
  For every positive natural modulus and coprime residue, infinitely many natural primes are
  congruent to that residue modulo the modulus. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory Dirichlets_Theorem
  imports Complex_Main
begin

definition nat_prime :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "nat_prime p \<longleftrightarrow>
    1 < p \<and> (\<forall>m :: nat. m dvd p \<longrightarrow> m = 1 \<or> m = p)"

theorem dirichlets_theorem:
  fixes d k :: nat
  assumes "1 \<le> d"
    and "coprime k d"
  shows "infinite {p :: nat. nat_prime p \<and> p mod d = k mod d}"
  sorry

end
