content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__048, "Dirichlet's Theorem": for every positive
;; natural modulus and every coprime natural residue, the primes congruent to
;; that residue modulo the modulus are unbounded. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun hundred-theorems-048-no-divisor-from-p (n d)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix (- n d))))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp d)
           (<= 2 d)
           (< d n))
      (and (not (equal (mod n d) 0))
           (hundred-theorems-048-no-divisor-from-p n (+ d 1)))
    t))

(defun hundred-theorems-048-primep (n)
  (and (natp n)
       (< 1 n)
       (hundred-theorems-048-no-divisor-from-p n 2)))

(defun hundred-theorems-048-has-common-divisor-through-p (a b d)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix d)))
  (if (and (natp a)
           (natp b)
           (natp d)
           (<= 2 d))
      (or (and (equal (mod a d) 0)
               (equal (mod b d) 0))
          (hundred-theorems-048-has-common-divisor-through-p
           a b (- d 1)))
    nil))

(defun hundred-theorems-048-coprimep (a b)
  (and (natp a)
       (natp b)
       (not (and (equal a 0)
                 (equal b 0)))
       (not (hundred-theorems-048-has-common-divisor-through-p
             a b (+ a b)))))

(defun hundred-theorems-048-congruent-p (x y modulus)
  (and (natp x)
       (natp y)
       (natp modulus)
       (if (equal modulus 0)
           (equal x y)
         (equal (mod x modulus)
                (mod y modulus)))))

(defun-sk hundred-theorems-048-prime-above-in-class-exists-p
  (bound modulus residue)
  (exists (p)
    (and (natp p)
         (< bound p)
         (hundred-theorems-048-primep p)
         (hundred-theorems-048-congruent-p p residue modulus))))

(defun-sk hundred-theorems-048-dirichlets-theorem-statement ()
  (forall (modulus residue bound)
    (implies
     (and (natp modulus)
          (natp residue)
          (natp bound)
          (< 0 modulus)
          (hundred-theorems-048-coprimep residue modulus))
     (hundred-theorems-048-prime-above-in-class-exists-p
      bound modulus residue))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 048_dirichlet_s_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Dirichlet's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 048:
-- every coprime residue class modulo a positive natural number contains a prime above every
-- natural bound. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; mod-helper)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _∣_
infixr 5 _×_
infixr 3 _∨_

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

record _×_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    left : A
    right : B

record _∣_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : divisor * quotient ≡ dividend

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record Prime (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two : 2 ≤ n
    divisor-is-trivial :
      (d : Nat) →
      d ∣ n →
      d ≡ 1 ∨ d ≡ n

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value : A
    property : P value

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

gcdWithFuel : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat
gcdWithFuel zero a b = a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a zero = a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a (suc b) =
  gcdWithFuel fuel (suc b) (naturalMod a (suc b))

naturalGCD : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalGCD a b =
  gcdWithFuel (suc (a + b)) a b

Coprime : Nat → Nat → Set
Coprime a b = naturalGCD a b ≡ 1

ModEq : Nat → Nat → Nat → Set
ModEq modulus lhs rhs =
  naturalMod lhs modulus ≡ naturalMod rhs modulus

dirichlet-s-theorem : Set
dirichlet-s-theorem =
  (d k : Nat) →
  1 ≤ d →
  Coprime k d →
  (bound : Nat) →
  Exists Nat
    (λ p →
      Prime p ×
      ((bound < p) × ModEq d p k))

title: 048_dirichlet_s_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Dirichlet's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 048:
% every residue class coprime to a positive modulus contains infinitely many primes.
% This file contains no proof.

dirichlet_s_theorem_048: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat): value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  coprime_nat(left, right: nat): bool =
    FORALL (divisor: posnat):
      nat_divides(divisor, left) AND nat_divides(divisor, right)
        IMPLIES divisor = 1

  nat_congruent(left, right, modulus: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (offset: int):
      (left :: int) - (right :: int) = (modulus :: int) * offset

  dirichlet_s_theorem: bool =
    FORALL (modulus, residue: nat):
      (modulus >= 1 AND coprime_nat(residue, modulus))
        IMPLIES
          FORALL (bound: nat):
            EXISTS (p: nat):
              bound < p
                AND prime_nat(p)
                AND nat_congruent(p, residue, modulus)

END dirichlet_s_theorem_048

title: 049_the_cayley-hamilton_theorem
content:
/-

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Eval.SMul
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Adjugate
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Block
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.MatrixPolynomialAlgebra

/-!
# Characteristic polynomials and the Cayley-Hamilton theorem

We define characteristic polynomials of matrices and
prove the Cayley–Hamilton theorem over arbitrary commutative rings.

See the file `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Charpoly/Coeff.lean` for corollaries of this theorem.

## Main definitions

* `Matrix.charpoly` is the characteristic polynomial of a matrix.

## Implementation details

We follow a nice proof from http://drorbn.net/AcademicPensieve/2015-12/CayleyHamilton.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

universe u v w

namespace Matrix

open Finset Matrix Polynomial

variable {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
variable {m n : Type*} [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
variable (M₁₁ : Matrix m m R) (M₁₂ : Matrix m n R) (M₂₁ : Matrix n m R) (M₂₂ M : Matrix n n R)
variable (i j : n)


/-- The "characteristic matrix" of `M : Matrix n n R` is the matrix of polynomials $t I - M$.
The determinant of this matrix is the characteristic polynomial.
-/
def charmatrix (M : Matrix n n R) : Matrix n n R[X] :=
  Matrix.scalar n (X : R[X]) - (C : R →+* R[X]).mapMatrix M

theorem charmatrix_apply :
    charmatrix M i j = (Matrix.diagonal fun _ : n => X) i j - C (M i j) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem charmatrix_apply_eq : charmatrix M i i = (X : R[X]) - C (M i i) := by sorry
theorem charmatrix_apply_ne (h : i ≠ j) : charmatrix M i j = -C (M i j) := by sorry
theorem charmatrix_zero : charmatrix (0 : Matrix n n R) = Matrix.scalar n (X : R[X]) := by sorry
theorem charmatrix_diagonal (d : n → R) :
    charmatrix (diagonal d) = diagonal fun i => X - C (d i) := by sorry
theorem charmatrix_one : charmatrix (1 : Matrix n n R) = diagonal fun _ => X - 1 :=
  charmatrix_diagonal _

@[simp]
theorem charmatrix_natCast (k : ℕ) :
    charmatrix (k : Matrix n n R) = diagonal fun _ => X - (k : R[X]) :=
  charmatrix_diagonal _

@[simp]
theorem charmatrix_ofNat (k : ℕ) [k.AtLeastTwo] :
    charmatrix (ofNat(k) : Matrix n n R) = diagonal fun _ => X - ofNat(k) :=
  charmatrix_natCast _

@[simp]
theorem charmatrix_transpose (M : Matrix n n R) : (Mᵀ).charmatrix = M.charmatrixᵀ := by sorry
theorem matPolyEquiv_charmatrix : matPolyEquiv (charmatrix M) = X - C M := by sorry
theorem charmatrix_reindex (e : n ≃ m) :
    charmatrix (reindex e e M) = reindex e e (charmatrix M) := by sorry
lemma charmatrix_map (M : Matrix n n R) (f : R →+* S) :
    charmatrix (M.map f) = (charmatrix M).map (Polynomial.map f) := by sorry
lemma charmatrix_fromBlocks :
    charmatrix (fromBlocks M₁₁ M₁₂ M₂₁ M₂₂) =
      fromBlocks (charmatrix M₁₁) (- M₁₂.map C) (- M₂₁.map C) (charmatrix M₂₂) := by sorry
lemma charmatrix_blockTriangular_iff {α : Type*} [Preorder α] {M : Matrix n n R} {b : n → α} :
    M.charmatrix.BlockTriangular b ↔ M.BlockTriangular b := by sorry
def charpoly (M : Matrix n n R) : R[X] :=
  (charmatrix M).det

theorem eval_charpoly (M : Matrix m m R) (t : R) :
    M.charpoly.eval t = (Matrix.scalar _ t - M).det := by sorry
theorem charpoly_isEmpty [IsEmpty n] {A : Matrix n n R} : charpoly A = 1 := by sorry
theorem charpoly_zero : charpoly (0 : Matrix n n R) = X ^ Fintype.card n := by sorry
theorem charpoly_diagonal (d : n → R) : charpoly (diagonal d) = ∏ i, (X - C (d i)) := by sorry
theorem charpoly_one : charpoly (1 : Matrix n n R) = (X - 1) ^ Fintype.card n := by sorry
theorem charpoly_natCast (k : ℕ) :
    charpoly (k : Matrix n n R) = (X - (k : R[X])) ^ Fintype.card n := by sorry
theorem charpoly_ofNat (k : ℕ) [k.AtLeastTwo] :
    charpoly (ofNat(k) : Matrix n n R) = (X - ofNat(k)) ^ Fintype.card n :=
  charpoly_natCast _

@[simp]
theorem charpoly_transpose (M : Matrix n n R) : (Mᵀ).charpoly = M.charpoly := by sorry
theorem charpoly_reindex (e : n ≃ m)
    (M : Matrix n n R) : (reindex e e M).charpoly = M.charpoly := by sorry
lemma charpoly_map (M : Matrix n n R) (f : R →+* S) :
    (M.map f).charpoly = M.charpoly.map f := by sorry
lemma charpoly_fromBlocks_zero₁₂ :
    (fromBlocks M₁₁ 0 M₂₁ M₂₂).charpoly = (M₁₁.charpoly * M₂₂.charpoly) := by sorry
lemma charpoly_fromBlocks_zero₂₁ :
    (fromBlocks M₁₁ M₁₂ 0 M₂₂).charpoly = (M₁₁.charpoly * M₂₂.charpoly) := by sorry
lemma charmatrix_toSquareBlock {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {b : n → α} {a : α} :
    (M.toSquareBlock b a).charmatrix = M.charmatrix.toSquareBlock b a := by sorry
lemma BlockTriangular.charpoly {α : Type*} {b : n → α} [LinearOrder α] (h : M.BlockTriangular b) :
    M.charpoly = ∏ a ∈ image b univ, (M.toSquareBlock b a).charpoly := by sorry
lemma charpoly_of_upperTriangular [LinearOrder n] (M : Matrix n n R) (h : M.BlockTriangular id) :
    M.charpoly = ∏ i : n, (X - C (M i i)) := by sorry
theorem aeval_self_charpoly (M : Matrix n n R) : aeval M M.charpoly = 0 := by sorry
theorem charpoly_mul_comm' (A : Matrix m n R) (B : Matrix n m R) :
    X ^ Fintype.card n * (A * B).charpoly = X ^ Fintype.card m * (B * A).charpoly := by sorry
theorem charpoly_mul_comm_of_le
    (A : Matrix m n R) (B : Matrix n m R) (hle : Fintype.card n ≤ Fintype.card m) :
    (A * B).charpoly = X ^ (Fintype.card m - Fintype.card n) * (B * A).charpoly := by sorry
theorem charpoly_mul_comm (A B : Matrix n n R) : (A * B).charpoly = (B * A).charpoly :=
  (isRegular_X_pow _).left.eq_iff.mp <| charpoly_mul_comm' A B

theorem charpoly_vecMulVec (u v : n → R) :
    (vecMulVec u v).charpoly = X ^ Fintype.card n - (u ⬝ᵥ v) • X ^ (Fintype.card n - 1) := by sorry
theorem charpoly_units_conj (M : (Matrix n n R)ˣ) (N : Matrix n n R) :
    (M.val * N * M⁻¹.val).charpoly = N.charpoly := by sorry
theorem charpoly_units_conj' (M : (Matrix n n R)ˣ) (N : Matrix n n R) :
    (M⁻¹.val * N * M.val).charpoly = N.charpoly :=
  charpoly_units_conj M⁻¹ N

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
theorem charpoly_sub_scalar (M : Matrix n n R) (μ : R) :
    (M - scalar n μ).charpoly = M.charpoly.comp (X + C μ) := by sorry
end Matrix

title: 049_the_cayley-hamilton_theorem
content:
(* This statement uses MathComp's algebra, matrix, and polynomial libraries. *)
From HB Require Import structures.
From mathcomp Require Import ssreflect ssrfun ssrbool eqtype ssrnat seq div.
From mathcomp Require Import choice fintype tuple finfun bigop fingroup perm.
From mathcomp Require Import nmodule algebra divalg decfield matrix mxalgebra.
From mathcomp Require Import poly polydiv.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Import GRing.Theory.
Local Open Scope ring_scope.

(**
  Cayley-Hamilton: evaluating a square matrix's characteristic polynomial at
  that matrix gives the zero matrix.
*)
Theorem Cayley_Hamilton (R : comNzRingType) n' (A : 'M[R]_n'.+1) :
  horner_mx A (char_poly A) = 0.
Proof.
Admitted.

title: 049_the_cayley-hamilton_theorem
content:
(*  Title:      Cayley_Hamilton/Cayley_Hamilton.thy
    Author:     Johannes Hölzl, TU München
    Author:     Stefan Hetzl, TU Wien
    Author:     Stephan Adelsberge, WU Wien
    Author:     Florian Pollak, TU Wien
*)

(*<*)
theory Cayley_Hamilton
imports
  Square_Matrix
  "HOL-Computational_Algebra.Polynomial"  
begin

definition C :: "'a \<Rightarrow> 'a::ring_1 poly" where "C c = [:c:]"
abbreviation CC (\<open>\<^bold>C\<close>) where "\<^bold>C \<equiv> map_sq_matrix C"

lemma degree_C[simp]: "degree (C a) = 0"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_C_0[simp]: "coeff (C x) 0 = x"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_C_gt0[simp]: "0 < n \<Longrightarrow> coeff (C x) n = 0"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_C_eq: "coeff (C x) n = (if n = 0 then x else 0)"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_mult_C[simp]: "coeff (a * C x) n = coeff a n * x"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_C_mult[simp]: "coeff (C x * a) n = x * coeff a n"
  by sorry

lemma C_0[simp]: "C 0 = 0"
  by sorry

lemma C_1[simp]: "C 1 = 1"
  by sorry

lemma C_linear:
  shows C_mult: "C (a * b) = C b * C a"
    and C_add: "C (a + b) = C a + C b"
    and C_minus: "C (- a) = - C a"
    and C_diff: "C (a - b) = C a - C b"
  by sorry

definition X :: "'a::ring_1 poly" where "X = [:0, 1:]"
abbreviation XX (\<open>\<^bold>X\<close>) where "\<^bold>X \<equiv> diag X"

lemma degree_X[simp]: "degree X = 1"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_X_Suc_0[simp]: "coeff X (Suc 0) = 1"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_X_mult[simp]: "coeff (X * p) (Suc i) = coeff p i"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_mult_X[simp]: "coeff (p * X) (Suc i) = coeff p i"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_X_mult_0[simp]: "coeff (X * p) 0 = 0"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_mult_X_0[simp]: "coeff (p * X) 0 = 0"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_X: "coeff X i = (if i = 1 then 1 else 0)"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_pow_X: "coeff (X ^ i) n = (if i = n then 1 else 0)"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_pow_X_eq[simp]: "coeff (X^i) i = 1"
  by sorry

lemma (in monoid_mult) power_ac: "a * (a^n * x) = a^n * (a * x)"
  by sorry

text\<open>This theory contains auxiliary lemmas on polynomials.\<close>

lemma degree_prod_le: "degree (\<Prod>i\<in>S. f i) \<le> (\<Sum>i\<in>S. degree (f i))"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_mult_sum:
  "degree p \<le> m \<Longrightarrow> degree q \<le> n \<Longrightarrow> coeff (p * q) (m + n) = coeff p m * coeff q n"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_mult_prod_sum:
  "coeff (\<Prod>i\<in>S. f i) (\<Sum>i\<in>S. degree (f i)) = (\<Prod>i\<in>S. coeff (f i) (degree (f i)))"
  by sorry

lemma degree_sum_less:
  "0 < n \<Longrightarrow> (\<And>x. x \<in> A \<Longrightarrow> degree (f x) < n) \<Longrightarrow> degree (\<Sum>x\<in>A. f x) < n" 
  by sorry

lemma degree_sum_le:
  shows "(\<And>x. x \<in> A \<Longrightarrow> degree (f x) \<le> n) \<Longrightarrow> degree (\<Sum>x\<in>A. f x) \<le> n"
  by sorry

lemma degree_sum_le_Max:
  "finite F \<Longrightarrow> degree (sum f F) \<le> Max ((\<lambda>x. degree (f x))`F)"
  by sorry

lemma poly_as_sum_of_monoms': assumes n: "degree p \<le> n" shows "(\<Sum>i\<le>n. X^i * C (coeff p i)) = p"
  by sorry

lemma poly_as_sum_of_monoms: "(\<Sum>i\<le>degree p. X^i * C (coeff p i)) = p"
  by sorry

lemma degree_sum_unique':
  assumes I: "finite I" "i \<notin> I" "\<And>j. j \<in> I \<Longrightarrow> degree (p j) < degree (p i)"
  shows "degree (\<Sum>i\<in>insert i I. p i) = degree (p i)"
  by sorry

lemma degree_sum_unique:
  "finite I \<Longrightarrow> i \<in> I \<Longrightarrow> (\<And>j. j \<in> I \<Longrightarrow> j \<noteq> i \<Longrightarrow> degree (p j) < degree (p i)) \<Longrightarrow>
    degree (\<Sum>i\<in>I. p i) = degree (p i)"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_sum_unique:
  fixes p :: "'a \<Rightarrow> 'b::semiring_0 poly"
  assumes I: "finite I" "i \<in> I" "\<And>j. j \<in> I \<Longrightarrow> j \<noteq> i \<Longrightarrow> degree (p j) < degree (p i)"
  shows "coeff (\<Sum>i\<in>I. p i) (degree (p i)) = coeff (p i) (degree (p i))"
  by sorry

lemma diag_coeff: "diag (coeff x i) = map_sq_matrix (\<lambda>x. coeff x i) (diag x)"
  by sorry

lemma smult_one: "x *\<^sub>S 1 = diag x"
  by sorry

lemma sum_telescope_Ico: "a \<le> b \<Longrightarrow> (\<Sum>i=a ..< b. f i - f (Suc i) ::_::ab_group_add) = f a - f b"
  by sorry

lemmas map_sq_matrix = map_sq_matrix_diff map_sq_matrix_add map_sq_matrix_smult map_sq_matrix_sum

lemma sign_permut: "degree (of_int (sign p) * q) = degree q" 
  by sorry

lemma degree_det:
  assumes "\<And>j. j permutes UNIV \<Longrightarrow> j \<noteq> id \<Longrightarrow> degree (\<Prod>i\<in>UNIV. to_fun A i (j i)) < degree (\<Prod>i\<in>UNIV. to_fun A i i)"
  shows "degree (det A) = degree (\<Prod>i\<in>UNIV. to_fun A i i)"
  by sorry

definition max_degree :: "'a::zero poly^^'n \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "max_degree A = Max (range (\<lambda>(i, j). degree (to_fun A i j)))"

lemma degree_le_max_degree: "degree (to_fun A i j) \<le> max_degree A"
  by sorry

definition "charpoly A = det (\<^bold>X - \<^bold>C A)"

lemma degree_diff_cancel: "degree q < degree p \<Longrightarrow> degree (p - q::_::ab_group_add poly) = degree p"
  by sorry

lemma
  fixes A :: "'a::comm_ring_1^^'n"
  shows degree_charpoly: "degree (charpoly A) = CARD('n)"
    and coeff_charpoly: "coeff (charpoly A) (degree (charpoly A)) = 1"
  by sorry

definition "max_perm_degree A = Max ((\<lambda>p. \<Sum>i\<in>UNIV. degree (to_fun A i (p i)))`{p. p permutes UNIV})"

lemma max_perm_degree_eqI:
  "(\<And>p. p permutes (UNIV::'a::finite set) \<Longrightarrow> (\<Sum>i\<in>UNIV. degree (to_fun A i (p i))) \<le> x) \<Longrightarrow>
    (\<exists>p. p permutes UNIV \<and> (\<Sum>i\<in>UNIV. degree (to_fun A i (p i))) = x) \<Longrightarrow>
    max_perm_degree A = x"
  by sorry

lemma degree_prod_le_max_perm_degree:
  "j permutes (UNIV::'a::finite set) \<Longrightarrow> degree (\<Prod>i\<in>UNIV. to_fun A i (j i)) \<le> max_perm_degree A"
  by sorry

lemma degree_le_max_perm_degree: "degree (det A) \<le> max_perm_degree A"
  by sorry

lemma max_degree_adjugate:
  fixes A :: "_^^'n"
  shows "max_degree (adjugate (\<^bold>X - \<^bold>C A)) = CARD('n) - 1"
    (is "?R = _")
  by sorry

definition poly_mat :: "'a::ring_1 poly \<Rightarrow> 'a^^'n \<Rightarrow> 'a^^'n" where
  "poly_mat p A = (\<Sum>i\<le>degree p. coeff p i *\<^sub>S A^i)"

lemma zero_smult[simp]: "0 *\<^sub>S M = (0::'a::semiring_1^^'n)"
  by sorry

lemma smult_smult: "a *\<^sub>S b *\<^sub>S M = (a * b::'a::monoid_mult) *\<^sub>S M"
  by sorry

lemma map_sq_matrix_mult_eq_smult[simp]: "map_sq_matrix ((*) a) M = a *\<^sub>S M"
  by sorry

lemma coeff_smult_1: "coeff p i *\<^sub>S m = m * map_sq_matrix (\<lambda>p. coeff p i) (p *\<^sub>S 1::_::comm_ring_1 ^^ 'n)"
  by sorry

lemma map_sq_matrix_if_distrib[simp]:
  "map_sq_matrix (\<lambda>x. if P then f x else g x) = (if P then map_sq_matrix f else map_sq_matrix g)"
  by sorry
(*>*)

theorem Cayley_Hamilton:
  fixes A :: "'a::comm_ring_1 ^^ 'n"
  shows "poly_mat (charpoly A) A = 0"
  by sorry
(*<*)

end
(*>*)

title: 049_the_cayley-hamilton_theorem
049_the_cayley-hamilton_theorem
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__049, "The Cayley-Hamilton Theorem": the
;; characteristic polynomial of every finite square matrix over a commutative
;; unital ring annihilates the matrix.  This is expressed by the equivalent
;; generic-matrix identity over an integer polynomial ring.  This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Multivariate integer polynomials are sorted lists of
;; (monomial . coefficient) pairs.  A monomial is a sorted list of variable
;; indices, with repetition recording powers.

(defun ht049-monomial-mul (left right)
  (declare (xargs :measure
                  (+ (acl2-count left) (acl2-count right))))
  (cond ((endp left) right)
        ((endp right) left)
        ((<= (car left) (car right))
         (cons (car left)
               (ht049-monomial-mul (cdr left) right)))
        (t
         (cons (car right)
               (ht049-monomial-mul left (cdr right))))))

(defun ht049-poly-insert-term (monomial coefficient polynomial)
  (cond ((equal coefficient 0) polynomial)
        ((endp polynomial)
         (list (cons monomial coefficient)))
        ((equal monomial (caar polynomial))
         (let ((sum (+ coefficient (cdar polynomial))))
           (if (equal sum 0)
               (cdr polynomial)
             (cons (cons monomial sum) (cdr polynomial)))))
        ((lexorder monomial (caar polynomial))
         (cons (cons monomial coefficient) polynomial))
        (t
         (cons (car polynomial)
               (ht049-poly-insert-term monomial coefficient
                                       (cdr polynomial))))))

(defun ht049-poly-add (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      right
    (ht049-poly-add
     (cdr left)
     (ht049-poly-insert-term (caar left) (cdar left) right))))

(defun ht049-poly-neg (polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (cons (cons (caar polynomial) (- (cdar polynomial)))
          (ht049-poly-neg (cdr polynomial)))))

(defun ht049-poly-mul-term (monomial coefficient polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (ht049-poly-insert-term
     (ht049-monomial-mul monomial (caar polynomial))
     (* coefficient (cdar polynomial))
     (ht049-poly-mul-term monomial coefficient (cdr polynomial)))))

(defun ht049-poly-mul (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      nil
    (ht049-poly-add
     (ht049-poly-mul-term (caar left) (cdar left) right)
     (ht049-poly-mul (cdr left) right))))

(defun ht049-poly-one ()
  (list (cons nil 1)))

(defun ht049-poly-variable (index)
  (list (cons (list index) 1)))

;; Univariate polynomials in the characteristic indeterminate are coefficient
;; lists in ascending degree; their coefficients are the polynomials above.

(defun ht049-upoly-normalize (coefficients)
  (if (endp coefficients)
      nil
    (let ((tail (ht049-upoly-normalize (cdr coefficients))))
      (if (and (equal (car coefficients) nil)
               (endp tail))
          nil
        (cons (car coefficients) tail)))))

(defun ht049-upoly-add (left right)
  (cond ((endp left) right)
        ((endp right) left)
        (t
         (ht049-upoly-normalize
          (cons (ht049-poly-add (car left) (car right))
                (ht049-upoly-add (cdr left) (cdr right)))))))

(defun ht049-upoly-neg (polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (ht049-upoly-normalize
     (cons (ht049-poly-neg (car polynomial))
           (ht049-upoly-neg (cdr polynomial))))))

(defun ht049-upoly-scale (coefficient polynomial)
  (if (or (equal coefficient nil)
          (endp polynomial))
      nil
    (cons (ht049-poly-mul coefficient (car polynomial))
          (ht049-upoly-scale coefficient (cdr polynomial)))))

(defun ht049-upoly-mul (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      nil
    (let ((tail-product (ht049-upoly-mul (cdr left) right)))
      (ht049-upoly-add
       (ht049-upoly-scale (car left) right)
       (if (endp tail-product)
           nil
         (cons nil tail-product))))))

(defun ht049-upoly-one ()
  (list (ht049-poly-one)))

(defun ht049-upoly-from-entry (entry diagonalp)
  (if diagonalp
      (list (ht049-poly-neg entry) (ht049-poly-one))
    (list (ht049-poly-neg entry))))

;; The generic n-by-n matrix has algebraically independent entries x_(i,j).

(defun ht049-range-from (start count)
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons start
          (ht049-range-from (+ 1 start) (- count 1)))))

(defun ht049-generic-row (n row columns)
  (if (endp columns)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-poly-variable
           (+ (* n row) (car columns)))
          (ht049-generic-row n row (cdr columns)))))

(defun ht049-generic-matrix-rows (n rows columns)
  (if (endp rows)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-generic-row n (car rows) columns)
          (ht049-generic-matrix-rows n (cdr rows) columns))))

(defun ht049-generic-matrix (n)
  (let ((indices (ht049-range-from 0 n)))
    (ht049-generic-matrix-rows n indices indices)))

;; Form tI-X, whose determinant is the characteristic polynomial of X.

(defun ht049-characteristic-row (row row-index column-index)
  (if (endp row)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-upoly-from-entry
           (car row)
           (equal row-index column-index))
          (ht049-characteristic-row
           (cdr row) row-index (+ 1 column-index)))))

(defun ht049-characteristic-matrix-rows (matrix row-index)
  (if (endp matrix)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-characteristic-row (car matrix) row-index 0)
          (ht049-characteristic-matrix-rows
           (cdr matrix) (+ 1 row-index)))))

(defun ht049-characteristic-matrix (matrix)
  (ht049-characteristic-matrix-rows matrix 0))

;; The determinant is the signed sum over permutations.

(defun ht049-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons (cons item (car lists))
          (ht049-prefix-each item (cdr lists)))))

(defun ht049-insert-everywhere (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list (list item))
    (cons (cons item list)
          (ht049-prefix-each
           (car list)
           (ht049-insert-everywhere item (cdr list))))))

(defun ht049-insert-into-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (append (ht049-insert-everywhere item (car lists))
            (ht049-insert-into-each item (cdr lists)))))

(defun ht049-permutations (list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list nil)
    (ht049-insert-into-each
     (car list)
     (ht049-permutations (cdr list)))))

(defun ht049-count-greater (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      0
    (+ (if (> item (car list)) 1 0)
       (ht049-count-greater item (cdr list)))))

(defun ht049-inversion-count (permutation)
  (if (endp permutation)
      0
    (+ (ht049-count-greater (car permutation) (cdr permutation))
       (ht049-inversion-count (cdr permutation)))))

(defun ht049-upoly-diagonal-product (matrix permutation row-index)
  (if (endp permutation)
      (ht049-upoly-one)
    (ht049-upoly-mul
     (nth (car permutation) (nth row-index matrix))
     (ht049-upoly-diagonal-product
      matrix (cdr permutation) (+ 1 row-index)))))

(defun ht049-determinant-sum (matrix permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      nil
    (let* ((permutation (car permutations))
           (product
            (ht049-upoly-diagonal-product matrix permutation 0))
           (signed-product
            (if (equal (mod (ht049-inversion-count permutation) 2) 0)
                product
              (ht049-upoly-neg product))))
      (ht049-upoly-add
       signed-product
       (ht049-determinant-sum matrix (cdr permutations))))))

(defun ht049-upoly-matrix-det (matrix n)
  (ht049-determinant-sum
   matrix
   (ht049-permutations (ht049-range-from 0 n))))

;; Matrix arithmetic over the multivariate integer polynomial ring.

(defun ht049-zero-row (n)
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (cons nil (ht049-zero-row (- n 1)))))

(defun ht049-zero-matrix-rows (n count)
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-zero-row n)
          (ht049-zero-matrix-rows n (- count 1)))))

(defun ht049-zero-matrix (n)
  (ht049-zero-matrix-rows n n))

(defun ht049-matrix-add-row (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-poly-add (car left) (car right))
          (ht049-matrix-add-row (cdr left) (cdr right)))))

(defun ht049-matrix-add (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-matrix-add-row (car left) (car right))
          (ht049-matrix-add (cdr left) (cdr right)))))

(defun ht049-matrix-column (column matrix)
  (if (endp matrix)
      nil
    (cons (nth column (car matrix))
          (ht049-matrix-column column (cdr matrix)))))

(defun ht049-poly-dot-product (left right)
  (if (or (endp left) (endp right))
      nil
    (ht049-poly-add
     (ht049-poly-mul (car left) (car right))
     (ht049-poly-dot-product (cdr left) (cdr right)))))

(defun ht049-matrix-mul-row (row right column count)
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-poly-dot-product
           row
           (ht049-matrix-column column right))
          (ht049-matrix-mul-row
           row right (+ 1 column) (- count 1)))))

(defun ht049-matrix-mul-rows (left right n)
  (if (endp left)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-matrix-mul-row (car left) right 0 n)
          (ht049-matrix-mul-rows (cdr left) right n))))

(defun ht049-matrix-mul (left right n)
  (ht049-matrix-mul-rows left right n))

(defun ht049-scalar-row (coefficient row column count)
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons (if (equal row column) coefficient nil)
          (ht049-scalar-row
           coefficient row (+ 1 column) (- count 1)))))

(defun ht049-scalar-matrix-rows (coefficient row n count)
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons (ht049-scalar-row coefficient row 0 n)
          (ht049-scalar-matrix-rows
           coefficient (+ 1 row) n (- count 1)))))

(defun ht049-scalar-matrix (coefficient n)
  (ht049-scalar-matrix-rows coefficient 0 n n))

(defun ht049-eval-upoly-at-matrix (coefficients matrix n)
  (if (endp coefficients)
      (ht049-zero-matrix n)
    (ht049-matrix-add
     (ht049-scalar-matrix (car coefficients) n)
     (ht049-matrix-mul
      matrix
      (ht049-eval-upoly-at-matrix (cdr coefficients) matrix n)
      n))))

(defun ht049-cayley-hamilton-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (let* ((matrix (ht049-generic-matrix n))
          (characteristic-polynomial
           (ht049-upoly-matrix-det
            (ht049-characteristic-matrix matrix)
            n)))
     (equal
      (ht049-eval-upoly-at-matrix
       characteristic-polynomial matrix n)
      (ht049-zero-matrix n)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 049_the_cayley-hamilton_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "The Cayley-Hamilton Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item
-- 049: every finite square matrix over a commutative ring is annihilated by its characteristic
-- polynomial. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; true; false)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat)
  renaming (zero to zeroN; suc to sucN)

data Fin : Nat → Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} → Fin (sucN n)
  fsuc : {n : Nat} → Fin n → Fin (sucN n)

record RingOperations (R : Set) : Set where
  field
    zero one : R
    add multiply : R → R → R
    negate : R → R

record CommutativeRing (R : Set) : Set where
  field
    operations : RingOperations R

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) →
      RingOperations.add operations x y ≡
      RingOperations.add operations y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      RingOperations.add operations
        (RingOperations.add operations x y) z ≡
      RingOperations.add operations x
        (RingOperations.add operations y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) →
      RingOperations.add operations x
        (RingOperations.zero operations) ≡ x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) →
      RingOperations.add operations x
        (RingOperations.negate operations x) ≡
      RingOperations.zero operations

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) →
      RingOperations.multiply operations x y ≡
      RingOperations.multiply operations y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      RingOperations.multiply operations
        (RingOperations.multiply operations x y) z ≡
      RingOperations.multiply operations x
        (RingOperations.multiply operations y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) →
      RingOperations.multiply operations x
        (RingOperations.one operations) ≡ x
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) →
      RingOperations.multiply operations x
        (RingOperations.add operations y z) ≡
      RingOperations.add operations
        (RingOperations.multiply operations x y)
        (RingOperations.multiply operations x z)

Polynomial : Set → Set
Polynomial R = List R

polynomialAdd :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  Polynomial R →
  Polynomial R →
  Polynomial R
polynomialAdd operations [] q = q
polynomialAdd operations p [] = p
polynomialAdd operations (x ∷ p) (y ∷ q) =
  RingOperations.add operations x y ∷
  polynomialAdd operations p q

polynomialNegate :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  Polynomial R →
  Polynomial R
polynomialNegate operations [] = []
polynomialNegate operations (x ∷ p) =
  RingOperations.negate operations x ∷
  polynomialNegate operations p

polynomialScale :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  R →
  Polynomial R →
  Polynomial R
polynomialScale operations scalar [] = []
polynomialScale operations scalar (x ∷ p) =
  RingOperations.multiply operations scalar x ∷
  polynomialScale operations scalar p

polynomialMultiply :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  Polynomial R →
  Polynomial R →
  Polynomial R
polynomialMultiply operations [] q = []
polynomialMultiply operations (x ∷ p) q =
  polynomialAdd operations
    (polynomialScale operations x q)
    (RingOperations.zero operations ∷
      polynomialMultiply operations p q)

polynomialOperations :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  RingOperations (Polynomial R)
polynomialOperations operations =
  record
    { zero = []
    ; one = RingOperations.one operations ∷ []
    ; add = polynomialAdd operations
    ; multiply = polynomialMultiply operations
    ; negate = polynomialNegate operations
    }

constantPolynomial :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  R →
  Polynomial R
constantPolynomial operations x = x ∷ []

variablePolynomial :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  Polynomial R
variablePolynomial operations =
  RingOperations.zero operations ∷
  RingOperations.one operations ∷
  []

Matrix : Set → Nat → Set
Matrix R n = Fin n → Fin n → R

MatrixEqual :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  Matrix R n →
  Set
MatrixEqual A B = (i j : Fin _) → A i j ≡ B i j

finEqual : {n : Nat} → Fin n → Fin n → Bool
finEqual fzero fzero = true
finEqual fzero (fsuc j) = false
finEqual (fsuc i) fzero = false
finEqual (fsuc i) (fsuc j) = finEqual i j

select : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
select true yes no = yes
select false yes no = no

sumFin :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  {n : Nat} →
  (Fin n → R) →
  R
sumFin operations {zeroN} term =
  RingOperations.zero operations
sumFin operations {sucN n} term =
  RingOperations.add operations
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin operations (λ i → term (fsuc i)))

zeroMatrix :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n
zeroMatrix operations i j =
  RingOperations.zero operations

scalarMatrix :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  {n : Nat} →
  R →
  Matrix R n
scalarMatrix operations scalar i j =
  select (finEqual i j)
    scalar
    (RingOperations.zero operations)

matrixAdd :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  Matrix R n →
  Matrix R n
matrixAdd operations A B i j =
  RingOperations.add operations (A i j) (B i j)

matrixMultiply :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  Matrix R n →
  Matrix R n
matrixMultiply operations A B i j =
  sumFin operations
    (λ k → RingOperations.multiply operations (A i k) (B k j))

skip :
  {n : Nat} →
  Fin (sucN n) →
  Fin n →
  Fin (sucN n)
skip {zeroN} column ()
skip {sucN n} fzero k = fsuc k
skip {sucN n} (fsuc column) fzero = fzero
skip {sucN n} (fsuc column) (fsuc k) =
  fsuc (skip column k)

firstRowMinor :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R (sucN n) →
  Fin (sucN n) →
  Matrix R n
firstRowMinor A column i j =
  A (fsuc i) (skip column j)

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Fin n →
  R
alternatingSign operations fzero =
  RingOperations.one operations
alternatingSign operations (fsuc i) =
  RingOperations.negate operations
    (alternatingSign operations i)

determinant :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  R
determinant operations {zeroN} A =
  RingOperations.one operations
determinant operations {sucN n} A =
  sumFin operations
    (λ column →
      RingOperations.multiply operations
        (alternatingSign operations column)
        (RingOperations.multiply operations
          (A fzero column)
          (determinant operations (firstRowMinor A column))))

characteristicMatrix :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  Matrix (Polynomial R) n
characteristicMatrix operations A i j =
  select (finEqual i j)
    (polynomialAdd operations
      (variablePolynomial operations)
      (polynomialNegate operations
        (constantPolynomial operations (A i j))))
    (polynomialNegate operations
      (constantPolynomial operations (A i j)))

characteristicPolynomial :
  {R : Set} →
  CommutativeRing R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  Polynomial R
characteristicPolynomial ring A =
  determinant
    (polynomialOperations (CommutativeRing.operations ring))
    (characteristicMatrix (CommutativeRing.operations ring) A)

evaluateAtMatrix :
  {R : Set} →
  RingOperations R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Polynomial R →
  Matrix R n →
  Matrix R n
evaluateAtMatrix operations [] A =
  zeroMatrix operations
evaluateAtMatrix operations (coefficient ∷ coefficients) A =
  matrixAdd operations
    (scalarMatrix operations coefficient)
    (matrixMultiply operations A
      (evaluateAtMatrix operations coefficients A))

the-cayley-hamilton-theorem : Set₁
the-cayley-hamilton-theorem =
  (R : Set) →
  (ring : CommutativeRing R) →
  (n : Nat) →
  (A : Matrix R n) →
  MatrixEqual
    (evaluateAtMatrix
      (CommutativeRing.operations ring)
      (characteristicPolynomial ring A)
      A)
    (zeroMatrix (CommutativeRing.operations ring))

title: 049_the_cayley-hamilton_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "The Cayley-Hamilton Theorem" from Hundred
  Theorems artifact 049. For a square matrix over an arbitrary commutative
  ring on a finite index carrier, the characteristic polynomial det(XI - A)
  evaluates at the matrix to the zero matrix. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory permutesTheory ringTheory;

val cayley_hamilton_theorem =
  ``let poly_zero =
      \(r : 'a ring) (k : num). r.sum.id
    in
    let poly_one =
      \(r : 'a ring) (k : num).
        if k = 0 then r.prod.id else r.sum.id
    in
    let poly_add =
      \(r : 'a ring) (p : num -> 'a) (q : num -> 'a) (k : num).
        r.sum.op (p k) (q k)
    in
    let poly_neg =
      \(r : 'a ring) (p : num -> 'a) (k : num).
        r.sum.inv (p k)
    in
    let poly_mul =
      \(r : 'a ring) (p : num -> 'a) (q : num -> 'a) (k : num).
        ITSET
          (\i acc. r.sum.op (r.prod.op (p i) (q (k - i))) acc)
          (count (SUC k)) r.sum.id
    in
    let char_entry =
      \(r : 'a ring) (A : 'i -> 'i -> 'a)
       (i : 'i) (j : 'i) (k : num).
        r.sum.op
          (if i = j /\ k = 1 then r.prod.id else r.sum.id)
          (if k = 0 then r.sum.inv (A i j) else r.sum.id)
    in
    let det_term =
      \(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool) (A : 'i -> 'i -> 'a)
       (p : 'i -> 'i).
        let diagonal_product =
          ITSET
            (\i q. poly_mul r (char_entry r A i (p i)) q)
            s (poly_one r)
        in
          if evenperm p then diagonal_product
          else poly_neg r diagonal_product
    in
    let char_poly =
      \(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool) (A : 'i -> 'i -> 'a).
        ITSET
          (\p q. poly_add r (det_term r s A p) q)
          {p : 'i -> 'i | p permutes s} (poly_zero r)
    in
    let matrix_zero =
      \(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool) (i : 'i) (j : 'i).
        r.sum.id
    in
    let matrix_one =
      \(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool) (i : 'i) (j : 'i).
        if i IN s /\ j IN s /\ i = j then r.prod.id else r.sum.id
    in
    let matrix_add =
      \(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool)
       (A : 'i -> 'i -> 'a) (B : 'i -> 'i -> 'a)
       (i : 'i) (j : 'i).
        if i IN s /\ j IN s
        then r.sum.op (A i j) (B i j)
        else r.sum.id
    in
    let matrix_mul =
      \(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool)
       (A : 'i -> 'i -> 'a) (B : 'i -> 'i -> 'a)
       (i : 'i) (j : 'i).
        if i IN s /\ j IN s
        then
          ITSET
            (\k acc. r.sum.op (r.prod.op (A i k) (B k j)) acc)
            s r.sum.id
        else r.sum.id
    in
    let matrix_scale =
      \(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool) (c : 'a)
       (A : 'i -> 'i -> 'a) (i : 'i) (j : 'i).
        if i IN s /\ j IN s
        then r.prod.op c (A i j)
        else r.sum.id
    in
    let matrix_pow =
      \(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool)
       (A : 'i -> 'i -> 'a) (k : num).
        FUNPOW (\B. matrix_mul r s B A) k (matrix_one r s)
    in
    let matrix_poly_eval =
      \(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool) (p : num -> 'a)
       (A : 'i -> 'i -> 'a).
        ITSET
          (\k B.
            matrix_add r s
              (matrix_scale r s (p k) (matrix_pow r s A k)) B)
          (count (SUC (CARD s))) (matrix_zero r s)
    in
      !(r : 'a ring) (s : 'i -> bool) (A : 'i -> 'i -> 'a).
        Ring r /\
        FINITE s /\
        (!i j. i IN s /\ j IN s ==> A i j IN r.carrier)
        ==>
        matrix_poly_eval r s (char_poly r s A) A = matrix_zero r s``;

title: 049_the_cayley-hamilton_theorem
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 049, the
  Cayley-Hamilton theorem.

  This reproduces the hypotheses and conclusion of set.mm theorem
  cayleyhamilton. A is the N-by-N matrix algebra over the commutative ring R,
  K is the coefficient function of the characteristic polynomial of M, and
  the displayed finite sum is that polynomial evaluated at M.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

${
  $d A n $.
  $d B n $.
  $d C n $.
  $d n M $.
  $d n N $.
  $d R n $.
  $d .* n $.
  $d .^ n $.

  hundred-theorems-049-matrix-algebra $e
    |- A = ( N Mat R )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-049-matrix-carrier $e
    |- B = ( Base ` A )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-049-zero-matrix $e
    |- .0. = ( 0g ` A )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-049-polynomial-matrix $e
    |- C = ( N CharPlyMat R )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-049-characteristic-coefficients $e
    |- K = ( coe1 ` ( C ` M ) )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-049-scalar-action $e
    |- .* = ( .s ` A )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-049-matrix-power $e
    |- .^ = ( .g ` ( mulGrp ` A ) )
  $.

  hundred-theorems-049-cayley-hamilton $a
    |- (
         ( N e. Fin /\ R e. CRing /\ M e. B )
         ->
         (
           A gsum
             ( n e. NN0 |-> ( ( K ` n ) .* ( n .^ M ) ) )
         )
         = .0.
       )
  $.
$}

title: 049_the_cayley-hamilton_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 049, "The Cayley-Hamilton
% Theorem": every finite square matrix over a commutative ring satisfies its
% characteristic polynomial. This file contains no proof.

the_cayley_hamilton_theorem_049[
  n: nat,
  R: TYPE+,
  zero, one: R,
  neg: [R -> R],
  add, mul: [R, R -> R]
]: THEORY
BEGIN
  polynomial: TYPE = [nat -> R]
  matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> R]

  commutative_ring_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (x, y: R): add(x, y) = add(y, x))
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: R):
        add(add(x, y), z) = add(x, add(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x: R): add(x, zero) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x: R): add(x, neg(x)) = zero)
      AND (FORALL (x, y: R): mul(x, y) = mul(y, x))
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: R):
        mul(mul(x, y), z) = mul(x, mul(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x: R): mul(x, one) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: R):
        mul(x, add(y, z)) =
          add(mul(x, y), mul(x, z)))

  ring_sum(
      values: [nat -> R],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE R =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      zero
    ELSE
      add(
        ring_sum(values, count - 1),
        values(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  quotient_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1
        + quotient_aux(
            numerator - denominator,
            denominator,
            fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_ndiv(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    quotient_aux(
      numerator,
      denominator,
      numerator + 1)

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  polynomial_zero: polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (degree: nat): zero)

  constant_polynomial(value: R): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (degree: nat):
      IF degree = 0 THEN value ELSE zero ENDIF)

  polynomial_one: polynomial =
    constant_polynomial(one)

  variable_polynomial: polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (degree: nat):
      IF degree = 1 THEN one ELSE zero ENDIF)

  polynomial_negate(p: polynomial): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (degree: nat): neg(p(degree)))

  polynomial_add(p, q: polynomial): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (degree: nat):
      add(p(degree), q(degree)))

  polynomial_scale(value: R, p: polynomial): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (degree: nat):
      mul(value, p(degree)))

  polynomial_multiply(p, q: polynomial): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (degree: nat):
      ring_sum(
        (LAMBDA (index: nat):
          IF index <= degree THEN
            mul(p(index), q(degree - index))
          ELSE
            zero
          ENDIF),
        degree + 1))

  zero_matrix: matrix =
    (LAMBDA (row, column: nat): zero)

  identity_matrix: matrix =
    (LAMBDA (row, column: nat):
      IF row < n AND column < n AND row = column THEN
        one
      ELSE
        zero
      ENDIF)

  matrix_add(A, B: matrix): matrix =
    (LAMBDA (row, column: nat):
      add(A(row, column), B(row, column)))

  matrix_scale(value: R, A: matrix): matrix =
    (LAMBDA (row, column: nat):
      mul(value, A(row, column)))

  matrix_multiply(A, B: matrix): matrix =
    (LAMBDA (row, column: nat):
      IF row < n AND column < n THEN
        ring_sum(
          (LAMBDA (index: nat):
            mul(A(row, index), B(index, column))),
          n)
      ELSE
        zero
      ENDIF)

  matrix_power(A: matrix, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE matrix =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      identity_matrix
    ELSE
      matrix_multiply(
        matrix_power(A, exponent - 1),
        A)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  matrix_sum(
      values: [nat -> matrix],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE matrix =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      zero_matrix
    ELSE
      matrix_add(
        matrix_sum(values, count - 1),
        values(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  matrix_polynomial_value(p: polynomial, A: matrix): matrix =
    matrix_sum(
      (LAMBDA (degree: nat):
        matrix_scale(
          p(degree),
          matrix_power(A, degree))),
      n + 1)

  function_code_count: nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN 1 ELSE n ^ n ENDIF

  permutation_entry(code, row: nat): nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      safe_mod(safe_ndiv(code, n ^ row), n)
    ENDIF

  permutation_code(code: nat): bool =
    code < function_code_count
      AND (FORALL (row_1, row_2: nat):
        (row_1 < n
          AND row_2 < n
          AND permutation_entry(code, row_1)
            = permutation_entry(code, row_2))
        IMPLIES row_1 = row_2)

  pair_row(pair: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(pair, n)

  pair_column(pair: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(pair, n)

  inversion_at(code, pair: nat): bool =
    pair_row(pair) < n
      AND pair_column(pair) < n
      AND pair_row(pair) < pair_column(pair)
      AND permutation_entry(code, pair_row(pair))
        > permutation_entry(code, pair_column(pair))

  count_true(
      property: [nat -> bool],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_true(property, count - 1)
        + IF property(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  inversion_count(code: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (pair: nat): inversion_at(code, pair)),
      n * n)

  permutation_sign(code: nat): R =
    IF mod(inversion_count(code), 2) = 0 THEN
      one
    ELSE
      neg(one)
    ENDIF

  characteristic_entry(
      A: matrix,
      row, column: nat): polynomial =
    IF row = column THEN
      polynomial_add(
        variable_polynomial,
        polynomial_negate(
          constant_polynomial(A(row, column))))
    ELSE
      polynomial_negate(
        constant_polynomial(A(row, column)))
    ENDIF

  permutation_product(
      A: matrix,
      code, count: nat): RECURSIVE polynomial =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      polynomial_one
    ELSE
      polynomial_multiply(
        permutation_product(A, code, count - 1),
        characteristic_entry(
          A,
          count - 1,
          permutation_entry(code, count - 1)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  determinant_sum(
      A: matrix,
      limit: nat): RECURSIVE polynomial =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      polynomial_zero
    ELSE
      LET code: nat = limit - 1 IN
        polynomial_add(
          determinant_sum(A, limit - 1),
          IF permutation_code(code) THEN
            polynomial_scale(
              permutation_sign(code),
              permutation_product(A, code, n))
          ELSE
            polynomial_zero
          ENDIF)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  characteristic_polynomial(A: matrix): polynomial =
    determinant_sum(A, function_code_count)

  matrix_equal_on_carrier(A, B: matrix): bool =
    FORALL (row, column: nat):
      (row < n AND column < n)
        IMPLIES A(row, column) = B(row, column)

  the_cayley_hamilton_theorem: bool =
    commutative_ring_laws IMPLIES
      (FORALL (A: matrix):
        matrix_equal_on_carrier(
          matrix_polynomial_value(
            characteristic_polynomial(A),
            A),
          zero_matrix))
END the_cayley_hamilton_theorem_049

(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 005, "The Prime Number Theorem":
  the ratio of the number of primes at most n to n / ln n tends to 1.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals List PeanoNat.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition primeb (p : nat) : bool :=
  andb (Nat.leb 2 p)
    (forallb
       (fun d => negb (Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo p d) 0))
       (seq 2 (p - 2))).

Definition prime_count (n : nat) : nat :=
  length (filter primeb (seq 0 (S n))).

Definition tends_to (u : nat -> R) (l : R) : Prop :=
  forall eps : R,
    0 < eps ->
    exists N : nat,
      forall n : nat,
        (N <= n)%nat ->
        Rabs (u n - l) < eps.

Theorem prime_number_theorem :
  tends_to
    (fun n =>
       INR (prime_count n) / (INR n / ln (INR n)))
    1.
Admitted.

title: 005_the_prime_number_theorem
content:
(*
  File:       Prime Number Theorem.thy
  Authors:    Manuel Eberl (TU München), Larry Paulson (University of Cambridge)

  A proof of the Prime Number Theorem and some related properties
*)
section \<open>The Prime Number Theorem\<close>
theory Prime_Number_Theorem
imports 
  Newman_Ingham_Tauberian
  Prime_Counting_Functions
begin

(*<*)
unbundle prime_counting_syntax
(*>*)

subsection \<open>Constructing Newman's function\<close>

text \<open>
  Starting from Mertens' first theorem, i.\,e.\ $\mathfrak M(x) = \ln x + O(1)$, we now 
  want to derive that $\mathfrak M(x) = \ln x + c + o(1)$. This result is considerably stronger
  and it implies the Prime Number Theorem quite directly.

  In order to do this, we define the Dirichlet series
  \[f(s) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\mathfrak{M}(n)}{n^s}\ .\]
  We will prove that this series extends meromorphically to $\mathfrak{R}(s)\geq 1$ and
  apply Ingham's theorem to it (after we subtracted its pole at $s = 1$).
\<close>
definition fds_newman where
  "fds_newman = fds (\<lambda>n. complex_of_real (\<MM> n))"

lemma fds_nth_newman:
  "fds_nth fds_newman n = of_real (\<MM> n)"
  by sorry

lemma norm_fds_nth_newman:
  "norm (fds_nth fds_newman n) = \<MM> n"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  The Dirichlet series $f(s) + \zeta'(s)$ has the coefficients $\mathfrak{M}(n) - \ln n$,
  so by Mertens' first theorem, $f(s) + \zeta'(s)$ has bounded coefficients.
\<close>
lemma bounded_coeffs_newman_minus_deriv_zeta:
  defines "f \<equiv> fds_newman + fds_deriv fds_zeta"
  shows   "Bseq (\<lambda>n. fds_nth f n)"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  A Dirichlet series with bounded coefficients converges for all $s$ with
  $\mathfrak{R}(s)>1$ and so does $\zeta'(s)$, so we can conclude that $f(s)$ does as well.
\<close>
lemma abs_conv_abscissa_newman: "abs_conv_abscissa fds_newman \<le> 1"
  and conv_abscissa_newman:     "conv_abscissa fds_newman \<le> 1"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  We now change the order of summation to obtain an alternative form of $f(s)$ in terms of a 
  sum of Hurwitz $\zeta$ functions.
\<close>
lemma eval_fds_newman_conv_infsetsum:
  assumes s: "Re s > 1"
  shows   "eval_fds fds_newman s = (\<Sum>\<^sub>ap | prime p. (ln (real p) / real p) * hurwitz_zeta p s)"
          "(\<lambda>p. ln (real p) / real p * hurwitz_zeta p s) abs_summable_on {p. prime p}"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  We now define a meromorphic continuation of $f(s)$ on $\mathfrak{R}(s) > \frac{1}{2}$.

  To construct $f(s)$, we express it as
  \[f(s) = \frac{1}{z-1}\left(\bar f(s) - \frac{\zeta'(s)}{\zeta(s)}\right)\ ,\]
  where $\bar f(s)$ (which we shall call \<open>pre_newman\<close>) is a function that is analytic on
  $\Re(s) > \frac{1}{2}$, which can be shown fairly easily using the Weierstra{\ss} M test.
  
  $\zeta'(s)/\zeta(s)$ is meromorphic except for a single pole at $s = 1$ and one $k$-th order
  pole for any $k$-th order zero of $\zeta$, but for the Prime Number Theorem, we are only
  concerned with the area $\mathfrak{R}(s) \geq 1$, where $\zeta$ does not have any zeros.

  Taken together, this means that $f(s)$ is analytic for $\mathfrak{R}(s)\geq 1$ except for a
  double pole at $s = 1$, which we will take care of later.
\<close>

context
  fixes A :: "nat \<Rightarrow> complex \<Rightarrow> complex" and B :: "nat \<Rightarrow> complex \<Rightarrow> complex"
  defines "A \<equiv> (\<lambda>p s. (s - 1) * pre_zeta (real p) s - 
                         of_nat p / (of_nat p powr s * (of_nat p powr s - 1)))"
  defines "B \<equiv> (\<lambda>p s. of_real (ln (real p)) / of_nat p * A p s)"
begin

definition pre_newman :: "complex \<Rightarrow> complex" where
  "pre_newman s = (\<Sum>p. if prime p then B p s else 0)"

definition newman where "newman s = 1 / (s - 1) * (pre_newman s - deriv zeta s / zeta s)"

text \<open>
  The sum used in the definition of \<open>pre_newman\<close> converges uniformly on any disc within the
  half-space with $\mathfrak{R}(s) > \frac{1}{2}$ by the Weierstra{\ss} M test.
\<close>
lemma uniform_limit_pre_newman:
  assumes r: "r \<ge> 0" "Re s - r > 1 / 2"
  shows "uniform_limit (cball s r)
           (\<lambda>n s. \<Sum>p<n. if prime p then B p s else 0) pre_newman at_top"
  by sorry

lemma sums_pre_newman: "Re s > 1 / 2 \<Longrightarrow> (\<lambda>p. if prime p then B p s else 0) sums pre_newman s"
  by sorry

lemma analytic_pre_newman [THEN analytic_on_subset, analytic_intros]:
  "pre_newman analytic_on {s. Re s > 1 / 2}"
  by sorry

lemma holomorphic_pre_newman [holomorphic_intros]:
  "X \<subseteq> {s. Re s > 1 / 2} \<Longrightarrow> pre_newman holomorphic_on X"
  by sorry

lemma eval_fds_newman:
  assumes s: "Re s > 1"
  shows   "eval_fds fds_newman s = newman s"
  by sorry

end

text \<open>
  Next, we shall attempt to get rid of the pole by subtracting suitable multiples of $\zeta(s)$
  and $\zeta'(s)$. To this end, we shall first prove the following alternative definition of 
  $\zeta'(s)$:
\<close>
lemma deriv_zeta_eq':
  assumes "0 < Re s" "s \<noteq> 1"
  shows "deriv zeta s = deriv (\<lambda>z. pre_zeta 1 z * (z - 1)) s / (s - 1) -
                          (pre_zeta 1 s * (s - 1) + 1) / (s - 1)\<^sup>2"
    (is "_ = ?rhs")
  by sorry

text \<open>
  From this, it follows that $(s - 1) \zeta'(s) - \zeta'(s) / \zeta(s)$ is analytic 
  for $\mathfrak{R}(s) \geq 1$:
\<close>
lemma analytic_zeta_derivdiff:
  obtains a where
    "(\<lambda>z. if z = 1 then a else (z - 1) * deriv zeta z - deriv zeta z / zeta z)
          analytic_on {s. Re s \<ge> 1}" 
  by sorry

text \<open>
  Finally, $f(s) + \zeta'(s) + c\zeta(s)$ is analytic.
\<close>
lemma analytic_newman_variant:
  obtains c a where
     "(\<lambda>z. if z = 1 then a else newman z + deriv zeta z + c * zeta z) analytic_on {s. Re s \<ge> 1}"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>The asymptotic expansion of \<open>\<MM>\<close>\<close>

text \<open>
  Our next goal is to show the key result that $\mathfrak{M}(x) = \ln n + c + o(1)$.

  As a first step, we invoke Ingham's Tauberian theorem on the function we have
  just defined and obtain that the sum
  \[\sum\limits_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\mathfrak{M}(n) - \ln n + c}{n}\]
  exists.
\<close>
lemma mertens_summable:
  obtains c :: real where "summable (\<lambda>n. (\<MM> n - ln n + c) / n)"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  Next, we prove a lemma given by Newman stating that if the sum $\sum a_n / n$ exists and
  $a_n + \ln n$ is nondecreasing, then $a_n$ must tend to 0. Unfortunately, the proof is
  rather tedious, but so is the paper version by Newman.
\<close>
lemma sum_goestozero_lemma:
  fixes d::real
  assumes d: "\<bar>\<Sum>i = M..N. a i / i\<bar> < d" and le: "\<And>n. a n + ln n \<le> a (Suc n) + ln (Suc n)"
      and "0 < M" "M < N"
    shows "a M \<le> d * N / (real N - real M) + (real N - real M) / M \<and>
          -a N \<le> d * N / (real N - real M) + (real N - real M) / M"
  by sorry

proposition sum_goestozero_theorem:
  assumes summ: "summable (\<lambda>i. a i / i)"
      and le:   "\<And>n. a n + ln n \<le> a (Suc n) + ln (Suc n)"
    shows "a \<longlonglongrightarrow> 0"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  This leads us to the main intermediate result:
\<close>
lemma Mertens_convergent: "convergent (\<lambda>n::nat. \<MM> n - ln n)"
  by sorry

corollary \<MM>_minus_ln_limit:
  obtains c where "((\<lambda>x::real. \<MM> x - ln x) \<longlongrightarrow> c) at_top"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>The asymptotics of the prime-counting functions\<close>

text \<open>
  We will now use the above result to prove the asymptotics of the prime-counting functions
  $\vartheta(x) \sim x$, $\psi(x) \sim x$, and $\pi(x) \sim x / \ln x$. The last of these is 
  typically called the Prime Number Theorem, but since these functions can be expressed in terms 
  of one another quite easily, knowing the asymptotics of any of them immediately gives the 
  asymptotics of the other ones.

  In this sense, all of the above are equivalent formulations of the Prime Number Theorem.
  The one we shall tackle first, due to its strong connection to the $\mathfrak{M}$ function, is
  $\vartheta(x) \sim x$.

  We know that $\mathfrak{M}(x)$ has the asymptotic expansion
  $\mathfrak{M}(x) = \ln x + c + o(1)$. We also know that
  \[\vartheta(x) = x\mathfrak{M}(x) - \int\nolimits_2^x \mathfrak{M}(t) \,\mathrm{d}t\ .\]
  Substituting in the above asymptotic equation, we obtain:
  \begin{align*}
  \vartheta(x) &= x\ln x + cx + o(x) - \int\nolimits_2^x \ln t + c + o(1) \,\mathrm{d}t\\
            &= x\ln x + cx + o(x) - (x\ln x - x + cx + o(x))\\
            &= x + o(x)
  \end{align*}
  In conclusion, $\vartheta(x) \sim x$.
\<close>
theorem \<theta>_asymptotics: "\<theta> \<sim>[at_top] (\<lambda>x. x)"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  The various other forms of the Prime Number Theorem follow as simple corollaries.
\<close>
corollary \<psi>_asymptotics: "\<psi> \<sim>[at_top] (\<lambda>x. x)"
  by sorry
  
corollary prime_number_theorem: "\<pi> \<sim>[at_top] (\<lambda>x. x / ln x)"
  by sorry

corollary ln_\<pi>_asymptotics: "(\<lambda>x. ln (\<pi> x)) \<sim>[at_top] ln"
  by sorry

corollary \<pi>_ln_\<pi>_asymptotics: "(\<lambda>x. \<pi> x * ln (\<pi> x)) \<sim>[at_top] (\<lambda>x. x)"
  by sorry

corollary nth_prime_asymptotics: "(\<lambda>n. real (nth_prime n)) \<sim>[at_top] (\<lambda>n. real n * ln (real n))"
  by sorry


text \<open>
  The following versions use a little less notation.
\<close>
corollary prime_number_theorem': "((\<lambda>x. \<pi> x / (x / ln x)) \<longlongrightarrow> 1) at_top"
  by sorry

corollary prime_number_theorem'':
  "(\<lambda>x. card {p. prime p \<and> real p \<le> x}) \<sim>[at_top] (\<lambda>x. x / ln x)"
  by sorry

corollary prime_number_theorem''':
  "(\<lambda>n. card {p. prime p \<and> p \<le> n}) \<sim>[at_top] (\<lambda>n. real n / ln (real n))"
  by sorry

(*<*)
unbundle no prime_counting_syntax
(*>*)

end

;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__005, "The Prime Number Theorem": the number of
;; primes at most n is asymptotic to n / ln(n). This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun pnt-has-divisor-at-most-p (n divisor)
  (if (or (not (natp n))
          (not (natp divisor))
          (< divisor 2))
      nil
    (or (equal (mod n divisor) 0)
        (pnt-has-divisor-at-most-p n (- divisor 1)))))

(defun pnt-prime-p (n)
  (and (natp n)
       (<= 2 n)
       (not (pnt-has-divisor-at-most-p n (- n 1)))))

(defun pnt-prime-count (n)
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (+ (if (pnt-prime-p n) 1 0)
       (pnt-prime-count (- n 1)))))

;; For z = (n - 1)/(n + 1), twice the limit of this sum is ln(n).
(defun pnt-atanh-series-prefix (z terms)
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (odd-exponent (+ (* 2 index) 1)))
      (+ (pnt-atanh-series-prefix z index)
         (/ (expt z odd-exponent) odd-exponent)))))

(defun pnt-natural-log-prefix (n terms)
  (if (and (natp n)
           (< 0 n)
           (natp terms))
      (* 2
         (pnt-atanh-series-prefix (/ (- n 1) (+ n 1))
                                  terms))
    0))

;; Quantifier order for the final predicate:
;;   for every epsilon > 0, there exists cutoff, for every n >= cutoff,
;;   there exists log-cutoff, for every terms >= log-cutoff.
(defun-sk pnt-log-tail-p (epsilon n log-cutoff)
  (forall (terms)
    (implies
     (and (natp terms)
          (<= log-cutoff terms))
     (< (abs (- (/ (* (pnt-prime-count n)
                       (pnt-natural-log-prefix n terms))
                    n)
                1))
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk pnt-log-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon n)
  (exists (log-cutoff)
    (and (natp log-cutoff)
         (pnt-log-tail-p epsilon n log-cutoff))))

(defun-sk pnt-prime-tail-p (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and (natp n)
          (<= cutoff n))
     (pnt-log-cutoff-exists-p epsilon n))))

(defun-sk pnt-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and (natp cutoff)
         (<= 2 cutoff)
         (pnt-prime-tail-p epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk prime-number-theorem-statement ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp epsilon)
          (< 0 epsilon))
     (pnt-cutoff-exists-p epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "The Prime Number Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 005.
-- This file contains no proof.

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat
  using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; mod-helper)

data Bottom : Set where

NotEqual : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
NotEqual x y = x == y -> Bottom

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    left  : A
    right : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  first  : A -> Either A B
  second : B -> Either A B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<= : {n : Nat} -> zero <= n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> suc m <= suc n

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = zero
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

natEqual : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

boolNot : Bool -> Bool
boolNot false = true
boolNot true = false

boolOr : Bool -> Bool -> Bool
boolOr false value = value
boolOr true _ = true

dividesBool : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
dividesBool divisor dividend =
  natEqual (naturalMod dividend divisor) zero

hasDivisorThrough : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
hasDivisorThrough n zero = false
hasDivisorThrough n (suc zero) = false
hasDivisorThrough n (suc (suc bound)) =
  boolOr
    (dividesBool (suc (suc bound)) n)
    (hasDivisorThrough n (suc bound))

isPrimeBool : Nat -> Bool
isPrimeBool zero = false
isPrimeBool (suc zero) = false
isPrimeBool (suc (suc n)) =
  boolNot (hasDivisorThrough (suc (suc n)) (suc n))

Prime : Nat -> Set
Prime n = isPrimeBool n == true

indicator : Bool -> Nat
indicator false = zero
indicator true = suc zero

-- This recursion counts exactly the primes in the initial segment [0, n].
primeCount : Nat -> Nat
primeCount zero = zero
primeCount (suc n) =
  primeCount n + indicator (isPrimeBool (suc n))

record StandardRealAnalysis (R : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate reciprocal : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    absoluteValue : R -> R
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      NotEqual oneR zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      NotEqual x zeroR ->
      multiply x (reciprocal x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)

    absolute-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      absoluteValue x == x
    absolute-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      absoluteValue x == negate x

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    completeness :
      (S : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R S ->
      Exists R
        (\ bound ->
          (x : R) -> S x -> lessOrEqual x bound) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> S x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
            ((bound : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> S x -> lessOrEqual x bound) ->
              lessOrEqual supremum bound))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  StandardRealAnalysis.add reals
    x
    (StandardRealAnalysis.negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  StandardRealAnalysis.multiply reals
    x
    (StandardRealAnalysis.reciprocal reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both
    (StandardRealAnalysis.lessOrEqual reals x y)
    (NotEqual x y)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (StandardRealAnalysis.zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <= n ->
      StandardRealAnalysis.lessOrEqual reals
        (StandardRealAnalysis.absoluteValue reals
          (subtract reals (sequence n) limit))
        epsilon)

power :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
power reals x zero =
  StandardRealAnalysis.oneR reals
power reals x (suc n) =
  StandardRealAnalysis.multiply reals x (power reals x n)

-- For x > 0, this is the standard expansion
-- log x = 2 * sum_j ((x - 1) / (x + 1))^(2j+1) / (2j+1).
naturalLogPartial :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalLogPartial reals x zero =
  StandardRealAnalysis.zeroR reals
naturalLogPartial reals x (suc count) =
  StandardRealAnalysis.add reals
    (naturalLogPartial reals x count)
    (StandardRealAnalysis.multiply reals
      (StandardRealAnalysis.fromNat reals (suc (suc zero)))
      (divide reals
        (power reals
          (divide reals
            (subtract reals x (StandardRealAnalysis.oneR reals))
            (StandardRealAnalysis.add reals
              x
              (StandardRealAnalysis.oneR reals)))
          (suc (count + count)))
        (StandardRealAnalysis.fromNat reals (suc (count + count)))))

NaturalLogValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
NaturalLogValue reals x value =
  Both
    (StrictLess reals (StandardRealAnalysis.zeroR reals) x)
    (SequentialLimit reals (naturalLogPartial reals x) value)

primeNumberRatio :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
primeNumberRatio reals n logarithm =
  divide reals
    (StandardRealAnalysis.fromNat reals (primeCount n))
    (divide reals
      (StandardRealAnalysis.fromNat reals n)
      logarithm)

the-prime-number-theorem : Set₁
the-prime-number-theorem =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (StandardRealAnalysis.zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <= n ->
      Exists R
        (\ logarithm ->
          Both
            (NaturalLogValue reals
              (StandardRealAnalysis.fromNat reals n)
              logarithm)
            (StrictLess reals
              (StandardRealAnalysis.absoluteValue reals
                (subtract reals
                  (primeNumberRatio reals n logarithm)
                  (StandardRealAnalysis.oneR reals)))
              epsilon)))

  Theorems item 005: the ratio of the number of primes at most n to
  n / log(n) converges to 1. This file contains no proof.

  database. In particular, ppi is the real prime-counting function defined by
  df-ppi, log is the natural logarithm, and RR and NN0 are the standard real
  and nonnegative-integer classes.

  The assertion is the epsilon-N expansion of the sequential limit in the
  source theorem: for every positive real error e, all natural n beyond some
  natural threshold m make the absolute difference from 1 smaller than e.
  Since df-ppi counts the primes less than or equal to its argument, ppi at a
  natural n is definitionally the source numerator. The final declaration is
  an unproved $a statement.
$)

hundred-theorems-005-prime-number-theorem $a
  |- A. e e. RR
       ( 0 < e ->
         E. m e. NN0
           A. n e. NN0
             ( m <_ n ->
               ( abs ` ( ( ( ppi ` n ) / ( n / ( log ` n ) ) ) - 1 ) )
                 < e ) ) )
