module

public import Mathlib.Probability.IdentDistrib
public import Mathlib.Probability.Independence.Integrable
public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DominatedConvergence
public import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.FloorPow
public import Mathlib.Analysis.PSeries
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Asymptotics.SpecificAsymptotics

/-!
# The strong law of large numbers

We prove the strong law of large numbers, in `ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae`:
If `X n` is a sequence of independent identically distributed integrable random
variables, then `∑ i ∈ range n, X i / n` converges almost surely to `𝔼[X 0]`.
We give here the strong version, due to Etemadi, that only requires pairwise independence.

This file also contains the Lᵖ version of the strong law of large numbers provided by
`ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_Lp` which shows `∑ i ∈ range n, X i / n` converges in Lᵖ to
`𝔼[X 0]` provided `X n` is independent identically distributed and is Lᵖ.

## Implementation

The main point is to prove the result for real-valued random variables, as the general case
of Banach-space-valued random variables follows from this case and approximation by simple
functions. The real version is given in `ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae_real`.

We follow the proof by Etemadi
[Etemadi, *An elementary proof of the strong law of large numbers*][etemadi_strong_law],
which goes as follows.

It suffices to prove the result for nonnegative `X`, as one can prove the general result by
splitting a general `X` into its positive part and negative part.
Consider `Xₙ` a sequence of nonnegative integrable identically distributed pairwise independent
random variables. Let `Yₙ` be the truncation of `Xₙ` up to `n`. We claim that
* Almost surely, `Xₙ = Yₙ` for all but finitely many indices. Indeed, `∑ ℙ (Xₙ ≠ Yₙ)` is bounded by
  `1 + 𝔼[X]` (see `sum_prob_mem_Ioc_le` and `tsum_prob_mem_Ioi_lt_top`).
* Let `c > 1`. Along the sequence `n = c ^ k`, then `(∑_{i=0}^{n-1} Yᵢ - 𝔼[Yᵢ])/n` converges almost
  surely to `0`. This follows from a variance control, as
```
  ∑_k ℙ (|∑_{i=0}^{c^k - 1} Yᵢ - 𝔼[Yᵢ]| > c^k ε)
    ≤ ∑_k (c^k ε)^{-2} ∑_{i=0}^{c^k - 1} Var[Yᵢ]    (by Markov inequality)
    ≤ ∑_i (C/i^2) Var[Yᵢ]                           (as ∑_{c^k > i} 1/(c^k)^2 ≤ C/i^2)
    ≤ ∑_i (C/i^2) 𝔼[Yᵢ^2]
    ≤ 2C 𝔼[X^2]                                     (see `sum_variance_truncation_le`)
```
* As `𝔼[Yᵢ]` converges to `𝔼[X]`, it follows from the two previous items and Cesàro that, along
  the sequence `n = c^k`, one has `(∑_{i=0}^{n-1} Xᵢ) / n → 𝔼[X]` almost surely.
* To generalize it to all indices, we use the fact that `∑_{i=0}^{n-1} Xᵢ` is nondecreasing and
  that, if `c` is close enough to `1`, the gap between `c^k` and `c^(k+1)` is small.
-/

@[expose] public section


noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Filter Finset Asymptotics

open Set (indicator)

open scoped Topology MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory ENNReal NNReal

open scoped Function -- required for scoped `on` notation

namespace ProbabilityTheory

/-! ### Prerequisites on truncations -/


section Truncation

variable {α : Type*}

/-- Truncating a real-valued function to the interval `(-A, A]`. -/
def truncation (f : α → ℝ) (A : ℝ) :=
  indicator (Set.Ioc (-A) A) id ∘ f

variable {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} {f : α → ℝ}

theorem _root_.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.truncation (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ)
    {A : ℝ} : AEStronglyMeasurable (truncation f A) μ := by sorry
theorem abs_truncation_le_bound (f : α → ℝ) (A : ℝ) (x : α) : |truncation f A x| ≤ |A| := by sorry
theorem truncation_zero (f : α → ℝ) : truncation f 0 = 0 := by simp [truncation]; rfl

theorem abs_truncation_le_abs_self (f : α → ℝ) (A : ℝ) (x : α) : |truncation f A x| ≤ |f x| := by sorry
theorem truncation_eq_self {f : α → ℝ} {A : ℝ} {x : α} (h : |f x| < A) :
    truncation f A x = f x := by sorry
theorem truncation_eq_of_nonneg {f : α → ℝ} {A : ℝ} (h : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) :
    truncation f A = indicator (Set.Ioc 0 A) id ∘ f := by sorry
theorem truncation_nonneg {f : α → ℝ} (A : ℝ) {x : α} (h : 0 ≤ f x) : 0 ≤ truncation f A x :=
  Set.indicator_apply_nonneg fun _ => h

theorem _root_.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.memLp_truncation [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) {A : ℝ} {p : ℝ≥0∞} : MemLp (truncation f A) p μ :=
  MemLp.of_bound hf.truncation |A| (Eventually.of_forall fun _ => abs_truncation_le_bound _ _ _)

theorem _root_.MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.integrable_truncation [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) {A : ℝ} : Integrable (truncation f A) μ := by sorry
theorem moment_truncation_eq_intervalIntegral (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) {A : ℝ} (hA : 0 ≤ A)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : ∫ x, truncation f A x ^ n ∂μ = ∫ y in -A..A, y ^ n ∂Measure.map f μ := by sorry
theorem moment_truncation_eq_intervalIntegral_of_nonneg (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) {A : ℝ}
    {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (h'f : 0 ≤ f) :
    ∫ x, truncation f A x ^ n ∂μ = ∫ y in 0..A, y ^ n ∂Measure.map f μ := by sorry
theorem integral_truncation_eq_intervalIntegral (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) {A : ℝ}
    (hA : 0 ≤ A) : ∫ x, truncation f A x ∂μ = ∫ y in -A..A, y ∂Measure.map f μ := by sorry
theorem integral_truncation_eq_intervalIntegral_of_nonneg (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) {A : ℝ}
    (h'f : 0 ≤ f) : ∫ x, truncation f A x ∂μ = ∫ y in 0..A, y ∂Measure.map f μ := by sorry
theorem integral_truncation_le_integral_of_nonneg (hf : Integrable f μ) (h'f : 0 ≤ f) {A : ℝ} :
    ∫ x, truncation f A x ∂μ ≤ ∫ x, f x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem tendsto_integral_truncation {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f μ) :
    Tendsto (fun A => ∫ x, truncation f A x ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂μ)) := by sorry
theorem IdentDistrib.truncation {β : Type*} [MeasurableSpace β] {ν : Measure β} {f : α → ℝ}
    {g : β → ℝ} (h : IdentDistrib f g μ ν) {A : ℝ} :
    IdentDistrib (truncation f A) (truncation g A) μ ν :=
  h.comp (measurable_id.indicator measurableSet_Ioc)

end Truncation

section StrongLawAeReal

variable {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]

section MomentEstimates

theorem sum_prob_mem_Ioc_le {X : Ω → ℝ} (hint : Integrable X) (hnonneg : 0 ≤ X) {K : ℕ} {N : ℕ}
    (hKN : K ≤ N) :
    ∑ j ∈ range K, ℙ {ω | X ω ∈ Set.Ioc (j : ℝ) N} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (𝔼[X] + 1) := by sorry
theorem tsum_prob_mem_Ioi_lt_top {X : Ω → ℝ} (hint : Integrable X) (hnonneg : 0 ≤ X) :
    (∑' j : ℕ, ℙ {ω | X ω ∈ Set.Ioi (j : ℝ)}) < ∞ := by sorry
theorem sum_variance_truncation_le {X : Ω → ℝ} (hint : Integrable X) (hnonneg : 0 ≤ X) (K : ℕ) :
    ∑ j ∈ range K, ((j : ℝ) ^ 2)⁻¹ * 𝔼[truncation X j ^ 2] ≤ 2 * 𝔼[X] := by sorry
end MomentEstimates

/-! Proof of the strong law of large numbers (almost sure version, assuming only
pairwise independence) for nonnegative random variables, following Etemadi's proof. -/
section StrongLawNonneg

variable (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (hint : Integrable (X 0))
  (hindep : Pairwise (IndepFun on X)) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0))
  (hnonneg : ∀ i ω, 0 ≤ X i ω)

include hint hindep hident hnonneg in
/-- The truncation of `Xᵢ` up to `i` satisfies the strong law of large numbers (with respect to
the truncated expectation) along the sequence `c^n`, for any `c > 1`, up to a given `ε > 0`.
This follows from a variance control. -/
theorem strong_law_aux1 {c : ℝ} (c_one : 1 < c) {ε : ℝ} (εpos : 0 < ε) : ∀ᵐ ω, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, := by sorry
theorem strong_law_aux2 {c : ℝ} (c_one : 1 < c) :
    ∀ᵐ ω, (fun n : ℕ => ∑ i ∈ range ⌊c ^ n⌋₊, truncation (X i) i ω -
      𝔼[∑ i ∈ range ⌊c ^ n⌋₊, truncation (X i) i]) =o[atTop] fun n : ℕ => (⌊c ^ n⌋₊ : ℝ) := by sorry
theorem strong_law_aux3 :
    (fun n => 𝔼[∑ i ∈ range n, truncation (X i) i] - n * 𝔼[X 0]) =o[atTop] ((↑) : ℕ → ℝ) := by sorry
theorem strong_law_aux4 {c : ℝ} (c_one : 1 < c) :
    ∀ᵐ ω, (fun n : ℕ => ∑ i ∈ range ⌊c ^ n⌋₊, truncation (X i) i ω - ⌊c ^ n⌋₊ * 𝔼[X 0]) =o[atTop]
    fun n : ℕ => (⌊c ^ n⌋₊ : ℝ) := by sorry
theorem strong_law_aux5 :
    ∀ᵐ ω, (fun n : ℕ => ∑ i ∈ range n, truncation (X i) i ω - ∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω) =o[atTop]
    fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) := by sorry
theorem strong_law_aux6 {c : ℝ} (c_one : 1 < c) :
    ∀ᵐ ω, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (∑ i ∈ range ⌊c ^ n⌋₊, X i ω) / ⌊c ^ n⌋₊) atTop (𝓝 𝔼[X 0]) := by sorry
theorem strong_law_aux7 :
    ∀ᵐ ω, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω) / n) atTop (𝓝 𝔼[X 0]) := by sorry
end StrongLawNonneg

/-- **Strong law of large numbers**, almost sure version: if `X n` is a sequence of independent
identically distributed integrable real-valued random variables, then `∑ i ∈ range n, X i / n`
converges almost surely to `𝔼[X 0]`. We give here the strong version, due to Etemadi, that only
requires pairwise independence. Superseded by `strong_law_ae`, which works for random variables
taking values in any Banach space. -/
theorem strong_law_ae_real {Ω : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω}
    (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (hint : Integrable (X 0) μ)
    (hindep : Pairwise ((· ⟂ᵢ[μ] ·) on X))
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω) / n) atTop (𝓝 μ[X 0]) := by sorry
end StrongLawAeReal

section StrongLawVectorSpace

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
  [MeasurableSpace E]

open Set TopologicalSpace

/-- Preliminary lemma for the strong law of large numbers for vector-valued random variables:
the composition of the random variables with a simple function satisfies the strong law of large
numbers. -/
lemma strong_law_ae_simpleFunc_comp (X : ℕ → Ω → E) (h' : Measurable (X 0))
    (hindep : Pairwise ((· ⟂ᵢ[μ] ·) on X))
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) (φ : SimpleFunc E E) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ,
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ • (∑ i ∈ range n, φ (X i ω))) atTop (𝓝 μ[φ ∘ (X 0)]) := by sorry
variable [BorelSpace E]

/-- Preliminary lemma for the strong law of large numbers for vector-valued random variables,
assuming measurability in addition to integrability. This is weakened to ae measurability in
the full version `ProbabilityTheory.strong_law_ae`. -/
lemma strong_law_ae_of_measurable
    (X : ℕ → Ω → E) (hint : Integrable (X 0) μ) (h' : StronglyMeasurable (X 0))
    (hindep : Pairwise ((· ⟂ᵢ[μ] ·) on X))
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ • (∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω)) atTop (𝓝 μ[X 0]) := by sorry
theorem strong_law_ae (X : ℕ → Ω → E) (hint : Integrable (X 0) μ)
    (hindep : Pairwise ((· ⟂ᵢ[μ] ·) on X))
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ • (∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω)) atTop (𝓝 μ[X 0]) := by sorry
end StrongLawVectorSpace

section StrongLawLp

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω}
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

/-- **Strong law of large numbers**, Lᵖ version: if `X n` is a sequence of independent
identically distributed random variables in Lᵖ, then `n⁻¹ • ∑ i ∈ range n, X i`
converges in `Lᵖ` to `𝔼[X 0]`. -/
theorem strong_law_Lp {p : ℝ≥0∞} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≠ ∞) (X : ℕ → Ω → E)
    (hℒp : MemLp (X 0) p μ) (hindep : Pairwise ((· ⟂ᵢ[μ] ·) on X))
    (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) :
    Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) => eLpNorm (fun ω => (n : ℝ)⁻¹ • (∑ i ∈ range n, X i ω) - μ[X 0]) p μ)
      atTop (𝓝 0) := by sorry
end StrongLawLp

end ProbabilityTheory

title: 059_the_laws_of_large_numbers
content:
(*
  The strong law of large numbers for independent, identically distributed
  integrable real random variables.  These are the two indexed statements
  from the retained probability-library development.
*)

Require Import Lra Lia Reals RealAdd RandomVariableL2 Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Require Import Morphisms FiniteType List ListAdd Permutation infprod Almost NumberIso.
Require Import Sums SimpleExpectation PushNeg.
Require Import EquivDec Classical ClassicalChoice.
Require Import IndefiniteDescription ClassicalDescription.
Require Import BorelSigmaAlgebra utils.Utils ConditionalExpectation.
Require Import Independence sumtest Dynkin Measures.

Set Bullet Behavior "Strict Subproofs".
Set Default Goal Selector "!".

Section StrongLaw.

Context {Ts : Type} {dom : SigmaAlgebra Ts} {Prts : ProbSpace dom}.

Lemma strong_law_zero_mean
    (X : nat -> Ts -> R)
    {rv : forall n, RandomVariable dom borel_sa (X n)}
    {isfe : forall n, IsFiniteExpectation Prts (X n)} :
  (forall n, FiniteExpectation Prts (X n) = 0) ->
  iid_rv_collection Prts borel_sa X ->
  almost Prts
    (fun omega =>
       is_lim_seq
         (fun n => (rvsum X n omega) / INR (S n))
         0).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma strong_law
    (X : nat -> Ts -> R) (mu : R)
    {rv : forall n, RandomVariable dom borel_sa (X n)}
    {isfe : forall n, IsFiniteExpectation Prts (X n)} :
  (forall n, FiniteExpectation Prts (X n) = mu) ->
  iid_rv_collection Prts borel_sa X ->
  almost Prts
    (fun omega =>
       is_lim_seq
         (fun n => (rvsum X n omega) / INR (S n))
         mu).
Proof.
Admitted.

End StrongLaw.

title: 059_the_laws_of_large_numbers
content:
(*
   File:     Laws_of_Large_Numbers.thy
   Author:   Manuel Eberl, TU München
*)
section \<open>The Laws of Large Numbers\<close>
theory Laws_of_Large_Numbers
  imports Ergodic_Theory.Shift_Operator
begin

text \<open>
  We prove the strong law of large numbers in the following form: Let $(X_i)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$
  be a sequence of i.i.d. random variables over a probability space \<open>M\<close>. Further assume that
  the expected value $E[X_0]$ of $X_0$ exists. Then the sequence of random variables
  \[\overline{X}_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=0}^n X_i\]
  of running averages almost surely converges to $E[X_0]$.
  This means that
  \[\mathcal{P}[\overline{X}_n \longrightarrow E[X_0]] = 1\ .\]

  We start with the strong law.
\<close>


subsection \<open>The strong law\<close>

text \<open>
  The proof uses Birkhoff's Theorem from Gouëzel's formalisation of ergodic theory~\<^cite>\<open>"gouezel"\<close>
  and the fact that the shift operator $T(x_1, x_2, x_3, \ldots) = (x_2, x_3, \ldots)$ is ergodic.
  This proof can be found in various textbooks on probability theory/ergodic
  theory, e.g. the ones by Krengel~\<^cite>\<open>\<open>p.~24\<close> in "krengel"\<close> and
  Simmonet~\<^cite>\<open>\<open>Chapter 15, pp.~311--325\<close> in "Simonnet1996"\<close>.
\<close>
theorem (in prob_space) strong_law_of_large_numbers_iid:
  fixes X :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real"
  assumes indep: "indep_vars (\<lambda>_. borel) X UNIV"
  assumes distr: "\<And>i. distr M borel (X i) = distr M borel (X 0)"
  assumes L1:    "integrable M (X 0)"
  shows "AE x in M. (\<lambda>n. (\<Sum>i<n. X i x) / n) \<longlonglongrightarrow> expectation (X 0)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>The weak law\<close>

text \<open>
  To go from the strong law to the weak one, we need the fact that almost sure convergence
  implies convergence in probability. We prove this for sequences of random variables here.
\<close>
lemma (in prob_space) AE_convergence_imp_convergence_in_prob:
  assumes [measurable]: "\<And>i. random_variable borel (X i)" "random_variable borel Y"
  assumes AE: "AE x in M. (\<lambda>i. X i x) \<longlonglongrightarrow> Y x"
  assumes "\<epsilon> > (0 :: real)"
  shows   "(\<lambda>i. prob {x\<in>space M. \<bar>X i x - Y x\<bar> > \<epsilon>}) \<longlonglongrightarrow> 0"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  The weak law is now a simple corollary: we again have the same setting as before. The weak
  law now states that $\overline{X}_n$ converges to $E[X_0]$ in probability. This means that
  for any \<open>\<epsilon> > 0\<close>, the probability that $|\overline{X}_n - X_0| > \varepsilon$ vanishes as
  \<open>n \<rightarrow> \<infinity>\<close>.
\<close>
corollary (in prob_space) weak_law_of_large_numbers_iid:
  fixes X :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real" and \<epsilon> :: real
  assumes indep: "indep_vars (\<lambda>_. borel) X UNIV"
  assumes distr: "\<And>i. distr M borel (X i) = distr M borel (X 0)"
  assumes L1:    "integrable M (X 0)"
  assumes "\<epsilon> > 0"
  shows   "(\<lambda>n. prob {x\<in>space M. \<bar>(\<Sum>i<n. X i x) / n - expectation (X 0)\<bar> > \<epsilon>}) \<longlonglongrightarrow> 0"
  by sorry

end

title: 059_the_laws_of_large_numbers
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "The Laws of Large Numbers" from Hundred
  Theorems artifact 059 (hundred-theorems__hol-light__059). It states the
  strong law for a sequence of pairwise independent, identically distributed,
  integrable real random variables: their sample averages converge almost
  surely to the common expectation. This file contains no proof.
*)

let HUNDRED_THEOREMS_059_STRONG_LAW_OF_LARGE_NUMBERS =
 `let seq_tends =
      \(u:num->real) l.
        !e. &0 < e ==> ?N. !n. N <= n ==> abs(u n - l) < e in
   let probability_space =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (p:(A->bool)->real).
        (!s. s IN events ==> s SUBSET carrier) /\
        {} IN events /\
        carrier IN events /\
        (!s. s IN events ==> carrier DIFF s IN events) /\
        (!sets:num->A->bool.
           (!n. sets n IN events)
           ==> {a:A | ?n. a IN sets n} IN events) /\
        p {} = &0 /\
        p carrier = &1 /\
        (!s. s IN events ==> &0 <= p s) /\
        (!sets:num->A->bool.
           (!n. sets n IN events) /\
           (!m n. ~(m = n) ==> DISJOINT (sets m) (sets n))
           ==> seq_tends
                 (\n. sum {k:num | k < n} (\k. p (sets k)))
                 (p {a:A | ?k. a IN sets k})) in
   let random_variable =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool) (Y:A->real).
        !x. {a:A | a IN carrier /\ Y a <= x} IN events in
   let pairwise_independent =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (p:(A->bool)->real) (X:num->A->real).
        (!n. random_variable carrier events (X n)) /\
        (!i j s t. ~(i = j)
           ==> p {a:A | a IN carrier /\ X i a <= s /\ X j a <= t} =
               p {a:A | a IN carrier /\ X i a <= s} *
               p {a:A | a IN carrier /\ X j a <= t}) in
   let identically_distributed =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (p:(A->bool)->real) (X:num->A->real).
        !n t.
          p {a:A | a IN carrier /\ X n a <= t} =
          p {a:A | a IN carrier /\ X 0 a <= t} in
   let nonnegative_expectation =
      \(p:(A->bool)->real) (carrier:A->bool) (Y:A->real) e.
        (!a. a IN carrier ==> &0 <= Y a) /\
        seq_tends
          (\n. inv(&(2 EXP n)) *
               sum {k:num | 1 <= k /\ k <= n * 2 EXP n}
                 (\k. p {a:A | a IN carrier /\
                                  &k / &(2 EXP n) <= Y a}))
          e in
   let has_expectation =
      \(p:(A->bool)->real) (carrier:A->bool) (Y:A->real) e.
        ?ep en.
          nonnegative_expectation p carrier
            (\a. if &0 <= Y a then Y a else &0) ep /\
          nonnegative_expectation p carrier
            (\a. if Y a < &0 then --(Y a) else &0) en /\
          e = ep - en in
   let integrable =
      \(p:(A->bool)->real) (carrier:A->bool) (Y:A->real).
        ?e. has_expectation p carrier Y e in
   let expectation =
      \(p:(A->bool)->real) (carrier:A->bool) (Y:A->real).
        @e. has_expectation p carrier Y e in
   let almost_surely =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (p:(A->bool)->real) (P:A->bool).
        ?negligible:A->bool.
          negligible IN events /\
          p negligible = &0 /\
          {a:A | a IN carrier /\ ~(P a)} SUBSET negligible in
   !carrier:A->bool
    events:(A->bool)->bool
    p:(A->bool)->real
    X:num->A->real.
      probability_space carrier events p /\
      pairwise_independent carrier events p X /\
      identically_distributed carrier p X /\
      integrable p carrier (X 0)
      ==> almost_surely carrier events p
            (\a. seq_tends
                   (\n. inv(&n) *
                        sum {i:num | i < n} (\i. X i a))
                   (expectation p carrier (X 0)))`;;

title: 059_the_laws_of_large_numbers
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems corpus artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__059, "The Laws of Large Numbers": pairwise
;; independent, identically distributed, integrable real random variables
;; have sample averages converging almost surely to their common expectation.
;; This file contains no proof.
;;
;; Semantic status: the direct DEFUN-SK rewrite below repairs the former
;; vacuous generated-lambda quantifiers, but standard ACL2 still ranges only
;; over coded events, random variables, and scalar values. It cannot preserve
;; the source's unrestricted real probability-space semantics and is not
;; counted as a faithful translation.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Function objects present the scalar operations, event operations, and
;; random-variable family. All mathematical quantifiers below are DEFUN-SK
;; quantifiers over ordinary ACL2 objects; no generated lambda calls an
;; unwarranted user function.

(defun ht059-apply1 (function x)
  (apply$ function (list x)))

(defun ht059-apply2 (function x y)
  (apply$ function (list x y)))

(defun ht059-apply3 (function x y z)
  (apply$ function (list x y z)))

(defun ht059-scalar-p (carrier x)
  (if (ht059-apply1 carrier x) t nil))

(defun ht059-sample-p (sample-carrier omega)
  (if (ht059-apply1 sample-carrier omega) t nil))

(defun ht059-less-p (less x y)
  (if (ht059-apply2 less x y) t nil))

(defun ht059-leq-p (less x y)
  (not (ht059-less-p less y x)))

(defun ht059-add (add x y)
  (ht059-apply2 add x y))

(defun ht059-mul (multiply x y)
  (ht059-apply2 multiply x y))

(defun ht059-neg (negate x)
  (ht059-apply1 negate x))

(defun ht059-sub (add negate x y)
  (ht059-add add x (ht059-neg negate y)))

(defun ht059-inv (inverse x)
  (ht059-apply1 inverse x))

(defun ht059-div (multiply inverse x y)
  (ht059-mul multiply x (ht059-inv inverse y)))

(defun ht059-abs (less negate zero x)
  (if (ht059-less-p less x zero)
      (ht059-neg negate x)
    x))

(defun ht059-max (less x y)
  (if (ht059-less-p less x y) y x))

(defun ht059-real-nat (add zero one n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (ht059-add
     add one
     (ht059-real-nat add zero one (1- n)))))

;; The scalar carrier is an Archimedean Dedekind-complete ordered field.

(defun-sk ht059-field-laws-p
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier x)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier y)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier z))
     (and
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier (ht059-add add x y))
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier (ht059-mul multiply x y))
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier (ht059-neg negate x))
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier (ht059-inv inverse x))
      (equal
       (ht059-add add (ht059-add add x y) z)
       (ht059-add add x (ht059-add add y z)))
      (equal (ht059-add add x y) (ht059-add add y x))
      (equal (ht059-add add x zero) x)
      (equal (ht059-add add x (ht059-neg negate x)) zero)
      (equal
       (ht059-mul multiply (ht059-mul multiply x y) z)
       (ht059-mul multiply x (ht059-mul multiply y z)))
      (equal (ht059-mul multiply x y) (ht059-mul multiply y x))
      (equal (ht059-mul multiply x one) x)
      (implies
       (equal x zero)
       (equal (ht059-inv inverse x) zero))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal (ht059-mul multiply x (ht059-inv inverse x)) one))
      (equal
       (ht059-mul multiply x (ht059-add add y z))
       (ht059-add
        add
        (ht059-mul multiply x y)
        (ht059-mul multiply x z)))))))

(defun-sk ht059-order-laws-p
    (carrier zero add multiply less)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier x)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier y)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier z))
     (and
      (not (ht059-less-p less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (ht059-less-p less x y)
       (ht059-less-p less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht059-less-p less x y)
        (ht059-less-p less y z))
       (ht059-less-p less x z))
      (implies
       (ht059-less-p less x y)
       (ht059-less-p
        less
        (ht059-add add x z)
        (ht059-add add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht059-less-p less zero x)
        (ht059-less-p less zero y))
       (ht059-less-p less zero (ht059-mul multiply x y)))))))

(defun-sk ht059-real-set-nonempty-p (carrier set)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (ht059-scalar-p carrier x)
     (ht059-apply1 set x))))

(defun-sk ht059-real-set-upper-bound-p (carrier less set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier x)
      (ht059-apply1 set x))
     (ht059-leq-p less x bound))))

(defun-sk ht059-real-set-bounded-above-p (carrier less set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (ht059-scalar-p carrier bound)
     (ht059-real-set-upper-bound-p carrier less set bound))))

(defun-sk ht059-real-set-least-upper-bound-p
    (carrier less set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier bound)
      (ht059-real-set-upper-bound-p carrier less set bound))
     (ht059-leq-p less supremum bound))))

(defun ht059-real-set-supremum-p
    (carrier less set supremum)
  (and
   (ht059-scalar-p carrier supremum)
   (ht059-real-set-upper-bound-p carrier less set supremum)
   (ht059-real-set-least-upper-bound-p
    carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk ht059-real-set-has-supremum-p (carrier less set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (ht059-real-set-supremum-p
     carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk ht059-dedekind-complete-p (carrier less)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (ht059-real-set-nonempty-p carrier set)
      (ht059-real-set-bounded-above-p carrier less set))
     (ht059-real-set-has-supremum-p carrier less set))))

(defun-sk ht059-archimedean-witness-p
    (carrier add zero one less x)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (natp n)
     (ht059-less-p
      less x (ht059-real-nat add zero one n)))))

(defun-sk ht059-archimedean-p
    (carrier add zero one less)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (ht059-scalar-p carrier x)
     (ht059-archimedean-witness-p
      carrier add zero one less x))))

(defun ht059-real-field-p
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp multiply)
   (tamep-functionp negate)
   (tamep-functionp inverse)
   (tamep-functionp less)
   (ht059-scalar-p carrier zero)
   (ht059-scalar-p carrier one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (ht059-less-p less zero one)
   (ht059-field-laws-p
    carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse)
   (ht059-order-laws-p
    carrier zero add multiply less)
   (ht059-dedekind-complete-p carrier less)
   (ht059-archimedean-p carrier add zero one less)))

;; Events are first-order event codes with an explicit membership relation.
;; The closure operations state their extensional meaning, so no event is
;; represented by a generated lambda.

(defun ht059-event-p (events event)
  (if (ht059-apply1 events event) t nil))

(defun ht059-in-event-p (event-member event omega)
  (if (ht059-apply2 event-member event omega) t nil))

(defun ht059-sequence-event
    (sequence-value sequence index)
  (ht059-apply2 sequence-value sequence index))

(defun-sk ht059-events-contained-p
    (sample-carrier events event-member)
  (forall (event omega)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-event-p events event)
      (ht059-in-event-p event-member event omega))
     (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega))))

(defun-sk ht059-empty-full-events-p
    (sample-carrier event-member empty-event full-event)
  (forall (omega)
    (implies
     (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega)
     (and
      (not
       (ht059-in-event-p event-member empty-event omega))
      (ht059-in-event-p event-member full-event omega)))))

(defun-sk ht059-complement-closure-p
    (events complement-event)
  (forall (event)
    (implies
     (ht059-event-p events event)
     (ht059-event-p
      events (ht059-apply1 complement-event event)))))

(defun-sk ht059-complement-membership-p
    (sample-carrier events event-member complement-event)
  (forall (event omega)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-event-p events event)
      (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega))
     (iff
      (ht059-in-event-p
       event-member
       (ht059-apply1 complement-event event)
       omega)
      (not (ht059-in-event-p event-member event omega))))))

(defun-sk ht059-intersection-closure-p
    (events intersection-event)
  (forall (left right)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-event-p events left)
      (ht059-event-p events right))
     (ht059-event-p
      events
      (ht059-apply2 intersection-event left right)))))

(defun-sk ht059-intersection-membership-p
    (sample-carrier events event-member intersection-event)
  (forall (left right omega)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-event-p events left)
      (ht059-event-p events right)
      (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega))
     (iff
      (ht059-in-event-p
       event-member
       (ht059-apply2 intersection-event left right)
       omega)
      (and
       (ht059-in-event-p event-member left omega)
       (ht059-in-event-p event-member right omega))))))

(defun-sk ht059-event-sequence-p
    (events sequence-value sequence)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (natp index)
     (ht059-event-p
      events
      (ht059-sequence-event
       sequence-value sequence index)))))

(defun-sk ht059-point-in-sequence-union-p
    (sequence-value event-member sequence omega)
  (exists (index)
    (and
     (natp index)
     (ht059-in-event-p
      event-member
      (ht059-sequence-event
       sequence-value sequence index)
      omega))))

(defun-sk ht059-countable-union-closure-p
    (events sequence-value countable-union-event)
  (forall (sequence)
    (implies
     (ht059-event-sequence-p events sequence-value sequence)
     (ht059-event-p
      events
      (ht059-apply1 countable-union-event sequence)))))

(defun-sk ht059-countable-union-membership-p
    (sample-carrier events event-member sequence-value
                    countable-union-event)
  (forall (sequence omega)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-event-sequence-p
       events sequence-value sequence)
      (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega))
     (iff
      (ht059-in-event-p
       event-member
       (ht059-apply1 countable-union-event sequence)
       omega)
      (ht059-point-in-sequence-union-p
       sequence-value event-member sequence omega)))))

(defun ht059-sigma-algebra-p
    (sample-carrier events event-member empty-event full-event
                    complement-event intersection-event
                    sequence-value countable-union-event)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp sample-carrier)
   (tamep-functionp events)
   (tamep-functionp event-member)
   (tamep-functionp complement-event)
   (tamep-functionp intersection-event)
   (tamep-functionp sequence-value)
   (tamep-functionp countable-union-event)
   (ht059-event-p events empty-event)
   (ht059-event-p events full-event)
   (ht059-events-contained-p
    sample-carrier events event-member)
   (ht059-empty-full-events-p
    sample-carrier event-member empty-event full-event)
   (ht059-complement-closure-p events complement-event)
   (ht059-complement-membership-p
    sample-carrier events event-member complement-event)
   (ht059-intersection-closure-p events intersection-event)
   (ht059-intersection-membership-p
    sample-carrier events event-member intersection-event)
   (ht059-countable-union-closure-p
    events sequence-value countable-union-event)
   (ht059-countable-union-membership-p
    sample-carrier events event-member sequence-value
    countable-union-event)))

(defun-sk ht059-events-equivalent-p
    (sample-carrier event-member left right)
  (forall (omega)
    (implies
     (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega)
     (iff
      (ht059-in-event-p event-member left omega)
      (ht059-in-event-p event-member right omega)))))

(defun-sk ht059-measure-extensional-p
    (sample-carrier events event-member measure)
  (forall (left right)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-event-p events left)
      (ht059-event-p events right)
      (ht059-events-equivalent-p
       sample-carrier event-member left right))
     (equal
      (ht059-apply1 measure left)
      (ht059-apply1 measure right)))))

(defun-sk ht059-measure-values-p
    (carrier zero less events measure)
  (forall (event)
    (implies
     (ht059-event-p events event)
     (and
      (ht059-scalar-p
       carrier (ht059-apply1 measure event))
      (ht059-leq-p
       less zero (ht059-apply1 measure event))))))

(defun-sk ht059-events-disjoint-p
    (sample-carrier event-member left right)
  (forall (omega)
    (implies
     (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega)
     (not
      (and
       (ht059-in-event-p event-member left omega)
       (ht059-in-event-p event-member right omega))))))

(defun-sk ht059-event-sequence-pairwise-disjoint-p
    (sample-carrier event-member sequence-value sequence)
  (forall (left-index right-index)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp left-index)
      (natp right-index)
      (not (equal left-index right-index)))
     (ht059-events-disjoint-p
      sample-carrier event-member
      (ht059-sequence-event
       sequence-value sequence left-index)
      (ht059-sequence-event
       sequence-value sequence right-index)))))

(defun ht059-measure-prefix
    (measure sequence-value sequence add zero count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (let ((index (1- count)))
      (ht059-add
       add
       (ht059-measure-prefix
        measure sequence-value sequence add zero index)
       (ht059-apply1
        measure
        (ht059-sequence-event
         sequence-value sequence index))))))

(defun-sk ht059-measure-prefix-tail-p
    (measure sequence-value sequence total
             add negate zero less epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (count)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp count)
      (natp cutoff)
      (<= cutoff count))
     (ht059-less-p
      less
      (ht059-abs
       less negate zero
       (ht059-sub
        add negate
        (ht059-measure-prefix
         measure sequence-value sequence add zero count)
        total))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht059-measure-prefix-cutoff-exists-p
    (measure sequence-value sequence total
             add negate zero less epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (ht059-measure-prefix-tail-p
      measure sequence-value sequence total
      add negate zero less epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk ht059-measure-prefix-converges-p
    (carrier measure sequence-value sequence total
             add negate zero less)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier epsilon)
      (ht059-less-p less zero epsilon))
     (ht059-measure-prefix-cutoff-exists-p
      measure sequence-value sequence total
      add negate zero less epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht059-countable-additivity-p
    (carrier add negate zero less
             sample-carrier events event-member
             sequence-value countable-union-event measure)
  (forall (sequence)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-event-sequence-p
       events sequence-value sequence)
      (ht059-event-sequence-pairwise-disjoint-p
       sample-carrier event-member sequence-value sequence))
     (ht059-measure-prefix-converges-p
      carrier measure sequence-value sequence
      (ht059-apply1
       measure
       (ht059-apply1 countable-union-event sequence))
      add negate zero less))))

(defun ht059-probability-space-p
    (carrier zero one add negate less
             sample-carrier events event-member
             empty-event full-event complement-event intersection-event
             sequence-value countable-union-event measure)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp measure)
   (ht059-sigma-algebra-p
    sample-carrier events event-member empty-event full-event
    complement-event intersection-event
    sequence-value countable-union-event)
   (ht059-measure-values-p
    carrier zero less events measure)
   (ht059-measure-extensional-p
    sample-carrier events event-member measure)
   (equal (ht059-apply1 measure empty-event) zero)
   (equal (ht059-apply1 measure full-event) one)
   (ht059-countable-additivity-p
    carrier add negate zero less
    sample-carrier events event-member
    sequence-value countable-union-event measure)))

;; Upper-ray events characterize measurability, equality in distribution,
;; and pairwise independence for real-valued random variables.

(defun-sk ht059-family-values-p
    (carrier sample-carrier x-family)
  (forall (index omega)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega))
     (ht059-scalar-p
      carrier (ht059-apply2 x-family index omega)))))

(defun-sk ht059-ray-event-closure-p
    (carrier events ray-event)
  (forall (index threshold)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier threshold))
     (ht059-event-p
      events (ht059-apply2 ray-event index threshold)))))

(defun-sk ht059-ray-event-membership-p
    (carrier sample-carrier event-member x-family ray-event less)
  (forall (index threshold omega)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier threshold)
      (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega))
     (iff
      (ht059-in-event-p
       event-member
       (ht059-apply2 ray-event index threshold)
       omega)
      (ht059-less-p
       less
       (ht059-apply2 x-family index omega)
       threshold)))))

(defun-sk ht059-identically-distributed-p
    (carrier events measure ray-event)
  (forall (index threshold)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier threshold)
      (ht059-event-p
       events (ht059-apply2 ray-event index threshold))
      (ht059-event-p
       events (ht059-apply2 ray-event 0 threshold)))
     (equal
      (ht059-apply1
       measure (ht059-apply2 ray-event index threshold))
      (ht059-apply1
       measure (ht059-apply2 ray-event 0 threshold))))))

(defun-sk ht059-pairwise-independent-p
    (carrier events intersection-event measure ray-event multiply)
  (forall (left-index right-index left-threshold right-threshold)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp left-index)
      (natp right-index)
      (not (equal left-index right-index))
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier left-threshold)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier right-threshold)
      (ht059-event-p
       events
       (ht059-apply2 ray-event left-index left-threshold))
      (ht059-event-p
       events
       (ht059-apply2 ray-event right-index right-threshold)))
     (let* ((left-event
             (ht059-apply2
              ray-event left-index left-threshold))
            (right-event
             (ht059-apply2
              ray-event right-index right-threshold))
            (joint-event
             (ht059-apply2
              intersection-event left-event right-event)))
       (equal
        (ht059-apply1 measure joint-event)
        (ht059-mul
         multiply
         (ht059-apply1 measure left-event)
         (ht059-apply1 measure right-event)))))))

;; The positive and negative expectation parts are limits of the standard
;; dyadic lower sums
;;
;;   2^-n * sum_{1 <= k <= n*2^n} P(k/2^n <= Y).
;;
;; This directly characterizes the Lebesgue expectation of a nonnegative
;; random variable and avoids an uninterpreted integral operator.

(defun ht059-positive-part (less zero value)
  (ht059-max less zero value))

(defun ht059-negative-part (less negate zero value)
  (ht059-max less zero (ht059-neg negate value)))

(defun ht059-signed-part
    (positivep less negate zero value)
  (if positivep
      (ht059-positive-part less zero value)
    (ht059-negative-part less negate zero value)))

(defun-sk ht059-level-event-closure-p
    (carrier zero less events level-event)
  (forall (index positivep threshold)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (booleanp positivep)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier threshold)
      (ht059-leq-p less zero threshold))
     (ht059-event-p
      events
      (ht059-apply3
       level-event index positivep threshold)))))

(defun-sk ht059-level-event-membership-p
    (carrier sample-carrier event-member x-family level-event
             zero negate less)
  (forall (index positivep threshold omega)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (booleanp positivep)
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier threshold)
      (ht059-leq-p less zero threshold)
      (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega))
     (iff
      (ht059-in-event-p
       event-member
       (ht059-apply3
        level-event index positivep threshold)
       omega)
      (ht059-leq-p
       less threshold
       (ht059-signed-part
        positivep less negate zero
        (ht059-apply2 x-family index omega)))))))

(defun ht059-dyadic-denominator (add multiply one exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      one
    (ht059-mul
     multiply
     (ht059-add add one one)
     (ht059-dyadic-denominator
      add multiply one (1- exponent)))))

(defun ht059-level-measure-sum
    (measure level-event index positivep
             add multiply inverse zero one denominator count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (let* ((k (nfix count))
           (threshold
            (ht059-div
             multiply inverse
             (ht059-real-nat add zero one k)
             denominator)))
      (ht059-add
       add
       (ht059-level-measure-sum
        measure level-event index positivep
        add multiply inverse zero one denominator (1- count))
       (ht059-apply1
        measure
        (ht059-apply3
         level-event index positivep threshold))))))

(defun ht059-expectation-approximation
    (measure level-event index positivep n
             add multiply inverse zero one)
  (let* ((native-n (nfix n))
         (native-power (expt 2 native-n))
         (count (* native-n native-power))
         (denominator
          (ht059-dyadic-denominator
           add multiply one native-n)))
    (ht059-mul
     multiply
     (ht059-inv inverse denominator)
     (ht059-level-measure-sum
      measure level-event index positivep
      add multiply inverse zero one denominator count))))

(defun-sk ht059-expectation-limit-tail-p
    (measure level-event index positivep limit
             add multiply negate inverse zero one less
             epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (natp cutoff)
      (<= cutoff n))
     (ht059-less-p
      less
      (ht059-abs
       less negate zero
       (ht059-sub
        add negate
        (ht059-expectation-approximation
         measure level-event index positivep n
         add multiply inverse zero one)
        limit))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht059-expectation-limit-cutoff-exists-p
    (measure level-event index positivep limit
             add multiply negate inverse zero one less epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (ht059-expectation-limit-tail-p
      measure level-event index positivep limit
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less
      epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk ht059-nonnegative-expectation-limit-p
    (carrier measure level-event index positivep limit
             add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier epsilon)
      (ht059-less-p less zero epsilon))
     (ht059-expectation-limit-cutoff-exists-p
      measure level-event index positivep limit
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less epsilon))))

(defun ht059-nonnegative-expectation-p
    (carrier measure level-event index positivep limit
             add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (and
   (ht059-scalar-p carrier limit)
   (ht059-leq-p less zero limit)
   (ht059-nonnegative-expectation-limit-p
    carrier measure level-event index positivep limit
    add multiply negate inverse zero one less)))

(defun-sk ht059-has-expectation-p
    (carrier measure level-event index mean
             add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (exists (positive-expectation negative-expectation)
    (and
     (ht059-nonnegative-expectation-p
      carrier measure level-event index t positive-expectation
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
     (ht059-nonnegative-expectation-p
      carrier measure level-event index nil negative-expectation
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
     (ht059-scalar-p carrier mean)
     (equal
      mean
      (ht059-sub
       add negate positive-expectation negative-expectation)))))

(defun-sk ht059-integrable-p
    (carrier measure level-event index
             add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (exists (mean)
    (ht059-has-expectation-p
     carrier measure level-event index mean
     add multiply negate inverse zero one less)))

;; Pointwise convergence and almost-sure convergence are direct epsilon-N
;; predicates. A measurable event of probability one supplies the AE witness.

(defun ht059-partial-sum
    (x-family count omega add zero)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (let ((index (1- count)))
      (ht059-add
       add
       (ht059-partial-sum
        x-family index omega add zero)
       (ht059-apply2 x-family index omega)))))

(defun ht059-running-average
    (x-family count omega add multiply inverse zero one)
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (ht059-div
     multiply inverse
     (ht059-partial-sum
      x-family count omega add zero)
     (ht059-real-nat add zero one count))))

(defun-sk ht059-pointwise-limit-tail-p
    (x-family omega mean
              add multiply negate inverse zero one less
              epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (count)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp count)
      (natp cutoff)
      (<= cutoff count))
     (ht059-less-p
      less
      (ht059-abs
       less negate zero
       (ht059-sub
        add negate
        (ht059-running-average
         x-family count omega
         add multiply inverse zero one)
        mean))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht059-pointwise-limit-cutoff-exists-p
    (x-family omega mean
              add multiply negate inverse zero one less epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (ht059-pointwise-limit-tail-p
      x-family omega mean
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less
      epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk ht059-pointwise-converges-p
    (carrier x-family omega mean
             add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-scalar-p carrier epsilon)
      (ht059-less-p less zero epsilon))
     (ht059-pointwise-limit-cutoff-exists-p
      x-family omega mean
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht059-converges-on-event-p
    (carrier sample-carrier event-member good-event x-family mean
             add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (forall (omega)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht059-sample-p sample-carrier omega)
      (ht059-in-event-p event-member good-event omega))
     (ht059-pointwise-converges-p
      carrier x-family omega mean
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less))))

(defun-sk ht059-almost-sure-convergence-p
    (carrier one sample-carrier events event-member measure
             x-family mean add multiply negate inverse zero less)
  (exists (good-event)
    (and
     (ht059-event-p events good-event)
     (equal (ht059-apply1 measure good-event) one)
     (ht059-converges-on-event-p
      carrier sample-carrier event-member good-event x-family mean
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less))))

(defun ht059-random-variable-family-p
    (carrier zero negate less
             sample-carrier events event-member
             x-family ray-event level-event)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp x-family)
   (tamep-functionp ray-event)
   (tamep-functionp level-event)
   (ht059-family-values-p
    carrier sample-carrier x-family)
   (ht059-ray-event-closure-p
    carrier events ray-event)
   (ht059-ray-event-membership-p
    carrier sample-carrier event-member x-family ray-event less)
   (ht059-level-event-closure-p
    carrier zero less events level-event)
   (ht059-level-event-membership-p
    carrier sample-carrier event-member x-family level-event
    zero negate less)))

(defun ht059-strong-law-context-p
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less
             sample-carrier events event-member
             empty-event full-event complement-event intersection-event
             sequence-value countable-union-event measure
             x-family ray-event level-event)
  (and
   (ht059-real-field-p
    carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less)
   (ht059-probability-space-p
    carrier zero one add negate less
    sample-carrier events event-member
    empty-event full-event complement-event intersection-event
    sequence-value countable-union-event measure)
   (ht059-random-variable-family-p
    carrier zero negate less
    sample-carrier events event-member
    x-family ray-event level-event)
   (ht059-identically-distributed-p
    carrier events measure ray-event)
   (ht059-pairwise-independent-p
    carrier events intersection-event measure ray-event multiply)
   (ht059-integrable-p
    carrier measure level-event 0
    add multiply negate inverse zero one less)))

(defun-sk ht059-strong-law-conclusion-p
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less
             sample-carrier events event-member measure
             x-family level-event)
  (exists (mean)
    (and
     (ht059-has-expectation-p
      carrier measure level-event 0 mean
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
     (ht059-almost-sure-convergence-p
      carrier one sample-carrier events event-member measure
      x-family mean add multiply negate inverse zero less))))

(defun hundred-theorems-059-laws-of-large-numbers-statement
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less
             sample-carrier events event-member
             empty-event full-event complement-event intersection-event
             sequence-value countable-union-event measure
             x-family ray-event level-event)
  (implies
   (ht059-strong-law-context-p
    carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less
    sample-carrier events event-member
    empty-event full-event complement-event intersection-event
    sequence-value countable-union-event measure
    x-family ray-event level-event)
   (ht059-strong-law-conclusion-p
    carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less
    sample-carrier events event-member measure
    x-family level-event)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 059_the_laws_of_large_numbers
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 059, "The Laws of Large Numbers":
-- the strong law for pairwise-independent, identically distributed, integrable real random variables,
-- whose sample averages converge almost surely to their common expectation.
-- This file contains no proof.

module LawsOfLargeNumbers where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data List (A : Set) : Set where
  empty : List A
  cons  : A -> List A -> List A

data Member {A : Set} (x : A) : List A -> Set where
  at-head : {xs : List A} -> Member x (cons x xs)
  in-tail : {y : A} {xs : List A} -> Member x xs -> Member x (cons y xs)

data NoDuplicates {A : Set} : List A -> Set where
  no-duplicates-empty :
    NoDuplicates empty
  no-duplicates-cons :
    {x : A} {xs : List A} ->
    Not (Member x xs) ->
    NoDuplicates xs ->
    NoDuplicates (cons x xs)

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate reciprocal absoluteValue : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    reciprocal-zero :
      reciprocal zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-reciprocal :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (reciprocal x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      Both (lessOrEqual zeroR oneR) (zeroR != oneR)

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    absolute-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      absoluteValue x == x
    absolute-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      absoluteValue x == negate x

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
              lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (reciprocal reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both (lessOrEqual reals x y) (x != y)

Close :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
Close reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (absoluteValue reals (subtract reals x center))
    radius

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      StrictLess reals
        (absoluteValue reals (subtract reals (sequence n) limit))
        epsilon)

BoundedFunction :
  {A R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (A -> R) ->
  Set
BoundedFunction {A} {R} reals f =
  Exists R
    (\ bound ->
      Both
        (lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) bound)
        ((x : A) ->
          lessOrEqual reals
            (absoluteValue reals (f x))
            bound))

Continuous :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
Continuous {R} reals f =
  (x epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      Both
        (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta)
        ((y : R) ->
          Close reals x delta y ->
          Close reals (f x) epsilon (f y)))

record BoundedContinuous
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (f : R -> R) : Set where
  field
    bounded    : BoundedFunction reals f
    continuous : Continuous reals f

power :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
power reals x zero =
  oneR reals
power reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals (power reals x n) x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingSign reals zero =
  oneR reals
alternatingSign reals (suc n) =
  negate reals (alternatingSign reals n)

evenIndex : Nat -> Nat
evenIndex n =
  n + n

oddIndex : Nat -> Nat
oddIndex n =
  suc (evenIndex n)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
sumFirst reals term zero =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals term (suc n) =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals term n)
    (term n)

exponentialPartialSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialPartialSum reals x n =
  sumFirst reals
    (\ k ->
      divide reals
        (power reals x k)
        (fromNat reals (factorial k)))
    n

cosinePartialSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
cosinePartialSum reals x n =
  sumFirst reals
    (\ k ->
      multiply reals
        (alternatingSign reals k)
        (divide reals
          (power reals x (evenIndex k))
          (fromNat reals (factorial (evenIndex k)))))
    n

sinePartialSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sinePartialSum reals x n =
  sumFirst reals
    (\ k ->
      multiply reals
        (alternatingSign reals k)
        (divide reals
          (power reals x (oddIndex k))
          (fromNat reals (factorial (oddIndex k)))))
    n

Predicate : Set -> Set1
Predicate A = A -> Set

emptySet :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A
emptySet _ =
  Bottom

wholeSet :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A
wholeSet _ =
  Top

complement :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A ->
  Predicate A
complement E x =
  Not (E x)

countableUnion :
  {A : Set} ->
  (Nat -> Predicate A) ->
  Predicate A
countableUnion sets x =
  Exists Nat (\ n -> sets n x)

record SigmaAlgebra (A : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    measurable : Predicate A -> Set

    measurable-empty :
      measurable emptySet
    measurable-complement :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      measurable E ->
      measurable (complement E)
    measurable-countable-union :
      (sets : Nat -> Predicate A) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> measurable (sets n)) ->
      measurable (countableUnion sets)
    measurable-congruent :
      (E F : Predicate A) ->
      ((x : A) -> Iff (E x) (F x)) ->
      measurable E ->
      measurable F

open SigmaAlgebra

record StandardRealAnalysis (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    algebra : CompleteOrderedField R
    squareRoot exponential cosine sine : R -> R

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      square algebra (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra x (zeroR algebra) ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR algebra

    exponential-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SequentialLimit algebra
        (exponentialPartialSum algebra x)
        (exponential x)
    cosine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SequentialLimit algebra
        (cosinePartialSum algebra x)
        (cosine x)
    sine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SequentialLimit algebra
        (sinePartialSum algebra x)
        (sine x)

    borel : SigmaAlgebra R
    borel-open-ray :
      (a : R) ->
      measurable borel (\ x -> StrictLess algebra a x)
    borel-minimal :
      (candidate : SigmaAlgebra R) ->
      ((a : R) ->
        measurable candidate (\ x -> StrictLess algebra a x)) ->
      (E : Predicate R) ->
      measurable borel E ->
      measurable candidate E

open StandardRealAnalysis

preimage :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Predicate B ->
  Predicate A
preimage f E x =
  E (f x)

MeasurableFunction :
  {A B : Set} ->
  SigmaAlgebra A ->
  SigmaAlgebra B ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set1
MeasurableFunction source target f =
  (E : Predicate _) ->
  measurable target E ->
  measurable source (preimage f E)

PairwiseDisjoint :
  {A : Set} ->
  (Nat -> Predicate A) ->
  Set
PairwiseDisjoint {A} sets =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  i != j ->
  (x : A) ->
  sets i x ->
  sets j x ->
  Bottom

record Measure
  {A R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) : Set1 where
  field
    mass : Predicate A -> R

    mass-congruent :
      (E F : Predicate A) ->
      ((x : A) -> Iff (E x) (F x)) ->
      mass E == mass F
    mass-empty :
      mass emptySet == zeroR (algebra analysis)
    mass-nonnegative :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      measurable events E ->
      lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
        (zeroR (algebra analysis))
        (mass E)
    countable-additivity :
      (sets : Nat -> Predicate A) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> measurable events (sets n)) ->
      PairwiseDisjoint sets ->
      SequentialLimit (algebra analysis)
        (\ count ->
          sumFirst (algebra analysis)
            (\ n -> mass (sets n))
            count)
        (mass (countableUnion sets))

open Measure

record Integration
  {A R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A)
  (measure : Measure analysis events) : Set1 where
  field
    integrable : (A -> R) -> Set
    integral : (A -> R) -> R
    indicator : Predicate A -> A -> R

    integrable-congruent :
      (f g : A -> R) ->
      ((x : A) -> f x == g x) ->
      Iff (integrable f) (integrable g)
    integral-congruent :
      (f g : A -> R) ->
      ((x : A) -> f x == g x) ->
      integral f == integral g

    integrable-zero :
      integrable (\ _ -> zeroR (algebra analysis))
    integral-zero :
      integral (\ _ -> zeroR (algebra analysis)) ==
      zeroR (algebra analysis)
    integrable-add :
      (f g : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integrable g ->
      integrable
        (\ x -> add (algebra analysis) (f x) (g x))
    integral-add :
      (f g : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integrable g ->
      integral
        (\ x -> add (algebra analysis) (f x) (g x)) ==
      add (algebra analysis) (integral f) (integral g)
    integrable-negate :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integrable (\ x -> negate (algebra analysis) (f x))
    integral-negate :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integral (\ x -> negate (algebra analysis) (f x)) ==
      negate (algebra analysis) (integral f)
    integrable-scale :
      (c : R) ->
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integrable
        (\ x -> multiply (algebra analysis) c (f x))
    integral-scale :
      (c : R) ->
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integral
        (\ x -> multiply (algebra analysis) c (f x)) ==
      multiply (algebra analysis) c (integral f)
    integrable-absolute :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      integrable
        (\ x -> absoluteValue (algebra analysis) (f x))
    integral-nonnegative :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      integrable f ->
      ((x : A) ->
        lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
          (zeroR (algebra analysis))
          (f x)) ->
      lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
        (zeroR (algebra analysis))
        (integral f)

    indicator-on :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      (x : A) ->
      E x ->
      indicator E x == oneR (algebra analysis)
    indicator-off :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      (x : A) ->
      Not (E x) ->
      indicator E x == zeroR (algebra analysis)
    indicator-integrable :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      measurable events E ->
      integrable (indicator E)
    integral-indicator :
      (E : Predicate A) ->
      measurable events E ->
      integral (indicator E) == mass measure E

    bounded-measurable-integrable :
      (f : A -> R) ->
      MeasurableFunction events (borel analysis) f ->
      BoundedFunction (algebra analysis) f ->
      integrable f

    monotone-convergence :
      (functions : Nat -> A -> R) ->
      (limitFunction : A -> R) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> integrable (functions n)) ->
      ((n : Nat) ->
        (x : A) ->
        lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
          (zeroR (algebra analysis))
          (functions n x)) ->
      ((n : Nat) ->
        (x : A) ->
        lessOrEqual (algebra analysis)
          (functions n x)
          (functions (suc n) x)) ->
      ((x : A) ->
        SequentialLimit (algebra analysis)
          (\ n -> functions n x)
          (limitFunction x)) ->
      (limitIntegral : R) ->
      SequentialLimit (algebra analysis)
        (\ n -> integral (functions n))
        limitIntegral ->
      Both
        (integrable limitFunction)
        (integral limitFunction == limitIntegral)

open Integration

record IntegratedMeasure
  {A R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) : Set1 where
  field
    measure : Measure analysis events
    integration : Integration analysis events measure

open IntegratedMeasure

record ProbabilitySpace
  {A R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) : Set1 where
  field
    integratedMeasure : IntegratedMeasure analysis events
    total-mass-one :
      mass (measure integratedMeasure) wholeSet ==
      oneR (algebra analysis)

open ProbabilitySpace

spaceMeasure :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  Measure analysis events
spaceMeasure space =
  measure (integratedMeasure space)

spaceIntegration :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  (space : ProbabilitySpace analysis events) ->
  Integration analysis events (spaceMeasure space)
spaceIntegration space =
  integration (integratedMeasure space)

probabilityOf :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  Predicate A ->
  R
probabilityOf space E =
  mass (spaceMeasure space) E

IsIntegrable :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (A -> R) ->
  Set
IsIntegrable space f =
  integrable (spaceIntegration space) f

expectation :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (A -> R) ->
  R
expectation space f =
  integral (spaceIntegration space) f

variance :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (A -> R) ->
  R
variance {analysis = analysis} space f =
  expectation space
    (\ x ->
      square (algebra analysis)
        (subtract (algebra analysis) (f x) (expectation space f)))

SquareIntegrable :
  {A R : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (A -> R) ->
  Set
SquareIntegrable {analysis = analysis} space f =
  IsIntegrable space
    (\ x -> square (algebra analysis) (f x))

record StandardProbabilityTheory (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R

open StandardProbabilityTheory

realAlgebra :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardProbabilityTheory R ->
  CompleteOrderedField R
realAlgebra theory =
  algebra (analysis theory)

realBorel :
  {R : Set} ->
  (theory : StandardProbabilityTheory R) ->
  SigmaAlgebra R
realBorel theory =
  borel (analysis theory)

finiteIntersection :
  {R A : Set} ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  (Nat -> Predicate R) ->
  List Nat ->
  Predicate A
finiteIntersection X sets empty _ =
  Top
finiteIntersection X sets (cons i indices) x =
  Both
    (sets i (X i x))
    (finiteIntersection X sets indices x)

finiteProbabilityProduct :
  {R A : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A} ->
  ProbabilitySpace analysis events ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  (Nat -> Predicate R) ->
  List Nat ->
  R
finiteProbabilityProduct {analysis = analysis} space X sets empty =
  oneR (algebra analysis)
finiteProbabilityProduct {analysis = analysis} space X sets
  (cons i indices) =
  multiply (algebra analysis)
    (probabilityOf space (\ x -> sets i (X i x)))
    (finiteProbabilityProduct space X sets indices)

record IndependentVariables
  {R A : Set}
  (theory : StandardProbabilityTheory R)
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A)
  (space : ProbabilitySpace (analysis theory) events)
  (X : Nat -> A -> R) : Set1 where
  field
    measurable-variable :
      (n : Nat) ->
      MeasurableFunction events (realBorel theory) (X n)
    independent-pairs :
      (i j : Nat) ->
      i != j ->
      (E F : Predicate R) ->
      measurable (realBorel theory) E ->
      measurable (realBorel theory) F ->
      probabilityOf space
        (\ x -> Both (E (X i x)) (F (X j x))) ==
      multiply (realAlgebra theory)
        (probabilityOf space (preimage (X i) E))
        (probabilityOf space (preimage (X j) F))

IdenticallyDistributed :
  {R A : Set} ->
  (theory : StandardProbabilityTheory R) ->
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) ->
  ProbabilitySpace (analysis theory) events ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  Set1
IdenticallyDistributed theory events space X =
  (n : Nat) ->
  (E : Predicate _) ->
  measurable (realBorel theory) E ->
  probabilityOf space (preimage (X n) E) ==
  probabilityOf space (preimage (X zero) E)

partialSum :
  {R A : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  A ->
  R
partialSum reals X n x =
  sumFirst reals (\ i -> X i x) n

sampleAverage :
  {R A : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> A -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  A ->
  R
sampleAverage reals X n x =
  divide reals
    (partialSum reals X n x)
    (fromNat reals n)

record AlmostSure
  {R A : Set}
  {analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R}
  {events : SigmaAlgebra A}
  (space : ProbabilitySpace analysis events)
  (property : Predicate A) : Set1 where
  field
    full-measure-event :
      Predicate A
    full-measure-event-measurable :
      measurable events full-measure-event
    full-measure-event-probability :
      probabilityOf space full-measure-event ==
      oneR (algebra analysis)
    property-on-full-measure-event :
      (x : A) ->
      full-measure-event x ->
      property x

strong-law-of-large-numbers : Set1
strong-law-of-large-numbers =
  (R A : Set) ->
  (theory : StandardProbabilityTheory R) ->
  (events : SigmaAlgebra A) ->
  (space : ProbabilitySpace (analysis theory) events) ->
  (X : Nat -> A -> R) ->
  IndependentVariables theory events space X ->
  IdenticallyDistributed theory events space X ->
  IsIntegrable space (X zero) ->
  AlmostSure space
    (\ x ->
      SequentialLimit (realAlgebra theory)
        (\ n -> sampleAverage (realAlgebra theory) X n x)
        (expectation space (X zero)))

title: 059_the_laws_of_large_numbers
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "The Laws of Large Numbers" from Hundred
  Theorems item 059. It states the strong law for identically distributed,
  pairwise-independent integrable real-valued random variables: their running
  averages converge almost surely to their common expectation. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory iterateTheory realTheory;
open topologyTheory real_topologyTheory extrealTheory measureTheory borelTheory;
open lebesgueTheory lebesgue_measureTheory probabilityTheory;

val strong_law_of_large_numbers_iid =
  ``!(p : 'a p_space) (X : num -> 'a -> extreal).
      prob_space p /\
      (!n. real_random_variable (X n) p) /\
      pairwise_indep_vars p X (\n. Borel) UNIV /\
      identical_distribution p X Borel UNIV /\
      integrable p (X 0)
      ==>
      (((\n x. SIGMA (\i. X i x) (count1 n) / &SUC n) -->
        (\x. expectation p (X 0)))
       (almost_everywhere p))``;

title: 059_the_laws_of_large_numbers
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 059, "The Laws
  of Large Numbers". It states the strong law for identically distributed
  integrable real-valued random variables, both for a mutually independent
  sequence on a probability space and for the pairwise-independent form over
  an arbitrary measure, where the latter starts from arbitrary functions and
  uses measurable versions equal outside measurable null sets. Almost-sure
  convergence is likewise stated outside an internally quantified measurable
  null set. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  All probability-theory notions below are the defined set.mm notions.
  A sequence X is represented by an actual function on NN0. Real random
  variables are measurable functions into BrSiga. Integrability means
  membership in the domain of the real Bochner integral RRfld itgm M.

  Mutual independence is expanded as the finite-family product identity for
  arbitrary Borel preimages. In the pairwise form, X ranges over arbitrary
  real-valued functions. An internally quantified sequence Y supplies Borel
  measurable versions. For each index, an internally quantified measurable
  null set contains every sample point where X_i and Y_i differ. Pairwise
  independence is the extended-real product identity for every two distinct
  indices, and identical distribution is equality of the measures of all
  Borel preimages. Membership of Y_0 in the domain of the real Bochner
  integral expresses integrability of X_0 up to equality off a null set.

  For each sample point x, the map

    n |-> ( sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ n ) ( ( X ` i ) ` x ) ) / n

  is the sequence of sample averages. Each conclusion internally quantifies a
  measurable null set and states convergence at every sample point outside
  that set.
$)

${
  $d N a f i n s x P X $.
  $d N a f i n s x $.
  $d N f i n s x $.
  $d N i n s x $.
  $d N n x $.
  $d a f i n s x $.
  $d f i n s x $.
  $d i n s x $.
  $d n x $.

  ht059-slln-iid $a |- (
    (
      P e. Prob
      /\
      (
        X : NN0 --> ( rRndVar ` P )
        /\
        (
          A. s e. ( Fin i^i ~P NN0 )
            A. f e. ( BrSiga ^m s )
              ( P ` (
                U. dom P i^i
                |^|_ i e. s ( `' ( X ` i ) " ( f ` i ) )
              ) )
              =
              prod_ i e. s ( P ` ( `' ( X ` i ) " ( f ` i ) ) )
          /\
          (
            A. i e. NN0 A. a e. BrSiga
              ( P ` ( `' ( X ` i ) " a ) )
              =
              ( P ` ( `' ( X ` 0 ) " a ) )
            /\
            ( X ` 0 ) e. dom ( RRfld itgm P )
          )
        )
      )
    )
    ->
    E. N e. dom P
      (
        ( P ` N ) = 0
        /\
        A. x e. ( U. dom P \ N )
        (
          (
            n e. NN0 |->
            (
              sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ n ) ( ( X ` i ) ` x )
            ) / n
          )
          ~~>
          ( ( RRfld itgm P ) ` ( X ` 0 ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d N a b i j n x M X Y $.
  $d N a b i j n x X Y $.
  $d N b i j n x X Y $.
  $d N i j n x X Y $.
  $d N j n x X Y $.
  $d N n x X Y $.
  $d N n x Y $.

  ht059-slln-pairwise $a |- (
    (
      M e. U. ran measures
      /\
      (
        X : NN0 --> ( RR ^m U. dom M )
        /\
        E. Y
          (
            Y : NN0 --> ( dom M MblFnM BrSiga )
            /\
            (
              A. i e. NN0
                E. N e. dom M
                  (
                    ( M ` N ) = 0

title: 059_the_laws_of_large_numbers
content:

:: Large Numbers": integrable identically distributed independent real random
:: variables have empirical averages converging almost surely to their common
:: expectation. This file contains no proof.

environ

 vocabularies NUMBERS, XBOOLE_0, PROB_1, MEASURE1, PARTFUN1, SUBSET_1,
      TARSKI, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, ARYTM_3, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, FUNCT_2,
      VALUED_0, MESFUNC1, SUPINF_2, FINSEQ_1, NAT_1, CARD_3, CARD_1,
      ZFMISC_1, FINSET_1, PROB_4, RANDOM_1, RANDOM_2, RANDOM_3, FUNCOP_1,
      FINANCE1, REAL_1, SETFAM_1, SEQ_1, SEQ_2, SEQ_4, PREPOWER,
      ORDINAL2, ABIAN, SQUARE_1, POWER, MEASUR12, SIN_COS, COMPLEX1,
      RVSUM_1, MESFUNC5, INTEGRA5, XCMPLX_0, ARYTM_1, VALUED_1;
 notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, SETFAM_1, RELAT_1,
      FUNCT_1, ORDINAL1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, FUNCOP_1, FINSET_1,
      CARD_1, NUMBERS, XXREAL_3, XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, NAT_1,
      XREAL_0, VALUED_0, FINSEQ_1, SUPINF_2, PROB_1, PROB_2, MEASURE1,
      MEASURE6, MESFUNC1, PROB_4, MESFUNC6, MESFUNC5, RANDOM_1, RANDOM_2,
      RANDOM_3, FINANCE1, REAL_1, SQUARE_1, POWER, RVSUM_1, MEASUR12,
      SIN_COS, COMPLEX1, VALUED_1, MESFUN6C, SEQ_1, SEQ_2, COMSEQ_2,
      SEQM_3, SEQ_4, PREPOWER, ABIAN;
 constructors REAL_1, MESFUNC6, MEASURE6, PROB_3, PROB_4, MESFUNC1,
      MESFUNC5, RELSET_1, COMSEQ_2, RANDOM_1, RANDOM_2, RANDOM_3, FINANCE1,
      RVSUM_1, MEASUR12, SIN_COS, SQUARE_1, POWER, SETFAM_1, MESFUN6C,
      COMPLEX1, SEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4, PREPOWER, ABIAN, BINOP_2;
 registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, NAT_1, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, ORDINAL1,
      MEASURE1, FUNCOP_1, FINANCE1, VALUED_0, FINSEQ_1, FUNCT_2, RELAT_1,
      FINSET_1, NUMBERS, PROB_1, PARTFUN1, RELSET_1, CARD_1, MEMBERED,
      SQUARE_1, XXREAL_3, RANDOM_2, RANDOM_3, MEASUR12, MESFUN6C,
      XCMPLX_0, SEQ_4, ABIAN, PREPOWER;
 requirements NUMERALS, BOOLE, SUBSET, ARITHM, REAL;
 definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, FINSET_1;
 equalities PROB_1, RANDOM_2, PROB_4, RELAT_1, FINSEQ_1;
 expansions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1, FINSEQ_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for Omega being non empty set,
      Sigma being SigmaField of Omega,
      P being Probability of Sigma,
      mu being Probability of Borel_Sets,
      X being Function of NAT,Funcs(Omega,REAL),
      X0 being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma
  st
    X is Sigma-Random-Variable-Family &
    X0 = X.0 &
    X0 is_integrable_on P &
    (for n being Nat,
         Xn being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma,
         FXn being random_variable of Sigma,Borel_Sets
      st Xn = X.n & FXn = Xn
      holds probability(FXn,P) = mu) &
    (for k being Nat,
         I being one-to-one FinSequence of NAT,
         B being FinSequence of Borel_Sets,
         E being FinSequence of Sigma,
         q being FinSequence of REAL
      st 0 < k &
         len I = k & len B = k & len E = k & len q = k &
         (for j being Nat st j in Seg k holds
           E.j = (X.(I.j))"(B.j) &
           q.j = (P.(E.j) qua Real))
      holds P.(meet rng E) = Product q)
  holds
    ex A being Element of Sigma st
      A = {omega where omega is Element of Omega :
        ex s being Real_Sequence st
          (for n being Nat holds
