subsection \<open>Bezout's theorem\<close>

text \<open>
  Function \<open>bezw\<close> returns a pair of witnesses to Bezout's theorem --
  see the theorems that follow the definition.
\<close>

fun bezw :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int * int"
  where "bezw x y =
    (if y = 0 then (1, 0)
     else
      (snd (bezw y (x mod y)),
       fst (bezw y (x mod y)) - snd (bezw y (x mod y)) * int(x div y)))"

lemma bezw_0 [simp]: "bezw x 0 = (1, 0)"
  by sorry

lemma bezw_non_0:
  "y > 0 \<Longrightarrow> bezw x y =
    (snd (bezw y (x mod y)), fst (bezw y (x mod y)) - snd (bezw y (x mod y)) * int(x div y))"
  by sorry

declare bezw.simps [simp del]


lemma bezw_aux: "int (gcd x y) = fst (bezw x y) * int x + snd (bezw x y) * int y"
  by sorry


lemma bezout_int: "\<exists>u v. u * x + v * y = gcd x y"
  for x y :: int
  by sorry


text \<open>Versions of Bezout for \<open>nat\<close>, by Amine Chaieb.\<close>

lemma Euclid_induct [case_names swap zero add]:
  fixes P :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
  assumes c: "\<And>a b. P a b \<longleftrightarrow> P b a"
    and z: "\<And>a. P a 0"
    and add: "\<And>a b. P a b \<longrightarrow> P a (a + b)"
  shows "P a b"
  by sorry

lemma bezout_lemma_nat:
  fixes d::nat
  shows "\<lbrakk>d dvd a; d dvd b; a * x = b * y + d \<or> b * x = a * y + d\<rbrakk>
    \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>x y. d dvd a \<and> d dvd a + b \<and> (a * x = (a + b) * y + d \<or> (a + b) * x = a * y + d)"
  by sorry

lemma bezout_add_nat: 
  "\<exists>(d::nat) x y. d dvd a \<and> d dvd b \<and> (a * x = b * y + d \<or> b * x = a * y + d)"
  by sorry

lemma bezout1_nat: "\<exists>(d::nat) x y. d dvd a \<and> d dvd b \<and> (a * x - b * y = d \<or> b * x - a * y = d)"
  by sorry

lemma bezout_add_strong_nat:
  fixes a b :: nat
  assumes a: "a \<noteq> 0"
  shows "\<exists>d x y. d dvd a \<and> d dvd b \<and> a * x = b * y + d"
  by sorry

lemma bezout_nat:
  fixes a :: nat
  assumes a: "a \<noteq> 0"
  shows "\<exists>x y. a * x = b * y + gcd a b"
  by sorry

subsection \<open>The complete divisibility lattice on \<^typ>\<open>nat\<close> and \<^typ>\<open>int\<close>\<close>

text \<open>
  Lifting \<open>gcd\<close> and \<open>lcm\<close> to sets (\<open>Gcd\<close> / \<open>Lcm\<close>).
  \<open>Gcd\<close> is defined via \<open>Lcm\<close> to facilitate the proof that we have a complete lattice.
\<close>

instantiation nat :: semiring_Gcd
begin

interpretation semilattice_neutr_set lcm "1::nat"
  by standard simp_all

definition "Lcm M = (if finite M then F M else 0)" for M :: "nat set"

lemma Lcm_nat_empty: "Lcm {} = (1::nat)"
  by sorry

lemma Lcm_nat_insert: "Lcm (insert n M) = lcm n (Lcm M)" for n :: nat
  by sorry

lemma Lcm_nat_infinite: "infinite M \<Longrightarrow> Lcm M = 0" for M :: "nat set"
  by sorry

lemma dvd_Lcm_nat [simp]:
  fixes M :: "nat set"
  assumes "m \<in> M"
  shows "m dvd Lcm M"
  by sorry

lemma Lcm_dvd_nat [simp]:
  fixes M :: "nat set"
  assumes "\<forall>m\<in>M. m dvd n"
  shows "Lcm M dvd n"
  by sorry

definition "Gcd M = Lcm {d. \<forall>m\<in>M. d dvd m}" for M :: "nat set"

instance
proof
  fix N :: "nat set"
  fix n :: nat
  show "Gcd N dvd n" if "n \<in> N"
    using that by (induct N rule: infinite_finite_induct) (auto simp: Gcd_nat_def)
  show "n dvd Gcd N" if "\<And>m. m \<in> N \<Longrightarrow> n dvd m"
    using that by (induct N rule: infinite_finite_induct) (auto simp: Gcd_nat_def)
  show "n dvd Lcm N" if "n \<in> N"
    using that by (induct N rule: infinite_finite_induct) auto
  show "Lcm N dvd n" if "\<And>m. m \<in> N \<Longrightarrow> m dvd n"
    using that by (induct N rule: infinite_finite_induct) auto
  show "normalize (Gcd N) = Gcd N" and "normalize (Lcm N) = Lcm N"
    by simp_all
qed

end

lemma Gcd_nat_eq_one: "1 \<in> N \<Longrightarrow> Gcd N = 1"
  for N :: "nat set"
  by sorry

instance nat :: semiring_gcd_mult_normalize
  by intro_classes (auto simp: unit_factor_nat_def)


text \<open>Alternative characterizations of Gcd:\<close>

lemma Gcd_eq_Max:
  fixes M :: "nat set"
  assumes "finite (M::nat set)" and "M \<noteq> {}" and "0 \<notin> M"
  shows "Gcd M = Max (\<Inter>m\<in>M. {d. d dvd m})"
  by sorry

lemma Gcd_remove0_nat: "Gcd M = Gcd (M - {0})"
  for M :: "nat set"
  by sorry

lemma Lcm_in_lcm_closed_set_nat:
  fixes M :: "nat set" 
  assumes "finite M" "M \<noteq> {}" "\<And>m n. \<lbrakk>m \<in> M; n \<in> M\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow> lcm m n \<in> M"
  shows "Lcm M \<in> M"
  by sorry

lemma Lcm_eq_Max_nat:
  fixes M :: "nat set" 
  assumes M: "finite M" "M \<noteq> {}" "0 \<notin> M" and lcm: "\<And>m n. \<lbrakk>m \<in> M; n \<in> M\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow> lcm m n \<in> M"
  shows "Lcm M = Max M"
  by sorry

lemma mult_inj_if_coprime_nat:
  "inj_on f A \<Longrightarrow> inj_on g B \<Longrightarrow> (\<And>a b. \<lbrakk>a\<in>A; b\<in>B\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow> coprime (f a) (g b)) \<Longrightarrow>
    inj_on (\<lambda>(a, b). f a * g b) (A \<times> B)"
  for f :: "'a \<Rightarrow> nat" and g :: "'b \<Rightarrow> nat"
  by sorry


subsubsection \<open>Setwise GCD and LCM for integers\<close>

instantiation int :: Gcd
begin

definition Gcd_int :: "int set \<Rightarrow> int"
  where "Gcd K = int (GCD k\<in>K. (nat \<circ> abs) k)"

definition Lcm_int :: "int set \<Rightarrow> int"
  where "Lcm K = int (LCM k\<in>K. (nat \<circ> abs) k)"

instance ..

end

lemma Gcd_int_eq [simp]:
  "(GCD n\<in>N. int n) = int (Gcd N)"
  by sorry

lemma Gcd_nat_abs_eq [simp]:
  "(GCD k\<in>K. nat \<bar>k\<bar>) = nat (Gcd K)"
  by sorry

lemma abs_Gcd_eq [simp]:
  "\<bar>Gcd K\<bar> = Gcd K" for K :: "int set"
  by sorry

lemma uminus_Gcd_eq [simp]: 
  fixes K::"int set"
  shows "Gcd (uminus ` K) = Gcd K"
  by sorry

lemma Gcd_int_greater_eq_0 [simp]:
  "Gcd K \<ge> 0"
  for K :: "int set"
  by sorry

lemma Gcd_abs_eq [simp]:
  "(GCD k\<in>K. \<bar>k\<bar>) = Gcd K"
  for K :: "int set"
  by sorry

lemma Lcm_int_eq [simp]:
  "(LCM n\<in>N. int n) = int (Lcm N)"
  by sorry

lemma Lcm_nat_abs_eq [simp]:
  "(LCM k\<in>K. nat \<bar>k\<bar>) = nat (Lcm K)"
  by sorry

lemma abs_Lcm_eq [simp]:
  "\<bar>Lcm K\<bar> = Lcm K" for K :: "int set"
  by sorry

lemma Lcm_int_greater_eq_0 [simp]:
  "Lcm K \<ge> 0"
  for K :: "int set"
  by sorry

lemma Lcm_abs_eq [simp]:
  "(LCM k\<in>K. \<bar>k\<bar>) = Lcm K"
  for K :: "int set"
  by sorry

instance int :: semiring_Gcd
proof
  fix K :: "int set" and k :: int
  show "Gcd K dvd k" and "k dvd Lcm K" if "k \<in> K"
    using that Gcd_dvd [of "nat \<bar>k\<bar>" "(nat \<circ> abs) ` K"]
      dvd_Lcm [of "nat \<bar>k\<bar>" "(nat \<circ> abs) ` K"]
    by (simp_all add: comp_def)
  show "k dvd Gcd K" if "\<And>l. l \<in> K \<Longrightarrow> k dvd l"
  proof -
    have "nat \<bar>k\<bar> dvd (GCD k\<in>K. nat \<bar>k\<bar>)"
      by (rule Gcd_greatest) (use that in auto)
    then show ?thesis by simp
  qed
  show "Lcm K dvd k" if "\<And>l. l \<in> K \<Longrightarrow> l dvd k"
  proof -
    have "(LCM k\<in>K. nat \<bar>k\<bar>) dvd nat \<bar>k\<bar>"
      by (rule Lcm_least) (use that in auto)
    then show ?thesis by simp
  qed
qed (simp_all add: sgn_mult)

instance int :: semiring_gcd_mult_normalize
  by intro_classes (auto simp: sgn_mult)

subsection \<open>Characteristic of a semiring\<close>

definition (in semiring_1) semiring_char :: "'a itself \<Rightarrow> nat" 
  where "semiring_char _ = Gcd {n. of_nat n = (0 :: 'a)}"

syntax "_type_char" :: "type => nat" (\<open>(\<open>indent=1 notation=\<open>mixfix CHAR\<close>\<close>CHAR/(1'(_')))\<close>)
syntax_consts "_type_char" \<rightleftharpoons> semiring_char
translations "CHAR('t)" \<rightharpoonup> "CONST semiring_char (CONST Pure.type :: 't itself)"
print_translation \<open>
  let
    fun char_type_tr' ctxt [Const (\<^const_syntax>\<open>Pure.type\<close>, Type (_, [T]))] =
      Syntax.const \<^syntax_const>\<open>_type_char\<close> $ Syntax_Phases.term_of_typ ctxt T
  in [(\<^const_syntax>\<open>semiring_char\<close>, char_type_tr')] end
\<close>

context semiring_1
begin

lemma of_nat_CHAR [simp]: "of_nat CHAR('a) = (0 :: 'a)"
  by sorry

lemma of_nat_eq_0_iff_char_dvd: "of_nat n = (0 :: 'a) \<longleftrightarrow> CHAR('a) dvd n"
  by sorry

lemma CHAR_eqI:
  assumes "of_nat c = (0 :: 'a)"
  assumes "\<And>x. of_nat x = (0 :: 'a) \<Longrightarrow> c dvd x"
  shows   "CHAR('a) = c"
  by sorry

lemma CHAR_eq0_iff: "CHAR('a) = 0 \<longleftrightarrow> (\<forall>n>0. of_nat n \<noteq> (0::'a))"
  by sorry

lemma CHAR_pos_iff: "CHAR('a) > 0 \<longleftrightarrow> (\<exists>n>0. of_nat n = (0::'a))"
  by sorry

lemma CHAR_eq_posI:
  assumes "c > 0" "of_nat c = (0 :: 'a)" "\<And>x. x > 0 \<Longrightarrow> x < c \<Longrightarrow> of_nat x \<noteq> (0 :: 'a)"
  shows   "CHAR('a) = c"
  by sorry

end

lemma (in semiring_char_0) CHAR_eq_0 [simp]: "CHAR('a) = 0"
  by sorry


lemma CHAR_not_1 [simp]: "CHAR('a :: {semiring_1, zero_neq_one}) \<noteq> Suc 0"
  by sorry

lemma (in idom) CHAR_not_1' [simp]: "CHAR('a) \<noteq> Suc 0"
  by sorry

lemma (in ring_1) uminus_CHAR_2:
  assumes "CHAR('a) = 2"
  shows   "-(x :: 'a) = x"
  by sorry

lemma (in ring_1) minus_CHAR_2:
  assumes "CHAR('a) = 2"
  shows   "(x - y :: 'a) = x + y"
  by sorry

lemma (in semiring_1_cancel) of_nat_eq_iff_char_dvd:
  assumes "m < n"
  shows   "of_nat m = (of_nat n :: 'a) \<longleftrightarrow> CHAR('a) dvd (n - m)"
  by sorry

lemma (in ring_1) of_int_eq_0_iff_char_dvd:
  "(of_int n = (0 :: 'a)) = (int CHAR('a) dvd n)"
  by sorry

lemma (in semiring_1_cancel) finite_imp_CHAR_pos:
  assumes "finite (UNIV :: 'a set)"
  shows   "CHAR('a) > 0"
  by sorry

end

;; Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__060, "Bézout's Theorem": for every pair of
;; integers x and y, explicitly computed integer coefficients u and v satisfy
;; u*x + v*y = gcd(|x|, |y|). This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun hundred-theorems-060-integer-abs (z)
  (if (integerp z)
      (if (< z 0)
          (- z)
        z)
    0))

(defun hundred-theorems-060-gcd (a b)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (nfix a) (nfix b))))
  (if (and (natp a) (natp b))
      (cond ((equal a 0) b)
            ((equal b 0) a)
            ((< a b)
             (hundred-theorems-060-gcd a (- b a)))
            (t
             (hundred-theorems-060-gcd (- a b) b)))
    0))

(defun hundred-theorems-060-bezout-coefficients (a b)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (nfix a) (nfix b))))
  (if (and (natp a) (natp b))
      (cond ((equal a 0)
             (cons 0 1))
            ((equal b 0)
             (cons 1 0))
            ((< a b)
             (let* ((coefficients
                     (hundred-theorems-060-bezout-coefficients
                      a (- b a)))
                    (u (car coefficients))
                    (v (cdr coefficients)))
               (cons (- u v) v)))
            (t
             (let* ((coefficients
                     (hundred-theorems-060-bezout-coefficients
                      (- a b) b))
                    (u (car coefficients))
                    (v (cdr coefficients)))
               (cons u (- v u)))))
    (cons 0 0)))

(defun hundred-theorems-060-sign (z)
  (if (and (integerp z)
           (< z 0))
      -1
    1))

(defun hundred-theorems-060-bezouts-theorem-statement (x y)
  (implies
   (and (integerp x)
        (integerp y))
   (let* ((absolute-x
           (hundred-theorems-060-integer-abs x))
          (absolute-y
           (hundred-theorems-060-integer-abs y))
          (coefficients
           (hundred-theorems-060-bezout-coefficients
            absolute-x absolute-y))
          (u (* (hundred-theorems-060-sign x)
                (car coefficients)))
          (v (* (hundred-theorems-060-sign y)
                (cdr coefficients))))
     (and (integerp u)
          (integerp v)
          (equal (+ (* u x) (* v y))
                 (hundred-theorems-060-gcd
                  absolute-x absolute-y))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact hundred-theorems__agda__060,
-- "Bézout's Theorem": any two integers admit integer coefficients whose linear combination
-- equals their nonnegative greatest common divisor. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; mod-helper)

infixl 6 _+z_
infixl 7 _*z_

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value : A
    property : P value

difference : Nat → Nat → Int
difference zero zero = pos zero
difference (suc m) zero = pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) = negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) = difference m n

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

_+z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m +z pos n = pos (m + n)
pos m +z negsuc n = difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +z pos n = difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +z negsuc n = negsuc (suc (m + n))

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

absInt : Int → Nat
absInt (pos n) = n
absInt (negsuc n) = suc n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = zero
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

gcdWithFuel : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat
gcdWithFuel zero a b = a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a zero = a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a (suc b) =
  gcdWithFuel fuel (suc b) (naturalMod a (suc b))

euclideanGCD : Nat → Nat → Nat
euclideanGCD a b =
  gcdWithFuel (suc (a + b)) a b

bézout-s-theorem : Set
bézout-s-theorem =
  (x y : Int) →
  Exists Int (λ u →
    Exists Int (λ v →
      (u *z x) +z (v *z y) ≡
      pos (euclideanGCD (absInt x) (absInt y))))

title: 060_bézout_s_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Bézout's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 060:
% every pair of integers has a nonnegative greatest common divisor expressible as an integer
% linear combination of the pair. This file contains no proof.

bezouts_theorem_060: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int): value = divisor * quotient

  is_nonnegative_gcd(d, a, b: int): bool =
    d >= 0 AND
      int_divides(d, a) AND
      int_divides(d, b) AND
      (FORALL (common_divisor: int):
        (int_divides(common_divisor, a) AND
          int_divides(common_divisor, b))
        IMPLIES int_divides(common_divisor, d))

  bezouts_theorem: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: int):
      EXISTS (d, x, y: int):
        is_nonnegative_gcd(d, a, b) AND
          d = a * x + b * y

END bezouts_theorem_060

Authors: Joseph Myers

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Affine.AddTorsor
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.AffineSpace.Ceva

/-!
# Ceva's theorem.

This file proves various versions of Ceva's theorem in a `NormedAddTorsor`.

## References

* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceva%27s_theorem

-/

@[expose] public section


open scoped Affine

variable {𝕜 V P : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V]

namespace Affine.Triangle

variable [PseudoMetricSpace P] [NormedAddTorsor V P] in
/-- **Ceva's theorem** for a triangle, expressed in terms of multiplying distances. -/
lemma prod_dist_eq_prod_dist_of_mem_line_of_mem_line {t : Triangle 𝕜 P} {p : Fin 3 → P} {p' : P}
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin 3, p i ∈ line[𝕜, t.points (i + 1), t.points (i + 2)])
    (hp' : ∀ i : Fin 3, p' ∈ line[𝕜, t.points i, p i]) :
    ∏ i, dist (t.points (i + 1)) (p i) = ∏ i, dist (p i) (t.points (i + 2)) := by sorry
variable [MetricSpace P] [NormedAddTorsor V P] in
/-- **Ceva's theorem** for a triangle, expressed using division of distances. -/
lemma prod_dist_div_dist_eq_one_of_mem_line_of_mem_line {t : Triangle 𝕜 P} {p : Fin 3 → P} {p' : P}
    (hp0 : ∀ i, p i ≠ t.points (i + 2))
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin 3, p i ∈ line[𝕜, t.points (i + 1), t.points (i + 2)])
    (hp' : ∀ i : Fin 3, p' ∈ line[𝕜, t.points i, p i]) :
    ∏ i, dist (t.points (i + 1)) (p i) / dist (p i) (t.points (i + 2)) = 1 := by sorry
end Affine.Triangle

content:
(***************************************************************************)
(* Formalization of the Chou, Gao and Zhang's decision procedure.          *)
(* Julien Narboux (Julien@narboux.fr)                                      *)
(* LIX/INRIA FUTURS 2004-2006                                              *)
(* University of Strasbourg 2008                                           *)
(***************************************************************************)

Require  Import area_method.

Lemma l3_43 : forall O A B X Y C D P Q R T r,
 mratio C A B r ->
 mratio D A B (0-r) ->
 inter_ll P O A X Y ->
 inter_ll Q O B X Y ->
 inter_ll R O C X Y ->
 inter_ll T O D X Y ->
 parallel P R R Q ->
 R<>Q ->
 parallel T P T Q ->
 T<>Q ->
 P<>T ->
 P<>R ->
 ~ Col P X Y ->
 harmonic P Q R T.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Ceva :
 forall A B C D E F G P : Point,
 inter_ll D B C A P ->
 inter_ll E A C B P ->
 inter_ll F A B C P ->
 F <> B ->
 D <> C ->
 E <> A ->
 parallel A F F B ->
 parallel B D D C ->
 parallel C E E A -> 
 (A ** F / F ** B) *  (B ** D / D ** C) *  (C ** E / E ** A) = 1.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma l6_217 : forall A B C D E F G H,
is_midpoint E A B  ->
is_midpoint F B C ->
is_midpoint G C D ->
is_midpoint H D A ->
parallel H E G F ->
G<>F ->
E<>H ->
~ Col E D A ->
H**E / G**F = 1.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Menelaus :
 forall A B C X Y D E F : Point,
 inter_ll D B C X Y ->
 inter_ll E A C X Y ->
 inter_ll F A B X Y ->
 F <> B -> 
 D <> C ->
 E <> A ->
 parallel A F F B ->
 parallel B D D C ->
 parallel C E E A -> 
 (A ** F / F ** B) * (B ** D / D ** C) * (C ** E / E ** A) = - (1).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Pascal :
 forall A B C A' B' C' : Point, A<>C' ->  
 on_line C A B -> 
 on_parallel B' A B A' -> 
 on_inter_line_parallel C' A A' B' C A' -> 
 parallel B C' B' C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Desargues :
 forall A B C X A' B' C' : Point, A' <>C' -> A' <> B' ->
 on_line A' X A ->
 on_inter_line_parallel B' A' X B A B -> 
 on_inter_line_parallel C' A' X C A C ->
 parallel B C B' C'.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem ex1_6auto :
forall A B C D E F G P : Point,
 inter_ll D B C A P ->
 inter_ll E A C B P ->
 inter_ll F A B C P ->
 A <> D ->
 B <> E ->
 C <> F ->
 parallel P D A D ->
 parallel P E B E ->
 parallel P F C F -> 
 P ** D / A ** D + P ** E / B ** E + P ** F / C ** F = 1.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem th2_41 :
 forall A B C D P Q M : Point,
 on_line C A P ->
 on_inter_line_parallel D C B P A B ->
 inter_ll Q A D B C -> 
 inter_ll M A B P Q -> 
 B <> M -> 
 parallel A M B M -> 
 C<>D ->
 A ** M / B ** M = - (1).
Proof.
Admitted.

(* The line going through the midpoints is parallel to the third side *)

Theorem Prop51Hartsshorne :
 forall A B C D E : Point, 
 is_midpoint D A B -> 
 is_midpoint E A C -> 
 parallel D E B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem is_midpoint_A :
 forall A B C A' B' : Point, 
 is_midpoint A' B C -> 
 is_midpoint B' A C -> 
 parallel A' B' A B.
Proof.
Admitted.


Theorem Prop51Hartsshornebis :
 forall A B C D E : Point,
 ~ Col D A C ->
 ~ Col A B C ->
 is_midpoint D A B ->
 is_midpoint E A C -> 
 parallel D E B C -> 
 B <> C -> 
 D ** E / B ** C = 1 / 2.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem th6_40_Centroid :
 forall A B C E F O : Point,
 is_midpoint F A B ->
 is_midpoint E B C -> 
 inter_ll O A E C F -> 
 O <> E -> 
 parallel A O O E -> 
 A ** O / O ** E = 2.
Proof.
Admitted.


Theorem Prop54Hartsshorne :
 forall A B C D E F G : Point,
 is_midpoint D A B ->
 is_midpoint E A C -> 
 is_midpoint F B C -> 
 inter_ll G E B C D -> 
 Col A G F.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Exo55Hartsshorne : 
 forall A B C D I J K L,
 is_midpoint I A B -> 
 is_midpoint J B C -> 
 is_midpoint K C D -> 
 is_midpoint L D A -> 
 parallel I J K L /\ parallel I L J K.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem th6_42 :
 forall A B C L M N P K : Point,
 is_midpoint M A B ->
 is_midpoint N A C ->
 is_midpoint K B C ->
 is_midpoint L A K -> 
 on_inter_parallel_parallel P A C M K B N -> 
 P<>A ->
 (2 + 2) * S A K P = (1 + 2) * S A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem th6_43 :
 forall A B C F N K : Point,
 is_midpoint F A B ->
 is_midpoint N C F ->
 inter_ll K B C A N ->
 K <> C ->
 parallel B K K C ->
 B ** K / K ** C = 2.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Conversemenelaus :
 forall (A B C D E G : Point) (r1 r2 : F),
 mratio D B C r1 ->
 mratio E C A r2 ->
 inter_ll G D E A B ->
 G <> A ->
 parallel B G G A ->
 B ** G / G ** A = - r1 * r2.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem MenelausQuadri :
 forall A B C D X Y A1 B1 C1 D1 : Point,
 inter_ll A1 A B X Y ->
 inter_ll B1 B C X Y ->
 inter_ll C1 C D X Y ->
 inter_ll D1 A D X Y ->
 B <> A1 ->
 C <> B1 ->
 D <> C1 ->
 A <> D1 ->
 parallel A A1 B A1 ->
 parallel B B1 C B1 ->
 parallel C C1 D C1 ->
 parallel D D1 A D1 ->
 A ** A1 / B ** A1 * (B ** B1 / C ** B1 * (C ** C1 / D ** C1 * (D ** D1 / A ** D1))) =
 1.
Proof.
Admitted.


Theorem ConverseMenelauseQuadri :
 forall (A B C D A1 B1 C1 D1 : Point) (r1 r2 : F),
 mratio B1 B C r1 ->
 mratio C1 C D r2 ->
 inter_ll D1 D A B1 C1 ->
 inter_ll A1 A B B1 C1 ->
 A1 <> A ->
 D1 <> A ->
 parallel B A1 A1 A ->
 parallel D D1 D1 A -> B ** A1 / A1 ** A = r1 * (r2 * (D ** D1 / D1 ** A)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem th6_6 :
 forall A B C L M N O : Point,
 inter_ll L B C A O ->
 inter_ll N B A C O ->
 inter_ll M A C B O ->
 A <> L ->
 B <> M ->
 C <> N ->
 parallel O L A L ->
 parallel O M B M ->
 parallel O N C N -> O ** L / A ** L + O ** M / B ** M + O ** N / C ** N = 1.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem th6_7 :
 forall A B C L M N O : Point,
 inter_ll L B C A O ->
 inter_ll N B A C O ->
 inter_ll M A C B O ->
 S A M L * (S B N M * S C L N) = S A N L * (S B L M * S C N M).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem th6_256_1 :
 forall (A B C D P Q R S : Point) (r1 r2 : F),
 on_parallel_d D A B C 1 ->
 on_line_d S D A r2 ->
 on_line_d P A B r1 -> 
 on_line_d R C D r1 -> 
 on_line_d Q B C r2 ->
 P <> S -> 
 parallel Q R P S.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem th6_257 :
 forall (A B C D P Q R S : Point) (r1 r2 : F),
 on_parallel_d D A B C 1 ->
 on_line_d S D A r2 ->
 on_line_d P A B r1 ->
 on_line_d R C D r1 ->
 on_line_d Q B C r2 ->
 S4 P Q R S = (2 * (r2 * r1) - r2 - r1 + 1) * S4 A B C D.
Proof.
Admitted.


Theorem gauss_line :
 forall A0 A1 A2 A3 X Y M1 M2 M3 : Point,
 inter_ll X A0 A3 A1 A2 ->
 inter_ll Y A2 A3 A1 A0 ->
 is_midpoint M1 A1 A3 ->
 is_midpoint M2 A0 A2 ->
 is_midpoint M3 X Y -> 
 S A0 A1 A2 <> 0 ->
 Col M1 M2 M3.
Proof.
Admitted.

(*  Author: Mathias Schack Rabing <mathiasrabing@outlook.com> *)

theory Ceva
imports
  Triangle.Triangle
begin

definition\<^marker>\<open>tag important\<close> Triangle_area :: "'a::real_inner \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real"
  where "Triangle_area x y z = abs(sin (angle x y z)) * dist x y * dist y z"

lemma Triangle_area_per1 : "Triangle_area a b c = Triangle_area b c a"
  by sorry

lemma Triangle_area_per2 : "Triangle_area a b c = Triangle_area b a c"
  by sorry

lemma collinear_angle: 
  fixes a b c :: "'a::euclidean_space"
  shows "collinear {a, b, c} \<Longrightarrow> a \<noteq> b \<Longrightarrow> b \<noteq> c \<Longrightarrow> angle a b c \<in> {0, pi}"
  by sorry

lemma Triangle_area_0 : 
  fixes c :: "'a::euclidean_space"
  shows "Triangle_area a b c = 0 \<longleftrightarrow> collinear {a,b,c}"
  by sorry


lemma Angle_longer_side : 
  fixes a :: "'a :: euclidean_space"
  assumes Col : "between (b,d) c"
  assumes NeqBC : "b \<noteq> c"
  shows "angle a b c = angle a b d"
  by sorry

lemma Triangle_area_comb :
  fixes c :: "'a::euclidean_space"
  assumes Col : "between (b,c) m"
  shows "Triangle_area a b m + Triangle_area a c m = Triangle_area a b c"
  by sorry

lemma Triangle_area_cal :
  fixes a :: "'a::euclidean_space"
  assumes Col : "collinear {a,m,b}"
  shows "\<exists> k. dist a m * k = Triangle_area a c m \<and> dist b m * k = Triangle_area b c m"
  by sorry

lemma Triangle_area_comb_alt :
  fixes a :: "'a::euclidean_space"
  assumes Col1 : "collinear {a,m,b}"
  assumes Col2 : "collinear {c,k,m}"
  shows Goal : "\<exists> h. dist a m * h = Triangle_area a c k \<and> dist b m * h = Triangle_area b c k"
  by sorry

lemma Cevas : 
  fixes a :: "'a::euclidean_space"
  assumes MidCol : "collinear {a,k,d} \<and> collinear {b,k,e} \<and> collinear {c,k,f}"
  assumes TriCol : "collinear {a,f,b} \<and> collinear {a,e,c} \<and> collinear {b,d,c}"
  assumes Triangle : "\<not> collinear {a,b,c}"
  shows "dist a f * dist b d * dist c e = dist f b * dist d c * dist e a"
  by sorry


end

title: 061_theorem_of_ceva
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 061,
;; "Theorem of Ceva." In a nondegenerate real triangle, points X, Y, Z lie
;; on the three side lines and the cevians AX, BY, CZ are concurrent. The
;; corresponding products of Euclidean distances are equal. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; ACL2 has no primitive full real-number sort. The scalar operations below
;; therefore describe an arbitrary real-closed ordered field, with every
;; algebraic, order, and real-closure law used by the statement made explicit.

(defstub ht061-carrier (x) t)
(defstub ht061-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht061-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht061-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub ht061-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub ht061-less-op (x y) t)

(defun ht061-member-p (x)
  (if (ht061-carrier x) t nil))

(defun ht061-add (x y)
  (ht061-add-op x y))

(defun ht061-multiply (x y)
  (ht061-multiply-op x y))

(defun ht061-negate (x)
  (ht061-negate-op x))

(defun ht061-inverse (x)
  (ht061-inverse-op x))

(defun ht061-subtract (x y)
  (ht061-add x (ht061-negate y)))

(defun ht061-less (x y)
  (if (ht061-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun ht061-square (x)
  (ht061-multiply x x))

(defun-sk ht061-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht061-member-p x)
      (ht061-member-p y)
      (ht061-member-p z))
     (and
      (ht061-member-p (ht061-add x y))
      (ht061-member-p (ht061-multiply x y))
      (ht061-member-p (ht061-negate x))
      (ht061-member-p (ht061-inverse x))
      (equal (ht061-add (ht061-add x y) z)
             (ht061-add x (ht061-add y z)))
      (equal (ht061-add x y)
             (ht061-add y x))
      (equal (ht061-add x zero) x)
      (equal (ht061-add x (ht061-negate x)) zero)
      (equal (ht061-multiply (ht061-multiply x y) z)
             (ht061-multiply x (ht061-multiply y z)))
      (equal (ht061-multiply x y)
             (ht061-multiply y x))
      (equal (ht061-multiply x one) x)
      (equal
       (ht061-multiply x (ht061-add y z))
       (ht061-add
        (ht061-multiply x y)
        (ht061-multiply x z)))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (ht061-multiply x (ht061-inverse x))
        one))))))

(defun-sk ht061-order-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht061-member-p x)
      (ht061-member-p y)
      (ht061-member-p z))
     (and
      (not (ht061-less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (ht061-less x y)
       (ht061-less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht061-less x y)
        (ht061-less y z))
       (ht061-less x z))
      (implies
       (ht061-less x y)
       (ht061-less
        (ht061-add x z)
        (ht061-add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht061-less zero x)
        (ht061-less zero y))
       (ht061-less zero (ht061-multiply x y)))))))

(defun ht061-carrier-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (ht061-member-p (car values))
       (ht061-carrier-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun ht061-polynomial-value (coefficients x zero)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (ht061-add
       (car coefficients)
       (ht061-multiply
        x
        (ht061-polynomial-value
         (cdr coefficients) x zero)))
    zero))

(defun ht061-odd-degree-polynomial-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (and
   (consp coefficients)
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (ht061-carrier-list-p coefficients)
   (evenp (len coefficients))
   (not (equal (car (last coefficients)) zero))))

(defun-sk ht061-has-square-root-p (x)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (ht061-member-p root)
     (equal (ht061-square root) x))))

(defun-sk ht061-polynomial-has-root-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (ht061-member-p root)
     (equal
      (ht061-polynomial-value coefficients root zero)
      zero))))

(defun-sk ht061-real-closure-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x coefficients)
    (and
     (implies
      (and
       (ht061-member-p x)
       (not (ht061-less x zero)))
      (ht061-has-square-root-p x))
     (implies
      (ht061-odd-degree-polynomial-p coefficients zero)
      (ht061-polynomial-has-root-p coefficients zero)))))

(defun ht061-real-scalar-context-p (zero one)
  (and
   (ht061-member-p zero)
   (ht061-member-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (ht061-less zero one)
   (ht061-field-laws-p zero one)
   (ht061-order-laws-p zero)
   (ht061-real-closure-laws-p zero)))

;; A point is a dotted pair (x . y) of field elements.

(defun ht061-point-p (point)
  (and
   (consp point)
   (ht061-member-p (car point))
   (ht061-member-p (cdr point))))

(defun ht061-collinear-p (point-a point-b point-c)
  (equal
   (ht061-multiply
    (ht061-subtract (car point-b) (car point-a))
    (ht061-subtract (cdr point-c) (cdr point-a)))
   (ht061-multiply
    (ht061-subtract (cdr point-b) (cdr point-a))
    (ht061-subtract (car point-c) (car point-a)))))

(defun ht061-distance-squared (left right)
  (let ((dx (ht061-subtract (car left) (car right)))
        (dy (ht061-subtract (cdr left) (cdr right))))
    (ht061-add
     (ht061-square dx)
     (ht061-square dy))))

(defun ht061-distance-value-p
    (left right distance zero)
  (and
   (ht061-point-p left)
   (ht061-point-p right)
   (ht061-member-p distance)
   (not (ht061-less distance zero))
   (equal
    (ht061-square distance)
    (ht061-distance-squared left right))))

(defun ht061-ceva-configuration-p
    (point-a point-b point-c
     point-x point-y point-z concurrent-point
     distance-bx distance-cy distance-az
     distance-xc distance-ya distance-zb
     zero)
  (and
   (ht061-point-p point-a)
   (ht061-point-p point-b)
   (ht061-point-p point-c)
   (ht061-point-p point-x)
   (ht061-point-p point-y)
   (ht061-point-p point-z)
   (ht061-point-p concurrent-point)
   (not (ht061-collinear-p point-a point-b point-c))

   ;; X, Y, Z lie on BC, CA, AB.
   (ht061-collinear-p point-b point-x point-c)
   (ht061-collinear-p point-c point-y point-a)
   (ht061-collinear-p point-a point-z point-b)

   ;; The three cevians are concurrent.
   (ht061-collinear-p point-a concurrent-point point-x)
   (ht061-collinear-p point-b concurrent-point point-y)
   (ht061-collinear-p point-c concurrent-point point-z)

   ;; These six nonnegative values are the Euclidean distances in the source.
   (ht061-distance-value-p
    point-b point-x distance-bx zero)
   (ht061-distance-value-p
    point-c point-y distance-cy zero)
   (ht061-distance-value-p
    point-a point-z distance-az zero)
   (ht061-distance-value-p
    point-x point-c distance-xc zero)
   (ht061-distance-value-p
    point-y point-a distance-ya zero)
   (ht061-distance-value-p
    point-z point-b distance-zb zero)))

(defun ht061-ceva-product (first second third)
  (ht061-multiply
   first
   (ht061-multiply second third)))

(defun-sk hundred-theorems-061-theorem-of-ceva-statement
    (zero one)
  (forall
   (point-a point-b point-c
    point-x point-y point-z concurrent-point
    distance-bx distance-cy distance-az
    distance-xc distance-ya distance-zb)
   (implies
    (and
     (ht061-real-scalar-context-p zero one)
     (ht061-ceva-configuration-p
      point-a point-b point-c
      point-x point-y point-z concurrent-point
      distance-bx distance-cy distance-az
      distance-xc distance-ya distance-zb
      zero))
    (equal
     (ht061-ceva-product
      distance-bx distance-cy distance-az)
     (ht061-ceva-product
      distance-xc distance-ya distance-zb)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 061_theorem_of_ceva
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Theorem of Ceva" from Hundred Theorems item 061:
-- three vertex lines through points on the opposite side lines of a nondegenerate
-- real Euclidean triangle meet at one point only if the corresponding triple
-- products of distances are equal. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Natural : Set where
  natZero : Natural
  natSuc  : Natural -> Natural

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    zero one : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Natural -> R

    one-not-zero :
      one != zero

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zero == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zero

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x one == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zero == zero
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zero ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == one

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zero x ->
      lessOrEqual zero y ->
      lessOrEqual zero (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zero one and zero != one

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat natZero == zero
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Natural) -> fromNat (natSuc n) == add (fromNat n) one
    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Natural (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

SquaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
SquaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

Collinear :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
Collinear reals a b c =
  subtract reals
    (multiply reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate a) (x-coordinate b))
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate c) (y-coordinate b)))
    (multiply reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate a) (y-coordinate b))
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate c) (x-coordinate b)))
  == zero reals

record EuclideanPlane
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) :
  Set₁ where

  field
    distance : Point R -> Point R -> R

    distance-nonnegative :
      (p q : Point R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zero reals) (distance p q)
    distance-self :
      (p : Point R) ->
      distance p p == zero reals
    distance-separates :
      (p q : Point R) ->
      distance p q == zero reals ->
      p == q
    distance-symmetric :
      (p q : Point R) ->
      distance p q == distance q p
    distance-triangle :
      (p q r : Point R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (distance p r)
        (add reals (distance p q) (distance q r))
    distance-square :
      (p q : Point R) ->
      square reals (distance p q) ==
      SquaredDistance reals p q

open EuclideanPlane

module CevaStatement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (plane : EuclideanPlane reals) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a b c d e f p : Point R) ->
    Not (Collinear reals a b c) ->
    Collinear reals b d c ->
    Collinear reals c e a ->
    Collinear reals a f b ->
    Collinear reals a p d ->
    Collinear reals b p e ->
    Collinear reals c p f ->
    multiply reals
      (multiply reals
        (distance plane b d)
        (distance plane c e))
      (distance plane a f)
    ==
    multiply reals
      (multiply reals
        (distance plane d c)
        (distance plane e a))
      (distance plane f b)

theorem-of-ceva : Set₁
theorem-of-ceva =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (plane : EuclideanPlane reals) ->
  CevaStatement.proposition reals plane

title: 061_theorem_of_ceva
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Theorem of Ceva" from Hundred Theorems
  item 061: for a noncollinear triangle in the real coordinate plane, three
  concurrent cevians through points on the opposite side lines imply equality
  of the corresponding triple products of distances. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open realTheory transcTheory;

val theorem_of_ceva =
  ``!ax ay bx by cx cy xx xy yx yy zx zy px py : real.
      ~((ax - bx) * (cy - by) = (ay - by) * (cx - bx)) /\
      (bx - xx) * (cy - xy) = (by - xy) * (cx - xx) /\
      (cx - yx) * (ay - yy) = (cy - yy) * (ax - yx) /\
      (ax - zx) * (by - zy) = (ay - zy) * (bx - zx) /\
      (ax - px) * (xy - py) = (ay - py) * (xx - px) /\
      (bx - px) * (yy - py) = (by - py) * (yx - px) /\
      (cx - px) * (zy - py) = (cy - py) * (zx - px)
      ==>
      sqrt ((bx - xx) pow 2 + (by - xy) pow 2) *
        sqrt ((cx - yx) pow 2 + (cy - yy) pow 2) *
        sqrt ((ax - zx) pow 2 + (ay - zy) pow 2) =
      sqrt ((xx - cx) pow 2 + (xy - cy) pow 2) *
        sqrt ((yx - ax) pow 2 + (yy - ay) pow 2) *
        sqrt ((zx - bx) pow 2 + (zy - by) pow 2)``;

title: 061_theorem_of_ceva
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 061, Ceva's theorem.

  This reproduces set.mm theorem cevath in the complex-plane model of
  Euclidean geometry. The essential hypotheses state the required
  collinearities and nondegeneracy conditions; the conclusion is the
  multiplicative Ceva relation.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

${
  $d x y A $.
  $d x B y $.
  $d x C y $.
  $d x D y $.
  $d x O y $.
  $d x E y $.
  $d x F y $.

  hundred-theorems-061-oriented-area $e
    |- G =
       ( x e. CC , y e. CC |->
         ( Im ` ( ( * ` x ) x. y ) ) )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-061-triangle $e
    |- ( ph -> ( A e. CC /\ B e. CC /\ C e. CC ) )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-061-side-points $e
    |- ( ph -> ( F e. CC /\ D e. CC /\ E e. CC ) )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-061-concurrency-point $e
    |- ( ph -> O e. CC )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-061-concurrent $e
    |- (
         ph
         ->
         (
           ( ( A - O ) G ( D - O ) ) = 0
           /\
           ( ( B - O ) G ( E - O ) ) = 0
           /\
           ( ( C - O ) G ( F - O ) ) = 0
         )
       )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-061-on-sides $e
    |- (
         ph
         ->
         (
           ( ( A - F ) G ( B - F ) ) = 0
           /\
           ( ( B - D ) G ( C - D ) ) = 0
           /\
           ( ( C - E ) G ( A - E ) ) = 0
         )
       )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-061-nondegenerate $e
    |- (
         ph
         ->
         (
           ( ( A - O ) G ( B - O ) ) =/= 0
           /\
           ( ( B - O ) G ( C - O ) ) =/= 0
           /\
           ( ( C - O ) G ( A - O ) ) =/= 0
         )
       )
  $.

  hundred-theorems-061-ceva $a
    |- (
         ph
         ->
         (
           ( ( A - F ) x. ( C - E ) ) x. ( B - D )
         )
         =
         (
           ( ( F - B ) x. ( E - A ) ) x. ( D - C )
         )
       )
  $.
$}

title: 061_theorem_of_ceva
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Theorem of Ceva" from Hundred Theorems item 061:
% concurrent cevians of a nondegenerate triangle give equality of the two products of
% the six associated side-segment distances. This file contains no proof.

theorem_of_ceva_061[
  V: TYPE+,
  zero: V,
  vadd: [V, V -> V],
  vneg: [V -> V],
  scale: [real, V -> V],
  inner: [V, V -> real]
]: THEORY
BEGIN
  vector_space_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (u, v: V): vadd(u, v) = vadd(v, u))
      AND (FORALL (u, v, w: V):
        vadd(vadd(u, v), w) = vadd(u, vadd(v, w)))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): vadd(u, zero) = u)
      AND (FORALL (u: V): vadd(u, vneg(u)) = zero)
      AND (FORALL (a: real), (u, v: V):
        scale(a, vadd(u, v)) = vadd(scale(a, u), scale(a, v)))
      AND (FORALL (a, b: real), (u: V):
        scale(a + b, u) = vadd(scale(a, u), scale(b, u)))
      AND (FORALL (a, b: real), (u: V):
        scale(a * b, u) = scale(a, scale(b, u)))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): scale(1, u) = u)
      AND (FORALL (u: V): scale(0, u) = zero)
      AND (FORALL (u: V): vneg(u) = scale(-1, u))

  inner_product_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (u, v, w: V):
      inner(vadd(u, v), w) = inner(u, w) + inner(v, w))
      AND (FORALL (a: real), (u, v: V):
        inner(scale(a, u), v) = a * inner(u, v))
      AND (FORALL (u, v: V): inner(u, v) = inner(v, u))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): 0 <= inner(u, u))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): inner(u, u) = 0 IFF u = zero)

  real_inner_product_space: bool =
    vector_space_laws AND inner_product_laws

  displacement(P, Q: V): V =
    vadd(Q, vneg(P))

  squared_distance(P, Q: V): real =
    inner(displacement(P, Q), displacement(P, Q))

  distance_value(length: real, P, Q: V): bool =
    0 <= length AND length * length = squared_distance(P, Q)

  on_line(X, A, B: V): bool =
    EXISTS (t: real):
      X = vadd(A, scale(t, displacement(A, B)))

  collinear(A, B, C: V): bool =
    A = B OR B = C OR C = A OR on_line(C, A, B)

  ceva_distance_identity(A, B, C, D, E, F: V): bool =
    EXISTS (AF, FB, BD, DC, CE, EA: real):
      distance_value(AF, A, F)
        AND distance_value(FB, F, B)
        AND distance_value(BD, B, D)
        AND distance_value(DC, D, C)
        AND distance_value(CE, C, E)
        AND distance_value(EA, E, A)
        AND AF * BD * CE = FB * DC * EA

  theorem_of_ceva: bool =
    real_inner_product_space IMPLIES
      (FORALL (A, B, C, D, E, F, P: V):
        (NOT collinear(A, B, C)
          AND on_line(D, B, C)
          AND on_line(E, C, A)
          AND on_line(F, A, B)
          AND on_line(P, A, D)
          AND on_line(P, B, E)
          AND on_line(P, C, F))
        IMPLIES ceva_distance_identity(A, B, C, D, E, F))
END theorem_of_ceva_061

title: 062_fair_games_theorem__optional_stopping
content:
/-

Authors: Kexing Ying

module

public import Mathlib.Probability.Notation
public import Mathlib.Probability.Process.HittingTime
public import Mathlib.Probability.Martingale.Basic

/-! # Optional stopping theorem (fair game theorem)

The optional stopping theorem states that a strongly adapted integrable process `f` is a
submartingale if and only if for all bounded stopping times `τ` and `π` such that `τ ≤ π`, the
stopped value of `f` at `τ` has expectation smaller than its stopped value at `π`.

This file also contains Doob's maximal inequality: given a non-negative submartingale `f`, for all
`ε : ℝ≥0`, we have `ε • μ {ε ≤ f* n} ≤ ∫ ω in {ε ≤ f* n}, f n` where `f * n ω = max_{k ≤ n}, f k ω`.

### Main results

* `MeasureTheory.submartingale_iff_expected_stoppedValue_mono`: the optional stopping theorem.
* `MeasureTheory.Submartingale.stoppedProcess`: the stopped process of a submartingale with
  respect to a stopping time is a submartingale.
* `MeasureTheory.maximal_ineq`: Doob's maximal inequality.

-/

public section


open scoped NNReal ENNReal MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

namespace MeasureTheory

variable {Ω : Type*} {m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω} {𝒢 : Filtration ℕ m0} {f : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
  {τ π : Ω → ℕ∞}

/-- Given a submartingale `f` and bounded stopping times `τ` and `π` such that `τ ≤ π`, the
expectation of `stoppedValue f τ` is less than or equal to the expectation of `stoppedValue f π`.
This is the forward direction of the optional stopping theorem. -/
theorem Submartingale.expected_stoppedValue_mono {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] [PartialOrder E] [IsOrderedAddMonoid E]
    [IsOrderedModule ℝ E] [ClosedIciTopology E] [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ 𝒢] {f : ℕ → Ω → E}
    (hf : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime 𝒢 τ) (hπ : IsStoppingTime 𝒢 π) (hle : τ ≤ π)
    {N : ℕ} (hbdd : ∀ ω, π ω ≤ N) : μ[stoppedValue f τ] ≤ μ[stoppedValue f π] := by sorry
theorem submartingale_of_expected_stoppedValue_mono [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ 𝒢]
    (hadp : StronglyAdapted 𝒢 f)
    (hint : ∀ i, Integrable (f i) μ) (hf : ∀ τ π : Ω → ℕ∞, IsStoppingTime 𝒢 τ → IsStoppingTime 𝒢 π →
      τ ≤ π → (∃ N : ℕ, ∀ ω, π ω ≤ N) → μ[stoppedValue f τ] ≤ μ[stoppedValue f π]) :
    Submartingale f 𝒢 μ := by sorry
theorem submartingale_iff_expected_stoppedValue_mono [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ 𝒢]
    (hadp : StronglyAdapted 𝒢 f) (hint : ∀ i, Integrable (f i) μ) :
    Submartingale f 𝒢 μ ↔ ∀ τ π : Ω → ℕ∞, IsStoppingTime 𝒢 τ → IsStoppingTime 𝒢 π →
      τ ≤ π → (∃ N : ℕ, ∀ x, π x ≤ N) → μ[stoppedValue f τ] ≤ μ[stoppedValue f π] :=
  ⟨fun hf _ _ hτ hπ hle ⟨_, hN⟩ => hf.expected_stoppedValue_mono hτ hπ hle hN,
    submartingale_of_expected_stoppedValue_mono hadp hint⟩

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- The stopped process of a submartingale with respect to a stopping time is a submartingale. -/
protected theorem Submartingale.stoppedProcess [SigmaFiniteFiltration μ 𝒢]
    (h : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ) (hτ : IsStoppingTime 𝒢 τ) :
    Submartingale (stoppedProcess f τ) 𝒢 μ := by sorry
section Maximal

open Finset

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
theorem smul_le_stoppedValue_hittingBtwn [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hsub : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ) {ε : ℝ≥0}
    (n : ℕ) : ε • μ {ω | (ε : ℝ) ≤ (range (n + 1)).sup' nonempty_range_add_one fun k => f k ω} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal
      (∫ ω in {ω | (ε : ℝ) ≤ (range (n + 1)).sup' nonempty_range_add_one fun k => f k ω},
      stoppedValue f (fun ω ↦ (hittingBtwn f {y : ℝ | ε ≤ y} 0 n ω : ℕ)) ω ∂μ) := by sorry
theorem maximal_ineq [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hsub : Submartingale f 𝒢 μ) (hnonneg : 0 ≤ f) {ε : ℝ≥0}
    (n : ℕ) : ε * μ {ω | (ε : ℝ) ≤ (range (n + 1)).sup' nonempty_range_add_one fun k => f k ω} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal
      (∫ ω in {ω | (ε : ℝ) ≤ (range (n + 1)).sup' nonempty_range_add_one fun k => f k ω},
        f n ω ∂μ) := by sorry
end Maximal

end MeasureTheory

title: 062_fair_games_theorem__optional_stopping
content:
(*
  The discrete-time optional stopping theorem.  The stopped value and all
  three standard sufficient conditions are explicit in the statement.
*)

Require Import QArith Morphisms Equivalence Program.Basics Lra Lia.
Require Import Classical ClassicalChoice RelationClasses.
Require Import FunctionalExtensionality.
Require Import IndefiniteDescription ClassicalDescription.

Require Export ConditionalExpectation.
Require Import RbarExpectation Event Almost DVector utils.Utils List PushNeg.
Require Import Reals Coquelicot.Rbar Coquelicot.Lim_seq Martingale.

Set Bullet Behavior "Strict Subproofs".

Section StoppedProcessDefinitions.

Context {Ts : Type}.

Definition lift1_min (n : nat) (time : option nat) : nat :=
  match time with
  | None => n
  | Some k => min n k
  end.

Definition process_stopped_at
    (Y : nat -> Ts -> R) (T : Ts -> option nat)
    (n : nat) (omega : Ts) : R :=
  Y (lift1_min n (T omega)) omega.

Definition process_under
    (Y : nat -> Ts -> R) (T : Ts -> option nat)
    (omega : Ts) : R :=
  match T omega with
  | None => 0
  | Some n => Y n omega
  end.

End StoppedProcessDefinitions.

Local Existing Instance Rge_pre.
Local Existing Instance Rle_pre.

Section OptionalStopping.

Context
  {Ts : Type}
  {sigma : SigmaAlgebra Ts}
  (prts : ProbSpace sigma)
  (F : nat -> SigmaAlgebra Ts)
  {filt : IsFiltration F}
  {sub : IsSubAlgebras sigma F}
  (tau : Ts -> option nat)
  {is_stop : IsStoppingTime tau F}
  (Y : nat -> Ts -> R)
  {rv : forall n, RandomVariable sigma borel_sa (Y n)}
  {isfe : forall n, IsFiniteExpectation prts (Y n)}
  {adapt : IsAdapted borel_sa Y F}
  (conditions :
    (exists N : nat,
       almost prts
         (fun omega =>
            match tau omega with
            | Some k => (k <= N)%nat
            | None => False
            end))
    \/
    (almost prts (fun omega => tau omega <> None) /\
     exists K : R,
       forall n, almost prts (fun omega => Rabs (Y n omega) < K))
    \/
    (Rbar_IsFiniteExpectation prts
       (fun omega =>
          match tau omega with
          | Some n => INR n
          | None => p_infty
          end) /\
     exists K : R,
       forall n,
         almost prts
           (fun omega => Rabs (Y (S n) omega - Y n omega) <= K))).

Instance optional_stopping_time_isfe :
  IsFiniteExpectation prts (process_under Y tau).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem optional_stopping_time
    {mart : IsMartingale prts eq Y F} :
  FiniteExpectation prts (process_under Y tau) =
  FiniteExpectation prts (Y 0%nat).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem optional_stopping_time_sub
    {mart : IsMartingale prts Rle Y F} :
  FiniteExpectation prts (process_under Y tau) >=
  FiniteExpectation prts (Y 0%nat).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem optional_stopping_time_super
    {mart : IsMartingale prts Rge Y F} :
  FiniteExpectation prts (process_under Y tau) <=
  FiniteExpectation prts (Y 0%nat).
Proof.
Admitted.

End OptionalStopping.

title: 062_fair_games_theorem__optional_stopping
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 062,
  "Fair Games Theorem (Optional Stopping)": discrete-time martingale,
  submartingale, and supermartingale expectation laws at stopping times.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory Fair_Games_Theorem_Optional_Stopping
  imports
    "HOL-Probability.Conditional_Expectation"
    "HOL-Probability.Stopping_Time"
begin

definition adapted_process ::
    "(nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure) \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  where
    "adapted_process F X \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>n. X n \<in> borel_measurable (F n))"

definition integrable_process ::
    "'a measure \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  where
    "integrable_process M X \<longleftrightarrow> (\<forall>n. integrable M (X n))"

definition martingale_process ::
    "'a measure \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure) \<Rightarrow>
      (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  where
    "martingale_process M F X \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>n. AE \<omega> in M.
        real_cond_exp M (F n) (X (Suc n)) \<omega> = X n \<omega>)"

definition submartingale_process ::
    "'a measure \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure) \<Rightarrow>
      (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  where
    "submartingale_process M F X \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>n. AE \<omega> in M.
        X n \<omega> \<le> real_cond_exp M (F n) (X (Suc n)) \<omega>)"

definition supermartingale_process ::
    "'a measure \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure) \<Rightarrow>
      (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  where
    "supermartingale_process M F X \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>n. AE \<omega> in M.
        real_cond_exp M (F n) (X (Suc n)) \<omega> \<le> X n \<omega>)"

definition extended_filtration ::
    "'a measure \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure) \<Rightarrow> enat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure"
  where
    "extended_filtration M F t =
      (case t of enat n \<Rightarrow> F n | \<infinity> \<Rightarrow> M)"

definition discrete_stopping_time ::
    "'a measure \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure) \<Rightarrow> ('a \<Rightarrow> enat) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  where
    "discrete_stopping_time M F T \<longleftrightarrow>
      stopping_time (extended_filtration M F) T"

definition stopped_value ::
    "(nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> ('a \<Rightarrow> enat) \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real"
  where
    "stopped_value X T \<omega> =
      (case T \<omega> of enat n \<Rightarrow> X n \<omega> | \<infinity> \<Rightarrow> 0)"

definition optional_stopping_conditions ::
    "'a measure \<Rightarrow> ('a \<Rightarrow> enat) \<Rightarrow>
      (nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  where
    "optional_stopping_conditions M T X \<longleftrightarrow>
      ((\<exists>N::nat. AE \<omega> in M. T \<omega> \<le> enat N) \<or>
       ((AE \<omega> in M. T \<omega> \<noteq> \<infinity>) \<and>
        (\<exists>K::real. \<forall>n. AE \<omega> in M. abs (X n \<omega>) < K)) \<or>
       ((AE \<omega> in M. T \<omega> \<noteq> \<infinity>) \<and>
        integrable M (\<lambda>\<omega>. real (the_enat (T \<omega>))) \<and>
        (\<exists>K::real. \<forall>n. AE \<omega> in M.
          abs (X (Suc n) \<omega> - X n \<omega>) \<le> K)))"

theorem submartingale_iff_expected_stopped_value_mono:
  fixes M :: "'a measure"
    and F :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure"
    and X :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real"
  assumes "filtration (space M) F"
    and "\<And>n. sigma_finite_subalgebra M (F n)"
    and "adapted_process F X"
    and "integrable_process M X"
  shows "submartingale_process M F X \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>T S :: 'a \<Rightarrow> enat.
      discrete_stopping_time M F T \<longrightarrow>
      discrete_stopping_time M F S \<longrightarrow>
      (\<forall>\<omega>. T \<omega> \<le> S \<omega>) \<longrightarrow>
      (\<exists>N::nat. \<forall>\<omega>. S \<omega> \<le> enat N) \<longrightarrow>
      (\<integral>\<omega>. stopped_value X T \<omega> \<partial>M) \<le>
        (\<integral>\<omega>. stopped_value X S \<omega> \<partial>M))"
  sorry

theorem fair_games_optional_stopping:
  fixes M :: "'a measure"
    and F :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure"
    and X :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real"
    and T :: "'a \<Rightarrow> enat"
  assumes "prob_space M"
    and "filtration (space M) F"
    and "\<And>n. subalgebra M (F n)"
    and "adapted_process F X"
    and "integrable_process M X"
    and "discrete_stopping_time M F T"
    and "optional_stopping_conditions M T X"
    and "martingale_process M F X"
  shows "(\<integral>\<omega>. stopped_value X T \<omega> \<partial>M) =
    (\<integral>\<omega>. X 0 \<omega> \<partial>M)"
  sorry

theorem submartingale_optional_stopping:
  fixes M :: "'a measure"
    and F :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure"
    and X :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real"
    and T :: "'a \<Rightarrow> enat"
  assumes "prob_space M"
    and "filtration (space M) F"
    and "\<And>n. subalgebra M (F n)"
    and "adapted_process F X"
    and "integrable_process M X"
    and "discrete_stopping_time M F T"
    and "optional_stopping_conditions M T X"
    and "submartingale_process M F X"
  shows "(\<integral>\<omega>. X 0 \<omega> \<partial>M) \<le>
    (\<integral>\<omega>. stopped_value X T \<omega> \<partial>M)"
  sorry

theorem supermartingale_optional_stopping:
  fixes M :: "'a measure"
    and F :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a measure"
    and X :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> real"
    and T :: "'a \<Rightarrow> enat"
  assumes "prob_space M"
    and "filtration (space M) F"
    and "\<And>n. subalgebra M (F n)"
    and "adapted_process F X"
    and "integrable_process M X"
    and "discrete_stopping_time M F T"
    and "optional_stopping_conditions M T X"
    and "supermartingale_process M F X"
  shows "(\<integral>\<omega>. stopped_value X T \<omega> \<partial>M) \<le>
    (\<integral>\<omega>. X 0 \<omega> \<partial>M)"
  sorry

end

title: 062_fair_games_theorem__optional_stopping
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Fair Games Theorem (Optional Stopping)"
  from Hundred Theorems artifact 062 (hundred-theorems__hol-light__062).
  It states both the bounded-stopping-time characterization of submartingales
  and the fair-game expectation conclusions for martingales, submartingales,
  and supermartingales under the standard optional-stopping hypotheses. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let HUNDRED_THEOREMS_062_FAIR_GAMES_THEOREM =
 `let seq_tends =
      \(u:num->real) l.
        !e. &0 < e ==> ?N. !n. N <= n ==> abs(u n - l) < e in
   let sigma_algebra =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool).
        (!s. s IN events ==> s SUBSET carrier) /\
        {} IN events /\
        carrier IN events /\
        (!s. s IN events ==> carrier DIFF s IN events) /\
        (!sets:num->A->bool.
           (!n. sets n IN events)
           ==> {x:A | ?n. x IN sets n} IN events) in
   let probability_space =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (p:(A->bool)->real).
        sigma_algebra carrier events /\
        p {} = &0 /\
        p carrier = &1 /\
        (!s. s IN events ==> &0 <= p s) /\
        (!sets:num->A->bool.
           (!n. sets n IN events) /\
           (!m n. ~(m = n) ==> DISJOINT (sets m) (sets n))
           ==> seq_tends
                 (\n. sum {k:num | k < n} (\k. p (sets k)))
                 (p {x:A | ?k. x IN sets k})) in
   let random_variable =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool) (Y:A->real).
        !r. {x:A | x IN carrier /\ Y x <= r} IN events in
   let filtration =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (FF:num->(A->bool)->bool).
        (!n. sigma_algebra carrier (FF n) /\ FF n SUBSET events) /\
        (!m n. m <= n ==> FF m SUBSET FF n) in
   let adapted =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (FF:num->(A->bool)->bool)
       (X:num->A->real).
        !n. random_variable carrier (FF n) (X n) in
   let nonnegative_expectation =
      \(p:(A->bool)->real) (carrier:A->bool) (Y:A->real) e.
        (!x. x IN carrier ==> &0 <= Y x) /\
        seq_tends
          (\n. inv(&(2 EXP n)) *
               sum {k:num | 1 <= k /\ k <= n * 2 EXP n}
                 (\k. p {x:A | x IN carrier /\
                                  &k / &(2 EXP n) <= Y x}))
          e in
   let has_expectation =
      \(p:(A->bool)->real) (carrier:A->bool) (Y:A->real) e.
        ?ep en.
          nonnegative_expectation p carrier
            (\x. if &0 <= Y x then Y x else &0) ep /\
          nonnegative_expectation p carrier
            (\x. if Y x < &0 then --(Y x) else &0) en /\
          e = ep - en in
   let integrable =
      \(p:(A->bool)->real) (carrier:A->bool) (Y:A->real).
        ?e. has_expectation p carrier Y e in
   let expectation =
      \(p:(A->bool)->real) (carrier:A->bool) (Y:A->real).
        @e. has_expectation p carrier Y e in
   let almost_surely =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (p:(A->bool)->real) (P:A->bool).
        ?negligible:A->bool.
          negligible IN events /\
          p negligible = &0 /\
          {x:A | x IN carrier /\ ~(P x)} SUBSET negligible in
   let indicator =
      \(a:A->bool) x. if x IN a then &1 else &0 in
   let martingale =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (p:(A->bool)->real) (FF:num->(A->bool)->bool)
       (X:num->A->real).
        filtration carrier events FF /\
        adapted carrier FF X /\
        (!n. integrable p carrier (X n)) /\
        (!n a. a IN FF n
          ==> expectation p carrier
                (\x. X (SUC n) x * indicator a x) =
              expectation p carrier
                (\x. X n x * indicator a x)) in
   let submartingale =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (p:(A->bool)->real) (FF:num->(A->bool)->bool)
       (X:num->A->real).
        filtration carrier events FF /\
        adapted carrier FF X /\
        (!n. integrable p carrier (X n)) /\
        (!n a. a IN FF n
          ==> expectation p carrier
                (\x. X n x * indicator a x) <=
              expectation p carrier
                (\x. X (SUC n) x * indicator a x)) in
   let supermartingale =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (p:(A->bool)->real) (FF:num->(A->bool)->bool)
       (X:num->A->real).
        filtration carrier events FF /\
        adapted carrier FF X /\
        (!n. integrable p carrier (X n)) /\
        (!n a. a IN FF n
          ==> expectation p carrier
                (\x. X (SUC n) x * indicator a x) <=
              expectation p carrier
                (\x. X n x * indicator a x)) in
   let stopping_time =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (FF:num->(A->bool)->bool) (tau:A->num).
        !n. {x:A | x IN carrier /\ tau x <= n} IN FF n in
   let option_stopping_time =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (FF:num->(A->bool)->bool)
       (tau:A->num option).
        !n. {x:A | x IN carrier /\
                    ?k. tau x = SOME k /\ k <= n} IN FF n in
   let option_stopped_value =
      \(X:num->A->real) (tau:A->num option) x.
        X (@n. tau x = SOME n) x in
   let optional_stopping_conditions =
      \(carrier:A->bool) (events:(A->bool)->bool)
       (p:(A->bool)->real) (X:num->A->real) (tau:A->num option).
        (?N. almost_surely carrier events p
               (\x. ?k. tau x = SOME k /\ k <= N)) \/
        (almost_surely carrier events p
           (\x. ?k. tau x = SOME k) /\
         ?K. !n. almost_surely carrier events p
                    (\x. abs(X n x) < K)) \/
        (almost_surely carrier events p
           (\x. ?k. tau x = SOME k) /\
         integrable p carrier (\x. &(@n. tau x = SOME n)) /\
         ?K. !n. almost_surely carrier events p
                    (\x. abs(X (SUC n) x - X n x) <= K)) in
   (!carrier:A->bool
     events:(A->bool)->bool
     p:(A->bool)->real
     FF:num->(A->bool)->bool
     X:num->A->real.
       probability_space carrier events p /\
       filtration carrier events FF /\
       adapted carrier FF X /\
       (!n. integrable p carrier (X n))
       ==>
       (submartingale carrier events p FF X <=>
        !sigma tau:A->num.
          stopping_time carrier FF sigma /\
          stopping_time carrier FF tau /\
          (!x. x IN carrier ==> sigma x <= tau x) /\
          (?N. !x. x IN carrier ==> tau x <= N)
          ==> expectation p carrier (\x. X (sigma x) x) <=
              expectation p carrier (\x. X (tau x) x))) /\
   (!carrier:A->bool
     events:(A->bool)->bool
     p:(A->bool)->real
     FF:num->(A->bool)->bool
     tau:A->num option
     X:num->A->real.
       probability_space carrier events p /\
       filtration carrier events FF /\
       option_stopping_time carrier FF tau /\
       adapted carrier FF X /\
       (!n. integrable p carrier (X n)) /\
       optional_stopping_conditions carrier events p X tau
       ==>
       (integrable p carrier (option_stopped_value X tau) /\
        (martingale carrier events p FF X
         ==> expectation p carrier (option_stopped_value X tau) =
             expectation p carrier (X 0)) /\
        (submartingale carrier events p FF X
         ==> expectation p carrier (X 0) <=
             expectation p carrier (option_stopped_value X tau)) /\
        (supermartingale carrier events p FF X
         ==> expectation p carrier (option_stopped_value X tau) <=
             expectation p carrier (X 0))))`;;

title: 062_fair_games_theorem__optional_stopping

;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems corpus artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__062, "Fair Games Theorem (Optional Stopping)".
;;
;; The five indexed statements below cover the bounded-stopping-time
;; characterization of submartingales and the standard optional-stopping
;; conclusions under the three hypotheses used by the Rocq source.
;; This file contains no proof.
;;
;; Semantic status: the first-order rewrite below repairs the former vacuous
;; APPLY$ quantifiers, but its stub-coded events, random variables, filtrations,
;; and expectations do not range over the unrestricted probability objects in
;; the source. Standard ACL2 therefore cannot count this as a faithful
;; translation.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The mathematical structures are ordinary first-order codes.  These
;; unconstrained operations provide their generic signature; every required
;; law is stated explicitly in the hypotheses below.  In particular, no
;; generated lambda or APPLY$ warrant is used to encode a quantifier.

;; Scalar field.

(defstub ht062-scalar-p (field value) t)
(defstub ht062-zero (field) t)
(defstub ht062-one (field) t)
(defstub ht062-add (field left right) t)

(defstub ht062-filtration-sigma (space filtration index) t)

;; Random-variable and process codes.

(defstub ht062-variable-p (field space variable) t)
(defstub ht062-variable-value (field space variable omega) t)
(defstub ht062-sublevel-event
  (field space variable threshold) t)

  (field space variable positivep threshold) t)

(defstub ht062-process-value
  (field space process index omega) t)
(defstub ht062-process-fiber
  (field space process index) t)

  (field space variable event) t)

;; Extended-natural stopping-time codes and their canonical constructions.

(defstub ht062-stopping-code-p (space stopping-time) t)

  (space stopping-time omega) t)

  (space stopping-time omega) t)

  (field space stopping-time) t)

;; Ordered-field operations.
