:q

title: 065_isosceles_triangle_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Isosceles Triangle Theorem" from Hundred Theorems
-- item 065: in a real inner-product space, equal sides from the apex imply equal
-- base angles, including for degenerate triangles. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Natural : Set where
  natZero : Natural
  natSuc  : Natural -> Natural

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zero one : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Natural -> R

    one-not-zero :
      one != zero

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zero == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zero

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x one == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zero == zero
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zero ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == one
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zero == zero

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zero x ->
      lessOrEqual zero y ->
      lessOrEqual zero (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zero one and zero != one

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat natZero == zero
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Natural) -> fromNat (natSuc n) == add (fromNat n) one
    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Natural (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

record RealInnerProductAngleSpace
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (V : Set) : Set1 where

  open CompleteOrderedField reals

  field
    zeroV : V
    addV : V -> V -> V
    negateV : V -> V
    scale : R -> V -> V

    addV-commutative :
      (u v : V) -> addV u v == addV v u
    addV-associative :
      (u v w : V) -> addV (addV u v) w == addV u (addV v w)
    addV-zero :
      (v : V) -> addV v zeroV == v
    addV-inverse :
      (v : V) -> addV v (negateV v) == zeroV

    scale-addV :
      (a : R) (u v : V) ->
      scale a (addV u v) == addV (scale a u) (scale a v)
    add-scale :
      (a b : R) (v : V) ->
      scale (add a b) v == addV (scale a v) (scale b v)
    multiply-scale :
      (a b : R) (v : V) ->
      scale (multiply a b) v == scale a (scale b v)
    one-scale :
      (v : V) -> scale one v == v

    inner : V -> V -> R
    inner-add-left :
      (u v w : V) ->
      inner (addV u v) w == add (inner u w) (inner v w)
    inner-scale-left :
      (a : R) (u v : V) ->
      inner (scale a u) v == multiply a (inner u v)
    inner-symmetric :
      (u v : V) -> inner u v == inner v u
    inner-nonnegative :
      (v : V) -> lessOrEqual zero (inner v v)
    inner-definite :
      (v : V) -> inner v v == zero -> v == zeroV

    norm : V -> R
    norm-nonnegative :
      (v : V) -> lessOrEqual zero (norm v)
    norm-square :
      (v : V) -> multiply (norm v) (norm v) == inner v v
    norm-zero :
      (v : V) -> norm v == zero -> v == zeroV
    norm-negate :
      (v : V) -> norm (negateV v) == norm v

    pi halfPi : R
    cosine : R -> R
    vectorAngle : V -> V -> R

    half-pi-doubles :
      add halfPi halfPi == pi
    cosine-half-pi :
      cosine halfPi == zero

    vector-angle-symmetric :
      (u v : V) -> vectorAngle u v == vectorAngle v u
    vector-angle-zero-left :
      (v : V) -> vectorAngle zeroV v == halfPi
    vector-angle-zero-right :
      (v : V) -> vectorAngle v zeroV == halfPi
    vector-angle-nonnegative :
      (u v : V) -> lessOrEqual zero (vectorAngle u v)
    vector-angle-at-most-pi :
      (u v : V) -> lessOrEqual (vectorAngle u v) pi
    vector-angle-cosine :
      (u v : V) ->
      inner u v ==
      multiply
        (multiply (norm u) (norm v))
        (cosine (vectorAngle u v))
    cosine-injective-on-angle-range :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zero x ->
      lessOrEqual x pi ->
      lessOrEqual zero y ->
      lessOrEqual y pi ->
      cosine x == cosine y ->
      x == y

open CompleteOrderedField
open RealInnerProductAngleSpace

subtractV :
  {R V : Set} ->
  {reals : CompleteOrderedField R} ->
  RealInnerProductAngleSpace reals V ->
  V ->
  V ->
  V
subtractV space u v =
  addV space u (negateV space v)

distance :
  {R V : Set} ->
  {reals : CompleteOrderedField R} ->
  RealInnerProductAngleSpace reals V ->
  V ->
  V ->
  R
distance space p q =
  norm space (subtractV space p q)

angleAt :
  {R V : Set} ->
  {reals : CompleteOrderedField R} ->
  RealInnerProductAngleSpace reals V ->
  V ->
  V ->
  V ->
  R
angleAt space a b c =
  vectorAngle space
    (subtractV space a b)
    (subtractV space c b)

module IsoscelesTriangleStatement
  {R V : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (space : RealInnerProductAngleSpace reals V) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a b c : V) ->
    distance space a c == distance space b c ->
    angleAt space b a c == angleAt space a b c

isosceles-triangle-theorem : Set1
isosceles-triangle-theorem =
  (R V : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (space : RealInnerProductAngleSpace reals V) ->
  IsoscelesTriangleStatement.proposition reals space

title: 065_isosceles_triangle_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Isosceles Triangle Theorem" from Hundred
  Theorems artifact 065: in any real inner-product space, equal lengths of the
  two sides meeting at the apex imply equality of the base angles, including
  degenerate triangles. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open realTheory transcTheory;

val isosceles_triangle_theorem =
  ``let is_real_inner_space =
      \(zero : 'a)
       (add : 'a -> 'a -> 'a)
       (neg : 'a -> 'a)
       (smul : real -> 'a -> 'a)
       (inner : 'a -> 'a -> real).
        (!x y z. add x (add y z) = add (add x y) z) /\
        (!x y. add x y = add y x) /\
        (!x. add zero x = x) /\
        (!x. add (neg x) x = zero) /\
        (!x. smul 1 x = x) /\
        (!r s x. smul (r * s) x = smul r (smul s x)) /\
        (!r x y. smul r (add x y) = add (smul r x) (smul r y)) /\
        (!r s x. smul (r + s) x = add (smul r x) (smul s x)) /\
        (!x y z. inner (add x y) z = inner x z + inner y z) /\
        (!r x y. inner (smul r x) y = r * inner x y) /\
        (!x y. inner x y = inner y x) /\
        (!x. 0 <= inner x x) /\
        (!x. (inner x x = 0 <=> x = zero))
    in
      !zero add neg smul inner.
        is_real_inner_space zero add neg smul inner
        ==>
        let sub = \x y. add x (neg y) in
        let norm = \x. sqrt (inner x x) in
        let dist = \P Q. norm (sub P Q) in
        let vector_angle =
          \u v.
            if u = zero \/ v = zero then
              pi / 2
            else
              acs (inner u v / (norm u * norm v))
        in
        let angle = \P Q R. vector_angle (sub P Q) (sub R Q) in
          !A B C.
            dist A C = dist B C
            ==>
            angle C A B = angle A B C``;

title: 065_isosceles_triangle_theorem
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 065, the isosceles
  triangle theorem.

  This reproduces set.mm theorem isosctr in its complex-plane geometry. If A
  and B are equidistant from C, the two base angles are equal.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

${
  $d x y A $.
  $d x B y $.
  $d x C y $.

  hundred-theorems-065-angle $e
    |- F =
       ( x e. ( CC \ { 0 } ) , y e. ( CC \ { 0 } ) |->
         ( Im ` ( log ` ( y / x ) ) ) )
  $.

  hundred-theorems-065-isosceles $a
    |- (
         (
           ( A e. CC /\ B e. CC /\ C e. CC )
           /\
           ( A =/= C /\ B =/= C /\ A =/= B )
           /\
           ( abs ` ( A - C ) ) = ( abs ` ( B - C ) )
         )
         ->
         (
           ( C - A ) F ( B - A )
         )
         =
         (
           ( A - B ) F ( C - B )
         )
       )
  $.
$}

title: 065_isosceles_triangle_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Isosceles Triangle Theorem" from Hundred
% Theorems item 065: in an arbitrary real inner-product space, equal side
% lengths from the apex imply equal unoriented base angles. This file contains no proof.

isosceles_triangle_theorem_065[
  V: TYPE+,
  zero: V,
  vadd: [V, V -> V],
  vneg: [V -> V],
  scale: [real, V -> V],
  inner: [V, V -> real]
]: THEORY
BEGIN
  vector_space_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (u, v: V): vadd(u, v) = vadd(v, u))
      AND (FORALL (u, v, w: V):
        vadd(vadd(u, v), w) = vadd(u, vadd(v, w)))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): vadd(u, zero) = u)
      AND (FORALL (u: V): vadd(u, vneg(u)) = zero)
      AND (FORALL (a: real), (u, v: V):
        scale(a, vadd(u, v)) = vadd(scale(a, u), scale(a, v)))
      AND (FORALL (a, b: real), (u: V):
        scale(a + b, u) = vadd(scale(a, u), scale(b, u)))
      AND (FORALL (a, b: real), (u: V):
        scale(a * b, u) = scale(a, scale(b, u)))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): scale(1, u) = u)
      AND (FORALL (u: V): scale(0, u) = zero)
      AND (FORALL (u: V): vneg(u) = scale(-1, u))

  inner_product_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (u, v, w: V):
      inner(vadd(u, v), w) = inner(u, w) + inner(v, w))
      AND (FORALL (a: real), (u, v: V):
        inner(scale(a, u), v) = a * inner(u, v))
      AND (FORALL (u, v: V): inner(u, v) = inner(v, u))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): 0 <= inner(u, u))
      AND (FORALL (u: V): inner(u, u) = 0 IFF u = zero)

  real_inner_product_space: bool =
    vector_space_laws AND inner_product_laws

  displacement(P, Q: V): V =
    vadd(Q, vneg(P))

  squared_distance(P, Q: V): real =
    inner(displacement(P, Q), displacement(P, Q))

  sqrt_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    0 <= root AND root * root = radicand

  angle_cosine_value(A, B, C: V, cosine: real): bool =
    IF squared_distance(B, A) = 0 OR squared_distance(B, C) = 0
    THEN
      cosine = 0
    ELSE
      EXISTS (BA_length, BC_length: real):
        sqrt_value(BA_length, squared_distance(B, A))
          AND sqrt_value(BC_length, squared_distance(B, C))
          AND cosine * BA_length * BC_length =
            inner(displacement(B, A), displacement(B, C))
    ENDIF

  same_unoriented_angle(A, B, C, D, E, F: V): bool =
    EXISTS (cosine: real):
      angle_cosine_value(A, B, C, cosine)
        AND angle_cosine_value(D, E, F, cosine)

  isosceles_triangle_theorem: bool =
    real_inner_product_space IMPLIES
      (FORALL (A, B, C: V):
        squared_distance(A, C) = squared_distance(B, C)
          IMPLIES
        same_unoriented_angle(C, A, B, A, B, C))
END isosceles_triangle_theorem_065

title: 066_sum_of_a_geometric_series
content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2019 Neil Strickland. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Neil Strickland
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Field.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.GeomSum

/-!
# Partial sums of geometric series in a field

This file determines the values of the geometric series $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x^i$ and
$\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x^i y^{n-1-i}$ and variants thereof.

## Main statements

* `geom_sum_Ico` proves that $\sum_{i=m}^{n-1} x^i=\frac{x^n-x^m}{x-1}$ in a division ring.
* `geom_sum₂_Ico` proves that $\sum_{i=m}^{n-1} x^iy^{n - 1 - i}=\frac{x^n-y^{n-m}x^m}{x-y}$
  in a field.

Several variants are recorded, generalising in particular to the case of a division ring in
which `x` and `y` commute.
-/

public section

assert_not_exists IsOrderedRing

variable {R K : Type*}

open Finset MulOpposite

section DivisionRing
variable [DivisionRing K] {x y : K}

protected theorem Commute.geom_sum₂ (h' : Commute x y) (h : x ≠ y)
    (n : ℕ) : ∑ i ∈ range n, x ^ i * y ^ (n - 1 - i) = (x ^ n - y ^ n) / (x - y) := by sorry
theorem geom_sum_eq (h : x ≠ 1) (n : ℕ) : ∑ i ∈ range n, x ^ i = (x ^ n - 1) / (x - 1) := by sorry
lemma geom_sum_Ico (hx : x ≠ 1) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico m n, x ^ i = (x ^ n - x ^ m) / (x - 1) := by sorry
lemma geom_sum_Ico' (hx : x ≠ 1) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico m n, x ^ i = (x ^ m - x ^ n) / (1 - x) := by sorry
lemma geom_sum_inv (hx1 : x ≠ 1) (hx0 : x ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ i ∈ range n, x⁻¹ ^ i = (x - 1)⁻¹ * (x - x⁻¹ ^ n * x) := by sorry
end DivisionRing

section Field
variable [Field K] {x y : K}

lemma geom₂_sum (h : x ≠ y) (n : ℕ) :
    ∑ i ∈ range n, x ^ i * y ^ (n - 1 - i) = (x ^ n - y ^ n) / (x - y) :=
  (Commute.all x y).geom_sum₂ h n

lemma geom_sum₂_Ico (hxy : x ≠ y) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) :
    (∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico m n, x ^ i * y ^ (n - 1 - i)) = (x ^ n - y ^ (n - m) * x ^ m) / (x - y) :=
  (Commute.all x y).geom_sum₂_Ico hxy hmn

end Field

Require Export CoRN.ftc.FunctSeries.
Require Export CoRN.ftc.MoreFunctions.

(** printing FSeries_Sum %\ensuremath{\sum_{\infty}}% #∑'<sub>∞</sub># *)

Section Definitions.

(**
* More on Sequences and Series

We will now extend our convergence definitions and results for
sequences and series of functions defined in compact intervals to
arbitrary intervals.

%\begin{convention}% Throughout this file, [J] will be an interval,
[f, g] will be sequences of continuous (in [J]) functions and [F,G]
will be continuous (in [J]) functions.
%\end{convention}%

** Sequences

First we will consider the case of sequences.

*** Definitions

Some of the definitions do not make sense in this more general setting
(for instance, because the norm of a function is no longer defined),
but the ones which do we simply adapt in the usual way.
*)

Variable J : interval.
Variable f : nat -> PartIR.
Variable F : PartIR.

Hypothesis contf : forall n : nat, Continuous J (f n).
Hypothesis contF : Continuous J F.

Definition Cauchy_fun_seq_IR :=  forall a b Hab (Hinc : included (compact a b Hab) J),
  Cauchy_fun_seq _ _ _ f (fun n => included_imp_Continuous _ _ (contf n) _ _ _ Hinc).

Definition conv_fun_seq_IR := forall a b Hab (Hinc : included (Compact Hab) J),
  conv_fun_seq a b Hab f (fun n => included_imp_Continuous _ _ (contf n) _ _ _ Hinc).

Definition conv_fun_seq'_IR := forall a b Hab (Hinc : included (Compact Hab) J),
  conv_fun_seq' a b Hab f F
    (fun n => included_imp_Continuous _ _ (contf n) _ _ _ Hinc)
    (included_imp_Continuous _ _ contF _ _ _ Hinc).

Definition Cauchy_fun_seq2_IR := forall a b Hab (Hinc : included (compact a b Hab) J),
  Cauchy_fun_seq2 _ _ _ f (fun n => included_imp_Continuous _ _ (contf n) _ _ _ Hinc).

(**
The equivalences between these definitions still hold.
*)

Lemma conv_Cauchy_fun_seq'_IR : conv_fun_seq'_IR -> Cauchy_fun_seq_IR.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Cauchy_fun_seq_Lim_char : forall a b Hab (Hinc : included (Compact Hab) J),
 Feq (Compact Hab) Cauchy_fun_seq_Lim_IR
  (Cauchy_fun_seq_Lim _ _ _ _ _ (conv a b Hab Hinc)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_char : forall a b Hab (Hinc : included (Compact Hab) J),
 Feq (Compact Hab) FSeries_Sum (Fun_Series_Sum (H a b Hab Hinc)).
Proof.
Admitted.

End Series_Definitions.

Arguments FSeries_Sum [J f].

Section More_Series_Definitions.

Variable J : interval.
Variable f : nat -> PartIR.

(**
Absolute convergence still exists.
*)

Definition fun_series_abs_convergent_IR :=
 fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => FAbs (f n)).

End More_Series_Definitions.

Section Convergence_Results.

(**
As before, any series converges to its sum.
*)

Variable J : interval.
Variable f : nat -> PartIR.

Lemma FSeries_conv : forall (convF : fun_series_convergent_IR J f) H H',
 conv_fun_seq'_IR J (fun n => FSum0 n f) (FSeries_Sum convF) H H'.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma convergent_imp_inc : fun_series_convergent_IR J f -> forall n, included J (Dom (f n)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma convergent_imp_Continuous : fun_series_convergent_IR J f -> forall n,
 Continuous J (f n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma Continuous_FSeries_Sum : forall H, Continuous J (FSeries_Sum (J:=J) (f:=f) H).
Proof.
Admitted.

End Convergence_Results.

#[global]
Hint Resolve convergent_imp_inc: included.
#[global]
Hint Resolve convergent_imp_Continuous Continuous_FSeries_Sum: continuous.

Section Operations.

(**
** Algebraic Operations

Convergence is well defined and preserved by operations.
*)

Variable J : interval.

Lemma conv_fun_const_series_IR : forall x : nat -> IR, convergent x ->
 fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => [-C-] (x n)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma fun_const_series_Sum_IR : forall y H
 (H' : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => [-C-] (y n))) x Hx, FSeries_Sum H' x Hx [=] series_sum y H.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma conv_zero_fun_series_IR : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => [-C-][0]).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_zero_IR : forall (H : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => [-C-][0]))
   x Hx, FSeries_Sum H x Hx [=] [0].
Proof.
Admitted.

Variables f g : nat -> PartIR.

Lemma fun_series_convergent_wd_IR : (forall n, Feq J (f n) (g n)) ->
 fun_series_convergent_IR J f -> fun_series_convergent_IR J g.
Proof.
Admitted.

(* begin show *)
Hypothesis convF : fun_series_convergent_IR J f.
Hypothesis convG : fun_series_convergent_IR J g.
(* end show *)

Lemma FSeries_Sum_wd' : (forall n, Feq J (f n) (g n)) -> Feq J (FSeries_Sum convF) (FSeries_Sum convG).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_plus_conv : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => f n{+}g n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_plus : forall H : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => f n{+}g n),
 Feq J (FSeries_Sum H) (FSeries_Sum convF{+}FSeries_Sum convG).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_inv_conv : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => {--} (f n)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_inv : forall H : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => {--} (f n)),
 Feq J (FSeries_Sum H) {--} (FSeries_Sum convF).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_minus_conv : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => f n{-}g n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_minus : forall H : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => f n{-}g n),
 Feq J (FSeries_Sum H) (FSeries_Sum convF{-}FSeries_Sum convG).
Proof.
Admitted.

(**
%\begin{convention}% Let [c:IR] and [H:PartIR] be continuous in [J].
%\end{convention}%
*)

Variable c : IR.
Variable H : PartIR.
Hypothesis contH : Continuous J H.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_scal_conv : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => H{*}f n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma FSeries_Sum_scal : forall H' : fun_series_convergent_IR J (fun n => H{*}f n),
 Feq J (FSeries_Sum H') (H{*}FSeries_Sum convF).
Proof.
Admitted.

End Operations.

Section Convergence_Criteria.

(**
*** Convergence Criteria

The most important tests for convergence of series still apply: the
comparison test (in both versions) and the ratio test.
*)

Variable J : interval.
Variable f : nat -> PartIR.
Hypothesis contF : forall n, Continuous J (f n).

Lemma fun_str_comparison_IR : forall g : nat -> PartIR, fun_series_convergent_IR J g ->
 {k : nat | forall n, k <= n -> forall x, J x -> forall Hx Hx', AbsIR (f n x Hx) [<=] g n x Hx'} ->
 fun_series_convergent_IR J f.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma fun_comparison_IR : forall g : nat -> PartIR, fun_series_convergent_IR J g ->
 (forall n x, J x -> forall Hx Hx', AbsIR (f n x Hx) [<=] g n x Hx') ->
 fun_series_convergent_IR J f.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma abs_imp_conv_IR : fun_series_abs_convergent_IR J f ->
 fun_series_convergent_IR J f.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma fun_ratio_test_conv_IR : {N : nat | {c : IR | c [<] [1] | [0] [<=] c /\ (forall x,
  J x -> forall n, N <= n -> forall Hx Hx', AbsIR (f (S n) x Hx') [<=] c[*]AbsIR (f n x Hx))}} ->
 fun_series_convergent_IR J f.
Proof.
Admitted.

End Convergence_Criteria.

Section Power_Series.

(** ***Power Series

The geometric series converges on the open interval (-1, 1)
*)

Lemma fun_power_series_conv_IR : fun_series_convergent_IR (olor ([--][1]) [1]) (fun (i:nat) => Fid IR{^}i).
Proof.
Admitted.

End Power_Series.

Section Insert_Series.

(**
*** Translation

When working in particular with power series and Taylor series, it is
sometimes useful to ``shift'' all the terms in the series one position
forward, that is, replacing each $f_{i+1}$#f<sub>i+1</sub># with
$f_i$#f<sub>i</sub># and inserting the null function in the first
position.  This does not affect convergence or the sum of the series.
*)

Variable J : interval.
Variable f : nat -> PartIR.
Hypothesis convF : fun_series_convergent_IR J f.

Definition insert_series n : PartIR :=
  match n with
  | O => [-C-][0]
  | S p => f p
  end.

Lemma insert_series_cont : forall n, Continuous J (insert_series n).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma insert_series_sum_char : forall n x Hx Hx',
 fun_seq_part_sum f n x Hx [=] fun_seq_part_sum insert_series (S n) x Hx'.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma insert_series_conv : fun_series_convergent_IR J insert_series.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma insert_series_sum : Feq J (FSeries_Sum convF) (FSeries_Sum insert_series_conv).
Proof.
Admitted.

End Insert_Series.

title: 066_sum_of_a_geometric_series
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of the sum of a geometric series from Hundred
  Theorems item 066. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory Sum_Of_A_Geometric_Series
  imports Complex_Main
begin

theorem geometric_series:
  fixes c :: "'a::real_normed_field"
  assumes "norm c < 1"
  shows "(\<lambda>n. c ^ n) sums (1 / (1 - c))"
  sorry

end

title: 066_sum_of_a_geometric_series
066_sum_of_a_geometric_series
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__066, "Sum of a Geometric Series": in the real
;; numbers, the first n terms of a geometric progression have their standard
;; closed form, and if |r| < 1 then the series sum of a*r^n converges to
;; a/(1-r). This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; ACL2 has no native real-number carrier. Following the corpus convention for
;; generic mathematical structures, these conservative interfaces describe an
;; arbitrary carrier together with the operations of a Dedekind-complete
;; Archimedean ordered field, hence the real field up to ordered-field
;; isomorphism. Subsets are unary tame APPLY$ predicates, so completeness ranges
;; over predicate-valued set representations rather than over a fixed finite
;; collection of set tags. The carrier is not enumerated or replaced by ACL2
;; rationals.

(defstub ht066-real-p (real-type value) t)
(defstub ht066-zero (real-type) t)
(defstub ht066-one (real-type) t)
(defstub ht066-add (real-type left right) t)
(defstub ht066-mul (real-type left right) t)
(defstub ht066-neg (real-type value) t)
(defstub ht066-inv (real-type value) t)
(defstub ht066-less (real-type left right) t)

(defstub ht066-supremum (real-type set) t)

(defun ht066-real-set-member-p (set value)
  (if (apply$ set (list value)) t nil))

(defun-sk ht066-valid-real-set-p (real-type set)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (ht066-real-set-member-p set value)
     (ht066-real-p real-type value))))

(defun ht066-leq (real-type left right)
  (not (ht066-less real-type right left)))

(defun ht066-sub (real-type left right)
  (ht066-add real-type left (ht066-neg real-type right)))

(defun ht066-div (real-type numerator denominator)
  (ht066-mul real-type numerator (ht066-inv real-type denominator)))

(defun ht066-abs (real-type value)
  (if (ht066-less real-type value (ht066-zero real-type))
      (ht066-neg real-type value)
    value))

(defun ht066-positive-p (real-type value)
  (and
   (ht066-real-p real-type value)
   (ht066-less real-type (ht066-zero real-type) value)))

(defun ht066-nat (real-type n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (ht066-zero real-type)
    (ht066-add
     real-type
     (ht066-one real-type)
     (ht066-nat real-type (1- n)))))

(defun ht066-power (real-type base exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (ht066-one real-type)
    (ht066-mul
     real-type
     base
     (ht066-power real-type base (1- exponent)))))

(defun ht066-geometric-prefix (real-type a r terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      (ht066-zero real-type)
    (let ((index (1- terms)))
      (ht066-add
       real-type
       (ht066-geometric-prefix real-type a r index)
       (ht066-mul
        real-type
        a
        (ht066-power real-type r index))))))

(defun-sk ht066-field-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht066-real-p real-type x)
      (ht066-real-p real-type y)
      (ht066-real-p real-type z))
     (let* ((zero (ht066-zero real-type))
            (one (ht066-one real-type))
            (xy-add (ht066-add real-type x y))
            (yz-add (ht066-add real-type y z))
            (xy-mul (ht066-mul real-type x y))
            (yz-mul (ht066-mul real-type y z))
            (neg-x (ht066-neg real-type x))
            (inv-x (ht066-inv real-type x)))
       (and
        (ht066-real-p real-type xy-add)
        (ht066-real-p real-type xy-mul)
        (ht066-real-p real-type neg-x)
        (ht066-real-p real-type inv-x)
        (equal
         (ht066-add real-type xy-add z)
         (ht066-add real-type x yz-add))
        (equal xy-add (ht066-add real-type y x))
        (equal (ht066-add real-type x zero) x)
        (equal (ht066-add real-type x neg-x) zero)
        (equal
         (ht066-mul real-type xy-mul z)
         (ht066-mul real-type x yz-mul))
        (equal xy-mul (ht066-mul real-type y x))
        (equal (ht066-mul real-type x one) x)
        (implies
         (equal x zero)
         (equal inv-x zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal (ht066-mul real-type x inv-x) one))
        (equal
         (ht066-mul real-type x yz-add)
         (ht066-add
          real-type
          (ht066-mul real-type x y)
          (ht066-mul real-type x z))))))))

(defun-sk ht066-order-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht066-real-p real-type x)
      (ht066-real-p real-type y)
      (ht066-real-p real-type z))
     (let ((zero (ht066-zero real-type)))
       (and
        (not (ht066-less real-type x x))
        (or
         (ht066-less real-type x y)
         (equal x y)
         (ht066-less real-type y x))
        (implies
         (and
          (ht066-less real-type x y)
          (ht066-less real-type y z))
         (ht066-less real-type x z))
        (implies
         (ht066-less real-type x y)
         (ht066-less
          real-type
          (ht066-add real-type x z)
          (ht066-add real-type y z)))
        (implies
         (and
          (ht066-less real-type zero x)
          (ht066-less real-type zero y))
         (ht066-less
          real-type
          zero
          (ht066-mul real-type x y))))))))

(defun-sk ht066-upper-bound-p (real-type set upper)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht066-real-p real-type x)
      (ht066-real-set-member-p set x))
     (ht066-leq real-type x upper))))

(defun-sk ht066-real-set-nonempty-p (real-type set)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (ht066-real-p real-type x)
     (ht066-real-set-member-p set x))))

(defun-sk ht066-real-set-bounded-p (real-type set)
  (exists (upper)
    (and
     (ht066-real-p real-type upper)
     (ht066-upper-bound-p real-type set upper))))

(defun-sk ht066-least-upper-bound-p
    (real-type set supremum)
  (forall (upper)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht066-real-p real-type upper)
      (ht066-upper-bound-p real-type set upper))
     (ht066-leq real-type supremum upper))))

(defun-sk ht066-completeness-p (real-type)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (ht066-valid-real-set-p real-type set)
      (ht066-real-set-nonempty-p real-type set)
      (ht066-real-set-bounded-p real-type set))
     (let ((supremum (ht066-supremum real-type set)))
       (and
        (ht066-real-p real-type supremum)
        (ht066-upper-bound-p real-type set supremum)
        (ht066-least-upper-bound-p
         real-type set supremum))))))

(defun-sk ht066-archimedean-witness-exists-p
    (real-type x)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (natp n)
     (ht066-less real-type x (ht066-nat real-type n)))))

(defun-sk ht066-archimedean-p (real-type)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (ht066-real-p real-type x)
     (ht066-archimedean-witness-exists-p real-type x))))

(defun ht066-real-field-p (real-type)
  (let ((zero (ht066-zero real-type))
        (one (ht066-one real-type)))
    (and
     (ht066-real-p real-type zero)
     (ht066-real-p real-type one)
     (not (equal zero one))
     (ht066-field-laws-p real-type)
     (ht066-order-laws-p real-type)
     (ht066-less real-type zero one)
     (ht066-completeness-p real-type)
     (ht066-archimedean-p real-type))))

;; This is
;;   sum_{i < n} a*r^i = a*(1-r^n)/(1-r)
;; for every natural n and every r different from 1.

(defun-sk ht066-finite-geometric-identity-p (real-type)
  (forall (a r terms)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht066-real-p real-type a)
      (ht066-real-p real-type r)
      (natp terms)
      (not (equal r (ht066-one real-type))))
     (equal
      (ht066-geometric-prefix real-type a r terms)
      (ht066-div
       real-type
       (ht066-mul
        real-type
        a
        (ht066-sub
         real-type
         (ht066-one real-type)
         (ht066-power real-type r terms)))
       (ht066-sub
        real-type
        (ht066-one real-type)
        r))))))

;; The next three predicates are the literal epsilon-N definition that the
;; partial sums of a*r^n converge to the supplied limit.

(defun-sk ht066-geometric-tail-p
    (real-type a r limit epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (terms)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp terms)
      (natp cutoff)
      (<= cutoff terms))
     (ht066-less
      real-type
      (ht066-abs
       real-type
       (ht066-sub
        real-type
        (ht066-geometric-prefix real-type a r terms)
        limit))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht066-geometric-cutoff-exists-p
    (real-type a r limit epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (ht066-geometric-tail-p
      real-type a r limit epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk ht066-geometric-limit-p
    (real-type a r limit)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (ht066-positive-p real-type epsilon)
     (ht066-geometric-cutoff-exists-p
      real-type a r limit epsilon))))

;; For every real a and r with |r| < 1, the geometric series converges to the
;; field quotient a/(1-r), with no cutoff supplied as an external parameter.

(defun-sk ht066-geometric-series-convergence-p (real-type)
  (forall (a r)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht066-real-p real-type a)
      (ht066-real-p real-type r)
      (ht066-less
       real-type
       (ht066-abs real-type r)
       (ht066-one real-type)))
     (ht066-geometric-limit-p
      real-type
      a
      r
      (ht066-div
       real-type
       a
       (ht066-sub
        real-type
        (ht066-one real-type)
        r))))))

(defun hundred-theorems-066-sum-of-a-geometric-series-statement
    (real-type)
  (implies
   (ht066-real-field-p real-type)
   (and
    (ht066-finite-geometric-identity-p real-type)
    (ht066-geometric-series-convergence-p real-type))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 066_sum_of_a_geometric_series
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems corpus artifact
-- hundred-theorems__agda__066, "Sum of a Geometric Series": the finite
-- geometric-sum identity and, for real |r| < 1, convergence of the series
-- with terms a*r^n to a/(1-r). This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=N  : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record DivisionRing (D : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroD oneD : D
    addD multiplyD : D -> D -> D
    negateD inverseD : D -> D

    oneD-not-zeroD :
      oneD != zeroD

    addD-commutative :
      (x y : D) -> addD x y == addD y x
    addD-associative :
      (x y z : D) -> addD (addD x y) z == addD x (addD y z)
    addD-zero-left :
      (x : D) -> addD zeroD x == x
    addD-zero-right :
      (x : D) -> addD x zeroD == x
    addD-inverse-left :
      (x : D) -> addD (negateD x) x == zeroD
    addD-inverse-right :
      (x : D) -> addD x (negateD x) == zeroD

    multiplyD-associative :
      (x y z : D) ->
      multiplyD (multiplyD x y) z == multiplyD x (multiplyD y z)
    multiplyD-one-left :
      (x : D) -> multiplyD oneD x == x
    multiplyD-one-right :
      (x : D) -> multiplyD x oneD == x
    multiplyD-zero-left :
      (x : D) -> multiplyD zeroD x == zeroD
    multiplyD-zero-right :
      (x : D) -> multiplyD x zeroD == zeroD
    distribute-left :
      (x y z : D) ->
      multiplyD x (addD y z) ==
      addD (multiplyD x y) (multiplyD x z)
    distribute-right :
      (x y z : D) ->
      multiplyD (addD x y) z ==
      addD (multiplyD x z) (multiplyD y z)
    multiplyD-inverse-left :
      (x : D) -> x != zeroD -> multiplyD (inverseD x) x == oneD
    multiplyD-inverse-right :
      (x : D) -> x != zeroD -> multiplyD x (inverseD x) == oneD
    inverseD-zero :
      inverseD zeroD == zeroD

subtractD :
  {D : Set} ->
  DivisionRing D ->
  D ->
  D ->
  D
subtractD division x y =
  DivisionRing.addD division x
    (DivisionRing.negateD division y)

divideD :
  {D : Set} ->
  DivisionRing D ->
  D ->
  D ->
  D
divideD division x y =
  DivisionRing.multiplyD division x
    (DivisionRing.inverseD division y)

powerD :
  {D : Set} ->
  DivisionRing D ->
  D ->
  Nat ->
  D
powerD division x zero =
  DivisionRing.oneD division
powerD division x (suc n) =
  DivisionRing.multiplyD division
    (powerD division x n)
    x

finiteSumD :
  {D : Set} ->
  DivisionRing D ->
  (Nat -> D) ->
  Nat ->
  D
finiteSumD division term zero =
  DivisionRing.zeroD division
finiteSumD division term (suc n) =
  DivisionRing.addD division
    (finiteSumD division term n)
    (term n)

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    addR multiplyR : R -> R -> R
    negateR inverseR absoluteValueR : R -> R
    lessOrEqualR : R -> R -> Set

    oneR-not-zeroR :
      oneR != zeroR

    addR-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> addR x y == addR y x
    addR-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> addR (addR x y) z == addR x (addR y z)
    addR-zero :
      (x : R) -> addR x zeroR == x
    addR-inverse :
      (x : R) -> addR x (negateR x) == zeroR

    multiplyR-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiplyR x y == multiplyR y x
    multiplyR-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiplyR (multiplyR x y) z == multiplyR x (multiplyR y z)
    multiplyR-one :
      (x : R) -> multiplyR x oneR == x
    multiplyR-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiplyR x zeroR == zeroR
    distributeR :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiplyR x (addR y z) ==
      addR (multiplyR x y) (multiplyR x z)
    multiplyR-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiplyR x (inverseR x) == oneR
    inverseR-zero :
      inverseR zeroR == zeroR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqualR x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR y z ->
      lessOrEqualR x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqualR x y) (lessOrEqualR y x)
    addR-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR (addR z x) (addR z y)
    multiplyR-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR (multiplyR x y)
    zeroR-less-than-oneR :
      Both (lessOrEqualR zeroR oneR) (zeroR != oneR)

    absoluteR-nonnegative :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqualR zeroR (absoluteValueR x)
    absoluteR-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR x ->
      absoluteValueR x == x
    absoluteR-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x zeroR ->
      absoluteValueR x == negateR x

    fromNatR : Nat -> R
    fromNatR-zero :
      fromNatR zero == zeroR
    fromNatR-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNatR (suc n) == addR (fromNatR n) oneR
    fromNatR-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNatR m == fromNatR n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqualR x (fromNatR n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x upper) ->
              lessOrEqualR supremum upper))

subtractR :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtractR reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.addR reals x
    (CompleteOrderedField.negateR reals y)

divideR :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divideR reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.multiplyR reals x
    (CompleteOrderedField.inverseR reals y)

powerR :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
powerR reals x zero =
  CompleteOrderedField.oneR reals
powerR reals x (suc n) =
  CompleteOrderedField.multiplyR reals
    (powerR reals x n)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both
    (CompleteOrderedField.lessOrEqualR reals x y)
    (x != y)

Positive :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Set
Positive reals x =
  StrictLess reals
    (CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals)
    x

partialSumR :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
partialSumR reals term zero =
  CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals
partialSumR reals term (suc n) =
  CompleteOrderedField.addR reals
    (partialSumR reals term n)
    (term n)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  Positive reals epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      StrictLess reals
        (CompleteOrderedField.absoluteValueR reals
          (subtractR reals (sequence n) limit))
        epsilon)

SeriesSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesSum reals term limit =
  SequentialLimit reals (partialSumR reals term) limit

record GeometricSeriesClaims : Set1 where
  field
    finite-geometric-sum :
      (D : Set) ->
      (division : DivisionRing D) ->
      (x : D) ->
      x != DivisionRing.oneD division ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      finiteSumD division (\ i -> powerD division x i) n ==
      divideD division
        (subtractD division
          (powerD division x n)
          (DivisionRing.oneD division))
        (subtractD division x (DivisionRing.oneD division))

    infinite-geometric-series :
      (R : Set) ->
      (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
      (a r : R) ->
      StrictLess reals
        (CompleteOrderedField.absoluteValueR reals r)
        (CompleteOrderedField.oneR reals) ->
      SeriesSum reals
        (\ n ->
          CompleteOrderedField.multiplyR reals a
            (powerR reals r n))
        (divideR reals a
          (subtractR reals
            (CompleteOrderedField.oneR reals)
            r))

sum-of-a-geometric-series : Set1
sum-of-a-geometric-series =
  GeometricSeriesClaims

(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 066, "Sum of a Geometric Series":
  for real a and r with |r| < 1, the partial sums of a * r^n converge to a / (1 - r).
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open real_topologyTheory;

val sum_of_a_geometric_series =
  ``!a r : real.
      abs r < 1
      ==>
      ((\k : num.
          SIGMA
            (\n : num. a * r pow n)
            (count k)) --> (a / (1 - r) : real)) sequentially``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 066, the finite
  geometric-series formula.

  This reproduces set.mm theorem geoser for a complex ratio A distinct from
  one and a nonnegative number N of terms.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

${
  $d A k $.
  $d k N $.
  $d ph k $.

  hundred-theorems-066-ratio $e
    |- ( ph -> A e. CC )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-066-nonunit $e
    |- ( ph -> A =/= 1 )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-066-length $e
    |- ( ph -> N e. NN0 )
  $.

  hundred-theorems-066-geometric-series $a
    |- (
         ph
         ->
         sum_ k e. ( 0 ... ( N - 1 ) ) ( A ^ k )
         =
         ( ( 1 - ( A ^ N ) ) / ( 1 - A ) )
       )
  $.
$}

title: 066_sum_of_a_geometric_series
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Sum of a Geometric Series" from Hundred
% Theorems item 066: for a real ratio of absolute value less than one, the
% geometric-series partial sums converge to one divided by one minus the ratio.
% This file contains no proof.

sum_of_a_geometric_series_066: THEORY
BEGIN
  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN 0 ELSE numerator / denominator ENDIF

  geometric_partial_sum(ratio: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      geometric_partial_sum(ratio, count - 1)
        + ratio ^ (count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: [nat -> real], value: real): bool =
    FORALL (eps: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(count) - value) < eps

  sum_of_a_geometric_series: bool =
    FORALL (ratio: real):
      abs(ratio) < 1 IMPLIES
        converges_to(
          (LAMBDA (count: nat): geometric_partial_sum(ratio, count)),
          safe_div(1, 1 - ratio))
END sum_of_a_geometric_series_066

-- Euler's number `exp 1` is not algebraic over the rationals. This file contains no proof.

import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Exp
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Algebraic.Defs

title: 067_e_is_transcendental
content:
From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import perm ssralg poly ssrnum polydiv mxpoly ssrint rat.
From mathcomp Require Import polyorder finmap order.
From SsrMultinomials Require Import mpoly.
From Lindemann Require Import archi Rstruct Cstruct prelim.
From Lindemann Require Import Lind_part1 Lind_part2 Lind_part3.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Import Prenex Implicits.

Open Scope ring_scope.
Import GRing.Theory Num.Theory Archi.Theory Archi.Order.

Local Notation RtoC := Cstruct.RtoC.
Local Notation Cnat := Cstruct.Cnat.
Local Notation Cint := Cstruct.Cint.

Notation "x 'is_algebraic'" := (algebraicOver QtoC x)
  (at level 55).

Definition lin_indep_over (P : pred_class) {n : nat} (x : complexR ^ n) :=
  forall (lambda : complexR ^ n), lambda \in ffun_on P ->
    lambda != 0 -> \sum_(i < n) (lambda i * x i) != 0.

Definition alg_indep_over (P : pred_class) {n : nat} (x : complexR ^ n) :=
  forall (p : {mpoly complexR[n]}), p \is a mpolyOver _ P ->
    p != 0 -> p.@[x] != 0.

Local Notation setZroots := ((fset_roots Cint) : 
    complexR -> qualifier 1 {fset complexR}).




(******************************************************************************)
(*                          Lindemann's theorems                              *)
(******************************************************************************)

Theorem LindemannBaker : forall (l : nat) (alpha : complexR ^ l) (a : complexR ^ l),
  (0%N < l)%N -> injective alpha -> (forall i : 'I_l, alpha i is_algebraic) ->
  (forall i : 'I_l, a i != 0) -> (forall i : 'I_l, a i is_algebraic) ->
  (Cexp_span a alpha != 0).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem LindemannWeierstrass n (alpha : complexR ^ n) :
  (n > 0)%N -> (forall i : 'I_n, alpha i is_algebraic) ->
  lin_indep_over Cint alpha -> alg_indep_over Cint (finfun (Cexp \o alpha)).
Proof.
Admitted.

(* Print Assumptions LindemannWeierstrass *)






Lemma ffun1_lin_indep_over (P : pred_class) (x : complexR) :
  x != 0 -> lin_indep_over P (finfun (fun (i : 'I_1) => x)).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma ffun1_alg_indep_over (x : complexR) :
   (x is_algebraic) -> ~ (alg_indep_over Cint (finfun (fun (i : 'I_1) => x))).
Proof.
Admitted.




(******************************************************************************)
(*                          Hermite-Lindemann theorem                         *)
(******************************************************************************)

Theorem HermiteLindemann (x : complexR) :
  x != 0 -> x is_algebraic -> ~ ((Cexp x) is_algebraic).
Proof.
Admitted.

(* Print Assumptions HermiteLindemann *)




(******************************************************************************)
(*                          Transcendence of e                                *)
(******************************************************************************)

Theorem e_trans_by_LB :
  ~ (RtoC (Rtrigo_def.exp 1) is_algebraic).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem e_trans_by_LW :
  ~ (RtoC (Rtrigo_def.exp 1) is_algebraic).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem e_trans_by_HL :
  ~ (RtoC (Rtrigo_def.exp 1) is_algebraic).
Proof.
Admitted.




(******************************************************************************)
(*                          Transcendence of pi                               *)
(******************************************************************************)

Lemma eiPI_eqm1 : Cexp (RtoC Rtrigo1.PI * 'i) = -1.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Pi_trans_by_LB : ~ (RtoC Rtrigo1.PI is_algebraic).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Pi_trans_by_LW : ~ (RtoC Rtrigo1.PI is_algebraic).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem Pi_trans_by_HL : ~ (RtoC Rtrigo1.PI is_algebraic).
Proof.
Admitted.

title: 067_e_is_transcendental
content:
(*
  File:       E_Transcendental.thy
  Author:     Manuel Eberl <manuel@pruvisto.org>

  A proof that e (Euler's number) is transcendental.
  Could possibly be extended to a transcendence proof for pi or
  the very general Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem.
*)
section \<open>Proof of the Transcendence of $e$\<close>
theory E_Transcendental
  imports
    "HOL-Complex_Analysis.Complex_Analysis"
    "HOL-Number_Theory.Number_Theory"
    "HOL-Computational_Algebra.Polynomial"
    "Polynomial_Interpolation.Ring_Hom_Poly"
begin

hide_const (open) UnivPoly.coeff  UnivPoly.up_ring.monom 
hide_const (open) Module.smult  Coset.order

subsection \<open>Various auxiliary facts\<close>

lemma fact_dvd_pochhammer:
  assumes "m \<le> n + 1"
  shows   "fact m dvd pochhammer (int n - int m + 1) m"
  by sorry

lemma prime_elem_int_not_dvd_neg1_power:
  "prime_elem (p :: int) \<Longrightarrow> \<not>p dvd (-1) ^ n"
  by sorry

lemma nat_fact [simp]: "nat (fact n) = fact n"
  by sorry

lemma prime_dvd_fact_iff_int:
  "p dvd fact n \<longleftrightarrow> p \<le> int n" if "prime p"
  by sorry

lemma power_over_fact_tendsto_0:
  "(\<lambda>n. (x :: real) ^ n / fact n) \<longlonglongrightarrow> 0"
  by sorry

lemma power_over_fact_tendsto_0':
  "(\<lambda>n. c * (x :: real) ^ n / fact n) \<longlonglongrightarrow> 0"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>General facts about polynomials\<close>

lemma fact_dvd_higher_pderiv:
  "[:fact n :: int:] dvd (pderiv ^^ n) p"
  by sorry

lemma fact_dvd_poly_higher_pderiv_aux:
  "(fact n :: int) dvd poly ((pderiv ^^ n) p) x"
  by sorry

lemma fact_dvd_poly_higher_pderiv_aux':
  "m \<le> n \<Longrightarrow> (fact m :: int) dvd poly ((pderiv ^^ n) p) x"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Main proof\<close>

lemma lindemann_weierstrass_integral:
  fixes u :: complex and f :: "complex poly"
  defines "df \<equiv> \<lambda>n. (pderiv ^^ n) f"
  defines "m \<equiv> degree f"
  defines "I \<equiv> \<lambda>f u. exp u * (\<Sum>j\<le>degree f. poly ((pderiv ^^ j) f) 0) -
                       (\<Sum>j\<le>degree f. poly ((pderiv ^^ j) f) u)"
  shows "((\<lambda>t. exp (u - t) * poly f t) has_contour_integral I f u) (linepath 0 u)"
  by sorry

locale lindemann_weierstrass_aux =
  fixes f :: "complex poly"
begin

definition I :: "complex \<Rightarrow> complex" where
  "I u = exp u * (\<Sum>j\<le>degree f. poly ((pderiv ^^ j) f) 0) -
                       (\<Sum>j\<le>degree f. poly ((pderiv ^^ j) f) u)"

lemma lindemann_weierstrass_integral_bound:
  fixes u :: complex
  assumes "C \<ge> 0" "\<And>t. t \<in> closed_segment 0 u \<Longrightarrow> norm (poly f t) \<le> C"
  shows "norm (I u) \<le> norm u * exp (norm u) * C"
  by sorry

end

lemma poly_higher_pderiv_aux1:
  fixes c :: "'a :: idom"
  assumes "k < n"
  shows   "poly ((pderiv ^^ k) ([:-c, 1:] ^ n * p)) c = 0"
  by sorry

lemma poly_higher_pderiv_aux1':
  fixes c :: "'a :: idom"
  assumes "k < n" "[:-c, 1:] ^ n dvd p"
  shows   "poly ((pderiv ^^ k) p) c = 0"
  by sorry

lemma poly_higher_pderiv_aux2:
  fixes c :: "'a :: {idom, semiring_char_0}"
  shows   "poly ((pderiv ^^ n) ([:-c, 1:] ^ n * p)) c = fact n * poly p c"
  by sorry

lemma poly_higher_pderiv_aux3:
  fixes c :: "'a :: {idom,semiring_char_0}"
  assumes "k \<ge> n"
  shows   "\<exists>q. poly ((pderiv ^^ k) ([:-c, 1:] ^ n * p)) c = fact n * poly q c"
  by sorry

lemma poly_higher_pderiv_aux3':
  fixes c :: "'a :: {idom, semiring_char_0}"
  assumes "k \<ge> n" "[:-c, 1:] ^ n dvd p"
  shows   "fact n dvd poly ((pderiv ^^ k) p) c"
  by sorry

lemma e_transcendental_aux_bound:
  obtains C where "C \<ge> 0"
    "\<And>x. x \<in> closed_segment 0 (of_nat n) \<Longrightarrow>
        norm (\<Prod>k\<in>{1..n}. (x - of_nat k :: complex)) \<le> C"
  by sorry


theorem e_transcendental_complex: "\<not> algebraic (exp 1 :: complex)"
  by sorry

corollary e_transcendental_real: "\<not> algebraic (exp 1 :: real)"
  by sorry

end

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of the hundred-theorems corpus artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__067, "e is Transcendental": Euler's number
;; exp(1) is not a root of any nonzero integer polynomial. Exact rational
;; partial sums of its defining exponential series represent exp(1).
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun ht067-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n (ht067-factorial (- n 1)))))

(defun ht067-exp-one-series-prefix (terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let ((index (- terms 1)))
      (+ (ht067-exp-one-series-prefix index)
         (/ 1 (ht067-factorial index))))))

;; The nth approximation is sum_{k=0}^n 1/k!, whose real limit is exp(1).
(defun ht067-exp-one-approximation (index)
  (ht067-exp-one-series-prefix (+ 1 (nfix index))))

(defun ht067-integer-coefficient-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and (integerp (car coefficients))
           (ht067-integer-coefficient-list-p
            (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun ht067-nonzero-coefficient-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (or (not (equal (car coefficients) 0))
          (ht067-nonzero-coefficient-list-p
           (cdr coefficients)))
    nil))

;; Coefficients are listed in ascending order of exponent.
(defun ht067-polynomial-value (coefficients x)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (car coefficients)
         (* x
            (ht067-polynomial-value
             (cdr coefficients) x)))
    0))

(defun-sk ht067-polynomial-zero-tail-p
  (coefficients epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and (natp index)
          (<= cutoff index))
     (<
      (abs
       (ht067-polynomial-value
        coefficients
        (ht067-exp-one-approximation index)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht067-polynomial-zero-cutoff-exists-p
  (coefficients epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (ht067-polynomial-zero-tail-p
      coefficients epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk ht067-polynomial-tends-to-zero-p (coefficients)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp epsilon)
          (< 0 epsilon))
     (ht067-polynomial-zero-cutoff-exists-p
      coefficients epsilon))))

(defun-sk ht067-exp-one-is-algebraic-p ()
  (exists (coefficients)
    (and
     (true-listp coefficients)
     (ht067-integer-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
     (ht067-nonzero-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
     (ht067-polynomial-tends-to-zero-p coefficients))))

(defun hundred-theorems-067-e-is-transcendental-statement ()
  (not (ht067-exp-one-is-algebraic-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 067_e_is_transcendental
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact hundred-theorems__agda__067,
-- "e is Transcendental": Euler's number, characterized by the series sum of 1/n!, is not a
-- root of any nonzero integer polynomial. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infix 4 _≠_ _≤_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 2 _∨_

data ⊥ : Set where

¬_ : Set → Set
¬ A = A → ⊥

_≠_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≠ y = ¬ (x ≡ y)

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R → R → R
    negate reciprocal absoluteValue : R → R
    lessOrEqual : R → R → Set
    fromNat : Nat → R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR ≠ zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) → add x y ≡ add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) → add (add x y) z ≡ add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) → add x zeroR ≡ x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) → add x (negate x) ≡ zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) → multiply x y ≡ multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiply (multiply x y) z ≡ multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) → multiply x oneR ≡ x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) → multiply x zeroR ≡ zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiply x (add y z) ≡
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) →
      x ≠ zeroR →
      multiply x (reciprocal x) ≡ oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) → lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y →
      lessOrEqual y z →
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y →
      lessOrEqual y x →
      x ≡ y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y ∨ lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) →
      lessOrEqual x y →
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) →
      lessOrEqual zeroR x →
      lessOrEqual zeroR y →
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR ∧ oneR ≠ zeroR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero ≡ zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) → fromNat (suc n) ≡ add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat (m + n) ≡ add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) →
      fromNat (m * n) ≡ multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    characteristic-zero :
      (m n : Nat) → fromNat m ≡ fromNat n → m ≡ n

    absolute-nonnegative :
      (x : R) → lessOrEqual zeroR (absoluteValue x)
    absolute-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) →
      lessOrEqual zeroR x →
      absoluteValue x ≡ x
    absolute-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) →
      lessOrEqual x zeroR →
      absoluteValue x ≡ negate x

    archimedean :
      (x : R) → Σ Nat (λ n → lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R → Set) →
      Σ R (λ x → P x) →
      Σ R (λ upper → (x : R) → P x → lessOrEqual x upper) →
      Σ R
        (λ supremum →
          ((x : R) → P x → lessOrEqual x supremum) ∧
          ((upper : R) →
            ((x : R) → P x → lessOrEqual x upper) →
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

subtract :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  R
subtract reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.add reals x
    (CompleteOrderedField.negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  R
divide reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.multiply reals x
    (CompleteOrderedField.reciprocal reals y)

fromInt :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Int →
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  CompleteOrderedField.negate reals
    (CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals (suc n))

factorial : Nat → Nat
factorial zero = suc zero
factorial (suc n) = suc n * factorial n

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  R →
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.lessOrEqual reals x y ∧ x ≠ y

Positive :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
Positive reals x =
  StrictLess reals (CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals) x

partialSum :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → R) →
  Nat →
  R
partialSum reals sequence zero =
  CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals
partialSum reals sequence (suc n) =
  CompleteOrderedField.add reals
    (partialSum reals sequence n)
    (sequence n)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → R) →
  R →
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) →
  Positive reals epsilon →
  Σ Nat
    (λ cutoff →
      (n : Nat) →
      cutoff ≤ n →
      CompleteOrderedField.lessOrEqual reals
        (CompleteOrderedField.absoluteValue reals
          (subtract reals (sequence n) limit))
        epsilon)

SeriesSum :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  (Nat → R) →
  R →
  Set
SeriesSum reals terms limit =
  SequentialLimit reals (partialSum reals terms) limit

eTerm :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  Nat →
  R
eTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (CompleteOrderedField.oneR reals)
    (CompleteOrderedField.fromNat reals (factorial n))

IsEulerNumber :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
IsEulerNumber reals e =
  SeriesSum reals (eTerm reals) e

data HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient : List Int → Set where
  here :
    {coefficient : Int} {coefficients : List Int} →
    coefficient ≠ pos zero →
    HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

  there :
    {coefficient : Int} {coefficients : List Int} →
    HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient coefficients →
    HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

evaluateIntegerPolynomial :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  List Int →
  R →
  R
evaluateIntegerPolynomial reals [] x =
  CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals
evaluateIntegerPolynomial reals
  (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  CompleteOrderedField.add reals
    (fromInt reals coefficient)
    (CompleteOrderedField.multiply reals x
      (evaluateIntegerPolynomial reals coefficients x))

Algebraic :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
Algebraic reals x =
  Σ (List Int)
    (λ coefficients →
      HasNonzeroIntegerCoefficient coefficients ∧
      evaluateIntegerPolynomial reals coefficients x ≡
      CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals)

Transcendental :
  {R : Set} →
  CompleteOrderedField R →
  R →
  Set
Transcendental reals x =
  ¬ Algebraic reals x

hundred-theorems-067 : Set₁
hundred-theorems-067 =
  (R : Set) →
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) →
  (e : R) →
  IsEulerNumber reals e →
  Transcendental reals e

(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 067, "e is Transcendental":
  Euler's number exp 1 is not a root of any nonzero polynomial with integer
  coefficients. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open integerTheory pred_setTheory realTheory intrealTheory real_sigmaTheory
     transcTheory;

val e_is_transcendental =
  ``!p : num -> int.
      FINITE {n | p n <> 0} /\
      (?n. p n <> 0)
      ==>
      SIGMA (\n. real_of_int (p n) * exp 1 pow n) {n | p n <> 0} <> 0``;

title: 067_e_is_transcendental
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "e is Transcendental" from Hundred Theorems
% artifact 067 (hundred-theorems__pvs__067): Euler's number, the real exponential
% of one, is not algebraic over the rationals. This file contains no proof.

hundred_theorems_067: THEORY
BEGIN
  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  real_exponential_partial(
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        real_exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: [nat -> real], value: real): bool =
    FORALL (eps: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(count) - value) < eps

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          (LAMBDA (count: nat):
            real_exponential_partial(x, count)),
          value))

  e: real = real_exponential(1)

  integer_polynomial_value(
      coefficients: [nat -> int],
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET degree: nat = count - 1 IN
        integer_polynomial_value(
          coefficients, x, count - 1)
          + (coefficients(degree) :: real) * x ^ degree
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  algebraic_real(x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (degree: nat):
      EXISTS (coefficients: [nat -> int]):
        NOT (coefficients(degree) = 0)
          AND integer_polynomial_value(
            coefficients, x, degree + 1) = 0

  e_is_transcendental: bool =
    NOT algebraic_real(e)
END hundred_theorems_067

title: 068_sum_of_an_arithmetic_series
content:
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Johannes Hölzl
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Group.LocallyFinite
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Interval.Finset.Basic
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Sub.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators

/-!
# Results about big operators over intervals

We prove results about big operators over intervals.
-/

public section

open Nat Finset

variable {α G M : Type*}

namespace Finset

section Generic
variable [CommMonoid M] {s₂ s₁ s : Finset α} {a : α} {g f : α → M}

@[to_additive]
theorem prod_Ico_add' [AddCommMonoid α] [PartialOrder α] [IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid α]
    [ExistsAddOfLE α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α]
    (f : α → M) (a b c : α) : (∏ x ∈ Ico a b, f (x + c)) = ∏ x ∈ Ico (a + c) (b + c), f x := by sorry
theorem prod_Ico_add [AddCommMonoid α] [PartialOrder α] [IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid α]
    [ExistsAddOfLE α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α]
    (f : α → M) (a b c : α) : (∏ x ∈ Ico a b, f (c + x)) = ∏ x ∈ Ico (a + c) (b + c), f x := by sorry
theorem prod_Ico_add_right_sub_eq [AddCommMonoid α] [PartialOrder α] [IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid α]
    [ExistsAddOfLE α] [LocallyFiniteOrder α] [Sub α] [OrderedSub α] (a b c : α) :
    ∏ x ∈ Ico (a + c) (b + c), f (x - c) = ∏ x ∈ Ico a b, f x := by sorry
theorem prod_Ico_succ_top {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) (f : ℕ → M) :
    (∏ k ∈ Ico a (b + 1), f k) = (∏ k ∈ Ico a b, f k) * f b := by sorry
theorem prod_Ico_consecutive (f : ℕ → M) {m n k : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) (hnk : n ≤ k) :
    ((∏ i ∈ Ico m n, f i) * ∏ i ∈ Ico n k, f i) = ∏ i ∈ Ico m k, f i :=
  Ico_union_Ico_eq_Ico hmn hnk ▸ Eq.symm (prod_union (Ico_disjoint_Ico_consecutive m n k))

@[to_additive]
theorem prod_Ioc_consecutive (f : ℕ → M) {m n k : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) (hnk : n ≤ k) :
    ((∏ i ∈ Ioc m n, f i) * ∏ i ∈ Ioc n k, f i) = ∏ i ∈ Ioc m k, f i := by sorry
theorem prod_Ioc_succ_top {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) (f : ℕ → M) :
    (∏ k ∈ Ioc a (b + 1), f k) = (∏ k ∈ Ioc a b, f k) * f (b + 1) := by sorry
theorem prod_Icc_succ_top {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b + 1) (f : ℕ → M) :
    (∏ k ∈ Icc a (b + 1), f k) = (∏ k ∈ Icc a b, f k) * f (b + 1) := by sorry
theorem prod_range_mul_prod_Ico (f : ℕ → M) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) :
    ((∏ k ∈ range m, f k) * ∏ k ∈ Ico m n, f k) = ∏ k ∈ range n, f k :=
  Nat.Ico_zero_eq_range ▸ Nat.Ico_zero_eq_range ▸ prod_Ico_consecutive f m.zero_le h

@[to_additive]
theorem prod_range_eq_mul_Ico (f : ℕ → M) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∏ x ∈ Finset.range n, f x = f 0 * ∏ x ∈ Ico 1 n, f x :=
  Finset.range_eq_Ico ▸ Finset.prod_eq_prod_Ico_succ_bot hn f

@[to_additive]
theorem prod_Ico_eq_mul_inv {δ : Type*} [CommGroup δ] (f : ℕ → δ) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) :
    ∏ k ∈ Ico m n, f k = (∏ k ∈ range n, f k) * (∏ k ∈ range m, f k)⁻¹ :=
  eq_mul_inv_iff_mul_eq.2 <| by (rw [mul_comm]; exact prod_range_mul_prod_Ico f h)

@[to_additive]
theorem prod_Ico_eq_div {δ : Type*} [CommGroup δ] (f : ℕ → δ) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) :
    ∏ k ∈ Ico m n, f k = (∏ k ∈ range n, f k) / ∏ k ∈ range m, f k := by sorry
theorem prod_range_div_prod_range {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] {f : ℕ → G} {n m : ℕ} (hnm : n ≤ m) :
    ((∏ k ∈ range m, f k) / ∏ k ∈ range n, f k) = ∏ k ∈ range m with n ≤ k, f k := by sorry
theorem sum_Ico_Ico_comm {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (a b : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℕ → M) :
    (∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico a b, ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico i b, f i j) =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico a b, ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico a (j + 1), f i j := by sorry
theorem sum_Ico_Ico_comm' {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (a b : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℕ → M) :
    (∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico a b, ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico (i + 1) b, f i j) =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico a b, ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico a j, f i j := by sorry
theorem prod_Ico_eq_prod_range (f : ℕ → M) (m n : ℕ) :
    ∏ k ∈ Ico m n, f k = ∏ k ∈ range (n - m), f (m + k) := by sorry
theorem prod_Ico_reflect (f : ℕ → M) (k : ℕ) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n + 1) :
    (∏ j ∈ Ico k m, f (n - j)) = ∏ j ∈ Ico (n + 1 - m) (n + 1 - k), f j := by sorry
theorem sum_Ico_reflect {δ : Type*} [AddCommMonoid δ] (f : ℕ → δ) (k : ℕ) {m n : ℕ}
    (h : m ≤ n + 1) : (∑ j ∈ Ico k m, f (n - j)) = ∑ j ∈ Ico (n + 1 - m) (n + 1 - k), f j :=
  @prod_Ico_reflect (Multiplicative δ) _ f k m n h

theorem prod_range_reflect (f : ℕ → M) (n : ℕ) :
    (∏ j ∈ range n, f (n - 1 - j)) = ∏ j ∈ range n, f j := by sorry
theorem sum_range_reflect {δ : Type*} [AddCommMonoid δ] (f : ℕ → δ) (n : ℕ) :
    (∑ j ∈ range n, f (n - 1 - j)) = ∑ j ∈ range n, f j :=
  @prod_range_reflect (Multiplicative δ) _ f n

@[simp]
theorem prod_Ico_id_eq_factorial : ∀ n : ℕ, (∏ x ∈ Ico 1 (n + 1), x) = n ! := by sorry
section GaussSum

/-- Gauss' summation formula -/
theorem sum_range_id_mul_two (n : ℕ) : (∑ i ∈ range n, i) * 2 = n * (n - 1) :=
  calc

theorem prod_Ico_div_bot (hmn : m < n) : (∏ i ∈ Ico m n, f i) / f m = ∏ i ∈ Ico (m + 1) n, f i :=

@[to_additive]

theorem prod_Icc_div (hmn : m ≤ n) (f : ℕ → M) :

-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems corpus artifact
-- hundred-theorems__agda__068, "Sum of an Arithmetic Series": twice the
-- inclusive natural-number arithmetic-series sum. This file contains no proof.

module ArithmeticSeries where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

sumThrough : Nat → (Nat → Nat) → Nat
sumThrough zero term = term zero
sumThrough (suc n) term =
  sumThrough n term + term (suc n)

sum-of-an-arithmetic-series : Set
sum-of-an-arithmetic-series =
  (a d n : Nat) →
  2 * sumThrough n (λ i → a + i * d)
    ≡ suc n * (2 * a + n * d)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  The included set.mm library supplies semirings, their carriers and additive
  operations, nonnegative integers, natural scalar multiplication, and finite
  group sums. The hypotheses below are definitional abbreviations for the
  carrier and additive operations of R.

  The expression ` sum_ j e. ( 0 ... N ) j ` is the triangular-number
  coefficient. The map expression in ` R gsum ` binds k and sums

  specializes to the natural-number statements in the other sources.

  ht068.t $e |- .x. = ( .g ` R ) $.

  $d .x. j $.  $d .+ j $.
  $d A k $.  $d D k $.  $d N k $.  $d R k $.  $d S k $.
