title: 076_fourier_series
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of corpus artifact hundred-theorems__agda__076,
-- "Fourier Series": every square-integrable real function on [-pi, pi] is the
-- L2-limit of its normalized trigonometric Fourier partial sums. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      Both (lessOrEqual zeroR oneR) (zeroR != oneR)

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
              lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both (lessOrEqual reals x y) (x != y)

maximum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
maximum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left _ = y
... | right _ = x

power :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
power reals x zero =
  oneR reals
power reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals (power reals x n) x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero = suc zero
factorial (suc n) = suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

sumThrough :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
sumThrough reals term zero =
  term zero
sumThrough reals term (suc n) =
  add reals
    (sumThrough reals term n)
    (term (suc n))

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      Both
        (StrictLess reals
          (subtract reals limit epsilon)
          (sequence n))
        (StrictLess reals
          (sequence n)
          (add reals limit epsilon)))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals term limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n term)
    limit

alternatingPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingPower reals n =
  power reals (negate reals (oneR reals)) n

sineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (power reals x (suc ((suc (suc zero)) * n))))
    (fromNat reals
      (factorial (suc ((suc (suc zero)) * n))))

cosineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
cosineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (power reals x ((suc (suc zero)) * n)))
    (fromNat reals
      (factorial ((suc (suc zero)) * n)))

leibnizTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
leibnizTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (alternatingPower reals n)
    (fromNat reals (suc ((suc (suc zero)) * n)))

SineValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
SineValue reals x value =
  SeriesHasSum reals (sineTerm reals x) value

CosineValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CosineValue reals x value =
  SeriesHasSum reals (cosineTerm reals x) value

record PiValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (value : R) : Set where
  field
    positive :
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) value
    leibniz-series :
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (leibnizTerm reals)
        (divide reals value
          (fromNat reals
            (suc (suc (suc (suc zero))))))

record SquareRootValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (x root : R) : Set where
  field
    nonnegative :
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) root
    squares-to :
      square reals root == x

Subset : Set -> Set1
Subset A = A -> Set

Contained :
  {A : Set} ->
  Subset A ->
  Subset A ->
  Set
Contained {A} S T =
  (x : A) -> S x -> T x

Intersection :
  {A : Set} ->
  Subset A ->
  Subset A ->
  Subset A
Intersection S T x =
  Both (S x) (T x)

Difference :
  {A : Set} ->
  Subset A ->
  Subset A ->
  Subset A
Difference S T x =
  Both (S x) (Not (T x))

InPeriod :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
InPeriod reals pi x =
  Both
    (lessOrEqual reals (negate reals pi) x)
    (lessOrEqual reals x pi)

OpenInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
OpenInterval reals a b x =
  Both
    (StrictLess reals a x)
    (StrictLess reals x b)

intervalLength :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
intervalLength reals a b =
  maximum reals
    (zeroR reals)
    (subtract reals b a)

record CoverCost
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (S : Subset R)
  (cost : R) : Set1 where
  field
    lower upper : Nat -> R
    covers :
      (x : R) ->
      S x ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> OpenInterval reals (lower n) (upper n) x)
    cost-series :
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (\ n -> intervalLength reals (lower n) (upper n))
        cost

record OuterMeasureValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (S : Subset R)
  (value : R) : Set1 where
  field
    inside-period :
      Contained S (InPeriod reals pi)
    nonnegative :
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) value
    lower-bound :
      (cost : R) ->
      CoverCost reals S cost ->
      lessOrEqual reals value cost
    greatest-lower-bound :
      (candidate : R) ->
      ((cost : R) ->
        CoverCost reals S cost ->
        lessOrEqual reals candidate cost) ->
      lessOrEqual reals candidate value

record LebesgueMeasurable
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (S : Subset R) : Set1 where
  field
    inside-period :
      Contained S (InPeriod reals pi)
    caratheodory :
      (A : Subset R) ->
      (whole leftPart rightPart : R) ->
      OuterMeasureValue reals pi A whole ->
      OuterMeasureValue reals pi (Intersection A S) leftPart ->
      OuterMeasureValue reals pi (Difference A S) rightPart ->
      whole == add reals leftPart rightPart

OpenPreimageOnPeriod :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Subset R
OpenPreimageOnPeriod reals pi f a b x =
  Both
    (InPeriod reals pi x)
    (OpenInterval reals a b (f x))

LebesgueMeasurableFunction :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set1
LebesgueMeasurableFunction {R} reals pi f =
  (a b : R) ->
  LebesgueMeasurable reals pi
    (OpenPreimageOnPeriod reals pi f a b)

positivePart :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
positivePart reals f x =
  maximum reals (zeroR reals) (f x)

negativePart :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
negativePart reals f x =
  maximum reals
    (zeroR reals)
    (negate reals (f x))

record NonnegativeSimpleBelow
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (upperFunction simpleFunction : R -> R) : Set1 where
  field
    cutoff : Nat
    values : Nat -> R
    pieces : Nat -> Subset R

    values-nonnegative :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <=N cutoff ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (values i)
    pieces-measurable :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <=N cutoff ->
      LebesgueMeasurable reals pi (pieces i)
    pieces-disjoint :
      (i j : Nat) ->
      i <=N cutoff ->
      j <=N cutoff ->
      i != j ->
      (x : R) ->
      Not (Both (pieces i x) (pieces j x))
    pieces-cover-period :
      (x : R) ->
      InPeriod reals pi x ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ i ->
          Both
            (i <=N cutoff)
            (pieces i x))
    represented-on-pieces :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <=N cutoff ->
      (x : R) ->
      InPeriod reals pi x ->
      pieces i x ->
      simpleFunction x == values i
    nonnegative-and-below :
      (x : R) ->
      InPeriod reals pi x ->
      Both
        (lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (simpleFunction x))
        (lessOrEqual reals (simpleFunction x) (upperFunction x))

record SimpleIntegralValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (upperFunction simpleFunction : R -> R)
  (value : R) : Set1 where
  field
    simple :
      NonnegativeSimpleBelow
        reals pi upperFunction simpleFunction
    measures : Nat -> R
    piece-measure :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <=N NonnegativeSimpleBelow.cutoff simple ->
      OuterMeasureValue reals pi
        (NonnegativeSimpleBelow.pieces simple i)
        (measures i)
    integral-equation :
      value ==
      sumThrough reals
        (\ i ->
          multiply reals
            (NonnegativeSimpleBelow.values simple i)
            (measures i))
        (NonnegativeSimpleBelow.cutoff simple)

record NonnegativeLebesgueIntegralValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (function : R -> R)
  (value : R) : Set1 where
  field
    function-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      InPeriod reals pi x ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (function x)
    upper-bound :
      (simpleFunction : R -> R) ->
      (simpleValue : R) ->
      SimpleIntegralValue
        reals pi function simpleFunction simpleValue ->
      lessOrEqual reals simpleValue value
    least-upper-bound :
      (upper : R) ->
      ((simpleFunction : R -> R) ->
        (simpleValue : R) ->
        SimpleIntegralValue
          reals pi function simpleFunction simpleValue ->
        lessOrEqual reals simpleValue upper) ->
      lessOrEqual reals value upper

record LebesgueIntegralValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (function : R -> R)
  (value : R) : Set1 where
  field
    measurable :
      LebesgueMeasurableFunction reals pi function
    positive-integral negative-integral : R
    positive-integral-value :
      NonnegativeLebesgueIntegralValue reals pi
        (positivePart reals function)
        positive-integral
    negative-integral-value :
      NonnegativeLebesgueIntegralValue reals pi
        (negativePart reals function)
        negative-integral
    integral-equation :
      value ==
      subtract reals positive-integral negative-integral

record LebesgueIntegrable
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (function : R -> R) : Set1 where
  field
    integral : R
    integral-value :
      LebesgueIntegralValue reals pi function integral

record SquareIntegrable
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (function : R -> R) : Set1 where
  field
    measurable :
      LebesgueMeasurableFunction reals pi function
    square-integrable :
      LebesgueIntegrable reals pi
        (\ x -> square reals (function x))

data Parity : Set where
  even odd : Parity

opposite : Parity -> Parity
opposite even = odd
opposite odd = even

parity : Nat -> Parity
parity zero = even
parity (suc n) = opposite (parity n)

half : Nat -> Nat
half zero = zero
half (suc zero) = zero
half (suc (suc n)) = suc (half n)

TrigonometricBasisValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
TrigonometricBasisValue {R} reals pi zero x value =
  Exists R
    (\ root ->
      Both
        (SquareRootValue reals
          (multiply reals
            (fromNat reals (suc (suc zero)))
            pi)
          root)
        (value == divide reals (oneR reals) root))
TrigonometricBasisValue {R} reals pi (suc n) x value
  with parity (suc n)
... | odd =
  Exists R
    (\ sineValue ->
      Exists R
        (\ root ->
          Both
            (SineValue reals
              (multiply reals
                (fromNat reals (suc (half (suc n))))
                x)
              sineValue)
            (Both
              (SquareRootValue reals pi root)
              (value == divide reals sineValue root))))
... | even =
  Exists R
    (\ cosineValue ->
      Exists R
        (\ root ->
          Both
            (CosineValue reals
              (multiply reals
                (fromNat reals (half (suc n)))
                x)
              cosineValue)
            (Both
              (SquareRootValue reals pi root)
              (value == divide reals cosineValue root))))

fourierPartialSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R -> R) ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
fourierPartialSum reals basis coefficients n x =
  sumThrough reals
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (coefficients i)
        (basis i x))
    n

record L2NormValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (function : R -> R)
  (value : R) : Set1 where
  field
    squared-integral : R
    squared-integral-value :
      LebesgueIntegralValue reals pi
        (\ x -> square reals (function x))
        squared-integral
    square-root-value :
      SquareRootValue reals squared-integral value

record FourierExpansionConverges
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (pi : R)
  (function : R -> R) : Set1 where
  field
    basis : Nat -> R -> R
    basis-values :
      (n : Nat) ->
      (x : R) ->
      TrigonometricBasisValue reals pi n x (basis n x)

    coefficients : Nat -> R
    coefficient-values :
      (n : Nat) ->
      LebesgueIntegralValue reals pi
        (\ x -> multiply reals (basis n x) (function x))
        (coefficients n)

    errors : Nat -> R
    error-values :
      (n : Nat) ->
      L2NormValue reals pi
        (\ x ->
          subtract reals
            (function x)
            (fourierPartialSum reals basis coefficients n x))
        (errors n)
    errors-converge-to-zero :
      ConvergesTo reals errors (zeroR reals)

record FourierSeriesStatement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) : Set1 where
  field
    pi : R
    pi-value : PiValue reals pi
    l2-convergence :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      SquareIntegrable reals pi function ->
      FourierExpansionConverges reals pi function

fourier-series : Set1
fourier-series =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  FourierSeriesStatement reals

  sums. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory iterateTheory realTheory transcTheory;
open topologyTheory real_topologyTheory extrealTheory measureTheory borelTheory;
open lebesgueTheory lebesgue_measureTheory;

val fourier_series_l2 =
  ``let domain = interval [(-pi : real), pi] in
    let trigonometric_set =
      \i x.
        if i = 0 then
          1 / sqrt (2 * pi)
        else if ODD i then
          sin ((&(i DIV 2 + 1) : real) * x) / sqrt pi
        else
          cos ((&(i DIV 2) : real) * x) / sqrt pi
    in
    let fourier_coefficient =
      \f i.
        real
          (integral lebesgue
            (\x. Normal (trigonometric_set i x * f x) *
                 indicator_fn domain x))
    in
    let l2norm =
      \g.
        sqrt
          (real
            (integral lebesgue
              (\x. Normal ((g x) pow 2) * indicator_fn domain x)))
    in
      !f : real -> real.
        (\x. Normal (f x) * indicator_fn domain x) IN
          measurable (m_space lebesgue, measurable_sets lebesgue) Borel /\
        integrable lebesgue
          (\x. Normal ((f x) pow 2) * indicator_fn domain x)
        ==>
        (((\n.
             l2norm
               (\x.
                  f x -
                  SIGMA
                    (\i. fourier_coefficient f i *
                         trigonometric_set i x)
                    (count (SUC n)))) -->
          (0 : real)) sequentially)``;

title: 076_fourier_series
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Fourier Series" from Hundred Theorems
  corpus artifact 076. It states that the normalized real trigonometric
  Fourier partial sums of every square-integrable real function on
  [-pi,pi] converge to that function in the L2 norm. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  The interval C below is (-pi,pi); replacing the closed source interval by
  this open interval does not change square-integrability, Fourier
  coefficients, or L2 convergence because the two endpoints have Lebesgue
  measure zero.

  HT076Basis is exactly the source basis in its source ordering:

    k = 0       : 1 / sqrt(2*pi)
    k = 2*j+1   : sin((j+1)*x) / sqrt(pi)
    k = 2*j+2   : cos((j+1)*x) / sqrt(pi).

  HT076Coeff is the Lebesgue integral of f times a basis element, and
  HT076Partial is the sum over 0 <= k < n. HT076SquareIntegrable says that
  the restriction of f to C is measurable and that its square is Lebesgue
  integrable there. The conclusion is the epsilon-N expansion of convergence
  of the squared-error integral to zero, which is equivalent to convergence
  in the L2 norm.

  All four definitions and the final theorem declaration are unproved $a
  statements; this database contains no $p proof statements.
$)

$c HT076Basis HT076Coeff HT076Partial HT076SquareIntegrable $.

ht076-basis-syntax $a class ( HT076Basis K X ) $.
ht076-coeff-syntax $a class ( HT076Coeff F K ) $.
ht076-partial-syntax $a class ( HT076Partial F N X ) $.
ht076-square-integrable-syntax $a wff ( HT076SquareIntegrable F ) $.

${
  $d j K $.
  $d j X $.

  ht076-basis-definition $a |- (
    ( HT076Basis K X )
    =
    if
      (
        K = 0 ,
        ( 1 / ( sqrt ` ( 2 x. _pi ) ) ) ,
        if
          (
            E. j e. NN0 K = ( ( 2 x. j ) + 1 ) ,
            (
              ( sin ` ( ( ( K + 1 ) / 2 ) x. X ) )
              /
              ( sqrt ` _pi )
            ) ,
            (
              ( cos ` ( ( K / 2 ) x. X ) )
              /
              ( sqrt ` _pi )
            )
          )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d x F $.
  $d x K $.

  ht076-coeff-definition $a |- (
    ( HT076Coeff F K )
    =
    S. ( -u _pi (,) _pi )
      ( ( F ` x ) x. ( HT076Basis K x ) )
      _d x
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k F $.
  $d k N $.
  $d k X $.

  ht076-partial-definition $a |- (
    ( HT076Partial F N X )
    =
    sum_ k e. ( 0 ..^ N )
      ( ( HT076Coeff F k ) x. ( HT076Basis k X ) )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d x F $.

  ht076-square-integrable-definition $a |- (
    ( HT076SquareIntegrable F )
    <->
    (
      F : RR --> RR
      /\
      (
        ( F |` ( -u _pi (,) _pi ) ) e. MblFn
        /\
        (
          x e. ( -u _pi (,) _pi )
          |->
          ( ( F ` x ) ^ 2 )
        )
        e. L^1
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d e F $.
  $d m F $.
  $d n F $.
  $d x F $.
  $d x n $.

  hundred-theorems-076-fourier-series $a |- (
    ( HT076SquareIntegrable F )
    ->
    A. e e. RR
      (
        0 < e
        ->
        E. m e. NN0
          A. n e. NN0
            (
              m <_ n
              ->
              S. ( -u _pi (,) _pi )
                (
                  (
                    ( F ` x )
                    -
                    ( HT076Partial F n x )
                  )
                  ^ 2
                )
                _d x
                < e
            )
      )
  ) $.
$}

title: 076_fourier_series
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact 076, "Fourier
:: Series": the normalized trigonometric Fourier partial sums of every
:: square-integrable real function on [-PI,PI] converge to it in L2. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ

 vocabularies NUMBERS, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
      PARTFUN1, CARD_1, CARD_3, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, VALUED_0,
      VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3,
      REAL_1, SQUARE_1, SIN_COS, SEQ_1, RVSUM_1,
      SUPINF_2, MEASURE1, MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5, MEASUR12, INTEGRA5;
 notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
      PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
      XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, XXREAL_3, NAT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, FINSEQ_1,
      SQUARE_1, SIN_COS, SEQ_1, RVSUM_1, SUPINF_2,
      MEASURE1, MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5, MESFUNC6, MEASUR12, INTEGRA5,
      EXTREAL1;
 constructors RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, REAL_1, SQUARE_1,
      SIN_COS, RVSUM_1, MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5, MESFUNC6,
      MEASUR12, INTEGRA5, EXTREAL1;
 registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
      ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, NAT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
      FINSEQ_1, SQUARE_1, XXREAL_3, MEASURE1, MEASUR12;
 requirements BOOLE, SUBSET, NUMERALS, REAL, ARITHM;
 definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0;
 equalities FINSEQ_1, SQUARE_1;
 expansions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1, FINSEQ_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for I being Element of L-Field,
      f,sqf being Function of REAL,REAL,
      basis,partial,error being Function of NAT,Funcs(REAL,REAL),
      coeff being Real_Sequence
  st
    I = [.-PI,PI.] &
    (for x being Real holds sqf.x = (f.x)^2) &
    f|I is_integrable_on L-Meas &
    sqf|I is_integrable_on L-Meas &
    (for b being Function of REAL,REAL st b = basis.0 holds
      for x being Real holds b.x = 1 / (sqrt(2)*sqrt(PI))) &
    (for k being Nat,
         b,c being Function of REAL,REAL
      st b = basis.(2*k+1) & c = basis.(2*k+2)
      holds for x being Real holds
        b.x = sin.(((k+1) qua Real)*x) / sqrt(PI) &
        c.x = cos.(((k+1) qua Real)*x) / sqrt(PI)) &
    (for n being Nat, b being Function of REAL,REAL
      st b = basis.n holds
      ex h being Function of REAL,REAL st
        (for x being Real holds
          h.x = b.x * f.x) &
        h|I is_integrable_on L-Meas &
        coeff.n = Integral(L-Meas,h|I)) &
    (for n being Nat, x being Real,
         p being Function of REAL,REAL
      st p = partial.n holds
      ex a being FinSequence of REAL st
        len a = n+1 &
        (for j being Nat st j in dom a holds
          ex b being Function of REAL,REAL st
            b = basis.(j-'1) &
            a.j = coeff.(j-'1) * b.x) &
        p.x = Sum a) &
    (for n being Nat,
         p,r being Function of REAL,REAL
      st p = partial.n & r = error.n holds
        for x being Real holds r.x = (f.x - p.x) * (f.x - p.x))
  holds
    (for n being Nat, r being Function of REAL,REAL
      st r = error.n holds r|I is_integrable_on L-Meas) &
    for e being positive Real
    ex N being Nat
    st for n being Nat, r being Function of REAL,REAL
      st N <= n & r = error.n holds
        ex q,t being ExtReal st
          q = Integral(L-Meas,r|I) &
          t = e^2 &
          q <= t
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 076_fourier_series
content:
% Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 076, "Fourier Series":
% every real Lebesgue-square-integrable function on [-pi, pi] is the L2 limit
% of its Fourier partial sums in the normalized sine-cosine basis.
% This file contains no proof.

fourier_series_076: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_set: TYPE = [real -> bool]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_set_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real_set]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  finite_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(values: real_sequence, limit: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(values(count) - limit) < epsilon_value

  sine_partial_sum(count: nat, x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        sine_partial_sum(count - 1, x)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index) * x ^ (2 * index + 1),
              factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  cosine_partial_sum(count: nat, x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial_sum(count - 1, x)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  sine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): sine_partial_sum(count, x),
          value))

  cosine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial_sum(count, x),
          value))

  is_pi(value: real): bool =
    2 < value
      AND value < 4
      AND cosine(value / 2) = 0

  pi: real =
    epsilon(LAMBDA (value: real): is_pi(value))

  nonnegative_square_root(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        value >= 0 AND value * value = x)

  closed_interval: real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      -pi <= x AND x <= pi

  interval_length(left_endpoint, right_endpoint: real): real =
    IF left_endpoint < right_endpoint THEN
      right_endpoint - left_endpoint
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  open_interval_cover(
      covered: real_set,
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      covered(x) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (index: nat):
          left_endpoints(index) < x
            AND x < right_endpoints(index)

  cover_partial_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      count: nat): real =
    finite_sum(
      LAMBDA (index: nat):
        interval_length(
          left_endpoints(index),
          right_endpoints(index)),
      count)

  cover_has_total_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      total: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat):
        cover_partial_length(
          left_endpoints, right_endpoints, count),
      total)

  has_outer_measure(covered: real_set, measure_value: real): bool =
    measure_value >= 0
      AND (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS
            (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
            (total: real):
          open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
            AND cover_has_total_length(
              left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total)
            AND total < measure_value + epsilon_value)
      AND (FORALL
          (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
          (total: real):
        (open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
          AND cover_has_total_length(
            left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total))
        IMPLIES measure_value <= total)

  set_intersection(left_set, right_set: real_set): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_set(x) AND right_set(x)

  set_difference(left_set, right_set: real_set): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_set(x) AND NOT right_set(x)

  lebesgue_measurable(measured_set: real_set): bool =
    FORALL
        (test_set: real_set),
        (test_measure, inside_measure, outside_measure: real):
      (has_outer_measure(test_set, test_measure)
        AND has_outer_measure(
          set_intersection(test_set, measured_set),
          inside_measure)
        AND has_outer_measure(
          set_difference(test_set, measured_set),
          outside_measure))
      IMPLIES
        test_measure = inside_measure + outside_measure

  lebesgue_measure(measured_set: real_set): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (measure_value: real):
        has_outer_measure(measured_set, measure_value))

  interval_sublevel_set(
      function_value: real_function,
      bound: real): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      closed_interval(x) AND function_value(x) <= bound

  measurable_on_interval(function_value: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (bound: real):
      lebesgue_measurable(
        interval_sublevel_set(function_value, bound))

  pairwise_disjoint_below(
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index < count
        AND right_index < count
        AND left_index /= right_index
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (x: real):
          NOT (pieces(left_index)(x)
            AND pieces(right_index)(x))

  simple_value(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat,
      x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      simple_value(coefficients, pieces, count - 1, x)
        + IF pieces(count - 1)(x)
            THEN coefficients(count - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  simple_integral(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      simple_integral(coefficients, pieces, count - 1)
        + coefficients(count - 1)
            * lebesgue_measure(pieces(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nonnegative_simple_minorant(
      function_value: real_function,
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    pairwise_disjoint_below(pieces, count)
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          coefficients(index) >= 0
            AND lebesgue_measurable(pieces(index))
            AND (FORALL (x: real):
              pieces(index)(x) IMPLIES closed_interval(x)))
      AND (FORALL (x: real):
        closed_interval(x) IMPLIES
          0 <= simple_value(
            coefficients, pieces, count, x)
          AND simple_value(
            coefficients, pieces, count, x)
              <= function_value(x))

  nonnegative_integral_upper_bound(
      function_value: real_function,
      upper_bound: real): bool =
    FORALL
        (coefficients: real_sequence),
        (pieces: real_set_sequence),
        (count: nat):
      nonnegative_simple_minorant(
        function_value, coefficients, pieces, count)
      IMPLIES
        simple_integral(coefficients, pieces, count)
          <= upper_bound

  has_nonnegative_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    measurable_on_interval(function_value)
      AND (FORALL (x: real):
        closed_interval(x) IMPLIES function_value(x) >= 0)
      AND integral_value >= 0
      AND nonnegative_integral_upper_bound(
        function_value, integral_value)
      AND (FORALL (upper_bound: real):
        nonnegative_integral_upper_bound(
          function_value, upper_bound)
        IMPLIES integral_value <= upper_bound)

  positive_part(function_value: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      IF function_value(x) >= 0
      THEN function_value(x)
      ELSE 0
      ENDIF

  negative_part(function_value: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      IF function_value(x) <= 0
      THEN -function_value(x)
      ELSE 0
      ENDIF

  has_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    measurable_on_interval(function_value)
      AND EXISTS (positive_integral, negative_integral: real):
        has_nonnegative_integral(
          positive_part(function_value), positive_integral)
          AND has_nonnegative_integral(
            negative_part(function_value), negative_integral)
          AND integral_value =
            positive_integral - negative_integral

  integral(function_value: real_function): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
        has_integral(function_value, integral_value))

  square_integrable(function_value: real_function): bool =
    measurable_on_interval(function_value)
      AND EXISTS (square_integral: real):
        has_nonnegative_integral(
          LAMBDA (x: real):
            function_value(x) * function_value(x),
          square_integral)

  squared_l2_integral(function_value: real_function): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (square_integral: real):
        has_nonnegative_integral(
          LAMBDA (x: real):
            function_value(x) * function_value(x),
          square_integral))

  l2_norm(function_value: real_function): real =
    nonnegative_square_root(
      squared_l2_integral(function_value))

  sine_basis_index(index, frequency: nat): bool =
    index = 2 * frequency + 1

  cosine_basis_index(index, frequency: nat): bool =
    index = 2 * frequency + 2

  trigonometric_basis(index: nat, x: real): real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      safe_div(1, nonnegative_square_root(2 * pi))
    ELSIF EXISTS (frequency: nat):
        sine_basis_index(index, frequency) THEN
      LET frequency: nat =
        epsilon(
          LAMBDA (candidate: nat):
            sine_basis_index(index, candidate))
      IN
        safe_div(
          sine(((frequency + 1) :: real) * x),
          nonnegative_square_root(pi))
    ELSE
      LET frequency: nat =
        epsilon(
          LAMBDA (candidate: nat):
            cosine_basis_index(index, candidate))
      IN
        safe_div(
          cosine(((frequency + 1) :: real) * x),
          nonnegative_square_root(pi))
    ENDIF

  fourier_coefficient(
      function_value: real_function,
      index: nat): real =
    integral(
      LAMBDA (x: real):
        trigonometric_basis(index, x)
          * function_value(x))

  fourier_partial_sum(
      function_value: real_function,
      count: nat,
      x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      fourier_partial_sum(
        function_value, count - 1, x)
        + fourier_coefficient(
            function_value, count - 1)
            * trigonometric_basis(count - 1, x)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  fourier_series: bool =
    FORALL (function_value: real_function):
      square_integrable(function_value)
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
            FORALL (index: nat):
              cutoff <= index IMPLIES
                l2_norm(
                  LAMBDA (x: real):
                    function_value(x)
                      - fourier_partial_sum(
                          function_value,
                          index + 1,
                          x))
                  < epsilon_value
END fourier_series_076

title: 077_sum_of_kth_powers
content:
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Johan Commelin, Kevin Buzzard
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Field
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.PowerSeries.Inverse
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.PowerSeries.Exp

/-!
# Bernoulli numbers

The Bernoulli numbers are a sequence of rational numbers that frequently show up in
number theory.

## Mathematical overview

The Bernoulli numbers $(B_0, B_1, B_2, \ldots)=(1, -1/2, 1/6, 0, -1/30, \ldots)$ are
a sequence of rational numbers. They show up in the formula for the sums of $k$th
powers. They are related to the Taylor series expansions of $x/\tan(x)$ and
of $\coth(x)$, and also show up in the values that the Riemann Zeta function
takes both at both negative and positive integers (and hence in the
theory of modular forms). For example, if $1 \leq n$ then

$$\zeta(2n)=\sum_{t\geq1}t^{-2n}=(-1)^{n+1}\frac{(2\pi)^{2n}B_{2n}}{2(2n)!}.$$

This result is formalised in Lean: `riemannZeta_two_mul_nat`.

The Bernoulli numbers can be formally defined using the power series

$$\sum B_n\frac{t^n}{n!}=\frac{t}{1-e^{-t}}$$

although that happens to not be the definition in mathlib (this is an *implementation
detail* and need not concern the mathematician).

Note that $B_1=-1/2$, meaning that we are using the $B_n^-$ of
[from Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernoulli_number).

## Implementation detail

The Bernoulli numbers are defined using well-founded induction, by the formula
$$B_n=1-\sum_{k\lt n}\frac{\binom{n}{k}}{n-k+1}B_k.$$
This formula is true for all $n$ and in particular $B_0=1$. Note that this is the definition
for positive Bernoulli numbers, which we call `bernoulli'`. The negative Bernoulli numbers are
then defined as `bernoulli := (-1)^n * bernoulli'`.

## Main theorems

`sum_bernoulli : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (n.choose k : ℚ) * bernoulli k = if n = 1 then 1 else 0`
-/

@[expose] public section


open Nat Finset Finset.Nat PowerSeries

variable (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra ℚ A]

/-! ### Definitions -/


/-- The Bernoulli numbers:
the $n$-th Bernoulli number $B_n$ is defined recursively via
$$B_n = 1 - \sum_{k < n} \binom{n}{k}\frac{B_k}{n+1-k}$$ -/
def bernoulli' (n : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  1 - ∑ k : Fin n, n.choose k / (n - k + 1) * bernoulli' k

theorem bernoulli'_def' (n : ℕ) :
    bernoulli' n = 1 - ∑ k : Fin n, n.choose k / (n - k + 1) * bernoulli' k := by sorry
theorem bernoulli'_def (n : ℕ) :
    bernoulli' n = 1 - ∑ k ∈ range n, n.choose k / (n - k + 1) * bernoulli' k := by sorry
theorem bernoulli'_spec (n : ℕ) :
    (∑ k ∈ range n.succ, (n.choose (n - k) : ℚ) / (n - k + 1) * bernoulli' k) = 1 := by sorry
theorem bernoulli'_spec' (n : ℕ) :
    (∑ k ∈ antidiagonal n, ((k.1 + k.2).choose k.2 : ℚ) / (k.2 + 1) * bernoulli' k.1) = 1 := by sorry
section Examples

@[simp]
theorem bernoulli'_zero : bernoulli' 0 = 1 := by sorry
theorem bernoulli'_one : bernoulli' 1 = 1 / 2 := by sorry
theorem bernoulli'_two : bernoulli' 2 = 1 / 6 := by sorry
theorem bernoulli'_three : bernoulli' 3 = 0 := by sorry
theorem bernoulli'_four : bernoulli' 4 = -1 / 30 := by sorry
end Examples

@[simp]
theorem sum_bernoulli' (n : ℕ) : (∑ k ∈ range n, (n.choose k : ℚ) * bernoulli' k) = n := by sorry
def bernoulli'PowerSeries :=
  mk fun n => algebraMap ℚ A (bernoulli' n / n !)

theorem bernoulli'PowerSeries_mul_exp_sub_one :
    bernoulli'PowerSeries A * (exp A - 1) = X * exp A := by sorry
theorem bernoulli'_eq_zero_of_odd {n : ℕ} (h_odd : Odd n) (hlt : 1 < n) : bernoulli' n = 0 := by sorry
def bernoulli (n : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  (-1) ^ n * bernoulli' n

theorem bernoulli'_eq_bernoulli (n : ℕ) : bernoulli' n = (-1) ^ n * bernoulli n := by sorry
theorem bernoulli_zero : bernoulli 0 = 1 := by simp [bernoulli]

@[simp]
theorem bernoulli_one : bernoulli 1 = -1 / 2 := by norm_num [bernoulli]

@[simp]
theorem bernoulli_two : bernoulli 2 = 6⁻¹ := by sorry
theorem bernoulli_eq_zero_of_odd {n : ℕ} (h_odd : Odd n) (hlt : 1 < n) : bernoulli n = 0 := by sorry
theorem bernoulli_eq_bernoulli'_of_ne_one {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 1) : bernoulli n = bernoulli' n := by sorry
theorem sum_bernoulli (n : ℕ) :
    (∑ k ∈ range n, (n.choose k : ℚ) * bernoulli k) = if n = 1 then 1 else 0 := by sorry
theorem bernoulli_spec' (n : ℕ) :
    (∑ k ∈ antidiagonal n, ((k.1 + k.2).choose k.2 : ℚ) / (k.2 + 1) * bernoulli k.1) =
      if n = 0 then 1 else 0 := by sorry
def bernoulliPowerSeries :=
  mk fun n => algebraMap ℚ A (bernoulli n / n !)

theorem bernoulliPowerSeries_mul_exp_sub_one : bernoulliPowerSeries A * (exp A - 1) = X := by sorry
section Faulhaber

/-- **Faulhaber's theorem** relating the **sum of p-th powers** to the Bernoulli numbers:
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} k^p = \sum_{i=0}^p B_i\binom{p+1}{i}\frac{n^{p+1-i}}{p+1}.$$
See https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Faulhaber%27s_Formula and [orosi2018faulhaber] for
the proof provided here. -/
theorem sum_range_pow (n p : ℕ) :
    (∑ k ∈ range n, (k : ℚ) ^ p) =
      ∑ i ∈ range (p + 1), bernoulli i * ((p + 1).choose i) * (n : ℚ) ^ (p + 1 - i) / (p + 1) := by sorry
theorem sum_Ico_pow (n p : ℕ) :
    (∑ k ∈ Ico 1 (n + 1), (k : ℚ) ^ p) =
      ∑ i ∈ range (p + 1), bernoulli' i * (p + 1).choose i * (n : ℚ) ^ (p + 1 - i) / (p + 1) := by sorry
end Faulhaber

Require Import Reals.
Open Scope R_scope.


Fixpoint bernoullicoeff (n:nat) (k:nat) : R:=
match n with |  O  => match k with | O => INR 1
                                   | _ => INR 0
                      end
             |(S m)=> 
  match k with 
| O    => (sum_f_R0 (fun l => -((bernoullicoeff m l)*(/INR (S l))*(INR n)*/ INR (S (S l)) )) m)
| (S l)=> (bernoullicoeff m l)*/(INR (S l))*(INR n)
  end
end.


Definition bernoulli_polynomial (n:nat) (x:R):=
(sum_f_R0 (fun l => (bernoullicoeff n l) *x^l) n).


Theorem bernoulli_polynomial_derivable_pt_lim:
forall n:nat,forall x:R,
derivable_pt_lim (bernoulli_polynomial (S n)) x ((bernoulli_polynomial n x)*(INR (S n))).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem bernoulli_polynomial_derivable_pt_lim_shift:
forall n:nat,forall x:R,
    derivable_pt_lim (fun x=> (bernoulli_polynomial (S n) (x+1))) x ((bernoulli_polynomial n (x+1))*(INR (S n))).
Proof.
Admitted.


Lemma sumzero : forall n:nat, sum_f_R0 (fun _ => 0:R) n=(0:R).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem bernoulli_polynomial_val_0_1:
  forall n:nat,n<>1%nat  -> bernoulli_polynomial n 0=bernoulli_polynomial n 1.
Proof.
Admitted.



Lemma primitive_diff : forall f g fp : (R->R), 
(forall x:R, derivable_pt_lim f x (fp x))->
(forall x:R, derivable_pt_lim g x (fp x))->
forall x:R, f x=(plus_fct g (fct_cte ((f 0)-(g 0)))) x.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma primitive_eq:forall f g fp : (R->R), 
(forall x:R, derivable_pt_lim f x (fp x))->
(forall x:R, derivable_pt_lim g x (fp x))->
f 0=g 0->
forall x:R, f x=g x.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma kthpowers : forall n:nat, forall x:R,
x^n*(INR (S n))=(bernoulli_polynomial (S n) (x+1))-(bernoulli_polynomial (S n) x).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma sum_kthpowers : forall r:nat, forall n:nat, 
(0<r)%nat->
sum_f_R0 (fun k => ((INR k)^r)%R) n
=((bernoulli_polynomial (S r) (INR n+1))-(bernoulli_polynomial (S r) 0))/(INR r+1).
Proof.
Admitted.

(*  
  File:       Bernoulli.thy
  Author:     Lukas Bulwahn <lukas.bulwahn-at-gmail.com> 
  Author:     Manuel Eberl <manuel@pruvisto.org> 
*)
section \<open>Bernoulli numbers\<close>

theory Bernoulli
imports Complex_Main
begin

subsection \<open>Preliminaries\<close>
  
lemma power_numeral_reduce: "a ^ numeral n = a * a ^ pred_numeral n"
  by sorry

lemma fact_diff_Suc: "n < Suc m \<Longrightarrow> fact (Suc m - n) = of_nat (Suc m - n) * fact (m - n)"
  by sorry

lemma of_nat_binomial_Suc:
  assumes "k \<le> n"
  shows   "(of_nat (Suc n choose k) :: 'a :: field_char_0) = 
             of_nat (Suc n) / of_nat (Suc n - k) * of_nat (n choose k)"
  by sorry

lemma integrals_eq:
  assumes "f 0 = g 0"
  assumes "\<And> x. ((\<lambda>x. f x - g x) has_real_derivative 0) (at x)"
  shows "f x = g x"
  by sorry

lemma sum_diff: "((\<Sum>i\<le>n::nat. f (i + 1) - f i)::'a::field) = f (n + 1) - f 0"
  by sorry
    
lemma Rats_sum: "(\<And>x. x \<in> A \<Longrightarrow> f x \<in> \<rat>) \<Longrightarrow> sum f A \<in> \<rat>"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Bernoulli Numbers and Bernoulli Polynomials\<close>

declare sum.cong [fundef_cong]

fun bernoulli :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a :: field_char_0"
where
  "bernoulli 0 = 1"
| "bernoulli (Suc n) =  (-1 / (of_nat n + 2)) * (\<Sum>k \<le> n. (of_nat (n + 2 choose k) * bernoulli k))"
  
declare bernoulli.simps[simp del]
  
lemmas bernoulli_0 [simp] = bernoulli.simps(1)
lemmas bernoulli_Suc = bernoulli.simps(2)
lemma bernoulli_1 [simp]: "bernoulli 1 = -1/2" by (simp add: bernoulli_Suc)
lemma bernoulli_Suc_0 [simp]: "bernoulli (Suc 0) = -1/2" by (simp add: bernoulli_Suc)

lemma of_rat_bernoulli: "of_rat (bernoulli n) = bernoulli n"
  by sorry

(* TODO: Move *)
lemma of_real_of_rat: "of_real (of_rat x) = (of_rat x :: 'a :: real_field)"
  by sorry

lemma of_real_bernoulli: "of_real (bernoulli n) = (bernoulli n :: 'a :: real_field)"
  by sorry

    
text \<open>
  The ``normal'' Bernoulli numbers are the negative Bernoulli numbers $B_n^{-}$ we just defined
  (so called because $B_1^{-} = -\frac{1}{2}$). There is also another convention, the 
  positive Bernoulli numbers $B_n^{+}$, which differ from the negative ones only in that 
  $B_1^{+} = \frac{1}{2}$. Both conventions have their justification, since a number of theorems 
  are easier to state with one than the other.
\<close>
definition bernoulli' :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a :: field_char_0" where
  "bernoulli' n = (if n = 1 then 1/2 else bernoulli n)"
  
lemma bernoulli'_0 [simp]: "bernoulli' 0 = 1" by (simp add: bernoulli'_def)
    
lemma bernoulli'_1 [simp]: "bernoulli' (Suc 0) = 1/2"
  by sorry

lemma bernoulli_conv_bernoulli': "n \<noteq> 1 \<Longrightarrow> bernoulli n = bernoulli' n"
  by sorry
    
lemma bernoulli'_conv_bernoulli: "n \<noteq> 1 \<Longrightarrow> bernoulli' n = bernoulli n"
  by sorry
    
lemma bernoulli_conv_bernoulli'_if: 
    "n \<noteq> 1 \<Longrightarrow> bernoulli n = (if n = 1 then -1/2 else bernoulli' n)"
  by sorry

lemma of_rat_bernoulli': "of_rat (bernoulli' n) = bernoulli' n"
  by sorry

lemma of_real_bernoulli': "of_real (bernoulli' n) = (bernoulli' n :: 'a :: real_field)"
  by sorry

lemma bernoulli_in_Rats: "bernoulli n \<in> \<rat>"
  by sorry

lemma bernoulli'_in_Rats: "bernoulli' n \<in> \<rat>"
  by sorry

definition bernpoly :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a :: real_algebra_1" where
  "bernpoly n = (\<lambda>x. \<Sum>k \<le> n. of_nat (n choose k) * of_real (bernoulli k) * x ^ (n - k))"
  
lemma bernpoly_altdef:
  "bernpoly n = (\<lambda>x. \<Sum>k\<le>n. of_nat (n choose k) * of_real (bernoulli (n - k)) * x ^ k)"
  by sorry

lemma bernoulli_Suc': 
  "bernoulli (Suc n) = -1/(of_nat n + 2) * (\<Sum>k\<le>n. of_nat (n + 2 choose (k + 2)) * bernoulli (n - k))" 
  by sorry
  

subsection \<open>Basic Observations on Bernoulli Polynomials\<close>

lemma bernpoly_0 [simp]: "bernpoly n 0 = of_real (bernoulli n)"
  by sorry

lemma continuous_on_bernpoly [continuous_intros]: 
  "continuous_on A (bernpoly n :: 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a :: real_normed_algebra_1)"
  by sorry

lemma isCont_bernpoly [continuous_intros]: 
  "isCont (bernpoly n :: 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a :: real_normed_algebra_1) x"
  by sorry

lemma has_field_derivative_bernpoly:
  "(bernpoly (Suc n) has_field_derivative 
     (of_nat (n + 1) * bernpoly n x :: 'a :: real_normed_field)) (at x)"
  by sorry
  
lemmas has_field_derivative_bernpoly' [derivative_intros] =
  DERIV_chain'[OF _ has_field_derivative_bernpoly]    

lemma sum_binomial_times_bernoulli:
  "(\<Sum>k\<le>n. of_nat ((Suc n) choose k) * bernoulli k) = (if n = 0 then 1 else 0)"
  by sorry
  
lemma sum_binomial_times_bernoulli':
  "(\<Sum>k<n. of_nat (n choose k) * bernoulli k :: 'a :: field_char_0) = (if n = 1 then 1 else 0)"
  by sorry
  
lemma binomial_unroll:
  "n > 0 \<Longrightarrow> (n choose k) = (if k = 0 then 1 else ((n - 1) choose (k - 1)) + ((n - 1) choose k))"
  by sorry

lemma sum_unroll:
  "(\<Sum>k\<le>n::nat. f k) = (if n = 0 then f 0 else f n + (\<Sum>k\<le>n - 1. f k))"
  by sorry

lemma bernoulli_unroll:
  "n > 0 \<Longrightarrow> bernoulli n = - 1 / (of_nat n + 1) * (\<Sum>k\<le>n - 1. of_nat (n + 1 choose k) * bernoulli k)"
  by sorry

lemmas bernoulli_unroll_all = binomial_unroll bernoulli_unroll sum_unroll bernpoly_def

lemma bernpoly_1_1: "bernpoly 1 1 = of_real (1/2)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Sum of Powers with Bernoulli Polynomials\<close>

(* TODO: Generalisation not possible here because mean-value theorem 
   is only available for reals *)
lemma diff_bernpoly:
  fixes x :: real
  shows "bernpoly n (x + 1) - bernpoly n x = of_nat n * x ^ (n - 1)"
  by sorry

lemma bernpoly_of_real: "bernpoly n (of_real x) = of_real (bernpoly n x)"
  by sorry
  
lemma bernpoly_1:
  assumes "n \<noteq> 1"
  shows   "bernpoly n 1 = of_real (bernoulli n)"
  by sorry
  
lemma bernpoly_1': "bernpoly n 1 = of_real (bernoulli' n)"
  by sorry

theorem sum_of_powers: 
  "(\<Sum>k\<le>n::nat. (real k) ^ m) = (bernpoly (Suc m) (n + 1) - bernpoly (Suc m) 0) / (m + 1)"
  by sorry
  
lemma sum_of_powers_nat_aux: 
  assumes "real a = b / c" "real b' = b" "real c' = c"
  shows   "a = b' div c'"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Instances for Square And Cubic Numbers\<close>

theorem sum_of_squares: "real (\<Sum>k\<le>n::nat. k ^ 2) = real (2 * n ^ 3 + 3 * n ^ 2 + n) / 6"
  by sorry

corollary sum_of_squares_nat: "(\<Sum>k\<le>n::nat. k ^ 2) = (2 * n ^ 3 + 3 * n ^ 2 + n) div 6"
  by sorry

theorem sum_of_cubes: "real (\<Sum>k\<le>n::nat. k ^ 3) = real (n ^ 2 + n) ^ 2 / 4"
  by sorry
                       
corollary sum_of_cubes_nat: "(\<Sum>k\<le>n::nat. k ^ 3) = (n ^ 2 + n) ^ 2 div 4"
  by sorry

end

(*

  artifact 077 (hundred-theorems__hol-light__077). It states Faulhaber's
  formula using Bernoulli numbers and Bernoulli polynomials. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

needs "Library/binomial.ml";;

prioritize_real();;

let SUM_OF_POWERS =
  `!bernoulli bernpoly.
      bernoulli 0 = &1 /\
      (!r. bernoulli (SUC r) =
           --sum(0..r) (\j. &(binom(r + 2,j)) * bernoulli j) /
           (&r + &2)) /\
      (!r x. bernpoly r x =
             sum(0..r)
               (\k. &(binom(r,k)) * bernoulli k * x pow (r - k)))
      ==> !m n.
          sum(0..n) (\k. &k pow m) =
          (bernpoly (SUC m) (&n + &1) -
           bernpoly (SUC m) (&0)) /
          (&m + &1)`;;

title: 077_sum_of_kth_powers
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__077, "Sum of kth Powers": for all natural numbers
;; n and m, the inclusive sum from k = 0 through n of k^m equals the
;; Bernoulli-polynomial finite-difference formula. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun hundred-theorems-077-binomial-coefficient (n k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (or (zp k)
          (zp n))
      (if (zp k) 1 0)
    (+ (hundred-theorems-077-binomial-coefficient
        (- n 1) k)
       (hundred-theorems-077-binomial-coefficient
        (- n 1) (- k 1)))))

(defun hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-weighted-sum
    (row k values)
  (if (consp values)
      (+ (* (hundred-theorems-077-binomial-coefficient row k)
            (car values))
         (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-weighted-sum
          row (+ k 1) (cdr values)))
    0))

(defun hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-prefix (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (list 1)
    (let* ((previous
            (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-prefix (- n 1)))
           (weighted-sum
            (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-weighted-sum
             (+ n 1) 0 previous))
           (next (/ (- weighted-sum) (+ n 1))))
      (append previous (list next)))))

(defun hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-number (n)
  (nth n (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-prefix n)))

(defun hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-polynomial-term
    (degree k x)
  (* (hundred-theorems-077-binomial-coefficient degree k)
     (* (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-number k)
        (expt x (- degree k)))))

(defun hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-polynomial-sum-through
    (degree k x)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix k)))
  (if (zp k)
      (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-polynomial-term degree 0 x)
    (+ (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-polynomial-sum-through
        degree (- k 1) x)
       (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-polynomial-term degree k x))))

(defun hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-polynomial (degree x)
  (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-polynomial-sum-through
   degree degree x))

(defun hundred-theorems-077-power-sum-through (n exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (expt 0 exponent)
    (+ (hundred-theorems-077-power-sum-through
        (- n 1) exponent)
       (expt n exponent))))

(defun hundred-theorems-077-sum-of-kth-powers-statement (n m)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (natp m))
   (equal
    (hundred-theorems-077-power-sum-through n m)
    (/ (- (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-polynomial
           (+ m 1) (+ n 1))
          (hundred-theorems-077-bernoulli-polynomial
           (+ m 1) 0))
       (+ m 1)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact
-- hundred-theorems__agda__077, "Sum of kth Powers": Faulhaber's formula
-- expressing an inclusive sum of natural-number powers using Bernoulli
-- numbers and Bernoulli polynomials over the real numbers. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infix 4 _!=_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    addR multiplyR : R -> R -> R
    negateR inverseR : R -> R
    lessOrEqualR : R -> R -> Set
    fromNatR : Nat -> R

    oneR-not-zeroR :
      oneR != zeroR

    addR-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> addR x y == addR y x
    addR-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> addR (addR x y) z == addR x (addR y z)
    addR-zero :
      (x : R) -> addR x zeroR == x
    addR-inverse :
      (x : R) -> addR x (negateR x) == zeroR

    multiplyR-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiplyR x y == multiplyR y x
    multiplyR-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiplyR (multiplyR x y) z == multiplyR x (multiplyR y z)
    multiplyR-one :
      (x : R) -> multiplyR x oneR == x
    multiplyR-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiplyR x zeroR == zeroR
    distributeR :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiplyR x (addR y z) ==
      addR (multiplyR x y) (multiplyR x z)
    multiplyR-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiplyR x (inverseR x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqualR x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR y z ->
      lessOrEqualR x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqualR x y) (lessOrEqualR y x)
    addR-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR (addR z x) (addR z y)
    multiplyR-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR (multiplyR x y)
    zeroR-less-than-oneR :
      Both (lessOrEqualR zeroR oneR) (zeroR != oneR)

    fromNatR-zero :
      fromNatR zero == zeroR
    fromNatR-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNatR (suc n) == addR (fromNatR n) oneR
    fromNatR-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNatR m == fromNatR n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Σ Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqualR x (fromNatR n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Σ R (\ x -> P x) ->
      Σ R (\ upper -> (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x upper) ->
      Σ R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x upper) ->
              lessOrEqualR supremum upper))

subtractR :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtractR reals x y =
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.addR reals x
    (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.negateR reals y)

divideR :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divideR reals x y =
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.multiplyR reals x
    (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.inverseR reals y)

powerR :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
powerR reals x zero =
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.oneR reals
powerR reals x (suc n) =
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.multiplyR reals
    (powerR reals x n)
    x

sumThroughR :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
sumThroughR reals term zero =
  term zero
sumThroughR reals term (suc n) =
  CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.addR reals
    (sumThroughR reals term n)
    (term (suc n))

choose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
choose n zero = suc zero
choose zero (suc k) = zero
choose (suc n) (suc k) = choose n (suc k) + choose n k

sum-of-kth-powers : Set1
sum-of-kth-powers =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField R) ->
  (bernoulli : Nat -> R) ->
  (bernpoly : Nat -> R -> R) ->
  bernoulli zero ==
    CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.oneR reals ->
  ((r : Nat) ->
    bernoulli (suc r) ==
      divideR reals
        (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.negateR reals
          (sumThroughR reals
            (\ j ->
              CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.multiplyR reals
                (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.fromNatR reals
                  (choose (suc (suc r)) j))
                (bernoulli j))
            r))
        (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.fromNatR reals
          (suc (suc r)))) ->
  ((r : Nat) ->
    (x : R) ->
    bernpoly r x ==
      sumThroughR reals
        (\ k ->
          CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.multiplyR reals
            (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.multiplyR reals
              (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.fromNatR reals
                (choose r k))
              (bernoulli k))
            (powerR reals x (r - k)))
        r) ->
  (m n : Nat) ->
  sumThroughR reals
      (\ k ->
        powerR reals
          (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.fromNatR reals k)
          m)
      n
    ==
  divideR reals
    (subtractR reals
      (bernpoly (suc m)
        (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.addR reals
          (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.fromNatR reals n)
          (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.oneR reals)))
      (bernpoly (suc m)
        (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.zeroR reals)))
    (CompleteArchimedeanOrderedField.fromNatR reals (suc m))

title: 077_sum_of_kth_powers
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 077, "Sum of kth Powers".
  Faulhaber's formula expresses each finite sum of natural-number powers using the
  recursively specified Bernoulli numbers and their Bernoulli polynomials. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory combinatoricsTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val sum_of_kth_powers =
  ``!bernoulli : num -> real.
      !bernpoly : num -> real -> real.
        bernoulli 0 = 1 /\
        (!r : num.
           bernoulli (SUC r) =
           -SIGMA
              (\j : num. &(binomial (r + 2) j) * bernoulli j)
              (count (SUC r)) /
           (&r + 2)) /\
        (!r : num. !x : real.
           bernpoly r x =
           SIGMA
             (\k : num.
                &(binomial r k) * bernoulli k * x pow (r - k))
             (count (SUC r)))
        ==>
        !m n : num.
          SIGMA (\k : num. &k pow m) (count (SUC n)) =
          (bernpoly (SUC m) (&n + 1) - bernpoly (SUC m) 0) /
          (&m + 1)``;

title: 077_sum_of_kth_powers
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Sum of kth Powers" from Hundred Theorems
  corpus artifact 077 (hundred-theorems__metamath__077): Faulhaber's formula
  expresses each inclusive finite sum of nonnegative-integer powers using
  Bernoulli polynomials. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  NN0 is the class of nonnegative integers, and BernPoly is set.mm's
  recursively defined Bernoulli polynomial operator. For K,M in NN0, the
  finite-sum binder ranges n over 0 through M, so the left side is

    0^K + 1^K + ... + M^K.

  The assertion is the target-native form of the same Bernoulli-polynomial
  identity stated over the reals or rationals in the source formalizations.
  Its final declaration is an unproved $a statement.
$)

${
  $d K n $.  $d M n $.

  hundred-theorems-077-sum-of-kth-powers $a
    |- ( ( K e. NN0 /\ M e. NN0 ) ->
         sum_ n e. ( 0 ... M ) ( n ^ K ) =
         ( ( ( ( K + 1 ) BernPoly ( M + 1 ) ) -
               ( ( K + 1 ) BernPoly 0 ) ) /
           ( K + 1 ) ) )
  $.
$}

title: 077_sum_of_kth_powers
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of "Sum of kth Powers" from Hundred Theorems
:: corpus artifact hundred-theorems__mizar__077. It states Faulhaber's formula
:: for finite sums of natural-number powers using Bernoulli numbers. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies NUMBERS, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, TARSKI, CARD_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, ORDINAL1, NEWTON, REALSET1, INT_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3,
    CARD_3, VALUED_0, VALUED_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, REAL_1, INT_1, NEWTON, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, FINSEQ_1, RVSUM_1, FINSEQ_2, NAT_1, NAT_D;
  constructors REAL_1, NAT_D, NEWTON, RELSET_1, NUMBERS, RVSUM_1,
    FINSEQOP, FUNCT_2;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XREAL_0, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    RVSUM_1, NEWTON, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, CARD_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for bernoulli being Function of NAT,REAL st
    bernoulli.0 = 1 &
    (for r being Nat
      ex recurrence being FinSequence of REAL st
        len recurrence = r + 1 &
        (for j being Nat st j <= r holds
          recurrence.(j + 1) =
            ((r + 2) choose j) * bernoulli.j) &
        (r + 2) * bernoulli.(r + 1) = -(Sum recurrence))
  holds
    for m,n being Nat
    ex powers,formula being FinSequence of REAL st
      len powers = n + 1 &
      (for k being Nat st k <= n holds
        powers.(k + 1) = k |^ m) &
      len formula = m + 1 &
      (for i being Nat st i <= m holds
        formula.(i + 1) =
          bernoulli.i * ((m + 1) choose i) *
          ((n + 1) |^ (m + 1 -' i))) &
      (m + 1) * Sum powers = Sum formula
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 077_sum_of_kth_powers
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Sum of kth Powers" from Hundred Theorems
% artifact 077 (hundred-theorems__pvs__077): Faulhaber's formula expresses
% inclusive sums of natural-number powers using Bernoulli polynomials. This
% file contains no proof.

sum_of_kth_powers_077: THEORY
BEGIN
  binomial_coefficient(n, k: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF k = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSIF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k - 1)
        + binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  real_prefix_sum(values: [nat -> real], count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      real_prefix_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  bernoulli_recurrence(bernoulli: [nat -> real]): bool =
    bernoulli(0) = 1
      AND (FORALL (r: nat):
        bernoulli(r + 1)
          = - real_prefix_sum(
              (LAMBDA (j: nat):
                (binomial_coefficient(r + 2, j) :: real)
                  * bernoulli(j)),
              r + 1)
            / ((r + 2) :: real))

  bernoulli_polynomial_spec(
      bernoulli: [nat -> real],
      bernoulli_polynomial: [nat, real -> real]): bool =
    FORALL (r: nat), (x: real):
      bernoulli_polynomial(r, x)
        = real_prefix_sum(
            (LAMBDA (k: nat):
              IF k <= r THEN
                (binomial_coefficient(r, k) :: real)
                  * bernoulli(k)
                  * x ^ (r - k)
              ELSE
                0
              ENDIF),
            r + 1)

  sum_of_kth_powers: bool =
    FORALL (bernoulli: [nat -> real]),
           (bernoulli_polynomial: [nat, real -> real]):
      (bernoulli_recurrence(bernoulli)
        AND bernoulli_polynomial_spec(
          bernoulli, bernoulli_polynomial))
      IMPLIES
        (FORALL (m, n: nat):
          real_prefix_sum(
            (LAMBDA (k: nat): (k :: real) ^ m),
            n + 1)
            = (bernoulli_polynomial(m + 1, (n :: real) + 1)
                - bernoulli_polynomial(m + 1, 0))
              / ((m + 1) :: real))
END sum_of_kth_powers_077

title: 078_the_cauchy-schwarz_inequality
content:
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Zhouhang Zhou, Sébastien Gouëzel, Frédéric Dupuis
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Field
public import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic
public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Defs
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.SesquilinearForm.Basic

/-!
# Properties of inner product spaces

This file proves many basic properties of inner product spaces (real or complex).

## Main results

- `inner_mul_inner_self_le`: the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (one of many variants).
- `norm_inner_eq_norm_iff`: the equality criterion in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (also in many
  variants).
- `inner_eq_sum_norm_sq_div_four`: the polarization identity.

## Tags

inner product space, Hilbert space, norm

-/

@[expose] public section


noncomputable section

open RCLike Real Filter Topology ComplexConjugate Finsupp

open LinearMap (BilinForm)

variable {𝕜 E F : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]

section BasicProperties_Seminormed

open scoped InnerProductSpace

variable [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
variable [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]

local notation "⟪" x ", " y "⟫" => inner 𝕜 x y

local postfix:90 "†" => starRingEnd _

export InnerProductSpace (norm_sq_eq_re_inner)

@[simp]
theorem inner_conj_symm (x y : E) : ⟪y, x⟫† = ⟪x, y⟫ :=
  InnerProductSpace.conj_inner_symm _ _

theorem real_inner_comm (x y : F) : ⟪y, x⟫_ℝ = ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ :=
  @inner_conj_symm ℝ _ _ _ _ x y

theorem inner_eq_zero_symm {x y : E} : ⟪x, y⟫ = 0 ↔ ⟪y, x⟫ = 0 := by sorry
instance {ι : Sort*} (v : ι → E) : Std.Symm fun i j => ⟪v i, v j⟫ = 0 where
  symm _ _ := inner_eq_zero_symm.1

theorem inner_self_im (x : E) : im ⟪x, x⟫ = 0 := by sorry
theorem inner_add_left (x y z : E) : ⟪x + y, z⟫ = ⟪x, z⟫ + ⟪y, z⟫ :=
  InnerProductSpace.add_left _ _ _

theorem inner_add_right (x y z : E) : ⟪x, y + z⟫ = ⟪x, y⟫ + ⟪x, z⟫ := by sorry
theorem inner_re_symm (x y : E) : re ⟪x, y⟫ = re ⟪y, x⟫ := by rw [← inner_conj_symm, conj_re]

theorem inner_im_symm (x y : E) : im ⟪x, y⟫ = -im ⟪y, x⟫ := by rw [← inner_conj_symm, conj_im]

section Algebra
variable {𝕝 : Type*} [CommSemiring 𝕝] [StarRing 𝕝] [Algebra 𝕝 𝕜] [Module 𝕝 E]
  [IsScalarTower 𝕝 𝕜 E] [StarModule 𝕝 𝕜]

/-- See `inner_smul_left` for the common special when `𝕜 = 𝕝`. -/
lemma inner_smul_left_eq_star_smul (x y : E) (r : 𝕝) : ⟪r • x, y⟫ = r† • ⟪x, y⟫ := by sorry
lemma inner_smul_left_eq_smul [TrivialStar 𝕝] (x y : E) (r : 𝕝) : ⟪r • x, y⟫ = r • ⟪x, y⟫ := by sorry
lemma inner_smul_right_eq_smul (x y : E) (r : 𝕝) : ⟪x, r • y⟫ = r • ⟪x, y⟫ := by sorry
end Algebra

/-- See `inner_smul_left_eq_star_smul` for the case of a general algebra action. -/
theorem inner_smul_left (x y : E) (r : 𝕜) : ⟪r • x, y⟫ = r† * ⟪x, y⟫ :=
  inner_smul_left_eq_star_smul ..

theorem real_inner_smul_left (x y : F) (r : ℝ) : ⟪r • x, y⟫_ℝ = r * ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ :=
  inner_smul_left _ _ _

theorem inner_smul_real_left (x y : E) (r : ℝ) : ⟪(r : 𝕜) • x, y⟫ = r • ⟪x, y⟫ := by sorry
theorem inner_smul_right (x y : E) (r : 𝕜) : ⟪x, r • y⟫ = r * ⟪x, y⟫ :=
  inner_smul_right_eq_smul ..

theorem real_inner_smul_right (x y : F) (r : ℝ) : ⟪x, r • y⟫_ℝ = r * ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ :=
  inner_smul_right _ _ _

theorem inner_smul_real_right (x y : E) (r : ℝ) : ⟪x, (r : 𝕜) • y⟫ = r • ⟪x, y⟫ := by sorry
variable (𝕜)

/-- The inner product as a sesquilinear map.

Note that in the case `𝕜 = ℝ` this is a bilinear form. -/
def innerₛₗ : E →ₗ⋆[𝕜] E →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜 :=
  LinearMap.mk₂'ₛₗ _ _ (fun v w => ⟪v, w⟫) inner_add_left (fun _ _ _ => inner_smul_left _ _ _)
    inner_add_right fun _ _ _ => inner_smul_right _ _ _

@[simp]
theorem coe_innerₛₗ_apply (v : E) : ⇑(innerₛₗ 𝕜 v) = fun w => ⟪v, w⟫ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem innerₛₗ_apply_apply (v w : E) : innerₛₗ 𝕜 v w = ⟪v, w⟫ :=
  rfl

variable (F)
/-- The inner product as a bilinear map in the real case. -/
def innerₗ : F →ₗ[ℝ] F →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ := innerₛₗ ℝ

@[simp] lemma flip_innerₗ : (innerₗ F).flip = innerₗ F := by sorry
variable {F}

@[simp] lemma innerₗ_apply_apply (v w : F) : innerₗ F v w = ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ := rfl

variable {𝕜}

@[deprecated (since := "2025-12-26")] alias sesqFormOfInner := innerₛₗ
@[deprecated (since := "2025-12-26")] noncomputable alias bilinFormOfRealInner := innerₗ

/-- An inner product with a sum on the left. -/
theorem sum_inner {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → E) (x : E) :
    ⟪∑ i ∈ s, f i, x⟫ = ∑ i ∈ s, ⟪f i, x⟫ :=
  map_sum ((innerₛₗ 𝕜).flip x) _ _

/-- An inner product with a sum on the right. -/
theorem inner_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → E) (x : E) :
    ⟪x, ∑ i ∈ s, f i⟫ = ∑ i ∈ s, ⟪x, f i⟫ :=
  map_sum (innerₛₗ 𝕜 x) _ _

/-- An inner product with a sum on the left, `Finsupp` version. -/
protected theorem Finsupp.sum_inner {ι : Type*} {M : Type*} [Zero M] (l : ι →₀ M)
    (v : ι → M → E) (x : E) : ⟪l.sum v, x⟫ = l.sum fun (i : ι) (a : M) ↦ ⟪v i a, x⟫ := by sorry
theorem inner_zero_left (x : E) : ⟪0, x⟫ = 0 := by sorry
theorem inner_re_zero_left (x : E) : re ⟪0, x⟫ = 0 := by sorry
theorem inner_zero_right (x : E) : ⟪x, 0⟫ = 0 := by sorry
theorem inner_re_zero_right (x : E) : re ⟪x, 0⟫ = 0 := by sorry
theorem inner_self_nonneg {x : E} : 0 ≤ re ⟪x, x⟫ :=
  PreInnerProductSpace.toCore.re_inner_nonneg x

theorem real_inner_self_nonneg {x : F} : 0 ≤ ⟪x, x⟫_ℝ :=
  @inner_self_nonneg ℝ F _ _ _ x

theorem inner_self_ofReal_re (x : E) : (re ⟪x, x⟫ : 𝕜) = ⟪x, x⟫ :=
  ((RCLike.is_real_TFAE (⟪x, x⟫ : 𝕜)).out 2 3).2 (inner_self_im (𝕜 := 𝕜) x)

@[simp]
theorem inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K (x : E) : ⟪x, x⟫ = (‖x‖ : 𝕜) ^ 2 := by sorry
theorem inner_self_re_eq_norm (x : E) : re ⟪x, x⟫ = ‖⟪x, x⟫‖ := by sorry
theorem inner_self_ofReal_norm (x : E) : (‖⟪x, x⟫‖ : 𝕜) = ⟪x, x⟫ := by sorry
theorem real_inner_self_abs (x : F) : |⟪x, x⟫_ℝ| = ⟪x, x⟫_ℝ :=
  @inner_self_ofReal_norm ℝ F _ _ _ x

theorem norm_inner_symm (x y : E) : ‖⟪x, y⟫‖ = ‖⟪y, x⟫‖ := by rw [← inner_conj_symm, norm_conj]

@[simp]
theorem inner_neg_left (x y : E) : ⟪-x, y⟫ = -⟪x, y⟫ := by sorry
theorem inner_neg_right (x y : E) : ⟪x, -y⟫ = -⟪x, y⟫ := by sorry
theorem inner_neg_neg (x y : E) : ⟪-x, -y⟫ = ⟪x, y⟫ := by simp

theorem inner_self_conj (x : E) : ⟪x, x⟫† = ⟪x, x⟫ := inner_conj_symm _ _

theorem inner_sub_left (x y z : E) : ⟪x - y, z⟫ = ⟪x, z⟫ - ⟪y, z⟫ := by sorry
theorem inner_sub_right (x y z : E) : ⟪x, y - z⟫ = ⟪x, y⟫ - ⟪x, z⟫ := by sorry
theorem inner_mul_symm_re_eq_norm (x y : E) : re (⟪x, y⟫ * ⟪y, x⟫) = ‖⟪x, y⟫ * ⟪y, x⟫‖ := by sorry
theorem inner_add_add_self (x y : E) : ⟪x + y, x + y⟫ = ⟪x, x⟫ + ⟪x, y⟫ + ⟪y, x⟫ + ⟪y, y⟫ := by sorry
theorem real_inner_add_add_self (x y : F) :
    ⟪x + y, x + y⟫_ℝ = ⟪x, x⟫_ℝ + 2 * ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ + ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ := by sorry
theorem inner_sub_sub_self (x y : E) : ⟪x - y, x - y⟫ = ⟪x, x⟫ - ⟪x, y⟫ - ⟪y, x⟫ + ⟪y, y⟫ := by sorry
theorem real_inner_sub_sub_self (x y : F) :
    ⟪x - y, x - y⟫_ℝ = ⟪x, x⟫_ℝ - 2 * ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ + ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ := by sorry
theorem parallelogram_law {x y : E} : ⟪x + y, x + y⟫ + ⟪x - y, x - y⟫ = 2 * (⟪x, x⟫ + ⟪y, y⟫) := by sorry
theorem inner_mul_inner_self_le (x y : E) : ‖⟪x, y⟫‖ * ‖⟪y, x⟫‖ ≤ re ⟪x, x⟫ * re ⟪y, y⟫ :=
  letI : PreInnerProductSpace.Core 𝕜 E := PreInnerProductSpace.toCore
  InnerProductSpace.Core.inner_mul_inner_self_le x y

/-- Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for real inner products. -/
theorem real_inner_mul_inner_self_le (x y : F) : ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ * ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ ≤ ⟪x, x⟫_ℝ * ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ :=
  calc
    ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ * ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ ≤ ‖⟪x, y⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖⟪y, x⟫_ℝ‖ := by sorry
theorem inner_eq_ofReal_norm_sq_left_iff {v w : E} : ⟪v, w⟫_𝕜 = ‖v‖ ^ 2 ↔ ⟪v, v - w⟫_𝕜 = 0 := by sorry
theorem inner_eq_norm_sq_left_iff {v w : F} : ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ = ‖v‖ ^ 2 ↔ ⟪v, v - w⟫_ℝ = 0 :=
  inner_eq_ofReal_norm_sq_left_iff

theorem inner_eq_ofReal_norm_sq_right_iff {v w : E} : ⟪v, w⟫_𝕜 = ‖w‖ ^ 2 ↔ ⟪v - w, w⟫_𝕜 = 0 := by sorry
theorem inner_eq_norm_sq_right_iff {v w : F} : ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ = ‖w‖ ^ 2 ↔ ⟪v - w, w⟫_ℝ = 0 :=
  inner_eq_ofReal_norm_sq_right_iff

end BasicProperties_Seminormed

section BasicProperties

variable [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]

local notation "⟪" x ", " y "⟫" => inner 𝕜 x y

export InnerProductSpace (norm_sq_eq_re_inner)

theorem inner_self_eq_zero {x : E} : ⟪x, x⟫ = 0 ↔ x = 0 := by sorry
theorem inner_self_ne_zero {x : E} : ⟪x, x⟫ ≠ 0 ↔ x ≠ 0 :=
  inner_self_eq_zero.not

variable (𝕜)

theorem ext_inner_left {x y : E} (h : ∀ v, ⟪v, x⟫ = ⟪v, y⟫) : x = y := by sorry
theorem ext_iff_inner_left {x y : E} : x = y ↔ ∀ v, ⟪v, x⟫ = ⟪v, y⟫ :=
  ⟨fun h _ ↦ h ▸ rfl, ext_inner_left 𝕜⟩

theorem ext_inner_right {x y : E} (h : ∀ v, ⟪x, v⟫ = ⟪y, v⟫) : x = y := by sorry
theorem ext_iff_inner_right {x y : E} : x = y ↔ ∀ v, ⟪x, v⟫ = ⟪y, v⟫ :=

theorem dist_div_norm_sq_smul {x y : F} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hy : y ≠ 0) (R : ℝ) :
    dist ((R / ‖x‖) ^ 2 • x) ((R / ‖y‖) ^ 2 • y) = R ^ 2 / (‖x‖ * ‖y‖) * dist x y :=
  calc
    dist ((R / ‖x‖) ^ 2 • x) ((R / ‖y‖) ^ 2 • y) =
        √(‖(R / ‖x‖) ^ 2 • x - (R / ‖y‖) ^ 2 • y‖ ^ 2) := by sorry

  norm_inner_div_norm_mul_norm_eq_one_of_ne_zero_of_ne_zero_mul hx hr

    List.TFAE [‖⟪x, y⟫‖ = ‖x‖ * ‖y‖,
      x = 0 ∨ y = (⟪x, y⟫ / ⟪x, x⟫) • x,
      x = 0 ∨ ∃ r : 𝕜, y = r • x,
      x = 0 ∨ y ∈ 𝕜 ∙ x] := by sorry

    ‖⟪x, y⟫‖ = ‖x‖ * ‖y‖ ↔ ∃ r : 𝕜, r ≠ 0 ∧ y = r • x :=
  calc
    ‖⟪x, y⟫‖ = ‖x‖ * ‖y‖ ↔ x = 0 ∨ ∃ r : 𝕜, y = r • x :=
      (norm_inner_eq_norm_tfae 𝕜 x y).out 0 2
    _ ↔ ∃ r : 𝕜, y = r • x := or_iff_right hx₀
    _ ↔ ∃ r : 𝕜, r ≠ 0 ∧ y = r • x :=

local notation "⟪" x ", " y "⟫" => inner 𝕜 x y

/-- A field `𝕜` satisfying `RCLike` is itself a `𝕜`-inner product space. -/
instance RCLike.innerProductSpace : InnerProductSpace 𝕜 𝕜 where
  inner x y := y * conj x
  norm_sq_eq_re_inner x := by simp only [mul_conj, ← ofReal_pow, ofReal_re]
  conj_inner_symm x y := by simp only [mul_comm, map_mul, starRingEnd_self_apply]
  add_left x y z := by simp only [mul_add, map_add]
  smul_left x y z := by simp only [mul_comm (conj z), mul_assoc, smul_eq_mul, map_mul]

@[simp]
theorem RCLike.inner_apply (x y : 𝕜) : ⟪x, y⟫ = y * conj x :=
  rfl

/-- A version of `RCLike.inner_apply` that swaps the order of multiplication. -/
theorem RCLike.inner_apply' (x y : 𝕜) : ⟪x, y⟫ = conj x * y := mul_comm _ _
