        radical(d$1) /\ radical(d$2) /\
        radical(e$1) /\ radical(e$2) /\
        radical(f$1) /\ radical(f$2) /\
        length(a,x) = length(b,c) /\
        length(d,x) = length(e,f) /\
        ~(a = d /\ length(b,c) = length(e,f))
        ==> radical(x$1) /\ radical(x$2)`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* So constructible points have radical coordinates.                         *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let CONSTRUCTIBLE_RADICAL = `!x. constructible x ==> radical(x$1) /\ radical(x$2)`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Impossibility of doubling the cube.                                       *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let DOUBLE_THE_CUBE_ALGEBRA = `~(?x. radical x /\ x pow 3 = &2)`;;

let DOUBLE_THE_CUBE = `!x. x pow 3 = &2 ==> ~(constructible(vector[x; &0]))`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Impossibility of trisecting                                               *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let COS_TRIPLE = `!x. cos(&3 * x) = &4 * cos(x) pow 3 - &3 * cos(x)`;;

let COS_PI3 = `cos(pi / &3) = &1 / &2`;;

let TRISECT_60_DEGREES_ALGEBRA = `~(?x. radical x /\ x pow 3 - &3 * x - &1 = &0)`;;

let TRISECT_60_DEGREES = `!y. ~(constructible(vector[cos(pi / &9); y]))`;;

title: 008_the_impossibility_of_trisecting_the_angle_and_doubling_the_c
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 008,
;; "The Impossibility of Trisecting the Angle and Doubling the Cube."
;; Constructible points are exactly those admitting a finite derivation from
;; rational points by the three straightedge-and-compass intersection rules.
;; No cube root of two, nor a point whose first coordinate is cos(pi/9), has
;; such a derivation. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The scalar operations describe an arbitrary real-closed ordered field.
;; This gives the full algebraic real geometry needed by the source without
;; restricting coordinates to ACL2's built-in rationals.

(defstub ht008-carrier (x) t)
(defstub ht008-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht008-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht008-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub ht008-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub ht008-less-op (x y) t)

(defun ht008-member-p (x)
  (if (ht008-carrier x) t nil))

(defun ht008-add (x y)
  (ht008-add-op x y))

(defun ht008-multiply (x y)
  (ht008-multiply-op x y))

(defun ht008-negate (x)
  (ht008-negate-op x))

(defun ht008-inverse (x)
  (ht008-inverse-op x))

(defun ht008-subtract (x y)
  (ht008-add x (ht008-negate y)))

(defun ht008-less (x y)
  (if (ht008-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun ht008-square (x)
  (ht008-multiply x x))

(defun ht008-cube (x)
  (ht008-multiply x (ht008-square x)))

(defun-sk ht008-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht008-member-p x)
      (ht008-member-p y)
      (ht008-member-p z))
     (and
      (ht008-member-p (ht008-add x y))
      (ht008-member-p (ht008-multiply x y))
      (ht008-member-p (ht008-negate x))
      (ht008-member-p (ht008-inverse x))
      (equal (ht008-add (ht008-add x y) z)
             (ht008-add x (ht008-add y z)))
      (equal (ht008-add x y)
             (ht008-add y x))
      (equal (ht008-add x zero) x)
      (equal (ht008-add x (ht008-negate x)) zero)
      (equal (ht008-multiply (ht008-multiply x y) z)
             (ht008-multiply x (ht008-multiply y z)))
      (equal (ht008-multiply x y)
             (ht008-multiply y x))
      (equal (ht008-multiply x one) x)
      (equal
       (ht008-multiply x (ht008-add y z))
       (ht008-add
        (ht008-multiply x y)
        (ht008-multiply x z)))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (ht008-multiply x (ht008-inverse x))
        one))))))

(defun-sk ht008-order-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht008-member-p x)
      (ht008-member-p y)
      (ht008-member-p z))
     (and
      (not (ht008-less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (ht008-less x y)
       (ht008-less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht008-less x y)
        (ht008-less y z))
       (ht008-less x z))
      (implies
       (ht008-less x y)
       (ht008-less
        (ht008-add x z)
        (ht008-add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (ht008-less zero x)
        (ht008-less zero y))
       (ht008-less zero (ht008-multiply x y)))))))

(defun ht008-carrier-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (ht008-member-p (car values))
       (ht008-carrier-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun ht008-polynomial-value (coefficients x zero)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (ht008-add
       (car coefficients)
       (ht008-multiply
        x
        (ht008-polynomial-value
         (cdr coefficients) x zero)))
    zero))

(defun ht008-odd-degree-polynomial-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (and
   (consp coefficients)
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (ht008-carrier-list-p coefficients)
   (evenp (len coefficients))
   (not (equal (car (last coefficients)) zero))))

(defun-sk ht008-has-square-root-p (x)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (ht008-member-p root)
     (equal (ht008-square root) x))))

(defun-sk ht008-polynomial-has-root-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (ht008-member-p root)
     (equal
      (ht008-polynomial-value coefficients root zero)
      zero))))

(defun-sk ht008-real-closure-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x coefficients)
    (and
     (implies
      (and
       (ht008-member-p x)
       (not (ht008-less x zero)))
      (ht008-has-square-root-p x))
     (implies
      (ht008-odd-degree-polynomial-p coefficients zero)
      (ht008-polynomial-has-root-p coefficients zero)))))

(defun ht008-real-scalar-context-p (zero one)
  (and
   (ht008-member-p zero)
   (ht008-member-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (ht008-less zero one)
   (ht008-field-laws-p zero one)
   (ht008-order-laws-p zero)
   (ht008-real-closure-laws-p zero)))

(defun ht008-natural-value (n zero one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (ht008-add
     one
     (ht008-natural-value (- n 1) zero one))))

(defun ht008-integer-value (integer zero one)
  (if (< integer 0)
      (ht008-negate
       (ht008-natural-value (- integer) zero one))
    (ht008-natural-value integer zero one)))

(defun-sk ht008-rational-element-p (x zero one)
  (exists (numerator denominator)
    (and
     (integerp numerator)
     (posp denominator)
     (equal
      (ht008-multiply
       x
       (ht008-integer-value denominator zero one))
      (ht008-integer-value numerator zero one)))))

;; Planar points and the exact incidence/radius relations from the sources.

(defun ht008-point-p (point)
  (and
   (consp point)
   (ht008-member-p (car point))
   (ht008-member-p (cdr point))))

(defun ht008-rational-point-p (point zero one)
  (and
   (ht008-point-p point)
   (ht008-rational-element-p (car point) zero one)
   (ht008-rational-element-p (cdr point) zero one)))

(defun ht008-point-equal-p (left right)
  (and
   (equal (car left) (car right))
   (equal (cdr left) (cdr right))))

(defun ht008-parallel-p (point-a point-b point-c point-d)
  (equal
   (ht008-multiply
    (ht008-subtract (car point-a) (car point-b))
    (ht008-subtract (cdr point-c) (cdr point-d)))
   (ht008-multiply
    (ht008-subtract (cdr point-a) (cdr point-b))
    (ht008-subtract (car point-c) (car point-d)))))

(defun ht008-collinear-p (point-a point-m point-b)
  (ht008-parallel-p point-a point-m point-a point-b))

(defun ht008-squared-distance (left right)
  (let ((dx (ht008-subtract (car left) (car right)))
        (dy (ht008-subtract (cdr left) (cdr right))))
    (ht008-add
     (ht008-square dx)
     (ht008-square dy))))

(defun ht008-same-distance-p
    (point-a point-b point-c point-d)
  (equal
   (ht008-squared-distance point-a point-b)
   (ht008-squared-distance point-c point-d)))

;; A construction is a finite sequence of steps. References in a step must
;; be equal to earlier complete steps, so cycles and forward references are
;; impossible. The second field of every step is its output point.

(defun ht008-step-output (step)
  (cadr step))

(defun ht008-prior-step-p (step prior-steps)
  (if (member-equal step prior-steps) t nil))

(defun ht008-valid-rational-step-p
    (step zero one)
  (and
   (true-listp step)
   (equal (len step) 2)
   (eq (car step) :rational-point)
   (ht008-rational-point-p
    (ht008-step-output step) zero one)))

(defun ht008-valid-line-line-step-p
    (step prior-steps)
  (let* ((point-m (nth 1 step))
         (step-a (nth 2 step))
         (step-b (nth 3 step))
         (step-c (nth 4 step))
         (step-d (nth 5 step))
         (point-a (ht008-step-output step-a))
         (point-b (ht008-step-output step-b))
         (point-c (ht008-step-output step-c))
         (point-d (ht008-step-output step-d)))
    (and
     (true-listp step)
     (equal (len step) 6)
     (eq (car step) :line-line)
     (ht008-point-p point-m)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-a prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-b prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-c prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-d prior-steps)
     (not (ht008-parallel-p
           point-a point-b point-c point-d))
     (ht008-collinear-p point-a point-m point-b)
     (ht008-collinear-p point-c point-m point-d))))

(defun ht008-valid-line-circle-step-p
    (step prior-steps)
  (let* ((point-m (nth 1 step))
         (step-a (nth 2 step))
         (step-b (nth 3 step))
         (step-c (nth 4 step))
         (step-d (nth 5 step))
         (step-e (nth 6 step))
         (point-a (ht008-step-output step-a))
         (point-b (ht008-step-output step-b))
         (point-c (ht008-step-output step-c))
         (point-d (ht008-step-output step-d))
         (point-e (ht008-step-output step-e)))
    (and
     (true-listp step)
     (equal (len step) 7)
     (eq (car step) :line-circle)
     (ht008-point-p point-m)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-a prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-b prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-c prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-d prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-e prior-steps)
     (not (ht008-point-equal-p point-a point-b))
     (ht008-collinear-p point-a point-m point-b)
     (ht008-same-distance-p
      point-c point-m point-d point-e))))

(defun ht008-valid-circle-circle-step-p
    (step prior-steps)
  (let* ((point-m (nth 1 step))
         (step-a (nth 2 step))
         (step-b (nth 3 step))
         (step-c (nth 4 step))
         (step-d (nth 5 step))
         (step-e (nth 6 step))
         (step-f (nth 7 step))
         (point-a (ht008-step-output step-a))
         (point-b (ht008-step-output step-b))
         (point-c (ht008-step-output step-c))
         (point-d (ht008-step-output step-d))
         (point-e (ht008-step-output step-e))
         (point-f (ht008-step-output step-f)))
    (and
     (true-listp step)
     (equal (len step) 8)
     (eq (car step) :circle-circle)
     (ht008-point-p point-m)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-a prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-b prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-c prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-d prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-e prior-steps)
     (ht008-prior-step-p step-f prior-steps)
     (not
      (and
       (ht008-point-equal-p point-a point-d)
       (ht008-same-distance-p
        point-b point-c point-e point-f)))
     (ht008-same-distance-p
      point-a point-m point-b point-c)
     (ht008-same-distance-p
      point-d point-m point-e point-f))))

(defun ht008-valid-step-p
    (step prior-steps zero one)
  (cond
   ((and (consp step)
         (eq (car step) :rational-point))
    (ht008-valid-rational-step-p step zero one))
   ((and (consp step)
         (eq (car step) :line-line))
    (ht008-valid-line-line-step-p step prior-steps))
   ((and (consp step)
         (eq (car step) :line-circle))
    (ht008-valid-line-circle-step-p step prior-steps))
   ((and (consp step)
         (eq (car step) :circle-circle))
    (ht008-valid-circle-circle-step-p step prior-steps))
   (t nil)))

(defun ht008-valid-construction-sequence-p
    (steps prior-steps zero one)
  (if (consp steps)
      (and
       (ht008-valid-step-p
        (car steps) prior-steps zero one)
       (ht008-valid-construction-sequence-p
        (cdr steps)
        (cons (car steps) prior-steps)
        zero one))
    (equal steps nil)))

(defun-sk ht008-constructible-point-p
    (point zero one)
  (exists (steps)
    (and
     (consp steps)
     (true-listp steps)
     (ht008-valid-construction-sequence-p
      steps nil zero one)
     (ht008-point-equal-p
      point
      (ht008-step-output (car (last steps)))))))

(defun ht008-cos-pi-over-nine-p
    (value zero one)
  (let* ((six (ht008-natural-value 6 zero one))
         (eight (ht008-natural-value 8 zero one))
         (polynomial-value
          (ht008-subtract
           (ht008-subtract
            (ht008-multiply eight (ht008-cube value))
            (ht008-multiply six value))
           one)))
    (and
     (ht008-member-p value)
     (ht008-less zero value)
     (equal polynomial-value zero))))

(defun-sk ht008-doubling-the-cube-impossible-p
    (zero one)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht008-member-p x)
      (equal
       (ht008-cube x)
       (ht008-natural-value 2 zero one)))
     (not
      (ht008-constructible-point-p
       (cons x zero) zero one)))))

(defun-sk ht008-trisecting-sixty-degrees-impossible-p
    (zero one)
  (forall (cosine-value ordinate)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht008-cos-pi-over-nine-p
       cosine-value zero one)
      (ht008-member-p ordinate))
     (not
      (ht008-constructible-point-p
       (cons cosine-value ordinate) zero one)))))

(defun hundred-theorems-008-impossibility-statement
    (zero one)
  (implies
   (ht008-real-scalar-context-p zero one)
   (and
    (ht008-doubling-the-cube-impossible-p zero one)
    (ht008-trisecting-sixty-degrees-impossible-p
     zero one))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 008_the_impossibility_of_trisecting_the_angle_and_doubling_the_c
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "The Impossibility of Trisecting the Angle and Doubling the
-- Cube" from Hundred Theorems item 008: straightedge-and-compass constructions cannot double
-- the cube or trisect a 60-degree angle. This file contains no proof.

module HundredTheorems008 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ; _,_)

infixr 4 _∧_
infix 3 ¬_

data ⊥ : Set where

data _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  conjunction : A → B → A ∧ B

¬_ : Set → Set
¬ A = A → ⊥

Exists : (A : Set) → (A → Set) → Set
Exists A P = Σ A P

data NatLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero-less-or-equal : {n : Nat} → NatLessOrEqual zero n
  suc-less-or-equal :
    {m n : Nat} →
    NatLessOrEqual m n →
    NatLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n)

natPred : Nat → Nat
natPred zero = zero
natPred (suc n) = n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract n zero = n
natSubtract zero (suc m) = zero
natSubtract (suc n) (suc m) = natSubtract n m

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

intNegate : Int → Int
intNegate (pos n) = negative n
intNegate (negsuc n) = pos (suc n)

intDifference : Nat → Nat → Int
intDifference zero zero = pos zero
intDifference (suc m) zero = pos (suc m)
intDifference zero (suc n) = negsuc n
intDifference (suc m) (suc n) = intDifference m n

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd (pos m) (pos n) = pos (m + n)
intAdd (pos m) (negsuc n) = intDifference m (suc n)
intAdd (negsuc m) (pos n) = intDifference n (suc m)
intAdd (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc (m + n))

intSubtract : Int → Int → Int
intSubtract a b = intAdd a (intNegate b)

intMultiply : Int → Int → Int
intMultiply (pos m) (pos n) = pos (m * n)
intMultiply (pos m) (negsuc n) = negative (m * suc n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (pos n) = negative (suc m * n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = pos (suc m * suc n)

scaleInt : Int → Nat → Int
scaleInt z n = intMultiply z (pos n)

intAbs : Int → Nat
intAbs (pos n) = n
intAbs (negsuc n) = suc n

record Rational : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator : Int
    denominator-minus-one : Nat

open Rational

denominator : Rational → Nat
denominator q = suc (denominator-minus-one q)

ratZero : Rational
ratZero = fraction (pos zero) zero

ratOne : Rational
ratOne = fraction (pos (suc zero)) zero

ratTwo : Rational
ratTwo = fraction (pos (suc (suc zero))) zero

ratFour : Rational
ratFour = fraction (pos (suc (suc (suc (suc zero))))) zero

rationalFromNat : Nat → Rational
rationalFromNat n = fraction (pos n) zero

ratNegate : Rational → Rational
ratNegate q =
  fraction
    (intNegate (numerator q))
    (denominator-minus-one q)

ratAdd : Rational → Rational → Rational
ratAdd p q =
  fraction
    (intAdd
      (intMultiply (numerator p) (pos (denominator q)))
      (intMultiply (numerator q) (pos (denominator p))))
    (natPred (denominator p * denominator q))

ratSubtract : Rational → Rational → Rational
ratSubtract p q = ratAdd p (ratNegate q)

ratMultiply : Rational → Rational → Rational
ratMultiply p q =
  fraction
    (intMultiply (numerator p) (numerator q))
    (natPred (denominator p * denominator q))

ratPower : Rational → Nat → Rational
ratPower q zero = ratOne
ratPower q (suc n) = ratMultiply q (ratPower q n)

data IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set where
  positive-less-or-equal-positive :
    {m n : Nat} →
    NatLessOrEqual m n →
    IntLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n)
  negative-less-or-equal-positive :
    {m n : Nat} →
    IntLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (pos n)
  negative-less-or-equal-negative :
    {m n : Nat} →
    NatLessOrEqual n m →
    IntLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n)

ratLessOrEqual : Rational → Rational → Set
ratLessOrEqual p q =
  IntLessOrEqual
    (scaleInt (numerator p) (denominator q))
    (scaleInt (numerator q) (denominator p))

ratAbsolute : Rational → Rational
ratAbsolute q =
  fraction
    (pos (intAbs (numerator q)))
    (denominator-minus-one q)

ratAbsDifference : Rational → Rational → Rational
ratAbsDifference p q = ratAbsolute (ratSubtract p q)

unitFraction : Nat → Rational
unitFraction precision = fraction (pos (suc zero)) precision

Sequence : Set
Sequence = Nat → Rational

Cauchy : Sequence → Set
Cauchy sequence =
  (precision : Nat) →
  Exists Nat
    (λ threshold →
      (m n : Nat) →
      NatLessOrEqual threshold m →
      NatLessOrEqual threshold n →
      ratLessOrEqual
        (ratAbsDifference (sequence m) (sequence n))
        (unitFraction precision))

SequenceEquivalent : Sequence → Sequence → Set
SequenceEquivalent left right =
  (precision : Nat) →
  Exists Nat
    (λ threshold →
      (n : Nat) →
      NatLessOrEqual threshold n →
      ratLessOrEqual
        (ratAbsDifference (left n) (right n))
        (unitFraction precision))

Real : Set
Real = Sequence

constantSequence : Rational → Real
constantSequence q n = q

realNegate : Real → Real
realNegate x n = ratNegate (x n)

realAdd : Real → Real → Real
realAdd x y n = ratAdd (x n) (y n)

realSubtract : Real → Real → Real
realSubtract x y n = ratSubtract (x n) (y n)

realMultiply : Real → Real → Real
realMultiply x y n = ratMultiply (x n) (y n)

realSquare : Real → Real
realSquare x = realMultiply x x

realCube : Real → Real
realCube x = realMultiply (realSquare x) x

realScaleNat : Nat → Real → Real
realScaleNat coefficient x n =
  ratMultiply (rationalFromNat coefficient) (x n)

RealEquivalent : Real → Real → Set
RealEquivalent = SequenceEquivalent

RationalReal : Real → Set
RationalReal x =
  Exists Rational
    (λ q → RealEquivalent x (constantSequence q))

record Point : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : Real
    y-coordinate : Real

open Point

ValidPoint : Point → Set
ValidPoint p = Cauchy (x-coordinate p) ∧ Cauchy (y-coordinate p)

PointEquivalent : Point → Point → Set
PointEquivalent p q =
  RealEquivalent (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q) ∧
  RealEquivalent (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)

Parallel : Point → Point → Point → Point → Set
Parallel a b c d =
  RealEquivalent
    (realMultiply
      (realSubtract (x-coordinate a) (x-coordinate b))
      (realSubtract (y-coordinate c) (y-coordinate d)))
    (realMultiply
      (realSubtract (y-coordinate a) (y-coordinate b))
      (realSubtract (x-coordinate c) (x-coordinate d)))

Collinear : Point → Point → Point → Set
Collinear a b c =
  RealEquivalent
    (realMultiply
      (realSubtract (x-coordinate a) (x-coordinate b))
      (realSubtract (y-coordinate b) (y-coordinate c)))
    (realMultiply
      (realSubtract (y-coordinate a) (y-coordinate b))
      (realSubtract (x-coordinate b) (x-coordinate c)))

SquaredDistance : Point → Point → Real
SquaredDistance p q =
  realAdd
    (realSquare
      (realSubtract (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (realSquare
      (realSubtract (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

EqualSquaredDistance : Point → Point → Point → Point → Set
EqualSquaredDistance a b c d =
  RealEquivalent (SquaredDistance a b) (SquaredDistance c d)

IsIntersection :
  Point →
  Point →
  Point →
  Point →
  Point →
  Set
IsIntersection a b c d m =
  Collinear a b m ∧ Collinear c d m

data Constructible : Point → Set where
  rational-point :
    {p : Point} →
    ValidPoint p →
    RationalReal (x-coordinate p) →
    RationalReal (y-coordinate p) →
    Constructible p

  line-line-intersection :
    {a b c d m : Point} →
    Constructible a →
    Constructible b →
    Constructible c →
    Constructible d →
    ¬ Parallel a b c d →
    IsIntersection a b c d m →
    ValidPoint m →
    Constructible m

  line-circle-intersection :
    {a b c d e m : Point} →
    Constructible a →
    Constructible b →
    Constructible c →
    Constructible d →
    Constructible e →
    ¬ PointEquivalent a b →
    Collinear a b m →
    EqualSquaredDistance c m d e →
    ValidPoint m →
    Constructible m

  circle-circle-intersection :
    {a b c d e f m : Point} →
    Constructible a →
    Constructible b →
    Constructible c →
    Constructible d →
    Constructible e →
    Constructible f →
    ¬ (PointEquivalent a d ∧ EqualSquaredDistance b c e f) →
    EqualSquaredDistance a m b c →
    EqualSquaredDistance d m e f →
    ValidPoint m →
    Constructible m

alternatingSign : Nat → Int
alternatingSign zero = pos (suc zero)
alternatingSign (suc n) = intNegate (alternatingSign n)

oddNatural : Nat → Nat
oddNatural n = suc (n + n)

leibnizTerm : Nat → Rational
leibnizTerm n =
  fraction
    (alternatingSign n)
    (natPred (oddNatural n))

leibnizPartialSum : Nat → Rational
leibnizPartialSum zero = leibnizTerm zero
leibnizPartialSum (suc n) =
  ratAdd (leibnizPartialSum n) (leibnizTerm (suc n))

piApproximation : Real
piApproximation n =
  ratMultiply ratFour (leibnizPartialSum n)

Pi : Real → Set
Pi value = RealEquivalent value piApproximation

factorial : Nat → Nat
factorial zero = suc zero
factorial (suc n) = suc n * factorial n

twice : Nat → Nat
twice n = n + n

ratDivideByFactorial : Rational → Nat → Rational
ratDivideByFactorial q n =
  fraction
    (numerator q)
    (natPred (denominator q * factorial n))

cosineSign : Nat → Rational
cosineSign n = fraction (alternatingSign n) zero

cosineTerm : Rational → Nat → Rational
cosineTerm x n =
  ratDivideByFactorial
    (ratMultiply
      (cosineSign n)
      (ratPower x (twice n)))
    (twice n)

cosinePartialSum : Rational → Nat → Rational
cosinePartialSum x zero = cosineTerm x zero
cosinePartialSum x (suc n) =
  ratAdd
    (cosinePartialSum x n)
    (cosineTerm x (suc n))

cosineApproximation : Real → Real
cosineApproximation angle n =
  cosinePartialSum (angle n) n

CosineAt : Real → Real → Set
CosineAt angle value =
  RealEquivalent value (cosineApproximation angle)

NinthOfPi : Real → Real → Set
NinthOfPi angle pi =
  RealEquivalent (realScaleNat (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc zero))))))))) angle) pi

CubeEqualsTwo : Real → Set
CubeEqualsTwo x =
  RealEquivalent (realCube x) (constantSequence ratTwo)

DoublingTheCube : Set
DoublingTheCube =
  (x : Real) →
  Cauchy x →
  CubeEqualsTwo x →
  ¬ Constructible (point x (constantSequence ratZero))

TrisectingSixtyDegrees : Set
TrisectingSixtyDegrees =
  (pi angle cosine-value y : Real) →
  Cauchy pi →
  Pi pi →
  Cauchy angle →
  NinthOfPi angle pi →
  Cauchy cosine-value →
  CosineAt angle cosine-value →
  Cauchy y →
  ¬ Constructible (point cosine-value y)

hundred-theorems-008 : Set
hundred-theorems-008 =
  DoublingTheCube ∧ TrisectingSixtyDegrees

title: 008_the_impossibility_of_trisecting_the_angle_and_doubling_the_c
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "The Impossibility of Trisecting the Angle and Doubling the
  Cube" from Hundred Theorems item 008. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory realTheory transcTheory;

val impossibility_of_trisecting_the_angle_and_doubling_the_cube =
  ``!(h8_rat : real -> bool)
      (h8_dist : real # real -> real # real -> real)
      (h8_parallel :
         real # real -> real # real ->
         real # real -> real # real -> bool)
      (h8_collinear :
         real # real -> real # real -> real # real -> bool)
      (h8_intersection :
         real # real -> real # real -> real # real ->
         real # real -> real # real -> bool)
      (h8_constructible : real # real -> bool).
      ((!x : real.
          h8_rat x <=>
          ?m n : num.
            ~(n = 0) /\
            (x = (&m : real) / (&n : real) \/
             x = ~((&m : real) / (&n : real)))) /\
       (!P Q : real # real.
          h8_dist P Q =
            sqrt ((FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2)) /\
       (!A B C D : real # real.
          h8_parallel A B C D <=>
            (FST A - FST B) * (SND C - SND D) =
            (SND A - SND B) * (FST C - FST D)) /\
       (!A M B : real # real.
          h8_collinear A M B <=> h8_parallel A M A B) /\
       (!M A B C D : real # real.
          h8_intersection M A B C D <=>
            h8_collinear A M B /\ h8_collinear C M D) /\
       (!M : real # real.
          h8_constructible M <=>
          !(S : real # real -> bool).
            ((!P : real # real.
                h8_rat (FST P) /\ h8_rat (SND P) ==> S P) /\
             (!A B C D P : real # real.
                S A /\ S B /\ S C /\ S D /\
                ~h8_parallel A B C D /\
                h8_intersection P A B C D
                ==> S P) /\
             (!A B C D E P : real # real.
                S A /\ S B /\ S C /\ S D /\ S E /\
                ~(A = B) /\
                h8_collinear A P B /\
                h8_dist C P = h8_dist D E
                ==> S P) /\
             (!A B C D E F P : real # real.
                S A /\ S B /\ S C /\ S D /\ S E /\ S F /\
                ~(A = D /\ h8_dist B C = h8_dist E F) /\
                h8_dist A P = h8_dist B C /\
                h8_dist D P = h8_dist E F
                ==> S P))
            ==> S M))
      ==>
      ((!x : real.
          x pow 3 = 2 ==> ~h8_constructible (x, 0)) /\
       (!y : real.
          ~h8_constructible (cos (pi / 9), y)))``;

title: 008_the_impossibility_of_trisecting_the_angle_and_doubling_the_c
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "The Impossibility of Trisecting the Angle
  and Doubling the Cube" from Hundred Theorems item 008: straightedge-and-
  compass constructibility in the real plane, including the impossibility of
  constructing a real cube root of 2 and of trisecting a 60-degree angle.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  A point with real coordinates (u,v) is represented by the complex number
  u + i*v.  The class HundredConstr008 is defined as the intersection of all
  subsets s of the complex plane that contain every rational-coordinate point
  and are closed under line-line, line-circle, and distinct-circle
  intersections.  Thus the quantifier over s ranges over every plane subset,
  giving exactly the least closure used by the HOL Light and Isabelle
  constructibility definitions.

  Lines are parametrized over RR.  Circle radii are distances between already
  constructible points.  The imaginary-part determinant is nonzero exactly
  when two line directions are nonparallel.  The final declarations are
  unproved $a statements, following the corpus convention for Metamath
  statement artifacts.
$)

$c HundredConstr008 $.

chundredconstr008 $a class HundredConstr008 $.

${
  $d a b c d e f r s t x y z $.

  df-hundredconstr008 $a |- HundredConstr008 = { z e. CC | A. s (
    (
      (
        s C_ CC
        /\
        A. x e. QQ A. y e. QQ
          ( x + ( _i x. y ) ) e. s
      )
      /\
      A. x e. CC
      (
        (
          E. a e. s E. b e. s E. c e. s E. d e. s
          E. t e. RR E. r e. RR
          (
            x = ( a + ( t x. ( b - a ) ) )
            /\
            (
              x = ( c + ( r x. ( d - c ) ) )
              /\
              ( Im ` ( ( * ` ( b - a ) ) x. ( d - c ) ) ) =/= 0
            )
          )
          \/
          E. a e. s E. b e. s E. c e. s E. d e. s E. e e. s
          E. t e. RR
          (
            a =/= b
            /\
            (
              x = ( a + ( t x. ( b - a ) ) )
              /\
              ( abs ` ( x - c ) ) = ( abs ` ( d - e ) )
            )
          )
          \/
          E. a e. s E. b e. s E. c e. s
          E. d e. s E. e e. s E. f e. s
          (
            -.
            (
              a = d
              /\
              ( abs ` ( b - c ) ) = ( abs ` ( e - f ) )
            )
            /\
            (
              ( abs ` ( x - a ) ) = ( abs ` ( b - c ) )
              /\
              ( abs ` ( x - d ) ) = ( abs ` ( e - f ) )
            )
          )
        )
        ->
        x e. s
      )
    )
    ->
    z e. s
  ) } $.
$}

$(
  Under the coordinate identification above, x is the source point (x,0),
  while cos(pi/9) + i*y is the source point (cos(pi/9),y).  The first
  trisection assertion is the Isabelle conclusion; the second is the stronger
  HOL Light conclusion for every real ordinate.
$)

hundred-doubling-cube-008 $a |- A. x e. RR
  ( ( x ^ 3 ) = 2 -> x e/ HundredConstr008 ) $.

hundred-trisect-sixty-axis-008 $a |-
  ( cos ` ( _pi / 9 ) ) e/ HundredConstr008 $.

hundred-trisect-sixty-any-ordinate-008 $a |- A. y e. RR
  ( ( ( cos ` ( _pi / 9 ) ) + ( _i x. y ) ) e/ HundredConstr008 ) $.

title: 008_the_impossibility_of_trisecting_the_angle_and_doubling_the_c
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of "The Impossibility of Trisecting the Angle and Doubling the
:: Cube" from Hundred Theorems item 008. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SETFAM_1, NUMBERS, SUBSET_1,
    INT_1, RAT_1, RELAT_1, ARYTM_1,
    NEWTON, ARYTM_3, CARD_1, PREPOWER, FUNCT_1, XXREAL_0, NAT_1,
    REAL_1, SEQ_1, SEQ_2, ORDINAL2, SQUARE_1, XXREAL_2, SEQ_4,
    COMPLEX1, VALUED_0, POWER, ABIAN, ORDINAL1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SETFAM_1, SUBSET_1, NEWTON,
    ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    COMPLEX1, INT_1, RAT_1, REAL_1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, SEQ_1, SEQ_2,
    COMSEQ_2, SEQM_3, SQUARE_1, SEQ_4, PREPOWER, ABIAN, XXREAL_2,
    POWER;
  constructors REAL_1, SQUARE_1, NAT_1, SEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4, NEWTON,
    PREPOWER, XXREAL_2, RELSET_1, ABIAN, BINOP_2, COMSEQ_2, POWER,
    SETFAM_1;
  registrations XREAL_0, SQUARE_1, NAT_1, INT_1, RAT_1, MEMBERED,
    NEWTON, PREPOWER, SEQ_4, ABIAN, ORDINAL1, POWER;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex R being Subset of REAL,
     C being Subset of [:REAL,REAL:] st
    :: R is the least real set generated by rational numbers under the field
    :: operations and square roots of nonnegative elements.
    R = meet {S where S is Subset of REAL :
      RAT c= S &
      (for x being Real st x in S holds -x in S) &
      (for x being Real st x in S & x <> 0 holds 1/x in S) &
      (for x,y being Real st x in S & y in S holds x+y in S) &
      (for x,y being Real st x in S & y in S holds x*y in S) &
      (for x being Real st x in S & 0 <= x holds sqrt x in S)} &
    :: C is the least set of planar points generated from rational points by
    :: the three straightedge-and-compass intersection rules in the sources.
    C = meet {D where D is Subset of [:REAL,REAL:] :
      (for x,y being Real st x in RAT & y in RAT holds [x,y] in D) &
      :: Intersection of two nonparallel lines AB and CD.
      (for a1,a2,b1,b2,c1,c2,d1,d2,p1,p2 being Real st
        [a1,a2] in D & [b1,b2] in D & [c1,c2] in D & [d1,d2] in D &
        not ((a1-b1)*(c2-d2) = (a2-b2)*(c1-d1)) &
        (a1-p1)*(a2-b2) = (a2-p2)*(a1-b1) &
        (c1-p1)*(c2-d2) = (c2-p2)*(c1-d1)
      holds [p1,p2] in D) &
      :: Intersection of line AB and the circle centered at C through the
      :: point whose distance from D equals the circle radius DE.
      (for a1,a2,b1,b2,c1,c2,d1,d2,e1,e2,p1,p2 being Real st
        [a1,a2] in D & [b1,b2] in D & [c1,c2] in D &
        [d1,d2] in D & [e1,e2] in D &
        not (a1=b1 & a2=b2) &
        (a1-p1)*(a2-b2) = (a2-p2)*(a1-b1) &
        sqrt ((p1-c1)^2 + (p2-c2)^2) =
          sqrt ((e1-d1)^2 + (e2-d2)^2)
      holds [p1,p2] in D) &
      :: Intersection of the circle centered at A with radius BC and the
      :: distinct circle centered at D with radius EF.
      (for a1,a2,b1,b2,c1,c2,d1,d2,e1,e2,f1,f2,p1,p2 being Real st
        [a1,a2] in D & [b1,b2] in D & [c1,c2] in D &
        [d1,d2] in D & [e1,e2] in D & [f1,f2] in D &
        not (a1=d1 & a2=d2 &
          sqrt ((c1-b1)^2 + (c2-b2)^2) =
            sqrt ((f1-e1)^2 + (f2-e2)^2)) &
        sqrt ((p1-a1)^2 + (p2-a2)^2) =
          sqrt ((c1-b1)^2 + (c2-b2)^2) &
        sqrt ((p1-d1)^2 + (p2-d2)^2) =
          sqrt ((f1-e1)^2 + (f2-e2)^2)
      holds [p1,p2] in D)} &
    :: Every geometrically constructible point has radical coordinates.
    (for x,y being Real st [x,y] in C holds x in R & y in R) &
    :: Algebraic obstruction lemmas used by the geometric conclusions.
    (not ex x being Real st x in R & x |^ 3 = 2) &
    (not ex t being Real st t in R & t |^ 3 - 3*t - 1 = 0) &
    :: Doubling the cube: no point (x,0) with x^3=2 is constructible.
    (for x being Real st x |^ 3 = 2 holds not [x,0] in C) &
    :: Trisecting 60 degrees: the positive root in (0,1) is cos(pi/9), and
    :: no point with that first coordinate is geometrically constructible.
    (for x,y being Real st
      0 < x & x < 1 & 8*(x |^ 3) - 6*x - 1 = 0
    holds not [x,y] in C)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 008_the_impossibility_of_trisecting_the_angle_and_doubling_the_c
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "The Impossibility of Trisecting the Angle and Doubling the
% Cube" from Hundred Theorems item 008. This file contains no proof.

hundred_theorems_008: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]

  make_point(x, y: real): point =
    (# x_coord := x, y_coord := y #)

  squared_distance(a, b: point): real =
    (x_coord(a) - x_coord(b)) * (x_coord(a) - x_coord(b))
      + (y_coord(a) - y_coord(b)) * (y_coord(a) - y_coord(b))

  same_distance(a, b, c, d: point): bool =
    squared_distance(a, b) = squared_distance(c, d)

  parallel(a, b, c, d: point): bool =
    (x_coord(a) - x_coord(b)) * (y_coord(c) - y_coord(d))
      = (y_coord(a) - y_coord(b)) * (x_coord(c) - x_coord(d))

  collinear(a, b, c: point): bool =
    parallel(a, b, a, c)

  is_intersection(m, a, b, c, d: point): bool =
    collinear(a, m, b) AND collinear(c, m, d)

  radical_closed(s: [real -> bool]): bool =
    (FORALL (x: real):
      rational?(x) IMPLIES s(x))
      AND
    (FORALL (x: real):
      s(x) IMPLIES s(-x))
      AND
    (FORALL (x, y: real):
      (s(x) AND NOT (x = 0) AND x * y = 1) IMPLIES s(y))
      AND
    (FORALL (x, y: real):
      (s(x) AND s(y)) IMPLIES s(x + y))
      AND
    (FORALL (x, y: real):
      (s(x) AND s(y)) IMPLIES s(x * y))
      AND
    (FORALL (x, y: real):
      (s(x) AND 0 <= x AND 0 <= y AND y * y = x) IMPLIES s(y))

  radical_sqrt(x: real): bool =
    FORALL (s: [real -> bool]):
      radical_closed(s) IMPLIES s(x)

  construction_closed(s: [point -> bool]): bool =
    (FORALL (p: point):
      (rational?(x_coord(p)) AND rational?(y_coord(p)))
        IMPLIES s(p))
      AND
    (FORALL (a, b, c, d, m: point):
      (s(a) AND s(b) AND s(c) AND s(d)
        AND NOT parallel(a, b, c, d)
        AND is_intersection(m, a, b, c, d))
        IMPLIES s(m))
      AND
    (FORALL (a, b, c, d, e, m: point):
      (s(a) AND s(b) AND s(c) AND s(d) AND s(e)
        AND NOT (a = b)
        AND collinear(a, m, b)
        AND same_distance(c, m, d, e))
        IMPLIES s(m))
      AND
    (FORALL (a, b, c, d, e, f, m: point):
      (s(a) AND s(b) AND s(c) AND s(d) AND s(e) AND s(f)
        AND NOT (a = d AND same_distance(b, c, e, f))
        AND same_distance(a, m, b, c)
        AND same_distance(d, m, e, f))
        IMPLIES s(m))

  constructible(p: point): bool =
    FORALL (s: [point -> bool]):
      construction_closed(s) IMPLIES s(p)

  cubic_polynomial(a, b, c, x: real): real =
    x * x * x + a * x * x + b * x + c

  cubic_root_radical_sqrt_rational: bool =
    FORALL (a, b, c, x: real):
      (rational?(a) AND rational?(b) AND rational?(c)
        AND radical_sqrt(x)
        AND cubic_polynomial(a, b, c, x) = 0)
      IMPLIES
        (EXISTS (r: real):
          rational?(r) AND cubic_polynomial(a, b, c, r) = 0)

  constructible_radical_sqrt: bool =
    FORALL (p: point):
      constructible(p)
        IMPLIES
          (radical_sqrt(x_coord(p)) AND radical_sqrt(y_coord(p)))

  impossibility_of_doubling_the_cube_algebra: bool =
    NOT (EXISTS (x: real):
      radical_sqrt(x) AND x * x * x = 2)

  impossibility_of_doubling_the_cube: bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      x * x * x = 2
        IMPLIES NOT constructible(make_point(x, 0))

  cos_pi_over_nine(c: real): bool =
    0 < c AND 8 * c * c * c - 6 * c - 1 = 0

  impossibility_of_trisecting_pi_over_3_algebra: bool =
    NOT (EXISTS (x: real):
      radical_sqrt(x) AND x * x * x - 3 * x - 1 = 0)

  impossibility_of_trisecting_angle_pi_over_3: bool =
    FORALL (c: real):
      cos_pi_over_nine(c)
        IMPLIES NOT constructible(make_point(c, 0))

  impossibility_of_trisecting_angle_pi_over_3_all_ordinates: bool =
    FORALL (c, y: real):
      cos_pi_over_nine(c)
        IMPLIES NOT constructible(make_point(c, y))
END hundred_theorems_008

title: 080_the_fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic
content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2015 Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Leonardo de Moura, Jeremy Avigad, Mario Carneiro
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.List
public import Mathlib.Data.Nat.GCD.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.List.Prime
public import Mathlib.Data.List.Sort
public import Mathlib.Data.List.Perm.Subperm

/-!
# Prime numbers

This file deals with the factors of natural numbers.

## Important declarations

- `Nat.primeFactorsList n`: the prime factorization of `n`
- `Nat.primeFactorsList_unique`: uniqueness of the prime factorisation

-/

@[expose] public section

assert_not_exists Multiset

open Bool Subtype

open Nat

namespace Nat

/-- `primeFactorsList n` is the prime factorization of `n`, listed in increasing order. -/
def primeFactorsList : ℕ → List ℕ
  | 0 => []
  | 1 => []
  | k + 2 =>
    let m := minFac (k + 2)
    m :: primeFactorsList ((k + 2) / m)
decreasing_by exact factors_lemma

@[simp]
theorem primeFactorsList_zero : primeFactorsList 0 = [] := by rw [primeFactorsList]

@[simp]
theorem primeFactorsList_one : primeFactorsList 1 = [] := by rw [primeFactorsList]

@[simp]
theorem primeFactorsList_two : primeFactorsList 2 = [2] := by simp [primeFactorsList]

theorem prime_of_mem_primeFactorsList {n : ℕ} : ∀ {p : ℕ}, p ∈ primeFactorsList n → Prime p := by sorry
theorem pos_of_mem_primeFactorsList {n p : ℕ} (h : p ∈ primeFactorsList n) : 0 < p :=
  Prime.pos (prime_of_mem_primeFactorsList h)

theorem prod_primeFactorsList : ∀ {n}, n ≠ 0 → List.prod (primeFactorsList n) = n := by sorry
theorem primeFactorsList_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) : p.primeFactorsList = [p] := by sorry
theorem isChain_cons_primeFactorsList {n : ℕ} :
    ∀ {a}, (∀ p, Prime p → p ∣ n → a ≤ p) → List.IsChain (· ≤ ·) (a :: primeFactorsList n) := by sorry
theorem isChain_two_cons_primeFactorsList (n) : List.IsChain (· ≤ ·) (2 :: primeFactorsList n) :=
  isChain_cons_primeFactorsList fun _ pp _ => pp.two_le

theorem isChain_primeFactorsList (n) : List.IsChain (· ≤ ·) (primeFactorsList n) :=
  (isChain_two_cons_primeFactorsList _).tail

theorem primeFactorsList_sorted (n : ℕ) : List.SortedLE (primeFactorsList n) :=
  (isChain_primeFactorsList _).sortedLE

/-- `primeFactorsList` can be constructed inductively by extracting `minFac`, for sufficiently
large `n`. -/
theorem primeFactorsList_add_two (n : ℕ) :
    primeFactorsList (n + 2) = minFac (n + 2) :: primeFactorsList ((n + 2) / minFac (n + 2)) := by sorry
theorem primeFactorsList_eq_nil (n : ℕ) : n.primeFactorsList = [] ↔ n = 0 ∨ n = 1 := by sorry
theorem primeFactorsList_ne_nil (n : ℕ) : n.primeFactorsList ≠ [] ↔ 1 < n := by sorry
open scoped List in
theorem eq_of_perm_primeFactorsList {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0)
    (h : a.primeFactorsList ~ b.primeFactorsList) : a = b := by sorry
open List

theorem mem_primeFactorsList_iff_dvd {n p : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (hp : Prime p) :
    p ∈ primeFactorsList n ↔ p ∣ n where
  mp h := prod_primeFactorsList hn ▸ List.dvd_prod h
  mpr h := mem_list_primes_of_dvd_prod (prime_iff.mp hp)
    (fun _ h ↦ prime_iff.mp (prime_of_mem_primeFactorsList h)) ((prod_primeFactorsList hn).symm ▸ h)

theorem dvd_of_mem_primeFactorsList {n p : ℕ} (h : p ∈ n.primeFactorsList) : p ∣ n := by sorry
theorem mem_primeFactorsList {n p} (hn : n ≠ 0) : p ∈ primeFactorsList n ↔ Prime p ∧ p ∣ n :=
  ⟨fun h => ⟨prime_of_mem_primeFactorsList h, dvd_of_mem_primeFactorsList h⟩, fun ⟨hprime, hdvd⟩ =>
    (mem_primeFactorsList_iff_dvd hn hprime).mpr hdvd⟩

@[simp] lemma mem_primeFactorsList' {n p} : p ∈ n.primeFactorsList ↔ p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n ∧ n ≠ 0 := by sorry
theorem le_of_mem_primeFactorsList {n p : ℕ} (h : p ∈ n.primeFactorsList) : p ≤ n := by sorry
theorem primeFactorsList_unique {n : ℕ} {l : List ℕ} (h₁ : prod l = n) (h₂ : ∀ p ∈ l, Prime p) :
    l ~ primeFactorsList n := by sorry
theorem Prime.primeFactorsList_pow {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (n : ℕ) :
    (p ^ n).primeFactorsList = List.replicate n p := by sorry
theorem eq_prime_pow_of_unique_prime_dvd {n p : ℕ} (hpos : n ≠ 0)
    (h : ∀ {d}, Nat.Prime d → d ∣ n → d = p) : n = p ^ n.primeFactorsList.length := by sorry
theorem perm_primeFactorsList_mul {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    (a * b).primeFactorsList ~ a.primeFactorsList ++ b.primeFactorsList := by sorry
theorem perm_primeFactorsList_mul_of_coprime {a b : ℕ} (hab : Coprime a b) :
    (a * b).primeFactorsList ~ a.primeFactorsList ++ b.primeFactorsList := by sorry
theorem primeFactorsList_sublist_right {n k : ℕ} (h : k ≠ 0) :
    n.primeFactorsList <+ (n * k).primeFactorsList := by sorry
theorem primeFactorsList_sublist_of_dvd {n k : ℕ} (h : n ∣ k) (h' : k ≠ 0) :
    n.primeFactorsList <+ k.primeFactorsList := by sorry
theorem primeFactorsList_subset_right {n k : ℕ} (h : k ≠ 0) :
    n.primeFactorsList ⊆ (n * k).primeFactorsList :=
  (primeFactorsList_sublist_right h).subset

theorem primeFactorsList_subset_of_dvd {n k : ℕ} (h : n ∣ k) (h' : k ≠ 0) :
    n.primeFactorsList ⊆ k.primeFactorsList :=
  (primeFactorsList_sublist_of_dvd h h').subset

theorem dvd_of_primeFactorsList_subperm {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0)
    (h : a.primeFactorsList <+~ b.primeFactorsList) : a ∣ b := by sorry
theorem replicate_subperm_primeFactorsList_iff {a b n : ℕ} (ha : Prime a) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    replicate n a <+~ primeFactorsList b ↔ a ^ n ∣ b := by sorry
end

theorem mem_primeFactorsList_mul {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) {p : ℕ} :
    p ∈ (a * b).primeFactorsList ↔ p ∈ a.primeFactorsList ∨ p ∈ b.primeFactorsList := by sorry
theorem coprime_primeFactorsList_disjoint {a b : ℕ} (hab : a.Coprime b) :
    List.Disjoint a.primeFactorsList b.primeFactorsList := by sorry
theorem mem_primeFactorsList_mul_of_coprime {a b : ℕ} (hab : Coprime a b) (p : ℕ) :
    p ∈ (a * b).primeFactorsList ↔ p ∈ a.primeFactorsList ∪ b.primeFactorsList := by sorry
open List

/-- If `p` is a prime factor of `a` then `p` is also a prime factor of `a * b` for any `b > 0` -/
theorem mem_primeFactorsList_mul_left {p a b : ℕ} (hpa : p ∈ a.primeFactorsList) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    p ∈ (a * b).primeFactorsList := by sorry
theorem mem_primeFactorsList_mul_right {p a b : ℕ} (hpb : p ∈ b.primeFactorsList) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    p ∈ (a * b).primeFactorsList := by sorry
theorem eq_two_pow_or_exists_odd_prime_and_dvd (n : ℕ) :
    (∃ k : ℕ, n = 2 ^ k) ∨ ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ p ∣ n ∧ Odd p :=
  (eq_or_ne n 0).elim (fun hn => Or.inr ⟨3, prime_three, hn.symm ▸ dvd_zero 3, ⟨1, rfl⟩⟩) fun hn =>
    or_iff_not_imp_right.mpr fun H =>
      ⟨n.primeFactorsList.length,
        eq_prime_pow_of_unique_prime_dvd hn fun {_} hprime hdvd =>
          hprime.eq_two_or_odd'.resolve_right fun hodd => H ⟨_, hprime, hdvd, hodd⟩⟩

theorem four_dvd_or_exists_odd_prime_and_dvd_of_two_lt {n : ℕ} (n2 : 2 < n) :
    4 ∣ n ∨ ∃ p, Prime p ∧ p ∣ n ∧ Odd p := by sorry
end Nat

title: 080_the_fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic
content:
(* Every positive natural number has a canonical prime-power decomposition. *)
From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect.

Theorem fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic_decomposition n :
  0 < n ->
  n = \prod_(f <- prime_decomp n) f.1 ^ f.2.
Proof.
exact: prod_prime_decomp.
Qed.

(* The multiplicity of every prime uniquely determines a positive integer. *)
Theorem fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic_uniqueness m n :
  0 < m ->
  0 < n ->
  (forall p, logn p m = logn p n) ->
  m = n.
Proof.
move=> Hm Hn Hlog.
exact: (eqn_from_log Hm Hn Hlog).
Qed.

Check fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic_decomposition.
Check fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic_uniqueness.

title: 080_the_fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic
content:
(*  Title:      HOL/Computational_Algebra/Primes.thy
    Author:     Christophe Tabacznyj
    Author:     Lawrence C. Paulson
    Author:     Amine Chaieb
    Author:     Thomas M. Rasmussen
    Author:     Jeremy Avigad
    Author:     Tobias Nipkow
    Author:     Manuel Eberl

This theory deals with properties of primes. Definitions and lemmas are
proved uniformly for the natural numbers and integers.

This file combines and revises a number of prior developments.

The original theories "GCD" and "Primes" were by Christophe Tabacznyj
and Lawrence C. Paulson, based on @{cite davenport92}. They introduced
gcd, lcm, and prime for the natural numbers.

The original theory "IntPrimes" was by Thomas M. Rasmussen, and
extended gcd, lcm, primes to the integers. Amine Chaieb provided
another extension of the notions to the integers, and added a number
of results to "Primes" and "GCD". IntPrimes also defined and developed
the congruence relations on the integers. The notion was extended to
the natural numbers by Chaieb.

Jeremy Avigad combined all of these, made everything uniform for the
natural numbers and the integers, and added a number of new theorems.

Tobias Nipkow cleaned up a lot.

Florian Haftmann and Manuel Eberl put primality and prime factorisation
onto an algebraic foundation and thus generalised these concepts to 
other rings, such as polynomials. (see also the Factorial_Ring theory).

There were also previous formalisations of unique factorisation by 
Thomas Marthedal Rasmussen, Jeremy Avigad, and David Gray.
*)

section \<open>Primes\<close>

theory Primes
imports Euclidean_Algorithm
begin

subsection \<open>Primes on \<^typ>\<open>nat\<close> and \<^typ>\<open>int\<close>\<close>

lemma Suc_0_not_prime_nat [simp]: "\<not> prime (Suc 0)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_ge_2_nat:
  "p \<ge> 2" if "prime p" for p :: nat
  by sorry

lemma prime_ge_2_int:
  "p \<ge> 2" if "prime p" for p :: int
  by sorry

lemma prime_ge_0_int: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p \<ge> (0::int)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_gt_0_nat: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p > (0::nat)"
  by sorry

(* As a simp or intro rule,

     prime p \<Longrightarrow> p > 0

   wreaks havoc here. When the premise includes \<forall>x \<in># M. prime x, it
   leads to the backchaining

     x > 0
     prime x
     x \<in># M   which is, unfortunately,
     count M x > 0  FIXME no, this is obsolete
*)

lemma prime_gt_0_int: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p > (0::int)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_ge_1_nat: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p \<ge> (1::nat)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_ge_Suc_0_nat: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p \<ge> Suc 0"
  by sorry

lemma prime_ge_1_int: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p \<ge> (1::int)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_gt_1_nat: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p > (1::nat)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_gt_Suc_0_nat: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p > Suc 0"
  by sorry

lemma prime_gt_1_int: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p > (1::int)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_natI:
  "prime p" if "p \<ge> 2" and "\<And>m n. p dvd m * n \<Longrightarrow> p dvd m \<or> p dvd n" for p :: nat
  by sorry

lemma prime_intI:
  "prime p" if "p \<ge> 2" and "\<And>m n. p dvd m * n \<Longrightarrow> p dvd m \<or> p dvd n" for p :: int
  by sorry

lemma prime_elem_nat_iff [simp]:
  "prime_elem n \<longleftrightarrow> prime n" for n :: nat
  by sorry

lemma prime_elem_iff_prime_abs [simp]:
  "prime_elem k \<longleftrightarrow> prime \<bar>k\<bar>" for k :: int
  by sorry

lemma prime_nat_int_transfer [simp]:
  "prime (int n) \<longleftrightarrow> prime n" (is "?P \<longleftrightarrow> ?Q")
  by sorry

lemma prime_nat_iff_prime [simp]:
  "prime (nat k) \<longleftrightarrow> prime k"
  by sorry

lemma prime_int_nat_transfer:
  "prime k \<longleftrightarrow> k \<ge> 0 \<and> prime (nat k)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_nat_naiveI:
  "prime p" if "p \<ge> 2" and dvd: "\<And>n. n dvd p \<Longrightarrow> n = 1 \<or> n = p" for p :: nat
  by sorry

lemma prime_int_naiveI:
  "prime p" if "p \<ge> 2" and dvd: "\<And>k. k dvd p \<Longrightarrow> \<bar>k\<bar> = 1 \<or> \<bar>k\<bar> = p" for p :: int
  by sorry

lemma prime_nat_iff:
  "prime (n :: nat) \<longleftrightarrow> (1 < n \<and> (\<forall>m. m dvd n \<longrightarrow> m = 1 \<or> m = n))"
  by sorry

lemma prime_nat_iff':
  "prime (p :: nat) \<longleftrightarrow> p > 1 \<and> (\<forall>n \<in> {2..<p}. \<not> n dvd p)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_int_iff:
  "prime (n::int) \<longleftrightarrow> (1 < n \<and> (\<forall>m. m \<ge> 0 \<and> m dvd n \<longrightarrow> m = 1 \<or> m = n))"
  by sorry

lemma prime_int_iff':
  "prime (p :: int) \<longleftrightarrow> p > 1 \<and> (\<forall>n \<in> {2..<p}. \<not> n dvd p)" (is "?P \<longleftrightarrow> ?Q")
  by sorry

lemma prime_nat_not_dvd:
  assumes "prime p" "p > n" "n \<noteq> (1::nat)"
  shows   "\<not>n dvd p"
  by sorry

lemma prime_int_not_dvd:
  assumes "prime p" "p > n" "n > (1::int)"
  shows   "\<not>n dvd p"
  by sorry

lemma prime_odd_nat: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p > (2::nat) \<Longrightarrow> odd p"
  by sorry

lemma prime_odd_int: "prime p \<Longrightarrow> p > (2::int) \<Longrightarrow> odd p"
  by sorry

lemma prime_int_altdef:
  "prime p = (1 < p \<and> (\<forall>m::int. m \<ge> 0 \<longrightarrow> m dvd p \<longrightarrow>
    m = 1 \<or> m = p))"
  by sorry

lemma not_prime_eq_prod_nat:
  assumes "m > 1" "\<not> prime (m::nat)"
  shows   "\<exists>n k. n = m * k \<and> 1 < m \<and> m < n \<and> 1 < k \<and> k < n"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Make prime naively executable\<close>

lemma prime_int_numeral_eq [simp]:
  "prime (numeral m :: int) \<longleftrightarrow> prime (numeral m :: nat)"
  by sorry

class check_prime_by_range = normalization_semidom + discrete_linordered_semidom +
  assumes prime_iff: \<open>prime a \<longleftrightarrow> 1 < a \<and> (\<forall>d\<in>{2..a div 2}. \<not> d dvd a)\<close>
begin

lemma two_is_prime [simp]:
  \<open>prime 2\<close>
  by sorry

end

lemma divisor_less_eq_half_nat:
  \<open>m \<le> n div 2\<close> if \<open>m dvd n\<close> \<open>m < n\<close> for m n :: nat
  by sorry

instance nat :: check_prime_by_range
  apply standard
  apply (auto simp add: prime_nat_iff)
  apply (rule ccontr)
  apply (auto simp add: neq_iff)
  apply (metis One_nat_def Suc_1 Suc_leI atLeastAtMost_iff divisor_less_eq_half_nat)
  done

lemma two_is_prime_nat [simp]:
  \<open>prime (2::nat)\<close>
  by sorry

lemma divisor_less_eq_half_int:
  \<open>k \<le> l div 2\<close> if \<open>k dvd l\<close> \<open>k < l\<close> \<open>l \<ge> 0\<close> \<open>k \<ge> 0\<close> for k l :: int
  by sorry

instance int :: check_prime_by_range
  apply standard
  apply (auto simp add: prime_int_iff)
  apply (smt (verit) int_div_less_self)
  apply (rule ccontr)
  apply (auto simp add: neq_iff zdvd_not_zless)
  apply (metis div_by_0 dvd_div_eq_0_iff less_le_not_le one_dvd order_le_less
      zdvd_not_zless)
  apply (metis atLeastAtMost_iff divisor_less_eq_half_int dvd_div_eq_0_iff
      int_one_le_iff_zero_less nle_le one_add_one pos_imp_zdiv_nonneg_iff zdiv_eq_0_iff
      zless_imp_add1_zle)
  done

lemma prime_nat_numeral_eq [simp]: \<comment> \<open>TODO Sieve Of Erathosthenes might speed this up\<close>
  "prime (numeral m :: nat) \<longleftrightarrow>
    (1::nat) < numeral m \<and>
    (\<forall>n::nat \<in> set [2..<Suc (numeral m div 2)]. \<not> n dvd numeral m)"
  by sorry

context check_prime_by_range
begin

definition check_divisors :: \<open>'a \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> bool\<close>
  where \<open>check_divisors l u a \<longleftrightarrow> (\<forall>d\<in>{l..u}. \<not> d dvd a)\<close>

lemma check_divisors_rec [code]:
  \<open>check_divisors l u a \<longleftrightarrow> u < l \<or> (\<not> l dvd a \<and> check_divisors (l + 1) u a)\<close>
  by sorry
  done

lemma prime_eq_check_divisors [code]:
  \<open>prime a \<longleftrightarrow> a > 1 \<and> check_divisors 2 (a div 2) a\<close>
  by sorry

end


subsection \<open>Largest exponent of a prime factor\<close>

lemma prime_factor_nat:
  "n \<noteq> (1::nat) \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>p. prime p \<and> p dvd n"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factor_int:
  fixes k :: int
  assumes "\<bar>k\<bar> \<noteq> 1"
  obtains p where "prime p" "p dvd k"
  by sorry

text\<open>Possibly duplicates other material, but avoid the complexities of multisets.\<close>
  
lemma prime_power_cancel_less:
  assumes "prime p" and eq: "m * (p ^ k) = m' * (p ^ k')" and less: "k < k'" and "\<not> p dvd m"
  shows False
  by sorry

lemma prime_power_cancel:
  assumes "prime p" and eq: "m * (p ^ k) = m' * (p ^ k')" and "\<not> p dvd m" "\<not> p dvd m'"
  shows "k = k'"
  by sorry

lemma prime_power_cancel2:
  assumes "prime p" "m * (p ^ k) = m' * (p ^ k')" "\<not> p dvd m" "\<not> p dvd m'"
  obtains "m = m'" "k = k'"
  by sorry

lemma prime_power_canonical:
  fixes m :: nat
  assumes "prime p" "m > 0"
  shows "\<exists>k n. \<not> p dvd n \<and> m = n * p ^ k"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Infinitely many primes\<close>

lemma next_prime_bound: "\<exists>p::nat. prime p \<and> n < p \<and> p \<le> fact n + 1"
  by sorry

lemma bigger_prime: "\<exists>p. prime p \<and> p > (n::nat)"
  by sorry

lemma primes_infinite: "\<not> (finite {(p::nat). prime p})"
  by sorry

subsection \<open>Powers of Primes\<close>

text\<open>Versions for type nat only\<close>

lemma prime_product:
  fixes p::nat
  assumes "prime (p * q)"
  shows "p = 1 \<or> q = 1"
  by sorry

(* TODO: Generalise? *)
lemma prime_power_mult_nat:
  fixes p :: nat
  assumes p: "prime p" and xy: "x * y = p ^ k"
  shows "\<exists>i j. x = p ^ i \<and> y = p^ j"
  by sorry

lemma prime_power_exp_nat:
  fixes p::nat
  assumes p: "prime p" and n: "n \<noteq> 0"
    and xn: "x^n = p^k" shows "\<exists>i. x = p^i"
  by sorry

lemma divides_primepow_nat:
  fixes p :: nat
  assumes p: "prime p"
  shows "d dvd p ^ k \<longleftrightarrow> (\<exists>i\<le>k. d = p ^ i)"
  by sorry

lemma gcd_prime_int:
  assumes "prime (p :: int)"
  shows   "gcd p k = (if p dvd k then p else 1)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Chinese Remainder Theorem Variants\<close>

lemma bezout_gcd_nat:
  fixes a::nat shows "\<exists>x y. a * x - b * y = gcd a b \<or> b * x - a * y = gcd a b"
  by sorry
by (metis bezout_nat diff_add_inverse gcd_add_mult gcd.commute
  gcd_nat.right_neutral mult_0)

lemma gcd_bezout_sum_nat:
  fixes a::nat
  assumes "a * x + b * y = d"
  shows "gcd a b dvd d"
  by sorry


text \<open>A binary form of the Chinese Remainder Theorem.\<close>

(* TODO: Generalise? *)
lemma chinese_remainder:
  fixes a::nat  assumes ab: "coprime a b" and a: "a \<noteq> 0" and b: "b \<noteq> 0"
  shows "\<exists>x q1 q2. x = u + q1 * a \<and> x = v + q2 * b"
  by sorry

text \<open>Primality\<close>

lemma coprime_bezout_strong:
  fixes a::nat assumes "coprime a b"  "b \<noteq> 1"
  shows "\<exists>x y. a * x = b * y + 1"
  by sorry

lemma bezout_prime:
  assumes p: "prime p" and pa: "\<not> p dvd a"
  shows "\<exists>x y. a*x = Suc (p*y)"
  by sorry
(* END TODO *)



subsection \<open>Multiplicity and primality for natural numbers and integers\<close>

lemma prime_factors_gt_0_nat:
  "p \<in> prime_factors x \<Longrightarrow> p > (0::nat)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factors_gt_0_int:
  "p \<in> prime_factors x \<Longrightarrow> p > (0::int)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factors_ge_0_int [elim]: (* FIXME !? *)
  fixes n :: int
  shows "p \<in> prime_factors n \<Longrightarrow> p \<ge> 0"
  by sorry
  
lemma prod_mset_prime_factorization_int:
  fixes n :: int
  assumes "n > 0"
  shows   "prod_mset (prime_factorization n) = n"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factorization_exists_nat:
  "n > 0 \<Longrightarrow> (\<exists>M. (\<forall>p::nat \<in> set_mset M. prime p) \<and> n = (\<Prod>i \<in># M. i))"
  by sorry

lemma prod_mset_prime_factorization_nat [simp]: 
  "(n::nat) > 0 \<Longrightarrow> prod_mset (prime_factorization n) = n"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factorization_nat:
    "n > (0::nat) \<Longrightarrow> n = (\<Prod>p \<in> prime_factors n. p ^ multiplicity p n)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factorization_int:
    "n > (0::int) \<Longrightarrow> n = (\<Prod>p \<in> prime_factors n. p ^ multiplicity p n)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factorization_unique_nat:
  fixes f :: "nat \<Rightarrow> _"
  assumes S_eq: "S = {p. 0 < f p}"
    and "finite S"
    and S: "\<forall>p\<in>S. prime p" "n = (\<Prod>p\<in>S. p ^ f p)"
  shows "S = prime_factors n \<and> (\<forall>p. prime p \<longrightarrow> f p = multiplicity p n)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factorization_unique_int:
  fixes f :: "int \<Rightarrow> _"
  assumes S_eq: "S = {p. 0 < f p}"
    and "finite S"
    and S: "\<forall>p\<in>S. prime p" "abs n = (\<Prod>p\<in>S. p ^ f p)"
  shows "S = prime_factors n \<and> (\<forall>p. prime p \<longrightarrow> f p = multiplicity p n)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factors_characterization_nat:
  "S = {p. 0 < f (p::nat)} \<Longrightarrow>
    finite S \<Longrightarrow> \<forall>p\<in>S. prime p \<Longrightarrow> n = (\<Prod>p\<in>S. p ^ f p) \<Longrightarrow> prime_factors n = S"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factors_characterization'_nat:
  "finite {p. 0 < f (p::nat)} \<Longrightarrow>
    (\<forall>p. 0 < f p \<longrightarrow> prime p) \<Longrightarrow>
      prime_factors (\<Prod>p | 0 < f p. p ^ f p) = {p. 0 < f p}"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factors_characterization_int:
  "S = {p. 0 < f (p::int)} \<Longrightarrow> finite S \<Longrightarrow>
    \<forall>p\<in>S. prime p \<Longrightarrow> abs n = (\<Prod>p\<in>S. p ^ f p) \<Longrightarrow> prime_factors n = S"
  by sorry

(* TODO Move *)
lemma abs_prod: "abs (prod f A :: 'a :: linordered_idom) = prod (\<lambda>x. abs (f x)) A"
  by sorry

lemma primes_characterization'_int [rule_format]:
  "finite {p. p \<ge> 0 \<and> 0 < f (p::int)} \<Longrightarrow> \<forall>p. 0 < f p \<longrightarrow> prime p \<Longrightarrow>
      prime_factors (\<Prod>p | p \<ge> 0 \<and> 0 < f p. p ^ f p) = {p. p \<ge> 0 \<and> 0 < f p}"
  by sorry

lemma multiplicity_characterization_nat:
  "S = {p. 0 < f (p::nat)} \<Longrightarrow> finite S \<Longrightarrow> \<forall>p\<in>S. prime p \<Longrightarrow> prime p \<Longrightarrow>
    n = (\<Prod>p\<in>S. p ^ f p) \<Longrightarrow> multiplicity p n = f p"
  by sorry

lemma multiplicity_characterization'_nat: "finite {p. 0 < f (p::nat)} \<longrightarrow>
    (\<forall>p. 0 < f p \<longrightarrow> prime p) \<longrightarrow> prime p \<longrightarrow>
      multiplicity p (\<Prod>p | 0 < f p. p ^ f p) = f p"
  by sorry

lemma multiplicity_characterization_int: "S = {p. 0 < f (p::int)} \<Longrightarrow>
    finite S \<Longrightarrow> \<forall>p\<in>S. prime p \<Longrightarrow> prime p \<Longrightarrow> n = (\<Prod>p\<in>S. p ^ f p) \<Longrightarrow> multiplicity p n = f p"
  by sorry

lemma multiplicity_characterization'_int [rule_format]:
  "finite {p. p \<ge> 0 \<and> 0 < f (p::int)} \<Longrightarrow>
    (\<forall>p. 0 < f p \<longrightarrow> prime p) \<Longrightarrow> prime p \<Longrightarrow>
      multiplicity p (\<Prod>p | p \<ge> 0 \<and> 0 < f p. p ^ f p) = f p"
  by sorry

lemma multiplicity_one_nat [simp]: "multiplicity p (Suc 0) = 0"
  by sorry

lemma multiplicity_eq_nat:
  fixes x and y::nat
  assumes "x > 0" "y > 0" "\<And>p. prime p \<Longrightarrow> multiplicity p x = multiplicity p y"
  shows "x = y"
  by sorry

lemma multiplicity_eq_int:
  fixes x y :: int
  assumes "x > 0" "y > 0" "\<And>p. prime p \<Longrightarrow> multiplicity p x = multiplicity p y"
  shows "x = y"
  by sorry

lemma multiplicity_prod_prime_powers:
  assumes "finite S" "\<And>x. x \<in> S \<Longrightarrow> prime x" "prime p"
  shows   "multiplicity p (\<Prod>p \<in> S. p ^ f p) = (if p \<in> S then f p else 0)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factorization_prod_mset:
  assumes "0 \<notin># A"
  shows "prime_factorization (prod_mset A) = \<Sum>\<^sub>#(image_mset prime_factorization A)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factors_prod:
  assumes "finite A" and "0 \<notin> f ` A"
  shows "prime_factors (prod f A) = \<Union>((prime_factors \<circ> f) ` A)"
  by sorry

lemma prime_factors_fact:
  "prime_factors (fact n) = {p \<in> {2..n}. prime p}" (is "?M = ?N")
  by sorry

lemma prime_dvd_fact_iff:
  assumes "prime p"
  shows "p dvd fact n \<longleftrightarrow> p \<le> n"
  by sorry

lemma dvd_choose_prime:
  assumes kn: "k < n" and k: "k \<noteq> 0" and n: "n \<noteq> 0" and prime_n: "prime n"
  shows "n dvd (n choose k)"
  by sorry

lemma (in ring_1) minus_power_prime_CHAR:
  assumes "p = CHAR('a)" "prime p"
  shows "(-x :: 'a) ^ p = -(x ^ p)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Rings and fields with prime characteristic\<close>

text \<open>
  We introduce some type classes for rings and fields with prime characteristic.
\<close>

class semiring_prime_char = semiring_1 +
  assumes prime_char_aux: "\<exists>n. prime n \<and> of_nat n = (0 :: 'a)"
begin

lemma CHAR_pos [intro, simp]: "CHAR('a) > 0"
  by sorry

lemma CHAR_nonzero [simp]: "CHAR('a) \<noteq> 0"
  by sorry

lemma CHAR_prime [intro, simp]: "prime CHAR('a)"
  by sorry

end

lemma semiring_prime_charI [intro?]:
  "prime CHAR('a :: semiring_1) \<Longrightarrow> OFCLASS('a, semiring_prime_char_class)"
  by sorry

lemma idom_prime_charI [intro?]:
  assumes "CHAR('a :: idom) > 0"
  shows   "OFCLASS('a, semiring_prime_char_class)"
  by sorry

class comm_semiring_prime_char = comm_semiring_1 + semiring_prime_char
class comm_ring_prime_char = comm_ring_1 + semiring_prime_char
begin
subclass comm_semiring_prime_char ..
end
class idom_prime_char = idom + semiring_prime_char
begin
subclass comm_ring_prime_char ..
end

class field_prime_char = field +
  assumes pos_char_exists: "\<exists>n>0. of_nat n = (0 :: 'a)"
begin
subclass idom_prime_char
  apply standard
  using pos_char_exists local.CHAR_pos_iff local.of_nat_CHAR local.prime_CHAR_semidom by blast
end

lemma field_prime_charI [intro?]:
  "n > 0 \<Longrightarrow> of_nat n = (0 :: 'a :: field) \<Longrightarrow> OFCLASS('a, field_prime_char_class)"
  by sorry

lemma field_prime_charI' [intro?]:
  "CHAR('a :: field) > 0 \<Longrightarrow> OFCLASS('a, field_prime_char_class)"
  by sorry


subsection \<open>Finite fields\<close>

class finite_field = field_prime_char + finite

lemma finite_fieldI [intro?]:
  assumes "finite (UNIV :: 'a :: field set)"
  shows   "OFCLASS('a, finite_field_class)"
  by sorry

text \<open>
  On a finite field with \<open>n\<close> elements, taking the \<open>n\<close>-th power of an element
  is the identity. This is an obvious consequence of the fact that the multiplicative group of
  the field is a finite group of order \<open>n - 1\<close>, so \<open>x^n = 1\<close> for any non-zero \<open>x\<close>.

  Note that this result is sharp in the sense that the multiplicative group of a
  finite field is cyclic, i.e.\ it contains an element of order \<open>n - 1\<close>.
  (We don't prove this here.)
\<close>
lemma finite_field_power_card_eq_same:
  fixes x :: "'a :: finite_field"
  shows   "x ^ card (UNIV :: 'a set) = x"
  by sorry

lemma finite_field_power_card_power_eq_same:
  fixes x :: "'a :: finite_field"
  assumes "m = card (UNIV :: 'a set) ^ n"
  shows   "x ^ m = x"
  by sorry

class enum_finite_field = finite_field +
  fixes enum_finite_field :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'a"
  assumes enum_finite_field: "enum_finite_field ` {..<card (UNIV :: 'a set)} = UNIV"
begin

lemma inj_on_enum_finite_field: "inj_on enum_finite_field {..<card (UNIV :: 'a set)}"
  by sorry

end

text \<open>
  To get rid of the pending sort hypotheses, we prove that the field with 2 elements is indeed
  a finite field.
\<close>
typedef gf2 = "{0, 1 :: nat}"
  by auto

setup_lifting type_definition_gf2

instantiation gf2 :: field
begin
lift_definition zero_gf2 :: "gf2" is "0" by auto
lift_definition one_gf2 :: "gf2" is "1" by auto
lift_definition uminus_gf2 :: "gf2 \<Rightarrow> gf2" is "\<lambda>x. x" .
lift_definition plus_gf2 :: "gf2 \<Rightarrow> gf2 \<Rightarrow> gf2" is "\<lambda>x y. if x = y then 0 else 1" by auto

;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__080, "The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic":
;; every positive natural number has a unique nondecreasing list of prime
;; factors whose product is that number. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun hundred-theorems-080-least-divisor-from (n d)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix (- n d))))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp d)
           (< 1 d)
           (< d n))
      (if (equal (mod n d) 0)
          d
        (hundred-theorems-080-least-divisor-from n (+ d 1)))
    n))

(defun hundred-theorems-080-least-divisor (n)
  (if (and (natp n)
           (< 1 n))
      (hundred-theorems-080-least-divisor-from n 2)
    n))

(defun hundred-theorems-080-primep (n)
  (and (natp n)
       (< 1 n)
       (equal (hundred-theorems-080-least-divisor n) n)))

(defun hundred-theorems-080-prime-factors-aux (n fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or (not (natp n))
          (< n 2)
          (zp fuel))
      nil
    (let ((p (hundred-theorems-080-least-divisor n)))
      (cons p
            (hundred-theorems-080-prime-factors-aux
             (floor n p)
             (- fuel 1))))))

(defun hundred-theorems-080-prime-factors (n)
  (hundred-theorems-080-prime-factors-aux n n))

(defun hundred-theorems-080-list-product (factors)
  (if (consp factors)
      (* (car factors)
         (hundred-theorems-080-list-product (cdr factors)))
    1))

(defun hundred-theorems-080-prime-list-p (factors)
  (if (consp factors)
      (and (hundred-theorems-080-primep (car factors))
           (hundred-theorems-080-prime-list-p (cdr factors)))
    (null factors)))

(defun hundred-theorems-080-nondecreasing-p (factors)
  (if (and (consp factors)
           (consp (cdr factors)))
      (and (<= (car factors) (cadr factors))
           (hundred-theorems-080-nondecreasing-p (cdr factors)))
    t))

(defun hundred-theorems-080-prime-decomposition-p (n factors)
  (and (natp n)
       (< 0 n)
       (hundred-theorems-080-prime-list-p factors)
       (hundred-theorems-080-nondecreasing-p factors)
       (equal (hundred-theorems-080-list-product factors) n)))

(defun hundred-theorems-080-fundamental-theorem-of-arithmetic-statement
  (n factors)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (< 0 n))
   (let ((canonical
          (hundred-theorems-080-prime-factors n)))
     (and
      (hundred-theorems-080-prime-decomposition-p n canonical)
      (implies
       (hundred-theorems-080-prime-decomposition-p n factors)
       (equal factors canonical))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 080_the_fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems corpus artifact
-- hundred-theorems__agda__080, "The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic": every positive
-- natural number has a unique nondecreasing list of prime factors whose product is the number.
-- This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infix 4 _≤_ _∣_
infixr 5 _∷_
infixr 3 _∨_

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

record _∣_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : divisor * quotient ≡ dividend

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record Prime (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two : 2 ≤ n
    divisor-is-trivial :
      (d : Nat) →
      d ∣ n →
      d ≡ 1 ∨ d ≡ n

data List (A : Set) : Set where
  [] : List A
  _∷_ : A → List A → List A

data AllPrime : List Nat → Set where
  all-prime-empty : AllPrime []
  all-prime-cons :
    {p : Nat} {factors : List Nat} →
    Prime p →
    AllPrime factors →
    AllPrime (p ∷ factors)

data Sorted : List Nat → Set where
  sorted-empty : Sorted []
  sorted-singleton : {p : Nat} → Sorted (p ∷ [])
  sorted-cons :
    {p q : Nat} {factors : List Nat} →
    p ≤ q →
    Sorted (q ∷ factors) →
    Sorted (p ∷ q ∷ factors)

product : List Nat → Nat
product [] = 1
product (p ∷ factors) = p * product factors

record PrimeFactorization (n : Nat) (factors : List Nat) : Set where
  field
    factors-are-sorted : Sorted factors
    factors-are-prime : AllPrime factors
    product-is-number : product factors ≡ n

record ExistsUnique (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  field
    value : A
    property : P value
    uniqueness : (other : A) → P other → other ≡ value

the-fundamental-theorem-of-arithmetic : Set
the-fundamental-theorem-of-arithmetic =
  (n : Nat) →
  1 ≤ n →
  ExistsUnique (List Nat) (PrimeFactorization n)

(*

  hundred-theorems__hol4__080, cataloged as "The Fundamental Theorem of
  Arithmetic": every nonzero natural number has a unique finitely supported
  assignment of natural exponents to primes whose prime-power product is that

open arithmeticTheory dividesTheory pred_setTheory;

val fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic =

      n <> 0 ==>
      ?!exponent : num -> num.

        (!p : num. exponent p <> 0 ==> prime p) /\
        n =
          PROD_IMAGE
            (\p : num. p EXP exponent p)

title: 080_the_fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic
content:
% Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 080, "The Fundamental
% Theorem of Arithmetic": every positive natural number has a unique
% prime-exponent factorization. This file contains no proof.

the_fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic_080: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat): value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  prime_power_product(
      exponents: [nat -> nat],
      bound: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF bound = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      prime_power_product(exponents, bound - 1)
        * bound ^ exponents(bound)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE bound

  prime_factorization(
      value: posnat,
      exponents: [nat -> nat]): bool =
    (FORALL (p: nat):
      exponents(p) > 0 IMPLIES prime_nat(p))
      AND (FORALL (p: nat):
        p > value IMPLIES exponents(p) = 0)
      AND prime_power_product(exponents, value) = value

  the_fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic: bool =
    FORALL (value: posnat):
      EXISTS (exponents: [nat -> nat]):
        prime_factorization(value, exponents)
          AND (FORALL (other: [nat -> nat]):
            prime_factorization(value, other)
              IMPLIES other = exponents)

END the_fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic_080

title: 081_divergence_of_the_prime_reciprocal_series
content:
/-
