title: 082_dissection_of_cubes__into_cubes
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Dissection of Cubes (into Cubes)" from Hundred Theorems item
-- 082. This file contains no proof.

module HundredTheorems082 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_
infix 2 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<= : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum) and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  CompleteOrderedField.lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

Point : Set -> Set
Point R = Fin (suc (suc (suc zero))) -> R

Region : Set -> Set1
Region R = Point R -> Set

record Cube
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) :
  Set where

  constructor cube
  field
    lower : Point R
    width : R
    positive-width :
      StrictLess reals
        (CompleteOrderedField.zeroR reals)
        width

open Cube public

cube-region :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  Cube reals ->
  Region R
cube-region {R} reals c p =
  (axis : Fin (suc (suc (suc zero)))) ->
  CompleteOrderedField.lessOrEqual reals
    (lower c axis)
    (p axis) and
  StrictLess reals
    (p axis)
    (CompleteOrderedField.add reals
      (lower c axis)
      (width c))

Disjoint :
  {R : Set} ->
  Region R ->
  Region R ->
  Set
Disjoint {R} left-region right-region =
  (p : Point R) ->
  left-region p ->
  right-region p ->
  Bottom

RegionEqual :
  {R : Set} ->
  Region R ->
  Region R ->
  Set
RegionEqual {R} left-region right-region =
  (p : Point R) ->
  left-region p iff right-region p

FiniteUnion :
  {R : Set} ->
  {count : Nat} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (Fin count -> Cube reals) ->
  Region R
FiniteUnion {count = count} reals pieces p =
  Exists (Fin count)
    (\ i -> cube-region reals (pieces i) p)

PairwiseDisjoint :
  {R : Set} ->
  {count : Nat} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (Fin count -> Cube reals) ->
  Set
PairwiseDisjoint {count = count} reals pieces =
  (i j : Fin count) ->
  i != j ->
  Disjoint
    (cube-region reals (pieces i))
    (cube-region reals (pieces j))

WidthsInjective :
  {R : Set} ->
  {count : Nat} ->
  {reals : CompleteOrderedField R} ->
  (Fin count -> Cube reals) ->
  Set
WidthsInjective {count = count} pieces =
  (i j : Fin count) ->
  width (pieces i) == width (pieces j) ->
  i == j

TwoOrMore : Nat -> Set
TwoOrMore count =
  suc (suc zero) <=N count

dissection-of-cubes-into-cubes : Set1
dissection-of-cubes-into-cubes =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (target : Cube reals) ->
  (count : Nat) ->
  TwoOrMore count ->
  (pieces : Fin count -> Cube reals) ->
  PairwiseDisjoint reals pieces ->
  RegionEqual
    (FiniteUnion reals pieces)
    (cube-region reals target) ->
  WidthsInjective pieces ->
  Bottom

title: 082_dissection_of_cubes__into_cubes
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 082, "Dissection
  of Cubes (into Cubes)": in every finite real dimension at least three, the
  unit cube has no finite dissection into at least two pairwise disjoint
  axis-aligned cubes with positive, pairwise distinct side lengths. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory;

val dissection_of_cubes_into_cubes =
  ``!(s : (('i -> real) # real) set).
      let cube_set =
        \(c : ('i -> real) # real).
          {x : 'i -> real |
             !j. FST c j <= x j /\ x j < FST c j + SND c}
      in
      let unit_cube =
        {x : 'i -> real | !j. 0 <= x j /\ x j < 1}
      in
        FINITE (UNIV : 'i set) /\
        3 <= CARD (UNIV : 'i set) /\
        FINITE s /\
        (!c. c IN s ==> 0 < SND c) /\
        (?c d. c IN s /\ d IN s /\ c <> d) /\
        (!c d.
           c IN s /\ d IN s /\ c <> d ==>
           DISJOINT (cube_set c) (cube_set d)) /\
        (!x.
           x IN unit_cube <=>
           ?c. c IN s /\ x IN cube_set c) /\
        (!c d.
           c IN s /\ d IN s /\ SND c = SND d ==>
           c = d)
        ==>
        F``;

title: 082_dissection_of_cubes__into_cubes
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Dissection of Cubes (into Cubes)" from
  Hundred Theorems corpus artifact 082: in every real dimension at least
  three, a cube cannot be partitioned into finitely many nontrivial
  axis-aligned cubes having pairwise distinct positive widths. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

$(
  Coordinates are indexed by 1 ... n.  The function B assigns each member
  of the finite family its bottom coordinate vector, and W assigns its real
  width.  HT082CubePoint uses the half-open convention

    B(i)(j) <= x(j) < B(i)(j) + W(i),

  matching the Lean and Isabelle sources.  HT082UnitPoint is the analogous
  half-open unit cube.  Exact equality of the union with the unit cube is
  expressed pointwise, so no geometric content is hidden in an
  uninterpreted predicate.

  Indexing the family by 1 ... k is equivalent to the source's arbitrary
  finite set of cubes.  The injectivity of W makes the indexed cubes
  distinct and states exactly that their widths are pairwise different.
  The final declaration is an unproved $a statement.
$)

$c HT082CubePoint HT082UnitPoint $.

ht082-cube-point-syntax $a
  wff ( x HT082CubePoint n B W i )
$.

ht082-unit-point-syntax $a
  wff ( x HT082UnitPoint n )
$.

${
  $d B W i j n x $.

  ht082-cube-point-definition $a
    |- (
      ( x HT082CubePoint n B W i )
      <->
      (
        x e. ( RR ^m ( 1 ... n ) )
        /\
        A. j e. ( 1 ... n )
          (
            ( ( ( B ` i ) ` j ) <_ ( x ` j ) )
            /\
            ( ( x ` j ) < ( ( ( B ` i ) ` j ) + ( W ` i ) ) )
          )
      )
    )
  $.
$}

${
  $d j n x $.

  ht082-unit-point-definition $a
    |- (
      ( x HT082UnitPoint n )
      <->
      (
        x e. ( RR ^m ( 1 ... n ) )
        /\
        A. j e. ( 1 ... n )
          ( 0 <_ ( x ` j ) /\ ( x ` j ) < 1 )
      )
    )
  $.
$}

${
  $d B W h i k n x $.

  hundred-theorems-082-dissection-of-cubes $a
    |- -.
      E. n e. NN E. k e. NN E. B E. W
        (
          (
            ( 3 <_ n /\ 2 <_ k )
            /\
            (
              B : ( 1 ... k ) --> ( RR ^m ( 1 ... n ) )
              /\
              W : ( 1 ... k ) -1-1-> RR
            )
          )
          /\
          (
            A. i e. ( 1 ... k ) 0 < ( W ` i )
            /\
            (
              A. i e. ( 1 ... k ) A. h e. ( 1 ... k )
                (
                  i =/= h
                  ->
                  -. E. x
                    (
                      ( x HT082CubePoint n B W i )
                      /\
                      ( x HT082CubePoint n B W h )
                    )
                )
              /\
              A. x
                (
                  ( x HT082UnitPoint n )
                  <->
                  E. i e. ( 1 ... k )
                    ( x HT082CubePoint n B W i )
                )
            )
          )
        )
  $.
$}

title: 082_dissection_of_cubes__into_cubes
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of "Dissection of Cubes (into Cubes)" for
:: corpus artifact hundred-theorems__mizar__082: no finite partition of the
:: three-dimensional unit cube into at least two axis-aligned cubes can have
:: all side lengths distinct. This file contains no proof.

environ

 vocabularies ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, CARD_1, CARD_3, EUCLID, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
      FINSET_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NUMBERS, ORDINAL4, PARTFUN1,
      REAL_1, RELAT_1, SETFAM_1, SUBSET_1, TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, XCMPLX_0,
      XXREAL_0, ZFMISC_1;
 notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS,
      XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, REAL_1, NAT_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
      RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, EUCLID, SETFAM_1;
 constructors REAL_1, NAT_1, RELSET_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, EUCLID, SETFAM_1;
 registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1,
      NUMBERS, XREAL_0, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2;
 requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
 definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0;
 equalities FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, SUBSET_1;
 expansions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, FINSEQ_1, FUNCT_1, RELAT_1;
 schemes FRAENKEL;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  not ex n being Nat,
      cubes being FinSequence of bool (REAL 3),
      base1,base2,base3 being FinSequence of REAL,
      widths being FinSequence of REAL st
    2 <= n &
    len cubes = n & len base1 = n & len base2 = n & len base3 = n &
    len widths = n &
    (for i being Nat st i in Seg n holds
      0 < widths/.i &
      cubes/.i =
        {p where p is Element of REAL 3:
          base1/.i <= p/.1 & p/.1 < base1/.i + widths/.i &
          base2/.i <= p/.2 & p/.2 < base2/.i + widths/.i &
          base3/.i <= p/.3 & p/.3 < base3/.i + widths/.i}) &
    (for i,j being Nat st
      i in Seg n & j in Seg n & i <> j
     holds cubes/.i misses cubes/.j) &
    union rng cubes =
      {p where p is Element of REAL 3:
        0 <= p/.1 & p/.1 < 1 &
        0 <= p/.2 & p/.2 < 1 &
        0 <= p/.3 & p/.3 < 1} &
    (for i,j being Nat st
      i in Seg n & j in Seg n & widths/.i = widths/.j
     holds i = j)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 082_dissection_of_cubes__into_cubes
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Dissection of Cubes (into Cubes)" from Hundred Theorems
% artifact 082: no finite nontrivial dissection of a unit cube in dimension at least three
% consists of pairwise disjoint axis-aligned cubes having distinct widths. This file contains
% no proof.

dissection_of_cubes_into_cubes_082: THEORY
BEGIN
  coordinate_vector: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  cube: TYPE = [# base: coordinate_vector, width: real #]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[cube]

  cube_family: TYPE = finite_set[cube]

  in_cube(dimension: nat, x: coordinate_vector, c: cube): bool =
    FORALL (axis: nat):
      axis < dimension IMPLIES
        base(c)(axis) <= x(axis)
          AND x(axis) < base(c)(axis) + width(c)

  in_unit_cube(dimension: nat, x: coordinate_vector): bool =
    FORALL (axis: nat):
      axis < dimension IMPLIES
        0 <= x(axis) AND x(axis) < 1

  positive_widths(family: cube_family): bool =
    FORALL (c: cube):
      family(c) IMPLIES 0 < width(c)

  nontrivial_family(family: cube_family): bool =
    EXISTS (c1, c2: cube):
      family(c1) AND family(c2) AND c1 /= c2

  pairwise_disjoint(
      dimension: nat,
      family: cube_family): bool =
    FORALL (c1, c2: cube):
      family(c1) AND family(c2) AND c1 /= c2
        IMPLIES
          NOT EXISTS (x: coordinate_vector):
            in_cube(dimension, x, c1)
              AND in_cube(dimension, x, c2)

  covers_unit_cube(
      dimension: nat,
      family: cube_family): bool =
    FORALL (x: coordinate_vector):
      in_unit_cube(dimension, x)
        IFF
          EXISTS (c: cube):
            family(c) AND in_cube(dimension, x, c)

  distinct_widths(family: cube_family): bool =
    FORALL (c1, c2: cube):
      family(c1) AND family(c2) AND width(c1) = width(c2)
        IMPLIES c1 = c2

  dissection_of_cubes_into_cubes: bool =
    FORALL (dimension: nat), (family: cube_family):
      dimension >= 3
        AND positive_widths(family)
        AND nontrivial_family(family)
        AND pairwise_disjoint(dimension, family)
        AND covers_unit_cube(dimension, family)
        AND distinct_widths(family)
      IMPLIES FALSE
END dissection_of_cubes_into_cubes_082

title: 083_the_friendship_theorem
content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2020 Aaron Anderson. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Aaron Anderson, Jalex Stark, Kyle Miller
-/
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.AdjMatrix
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Charpoly.FiniteField

/-!
# The Friendship Theorem

## Definitions and Statement
- A `Friendship` graph is one in which any two distinct vertices have exactly one neighbor in common
- A `Politician`, at least in the context of this problem, is a vertex in a graph which is adjacent
  to every other vertex.
- The friendship theorem (Erdős, Rényi, Sós 1966) states that every finite friendship graph has a
  politician.

## Proof outline
The proof revolves around the theory of adjacency matrices, although some steps could equivalently
be phrased in terms of counting walks.
- Assume `G` is a finite friendship graph.
- First we show that any two nonadjacent vertices have the same degree
- Assume for contradiction that `G` does not have a politician.
- Conclude from the last two points that `G` is `d`-regular for some `d : ℕ`.
- Show that `G` has `d ^ 2 - d + 1` vertices.
- By casework, show that if `d = 0, 1, 2`, then `G` has a politician.
- If `3 ≤ d`, let `p` be a prime factor of `d - 1`.
- If `A` is the adjacency matrix of `G` with entries in `ℤ/pℤ`, we show that `A ^ p` has trace `1`.
- This gives a contradiction, as `A` has trace `0`, and thus `A ^ p` has trace `0`.

## References
- [P. Erdős, A. Rényi, V. Sós, *On A Problem of Graph Theory*][erdosrenyisos]
- [C. Huneke, *The Friendship Theorem*][huneke2002]

-/

namespace Theorems100

noncomputable section

open Finset SimpleGraph Matrix

universe u v

variable {V : Type u} {R : Type v} [Semiring R]

section FriendshipDef

variable (G : SimpleGraph V)

open scoped Classical in
/-- This property of a graph is the hypothesis of the friendship theorem:
every pair of nonadjacent vertices has exactly one common friend,
a vertex to which both are adjacent.
-/
def Friendship [Fintype V] : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃v w : V⦄, v ≠ w → Fintype.card (G.commonNeighbors v w) = 1

/-- A politician is a vertex that is adjacent to all other vertices.
-/
def ExistsPolitician : Prop :=
  ∃ v : V, ∀ w : V, v ≠ w → G.Adj v w

end FriendshipDef

variable [Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} {d : ℕ} (hG : Friendship G)

namespace Friendship

variable (R)

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- One characterization of a friendship graph is that there is exactly one walk of length 2
  between distinct vertices. These walks are counted in off-diagonal entries of the square of
  the adjacency matrix, so for a friendship graph, those entries are all 1. -/
theorem adjMatrix_sq_of_ne {v w : V} (hvw : v ≠ w) :
    (G.adjMatrix R ^ 2 : Matrix V V R) v w = 1 := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- This calculation amounts to counting the number of length 3 walks between nonadjacent vertices.
  We use it to show that nonadjacent vertices have equal degrees. -/
theorem adjMatrix_pow_three_of_not_adj {v w : V} (non_adj : ¬G.Adj v w) :
    (G.adjMatrix R ^ 3 : Matrix V V R) v w = degree G v := by sorry
variable {R}

open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- As `v` and `w` not being adjacent implies
  `degree G v = ((G.adjMatrix R) ^ 3) v w` and `degree G w = ((G.adjMatrix R) ^ 3) v w`,
  the degrees are equal if `((G.adjMatrix R) ^ 3) v w = ((G.adjMatrix R) ^ 3) w v`

  This is true as the adjacency matrix is symmetric. -/
theorem degree_eq_of_not_adj {v w : V} (hvw : ¬G.Adj v w) : degree G v = degree G w := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- Let `A` be the adjacency matrix of a graph `G`.
  If `G` is a friendship graph, then all of the off-diagonal entries of `A^2` are 1.
  If `G` is `d`-regular, then all of the diagonal entries of `A^2` are `d`.
  Putting these together determines `A^2` exactly for a `d`-regular friendship graph. -/
theorem adjMatrix_sq_of_regular (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) :
    G.adjMatrix R ^ 2 = of fun v w => if v = w then (d : R) else (1 : R) := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
theorem adjMatrix_sq_mod_p_of_regular {p : ℕ} (dmod : (d : ZMod p) = 1)
    (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) : G.adjMatrix (ZMod p) ^ 2 = of fun _ _ => 1 := by sorry
section Nonempty

variable [Nonempty V]

open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- If `G` is a friendship graph without a politician (a vertex adjacent to all others), then
  it is regular. We have shown that nonadjacent vertices of a friendship graph have the same degree,
  and if there isn't a politician, we can show this for adjacent vertices by finding a vertex
  neither is adjacent to, and then using transitivity. -/
theorem isRegularOf_not_existsPolitician (hG' : ¬ExistsPolitician G) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, G.IsRegularOfDegree d := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- Let `A` be the adjacency matrix of a `d`-regular friendship graph, and let `v` be a vector
  all of whose components are `1`. Then `v` is an eigenvector of `A ^ 2`, and we can compute
  the eigenvalue to be `d * d`, or as `d + (Fintype.card V - 1)`, so those quantities must be equal.

  This essentially means that the graph has `d ^ 2 - d + 1` vertices. -/
theorem card_of_regular (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) : d + (Fintype.card V - 1) = d * d := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- The size of a `d`-regular friendship graph is `1 mod (d-1)`, and thus `1 mod p` for a
  factor `p ∣ d-1`. -/
theorem card_mod_p_of_regular {p : ℕ} (dmod : (d : ZMod p) = 1) (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) :
    (Fintype.card V : ZMod p) = 1 := by sorry
end Nonempty

open scoped Classical in
theorem adjMatrix_sq_mul_const_one_of_regular (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) :
    G.adjMatrix R * of (fun _ _ => 1) = of (fun _ _ => (d : R)) := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
theorem adjMatrix_mul_const_one_mod_p_of_regular {p : ℕ} (dmod : (d : ZMod p) = 1)
    (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) :
    G.adjMatrix (ZMod p) * of (fun _ _ => 1) = of (fun _ _ => 1) := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- Modulo a factor of `d-1`, the square and all higher powers of the adjacency matrix
  of a `d`-regular friendship graph reduce to the matrix whose entries are all 1. -/
theorem adjMatrix_pow_mod_p_of_regular {p : ℕ} (dmod : (d : ZMod p) = 1)
    (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    G.adjMatrix (ZMod p) ^ k = of (fun _ _ => 1) := by sorry
variable [Nonempty V]

open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- This is the main proof. Assuming that `3 ≤ d`, we take `p` to be a prime factor of `d-1`.
  Then the `p`th power of the adjacency matrix of a `d`-regular friendship graph must have trace 1
  mod `p`, but we can also show that the trace must be the `p`th power of the trace of the original
  adjacency matrix, which is 0, a contradiction.
-/
theorem false_of_three_le_degree (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (h : 3 ≤ d) : False := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- If `d ≤ 1`, a `d`-regular friendship graph has at most one vertex, which is
  trivially a politician. -/
theorem existsPolitician_of_degree_le_one (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (hd1 : d ≤ 1) :
    ExistsPolitician G := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
/-- If `d = 2`, a `d`-regular friendship graph has 3 vertices, so it must be complete graph,
  and all the vertices are politicians. -/
theorem neighborFinset_eq_of_degree_eq_two (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree 2) (v : V) :
    G.neighborFinset v = Finset.univ.erase v := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
theorem existsPolitician_of_degree_eq_two (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree 2) : ExistsPolitician G := by sorry
open scoped Classical in
include hG in
theorem existsPolitician_of_degree_le_two (hd : G.IsRegularOfDegree d) (h : d ≤ 2) :
    ExistsPolitician G := by sorry
end Friendship

include hG in
/-- **Friendship theorem**: We wish to show that a friendship graph has a politician (a vertex
  adjacent to all others). We proceed by contradiction, and assume the graph has no politician.
  We have already proven that a friendship graph with no politician is `d`-regular for some `d`,
  and now we do casework on `d`.
  If the degree is at most 2, we observe by casework that it has a politician anyway.
  If the degree is at least 3, the graph cannot exist. -/
theorem friendship_theorem [Nonempty V] : ExistsPolitician G := by sorry
end

end Theorems100

title: 083_the_friendship_theorem
content:
From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Require Import Friendship.combinatorics.
Require Import Friendship.statement_reduction.


(* Longer version *)
Theorem Friendship'
  (T: finType) (T_nonempty: [set: T] != set0)
  (F (* friendship relation *): rel T) (Fsym: symmetric F) (Firr: irreflexive F)
  (Co: T -> T -> T) (Col: forall u v : T, u != v -> F u (Co u v))
  (Cor: forall u v : T, u != v -> F v (Co u v))
  (CoUnique: forall u v w : T, u != v -> F u w -> F v w -> w = Co u v):
  {u : T | forall v : T, u != v -> F u v}.
Proof.
Admitted.

  
(* Shorter version *)
Theorem Friendship
  (T: finType) (T_nonempty: [set: T] != set0)
  (F (* friendship relation *): rel T) (Fsym: symmetric F) (Firr: irreflexive F) :

  (* u!= v have exactly 1 common friend *)
  (forall (u v: T), u != v -> #|[set w | F u w & F v w]| == 1) ->
  {u : T | forall v : T, u != v -> F u v}.
Proof.
Admitted.

title: 083_the_friendship_theorem
content:
(*
Title: FriendshipTheory.thy
Author:Wenda Li
*)

theory FriendshipTheory 
  imports MoreGraph  "HOL-Number_Theory.Number_Theory"
begin

(*Proofs in this section are the common steps for both combinatorial and algebraic proofs for the
Friendship Theorem*)
section\<open>Common steps\<close>

definition (in valid_unSimpGraph) non_adj :: "'v \<Rightarrow> 'v \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "non_adj v v' \<equiv> v\<in>V \<and> v'\<in>V \<and> v\<noteq>v' \<and> \<not>adjacent v v'" 

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) no_quad:
  assumes "\<And>v u. v\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> u\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> v\<noteq>u \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>! n. adjacent v n \<and> adjacent u n"
  shows "\<not> (\<exists>v1 v2 v3 v4. v2\<noteq>v4 \<and> v1\<noteq>v3 \<and> adjacent v1 v2 \<and> adjacent v2 v3 \<and> adjacent v3 v4 
      \<and> adjacent v4 v1)"
  by sorry

lemma even_card_set: 
  assumes "finite A" and "\<forall>x\<in>A. f x\<in>A \<and> f x\<noteq> x \<and> f (f x)=x"
  shows "even(card A)" using assms
  by sorry

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) even_degree:
  assumes friend_assm:"\<And>v u. v\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> u\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> v\<noteq>u \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>! n. adjacent v n \<and> adjacent u n" 
      and "finite E"
  shows "\<forall>v\<in>V. even(degree v G)"
  by sorry

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) degree_two_windmill:
  assumes friend_assm:"\<And>v u. v\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> u\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> v\<noteq>u \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>! n. adjacent v n \<and> adjacent u n"
      and "finite E" and "card V\<ge>2"
  shows "(\<exists>v\<in>V. degree v G = 2) \<longleftrightarrow>(\<exists>v. \<forall>n\<in>V. n\<noteq>v \<longrightarrow> adjacent v n)"
  by sorry

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) regular:
  assumes friend_assm:"\<And>v u. v\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> u\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> v\<noteq>u \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>! n. adjacent v n \<and> adjacent u n" 
      and "finite E" and "finite V" and "\<not>(\<exists>v\<in>V. degree v G = 2)"
  shows "\<exists>k. \<forall>v\<in>V. degree v G = k"
  by sorry

(*In this section, combinatorial proofs for the Friendship Theorem differ from the algebraic ones.
The main difference between these two approaches is that combinatorial proofs show Lemma 
exist_degree_two by counting the number of paths while algebraic proofs show it by computing
the eigenvalue of adjacency matrices.*)
section\<open>Exclusive steps for combinatorial proofs\<close>

fun (in valid_unSimpGraph) adj_path:: "'v \<Rightarrow> 'v list \<Rightarrow>bool" where
  "adj_path v [] =  (v\<in>V)" 
  | "adj_path v (u#us)= (adjacent v u \<and> adj_path u us)"

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) adj_path_butlast:
  "adj_path v ps \<Longrightarrow> adj_path v (butlast ps)"
  by sorry

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) adj_path_V:
  "adj_path v ps \<Longrightarrow> set ps \<subseteq> V"
  by sorry

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) adj_path_V':
  "adj_path v ps \<Longrightarrow> v\<in> V"
  by sorry

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) adj_path_app:
  "adj_path v ps \<Longrightarrow> ps\<noteq>[] \<Longrightarrow> adjacent (last ps) u \<Longrightarrow> adj_path v (ps@[u])"
  by sorry


lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) adj_path_app':
  "adj_path v (ps @ [q] ) \<Longrightarrow> ps \<noteq> [] \<Longrightarrow> adjacent (last ps) q"
  by sorry

lemma card_partition':
  assumes "\<forall>v\<in>A. card {n. R v n} = k" "k>0" "finite A" 
      "\<forall>v1 v2. v1\<noteq>v2 \<longrightarrow> {n. R v1 n} \<inter> {n. R v2 n}={}"
  shows "card (\<Union>v\<in>A. {n. R v n}) = k * card A"
  by sorry

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) path_count:
  assumes k_adj:"\<And>v. v\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> card {n. adjacent v n} = k" and  "v\<in>V" and "finite V" and "k>0"
  shows "card {ps. length ps=l \<and> adj_path v ps}=k^l"
  by sorry

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) total_v_num:
  assumes friend_assm:"\<And>v u. v\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> u\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> v\<noteq>u \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>! n. adjacent v n \<and> adjacent u n" 
      and "finite E" and "finite V" and "V\<noteq>{}" and " \<forall>v\<in>V. degree v G = k" and "k>0"
  shows "card V= k*k - k +1"
  by sorry

lemma rotate_eq:"rotate1 xs=rotate1 ys \<Longrightarrow> xs=ys" 
  by sorry
  

lemma rotate_diff:"rotate m xs=rotate n xs \<Longrightarrow>rotate (m-n) xs = xs"
  by sorry

lemma (in valid_unSimpGraph) exist_degree_two:
  assumes friend_assm:"\<And>v u. v\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> u\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> v\<noteq>u \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>! n. adjacent v n \<and> adjacent u n"
      and "finite E" and "finite V" and "card V\<ge>2" 
  shows "\<exists>v\<in>V. degree v G = 2"
  by sorry

theorem (in valid_unSimpGraph) friendship_thm:
  assumes friend_assm:"\<And>v u. v\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> u\<in>V \<Longrightarrow> v\<noteq>u \<Longrightarrow> \<exists>! n. adjacent v n \<and> adjacent u n"
      and "finite V" 
  shows "\<exists>v. \<forall>n\<in>V. n\<noteq>v \<longrightarrow> adjacent v n"    
  by sorry

end

083_the_friendship_theorem
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__083, "The Friendship Theorem": every finite simple
;; undirected graph in which each pair of distinct vertices has exactly one
;; common neighbor has a vertex adjacent to every other vertex. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The duplicate-free list VERTICES is the finite carrier.  Each member
;; (u v) of EDGES denotes the ordered adjacency pair from u to v.

(defun ht083-carrier-p (vertices)
  (and (true-listp vertices)
       (no-duplicatesp-equal vertices)))

(defun ht083-edge-recordp (edge vertices)
  (and (true-listp edge)
       (equal (len edge) 2)
       (member-equal (nth 0 edge) vertices)
       (member-equal (nth 1 edge) vertices)))

(defun ht083-edge-listp (edges vertices)
  (if (consp edges)
      (and (ht083-edge-recordp (car edges) vertices)
           (ht083-edge-listp (cdr edges) vertices))
    (equal edges nil)))

(defun ht083-adjacent-p (edges u v)
  (if (member-equal (list u v) edges)
      t
    nil))

(defun ht083-symmetric-p (remaining-edges edges)
  (if (consp remaining-edges)
      (let ((edge (car remaining-edges)))
        (and
         (ht083-adjacent-p
          edges
          (nth 1 edge)
          (nth 0 edge))
         (ht083-symmetric-p (cdr remaining-edges) edges)))
    t))

(defun ht083-irreflexive-p (vertices edges)
  (if (consp vertices)
      (and
       (not (ht083-adjacent-p edges (car vertices) (car vertices)))
       (ht083-irreflexive-p (cdr vertices) edges))
    t))

(defun ht083-common-neighbor-count (u v candidates edges)
  (if (consp candidates)
      (+
       (if (and (ht083-adjacent-p edges u (car candidates))
                (ht083-adjacent-p edges v (car candidates)))
           1
         0)
       (ht083-common-neighbor-count u v (cdr candidates) edges))
    0))

(defun ht083-friendship-row-p (u remaining vertices edges)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (or
        (equal u (car remaining))
        (equal
         (ht083-common-neighbor-count
          u (car remaining) vertices edges)
         1))
       (ht083-friendship-row-p
        u (cdr remaining) vertices edges))
    t))

(defun ht083-friendship-p (remaining vertices edges)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (ht083-friendship-row-p
        (car remaining) vertices vertices edges)
       (ht083-friendship-p (cdr remaining) vertices edges))
    t))

(defun ht083-finite-friendship-graph-p (vertices edges)
  (and
   (ht083-carrier-p vertices)
   (ht083-edge-listp edges vertices)
   (ht083-symmetric-p edges edges)
   (ht083-irreflexive-p vertices edges)
   (ht083-friendship-p vertices vertices edges)))

(defun ht083-politician-p (candidate vertices edges)
  (if (consp vertices)
      (and
       (or
        (equal candidate (car vertices))
        (ht083-adjacent-p edges candidate (car vertices)))
       (ht083-politician-p candidate (cdr vertices) edges))
    t))

(defun ht083-politician-in-list-p
    (remaining vertices edges)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (or
       (ht083-politician-p (car remaining) vertices edges)
       (ht083-politician-in-list-p
        (cdr remaining) vertices edges))
    nil))

(defun ht083-has-politician-p (vertices edges)
  (ht083-politician-in-list-p vertices vertices edges))

(defun hundred-theorems-083-the-friendship-theorem-statement
    (vertices edges)
  (implies
   (and
    (consp vertices)
    (ht083-finite-friendship-graph-p vertices edges))
   (ht083-has-politician-p vertices edges)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 083_the_friendship_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "The Friendship Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 083. This
-- file contains no proof.

module FriendshipTheorem where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; suc)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not proposition = proposition -> Bottom

NotEqual : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
NotEqual left right = Not (left == right)

record Nonempty (A : Set) : Set where
  constructor inhabited
  field
    element : A

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

infixr 3 _and_

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    exists-value : A
    exists-property : P exists-value

record ExistsUnique (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor unique-witness
  field
    unique-value : A
    unique-property : P unique-value
    uniqueness : (other : A) -> P other -> other == unique-value

friendship-theorem : Set₁
friendship-theorem =
  (number-of-vertices : Nat) ->
  (friend : Fin number-of-vertices -> Fin number-of-vertices -> Set) ->
  Nonempty (Fin number-of-vertices) ->
  ((vertex : Fin number-of-vertices) -> Not (friend vertex vertex)) ->
  ((left right : Fin number-of-vertices) ->
    friend left right ->
    friend right left) ->
  ((left right : Fin number-of-vertices) ->
    NotEqual left right ->
    ExistsUnique (Fin number-of-vertices)
      (\ common ->
        friend left common and friend right common)) ->
  Exists (Fin number-of-vertices)
    (\ politician ->
      (other : Fin number-of-vertices) ->
      NotEqual other politician ->
      friend politician other)

title: 083_the_friendship_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact
  hundred-theorems__hol4__083, cataloged as "The Friendship Theorem": every
  finite irreflexive symmetric friendship relation in which each pair of
  distinct vertices has exactly one common friend has a vertex adjacent to
  every other vertex. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory;

val friendship_theorem =
  ``!friend : 'a -> 'a -> bool.
      FINITE (UNIV : 'a set) /\
      (!x. ~friend x x) /\
      (!x y. friend x y ==> friend y x) /\
      (!x y. x <> y ==> ?!z. friend x z /\ friend y z)
      ==>
      ?u. !v. v <> u ==> friend u v``;

  existence of a common neighbor for every pair of distinct vertices.  The

title: 083_the_friendship_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 083, "The Friendship
% Theorem": every finite nonempty simple undirected graph in which each pair of
% distinct vertices has exactly one common neighbor has a vertex adjacent to
% every other vertex. This file contains no proof.

the_friendship_theorem_083[Person: TYPE+]: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[Person]

  nonempty_vertices(vertices: finite_set[Person]): bool =
    EXISTS (person: Person):
      vertices(person)

  irreflexive_on(
      vertices: finite_set[Person],
      friend: [Person, Person -> bool]): bool =
    FORALL (person: Person):
      vertices(person) IMPLIES NOT friend(person, person)

  symmetric_on(
      vertices: finite_set[Person],
      friend: [Person, Person -> bool]): bool =
    FORALL (first, second: Person):
      vertices(first) AND vertices(second) AND friend(first, second)
        IMPLIES friend(second, first)

  has_unique_common_friend(
      vertices: finite_set[Person],
      friend: [Person, Person -> bool],
      first, second: Person): bool =
    EXISTS (common: Person):
      vertices(common)
        AND friend(first, common)
        AND friend(second, common)
        AND
          (FORALL (candidate: Person):
            vertices(candidate)
              AND friend(first, candidate)
              AND friend(second, candidate)
            IMPLIES candidate = common)

  friendship_theorem: bool =
    FORALL (vertices: finite_set[Person]),
           (friend: [Person, Person -> bool]):
      nonempty_vertices(vertices)
        AND irreflexive_on(vertices, friend)
        AND symmetric_on(vertices, friend)
        AND
          (FORALL (first, second: Person):
            vertices(first)
              AND vertices(second)
              AND first /= second
            IMPLIES
              has_unique_common_friend(
                vertices,
                friend,
                first,
                second))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (universal: Person):
          vertices(universal)
            AND
              (FORALL (other: Person):
                vertices(other) AND other /= universal
                  IMPLIES friend(universal, other))
END the_friendship_theorem_083

title: 084_morley_s_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Morley's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 084.
-- The adjacent internal angle trisectors of a nondegenerate real-plane triangle meet in an
-- equilateral triangle. This file contains no proof.

import Mathlib.Geometry.Euclidean.Triangle

open Set

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Theorems100

abbrev Plane := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- Morley's theorem: the intersections of adjacent internal angle trisectors form an
equilateral triangle. -/
theorem morley (a b c p q r : Plane)
    (h_noncollinear : ¬Collinear ℝ ({a, b, c} : Set Plane))
    (h_interior : ({p, q, r} : Set Plane) ⊆ convexHull ℝ ({a, b, c} : Set Plane))
    (h_abr : ∠ a b r = ∠ a b c / 3)
    (h_bar : ∠ b a r = ∠ b a c / 3)
    (h_bcp : ∠ b c p = ∠ b c a / 3)
    (h_cbp : ∠ c b p = ∠ c b a / 3)
    (h_caq : ∠ c a q = ∠ c a b / 3)
    (h_acq : ∠ a c q = ∠ a c b / 3) :
    dist r p = dist p q ∧ dist q r = dist p q := sorry

end Theorems100

title: 084_morley_s_theorem
content:
From HighSchoolGeometry Require Export trigo.
Set  Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
(* Formules de trigonometrie necessaires.*)
 
Lemma prod_sin:
 forall (a b : R),  2 * (sin (a + b) * sin (a - b)) = cos (2 * b) - cos (2 * a).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma sin_3_a: forall (a : R),  sin (3 * a) = sin a * (2 * cos (2 * a) + 1).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma Al_Kashi_sin_cos:
 forall (a b c : R),
 (a + b) + c = pi ->
  Rsqr (sin c) = (Rsqr (sin a) + Rsqr (sin b)) - ((2 * sin a) * sin b) * cos c.
Proof.
Admitted.
(* Definition de pisurtrois et formules de trigonometrie.*)
Parameter pisurtrois : R.
 
Axiom pisurtrois_def : 3 * pisurtrois = pi.
 
Axiom sin_pisurtrois_non_zero : sin pisurtrois <> 0.
 
Lemma cos_2_pisurtrois: 2 * cos (2 * pisurtrois) + 1 = 0.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma sin_3_a_pisurtrois:
 forall (a : R),
  sin (3 * a) = 4 * (sin a * (sin (pisurtrois + a) * sin (pisurtrois - a))).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma Al_Kashi_pisurtrois:
 forall a b c,
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
  Rsqr (sin b) =
  (Rsqr (sin (pisurtrois + a)) + Rsqr (sin (pisurtrois + c))) -
  ((2 * sin (pisurtrois + a)) * sin (pisurtrois + c)) * cos b.
Proof.
Admitted.
From HighSchoolGeometry Require Export cocyclicite.
(* lemme a mettre dans distance_euclidienne apres colinearite_distance*)
 
Lemma distance_double_milieu:
 forall (B C A' : PO), A' = milieu B C ->  distance B C = 2 * distance A' C.
Proof.
Admitted.
(* corollaire du theoreme de l'angle inscrit et de l'angle au centre
   on utilise le triangle rectangle forme par un cote et sa mediatrice*)
 
Lemma demi_angle_centre:
 forall (A B C A' O : PO),
 triangle A B C ->
 O <> A' ->
 A' = milieu B C ->
 circonscrit O A B C ->
  double_AV (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C)) =
  double_AV (cons_AV (vec O A') (vec O C)).
Proof.
Admitted.
(*deux angles ayant des mesures differant d'un multiple de pi ont des sinus egaux ou opposes*)
 
Axiom
   egalite_double_abs_Sin :
   forall A B C E F G,
   double_AV (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C)) =
   double_AV (cons_AV (vec E F) (vec E G)) ->
    Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C))) =
    Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec E F) (vec E G))).

From HighSchoolGeometry Require Export complements_cercle.
(* theoreme : dans un triangle avec les notations habituelles  a = 2 R sin A
   cas particulier : le cote est un diametre du cercle circonscrit*)
 
Lemma diametre_Sinus:
 forall (A B C O : PO),
 triangle A B C ->
 O = milieu B C ->
 circonscrit O A B C ->
  distance B C = 2 * (distance O C * Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C)))).
Proof.
Admitted.
(* cas general*)
 
Lemma rayon_Sinus_general:
 forall (A B C A' O : PO),
 triangle A B C ->
 O <> A' ->
 A' = milieu B C ->
 circonscrit O A B C ->
  distance B C = 2 * (distance O C * Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C)))).
Proof.
Admitted.
(* Ce theoreme montre que dans un triangle  a = 2R sin A  avec les notations habituelles.*)
 
Theorem rayon_Sinus:
 forall A B C O,
 triangle A B C ->
 circonscrit O A B C ->
  distance B C = 2 * (distance O C * Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C)))).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma existence_rayon_circonscrit:
 forall A B C,
 triangle A B C ->
  (exists O : PO , circonscrit O A B C /\ (exists r : R , r = distance O C ) ).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Ltac
soit_rayon_circonscrit A B C O r :=
elim (existence_rayon_circonscrit (A:=A) (B:=B) (C:=C)); [intros O | auto];
 intros toto; elim toto; clear toto; intro; intros toto; elim toto; clear toto;
 intros r; intro.
(* on doit pouvoir le demontrer*)
 
Axiom
   triangle_Sin_not_0 :
   forall A B C, triangle A B C ->  (Sin (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C)) <> 0).
#[export] Hint Resolve triangle_Sin_not_0 :geo.
 
Lemma triangle_abs_Sin_not_0:
 forall A B C,
 triangle A B C ->  (Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C))) <> 0).
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve triangle_abs_Sin_not_0 :geo.
(* Theoreme connu sous le nom de loi des Sinus.*)
 
Theorem loi_Sinus:
 forall A B C,
 triangle A B C ->
  and
   (distance B C / Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C))) =
    distance A B / Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C B))))
   (distance B C / Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C))) =
    distance C A / Rabs (Sin (cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B A)))).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Definition rayon_circonscrit (A B C : PO) (r : R) : Prop :=
   exists O : PO , circonscrit O A B C /\ r = distance O C .
 
Lemma triangle_sin_not_0:
 forall A B C x,
 triangle A B C -> image_angle x = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->  (sin x <> 0).
Proof.
Admitted.
(* consequence de l'enroulement de la droite des reels sur le cercle trigonometrique dans le sens positif*)
 
Axiom sin_pos : forall (x : R), ( 0 <= x <= pi ) ->  (sin x >= 0).
 
Axiom
   non_multiple_pi_triangle :
   forall a A B C,
   ( 0 < a < pi ) ->
   A <> B ->
   A <> C -> image_angle a = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->  triangle A B C.
(* debut de la demonstration du theoreme de Morley*)
 
Lemma pisurtrois_utile:
 forall a b c,
 0 < a -> 0 < b -> 0 < c -> (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->  ( 0 <= 3 * a <= pi ).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma pisurtrois_utile1:
 forall a b c,
 0 < a -> 0 < b -> 0 < c -> (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->  ( 0 <= b + c <= pi ).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma pisurtrois_utile2:
 forall a b c,
 0 < a -> 0 < b -> 0 < c -> (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->  ( 0 <= c <= pi ).
Proof.
Admitted.
#[export] Hint Resolve pisurtrois_utile sin_pos pisurtrois_utile1 pisurtrois_utile2 :geo.
 
Lemma pisurtrois_triangle_utile:
 forall a b c A B C,
 0 < a ->
 0 < b ->
 0 < c ->
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
 A <> B ->
 A <> C -> image_angle (3 * a) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->  triangle A B C.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma pisurtrois_triangle_utile2:
 forall a b c B C P,
 0 < a ->
 0 < b ->
 0 < c ->
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
 B <> C ->
 B <> P -> image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B P) ->  triangle B C P.
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Lemma Rabs_neg: forall (r : R), r <= 0 ->  Rabs r = - r.
Proof.
Admitted.
(* Application des theoremes rayon_Sinus et loi_Sinus dans un triangle forme par un cote et deux trissectrices.
   Calcul de la longueur du cote BP dans le triangle BPC.*)
 
Lemma Morley_1:
 forall (a b c r : R) (A B C P : PO),
 0 < a ->
 0 < b ->
 0 < c ->
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 B <> C ->
 B <> P ->
 rayon_circonscrit A B C r ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B P) ->
 image_angle c = cons_AV (vec C P) (vec C B) ->
 image_angle (3 * a) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->
  distance B P = (2 * (r * sin (3 * a))) * (sin c / sin (pisurtrois - a)).
Proof.
Admitted.
(* application de la formule sin 3 a  qui utilise pisurtrois dons le calcul de BP*)
 
Lemma Morley_2:
 forall (a b c r : R) (A B C P : PO),
 0 < a ->
 0 < b ->
 0 < c ->
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 B <> C ->
 B <> P ->
 rayon_circonscrit A B C r ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B P) ->
 image_angle c = cons_AV (vec C P) (vec C B) ->
 image_angle (3 * a) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->
  distance B P = (8 * (r * sin a)) * (sin c * sin (pisurtrois + a)).
Proof.
Admitted.
(* calcul de la longueur du cote  CP dans le triangle BPC*)
 
Lemma Morley_3:
 forall (a b c r : R) (A B C P : PO),
 0 < a ->
 0 < b ->
 0 < c ->
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 B <> C ->
 B <> P ->
 rayon_circonscrit A B C r ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B P) ->
 image_angle c = cons_AV (vec C P) (vec C B) ->
 image_angle (3 * a) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->
  distance C P = (8 * (r * sin a)) * (sin b * sin (pisurtrois + a)).
Proof.
Admitted.
(* on applique le lemme precedent dans un autre triangle ABQ forme par un cote et deux trissectrices*)
 
Lemma Morley_4:
 forall (a b c r : R) (A B C Q : PO),
 0 < a ->
 0 < b ->
 0 < c ->
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 B <> C ->
 A <> Q ->
 rayon_circonscrit A B C r ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B Q) (vec B A) ->
 image_angle a = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A Q) ->
 image_angle (3 * c) = cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C B) ->
  distance B Q = (8 * (r * sin c)) * (sin a * sin (pisurtrois + c)).
Proof.
Admitted.
(*dans le triangle BPQ on peut caculer le 3eme cote en utilisant Al_Kashi*)
 
Lemma Morley_5:
 forall (a b c r : R) (A B C P Q : PO),
 0 < a ->
 0 < b ->
 0 < c ->
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 B <> C ->
 B <> P ->
 B <> Q ->
 A <> Q ->
 rayon_circonscrit A B C r ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B Q) (vec B A) ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B P) ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B P) (vec B Q) ->
 image_angle c = cons_AV (vec C P) (vec C B) ->
 image_angle a = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A Q) ->
 image_angle (3 * a) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->
 image_angle (3 * c) = cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C B) ->
  Rsqr (distance P Q) =
  (Rsqr 8 * (Rsqr r * (Rsqr (sin a) * Rsqr (sin c)))) *
  ((Rsqr (sin (pisurtrois + a)) + Rsqr (sin (pisurtrois + c))) -
   2 * (sin (pisurtrois + a) * (sin (pisurtrois + c) * cos b))).
Proof.
Admitted.
(* utilisation de la formule de trigonometrie Al_Kashi_pisurtrois pour simplifier le calcul.*)
 
Lemma Morley_6:
 forall (a b c r : R) (A B C P Q : PO),
 0 < a ->
 0 < b ->
 0 < c ->
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 B <> C ->
 B <> P ->
 B <> Q ->
 A <> Q ->
 rayon_circonscrit A B C r ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B Q) (vec B A) ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B P) ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B P) (vec B Q) ->
 image_angle c = cons_AV (vec C P) (vec C B) ->
 image_angle a = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A Q) ->
 image_angle (3 * a) = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A C) ->
 image_angle (3 * c) = cons_AV (vec C A) (vec C B) ->
  Rsqr (distance P Q) =
  (Rsqr 8 * (Rsqr r * (Rsqr (sin a) * Rsqr (sin b)))) * Rsqr (sin c).
Proof.
Admitted.
 
Definition equilateral (A B C : PO) := and (isocele A B C) (isocele B C A).
(*Theoreme de Morley : utilisation de la symetrie de la formule pour conclure.*)
 
Theorem Morley:
 forall (a b c : R) (A B C P Q T : PO),
 0 < a ->
 0 < b ->
 0 < c ->
 (a + b) + c = pisurtrois ->
 A <> B ->
 A <> C ->
 B <> C ->
 B <> P ->
 B <> Q ->
 A <> T ->
 C <> T ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B C) (vec B P) ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B P) (vec B Q) ->
 image_angle b = cons_AV (vec B Q) (vec B A) ->
 image_angle c = cons_AV (vec C P) (vec C B) ->
 image_angle c = cons_AV (vec C T) (vec C P) ->
 image_angle a = cons_AV (vec A B) (vec A Q) ->
 image_angle a = cons_AV (vec A Q) (vec A T) ->
 image_angle a = cons_AV (vec A T) (vec A C) ->  equilateral P Q T.
Proof.
Admitted.
