content:
theory Morley 


imports Complex_Axial_Symmetry 

begin

section \<open>Rotations\<close>

locale complex_rotation =
  fixes A::complex and \<theta>::real
begin

definition \<open>r z = A + (z-A)*cis(\<theta>)\<close>

lemma cmod_inv_rotation:\<open>cmod (z-A) = cmod (r z - A)\<close>
  by sorry

lemma inner_ang:\<open>cos (\<angle> z1 z2)*(cmod z1 *cmod z2) = Re (innerprod z1 z2)\<close>
  by sorry

lemma ang_eq_cos_theta:\<open>z\<noteq>A \<Longrightarrow> cos (angle_c z A (r z)) = cos (\<theta>)\<close>
  by sorry

lemma cdist_dist:\<open>cdist = dist\<close>
  by sorry

lemma ang_eq_theta:assumes h:\<open>z\<noteq>A\<close> shows \<open>angle_c z A (r z) = \<downharpoonright>\<theta>\<downharpoonleft>\<close>
  by sorry

lemma inj_r:\<open>inj r\<close>
  by sorry

lemma img_eqI:\<open>cdist A z1 = cdist A z2 \<and> angle_c z1 A z2 = \<theta> \<Longrightarrow> z2 = r z1\<close>
  by sorry

lemma r_id_iff:\<open>\<downharpoonright>\<theta>\<downharpoonleft> = 0 \<longleftrightarrow> r = id\<close>
  by sorry

end


lemma axial_symmetry_eq:\<open>axial_symmetry B C P = axial_symmetry C B P\<close> if \<open>C\<noteq>B\<close> for C B P
  by sorry

lemma img_r_sym:
  assumes h:\<open>z1 \<noteq> z2\<close> \<open>z \<notin> line z1 z2\<close>
  shows \<open>axial_symmetry z1 z2 z = complex_rotation.r z1 (\<downharpoonright>2*angle_c z z1 z2\<downharpoonleft>) z\<close>
  by sorry

lemma img_r_sym':
  assumes h:\<open>z1 \<noteq> z2\<close> \<open>z\<notin>line z1 z2\<close>
  shows \<open>axial_symmetry z1 z2 z = complex_rotation.r z1 (\<downharpoonright>-2*angle_c z2 z1 z\<downharpoonleft>) z\<close>
  by sorry

lemma equality_for_pqr:
  assumes 1:\<open>(a2::complex)*a3\<noteq>1\<close> and 2:\<open>\<And>z. h z = a3*z + b3\<close> and 3:\<open>\<And>z. g z = a2*z + b2\<close> and 4:\<open>g (h z) = z\<close>
  shows \<open>z = (a2*b3 + b2)/(1-a2*a3)\<close>
  by sorry

lemma equality_for_comp:
  assumes 2:\<open>\<And>z. h z = (a3::complex)*z + b3\<close> and 3:\<open>\<And>z. g z = a2*z + b2\<close> 
    and 4:\<open>\<And>z. f z = a1*z +b1\<close> 
  shows \<open>((f\<circ>f\<circ>f)\<circ>(g\<circ>g\<circ>g)\<circ>(h\<circ>h\<circ>h)) z = (a1*a2*a3)^3*z +(a1^2+a1+1)*b1 +a1^3*(a2^2+a2+1)*b2 
+a1^3*a2^3*(a3^2+a3+1)*b3 \<close>
  by sorry

lemma eq_translation_id:
  assumes \<open>h = complex_rotation.r A 0\<close> \<open>h B = B\<close>
  shows \<open>h = id\<close>
  by sorry

lemma r_eqI: 
  assumes \<open>A = B\<close> \<open>\<theta>1 = \<theta>2\<close> 
  shows \<open>r A \<theta>1 = r B \<theta>2\<close>
  by sorry

lemma r_eqI': 
  assumes \<open>A = B\<close> \<open>\<theta>1 = \<theta>2\<close> 
  shows \<open>r A \<theta>1 z = r B \<theta>2 z\<close>
  by sorry

lemma composed_rotations_same_center:
  shows \<open>(complex_rotation.r A \<theta>1 \<circ> complex_rotation.r A \<theta>2) = complex_rotation.r A (\<theta>1 + \<theta>2)\<close>
  by sorry


lemma composed_rotations:
  assumes h:\<open>\<downharpoonright>\<theta>1 + \<theta>2\<downharpoonleft> \<noteq> 0\<close>
  shows \<open>(complex_rotation.r A \<theta>1 \<circ> complex_rotation.r B \<theta>2) = 
           complex_rotation.r ((A*(1-cis \<theta>1) + B*cis \<theta>1*(1-cis \<theta>2))/(1-cis (\<theta>1+\<theta>2))) (\<theta>1 + \<theta>2)\<close>
  by sorry


lemma composed_rotation_is_trans:
  assumes \<open>\<downharpoonright>\<theta>1 + \<theta>2\<downharpoonleft> = 0\<close>  
  shows \<open>(complex_rotation.r A \<theta>1 \<circ> complex_rotation.r B \<theta>2) z = z + (B - A)*(cis(\<theta>1) - 1)\<close>
  by sorry

section \<open>Morley's theorem\<close>

text \<open>We begin by proving the Morley's theorem in the case where angles are positives
then using the congruence between two triangles with the same angles only not of the same sign
we prove Morley's theorem when angles are negatives.

We then proceed to conclude because in a triangle either angles are all negatives or all the
angles are positives depending on orientation.\<close>

theorem Morley_pos:
  assumes\<open>\<not>collinear A B C\<close>
    \<open>angle_c A B R = angle_c A B C / 3\<close> (is \<open>?abr = ?abc\<close>)
    "angle_c B A R = angle_c B A C / 3" (is \<open>?bar = ?\<alpha>\<close>)
    "angle_c B C P = angle_c B C A / 3" (is \<open>?bcp = ?bca\<close>)
    "angle_c C B P = angle_c C B A / 3" (is \<open>?cbp = ?\<beta>\<close>)
    "angle_c C A Q = angle_c C A B / 3" (is \<open>?caq = ?cab\<close>)
    "angle_c A C Q = angle_c A C B / 3" (is \<open>?acq = ?\<gamma>\<close>)
    and hhh:\<open>\<downharpoonright>angle_c B A C / 3+angle_c C B A / 3+angle_c A C B / 3\<downharpoonleft> = pi/3\<close>
  shows  \<open>cdist R P = cdist P Q \<and> cdist Q R = cdist P Q\<close>
  by sorry

theorem Morley_neg: 
  assumes\<open>\<not>collinear A B C\<close>
    \<open>angle_c A B R = angle_c A B C / 3\<close> (is \<open>?abr = ?abc\<close>)
    "angle_c B A R = angle_c B A C / 3" (is \<open>?bar = ?\<alpha>\<close>)
    "angle_c B C P = angle_c B C A / 3" (is \<open>?bcp = ?bca\<close>)
    "angle_c C B P = angle_c C B A / 3" (is \<open>?cbp = ?\<beta>\<close>)
    "angle_c C A Q = angle_c C A B / 3" (is \<open>?caq = ?cab\<close>)
    "angle_c A C Q = angle_c A C B / 3" (is \<open>?acq = ?\<gamma>\<close>)
    and hhh:\<open>\<downharpoonright>angle_c B A C / 3+angle_c C B A / 3+angle_c A C B / 3\<downharpoonleft> = -pi/3\<close>
  shows  \<open>cdist R P = cdist P Q \<and> cdist Q R = cdist P Q\<close>
  by sorry

theorem Morley:
  assumes\<open>\<not>collinear A B C\<close>
    \<open>angle_c A B R = angle_c A B C / 3\<close> (is \<open>?abr = ?abc\<close>)
    "angle_c B A R = angle_c B A C / 3" (is \<open>?bar = ?\<alpha>\<close>)
    "angle_c B C P = angle_c B C A / 3" (is \<open>?bcp = ?bca\<close>)
    "angle_c C B P = angle_c C B A / 3" (is \<open>?cbp = ?\<beta>\<close>)
    "angle_c C A Q = angle_c C A B / 3" (is \<open>?caq = ?cab\<close>)
    "angle_c A C Q = angle_c A C B / 3" (is \<open>?acq = ?\<gamma>\<close>)
  shows  \<open>cdist R P = cdist P Q \<and> cdist Q R = cdist P Q\<close>
  by sorry

end

title: 084_morley_s_theorem
content:
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* Formalization of Alain Connes's paper "A new proof of Morley's theorem".  *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

needs "Library/iter.ml";;
needs "Multivariate/geom.ml";;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Reflection about the line[0,e^{i t}]                                      *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let reflect2d = new_definition
 `reflect2d t = rotate2d t o cnj o rotate2d(--t)`;;

let REFLECT2D_COMPOSE = `!s t. reflect2d s o reflect2d t = rotate2d (&2 * (s - t))`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Rotation about point "a" by angle "t".                                    *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let rotate_about = new_definition
 `rotate_about a t x = a + rotate2d t (x - a)`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Reflection across line (a,b).                                             *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let reflect_across = new_definition
 `reflect_across (a,b) x = a + reflect2d (Arg(b - a)) (x - a)`;;

let REFLECT_ACROSS_COMPOSE = `!a b c.
        ~(b = a) /\ ~(c = a)
        ==> reflect_across(a,b) o reflect_across(a,c) =
            rotate_about a (&2 * Arg((b - a) / (c - a)))`;;

let REFLECT_ACROSS_COMPOSE_ANGLE = `!a b c.
        ~(b = a) /\ ~(c = a) /\ &0 <= Im((c - a) / (b - a))
        ==> reflect_across(a,c) o reflect_across(a,b) =
            rotate_about a (&2 * angle(c,a,b))`;;

let REFLECT_ACROSS_COMPOSE_INVOLUTION = `!a b. ~(a = b) ==> reflect_across(a,b) o reflect_across(a,b) = I`;;

let REFLECT_ACROSS_SYM = `!a b. reflect_across(a,b) = reflect_across(b,a)`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Some additional lemmas.                                                   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let ITER_ROTATE_ABOUT = `!n a t. ITER n (rotate_about a t) = rotate_about a (&n * t)`;;

let REAL_LE_IM_DIV_CYCLIC = `!a b c. &0 <= Im ((c - a) / (b - a)) <=> &0 <= Im((a - b) / (c - b))`;;

let ROTATE_ABOUT_INVERT = `rotate_about a t w = z <=> w = rotate_about a (--t) z`;;

let ROTATE_EQ_REFLECT_LEMMA = `!a b z t.
        ~(b = a) /\ &2 * Arg((b - a) / (z - a)) = t
        ==> rotate_about a t z = reflect_across (a,b) z`;;

let ROTATE_EQ_REFLECT_PI_LEMMA = `!a b z t.
        ~(b = a) /\ &2 * Arg((b - a) / (z - a)) = &4 * pi + t
        ==> rotate_about a t z = reflect_across (a,b) z`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Algebraic characterization of equilateral triangle.                       *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let EQUILATERAL_TRIANGLE_ALGEBRAIC = `!A B C j.
        j pow 3 = Cx(&1) /\ ~(j = Cx(&1)) /\
        A + j * B + j pow 2 * C = Cx(&0)
        ==> dist(A,B) = dist(B,C) /\ dist(C,A) = dist(B,C)`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* The main algebraic lemma.                                                 *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let AFFINE_GROUP_ITER_3 = `ITER 3 (\z. a * z + b) = (\z. a pow 3 * z + b * (Cx(&1) + a + a pow 2))`;;

let AFFINE_GROUP_COMPOSE = `(\z. a1 * z + b1) o (\z. a2 * z + b2) =
   (\z. (a1 * a2) * z + (b1 + a1 * b2))`;;

let AFFINE_GROUP_I = `I = (\z. Cx(&1) * z + Cx(&0))`;;

let AFFINE_GROUP_EQ = `!a b a' b. (\z. a * z + b) = (\z. a' * z + b') <=> a = a' /\ b = b'`;;

let AFFINE_GROUP_ROTATE_ABOUT = `!a t. rotate_about a t =
         (\z. cexp(ii * Cx(t)) * z + (Cx(&1) - cexp(ii * Cx(t))) * a)`;;

let ALGEBRAIC_LEMMA = `!a1 a2 a3 b1 b2 b3 A B C.
        (\z. a3 * z + b3) ((\z. a1 * z + b1) B) = B /\
        (\z. a1 * z + b1) ((\z. a2 * z + b2) C) = C /\
        (\z. a2 * z + b2) ((\z. a3 * z + b3) A) = A /\
        ITER 3 (\z. a1 * z + b1) o ITER 3 (\z. a2 * z + b2) o
        ITER 3 (\z. a3 * z + b3) = I /\
        ~(a1 * a2 * a3 = Cx(&1)) /\
        ~(a1 * a2 = Cx(&1)) /\
        ~(a2 * a3 = Cx(&1)) /\
        ~(a3 * a1 = Cx(&1))
        ==> (a1 * a2 * a3) pow 3 = Cx (&1) /\
            ~(a1 * a2 * a3 = Cx (&1)) /\
            C + (a1 * a2 * a3) * A + (a1 * a2 * a3) pow 2 * B = Cx(&0)`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* A tactic to avoid some duplication over cyclic permutations.              *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let CYCLIC_PERM_SUBGOAL_THEN =
  let lemma = MESON[]
   `(!A B C P Q R a b c g1 g2 g3.
       Ant A B C P Q R a b c g1 g2 g3 ==> Cns A B C P Q R a b c g1 g2 g3)
    ==> (!A B C P Q R a b c g1 g2 g3.
           Ant A B C P Q R a b c g1 g2 g3
           ==> Ant B C A Q R P b c a g2 g3 g1)
        ==> (!A B C P Q R a b c g1 g2 g3.
                   Ant A B C P Q R a b c g1 g2 g3
                   ==> Cns A B C P Q R a b c g1 g2 g3 /\
                       Cns B C A Q R P b c a g2 g3 g1 /\
                       Cns C A B R P Q c a b g3 g1 g2)`
  and vars =
   [`A:complex`; `B:complex`; `C:complex`;
    `P:complex`; `Q:complex`; `R:complex`;
    `a:real`; `b:real`; `c:real`;
    `g1:complex->complex`; `g2:complex->complex`; `g3:complex->complex`] in
  fun t ttac (asl,w) ->
      let asm = list_mk_conj (map (concl o snd) (rev asl)) in
      let gnw = list_mk_forall(vars,mk_imp(asm,t)) in
      let th1 = MATCH_MP lemma (ASSUME gnw) in
      let tm1 = fst(dest_imp(concl th1)) in
      let th2 = REWRITE_CONV[INSERT_AC; CONJ_ACI; ANGLE_SYM; EQ_SYM_EQ] tm1 in
      let th3 = DISCH_ALL(MP th1 (EQT_ELIM th2)) in
      (MP_TAC th3 THEN ANTS_TAC THENL
        [POP_ASSUM_LIST(K ALL_TAC) THEN REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC;
         DISCH_THEN(MP_TAC o SPEC_ALL) THEN ANTS_TAC THENL
          [REPEAT CONJ_TAC THEN FIRST_ASSUM ACCEPT_TAC;
           DISCH_THEN(CONJUNCTS_THEN2 ttac MP_TAC) THEN
           DISCH_THEN(CONJUNCTS_THEN ttac)]]) (asl,w);;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Morley's theorem a la Connes.                                             *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let MORLEY = `!A B C:real^2 P Q R.
     ~collinear{A,B,C} /\ {P,Q,R} SUBSET convex hull {A,B,C} /\
     angle(A,B,R) = angle(A,B,C) / &3 /\
     angle(B,A,R) = angle(B,A,C) / &3 /\
     angle(B,C,P) = angle(B,C,A) / &3 /\
     angle(C,B,P) = angle(C,B,A) / &3 /\
     angle(C,A,Q) = angle(C,A,B) / &3 /\
     angle(A,C,Q) = angle(A,C,B) / &3
     ==> dist(R,P) = dist(P,Q) /\ dist(Q,R) = dist(P,Q)`;;

title: 084_morley_s_theorem
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 084, "Morley's
;; Theorem": the intersections of adjacent internal angle trisectors of a
;; nondegenerate plane triangle form an equilateral triangle.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Morley's conclusion and the selected-third-angle hypotheses are polynomial
;; in dot products, cross products, and order.  Conservative generic symbols
;; therefore preserve the real-coordinate theorem without restricting its
;; scalars to ACL2's executable rationals.  Every ordered-ring law used by the
;; statement remains an explicit hypothesis.
(defstub ht084-carrier (x) t)
(defstub ht084-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht084-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub ht084-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub ht084-less-op (x y) t)

(defun ht084-member-p (x)
  (if (ht084-carrier x) t nil))

(defun ht084-add (x y)
  (ht084-add-op x y))

(defun ht084-mul (x y)
  (ht084-multiply-op x y))

(defun ht084-neg (x)
  (ht084-negate-op x))

(defun ht084-sub (x y)
  (ht084-add x (ht084-neg y)))

(defun ht084-less (x y)
  (if (ht084-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun ht084-leq (x y)
  (not (ht084-less y x)))

(defun-sk ht084-ring-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht084-member-p x)
      (ht084-member-p y)
      (ht084-member-p z))
     (and
      (ht084-member-p (ht084-add x y))
      (ht084-member-p (ht084-mul x y))
      (ht084-member-p (ht084-neg x))
      (equal (ht084-add (ht084-add x y) z)
             (ht084-add x (ht084-add y z)))
      (equal (ht084-add x y) (ht084-add y x))
      (equal (ht084-add x zero) x)
      (equal (ht084-add x (ht084-neg x)) zero)
      (equal (ht084-mul (ht084-mul x y) z)
             (ht084-mul x (ht084-mul y z)))
      (equal (ht084-mul x y) (ht084-mul y x))
      (equal (ht084-mul x one) x)
      (equal
       (ht084-mul x (ht084-add y z))
       (ht084-add (ht084-mul x y)
                  (ht084-mul x z)))))))

(defun-sk ht084-order-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (ht084-member-p x)
      (ht084-member-p y)
      (ht084-member-p z))
     (and
      (not (ht084-less x x))
      (or (equal x y)
          (ht084-less x y)
          (ht084-less y x))
      (implies
       (and (ht084-less x y)
            (ht084-less y z))
       (ht084-less x z))
      (implies
       (ht084-less x y)
       (ht084-less (ht084-add x z)
                   (ht084-add y z)))
      (implies
       (and (ht084-less zero x)
            (ht084-less zero y))
       (ht084-less zero (ht084-mul x y)))))))

(defun ht084-ordered-ring-p (zero one)
  (and
   (ht084-member-p zero)
   (ht084-member-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (ht084-less zero one)
   (ht084-ring-laws-p zero one)
   (ht084-order-laws-p zero)))

(defun ht084-point-p (point)
  (and
   (true-listp point)
   (equal (len point) 2)
   (ht084-member-p (nth 0 point))
   (ht084-member-p (nth 1 point))))

(defun ht084-all-points-p (points)
  (if (consp points)
      (and
       (ht084-point-p (car points))
       (ht084-all-points-p (cdr points)))
    (equal points nil)))

(defun ht084-square (x)
  (ht084-mul x x))

(defun ht084-three (one)
  (ht084-add one (ht084-add one one)))

(defun ht084-four (one)
  (ht084-add (ht084-add one one)
             (ht084-add one one)))

(defun ht084-orientation (first second third)
  (ht084-sub
   (ht084-mul
    (ht084-sub (nth 0 second) (nth 0 first))
    (ht084-sub (nth 1 third) (nth 1 first)))
   (ht084-mul
    (ht084-sub (nth 1 second) (nth 1 first))
    (ht084-sub (nth 0 third) (nth 0 first)))))

(defun ht084-distance-squared (first second)
  (ht084-add
   (ht084-square
    (ht084-sub (nth 0 first) (nth 0 second)))
   (ht084-square
    (ht084-sub (nth 1 first) (nth 1 second)))))

(defun ht084-in-closed-triangle-p (zero point a b c)
  (let ((abc (ht084-orientation a b c))
        (abp (ht084-orientation a b point))
        (bcp (ht084-orientation b c point))
        (cap (ht084-orientation c a point)))
    (or (and (ht084-less zero abc)
             (ht084-leq zero abp)
             (ht084-leq zero bcp)
             (ht084-leq zero cap))
        (and (ht084-less abc zero)
             (ht084-leq abp zero)
             (ht084-leq bcp zero)
             (ht084-leq cap zero)))))

;; For rays u and w at V, conjugate(u)*w represents the directed angle from
;; u to w.  Cubing conjugate(u)*v gives that full angle exactly when v is an
;; angle trisector.  The strict sector conditions select the internal third.
(defun ht084-angle-third-p (zero one first vertex trisector third)
  (let* ((ux (ht084-sub (nth 0 first) (nth 0 vertex)))
         (uy (ht084-sub (nth 1 first) (nth 1 vertex)))
         (vx (ht084-sub (nth 0 trisector) (nth 0 vertex)))
         (vy (ht084-sub (nth 1 trisector) (nth 1 vertex)))
         (wx (ht084-sub (nth 0 third) (nth 0 vertex)))
         (wy (ht084-sub (nth 1 third) (nth 1 vertex)))
         (z-real (ht084-add (ht084-mul ux vx)
                            (ht084-mul uy vy)))
         (z-imag (ht084-sub (ht084-mul ux vy)
                            (ht084-mul uy vx)))
         (t-real (ht084-add (ht084-mul ux wx)
                            (ht084-mul uy wy)))
         (t-imag (ht084-sub (ht084-mul ux wy)
                            (ht084-mul uy wx)))
         (z-real-squared (ht084-square z-real))
         (z-imag-squared (ht084-square z-imag))
         (z-cubed-real
          (ht084-sub
           (ht084-mul z-real z-real-squared)
           (ht084-mul
            (ht084-three one)
            (ht084-mul z-real z-imag-squared))))
         (z-cubed-imag
          (ht084-sub
           (ht084-mul
            (ht084-three one)
            (ht084-mul z-real-squared z-imag))
           (ht084-mul z-imag z-imag-squared))))
    (and
     (ht084-less zero z-real)
     (ht084-less
      (ht084-add z-real-squared z-imag-squared)
      (ht084-mul (ht084-four one) z-real-squared))
     (equal
      (ht084-sub (ht084-mul z-cubed-real t-imag)
                 (ht084-mul z-cubed-imag t-real))
      zero)
     (ht084-less
      zero
      (ht084-add (ht084-mul z-cubed-real t-real)
                 (ht084-mul z-cubed-imag t-imag))))))

(defun hundred-theorems-084-morleys-theorem-statement
    (zero one a b c p q r)
  (implies
   (and
    (ht084-ordered-ring-p zero one)
    (ht084-all-points-p (list a b c p q r))
    (not (equal (ht084-orientation a b c) zero))
    (ht084-in-closed-triangle-p zero p a b c)
    (ht084-in-closed-triangle-p zero q a b c)
    (ht084-in-closed-triangle-p zero r a b c)
    (ht084-angle-third-p zero one a b r c)
    (ht084-angle-third-p zero one b a r c)
    (ht084-angle-third-p zero one b c p a)
    (ht084-angle-third-p zero one c b p a)
    (ht084-angle-third-p zero one c a q b)
    (ht084-angle-third-p zero one a c q b))
   (and
    (equal (ht084-distance-squared r p)
           (ht084-distance-squared p q))
    (equal (ht084-distance-squared q r)
           (ht084-distance-squared p q)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 084_morley_s_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "Morley's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 084.
-- In the real Euclidean plane, the intersections of adjacent internal angle
-- trisectors of a nondegenerate triangle form an equilateral triangle.
-- This file contains no proof.

module HundredTheorems084 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Natural : Set where
  natZero : Natural
  natSuc  : Natural -> Natural

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zero one : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Natural -> R

    one-not-zero :
      one != zero

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zero == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zero

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x one == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zero == zero
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zero ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == one
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zero == zero

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zero x ->
      lessOrEqual zero y ->
      lessOrEqual zero (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zero one and zero != one

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat natZero == zero
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Natural) -> fromNat (natSuc n) == add (fromNat n) one
    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Natural (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

Positive :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Set
Positive reals x =
  StrictLess reals (zero reals) x

Nonnegative :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Set
Nonnegative reals x =
  lessOrEqual reals (zero reals) x

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

xVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
xVector reals origin endpoint =
  subtract reals
    (x-coordinate endpoint)
    (x-coordinate origin)

yVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
yVector reals origin endpoint =
  subtract reals
    (y-coordinate endpoint)
    (y-coordinate origin)

DotAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
DotAt reals vertex firstRay secondRay =
  add reals
    (multiply reals
      (xVector reals vertex firstRay)
      (xVector reals vertex secondRay))
    (multiply reals
      (yVector reals vertex firstRay)
      (yVector reals vertex secondRay))

CrossAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
CrossAt reals vertex firstRay secondRay =
  subtract reals
    (multiply reals
      (xVector reals vertex firstRay)
      (yVector reals vertex secondRay))
    (multiply reals
      (yVector reals vertex firstRay)
      (xVector reals vertex secondRay))

SquaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
SquaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals (xVector reals p q))
    (square reals (yVector reals p q))

Noncollinear :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
Noncollinear reals a b c =
  CrossAt reals a b c != zero reals

-- Barycentric membership is the target-native form of membership in the
-- convex hull of the three vertices.
TriangleHullMember :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
TriangleHullMember {R} reals a b c p =
  Exists R
    (\ alpha ->
      Exists R
        (\ beta ->
          Exists R
            (\ gamma ->
              Nonnegative reals alpha
              and Nonnegative reals beta
              and Nonnegative reals gamma
              and add reals alpha (add reals beta gamma) == one reals
              and x-coordinate p ==
                add reals
                  (multiply reals alpha (x-coordinate a))
                  (add reals
                    (multiply reals beta (x-coordinate b))
                    (multiply reals gamma (x-coordinate c)))
              and y-coordinate p ==
                add reals
                  (multiply reals alpha (y-coordinate a))
                  (add reals
                    (multiply reals beta (y-coordinate b))
                    (multiply reals gamma (y-coordinate c))))))

SameDirectedAngle :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
SameDirectedAngle {R} reals vertex a b c d =
  Exists R
    (\ scale ->
      Positive reals scale
      and
      DotAt reals vertex a b ==
        multiply reals scale (DotAt reals vertex c d)
      and
      CrossAt reals vertex a b ==
        multiply reals scale (CrossAt reals vertex c d))

SameNonzeroSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
SameNonzeroSign reals x y =
  (Positive reals x and Positive reals y)
  or
  (Positive reals (negate reals x)
   and Positive reals (negate reals y))

TrisectedAngle :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
TrisectedAngle reals vertex firstBoundary firstTrisector secondTrisector secondBoundary =
  firstBoundary != vertex
  and firstTrisector != vertex
  and secondTrisector != vertex
  and secondBoundary != vertex
  and Positive reals
    (DotAt reals vertex firstBoundary firstTrisector)
  and Positive reals
    (DotAt reals vertex firstTrisector secondTrisector)
  and Positive reals
    (DotAt reals vertex secondTrisector secondBoundary)
  and SameNonzeroSign reals
    (CrossAt reals vertex firstBoundary firstTrisector)
    (CrossAt reals vertex firstBoundary secondBoundary)
  and SameDirectedAngle reals
    vertex
    firstBoundary
    firstTrisector
    firstTrisector
    secondTrisector
  and SameDirectedAngle reals
    vertex
    firstTrisector
    secondTrisector
    secondTrisector
    secondBoundary

module MorleyStatement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a b c p q r : Point R) ->
    Noncollinear reals a b c ->
    TriangleHullMember reals a b c p ->
    TriangleHullMember reals a b c q ->
    TriangleHullMember reals a b c r ->
    TrisectedAngle reals b a r p c ->
    TrisectedAngle reals a b r q c ->
    TrisectedAngle reals c b p q a ->
    SquaredDistance reals r p == SquaredDistance reals p q
    and
    SquaredDistance reals q r == SquaredDistance reals p q

morleys-theorem : Set1
morleys-theorem =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  MorleyStatement.proposition reals

title: 084_morley_s_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact
  hundred-theorems__hol4__084, cataloged as "Morley's Theorem": the adjacent
  internal angle trisectors of a nondegenerate real-plane triangle determine
  three points forming an equilateral triangle. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pairTheory realTheory transcTheory;

val morleys_theorem =
  ``let collinear =
      \P Q R : real # real.
        (FST P - FST Q) * (SND R - SND Q) =
        (SND P - SND Q) * (FST R - FST Q)
    in
    let dist =
      \P Q : real # real.
        sqrt ((FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2)
    in
    let angle =
      \P Q R : real # real.
        if P = Q \/ R = Q then
          pi / 2
        else
          acs
            (((FST P - FST Q) * (FST R - FST Q) +
               (SND P - SND Q) * (SND R - SND Q)) /
             (dist P Q * dist R Q))
    in
    let in_triangle =
      \X A B C : real # real.
        ?u v w : real.
          0 <= u /\ 0 <= v /\ 0 <= w /\ u + v + w = 1 /\
          X = (u * FST A + v * FST B + w * FST C,
               u * SND A + v * SND B + w * SND C)
    in
      !A B C P Q R : real # real.
        ~collinear A B C /\
        in_triangle P A B C /\
        in_triangle Q A B C /\
        in_triangle R A B C /\
        angle A B R = angle A B C / 3 /\
        angle B A R = angle B A C / 3 /\
        angle B C P = angle B C A / 3 /\
        angle C B P = angle C B A / 3 /\
        angle C A Q = angle C A B / 3 /\
        angle A C Q = angle A C B / 3
        ==>
        dist R P = dist P Q /\ dist Q R = dist P Q``;

title: 084_morley_s_theorem
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of "Morley's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems
  artifact 084: the intersections of adjacent internal angle trisectors of a
  noncollinear Euclidean triangle form an equilateral triangle. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  HT084R2 is the real Euclidean plane with coordinate index set HT084I.
  HT084Dist is ordinary Euclidean distance, and HT084Angle A B C is the total
  unoriented angle at B, with the same pi/2 convention for a zero ray as the
  HOL Light source. HT084Hull is the convex hull of three points through
  nonnegative barycentric coordinates, and HT084Noncol is planar
  noncollinearity via the two-dimensional determinant.

  The convex-hull hypotheses select the internal trisectors. The six angle
  equalities are the direct HOL Light and Isabelle formulation; they are
  equivalent to the positive angle-chain presentation in the Rocq source
  under the point correspondence (P,Q,T)_Rocq = (P,R,Q)_here. The conclusion
  states the two distance equalities making triangle R P Q equilateral. Every
  declaration below is an unproved $a statement.
$)

$c
  HT084I HT084R2 HT084Dist HT084Dot HT084Angle HT084Hull HT084Noncol
$.

ht084-index-syntax $a class HT084I $.
ht084-plane-syntax $a class HT084R2 $.
ht084-distance-syntax $a class ( HT084Dist A B ) $.
ht084-dot-syntax $a class ( HT084Dot A B C ) $.
ht084-angle-syntax $a class ( HT084Angle A B C ) $.
ht084-hull-syntax $a class ( HT084Hull A B C ) $.
ht084-noncollinear-syntax $a wff ( HT084Noncol A B C ) $.

ht084-index-definition $a |- HT084I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

ht084-plane-definition $a |- HT084R2 = ( RR ^m HT084I ) $.

${
  $d A B k $.

  ht084-distance-definition $a |- (
    HT084Dist A B
  ) = (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      sum_ k e. HT084I
        ( ( ( A ` k ) - ( B ` k ) ) ^ 2 )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d A B C k $.

  ht084-dot-definition $a |- (
    HT084Dot A B C
  ) = (
    sum_ k e. HT084I
      (
        ( ( A ` k ) - ( B ` k ) )
        x.
        ( ( C ` k ) - ( B ` k ) )
      )
  ) $.
$}

ht084-angle-definition $a |- (
  HT084Angle A B C
) = if (
  (
    ( ( HT084Dist A B ) = 0 )
    \/
    ( ( HT084Dist C B ) = 0 )
  )
  ,
  ( _pi / 2 )
  ,
  (
    arccos
    `
    (
      ( HT084Dot A B C )
      /
      (
        ( HT084Dist A B )
        x.
        ( HT084Dist C B )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d A B C k u v w x $.

  ht084-hull-definition $a |- (
    HT084Hull A B C
  ) = {
    x e. HT084R2 |
    E. u e. RR E. v e. RR E. w e. RR
      (
        (
          0 <_ u
          /\
          (
            0 <_ v
            /\
            0 <_ w
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          ( ( u + v ) + w ) = 1
          /\
          x =
            (
              k e. HT084I |->
                (
                  (
                    ( u x. ( A ` k ) )
                    +
                    ( v x. ( B ` k ) )
                  )
                  +
                  ( w x. ( C ` k ) )
                )
            )
        )
      )
  } $.
$}

ht084-noncollinear-definition $a |- (
  ( HT084Noncol A B C )
  <->
  (
    (
      ( ( B ` 1 ) - ( A ` 1 ) )
      x.
      ( ( C ` 2 ) - ( A ` 2 ) )
    )
    =/=
    (
      ( ( B ` 2 ) - ( A ` 2 ) )
      x.
      ( ( C ` 1 ) - ( A ` 1 ) )
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d A B C P Q R $.

  hundred-theorems-084-morley $a |- (
    A. A e. HT084R2
    A. B e. HT084R2
    A. C e. HT084R2
    A. P e. HT084R2
    A. Q e. HT084R2
    A. R e. HT084R2
      (
        (
          (
            ( HT084Noncol A B C )
            /\
            (
              P e. ( HT084Hull A B C )
              /\
              (
                Q e. ( HT084Hull A B C )
                /\
                R e. ( HT084Hull A B C )
              )
            )
          )
          /\
          (
            ( ( HT084Angle A B R ) = ( ( HT084Angle A B C ) / 3 ) )
            /\
            (
              ( ( HT084Angle B A R ) = ( ( HT084Angle B A C ) / 3 ) )
              /\
              (
                ( ( HT084Angle B C P ) = ( ( HT084Angle B C A ) / 3 ) )
                /\
                (
                  ( ( HT084Angle C B P ) = ( ( HT084Angle C B A ) / 3 ) )
                  /\
                  (
                    ( ( HT084Angle C A Q ) = ( ( HT084Angle C A B ) / 3 ) )
                    /\
                    ( ( HT084Angle A C Q ) = ( ( HT084Angle A C B ) / 3 ) )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
          )
        )
        ->
        (
          ( ( HT084Dist R P ) = ( HT084Dist P Q ) )
          /\
          ( ( HT084Dist Q R ) = ( HT084Dist P Q ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

title: 084_morley_s_theorem
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 084,
:: "Morley's Theorem" (hundred-theorems__mizar__084). For a noncollinear
:: Euclidean triangle, three points in its convex hull formed by the adjacent
:: internal angle trisectors determine an equilateral triangle. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ

 vocabularies REAL_1, NAT_1, SUBSET_1, NUMBERS, CARD_1, RELAT_1, ARYTM_3,
      EUCLID, FINSEQ_2, COMPLEX1, ARYTM_1, SQUARE_1, RVSUM_1, FINSEQ_1,

      EUCLID_3, EUCLID_6;

      EUCLID, RELSET_1, BINOP_1, SIN_COS, SIN_COS6, EUCLID_3, EUCLID_6;
 registrations RELSET_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, BINOP_2, MEMBERED, MONOID_0,
      EUCLID, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, SQUARE_1, SIN_COS, SIN_COS6, ORDINAL1;
 requirements NUMERALS, BOOLE, SUBSET, ARITHM, REAL;

 expansions XBOOLE_0, RVSUM_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for A,B,C,P,Q,R being Point of TOP-REAL 2 st
    A,B,C is_a_triangle &
    P in closed_inside_of_triangle(A,B,C) &
    Q in closed_inside_of_triangle(A,B,C) &
    R in closed_inside_of_triangle(A,B,C) &
    arccos (|(A-B,R-B)| / (|.A-B.| * |.R-B.|)) =
      arccos (|(A-B,C-B)| / (|.A-B.| * |.C-B.|)) / 3 &
    arccos (|(B-A,R-A)| / (|.B-A.| * |.R-A.|)) =
      arccos (|(B-A,C-A)| / (|.B-A.| * |.C-A.|)) / 3 &
    arccos (|(B-C,P-C)| / (|.B-C.| * |.P-C.|)) =
      arccos (|(B-C,A-C)| / (|.B-C.| * |.A-C.|)) / 3 &
    arccos (|(C-B,P-B)| / (|.C-B.| * |.P-B.|)) =
      arccos (|(C-B,A-B)| / (|.C-B.| * |.A-B.|)) / 3 &
    arccos (|(C-A,Q-A)| / (|.C-A.| * |.Q-A.|)) =
      arccos (|(C-A,B-A)| / (|.C-A.| * |.B-A.|)) / 3 &
    arccos (|(A-C,Q-C)| / (|.A-C.| * |.Q-C.|)) =
      arccos (|(A-C,B-C)| / (|.A-C.| * |.B-C.|)) / 3
  holds
    |.R-P.| = |.P-Q.| & |.Q-R.| = |.P-Q.|
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 084_morley_s_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Morley's Theorem" from Hundred Theorems item 084. This file
% contains no proof.

morley_s_theorem_084: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) * (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q))
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) * (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q))

  dot_from(O, P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(O)) * (x_coord(Q) - x_coord(O))
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(O)) * (y_coord(Q) - y_coord(O))

  cross_from(O, P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(O)) * (y_coord(Q) - y_coord(O))
      - (y_coord(P) - y_coord(O)) * (x_coord(Q) - x_coord(O))

  collinear(P, Q, R: point): bool =
    cross_from(P, Q, R) = 0

  in_triangle(X, A, B, C: point): bool =
    EXISTS (alpha, beta, gamma: real):
      0 <= alpha
        AND 0 <= beta
        AND 0 <= gamma
        AND alpha + beta + gamma = 1
        AND x_coord(X) =
          alpha * x_coord(A) + beta * x_coord(B) + gamma * x_coord(C)
        AND y_coord(X) =
          alpha * y_coord(A) + beta * y_coord(B) + gamma * y_coord(C)

  positive_length(length: real, P, Q: point): bool =
    0 < length
      AND length * length = squared_distance(P, Q)

  cosine_triple(cosine: real): real =
    4 * cosine * cosine * cosine - 3 * cosine

  sine_triple(sine: real): real =
    3 * sine - 4 * sine * sine * sine

  angle_is_one_third(A, V, X, B: point): bool =
    EXISTS
        (VA_length, VX_length, VB_length, cosine, sine: real):
      positive_length(VA_length, V, A)
        AND positive_length(VX_length, V, X)
        AND positive_length(VB_length, V, B)
        AND 0 <= sine
        AND 1 <= 2 * cosine
        AND cosine * cosine + sine * sine = 1
        AND dot_from(V, A, X) =
          VA_length * VX_length * cosine
        AND abs(cross_from(V, A, X)) =
          VA_length * VX_length * sine
        AND dot_from(V, A, B) =
          VA_length * VB_length * cosine_triple(cosine)
        AND abs(cross_from(V, A, B)) =
          VA_length * VB_length * sine_triple(sine)

  equilateral(P, Q, R: point): bool =
    squared_distance(R, P) = squared_distance(P, Q)
      AND squared_distance(Q, R) = squared_distance(P, Q)

  morley_s_theorem: bool =
    FORALL (A, B, C, P, Q, R: point):
      (NOT collinear(A, B, C)
        AND in_triangle(P, A, B, C)
        AND in_triangle(Q, A, B, C)
        AND in_triangle(R, A, B, C)
        AND angle_is_one_third(A, B, R, C)
        AND angle_is_one_third(B, A, R, C)
        AND angle_is_one_third(B, C, P, A)
        AND angle_is_one_third(C, B, P, A)
        AND angle_is_one_third(C, A, Q, B)
        AND angle_is_one_third(A, C, Q, B))
      IMPLIES equilateral(P, Q, R)
END morley_s_theorem_084

title: 085_divisibility_by_3_rule
content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2020 Kim Morrison. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Kim Morrison, Shing Tak Lam, Mario Carneiro
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Data.List.Palindrome
public import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Digits.Lemmas

/-!
# Divisibility tests for natural numbers in terms of digits.

We prove some divisibility tests based on digits, in particular completing
Theorem #85 from https://www.cs.ru.nl/~freek/100/.

-/

public section

namespace Nat

variable {n : ℕ}

theorem modEq_three_digits_sum (n : ℕ) : n ≡ (digits 10 n).sum [MOD 3] :=
  modEq_digits_sum 3 10 (by simp) n

theorem modEq_nine_digits_sum (n : ℕ) : n ≡ (digits 10 n).sum [MOD 9] :=
  modEq_digits_sum 9 10 (by simp) n

theorem modEq_eleven_digits_sum (n : ℕ) :
    n ≡ ((digits 10 n).map fun n : ℕ => (n : ℤ)).alternatingSum [ZMOD 11] := by sorry
theorem dvd_iff_dvd_digits_sum (b b' : ℕ) (h : b' % b = 1) (n : ℕ) :
    b ∣ n ↔ b ∣ (digits b' n).sum := by sorry
theorem three_dvd_iff (n : ℕ) : 3 ∣ n ↔ 3 ∣ (digits 10 n).sum :=
  dvd_iff_dvd_digits_sum 3 10 (by simp) n

theorem nine_dvd_iff (n : ℕ) : 9 ∣ n ↔ 9 ∣ (digits 10 n).sum :=
  dvd_iff_dvd_digits_sum 9 10 (by simp) n

theorem dvd_iff_dvd_ofDigits (b b' : ℕ) (c : ℤ) (h : (b : ℤ) ∣ (b' : ℤ) - c) (n : ℕ) :
    b ∣ n ↔ (b : ℤ) ∣ ofDigits c (digits b' n) := by sorry
theorem eleven_dvd_iff :
    11 ∣ n ↔ (11 : ℤ) ∣ ((digits 10 n).map fun n : ℕ => (n : ℤ)).alternatingSum := by sorry
theorem eleven_dvd_of_palindrome (p : (digits 10 n).Palindrome) (h : Even (digits 10 n).length) :
    11 ∣ n := by sorry
end Nat

Require Import ZArith.
Require Import Znumtheory.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Fixpoint sumdigits n (f : nat -> Z) :=
  match n with
  | O => f O
  | S n => f (S n) + sumdigits n f
  end.

Fixpoint number n (f : nat -> Z) :=
  match n with
  | O => f O
  | S n => f (S n) + 10 * number n f
  end.

Theorem div3 : forall n d,
  (number n d) mod 3 = (sumdigits n d) mod 3.
Proof.
Admitted.

title: 085_divisibility_by_3_rule
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of the divisibility-by-3 rule from Hundred
  Theorems item 085. The left side is a base-10 numeral with digits d i, and
  the right side is its digit sum. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory Divisibility_By_3_Rule
  imports Main
begin

theorem divisibility_by_3:
  fixes d :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
    and n :: nat
  shows "(3::nat) dvd (\<Sum>i\<le>n. 10 ^ i * d i) \<longleftrightarrow>
    3 dvd (\<Sum>i\<le>n. d i)"
  sorry

end

title: 085_divisibility_by_3_rule
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__085, "Divisibility by 3 Rule": the base-10 value
;; of any finite integer coefficient sequence has the same residue modulo 3
;; as its coefficient sum, so both are divisible by 3 together; equivalently,
;; a natural number is divisible by 3 exactly when its decimal digit sum is.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; COEFFICIENTS is ordered least-significant first.  For every source function
;; d and bound n, the list (d(0), ..., d(n)) gives the same base-10 polynomial
;; and coefficient sum; conversely, every nonempty integer list extends to such
;; a total integer-valued function.  The empty list also represents the decimal
;; digit list of zero.

(defun ht085-integer-listp (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and (integerp (car coefficients))
           (ht085-integer-listp (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun ht085-coefficient-sum (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (car coefficients)
         (ht085-coefficient-sum (cdr coefficients)))
    0))

(defun ht085-base10-value (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (car coefficients)
         (* 10
            (ht085-base10-value (cdr coefficients))))
    0))

(defun ht085-decimal-digit-sum-aux (fuel n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or (zp fuel)
          (zp n))
      0
    (+ (mod n 10)
       (ht085-decimal-digit-sum-aux
        (- fuel 1)
        (floor n 10)))))

(defun ht085-decimal-digit-sum (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (ht085-decimal-digit-sum-aux (+ n 1) n)
    0))

(defun ht085-divisible-by-3-p (x)
  (and (integerp x)
       (equal (mod x 3) 0)))

(defun hundred-theorems-085-divisibility-by-3-rule-statement
    (coefficients n)
  (and
   (implies
    (ht085-integer-listp coefficients)
    (let ((value (ht085-base10-value coefficients))
          (sum (ht085-coefficient-sum coefficients)))
      (and
       (equal (mod value 3)
              (mod sum 3))
       (equal (ht085-divisible-by-3-p value)
              (ht085-divisible-by-3-p sum)))))
   (implies
    (natp n)
    (equal
     (ht085-divisible-by-3-p n)
     (ht085-divisible-by-3-p
      (ht085-decimal-digit-sum n))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of "Divisibility by 3 Rule" from Hundred Theorems item 085. This
-- file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _∣_
infix 2 _↔_
infixr 8 _^_

record _∣_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : divisor * quotient ≡ dividend

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

_^_ : Nat → Nat → Nat
base ^ zero = 1
base ^ suc exponent = base * (base ^ exponent)

sumThrough : Nat → (Nat → Nat) → Nat
sumThrough zero term = term zero
sumThrough (suc n) term =
  sumThrough n term + term (suc n)

divisibility-by-3-rule : Set
divisibility-by-3-rule =
  (n : Nat) →
  (digits : Nat → Nat) →
  (3 ∣ sumThrough n (λ i → (10 ^ i) * digits i))
    ↔ (3 ∣ sumThrough n digits)

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of "Divisibility by 3 Rule" for corpus artifact
:: hundred-theorems__mizar__085. For every finite prefix of an arbitrary
:: natural-number coefficient function, its base-10 weighted sum is congruent
:: modulo 3 to its ordinary sum, hence the two sums are divisible by 3
:: equivalently. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies NUMBERS, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, TARSKI, CARD_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, ORDINAL1, NEWTON, REALSET1, INT_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3,
    CARD_3;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, NEWTON, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, FINSEQ_1, RVSUM_1, FINSEQ_2, NAT_1, NAT_D, WSIERP_1;
  constructors REAL_1, NAT_D, NEWTON, RELSET_1, NUMBERS, RVSUM_1,
    FINSEQOP, FUNCT_2, WSIERP_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XREAL_0, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    RVSUM_1, NEWTON, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, CARD_1, RELSET_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat, d being Function of NAT,NAT
  for weighted, plain being FinSequence of NAT st
    len weighted = n + 1 &
    len plain = n + 1 &
    (for k being Nat st k <= n holds
      weighted.(k + 1) = ((10 qua Nat) |^ k) * d.k &
      plain.(k + 1) = d.k)
  holds
    (Sum weighted) mod 3 = (Sum plain) mod 3 &
    (3 divides Sum weighted iff 3 divides Sum plain)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: 085_divisibility_by_3_rule
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Divisibility by 3 Rule" from Hundred
% Theorems item 085: a finite base-ten numeral is divisible by three exactly
% when the sum of its digits is divisible by three. This file contains no proof.

divisibility_by_3_rule_085: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat): value = divisor * quotient

  digit_sum(digits: [nat -> nat], last: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF last = 0 THEN
      digits(0)
    ELSE
      digit_sum(digits, last - 1) + digits(last)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE last

  decimal_value(digits: [nat -> nat], last: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF last = 0 THEN
      digits(0)
    ELSE
      decimal_value(digits, last - 1) + (10 ^ last) * digits(last)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE last

  divisibility_by_3_rule: bool =
    FORALL (digits: [nat -> nat]), (last: nat):
      nat_divides(3, decimal_value(digits, last))
        IFF nat_divides(3, digit_sum(digits, last))

END divisibility_by_3_rule_085

title: 086_lebesgue_measure_and_integration
content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2018 Mario Carneiro. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Mario Carneiro, Johannes Hölzl
-/
module

public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.SimpleFunc
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Pi

/-!
# Lower Lebesgue integral for `ℝ≥0∞`-valued functions

We define the lower Lebesgue integral of an `ℝ≥0∞`-valued function.

## Notation

We introduce the following notation for the lower Lebesgue integral of a function `f : α → ℝ≥0∞`.

* `∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ`: integral of a function `f : α → ℝ≥0∞` with respect to a measure `μ`;
* `∫⁻ x, f x`: integral of a function `f : α → ℝ≥0∞` with respect to the canonical measure
  `volume` on `α`;
* `∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ`: integral of a function `f : α → ℝ≥0∞` over a set `s` with respect
  to a measure `μ`, defined as `∫⁻ x, f x ∂(μ.restrict s)`;
* `∫⁻ x in s, f x`: integral of a function `f : α → ℝ≥0∞` over a set `s` with respect
  to the canonical measure `volume`, defined as `∫⁻ x, f x ∂(volume.restrict s)`.
-/

@[expose] public section

assert_not_exists Module.Basis Norm MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac

open Set hiding restrict restrict_apply

open Filter ENNReal Topology NNReal

namespace MeasureTheory

local infixr:25 " →ₛ " => SimpleFunc

variable {α β γ : Type*}

open SimpleFunc

variable {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ ν : Measure α} {s : Set α}

/-- The **lower Lebesgue integral** of a function `f` with respect to a measure `μ`. -/
noncomputable irreducible_def lintegral (μ : Measure α) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (g : α →ₛ ℝ≥0∞) (_ : ⇑g ≤ f), g.lintegral μ

/-! In the notation for integrals, an expression like `∫⁻ x, g ‖x‖ ∂μ` will not be parsed correctly,
  and needs parentheses. We do not set the binding power of `r` to `0`, because then
  `∫⁻ x, f x = 0` will be parsed incorrectly. -/

@[inherit_doc MeasureTheory.lintegral]
notation3 "∫⁻ "(...)", "r:60:(scoped f => f)" ∂"μ:70 => lintegral μ r

@[inherit_doc MeasureTheory.lintegral]
notation3 "∫⁻ "(...)", "r:60:(scoped f => lintegral volume f) => r

@[inherit_doc MeasureTheory.lintegral]
notation3"∫⁻ "(...)" in "s", "r:60:(scoped f => f)" ∂"μ:70 => lintegral (Measure.restrict μ s) r

@[inherit_doc MeasureTheory.lintegral]
notation3"∫⁻ "(...)" in "s", "r:60:(scoped f => lintegral (Measure.restrict volume s) f) => r

theorem SimpleFunc.lintegral_eq_lintegral {m : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α →ₛ ℝ≥0∞) (μ : Measure α) :
    ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = f.lintegral μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_mono' {m : MeasurableSpace α} ⦃μ ν : Measure α⦄ (hμν : μ ≤ ν) ⦃f g : α → ℝ≥0∞⦄
    (hfg : f ≤ g) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a, g a ∂ν := by sorry
theorem lintegral_mono ⦃f g : α → ℝ≥0∞⦄ (hfg : f ≤ g) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ :=
  lintegral_mono' (le_refl μ) hfg

theorem lintegral_mono_nnreal {f g : α → ℝ≥0} (h : f ≤ g) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ :=
  lintegral_mono fun a => ENNReal.coe_le_coe.2 (h a)

theorem iSup_lintegral_measurable_le_eq_lintegral (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ⨆ (g : α → ℝ≥0∞) (_ : Measurable g) (_ : g ≤ f), ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_mono_set {_ : MeasurableSpace α} ⦃μ : Measure α⦄ {s t : Set α} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞}
    (hst : s ⊆ t) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x in t, f x ∂μ :=
  lintegral_mono' (Measure.restrict_mono hst (le_refl μ)) (le_refl f)

theorem lintegral_mono_set' {_ : MeasurableSpace α} ⦃μ : Measure α⦄ {s t : Set α} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞}
    (hst : s ≤ᵐ[μ] t) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x in t, f x ∂μ :=
  lintegral_mono' (Measure.restrict_mono' hst (le_refl μ)) (le_refl f)

theorem monotone_lintegral {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (μ : Measure α) : Monotone (lintegral μ) :=
  lintegral_mono

@[simp]
theorem lintegral_const (c : ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ _, c ∂μ = c * μ univ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_zero : ∫⁻ _ : α, 0 ∂μ = 0 := by simp

theorem lintegral_zero_fun : lintegral μ (0 : α → ℝ≥0∞) = 0 :=
  lintegral_zero

theorem lintegral_one : ∫⁻ _, (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μ = μ univ := by rw [lintegral_const, one_mul]

theorem setLIntegral_const (s : Set α) (c : ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ _ in s, c ∂μ = c * μ s := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_one (s) : ∫⁻ _ in s, 1 ∂μ = μ s := by rw [setLIntegral_const, one_mul]

lemma iInf_mul_le_lintegral (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : (⨅ x, f x) * μ .univ ≤ ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ := by sorry
lemma lintegral_le_iSup_mul (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ ≤ (⨆ x, f x) * μ .univ := by sorry
variable (μ) in
/-- For any function `f : α → ℝ≥0∞`, there exists a measurable function `g ≤ f` with the same
integral. -/
theorem exists_measurable_le_lintegral_eq (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∃ g : α → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ g ≤ f ∧ ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_eq_nnreal {m : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (μ : Measure α) :
    ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ =
      ⨆ (φ : α →ₛ ℝ≥0) (_ : ∀ x, ↑(φ x) ≤ f x), (φ.map ((↑) : ℝ≥0 → ℝ≥0∞)).lintegral μ := by sorry
theorem exists_simpleFunc_forall_lintegral_sub_lt_of_pos {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h : ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ ≠ ∞)
    {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : ε ≠ 0) :
    ∃ φ : α →ₛ ℝ≥0,
      (∀ x, ↑(φ x) ≤ f x) ∧
        ∀ ψ : α →ₛ ℝ≥0, (∀ x, ↑(ψ x) ≤ f x) → (map (↑) (ψ - φ)).lintegral μ < ε := by sorry
theorem iSup_lintegral_le {ι : Sort*} (f : ι → α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ⨆ i, ∫⁻ a, f i a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a, ⨆ i, f i a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem iSup₂_lintegral_le {ι : Sort*} {ι' : ι → Sort*} (f : ∀ i, ι' i → α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ⨆ (i) (j), ∫⁻ a, f i j a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a, ⨆ (i) (j), f i j a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem le_iInf_lintegral {ι : Sort*} (f : ι → α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a, ⨅ i, f i a ∂μ ≤ ⨅ i, ∫⁻ a, f i a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem le_iInf₂_lintegral {ι : Sort*} {ι' : ι → Sort*} (f : ∀ i, ι' i → α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a, ⨅ (i) (h : ι' i), f i h a ∂μ ≤ ⨅ (i) (h : ι' i), ∫⁻ a, f i h a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_mono_ae {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, f a ≤ g a) :
    ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_mono_ae {s : Set α} {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hg : AEMeasurable g (μ.restrict s))
    (hfg : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ s → f x ≤ g x) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x in s, g x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_mono {s : Set α} {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hg : Measurable g)
    (hfg : ∀ x ∈ s, f x ≤ g x) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x in s, g x ∂μ :=
  setLIntegral_mono_ae hg.aemeasurable (ae_of_all _ hfg)

theorem setLIntegral_mono_ae' {s : Set α} {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    (hfg : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ s → f x ≤ g x) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x in s, g x ∂μ :=
  lintegral_mono_ae <| (ae_restrict_iff' hs).2 hfg

theorem setLIntegral_mono' {s : Set α} {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    (hfg : ∀ x ∈ s, f x ≤ g x) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x in s, g x ∂μ :=
  setLIntegral_mono_ae' hs (ae_of_all _ hfg)

theorem setLIntegral_le_lintegral (s : Set α) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ :=
  lintegral_mono' Measure.restrict_le_self le_rfl

lemma iInf_mul_le_setLIntegral (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (⨅ x ∈ s, f x) * μ s ≤ ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ := by sorry
lemma setLIntegral_le_iSup_mul (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ ≤ (⨆ x ∈ s, f x) * μ s := by sorry
theorem lintegral_congr_ae {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h : f =ᵐ[μ] g) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ :=
  le_antisymm (lintegral_mono_ae <| h.le) (lintegral_mono_ae <| h.symm.le)

theorem lintegral_congr {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h : ∀ a, f a = g a) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, g a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_congr {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} {s t : Set α} (h : s =ᵐ[μ] t) :
    ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ = ∫⁻ x in t, f x ∂μ := by rw [Measure.restrict_congr_set h]

theorem setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    (hfg : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ s → f x = g x) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ = ∫⁻ x in s, g x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_congr_fun {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    (hfg : EqOn f g s) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ = ∫⁻ x in s, g x ∂μ :=
  setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae hs <| Eventually.of_forall hfg

lemma setLIntegral_eq_zero {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (h's : EqOn f 0 s) :
    ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ = 0 := by sorry
theorem lintegral_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h : f =ᵐ[μ] 0) :
    ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = 0 :=
  (lintegral_congr_ae h).trans lintegral_zero

/-- The Lebesgue integral is zero iff the function is a.e. zero.

The measurability assumption is necessary, otherwise there are counterexamples: for instance, the
conclusion fails if `f` is the characteristic function of a Vitali set. -/
@[simp]
theorem lintegral_eq_zero_iff' {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) :
    ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = 0 ↔ f =ᵐ[μ] 0 := by sorry
theorem lintegral_eq_zero_iff {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = 0 ↔ f =ᵐ[μ] 0 :=
  lintegral_eq_zero_iff' hf.aemeasurable

/-- The measurability assumption is necessary, otherwise there are counterexamples: for instance,
the conclusion fails if `s = univ` and `f` is the characteristic function of a Vitali set. -/
theorem setLIntegral_eq_zero_iff' {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s)
    {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEMeasurable f (μ.restrict s)) :
    ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ = 0 ↔ ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ s → f x = 0 :=
  (lintegral_eq_zero_iff' hf).trans (ae_restrict_iff' hs)

theorem setLIntegral_eq_zero_iff {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) {f : α → ℝ≥0∞}
    (hf : Measurable f) : ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ = 0 ↔ ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ s → f x = 0 :=
  setLIntegral_eq_zero_iff' hs hf.aemeasurable

theorem lintegral_pos_iff_support {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) :
    (0 < ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ) ↔ 0 < μ (Function.support f) := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_pos_iff {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) {s : Set α} :
    0 < ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ ↔ 0 < μ (Function.support f ∩ s) := by sorry
end

/-- If `f` has finite integral, then `∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ` is absolutely continuous in `s`: it tends
to zero as `μ s` tends to zero. This lemma states this fact in terms of `ε` and `δ`. -/
theorem exists_pos_setLIntegral_lt_of_measure_lt {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h : ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ ≠ ∞) {ε : ℝ≥0∞}
    (hε : ε ≠ 0) : ∃ δ > 0, ∀ s, μ s < δ → ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ < ε := by sorry
theorem tendsto_setLIntegral_zero {ι} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (h : ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ ≠ ∞) {l : Filter ι}
    {s : ι → Set α} (hl : Tendsto (μ ∘ s) l (𝓝 0)) :
    Tendsto (fun i => ∫⁻ x in s i, f x ∂μ) l (𝓝 0) := by sorry
theorem lintegral_smul_measure {R : Type*} [SMul R ℝ≥0∞] [IsScalarTower R ℝ≥0∞ ℝ≥0∞]
    (c : R) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ a, f a ∂c • μ = c • ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ := by sorry
lemma setLIntegral_smul_measure {R : Type*} [SMul R ℝ≥0∞] [IsScalarTower R ℝ≥0∞ ℝ≥0∞]
    (c : R) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (s : Set α) :
    ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂(c • μ) = c • ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_zero_measure {m : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a, f a ∂(0 : Measure α) = 0 := by sorry
theorem lintegral_add_measure (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (μ ν : Measure α) :
    ∫⁻ a, f a ∂(μ + ν) = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a, f a ∂ν := by sorry
theorem lintegral_finset_sum_measure {ι} (s : Finset ι) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (μ : ι → Measure α) :
    ∫⁻ a, f a ∂(∑ i ∈ s, μ i) = ∑ i ∈ s, ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ i :=
  let F : Measure α →+ ℝ≥0∞ :=
    { toFun := (lintegral · f),
      map_zero' := lintegral_zero_measure f,
      map_add' := lintegral_add_measure f }
  map_sum F μ s

@[simp]
theorem lintegral_sum_measure {m : MeasurableSpace α} {ι} (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (μ : ι → Measure α) :
    ∫⁻ a, f a ∂Measure.sum μ = ∑' i, ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ i := by sorry
theorem hasSum_lintegral_measure {ι} {_ : MeasurableSpace α} (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (μ : ι → Measure α) :
    HasSum (fun i => ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ i) (∫⁻ a, f a ∂Measure.sum μ) :=
  (lintegral_sum_measure f μ).symm ▸ ENNReal.summable.hasSum

@[simp]
theorem lintegral_of_isEmpty {α} [MeasurableSpace α] [IsEmpty α] (μ : Measure α) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ = 0 := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_empty (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ x in ∅, f x ∂μ = 0 := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_univ (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ x in univ, f x ∂μ = ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_measure_zero (s : Set α) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (hs' : μ s = 0) :
    ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ = 0 := by sorry
theorem lintegral_rw₁ {f f' : α → β} (h : f =ᵐ[μ] f') (g : β → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a, g (f a) ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, g (f' a) ∂μ :=
  lintegral_congr_ae <| h.mono fun a h => by dsimp only; rw [h]

-- TODO: Need a better way of rewriting inside of an integral
theorem lintegral_rw₂ {f₁ f₁' : α → β} {f₂ f₂' : α → γ} (h₁ : f₁ =ᵐ[μ] f₁') (h₂ : f₂ =ᵐ[μ] f₂')
    (g : β → γ → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ a, g (f₁ a) (f₂ a) ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, g (f₁' a) (f₂' a) ∂μ :=
  lintegral_congr_ae <| h₁.mp <| h₂.mono fun _ h₂ h₁ => by dsimp only; rw [h₁, h₂]

theorem lintegral_indicator_le (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (s : Set α) :
    ∫⁻ a, s.indicator f a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_indicator {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a, s.indicator f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ := by sorry
lemma setLIntegral_indicator {s t : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a in t, s.indicator f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a in s ∩ t, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_indicator₀ {s : Set α} (hs : NullMeasurableSet s μ) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a, s.indicator f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ := by sorry
lemma setLIntegral_indicator₀ (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) {s t : Set α}
    (hs : NullMeasurableSet s (μ.restrict t)) :
    ∫⁻ a in t, s.indicator f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a in s ∩ t, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_indicator_const_le (s : Set α) (c : ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a, s.indicator (fun _ => c) a ∂μ ≤ c * μ s :=
  (lintegral_indicator_le _ _).trans (setLIntegral_const s c).le

theorem lintegral_indicator_const₀ {s : Set α} (hs : NullMeasurableSet s μ) (c : ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a, s.indicator (fun _ => c) a ∂μ = c * μ s := by sorry
theorem lintegral_indicator_const {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (c : ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a, s.indicator (fun _ => c) a ∂μ = c * μ s :=
  lintegral_indicator_const₀ hs.nullMeasurableSet c

lemma setLIntegral_eq_of_support_subset {s : Set α} {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hsf : f.support ⊆ s) :
    ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ = ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_eq_const {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) (r : ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ x in { x | f x = r }, f x ∂μ = r * μ { x | f x = r } := by sorry
theorem lintegral_indicator_one_le (s : Set α) : ∫⁻ a, s.indicator 1 a ∂μ ≤ μ s :=
  (lintegral_indicator_const_le _ _).trans <| (one_mul _).le

@[simp]
theorem lintegral_indicator_one₀ {s : Set α} (hs : NullMeasurableSet s μ) :
    ∫⁻ a, s.indicator 1 a ∂μ = μ s :=
  (lintegral_indicator_const₀ hs _).trans <| one_mul _

theorem lintegral_indicator_one {s : Set α} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    ∫⁻ a, s.indicator 1 a ∂μ = μ s := by sorry
theorem Measure.ext_iff_lintegral (ν : Measure α) :
    μ = ν ↔ ∀ f : α → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable f → ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂ν := by sorry
theorem Measure.ext_of_lintegral (ν : Measure α)
    (hμν : ∀ f : α → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable f → ∫⁻ a, f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a, f a ∂ν) : μ = ν :=
  (μ.ext_iff_lintegral ν).mpr hμν

open Measure

open scoped Function -- required for scoped `on` notation

theorem lintegral_iUnion₀ [Countable β] {s : β → Set α} (hm : ∀ i, NullMeasurableSet (s i) μ)
    (hd : Pairwise (AEDisjoint μ on s)) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a in ⋃ i, s i, f a ∂μ = ∑' i, ∫⁻ a in s i, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_iUnion [Countable β] {s : β → Set α} (hm : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (s i))
    (hd : Pairwise (Disjoint on s)) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a in ⋃ i, s i, f a ∂μ = ∑' i, ∫⁻ a in s i, f a ∂μ :=
  lintegral_iUnion₀ (fun i => (hm i).nullMeasurableSet) hd.aedisjoint f

theorem lintegral_biUnion₀ {t : Set β} {s : β → Set α} (ht : t.Countable)
    (hm : ∀ i ∈ t, NullMeasurableSet (s i) μ) (hd : t.Pairwise (AEDisjoint μ on s)) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a in ⋃ i ∈ t, s i, f a ∂μ = ∑' i : t, ∫⁻ a in s i, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_biUnion {t : Set β} {s : β → Set α} (ht : t.Countable)
    (hm : ∀ i ∈ t, MeasurableSet (s i)) (hd : t.PairwiseDisjoint s) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a in ⋃ i ∈ t, s i, f a ∂μ = ∑' i : t, ∫⁻ a in s i, f a ∂μ :=
  lintegral_biUnion₀ ht (fun i hi => (hm i hi).nullMeasurableSet) hd.aedisjoint f

theorem lintegral_biUnion_finset₀ {s : Finset β} {t : β → Set α}
    (hd : Set.Pairwise (↑s) (AEDisjoint μ on t)) (hm : ∀ b ∈ s, NullMeasurableSet (t b) μ)
    (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) : ∫⁻ a in ⋃ b ∈ s, t b, f a ∂μ = ∑ b ∈ s, ∫⁻ a in t b, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_biUnion_finset {s : Finset β} {t : β → Set α} (hd : Set.PairwiseDisjoint (↑s) t)
    (hm : ∀ b ∈ s, MeasurableSet (t b)) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a in ⋃ b ∈ s, t b, f a ∂μ = ∑ b ∈ s, ∫⁻ a in t b, f a ∂μ :=
  lintegral_biUnion_finset₀ hd.aedisjoint (fun b hb => (hm b hb).nullMeasurableSet) f

theorem lintegral_iUnion_le [Countable β] (s : β → Set α) (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    ∫⁻ a in ⋃ i, s i, f a ∂μ ≤ ∑' i, ∫⁻ a in s i, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_union {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} {A B : Set α} (hB : MeasurableSet B) (hAB : Disjoint A B) :
    ∫⁻ a in A ∪ B, f a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a in A, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a in B, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_union_le (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (s t : Set α) :
    ∫⁻ a in s ∪ t, f a ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a in t, f a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_inter_add_diff {B : Set α} (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set α) (hB : MeasurableSet B) :
    ∫⁻ x in A ∩ B, f x ∂μ + ∫⁻ x in A \ B, f x ∂μ = ∫⁻ x in A, f x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_add_compl (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) {A : Set α} (hA : MeasurableSet A) :
    ∫⁻ x in A, f x ∂μ + ∫⁻ x in Aᶜ, f x ∂μ = ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ := by sorry
lemma lintegral_piecewise (hs : MeasurableSet s) (f g : α → ℝ≥0∞) [∀ j, Decidable (j ∈ s)] :
    ∫⁻ a, s.piecewise f g a ∂μ = ∫⁻ a in s, f a ∂μ + ∫⁻ a in sᶜ, g a ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_compl {f : α → ℝ≥0∞} {s : Set α} (hsm : MeasurableSet s)
    (hfs : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ ≠ ∞) :
    ∫⁻ x in sᶜ, f x ∂μ = ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ - ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_iUnion_of_directed {ι : Type*} [Countable ι]
    (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) {s : ι → Set α} (hd : Directed (· ⊆ ·) s) :
    ∫⁻ x in ⋃ i, s i, f x ∂μ = ⨆ i, ∫⁻ x in s i, f x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem lintegral_max {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) (hg : Measurable g) :
    ∫⁻ x, max (f x) (g x) ∂μ =
      ∫⁻ x in { x | f x ≤ g x }, g x ∂μ + ∫⁻ x in { x | g x < f x }, f x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_max {f g : α → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) (hg : Measurable g) (s : Set α) :
    ∫⁻ x in s, max (f x) (g x) ∂μ =
      ∫⁻ x in s ∩ { x | f x ≤ g x }, g x ∂μ + ∫⁻ x in s ∩ { x | g x < f x }, f x ∂μ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_lt_top_of_le_nnreal {s : Set α} (hs : μ s ≠ ∞) {f : α → ℝ≥0∞}
    (hbdd : ∃ y : ℝ≥0, ∀ x ∈ s, f x ≤ y) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ < ∞ := by sorry
theorem setLIntegral_lt_top_of_bddAbove {s : Set α} (hs : μ s ≠ ∞) {f : α → ℝ≥0}
    (hbdd : BddAbove (f '' s)) : ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ < ∞ :=
  setLIntegral_lt_top_of_le_nnreal hs <| hbdd.imp fun _M hM _x hx ↦
    ENNReal.coe_le_coe.2 <| hM (mem_image_of_mem f hx)

theorem setLIntegral_lt_top_of_isCompact [TopologicalSpace α] {s : Set α}
    (hs : μ s ≠ ∞) (hsc : IsCompact s) {f : α → ℝ≥0} (hf : Continuous f) :
    ∫⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ < ∞ :=
  setLIntegral_lt_top_of_bddAbove hs (hsc.image hf).bddAbove

end MeasureTheory

title: 086_lebesgue_measure_and_integration
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Lebesgue Measure and Integration" from
  Hundred Theorems artifact 086. It specifies Borel and Lebesgue measure,
  nonnegative and signed Lebesgue integrals, and their principal convergence,
  sigma-finite product-integration, and local differentiation laws.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals List ClassicalDescription.

Set Implicit Arguments.
#[local] Open Scope R_scope.

Definition set (A : Type) := A -> Prop.

Definition empty_set {A : Type} : set A :=
  fun _ => False.

Definition full_set {A : Type} : set A :=
  fun _ => True.

Definition set_complement {A : Type} (E : set A) : set A :=
  fun x => ~ E x.

Definition countable_union {A : Type} (E : nat -> set A) : set A :=
  fun x => exists n : nat, E n x.

Definition same_set {A : Type} (E F : set A) : Prop :=
  forall x : A, E x <-> F x.

Definition disjoint_sets {A : Type} (E F : set A) : Prop :=
  forall x : A, ~ (E x /\ F x).

Definition pairwise_disjoint {A : Type} (E : nat -> set A) : Prop :=
  forall i j : nat, i <> j -> disjoint_sets (E i) (E j).

Definition sigma_class {A : Type} (C : set (set A)) : Prop :=
  C empty_set /\
  (forall E : set A, C E -> C (set_complement E)) /\
  (forall E : nat -> set A,
      (forall n : nat, C (E n)) ->
      C (countable_union E)).

Definition open_real_set (U : set R) : Prop :=
  forall x : R,
    U x ->
    exists epsilon : R,
      0 < epsilon /\
      forall y : R, Rabs (y - x) < epsilon -> U y.

Definition borel_set (E : set R) : Prop :=
  forall C : set (set R),
    sigma_class C ->
    (forall U : set R, open_real_set U -> C U) ->
    C E.

Inductive extended_nonnegative : Type :=
| ennreal_finite :
    forall value : R, 0 <= value -> extended_nonnegative
| ennreal_infinity : extended_nonnegative.

Arguments ennreal_finite value nonnegative : clear implicits.

Definition ennreal_zero : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite 0 (Rle_refl 0).

Definition ennreal_one : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite 1 Rle_0_1.

Record nonnegative_real : Type := {
  nnreal_value : R;
  nnreal_nonnegative : 0 <= nnreal_value
}.

Definition ennreal_of_nonnegative
    (x : nonnegative_real) : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite (nnreal_value x) (nnreal_nonnegative x).

Definition ennreal_represents
    (x : extended_nonnegative) (value : R) : Prop :=
  exists nonnegative : 0 <= value,
    x = ennreal_finite value nonnegative.

Definition ennreal_finite_value (x : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  exists value : R, ennreal_represents x value.

Definition ennreal_le
    (x y : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  match x, y with
  | ennreal_finite a _, ennreal_finite b _ => a <= b
  | ennreal_finite _ _, ennreal_infinity => True
  | ennreal_infinity, ennreal_finite _ _ => False
  | ennreal_infinity, ennreal_infinity => True
  end.

Definition ennreal_add
  (x y : extended_nonnegative) : extended_nonnegative :=
  match x, y with
  | ennreal_finite a a_nonnegative,
    ennreal_finite b b_nonnegative =>
      ennreal_finite (a + b)
        (Rplus_le_le_0_compat a b a_nonnegative b_nonnegative)
  | _, _ => ennreal_infinity
  end.

Definition ennreal_mul
  (x y : extended_nonnegative) : extended_nonnegative :=
  match x, y with
  | ennreal_finite a a_nonnegative,
    ennreal_finite b b_nonnegative =>
      ennreal_finite (a * b)
        (Rmult_le_pos a b a_nonnegative b_nonnegative)
  | ennreal_finite a _, ennreal_infinity
  | ennreal_infinity, ennreal_finite a _ =>
      if Req_EM_T a 0 then ennreal_zero else ennreal_infinity
  | ennreal_infinity, ennreal_infinity => ennreal_infinity
  end.

Definition ennreal_scale
    (c x : extended_nonnegative) : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_mul c x.

Fixpoint ennreal_partial_sum
    (u : nat -> extended_nonnegative) (n : nat) : extended_nonnegative :=
  match n with
  | O => ennreal_zero
  | S k => ennreal_add (ennreal_partial_sum u k) (u k)
  end.

Definition ennreal_supremum
    (values : extended_nonnegative -> Prop)
    (bound : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  (forall value : extended_nonnegative,
      values value -> ennreal_le value bound) /\
  (forall upper : extended_nonnegative,
      (forall value : extended_nonnegative,
          values value -> ennreal_le value upper) ->
      ennreal_le bound upper).

Definition ennreal_series_sum
    (u : nat -> extended_nonnegative)
    (sum : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  ennreal_supremum
    (fun value =>
      exists n : nat, value = ennreal_partial_sum u n)
    sum.

Record measure_space (A : Type) := {
  measurable : set A -> Prop;
  measurable_empty : measurable empty_set;
  measurable_complement :
    forall E : set A,
      measurable E ->
      measurable (set_complement E);
  measurable_countable_union :
    forall E : nat -> set A,
      (forall n : nat, measurable (E n)) ->
      measurable (countable_union E);
  measure : set A -> extended_nonnegative;
  measure_extensional :
    forall E F : set A,
      same_set E F ->
      measure E = measure F;
  measure_empty : measure empty_set = ennreal_zero;
  measure_countable_additive :
    forall E : nat -> set A,
      (forall n : nat, measurable (E n)) ->
      pairwise_disjoint E ->
      ennreal_series_sum
        (fun n => measure (E n))
        (measure (countable_union E))
}.

Definition is_borel_measure (mu : measure_space R) : Prop :=
  forall E : set R, measurable mu E <-> borel_set E.

Definition half_open_interval (a b : R) : set R :=
  fun x => a <= x < b.

Definition is_lebesgue_measure (mu : measure_space R) : Prop :=
  is_borel_measure mu /\
  forall a b : R,
    a <= b ->
    ennreal_represents
      (measure mu (half_open_interval a b)) (b - a).

Theorem lebesgue_measure_exists_unique :
  exists mu : measure_space R,
    is_lebesgue_measure mu /\
    forall nu : measure_space R,
      is_lebesgue_measure nu ->
      forall E : set R,
        borel_set E ->
        measure mu E = measure nu E.
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition ennreal_below
    (x : extended_nonnegative) (bound : R) : Prop :=
  match x with
  | ennreal_finite value _ => value < bound
  | ennreal_infinity => False
  end.

Definition measurable_ennreal_function {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (f : A -> extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  forall bound : R,
    measurable mu (fun x => ennreal_below (f x) bound).

Definition measurable_real_function {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (f : A -> R) : Prop :=
  forall bound : R,
    measurable mu (fun x => f x < bound).

Definition finite_partition {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A)
    (n : nat) (cells : nat -> set A) : Prop :=
  (0 < n)%nat /\
  (forall i : nat, (i < n)%nat -> measurable mu (cells i)) /\
  (forall i j : nat,
      (i < n)%nat ->
      (j < n)%nat ->
      i <> j ->
      disjoint_sets (cells i) (cells j)) /\
  (forall x : A,
      exists i : nat, (i < n)%nat /\ cells i x).

Definition simple_integral_below {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A)
    (f : A -> extended_nonnegative)
    (value : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  exists (n : nat)
         (coefficients : nat -> nonnegative_real)
         (cells : nat -> set A),
    finite_partition mu n cells /\
    (forall (x : A) (i : nat),
      (i < n)%nat ->
      cells i x ->
      ennreal_le (ennreal_of_nonnegative (coefficients i)) (f x)) /\
    value =
      ennreal_partial_sum
        (fun i =>
          ennreal_scale
            (ennreal_of_nonnegative (coefficients i))
            (measure mu (cells i)))
        n.

Definition lintegral_has_value {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A)
    (f : A -> extended_nonnegative)
    (value : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  ennreal_supremum (simple_integral_below mu f) value.

Definition ennreal_indicator {A : Type}
    (E : set A) (f : A -> extended_nonnegative)
    (x : A) : extended_nonnegative :=
  if excluded_middle_informative (E x) then f x else ennreal_zero.

Definition set_lintegral_has_value {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (E : set A)
    (f : A -> extended_nonnegative)
    (value : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  lintegral_has_value mu (ennreal_indicator E f) value.

Theorem lintegral_exists :
  forall (A : Type) (mu : measure_space A)
         (f : A -> extended_nonnegative),
    exists value : extended_nonnegative,
      lintegral_has_value mu f value.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem lintegral_unique :
  forall (A : Type) (mu : measure_space A)
         (f : A -> extended_nonnegative)
         (left right : extended_nonnegative),
    lintegral_has_value mu f left ->
    lintegral_has_value mu f right ->
    left = right.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem lintegral_indicator_one :
  forall (A : Type) (mu : measure_space A) (E : set A),
    measurable mu E ->
    lintegral_has_value
      mu (ennreal_indicator E (fun _ => ennreal_one))
      (measure mu E).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem lintegral_monotone :
  forall (A : Type) (mu : measure_space A)
         (f g : A -> extended_nonnegative)
         (f_integral g_integral : extended_nonnegative),
    (forall x : A, ennreal_le (f x) (g x)) ->
    lintegral_has_value mu f f_integral ->
    lintegral_has_value mu g g_integral ->
    ennreal_le f_integral g_integral.
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem lintegral_add :
  forall (A : Type) (mu : measure_space A)
         (f g : A -> extended_nonnegative)
         (f_integral g_integral : extended_nonnegative),
    measurable_ennreal_function mu f ->
    measurable_ennreal_function mu g ->
    lintegral_has_value mu f f_integral ->
    lintegral_has_value mu g g_integral ->
    lintegral_has_value mu
      (fun x => ennreal_add (f x) (g x))
      (ennreal_add f_integral g_integral).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem lintegral_scale :
  forall (A : Type) (mu : measure_space A)
         (f : A -> extended_nonnegative)
         (c value : extended_nonnegative),
    measurable_ennreal_function mu f ->
    lintegral_has_value mu f value ->
    lintegral_has_value mu
      (fun x => ennreal_scale c (f x))
      (ennreal_scale c value).
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition pointwise_ennreal_monotone {A : Type}
    (f : nat -> A -> extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  forall (n : nat) (x : A),
    ennreal_le (f n x) (f (S n) x).

Definition pointwise_ennreal_supremum {A : Type}
    (f : nat -> A -> extended_nonnegative)
    (limit : A -> extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  forall x : A,
    ennreal_supremum
      (fun value =>
        exists n : nat, value = f n x)
      (limit x).

Theorem lintegral_monotone_convergence :
  forall (A : Type) (mu : measure_space A)
         (f : nat -> A -> extended_nonnegative)
         (limit : A -> extended_nonnegative)
         (integrals : nat -> extended_nonnegative)
         (limit_integral : extended_nonnegative),
    (forall n : nat, measurable_ennreal_function mu (f n)) ->
    pointwise_ennreal_monotone f ->
    pointwise_ennreal_supremum f limit ->
    (forall n : nat, lintegral_has_value mu (f n) (integrals n)) ->
    ennreal_supremum
      (fun value =>
        exists n : nat, value = integrals n)
      limit_integral ->
    lintegral_has_value mu limit limit_integral.
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition positive_part (x : R) : R :=
  Rmax x 0.

Definition negative_part (x : R) : R :=
  Rmax (- x) 0.

Definition absolute_ennreal (x : R) : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite (Rabs x) (Rabs_pos x).

Definition positive_ennreal (x : R) : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite (positive_part x) (Rmax_r x 0).

Definition negative_ennreal (x : R) : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite (negative_part x) (Rmax_r (- x) 0).

Definition integrable {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (f : A -> R) : Prop :=
  measurable_real_function mu f /\
  exists value : extended_nonnegative,
    lintegral_has_value mu (fun x => absolute_ennreal (f x)) value /\
    ennreal_finite_value value.

Definition lebesgue_integral_has_value {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (f : A -> R) (value : R) : Prop :=
  measurable_real_function mu f /\
  exists (positive_integral negative_integral : extended_nonnegative)
         (positive_value negative_value : R),
    lintegral_has_value mu
      (fun x => positive_ennreal (f x)) positive_integral /\
    lintegral_has_value mu
      (fun x => negative_ennreal (f x)) negative_integral /\
    ennreal_represents positive_integral positive_value /\
    ennreal_represents negative_integral negative_value /\
    value = positive_value - negative_value.

Definition real_indicator {A : Type}
    (E : set A) (f : A -> R) (x : A) : R :=
  if excluded_middle_informative (E x) then f x else 0.

Definition set_integral_has_value {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (E : set A)
    (f : A -> R) (value : R) : Prop :=
  lebesgue_integral_has_value mu (real_indicator E f) value.

Definition integrable_on {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (E : set A) (f : A -> R) : Prop :=
  integrable mu (real_indicator E f).

Theorem integrable_has_unique_integral :
  forall (A : Type) (mu : measure_space A) (f : A -> R),
    integrable mu f ->
