Require Import Lists.List.
Require Import ZArith.
Require Import Setoid.
Require Import Coq.Classes.Morphisms.
Require Import Lia.

Open Scope Z_scope.
Import ListNotations.

(**

 Short proof of the inclusion-exclusion principle, which gives the
 cardinality of a finite union of finite sets as an alternating sum of
 cardinalities of the intersections of those sets.

 We choose a formalization of finite sets particularly well suited for
 our purposes: [X] is the universe, or support, of the base sets. We
 suppose the union is finite, and hence we assume a list [enum_X] to
 enumerate all the elements that are in all the considered sets.  In
 fact, we only use [enum_X] to define a constructive [cardinal]
 function, so if enum_X happens to enumerate some elements several
 times, the theorem still holds, which means that it also works if the
 cardinality is "weighted".
 
 Finally, the finiteness of the set of sets is enforced by using a
 list of sets, in which we do not require each set to be unique, so
 the inclusion-exclusion principle also works for a multiset of sets.

*)

Section InclusionExclusion.

Variable X : Set.
Variable enum_X : list X.

Definition set := X -> bool.

Definition cardinal (A : set) := Z.of_nat (length (filter A enum_X)).

Definition empty_set : set := fun _ => false.

Definition binary_union (A B : set) x := orb (A x) (B x).

Definition binary_intersection (A B : set) x := andb (A x) (B x).

Infix " ∪ " := binary_union (at level 50).

Infix " ∩ " := binary_intersection (at level 50).

Notation " # " := cardinal.

Lemma cardinal_union_lemma A B : # (A ∪ B) = # A + # B - # (A ∩ B).
Proof.
Admitted.

Definition list_union (A : list set) :=
  fold_right binary_union empty_set A.

Definition fold1 {A} (f : A -> A -> A) (l : list A) (default : A) :=
  match l with
  | nil => default
  | x :: xs => fold_right f x xs
  end.

Definition list_intersection (A : list set) :=
  fold1 binary_intersection A empty_set.

Definition set_eq (A B : set) := forall x, A x = B x.
Infix " == " := set_eq (at level 90).

Lemma set_eq_refl : Reflexive set_eq.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma set_eq_sym : Symmetric set_eq.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma set_eq_trans : Transitive set_eq.
Proof.
Admitted.

Add Parametric Relation : set set_eq
    reflexivity proved by set_eq_refl
    symmetry proved by set_eq_sym
    transitivity proved by set_eq_trans
      as Set_eq.

Instance union_morphism :
  Proper (set_eq ==> set_eq ==> set_eq) binary_union | 10.
Proof.
Admitted.

Instance intersection_morphism :
  Proper (set_eq ==> set_eq ==> set_eq) binary_intersection | 10.
Proof.
Admitted.

Instance cardinal_morphism :
  Proper (set_eq ==> @eq Z) cardinal | 10.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma cardinal_set_eq (A B : set) : A == B -> # A = # B.
Proof.
Admitted.

Ltac iftac :=
  let x := fresh "x" in
  intro x; compute;
  repeat
    match goal with
      |- context [ if ?b x then _ else _] => destruct b
    end; try reflexivity.

Ltac Rewrite H :=
  let E := fresh "E" in
  assert (E : H) by iftac; rewrite E; clear E.

Lemma cardinal_ternary_union A B C :
  # (A ∪ B ∪ C) = # A + # B + # C - # (A ∩ B) - #(B ∩ C) - # (C ∩ A) + #(A ∩ B ∩ C).
Proof.
Admitted.

Fixpoint sublists {A} (xs : list A) : list (list A) :=
  match xs with
  | nil => [[]]
  | x :: xs =>
    let xss := sublists xs in
    xss ++ (map (fun l => x :: l)) xss
  end.

Definition nonempty {A} (xs : list A) :=
  match xs with
    [] => false
  | _ :: _ => true
  end.

Fixpoint sum l :=
  match l with
  | nil => 0
  | x :: l => x + sum l
  end.

Fixpoint alternating_sign n :=
  match n with
  | O => 1
  | S n => - alternating_sign n
  end.

Lemma cardinal_empty : cardinal empty_set = 0.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma sum_app l1 l2 : sum (l1 ++ l2) = sum l1 + sum l2.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma filter_app {A} f (l1 l2 : list A) :
  filter f (l1 ++ l2) = filter f l1 ++ filter f l2.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma filter_map_always {A B} f (g : A -> B) l :
  (forall x, f (g x) = true) ->
  filter f (map g l) = map g l.
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma sublists_proper {A} (l : list A) :
  sublists l = [] :: filter nonempty (sublists l).
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma sublists_map {A B} (f : A -> B) l :
  sublists (map f l) = map (map f) (sublists l).
Proof.
Admitted.

Theorem inclusion_exclusion (l : list set) :
  cardinal (list_union l) =
  sum
    (map (fun l' => cardinal (list_intersection l') *
                 alternating_sign (1 + length l'))
         (filter nonempty (sublists l))).
Proof.
Admitted.

End InclusionExclusion.

Arguments list_union [X].
Arguments list_intersection [X].
Arguments cardinal [X] [enum_X].

(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 096, "Principle of
  Inclusion / Exclusion". It states the alternating-sum formula for the
  cardinality of a finite union of finitely indexed finite sets. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory Principle_of_Inclusion_Exclusion
  imports Main
begin

theorem principle_of_inclusion_exclusion:
  fixes A :: "'i set"
    and X :: "'i \<Rightarrow> 'a set"
  assumes "finite A"
    and "\<And>i. i \<in> A \<Longrightarrow> finite (X i)"
  shows "int (card (\<Union>(X ` A))) =
    (\<Sum>B | B \<subseteq> A \<and> B \<noteq> {}.
      (-1) ^ (card B + 1) * int (card (\<Inter>(X ` B))))"
  sorry

end

title: 096_principle_of_inclusion___exclusion
content:
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* Inclusion-exclusion principle, the usual and generalized forms.           *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Simple set theory lemmas.                                                 *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let SUBSET_INSERT_EXISTS = `!s x:A t. s SUBSET (x INSERT t) <=>
                s SUBSET t \/ ?u. u SUBSET t /\ s = x INSERT u`;;

let FINITE_SUBSETS_RESTRICT = `!s:A->bool p. FINITE s ==> FINITE {t | t SUBSET s /\ p t}`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Versions for additive real functions, where the additivity applies only   *)
(* to some specific subsets (e.g. cardinality of finite sets, measurable     *)
(* sets with bounded measure).                                               *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let INCLUSION_EXCLUSION_REAL_RESTRICTED_INDEXED = `!P (f:(A->bool)->real) (A:I->bool) (x:I->(A->bool)).
        (!s t. P s /\ P t /\ DISJOINT s t
               ==> f(s UNION t) = f(s) + f(t)) /\
        P {} /\
        (!s t. P s /\ P t ==> P(s INTER t) /\ P(s UNION t) /\ P(s DIFF t)) /\
        FINITE A /\ (!a. a IN A ==> P(x a))
        ==> f(UNIONS(IMAGE x A)) =
            sum {B | B SUBSET A /\ ~(B = {})}
                (\B. (-- &1) pow (CARD B + 1) * f(INTERS(IMAGE x B)))`;;

let INCLUSION_EXCLUSION_REAL_RESTRICTED = `!P (f:(A->bool)->real) (A:(A->bool)->bool).
        (!s t. P s /\ P t /\ DISJOINT s t
               ==> f(s UNION t) = f(s) + f(t)) /\
        P {} /\
        (!s t. P s /\ P t ==> P(s INTER t) /\ P(s UNION t) /\ P(s DIFF t)) /\
        FINITE A /\ (!a. a IN A ==> P(a))
        ==> f(UNIONS A) =
            sum {B | B SUBSET A /\ ~(B = {})}
                (\B. (-- &1) pow (CARD B + 1) * f(INTERS B))`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Versions for unrestrictedly additive functions.                           *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let INCLUSION_EXCLUSION_REAL_INDEXED = `!(f:(A->bool)->real) (A:I->bool) (x:I->(A->bool)).
        (!s t. DISJOINT s t ==> f(s UNION t) = f(s) + f(t)) /\ FINITE A
        ==> f(UNIONS(IMAGE x A)) =
            sum {B | B SUBSET A /\ ~(B = {})}
                (\B. (-- &1) pow (CARD B + 1) * f(INTERS(IMAGE x B)))`;;

let INCLUSION_EXCLUSION_REAL = `!(f:(A->bool)->real) (A:(A->bool)->bool).
        (!s t. DISJOINT s t ==> f(s UNION t) = f(s) + f(t)) /\ FINITE A
        ==> f(UNIONS A) =
            sum {B | B SUBSET A /\ ~(B = {})}
                (\B. (-- &1) pow (CARD B + 1) * f(INTERS B))`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Special case of cardinality, the most common case.                        *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let INCLUSION_EXCLUSION = `!s:(A->bool)->bool.
        FINITE s /\ (!k. k IN s ==> FINITE k)
        ==> &(CARD(UNIONS s)) =
                sum {t | t SUBSET s /\ ~(t = {})}
                    (\t. (-- &1) pow (CARD t + 1) * &(CARD(INTERS t)))`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* A more conventional form.                                                 *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let INCLUSION_EXCLUSION_USUAL = `!s:(A->bool)->bool.
        FINITE s /\ (!k. k IN s ==> FINITE k)
        ==> &(CARD(UNIONS s)) =
                sum (1..CARD s) (\n. (-- &1) pow (n + 1) *
                                     sum {t | t SUBSET s /\ t HAS_SIZE n}
                                         (\t. &(CARD(INTERS t))))`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* A combinatorial lemma about subsets of a finite set.                      *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let FINITE_SUBSETS_RESTRICT = `!s:A->bool p. FINITE s ==> FINITE {t | t SUBSET s /\ p t}`;;

let CARD_ADJUST_LEMMA = `!f:A->B s x y.
        FINITE s /\
        (!x y. x IN s /\ y IN s /\ f x = f y ==> x = y) /\
        x = y + CARD (IMAGE f s)
        ==> x = y + CARD s`;;

let CARD_SUBSETS_STEP = `!x:A s. FINITE s /\ ~(x IN s) /\ u SUBSET s
           ==> CARD {t | t SUBSET (x INSERT s) /\ u SUBSET t /\ ODD(CARD t)} =
                 CARD {t | t SUBSET s /\ u SUBSET t /\ ODD(CARD t)} +
                 CARD {t | t SUBSET s /\ u SUBSET t /\ EVEN(CARD t)} /\
               CARD {t | t SUBSET (x INSERT s) /\ u SUBSET t /\ EVEN(CARD t)} =
                 CARD {t | t SUBSET s /\ u SUBSET t /\ EVEN(CARD t)} +
                 CARD {t | t SUBSET s /\ u SUBSET t /\ ODD(CARD t)}`;;

let CARD_SUBSUPERSETS_EVEN_ODD = `!s u:A->bool.
        FINITE u /\ s PSUBSET u
        ==> CARD {t | s SUBSET t /\ t SUBSET u /\ EVEN(CARD t)} =
            CARD {t | s SUBSET t /\ t SUBSET u /\ ODD(CARD t)}`;;

let SUM_ALTERNATING_CANCELS = `!s:A->bool f.
        FINITE s /\
        CARD {x | x IN s /\ EVEN(f x)} = CARD {x | x IN s /\ ODD(f x)}
        ==> sum s (\x. (-- &1) pow (f x)) = &0`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Hence a general "Moebius inversion" inclusion-exclusion principle.        *)
(* This "symmetric" form is from Ira Gessel: "Symmetric Inclusion-Exclusion" *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let INCLUSION_EXCLUSION_SYMMETRIC = `!f g:(A->bool)->real.
    (!s. FINITE s
         ==> g(s) = sum {t | t SUBSET s} (\t. (-- &1) pow (CARD t) * f(t)))
    ==> !s. FINITE s
            ==> f(s) = sum {t | t SUBSET s} (\t. (-- &1) pow (CARD t) * g(t))`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* The more typical non-symmetric version.                                   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let INCLUSION_EXCLUSION_MOBIUS = `!f g:(A->bool)->real.
        (!s. FINITE s ==> g(s) = sum {t | t SUBSET s} f)
        ==> !s. FINITE s
                ==> f(s) = sum {t | t SUBSET s}
                               (\t. (-- &1) pow (CARD s - CARD t) * g(t))`;;

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* A related principle for real functions.                                   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(*** Not clear how useful this is

needs "Library/products.ml";;

let INCLUSION_EXCLUSION_REAL_FUNCTION = `!f s:A->bool.
        FINITE s
        ==> product s (\x. &1 - f x) =
            sum {t | t SUBSET s} (\t. (-- &1) pow (CARD t) * product t f)`;;

***)

title: 096_principle_of_inclusion___exclusion
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems corpus artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__096, "Principle of Inclusion / Exclusion": for
;; every finite indexed family of finite sets, the cardinality of its union is
;; the alternating sum of the cardinalities of the intersections indexed by
;; its nonempty subfamilies. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Duplicate-free true lists represent finite sets of arbitrary ACL2 objects.
;; Positions in the outer list are the family indices, so equal member sets
;; may repeat without identifying their distinct indices.
(defun ht096-finite-set-family-p (family)
  (if (consp family)
      (and (true-listp (car family))
           (no-duplicatesp-equal (car family))
           (ht096-finite-set-family-p (cdr family)))
    (equal family nil)))

(defun ht096-set-union (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (if (member-equal (car left) right)
          (ht096-set-union (cdr left) right)
        (cons (car left)
              (ht096-set-union (cdr left) right)))
    right))

(defun ht096-family-union (family)
  (if (consp family)
      (ht096-set-union
       (car family)
       (ht096-family-union (cdr family)))
    nil))

(defun ht096-set-intersection (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (if (member-equal (car left) right)
          (cons
           (car left)
           (ht096-set-intersection (cdr left) right))
        (ht096-set-intersection (cdr left) right))
    nil))

(defun ht096-family-intersection (family)
  (if (consp family)
      (if (consp (cdr family))
          (ht096-set-intersection
           (car family)
           (ht096-family-intersection (cdr family)))
        (car family))
    nil))

(defun ht096-prepend-to-each (value families)
  (if (consp families)
      (cons
       (cons value (car families))
       (ht096-prepend-to-each value (cdr families)))
    nil))

;; This power-set enumeration is positional. If two indices carry equal sets,
;; the corresponding equal-looking subfamilies remain separate list entries.
(defun ht096-index-subfamilies (family)
  (if (consp family)
      (let ((tail-subfamilies
             (ht096-index-subfamilies (cdr family))))
        (append
         tail-subfamilies
         (ht096-prepend-to-each
          (car family) tail-subfamilies)))
    (list nil)))

(defun ht096-inclusion-exclusion-sum (subfamilies)
  (if (consp subfamilies)
      (let ((subfamily (car subfamilies)))
        (+
         (if (consp subfamily)
             (*
              (expt -1 (+ (len subfamily) 1))
              (len (ht096-family-intersection subfamily)))
           0)
         (ht096-inclusion-exclusion-sum
          (cdr subfamilies))))
    0))

(defun hundred-theorems-096-principle-of-inclusion-exclusion-statement
    (family)
  (implies
   (ht096-finite-set-family-p family)
   (equal
    (len (ht096-family-union family))
    (ht096-inclusion-exclusion-sum
     (ht096-index-subfamilies family)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 096_principle_of_inclusion___exclusion
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact hundred-theorems__agda__096,
-- "Principle of Inclusion / Exclusion": for a finite enumeration and a list-indexed family
-- of decidable subsets, the cardinality of their union is the alternating sum of the
-- cardinalities of all nonempty subfamily intersections. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)
open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc)

infixr 5 _++_
infixl 6 _+z_
infixl 7 _*z_

SetPredicate :
  {a : Level} →
  Set a →
  Set a
SetPredicate X = X → Bool

_++_ :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  List A →
  List A →
  List A
[] ++ ys = ys
(x ∷ xs) ++ ys = x ∷ (xs ++ ys)

mapList :
  {a b : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  {B : Set b} →
  (A → B) →
  List A →
  List B
mapList function [] = []
mapList function (x ∷ xs) =
  function x ∷ mapList function xs

filterList :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  (A → Bool) →
  List A →
  List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) with predicate x
... | true = x ∷ filterList predicate xs
... | false = filterList predicate xs

length :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  List A →
  Nat
length [] = zero
length (x ∷ xs) = suc (length xs)

boolOr : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolOr false right = right
boolOr true right = true

boolAnd : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolAnd false right = false
boolAnd true right = right

emptySet :
  {a : Level} →
  {X : Set a} →
  SetPredicate X
emptySet x = false

binaryUnion :
  {a : Level} →
  {X : Set a} →
  SetPredicate X →
  SetPredicate X →
  SetPredicate X
binaryUnion left right x =
  boolOr (left x) (right x)

binaryIntersection :
  {a : Level} →
  {X : Set a} →
  SetPredicate X →
  SetPredicate X →
  SetPredicate X
binaryIntersection left right x =
  boolAnd (left x) (right x)

foldRight :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  (A → A → A) →
  A →
  List A →
  A
foldRight operation base [] = base
foldRight operation base (x ∷ xs) =
  operation x (foldRight operation base xs)

foldOne :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  (A → A → A) →
  List A →
  A →
  A
foldOne operation [] default = default
foldOne operation (x ∷ xs) default =
  foldRight operation x xs

listUnion :
  {a : Level} →
  {X : Set a} →
  List (SetPredicate X) →
  SetPredicate X
listUnion sets =
  foldRight binaryUnion emptySet sets

listIntersection :
  {a : Level} →
  {X : Set a} →
  List (SetPredicate X) →
  SetPredicate X
listIntersection sets =
  foldOne binaryIntersection sets emptySet

sublists :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  List A →
  List (List A)
sublists [] = [] ∷ []
sublists (x ∷ xs) =
  let xss = sublists xs
  in xss ++ mapList (λ ys → x ∷ ys) xss

nonempty :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  List A →
  Bool
nonempty [] = false
nonempty (x ∷ xs) = true

difference : Nat → Nat → Int
difference zero zero = pos zero
difference (suc m) zero = pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) = negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) = difference m n

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

_+z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m +z pos n = pos (m + n)
pos m +z negsuc n = difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +z pos n = difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +z negsuc n = negsuc (suc (m + n))

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

negateInt : Int → Int
negateInt (pos zero) = pos zero
negateInt (pos (suc n)) = negsuc n
negateInt (negsuc n) = pos (suc n)

alternatingSign : Nat → Int
alternatingSign zero = pos (suc zero)
alternatingSign (suc n) =
  negateInt (alternatingSign n)

sumInt : List Int → Int
sumInt [] = pos zero
sumInt (x ∷ xs) = x +z sumInt xs

cardinal :
  {a : Level} →
  {X : Set a} →
  List X →
  SetPredicate X →
  Int
cardinal enumeration subset =
  pos (length (filterList subset enumeration))

inclusionExclusionTerm :
  {a : Level} →
  {X : Set a} →
  List X →
  List (SetPredicate X) →
  Int
inclusionExclusionTerm enumeration selected =
  cardinal enumeration (listIntersection selected) *z
  alternatingSign (suc (length selected))

principle-of-inclusion-exclusion :
  {a : Level} →
  Set (lsuc a)
principle-of-inclusion-exclusion {a} =
  (X : Set a) →
  (enumeration : List X) →
  (family : List (SetPredicate X)) →
  cardinal enumeration (listUnion family) ≡
  sumInt
    (mapList
      (inclusionExclusionTerm enumeration)
      (filterList nonempty (sublists family)))

(*
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact
  hundred-theorems__hol4__096, cataloged as "Principle of Inclusion / Exclusion":
  the cardinality of a finite indexed union of finite sets is the alternating
  integer sum of the cardinalities of all nonempty indexed subfamily
  intersections. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val principle_of_inclusion_exclusion =
  ``!A : 'i set. !x : 'i -> 'a set.
      FINITE A /\ (!i. i IN A ==> FINITE (x i)) ==>
      &(CARD (BIGUNION (IMAGE x A))) =
        SIGMA
          (\B.
             (~1 : int) ** (CARD B + 1) *
             &(CARD (BIGINTER (IMAGE x B))))
          {B | B SUBSET A /\ B <> {}}``;

title: 096_principle_of_inclusion___exclusion
content:
% Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems artifact 096, "Principle of
% Inclusion / Exclusion": the cardinality of a finite union of finite sets is
% the alternating sum of the cardinalities of their nonempty subfamily
% intersections. This file contains no proof.

principle_of_inclusion_exclusion_096[Element: TYPE]: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING
    finite_sets[Element],
    finite_sets_of_sets[Element]

  element_set: TYPE = finite_set[Element]
  finite_family: TYPE = finite_set[element_set]
  subfamily_collection: TYPE = finite_set[finite_family]

  nonempty_subfamilies(A: finite_family): subfamily_collection =
    intersection(
      powerset(A),
      {B: finite_family | NOT empty?(B)})

  finite_sum_value(
      S: subfamily_collection,
      f: [finite_family -> int],
      total: int): bool =
    EXISTS
      (enumeration: [below(card(S)) -> (S)]),
      (partial_sums: [upto(card(S)) -> int]):
        bijective?(enumeration)
          AND partial_sums(0) = 0
          AND
            (FORALL (index: below(card(S))):
              partial_sums(index + 1)
                = partial_sums(index) + f(enumeration(index)))
          AND total = partial_sums(card(S))

  principle_of_inclusion_exclusion: bool =
    FORALL (A: finite_family):
      EXISTS
        (union_set: element_set),
        (intersection_sets: [finite_family -> element_set]),
        (alternating_sum: int):
          union_set = Union(A)
            AND
              (FORALL (B: finite_family):
                member(B, nonempty_subfamilies(A))
                  IMPLIES intersection_sets(B) = Intersection(B))
            AND
              finite_sum_value(
            nonempty_subfamilies(A),
            (LAMBDA (B: finite_family):
              (-1) ^ (card(B) + 1)
                    * (card(intersection_sets(B)) :: int)),
                alternating_sum)
            AND (card(union_set) :: int) = alternating_sum
END principle_of_inclusion_exclusion_096

title: 097_cramer_s_rule
content:
/-
Copyright (c) 2019 Anne Baanen. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Anne Baanen
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Regular.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Symmetric
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.MvPolynomial
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Polynomial
public import Mathlib.GroupTheory.GroupAction.Ring

/-!
# Cramer's rule and adjugate matrices

The adjugate matrix is the transpose of the cofactor matrix.
It is calculated with Cramer's rule, which we introduce first.
The vectors returned by Cramer's rule are given by the linear map `cramer`,
which sends a matrix `A` and vector `b` to the vector consisting of the
determinant of replacing the `i`th column of `A` with `b` at index `i`
(written as `(A.updateCol i b).det`).
Using Cramer's rule, we can compute for each matrix `A` the matrix `adjugate A`.
The entries of the adjugate are the minors of `A`.
Instead of defining a minor by deleting row `i` and column `j` of `A`, we
replace the `i`th row of `A` with the `j`th basis vector; the resulting matrix
has the same determinant but more importantly equals Cramer's rule applied
to `A` and the `j`th basis vector, simplifying the subsequent proofs.
We prove the adjugate behaves like `det A • A⁻¹`.

## Main definitions

* `Matrix.cramer A b`: the vector output by Cramer's rule on `A` and `b`.
* `Matrix.adjugate A`: the adjugate (or classical adjoint) of the matrix `A`.

## References

  * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cramer's_rule#Finding_inverse_matrix

## Tags

cramer, cramer's rule, adjugate
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace Matrix

universe u v w

variable {m : Type u} {n : Type v} {α : Type w}
variable [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype m] [CommRing α]

open Matrix Polynomial Equiv Equiv.Perm Finset

section Cramer

/-!
  ### `cramer` section

  Introduce the linear map `cramer` with values defined by `cramerMap`.
  After defining `cramerMap` and showing it is linear,
  we will restrict our proofs to using `cramer`.
-/


variable (A : Matrix n n α) (b : n → α)

/-- `cramerMap A b i` is the determinant of the matrix `A` with column `i` replaced with `b`,
  and thus `cramerMap A b` is the vector output by Cramer's rule on `A` and `b`.

  If `A * x = b` has a unique solution in `x`, `cramerMap A` sends the vector `b` to `A.det • x`.
  Otherwise, the outcome of `cramerMap` is well-defined but not necessarily useful.
-/
def cramerMap (i : n) : α :=
  (A.updateCol i b).det

theorem cramerMap_is_linear (i : n) : IsLinearMap α fun b => cramerMap A b i :=
  { map_add := det_updateCol_add _ _
    map_smul := det_updateCol_smul _ _ }

theorem cramer_is_linear : IsLinearMap α (cramerMap A) := by sorry
def cramer (A : Matrix n n α) : (n → α) →ₗ[α] (n → α) :=
  IsLinearMap.mk' (cramerMap A) (cramer_is_linear A)

theorem cramer_apply (i : n) : cramer A b i = (A.updateCol i b).det :=
  rfl

theorem cramer_transpose_apply (i : n) : cramer Aᵀ b i = (A.updateRow i b).det := by sorry
theorem cramer_transpose_row_self (i : n) : Aᵀ.cramer (A i) = Pi.single i A.det := by sorry
theorem cramer_row_self (i : n) (h : ∀ j, b j = A j i) : A.cramer b = Pi.single i A.det := by sorry
theorem cramer_one : cramer (1 : Matrix n n α) = 1 := by sorry
theorem cramer_smul (r : α) (A : Matrix n n α) :
    cramer (r • A) = r ^ (Fintype.card n - 1) • cramer A :=
  LinearMap.ext fun _ => funext fun _ => det_updateCol_smul_left _ _ _ _

@[simp]
theorem cramer_subsingleton_apply [Subsingleton n] (A : Matrix n n α) (b : n → α) (i : n) :
    cramer A b i = b i := by rw [cramer_apply, det_eq_elem_of_subsingleton _ i, updateCol_self]

theorem cramer_zero [Nontrivial n] : cramer (0 : Matrix n n α) = 0 := by sorry
theorem sum_cramer {β} (s : Finset β) (f : β → n → α) :
    (∑ x ∈ s, cramer A (f x)) = cramer A (∑ x ∈ s, f x) :=
  (map_sum (cramer A) ..).symm

/-- Use linearity of `cramer` and vector evaluation to take `cramer A _ i` out of a summation. -/
theorem sum_cramer_apply {β} (s : Finset β) (f : n → β → α) (i : n) :
    (∑ x ∈ s, cramer A (fun j => f j x) i) = cramer A (fun j : n => ∑ x ∈ s, f j x) i :=
  calc
    (∑ x ∈ s, cramer A (fun j => f j x) i) = (∑ x ∈ s, cramer A fun j => f j x) i :=
      (Finset.sum_apply i s _).symm
    _ = cramer A (fun j : n => ∑ x ∈ s, f j x) i := by sorry
theorem cramer_submatrix_equiv (A : Matrix m m α) (e : n ≃ m) (b : n → α) :
    cramer (A.submatrix e e) b = cramer A (b ∘ e.symm) ∘ e := by sorry
theorem cramer_reindex (e : m ≃ n) (A : Matrix m m α) (b : n → α) :
    cramer (reindex e e A) b = cramer A (b ∘ e) ∘ e.symm :=
  cramer_submatrix_equiv _ _ _

end Cramer

section Adjugate

/-!
### `adjugate` section

Define the `adjugate` matrix and a few equations.
These will hold for any matrix over a commutative ring.
-/


/-- The adjugate matrix is the transpose of the cofactor matrix.

  Typically, the cofactor matrix is defined by taking minors,
  i.e. the determinant of the matrix with a row and column removed.
  However, the proof of `mul_adjugate` becomes a lot easier if we use the
  matrix replacing a column with a basis vector, since it allows us to use
  facts about the `cramer` map.
-/
def adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) : Matrix n n α :=
  of fun i => cramer Aᵀ (Pi.single i 1)

theorem adjugate_def (A : Matrix n n α) : adjugate A = of fun i => cramer Aᵀ (Pi.single i 1) :=
  rfl

theorem adjugate_apply (A : Matrix n n α) (i j : n) :
    adjugate A i j = (A.updateRow j (Pi.single i 1)).det := by sorry
theorem adjugate_transpose (A : Matrix n n α) : (adjugate A)ᵀ = adjugate Aᵀ := by sorry
theorem IsSymm.adjugate {A : Matrix n n α} (hA : A.IsSymm) : A.adjugate.IsSymm := by sorry
theorem adjugate_submatrix_equiv_self (e : n ≃ m) (A : Matrix m m α) :
    adjugate (A.submatrix e e) = (adjugate A).submatrix e e := by sorry
theorem adjugate_reindex (e : m ≃ n) (A : Matrix m m α) :
    adjugate (reindex e e A) = reindex e e (adjugate A) :=
  adjugate_submatrix_equiv_self _ _

/-- Since the map `b ↦ cramer A b` is linear in `b`, it must be multiplication by some matrix. This
matrix is `A.adjugate`. -/
theorem cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec (A : Matrix n n α) (b : n → α) :
    cramer A b = A.adjugate *ᵥ b := by sorry
theorem mul_adjugate_apply (A : Matrix n n α) (i j k) :
    A i k * adjugate A k j = cramer Aᵀ (Pi.single k (A i k)) j := by sorry
theorem mul_adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) : A * adjugate A = A.det • (1 : Matrix n n α) := by sorry
theorem adjugate_mul (A : Matrix n n α) : adjugate A * A = A.det • (1 : Matrix n n α) :=
  calc
    adjugate A * A = (Aᵀ * adjugate Aᵀ)ᵀ := by sorry
theorem adjugate_smul (r : α) (A : Matrix n n α) :
    adjugate (r • A) = r ^ (Fintype.card n - 1) • adjugate A := by sorry
theorem mulVec_cramer (A : Matrix n n α) (b : n → α) : A *ᵥ cramer A b = A.det • b := by sorry
theorem adjugate_subsingleton [Subsingleton n] (A : Matrix n n α) : adjugate A = 1 := by sorry
theorem adjugate_eq_one_of_card_eq_one {A : Matrix n n α} (h : Fintype.card n = 1) :
    adjugate A = 1 :=
  haveI : Subsingleton n := Fintype.card_le_one_iff_subsingleton.mp h.le
  adjugate_subsingleton _

@[simp]
theorem adjugate_zero [Nontrivial n] : adjugate (0 : Matrix n n α) = 0 := by sorry
theorem adjugate_one : adjugate (1 : Matrix n n α) = 1 := by sorry
theorem adjugate_diagonal (v : n → α) :
    adjugate (diagonal v) = diagonal fun i => ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, v j := by sorry
theorem _root_.RingHom.map_adjugate {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S)
    (M : Matrix n n R) : f.mapMatrix M.adjugate = Matrix.adjugate (f.mapMatrix M) := by sorry
theorem _root_.AlgHom.map_adjugate {R A B : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (M : Matrix n n A) :
    f.mapMatrix M.adjugate = Matrix.adjugate (f.mapMatrix M) :=
  f.toRingHom.map_adjugate _

theorem det_adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) : (adjugate A).det = A.det ^ (Fintype.card n - 1) := by sorry
theorem adjugate_fin_zero (A : Matrix (Fin 0) (Fin 0) α) : adjugate A = 0 :=
  Subsingleton.elim _ _

@[simp]
theorem adjugate_fin_one (A : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) α) : adjugate A = 1 :=
  adjugate_subsingleton A

theorem adjugate_fin_succ_eq_det_submatrix {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n.succ) (Fin n.succ) α) (i j) :
    adjugate A i j = (-1) ^ (j + i : ℕ) * det (A.submatrix j.succAbove i.succAbove) := by sorry
theorem adjugate_fin_two (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) α) :
    adjugate A = !![A 1 1, -A 0 1; -A 1 0, A 0 0] := by sorry
theorem adjugate_fin_two_of (a b c d : α) : adjugate !![a, b; c, d] = !![d, -b; -c, a] :=
  adjugate_fin_two _

theorem adjugate_fin_three (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) α) :
    adjugate A =
    !![A 1 1 * A 2 2 - A 1 2 * A 2 1,
      -(A 0 1 * A 2 2) + A 0 2 * A 2 1,
      A 0 1 * A 1 2 - A 0 2 * A 1 1;
      -(A 1 0 * A 2 2) + A 1 2 * A 2 0,
      A 0 0 * A 2 2 - A 0 2 * A 2 0,
      -(A 0 0 * A 1 2) + A 0 2 * A 1 0;
      A 1 0 * A 2 1 - A 1 1 * A 2 0,
      -(A 0 0 * A 2 1) + A 0 1 * A 2 0,
      A 0 0 * A 1 1 - A 0 1 * A 1 0] := by sorry
theorem adjugate_fin_three_of (a b c d e f g h i : α) :
    adjugate !![a, b, c; d, e, f; g, h, i] =
      !![  e * i  - f * h, -(b * i) + c * h,   b * f  - c * e;
         -(d * i) + f * g,   a * i  - c * g, -(a * f) + c * d;
           d * h  - e * g, -(a * h) + b * g,   a * e  - b * d] :=
  adjugate_fin_three _

theorem det_eq_sum_mul_adjugate_row (A : Matrix n n α) (i : n) :
    det A = ∑ j : n, A i j * adjugate A j i := by sorry
theorem det_eq_sum_mul_adjugate_col (A : Matrix n n α) (j : n) :
    det A = ∑ i : n, A i j * adjugate A j i := by sorry
theorem adjugate_conjTranspose [StarRing α] (A : Matrix n n α) : A.adjugateᴴ = adjugate Aᴴ := by sorry
theorem isRegular_of_isLeftRegular_det {A : Matrix n n α} (hA : IsLeftRegular A.det) :
    IsRegular A := by sorry
theorem adjugate_mul_distrib_aux (A B : Matrix n n α) (hA : IsLeftRegular A.det)
    (hB : IsLeftRegular B.det) : adjugate (A * B) = adjugate B * adjugate A := by sorry
theorem adjugate_mul_distrib (A B : Matrix n n α) : adjugate (A * B) = adjugate B * adjugate A := by sorry
theorem adjugate_pow (A : Matrix n n α) (k : ℕ) : adjugate (A ^ k) = adjugate A ^ k := by sorry
theorem det_smul_adjugate_adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) :
    det A • adjugate (adjugate A) = det A ^ (Fintype.card n - 1) • A := by sorry
theorem adjugate_adjugate (A : Matrix n n α) (h : Fintype.card n ≠ 1) :
    adjugate (adjugate A) = det A ^ (Fintype.card n - 2) • A := by sorry
theorem adjugate_adjugate' (A : Matrix n n α) [Nontrivial n] :
    adjugate (adjugate A) = det A ^ (Fintype.card n - 2) • A :=
  adjugate_adjugate _ <| Fintype.one_lt_card.ne'

end Adjugate

end Matrix

content:
(* (c) Copyright 2006-2016 Microsoft Corporation and Inria.                  *)

From HB Require Import structures.
From mathcomp Require Import ssreflect ssrfun ssrbool eqtype ssrnat seq choice.
From mathcomp Require Import fintype finfun bigop finset nmodule fingroup perm.
From mathcomp Require Import order algebra divalg countalg finalg zmodp.

(******************************************************************************)
(* Basic concrete linear algebra : definition of type for matrices, and all   *)
(* basic matrix operations including determinant, trace and support for block *)
(* decomposition. Matrices are represented by a row-major list of their       *)
(* coefficients but this implementation is hidden by three levels of wrappers *)
(* (Matrix/Finfun/Tuple) so the matrix type should be treated as abstract and *)
(* handled using only the operations described below:                         *)
(*   'M[R]_(m, n) == the type of m rows by n columns matrices with            *)
(*   'M_(m, n)       coefficients in R; the [R] is optional and is usually    *)
(*                   omitted.                                                 *)
(*  'M[R]_n, 'M_n == the type of n x n square matrices.                       *)
(* 'rV[R]_n, 'rV_n == the type of 1 x n row vectors.                          *)
(* 'cV[R]_n, 'cV_n == the type of n x 1 column vectors.                       *)
(*  \matrix_(i < m, j < n) Expr(i, j) ==                                      *)
(*                   the m x n matrix with general coefficient Expr(i, j),    *)
(*                   with i : 'I_m and j : 'I_n. the < m bound can be omitted *)
(*                   if it is equal to n, though usually both bounds are      *)
(*                   omitted as they can be inferred from the context.        *)
(*  \row_(j < n) Expr(j), \col_(i < m) Expr(i)                                *)
(*                   the row / column vectors with general term Expr; the     *)
(*                   parentheses can be omitted along with the bound.         *)
(* \matrix_(i < m) RowExpr(i) ==                                              *)
(*                   the m x n matrix with row i given by RowExpr(i) : 'rV_n. *)
(*          A i j == the coefficient of matrix A : 'M_(m, n) in column j of   *)
(*                   row i, where i : 'I_m, and j : 'I_n (via the coercion    *)
(*                   fun_of_matrix : matrix >-> Funclass).                    *)
(*     const_mx a == the constant matrix whose entries are all a (dimensions  *)
(*                   should be determined by context).                        *)
(*     map_mx f A == the pointwise image of A by f, i.e., the matrix Af       *)
(*                   congruent to A with Af i j = f (A i j) for all i and j.  *)
(*     map2_mx f A B == the pointwise image of A and B by f, i.e., the matrix *)
(*                     ABf congruent to A with ABf i j = f (A i j) (B i j)    *)
(*                     for all i and j.                                       *)
(*            A^T == the matrix transpose of A.                               *)
(*        row i A == the i'th row of A (this is a row vector).                *)
(*        col j A == the j'th column of A (a column vector).                  *)
(*       row' i A == A with the i'th row spliced out.                         *)
(*       col' i A == A with the j'th column spliced out.                      *)
(*   xrow i1 i2 A == A with rows i1 and i2 interchanged.                      *)
(*   xcol j1 j2 A == A with columns j1 and j2 interchanged.                   *)
(*   row_perm s A == A : 'M_(m, n) with rows permuted by s : 'S_m.            *)
(*   col_perm s A == A : 'M_(m, n) with columns permuted by s : 'S_n.         *)
(*   row_mx Al Ar == the row block matrix <Al Ar> obtained by concatenating   *)
(*                   two matrices Al and Ar of the same height.               *)
(*   col_mx Au Ad == the column block matrix / Au \ (Au and Ad must have the  *)
(*                   same width).            \ Ad /                           *)
(* block_mx Aul Aur Adl Adr == the block matrix / Aul Aur \                   *)
(*                                              \ Adl Adr /                   *)
(* \mxblock_(i < m, j < n) B i j                                              *)
(*                == the block matrix of type 'M_(\sum_i p_ i, \sum_j q_ j)   *)
(*                             / (B 0 0) ⋯ (B 0 j) ⋯ (B 0 n) \                *)
(*                             |   ...       ...       ...   |                *)
(*                             | (B i 0) ⋯ (B i j) ⋯ (B i n) |                *)
(*                             |   ...       ...       ...   |                *)
(*                             \ (B m 0) ⋯ (B m j) ⋯ (B m n) /                *)
(*                   where each block (B i j) has type 'M_(p_ i, q_ j).       *)
(* \mxdiag_(i < n) B i == the block square matrix of type 'M_(\sum_i p_ i)    *)
(*                                / (B 0)      0      \                       *)
(*                                |     ...     ...   |                       *)
(*                                |  0    (B i)    0  |                       *)
(*                                |   ...     ...     |                       *)
(*                                \      0      (B n) /                       *)
(*                        where each block (B i) has type 'M_(p_ i).          *)
(*  \mxrow_(j < n) B j ==  the block matrix of type 'M_(m, \sum_j q_ j).      *)
(*                                 < (B 0) ... (B n) >                        *)
(*                         where each block (B j) has type 'M_(m, q_ j).      *)
(*  \mxcol_(i < m) B i ==  the block matrix of type 'M_(\sum_i p_ i, n)       *)
(*                                      / (B 0) \                             *)
(*                                      |  ...  |                             *)
(*                                      \ (B m) /                             *)
(*                         where each block (B i) has type 'M(p_ i, n).       *)
(*   [l|r]submx A == the left/right submatrices of a row block matrix A.      *)
(*                   Note that the type of A, 'M_(m, n1 + n2) indicates how A *)
(*                   should be decomposed.                                    *)
(*   [u|d]submx A == the up/down submatrices of a column block matrix A.      *)
(* [u|d][l|r]submx A == the upper left, etc submatrices of a block matrix A.  *)
(*  submxblock A i j == the block submatrix of type 'M_(p_ i, q_ j) of A.     *)
(*                      The type of A, 'M_(\sum_i p_ i, \sum_i q_ i)          *)
(*                      indicates how A should be decomposed.                 *)
(*                      There is no analogous for mxdiag since one can use    *)
(*                      submxblock A i i to extract a diagonal block.         *)
(*   submxrow A j == the submatrix of type 'M_(m, q_ j) of A. The type of A,  *)
(*                   'M_(m, \sum_j q_ j) indicates how A should be decomposed.*)
(*   submxrow A j == the submatrix of type 'M_(p_ i, n) of A. The type of A,  *)
(*                   'M_(\sum_i p_ i, n) indicates how A should be decomposed.*)
(*    mxsub f g A == generic reordered submatrix, given by functions f and g  *)
(*                   which specify which subset of rows and columns to take   *)
(*                   and how to reorder them, e.g. picking f and g to be      *)
(*                   increasing yields traditional submatrices.               *)
(*                := \matrix_(i, j) A (f i) (g i)                             *)
(*     rowsub f A := mxsub f id A                                             *)
(*     colsub g A := mxsub id g A                                             *)
(* castmx eq_mn A == A : 'M_(m, n) cast to 'M_(m', n') using the equation     *)
(*                   pair eq_mn : (m = m') * (n = n'). This is the usual      *)
(*                   workaround for the syntactic limitations of dependent    *)
(*                   types in Coq, and can be used to introduce a block       *)
(*                   decomposition. It simplifies to A when eq_mn is the      *)
(*                   pair (erefl m, erefl n) (using rewrite /castmx /=).      *)
(* conform_mx B A == A if A and B have the same dimensions, else B.           *)
(*        mxvec A == a row vector of width m * n holding all the entries of   *)
(*                   the m x n matrix A.                                      *)
(* mxvec_index i j == the index of A i j in mxvec A.                          *)
(*       vec_mx v == the inverse of mxvec, reshaping a vector of width m * n  *)
(*                   back into into an m x n rectangular matrix.              *)
(* In 'M[R]_(m, n), R can be any type, but 'M[R]_(m, n) inherits the eqType,  *)
(* choiceType, countType, finType, nmodType, and zmodType structures from R;  *)
(* 'M[R]_(m, n) also forms a natural lmodType R when R is a pzRingType.       *)
(* Square matrices of type 'M[R]_n (resp. non-trivial square matrices of type *)
(* 'M[R]_n.+1) inherit the pz(Semi)RingType (resp. nz(Semi)RingType) structure*)
(* from R; indeed they then have an algebra structure (lalgType R, or algType *)
(* R if R is a comNzRingType, or even unitAlgType if R is a comUnitRingType). *)
(*   We thus provide separate syntax for the general matrix multiplication,   *)
(* and other operations for matrices over a pzRingType R:                     *)
(*         A *m B == the matrix product of A and B; the width of A must be    *)
(*                   equal to the height of B.                                *)
(*           a%:M == the scalar matrix with a's on the main diagonal; in      *)
(*                   particular 1%:M denotes the identity matrix, and is      *)
(*                   equal to 1%R when n is of the form n'.+1 (e.g., n >= 1). *)
(* is_scalar_mx A <=> A is a scalar matrix (A = a%:M for some A).             *)
(*      diag_mx d == the diagonal matrix whose main diagonal is d : 'rV_n.    *)
(*  is_diag_mx A <=> A is a diagonal matrix:  forall i j, i != j -> A i j = 0 *)
(*  is_trig_mx A <=> A is a triangular matrix: forall i j, i < j -> A i j = 0 *)
(*   delta_mx i j == the matrix with a 1 in row i, column j and 0 elsewhere.  *)
(*       pid_mx r == the partial identity matrix with 1s only on the r first  *)
(*                   coefficients of the main diagonal; the dimensions of     *)
(*                   pid_mx r are determined by the context, and pid_mx r can *)
(*                   be rectangular.                                          *)
(*     copid_mx r == the complement to 1%:M of pid_mx r: a square diagonal    *)
(*                   matrix with 1s on all but the first r coefficients on    *)
(*                   its main diagonal.                                       *)
(*      perm_mx s == the n x n permutation matrix for s : 'S_n.               *)
(* tperm_mx i1 i2 == the permutation matrix that exchanges i1 i2 : 'I_n.      *)
(*   is_perm_mx A == A is a permutation matrix.                               *)
(*     lift0_mx A == the 1 + n square matrix block_mx 1 0 0 A when A : 'M_n.  *)
(*          \tr A == the trace of a square matrix A.                          *)
(*         \det A == the determinant of A, using the Leibnitz formula.        *)
(* cofactor i j A == the i, j cofactor of A (the signed i, j minor of A),     *)
(*         \adj A == the adjugate matrix of A (\adj A i j = cofactor j i A).  *)
(*   A \in unitmx == A is invertible (R must be a comUnitRingType).           *)
(*        invmx A == the inverse matrix of A if A \in unitmx A, otherwise A.  *)
(* A \is a mxOver S == the matrix A has its coefficients in S.                *)
(*       comm_mx A B := A *m B = B *m A                                       *)
(*      comm_mxb A B := A *m B == B *m A                                      *)
(* all_comm_mx As fs := all2rel comm_mxb fs                                   *)
(* The following operations provide a correspondence between linear functions *)
(* and matrices:                                                              *)
(*     lin1_mx f == the m x n matrix that emulates via right product          *)
(*                  a (linear) function f : 'rV_m -> 'rV_n on ROW VECTORS     *)
(*      lin_mx f == the (m1 * n1) x (m2 * n2) matrix that emulates, via the   *)
(*                  right multiplication on the mxvec encodings, a linear     *)
(*                  function f : 'M_(m1, n1) -> 'M_(m2, n2)                   *)
(* lin_mul_row u := lin1_mx (mulmx u \o vec_mx) (applies a row-encoded        *)
(*                  function to the row-vector u).                            *)
(*       mulmx A == partially applied matrix multiplication (mulmx A B is     *)
(*                  displayed as A *m B), with, for A : 'M_(m, n), a          *)
(*                  canonical {linear 'M_(n, p) -> 'M(m, p}} structure.       *)
(*      mulmxr A == self-simplifying right-hand matrix multiplication, i.e.,  *)
(*                  mulmxr A B simplifies to B *m A, with, for A : 'M_(n, p), *)
(*                  a canonical {linear 'M_(m, n) -> 'M(m, p}} structure.     *)
(*   lin_mulmx A := lin_mx (mulmx A).                                         *)
(*  lin_mulmxr A := lin_mx (mulmxr A).                                        *)
(* We also extend any finType structure of R to 'M[R]_(m, n), and define:     *)
(*     {'GL_n[R]} == the finGroupType of units of 'M[R]_n.-1.+1.              *)
(*      'GL_n[R]  == the general linear group of all matrices in {'GL_n(R)}.  *)
(*      'GL_n(p)  == 'GL_n['F_p], the general linear group of a prime field.  *)
(*       GLval u  == the coercion of u : {'GL_n(R)} to a matrix.              *)
(*   In addition to the lemmas relevant to these definitions, this file also  *)
(* proves several classic results, including :                                *)
(* - The determinant is a multilinear alternate form.                         *)
(* - The Laplace determinant expansion formulas: expand_det_[row|col].        *)
(* - The Cramer rule : mul_mx_adj & mul_adj_mx.                               *)
(* Vandermonde m a == the 'M[R]_(m, n) Vandermonde matrix, given a : 'rV_n    *)
(*                    /         1          ...           1              \     *)
(*                    |      (a 0 0)       ...      (a 0 (n - 1))       |     *)
(*                    |    (a 0 0 ^+ 2)    ...    (a 0 (n - 1) ^+ 2)    |     *)
(*                    |        ...                      ...             |     *)
(*                    \ (a 0 0 ^+ (m - 1)) ... (a 0 (n - 1) ^+ (m - 1)) /     *)
(*                 := \matrix_(i < m, j < n) a 0 j ^+ i.                      *)
(* Finally, as an example of the use of block products, we program and prove  *)
(* the correctness of a classical linear algebra algorithm:                   *)
(*   cormen_lup A == the triangular decomposition (L, U, P) of a nontrivial   *)
(*                   square matrix A into a lower triagular matrix L with 1s  *)
(*                   on the main diagonal, an upper matrix U, and a           *)
(*                   permutation matrix P, such that P * A = L * U.           *)
(* This is example only; we use a different, more precise algorithm to        *)
(* develop the theory of matrix ranks and row spaces in mxalgebra.v           *)
(******************************************************************************)

Variables m n : nat.

(* Reshape a matrix, to accommodate the block functions for instance. *)
Definition castmx m' n' (eq_mn : (m = m') * (n = n')) A : 'M_(m', n') :=
  let: erefl in _ = m' := eq_mn.1 return 'M_(m', n') in
  let: erefl in _ = n' := eq_mn.2 return 'M_(m, n') in A.

Definition conform_mx m' n' B A :=
  match m =P m', n =P n' with
  | ReflectT eq_m, ReflectT eq_n => castmx (eq_m, eq_n) A
  | _, _ => B
  end.

(* Transpose a matrix *)
Fact trmx_key : unit.
Proof.
Admitted.
Definition trmx A := \matrix[trmx_key]_(i, j) A j i.

(* Permute a matrix vertically (rows) or horizontally (columns) *)
Fact row_perm_key : unit.
Proof.
Admitted.
Definition row_perm (s : 'S_m) A := \matrix[row_perm_key]_(i, j) A (s i) j.
Fact col_perm_key : unit.
Proof.
Admitted.
Definition col_perm (s : 'S_n) A := \matrix[col_perm_key]_(i, j) A i (s j).

(* Exchange two rows/columns of a matrix *)
Definition xrow i1 i2 := row_perm (tperm i1 i2).
Definition xcol j1 j2 := col_perm (tperm j1 j2).

(* Row/Column sub matrices of a matrix *)
Definition row i0 A := \row_j A i0 j.
Definition col j0 A := \col_i A i j0.

(* Removing a row/column from a matrix *)
Definition row' i0 A := \matrix_(i, j) A (lift i0 i) j.
Definition col' j0 A := \matrix_(i, j) A i (lift j0 j).

(* reindexing/subindex a matrix *)
Definition mxsub m' n' f g A := \matrix_(i < m', j < n') A (f i) (g j).
Local Notation colsub g := (mxsub id g).
Local Notation rowsub f := (mxsub f id).

Section CommMx.
(***********************************************************************)
(* Commutation property specialized to 'M[R]_n                         *)
(*                                                                     *)
(* GRing.comm is bound to (non trivial) rings, and matrices form a     *)
(* (non trivial) ring only when they are square and of manifestly      *)
(* positive size. However during proofs in endomorphism reduction, we  *)
(* take restrictions, which are matrices of size #|V| (with V a matrix *)
(* space) and it becomes cumbersome to state commutation between       *)
(* restrictions, unless we relax the setting, and this relaxation      *)
(* corresponds to comm_mx A B := A *m B = B *m A.                      *)
(* As witnessed by comm_mxE, when A and B have type 'M_n.+1,           *)
(*   comm_mx A B is convertible to GRing.comm A B.                     *)
(* The boolean version comm_mxb is designed to be used with seq.allrel *)
(***********************************************************************)

Context {R : pzSemiRingType} {n : nat}.
Implicit Types (f g p : 'M[R]_n) (fs : seq 'M[R]_n) (d : 'rV[R]_n) (I : Type).

Definition comm_mx  f g : Prop := f *m g =  g *m f.
Definition comm_mxb f g : bool := f *m g == g *m f.

Proof.
Admitted.

Proof.
Admitted.

Proof.
Admitted.

Proof.
Admitted.

Proof.
Admitted.

Proof.
Admitted.

Hint Resolve comm_mx0 comm0mx comm_mx1 comm1mx : core.

Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma comm_mxM f g g' : comm_mx f g -> comm_mx f g' -> comm_mx f (g *m g').
Proof.
Admitted.

Lemma comm_mx_sum I (s : seq I) (P : pred I) (F : I -> 'M[R]_n) (f : 'M[R]_n) :
  (forall i : I, P i -> comm_mx f (F i)) -> comm_mx f (\sum_(i <- s | P i) F i).

Admitted.

Lemma comm_mxP f g : reflect (comm_mx f g) (comm_mxb f g).
Proof.
Admitted.

Notation all_comm_mx fs := (all2rel comm_mxb fs).

Admitted.

Proof.
Admitted.

Proof.
Admitted.

(* Determinants and adjugates are defined here, but most of their properties *)
(* only hold for matrices over a commutative ring, so their theory is        *)
(* deferred to that section.                                                 *)

(* The determinant, in one line with the Leibniz Formula *)
Definition determinant n (A : 'M_n) : R :=
  \sum_(s : 'S_n) (-1) ^+ s * \prod_i A i (s i).

(* The cofactor of a matrix on the indexes i and j *)
Definition cofactor n A (i j : 'I_n) : R :=
  (-1) ^+ (i + j) * determinant (row' i (col' j A)).

(* The adjugate matrix : defined as the transpose of the matrix of cofactors *)
Fact adjugate_key : unit.
Proof.
Admitted.
Definition adjugate n (A : 'M_n) := \matrix[adjugate_key]_(i, j) cofactor A j i.

Section CormenLUP.

Variable F : fieldType.

(* Decomposition of the matrix A to P A = L U with *)
(*   - P a permutation matrix                      *)
(*   - L a unipotent lower triangular matrix       *)
(*   - U an upper triangular matrix                *)

Fixpoint cormen_lup {n} :=
  match n return let M := 'M[F]_n.+1 in M -> M * M * M with
  | 0 => fun A => (1, 1, A)
  | _.+1 => fun A =>
    let k := odflt 0 [pick k | A k 0 != 0] in
    let A1 : 'M_(1 + _) := xrow 0 k A in
    let P1 : 'M_(1 + _) := tperm_mx 0 k in
    let Schur := ((A k 0)^-1 *: dlsubmx A1) *m ursubmx A1 in
    let: (P2, L2, U2) := cormen_lup (drsubmx A1 - Schur) in
    let P := block_mx 1 0 0 P2 *m P1 in
    let L := block_mx 1 0 ((A k 0)^-1 *: (P2 *m dlsubmx A1)) L2 in
    let U := block_mx (ulsubmx A1) (ursubmx A1) 0 U2 in
    (P, L, U)
  end.

title: 097_cramer_s_rule
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Cramer's rule from Hundred Theorems
  item 097. It gives the unique solution of a nonsingular square linear
  system by column-replacement determinants. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory Cramers_Rule
  imports Complex_Main
begin

fun insert_everywhere :: "'a \<Rightarrow> 'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a list list"
  where
    "insert_everywhere x [] = [[x]]"
  | "insert_everywhere x (y # ys) =
      (x # y # ys) # map ((#) y) (insert_everywhere x ys)"

fun list_permutations :: "'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a list list"
  where
    "list_permutations [] = [[]]"
  | "list_permutations (x # xs) =
      concat (map (insert_everywhere x) (list_permutations xs))"

definition inversion_count :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat"
  where
    "inversion_count p =
      card {(i, j). i < j \<and> j < length p \<and> p ! j < p ! i}"

definition permutation_sign :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> int"
  where
    "permutation_sign p = (if even (inversion_count p) then 1 else -1)"

definition list_determinant :: "'a::field list list \<Rightarrow> 'a"
  where
    "list_determinant A =
      (let n = length A
       in sum_list
         (map
           (\<lambda>p. of_int (permutation_sign p)
             * prod_list (map (\<lambda>i. (A ! i) ! (p ! i)) [0..<n]))
           (list_permutations [0..<n])))"

definition matrix_vector_product ::
    "'a::field list list \<Rightarrow> 'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a list"
  where
    "matrix_vector_product A x =
      map (\<lambda>row. sum_list (map2 (*) row x)) A"

definition replace_matrix_column ::
    "'a::field list list \<Rightarrow> 'a list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> 'a list list"
  where
    "replace_matrix_column A b k =
      map
        (\<lambda>i. map
          (\<lambda>j. if j = k then b ! i else (A ! i) ! j)
          [0..<length A])
        [0..<length A]"

theorem hundred_theorems_cramer:
  fixes A :: "'a::field list list"
    and x b :: "'a list"
  assumes square: "\<forall>row \<in> set A. length row = length A"
    and x_dimension: "length x = length A"
    and b_dimension: "length b = length A"
    and nonsingular: "list_determinant A \<noteq> 0"
  shows
    "matrix_vector_product A x = b \<longleftrightarrow>
      x = map
        (\<lambda>k. list_determinant (replace_matrix_column A b k)
          / list_determinant A)
        [0..<length A]"
  sorry

end

title: 097_cramer_s_rule
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Cramer's Rule" from Hundred Theorems
  artifact 097 (hundred-theorems__hol-light__097). It states the determinant
  formula for the unique solution of a nonsingular real square linear system.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

needs "Multivariate/determinants.ml";;

let HUNDRED_THEOREMS_097_CRAMER =
  `!A:real^N^N x b.
      ~(det A = &0)
      ==> (A ** x = b <=>
           x = lambda k.
                 det((lambda i j.
                        if j = k then b$i else A$i$j):real^N^N) /
                 det A)`;;

title: 097_cramer_s_rule
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of hundred-theorems artifact
;; hundred-theorems__acl2__097, "Cramer's Rule": for every finite square
;; matrix A and vector b over a commutative unital ring, multiplying A by the
;; vector of determinants obtained by replacing each column of A with b gives
;; det(A) times b.  This is the numerator form of the usual nonzero-determinant
;; solution formula and is expressed by the equivalent generic-matrix identity
;; over an integer polynomial ring.  This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Multivariate integer polynomials are sorted lists of
;; (monomial . coefficient) pairs.  A monomial is a sorted list of variable
;; indices, with repetition recording powers.

(defun ht097-monomial-mul (left right)
  (declare (xargs :measure
                  (+ (acl2-count left) (acl2-count right))))
  (cond ((endp left) right)
        ((endp right) left)
        ((<= (car left) (car right))
         (cons (car left)
               (ht097-monomial-mul (cdr left) right)))
        (t
         (cons (car right)
               (ht097-monomial-mul left (cdr right))))))

(defun ht097-poly-insert-term (monomial coefficient polynomial)
  (cond ((equal coefficient 0) polynomial)
        ((endp polynomial)
         (list (cons monomial coefficient)))
        ((equal monomial (caar polynomial))
         (let ((sum (+ coefficient (cdar polynomial))))
           (if (equal sum 0)
               (cdr polynomial)
             (cons (cons monomial sum) (cdr polynomial)))))
        ((lexorder monomial (caar polynomial))
         (cons (cons monomial coefficient) polynomial))
        (t
         (cons (car polynomial)
               (ht097-poly-insert-term monomial coefficient
                                       (cdr polynomial))))))

(defun ht097-poly-add (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      right
    (ht097-poly-add
     (cdr left)
     (ht097-poly-insert-term (caar left) (cdar left) right))))

(defun ht097-poly-neg (polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (cons (cons (caar polynomial) (- (cdar polynomial)))
          (ht097-poly-neg (cdr polynomial)))))

(defun ht097-poly-mul-term (monomial coefficient polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (ht097-poly-insert-term
     (ht097-monomial-mul monomial (caar polynomial))
     (* coefficient (cdar polynomial))
     (ht097-poly-mul-term monomial coefficient (cdr polynomial)))))

(defun ht097-poly-mul (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      nil
    (ht097-poly-add
     (ht097-poly-mul-term (caar left) (cdar left) right)
     (ht097-poly-mul (cdr left) right))))

(defun ht097-poly-one ()
  (list (cons nil 1)))

(defun ht097-poly-variable (index)
  (list (cons (list index) 1)))

;; The generic n-by-n matrix and n-vector have algebraically independent
;; entries.

(defun ht097-range-from (start count)
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons start
          (ht097-range-from (+ 1 start) (- count 1)))))

(defun ht097-generic-row (n row columns)
  (if (endp columns)
      nil
    (cons (ht097-poly-variable
           (+ (* n row) (car columns)))
          (ht097-generic-row n row (cdr columns)))))

(defun ht097-generic-matrix-rows (n rows columns)
  (if (endp rows)
      nil
    (cons (ht097-generic-row n (car rows) columns)
          (ht097-generic-matrix-rows n (cdr rows) columns))))

(defun ht097-generic-matrix (n)
  (let ((indices (ht097-range-from 0 n)))
    (ht097-generic-matrix-rows n indices indices)))

(defun ht097-generic-vector-from (start count)
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons (ht097-poly-variable start)
          (ht097-generic-vector-from (+ 1 start) (- count 1)))))

(defun ht097-generic-vector (n)
  (ht097-generic-vector-from (* n n) n))

;; The determinant is the signed sum over permutations.

(defun ht097-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons (cons item (car lists))
          (ht097-prefix-each item (cdr lists)))))

(defun ht097-insert-everywhere (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list (list item))
    (cons (cons item list)
          (ht097-prefix-each
           (car list)
           (ht097-insert-everywhere item (cdr list))))))

(defun ht097-insert-into-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (append (ht097-insert-everywhere item (car lists))
            (ht097-insert-into-each item (cdr lists)))))

(defun ht097-permutations (list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list nil)
    (ht097-insert-into-each
     (car list)
     (ht097-permutations (cdr list)))))

(defun ht097-count-greater (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      0
    (+ (if (> item (car list)) 1 0)
       (ht097-count-greater item (cdr list)))))

(defun ht097-inversion-count (permutation)
  (if (endp permutation)
      0
    (+ (ht097-count-greater (car permutation) (cdr permutation))
       (ht097-inversion-count (cdr permutation)))))

(defun ht097-diagonal-product (matrix permutation row-index)
  (if (endp permutation)
      (ht097-poly-one)
    (ht097-poly-mul
     (nth (car permutation) (nth row-index matrix))
     (ht097-diagonal-product
      matrix (cdr permutation) (+ 1 row-index)))))

(defun ht097-determinant-sum (matrix permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      nil
    (let* ((permutation (car permutations))
           (product
            (ht097-diagonal-product matrix permutation 0))
           (signed-product
            (if (equal (mod (ht097-inversion-count permutation) 2) 0)
                product
              (ht097-poly-neg product))))
      (ht097-poly-add
       signed-product
       (ht097-determinant-sum matrix (cdr permutations))))))

(defun ht097-matrix-det (matrix n)
  (ht097-determinant-sum
   matrix
   (ht097-permutations (ht097-range-from 0 n))))

;; Replacing column k with b produces the kth determinant in Cramer's vector.

(defun ht097-replace-at (index value list)
  (cond ((endp list) nil)
        ((zp index) (cons value (cdr list)))
        (t
         (cons (car list)
               (ht097-replace-at (- index 1) value (cdr list))))))

(defun ht097-replace-column (matrix vector column)
  (if (or (endp matrix) (endp vector))
      nil
    (cons (ht097-replace-at column (car vector) (car matrix))
          (ht097-replace-column
           (cdr matrix) (cdr vector) column))))

(defun ht097-cramer-vector-columns (matrix vector n columns)
  (if (endp columns)
      nil
    (cons (ht097-matrix-det
           (ht097-replace-column matrix vector (car columns))
           n)
          (ht097-cramer-vector-columns
           matrix vector n (cdr columns)))))

(defun ht097-cramer-vector (matrix vector n)
  (ht097-cramer-vector-columns
   matrix vector n (ht097-range-from 0 n)))

;; Matrix-vector multiplication and scalar multiplication use the same
;; polynomial-ring operations.

(defun ht097-poly-dot-product (left right)
  (if (or (endp left) (endp right))
      nil
    (ht097-poly-add
     (ht097-poly-mul (car left) (car right))
     (ht097-poly-dot-product (cdr left) (cdr right)))))

(defun ht097-matrix-vector-mul (matrix vector)
  (if (endp matrix)
      nil
    (cons (ht097-poly-dot-product (car matrix) vector)
          (ht097-matrix-vector-mul (cdr matrix) vector))))

(defun ht097-vector-scale (coefficient vector)
  (if (endp vector)
      nil
    (cons (ht097-poly-mul coefficient (car vector))
          (ht097-vector-scale coefficient (cdr vector)))))

(defun ht097-cramers-rule-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (let* ((matrix (ht097-generic-matrix n))
          (vector (ht097-generic-vector n))
          (determinant (ht097-matrix-det matrix n))
          (cramer-vector (ht097-cramer-vector matrix vector n)))
     (equal
      (ht097-matrix-vector-mul matrix cramer-vector)
      (ht097-vector-scale determinant vector)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: 097_cramer_s_rule
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems corpus artifact
-- hundred-theorems__agda__097, "Cramer's Rule": the determinant-scaled
-- column-replacement vector solves a square linear system, and for a
-- nonsingular matrix gives the solution coordinatewise. This file contains no proof.

module CramersRule where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; true; false)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _≠_
infix 1 _↔_

data Bottom : Set where

_≠_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≠ y = x ≡ y → Bottom

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  field
    forward  : A → B
    backward : B → A

record CommutativeRing (R : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    addR multiplyR : R → R → R
    negateR : R → R

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) →
      addR x y ≡ addR y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      addR (addR x y) z ≡ addR x (addR y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) →
      addR x zeroR ≡ x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) →
      addR x (negateR x) ≡ zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) →
      multiplyR x y ≡ multiplyR y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiplyR (multiplyR x y) z ≡
      multiplyR x (multiplyR y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) →
      multiplyR x oneR ≡ x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) →
      multiplyR x zeroR ≡ zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiplyR x (addR y z) ≡
      addR (multiplyR x y) (multiplyR x z)

record Field (F : Set) : Set₁ where
  field
    ring : CommutativeRing F
    inverse : F → F
    one-not-zero :
      CommutativeRing.oneR ring ≠
      CommutativeRing.zeroR ring
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : F) →
      x ≠ CommutativeRing.zeroR ring →
      CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring x (inverse x) ≡
      CommutativeRing.oneR ring

data Fin : Nat → Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} → Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} → Fin n → Fin (suc n)

finEqual : {n : Nat} → Fin n → Fin n → Bool
finEqual fzero fzero = true
finEqual fzero (fsuc j) = false
finEqual (fsuc i) fzero = false
finEqual (fsuc i) (fsuc j) = finEqual i j

select : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
select true yes no = yes
select false yes no = no

sumFin :
  {R : Set} →
  CommutativeRing R →
  {n : Nat} →
  (Fin n → R) →
  R
sumFin ring {zero} term =
  CommutativeRing.zeroR ring
sumFin ring {suc n} term =
  CommutativeRing.addR ring
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin ring (λ i → term (fsuc i)))

Matrix : Set → Nat → Set
Matrix R n = Fin n → Fin n → R

Vector : Set → Nat → Set
Vector R n = Fin n → R

VectorEqual :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n →
  Set
VectorEqual x y = (i : Fin _) → x i ≡ y i

skip :
  {n : Nat} →
  Fin (suc n) →
  Fin n →
  Fin (suc n)
skip {zero} column ()
skip {suc n} fzero k = fsuc k
skip {suc n} (fsuc column) fzero = fzero
skip {suc n} (fsuc column) (fsuc k) =
  fsuc (skip column k)

firstRowMinor :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R (suc n) →
  Fin (suc n) →
  Matrix R n
firstRowMinor A column i j =
  A (fsuc i) (skip column j)

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} →
  CommutativeRing R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Fin n →
  R
alternatingSign ring fzero =
  CommutativeRing.oneR ring
alternatingSign ring (fsuc i) =
  CommutativeRing.negateR ring
    (alternatingSign ring i)

determinant :
  {R : Set} →
  CommutativeRing R →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  R
determinant ring {zero} A =
  CommutativeRing.oneR ring
determinant ring {suc n} A =
  sumFin ring
    (λ column →
      CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring
        (alternatingSign ring column)
        (CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring
          (A fzero column)
          (determinant ring (firstRowMinor A column))))

replaceColumn :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  Fin n →
  Vector R n →
  Matrix R n
replaceColumn A column b i j =
  select (finEqual j column) (b i) (A i j)

cramerVector :
  {R : Set} →
  (ring : CommutativeRing R) →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n
cramerVector ring A b i =
  determinant ring (replaceColumn A i b)

matrixVectorProduct :
  {R : Set} →
  (ring : CommutativeRing R) →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix R n →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n
matrixVectorProduct ring A x i =
  sumFin ring
    (λ j →
      CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring (A i j) (x j))

scalarVector :
  {R : Set} →
  (ring : CommutativeRing R) →
  {n : Nat} →
  R →
  Vector R n →
  Vector R n
scalarVector ring scalar x i =
  CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring scalar (x i)

divide :
  {F : Set} →
  Field F →
  F →
  F →
  F
divide fieldStructure numerator denominator =
  CommutativeRing.multiplyR (Field.ring fieldStructure)
    numerator
    (Field.inverse fieldStructure denominator)

cramerSolution :
  {F : Set} →
  (fieldStructure : Field F) →
  {n : Nat} →
  Matrix F n →
  Vector F n →
  Vector F n
cramerSolution fieldStructure A b i =
  divide fieldStructure
    (determinant (Field.ring fieldStructure)
      (replaceColumn A i b))
    (determinant (Field.ring fieldStructure) A)

record CramersRuleStatement : Set₁ where
  field
    determinant-scaled-rule :
      (R : Set) →
      (ring : CommutativeRing R) →
      (n : Nat) →
      (A : Matrix R n) →
      (b : Vector R n) →
      VectorEqual
        (matrixVectorProduct ring A
          (cramerVector ring A b))
        (scalarVector ring
          (determinant ring A)
          b)

    nonsingular-solution-rule :
      (F : Set) →
      (fieldStructure : Field F) →
      (n : Nat) →
      (A : Matrix F n) →
      (x b : Vector F n) →
      determinant (Field.ring fieldStructure) A ≠
        CommutativeRing.zeroR (Field.ring fieldStructure) →
      VectorEqual
        (matrixVectorProduct (Field.ring fieldStructure) A x)
        b
      ↔
      VectorEqual x (cramerSolution fieldStructure A b)

cramers-rule : Set₁
cramers-rule = CramersRuleStatement

title: 097_cramer_s_rule
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of "Cramer's Rule" from Hundred Theorems
  artifact hundred-theorems__hol4__097. For a square real matrix on an
  arbitrary finite index set with nonzero determinant, Ax = b holds exactly
  when each coordinate of x is the determinant obtained by replacing the
  corresponding column with b, divided by the determinant of A. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory permutesTheory realTheory;

val cramer_s_rule =
  ``let determinant =
      \(s : 'i -> bool) (A : 'i -> 'i -> real).
        ITSET
          (\p acc.
            (if evenperm p then
               ITSET (\i q. A i (p i) * q) s 1
             else
               -(ITSET (\i q. A i (p i) * q) s 1)) + acc)
          {p : 'i -> 'i | p permutes s} 0
    in
    let replace_column =
      \(A : 'i -> 'i -> real) (b : 'i -> real) (k : 'i)
       (i : 'i) (j : 'i).
        if j = k then b i else A i j
    in
    let matrix_vec_mul =
      \(s : 'i -> bool) (A : 'i -> 'i -> real) (x : 'i -> real)
       (i : 'i).
        ITSET (\j acc. A i j * x j + acc) s 0
    in
      !(s : 'i -> bool) (A : 'i -> 'i -> real)
       (x : 'i -> real) (b : 'i -> real).
        FINITE s /\ determinant s A <> 0
        ==>
        ((!i. i IN s ==> matrix_vec_mul s A x i = b i) <=>
         (!k. k IN s ==>
              x k = determinant s (replace_column A b k) / determinant s A))``;

title: 097_cramer_s_rule
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of Hundred Theorems item 097, Cramer's rule
  over a commutative ring.

  This reproduces set.mm theorem cramer. The determinant of X is required to
  be a unit, and Z is the componentwise determinant quotient exactly when it
  solves XZ = Y.
$)

$[ library/set.mm $]

${
  $d B i $.
  $d D i $.
  $d i N $.
  $d R i $.
  $d i V $.
  $d i X $.
  $d i Y $.
  $d i Z $.
  $d .x. i $.
  $d ./ i $.

  hundred-theorems-097-matrix-algebra $e
    |- A = ( N Mat R )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-097-matrix-carrier $e
    |- B = ( Base ` A )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-097-vector-carrier $e
    |- V = ( ( Base ` R ) ^m N )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-097-determinant $e
    |- D = ( N maDet R )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-097-matrix-vector-product $e
    |- .x. = ( R maVecMul <. N , N >. )
  $.
  hundred-theorems-097-division $e
    |- ./ = ( /r ` R )
  $.

  hundred-theorems-097-cramer $a
    |- (
         (
           ( R e. CRing /\ N =/= (/) )
           /\
           ( X e. B /\ Y e. V )
           /\
           ( D ` X ) e. ( Unit ` R )
         )
         ->
         (
           Z =
             (
               i e. N |->
               (
                 ( D ` ( ( X ( N matRepV R ) Y ) ` i ) )
                 ./
                 ( D ` X )
               )
             )
           <->
           ( X .x. Z ) = Y
         )
       )
  $.
$}

title: 097_cramer_s_rule
content:
% Statement-only formalization of "Cramer's Rule" from Hundred Theorems
% artifact 097 (hundred-theorems__pvs__097): a nonsingular real square
% linear system is equivalent to the column-replacement determinant formula
% for every component of its solution. This file contains no proof.

cramer_s_rule_097[n: posnat]: THEORY
BEGIN
  vector: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> real]

  real_sum(values: [nat -> real], count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      real_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  real_product(values: [nat -> real], count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      real_product(values, count - 1) * values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  quotient_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1
        + quotient_aux(
            numerator - denominator,
            denominator,
            fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_ndiv(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    quotient_aux(
      numerator,
      denominator,
      numerator + 1)

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  function_code_count: nat = n ^ n

  permutation_entry(code, row: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(safe_ndiv(code, n ^ row), n)

  permutation_code(code: nat): bool =
    code < function_code_count
      AND (FORALL (row_1, row_2: nat):
        (row_1 < n
          AND row_2 < n
          AND permutation_entry(code, row_1)
            = permutation_entry(code, row_2))
        IMPLIES row_1 = row_2)

  pair_row(pair: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(pair, n)

  pair_column(pair: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(pair, n)

  inversion_at(code, pair: nat): bool =
    pair_row(pair) < n
      AND pair_column(pair) < n
      AND pair_row(pair) < pair_column(pair)
      AND permutation_entry(code, pair_row(pair))
        > permutation_entry(code, pair_column(pair))

  count_true(
      property: [nat -> bool],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_true(property, count - 1)
        + IF property(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  inversion_count(code: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (pair: nat): inversion_at(code, pair)),
      n * n)

  permutation_sign(code: nat): real =
    IF mod(inversion_count(code), 2) = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -1
    ENDIF

  permutation_product(
      A: matrix,
      code, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      permutation_product(A, code, count - 1)
        * A(
            count - 1,
            permutation_entry(code, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  determinant_sum(
      A: matrix,
      limit: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET code: nat = limit - 1 IN
        determinant_sum(A, limit - 1)
          + IF permutation_code(code) THEN
              permutation_sign(code)
                * permutation_product(A, code, n)
            ELSE
              0
            ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  determinant(A: matrix): real =
    determinant_sum(A, function_code_count)

  matrix_vector_product(A: matrix, x: vector, row: nat): real =
    real_sum(
      (LAMBDA (column: nat): A(row, column) * x(column)),
      n)

  linear_system(A: matrix, x, b: vector): bool =
    FORALL (row: nat):
      row < n IMPLIES matrix_vector_product(A, x, row) = b(row)

  replace_column(A: matrix, b: vector, column: nat): matrix =
    (LAMBDA (row, current_column: nat):
      IF current_column = column THEN
        b(row)
      ELSE
        A(row, current_column)
      ENDIF)

  cramer_s_rule: bool =
    FORALL (A: matrix), (x, b: vector):
      determinant(A) /= 0 IMPLIES
        (linear_system(A, x, b) IFF
          (FORALL (column: nat):
            column < n IMPLIES
              x(column)
                = determinant(replace_column(A, b, column))
                    / determinant(A)))
END cramer_s_rule_097

title: 098_bertrand_s_postulate
content:
/-
